- `calor ids index` synchronises the identity sidecar for the files it is given before it exports (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/IdsCommand.cs:184`), and the shim passes the workspace file (`run-pair.sh:1102`). Whether this creates `.calor/ids.json` in the agent's workspace on 0.30 was not verified by execution.
- `validate-telemetry.sh` is called by no test and no workflow. Its entry check also restricts `code` to `Calor` plus four digits (`:201`), which is narrower than the JSON schema.
- `extract_metrics` filters journal records on the literal `loop-telemetry/2` when it computes `meanFeedbackLatencyMs` and `envelopeValidAll` (`run-pair.sh:1598-1602`). Three epoch drivers pin the same literal (`run-epoch.sh:46`, `run-m5-epoch.sh:207`, `run-guarantees-epoch.sh:150`); the last two serve a paused and a closed programme. `ppw-run-observer.py:421` writes its own `/2` records for the paused PP-W design and is not touched.

## Why

The 0.30 evaluation has to say, per arm, which kinds of error cost the agent iterations and how many of the diagnostics it hit offered a fix. Archived runs answer neither question, and the missing fields cannot be recomputed later. An entry records only a code and a declaration id, the source of each iteration is not kept, and whether a fix is safe depends on the instance and not on the code: the tab-indentation fix is marked safe only when the file has no mixed indentation (`src/Calor.Compiler/Parsing/Lexer.cs:398`). No diagnostic at all is recorded for the C# arm, so a per-arm comparison of failure classes has one empty side. These fields must exist before the first paid run of #1605. The report that reads them (#1760) can follow later.

## Done when

- Unit tests under `bench/phase0-agent-native/tests/` (run by `.github/workflows/test.yml:124`) cover:
  - a compiler JSON fixture with one diagnostic carrying a safe fix, one carrying an unsafe fix and one with none, yielding the three flag combinations;
  - an MSBuild log fixture with a `CS` error in a hand-written file, a `CS` error in a `.g.cs` file, a warning and a `Calor` error, yielding two error entries (one with `generated: true`), one warning entry and no `Calor` entry;
  - `validate-telemetry.sh` accepting a `/3` record and an archived `/2` record, and rejecting a `/3` record without the new fields.
- With a built 0.30 product, `run-pair.sh --null-agent --exemplar <file>` on one pair writes journal records whose `schema` is `loop-telemetry/3`, whose `arm` is `calor+exemplar` and whose `envelope_valid` is `true`, and a `result.json` whose `meanFeedbackLatencyMs` is a number and whose `envelopeValidAll` is `true`. This is a product-backed test, skipped without a product like `NullAgentEndToEnd` (`tests/test_harness_capture.py:1541`); the pull request records where it ran.
- A null epoch written by `run-epoch.sh` after the change has `telemetrySchema: "loop-telemetry/3"` in its `pins.json`, and `git grep -n 'telemetrySchema:"loop-telemetry/2"' -- bench/phase0-agent-native` prints nothing.
- A run of the C# arm with a local `claude` stub in place of the agent (the precedent is `tests/test_initialized_workspace.py:336-404`; the stub writes a compile error, builds, fixes it, builds) yields a first record with a `CS` code in `build_diagnostics` and a second record with none. The test is skipped where no .NET SDK is installed.
- A product-backed test asserts, before cleanup, that a Calor-arm workspace contains no `.calor/` directory that the starter did not ship.
- `envelopes/` and `build-logs/` in a run directory hold one file per distinct `src_tree_hash` in the journal.
- `loop-telemetry-schema.md` documents every new field and states whether `declarationId` is populated on 0.30, where declaration ids live in a sidecar and the telemetry compile sees copies without one.

## Not in scope

- Any metric computed from these fields: #1760.
- A target for the share of diagnostics with a safe fix. It is reported descriptively. That no effect-row or contract fix is ever marked safe is pinned by #1801.

Part of epic #1761. Depends on #1766 and #1762. Blocks #1767, #1760 and #1605.

issues.title: [0.31] Harness support for delivery variants: variant selection, CLI-only switch, primer-read log, starter-less fixtures
issues.body:
## Change

Extend `bench/phase0-agent-native/run-pair.sh --initialized-workspace`, the mode that runs the real `calor init` in a fresh workspace, so that stage 2 of #1605 can run. Stage 2 compares how the syntax primer reaches the agent, on the two pairs where Calor cost extra iterations in July (`N1-003-csv-row`, `W3-003-kv-journal`). Its arms and n are fixed in #1770. No paid agent run is part of this issue. Paths below without a directory are under `bench/phase0-agent-native/`.

Terms: a *pair* is one task with a specification, a hidden test suite and a starting fixture (the *starter*) per arm; an *arm* is one configuration under test; the *primer* is the syntax sheet served as the MCP resource `calor://primer`; a *delivery variant* is one way that sheet reaches the agent; an *iteration* is one journalled build or test invocation that follows an edit; `--null-agent` applies the reference solution in place of an agent and costs nothing.

Gate. This issue is built only if the design entry of #1770 registers stage 2 (its option with stage 1 and stage 2). The gate's value is that entry, an entry in Annex A of `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md`; it has no numeric threshold.

- *Open:* the entry is merged and registers stage 2. Work starts; the spend record of #1770 may follow later.
- *Shut:* the entry is merged and registers no stage 2 (stage 1 only, the reduced design, or no paid run). Close this issue as not planned and link the entry.
- *Held:* the entry is not merged. No part starts and the issue stays open. It gates stage 2 only, which does not hold the 0.31 release; stage 2 must publish, or be recorded on #1605 as not run, before #1823 is decided.

1. **Variant selection.** A `--delivery <variant>` option whose values are the `calor init` options #1773 adds: the pointer (as shipped), the primer inlined in the generated agent file, and the primer inlined plus the starter `.calr` file that `calor init` writes. The harness passes the option to the real `init` command and never rewrites a generated file. The variant goes into `initialization.json` and into the arm label, so two variants cannot share an output directory.
2. **CLI-only switch.** An option under which no MCP server is offered to the agent. Pass an empty server list with `--strict-mcp-config`, so that neither the registration `calor init` generated nor the operator's own servers load. Initialization must not fail for lack of an MCP primer read in this arm; the pre-run primer check goes through the CLI command #1771 adds. The `calor` command stays on `PATH`.
3. **Primer-read log.** `result.json` gains `primerRead`: a count per channel (the MCP resource `calor://primer`, `calor_help`, the CLI command) and whether the first read precedes the first edit of a `.calr` file. Take it from the traffic itself, journalled outside the agent. For the two MCP channels that is either a journal the server writes when an environment variable is set (the precedent is `CALOR_MCP_WRITE_LOG`, `src/Calor.Compiler/Mcp/Tools/FileWriteTool.cs:65`) or a stdio proxy the harness places in front of the server; the implementer chooses and the README says which. For the CLI channel it is a journal written by the `calor` wrapper the harness already puts on `PATH`. The transcript is a cross-check only: no archived transcript in the repository contains a resource read, so its event shape in the client's stream is unverified.
4. **Starter-less fixtures.** For each pair #1770 registers for stage 2, add a new pair directory (a new id, valid under `task-spec-schema.json`) whose starting fixture holds no source file in either arm. Its `spec.md` states the whole public surface, including the operations the original starter already implemented, and names for each arm the file, the namespace and the container the hidden suite's shim binds to. The hidden tests, shims and reference solutions are those of the original pair, with the Calor reference in 0.30 syntax. `materialize` must accept a fixture without a source file.
5. **`calor check` is an iteration.** In an initialized workspace the `calor` wrapper runs the CLI directly, so a `calor check` (build, test and verify in one command) leaves no journal record and is not counted, while every `dotnet build` of the C# arm is. Journal each `calor check` through the same observation as `dotnet build` (edit detection, iteration ordinal, silent hidden-suite run), as a record with `cmd: "check"` in the schema #1764 leaves; add that value to the `cmd` enum of `loop-telemetry.schema.json` and to `validate-telemetry.sh`. Other `calor` subcommands stay unjournalled.
6. **MCP compiles are counted.** The generated agent file tells the agent to compile with the MCP tool `calor_compile` after each edit, and those calls leave no journal record either. Record in `result.json` the number of `calor_compile` calls per run and how many followed an edit of a `.calr` file, from the step-3 journal or proxy. Whether such a call is an iteration is a rule of the #1770 design entry. If the entry says yes, journal each one as step 5 does, with `cmd: "compile"`; if it says no or is silent, `iterations` is unchanged and the README states that MCP compiles are reported beside it.

Deviation to state, not to fix: initialized-workspace arms run without the harness's `.g.cs` write block, and the product hook they run with allows `.g.cs` writes. The #1770 design entry records this deviation; the README section for this mode repeats it.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- `--initialized-workspace` accepts only the ordinary strict Calor arm with raw edits and rejects `--arm-label` and `--canary-only` (`run-pair.sh:294-310`). It rejects pairs that have a `smoke/` directory or a `defect.json` (`:364-367`). The label gains the suffix `+initialized` (`:359`): `calor+initialized`, or `calor+exemplar+initialized` with `--exemplar`.
- `harness-capture.py initialize_workspace` always runs `init --ai claude --project src/Src.csproj` (`:610-611`), fails unless init generated the `calor` MCP registration with arguments `mcp --stdio` (`:634-638`), reads `calor://primer` from the selected compiler over MCP as a control (`:640-658`), and always writes `mcp-config.json` (`:676-678`). Its docstring forbids reconstructing generated files (`:564-567`). `run-pair.sh:1331` passes `--mcp-config … --strict-mcp-config` whenever that file exists, so no arm runs without the server.
- `calor init` has four options: `--ai`, `--project`, `--solution`, `--force` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/InitCommand.cs:16-33`). The generated agent file says "Read `calor://primer`" (`src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Templates/CLAUDE.md.template:9`) and "Compile with `calor_compile` after each edit" (`:13`), and init writes no copy of the primer. The primer is registered only as an MCP resource (`src/Calor.Compiler/Mcp/McpMessageHandler.cs:124-130`).
- `--exemplar` only appends text to the prompt (`run-pair.sh:1261-1263`). In this mode its bytes are archived with the initialized inputs (`:752-756`).
- In this mode the harness writes a `calor` wrapper into the shim directory (`run-pair.sh:982-985`). The wrapper execs the real `dotnet` with the CLI, bypassing the journalling `dotnet` shim, so no `calor` invocation produces a journal record. `calor check` is the CLI's "Build, test and verify one source snapshot" command (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/TestCommand.cs:65`). `iterations` in `result.json` counts journal records with `edited: true` (`run-pair.sh:1496`), and the journal's `cmd` enum is `build`, `test`, `run` (`loop-telemetry.schema.json:16`).
- In this mode the harness does not install its `.g.cs` write block (`run-pair.sh:899`), and the product hook that `calor init` installs allows `.g.cs` writes (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/HookCommand.cs:283-287`).
- Every two-arm pair ships a starter in both arms, and the specifications rely on it. `pairs/N1-003-csv-row/spec.md` has a section "Existing behavior (already implemented in the starting fixture)" and names functions only. The names the hidden suite binds to are in the shims: `CsvRow.CsvRowModule` for Calor and `CsvRowLib.CsvRow` for C# (`pairs/N1-003-csv-row/tests/shims/TestShim.calor.cs`, `TestShim.csharp.cs`). `materialize` requires the fixture directory to exist (`run-pair.sh:735`).
- A no-provider test already drives this mode with a local `claude` stub (`tests/test_initialized_workspace.py:336-404`).

## Why

The only lever with a measured effect on the cost of writing new Calor is the in-context syntax reference: in July a 60-line exemplar appended to the prompt removed 55% of the excess iterations (`epochs/e1a-attribution/VERDICT.md:11-28`, pre-0.30 syntax, unpinned model). `calor init` ships a pointer to that reference, and whether agents follow the pointer has never been measured. Stage 2 measures it. Three things stand in the way: the harness can produce no variant but the pointer, it cannot run without the MCP server, and every pair hands the agent a starter file, which #1605 itself calls "the main exemplar" and which would mask the difference between variants. A fourth distorts the reading: iterations are counted from journalled `dotnet` invocations, so a Calor agent that checks its work with `calor check` appears to iterate less than a C# agent that runs `dotnet build`. An agent that compiles through the MCP tool is undercounted the same way. The same count is read again for the per-agent Calor arms in 0.33 (#1811, through the drivers of #1651).

## Done when

- A product-backed test (skipped without a built compiler) initializes a workspace for each variant. It asserts that the archived agent file differs between pointer and inline as #1773 specifies, that the starter variant contains the `.calr` file `calor init` wrote, and that `initialization.json` records the variant.
- A stub-agent test under the CLI-only switch asserts that the client's argument list offers no `calor` server, and that `calor` on `PATH` prints the primer through the #1771 command.
- A no-provider test with four sessions (one reads the MCP resource by speaking MCP to the journalled server, as `harness-capture.py:640-658` already does; one calls `calor_help` for the primer; one runs the CLI command through the wrapper; one reads nothing) yields `primerRead` counts for resource, help and CLI of 1/0/0, 0/1/0, 0/0/1 and 0/0/0.
- For each registered stage-2 pair, the starter-less pair passes `--null-agent` in both arms (ordinary mode for C#, initialized mode for Calor) with `escapedBugs: 0`, and its `pair.json` validates against `task-spec-schema.json`.
- Two variants run back to back write to different run directories.
- A no-provider test in an initialized workspace whose stub edits a `.calr` file, runs `calor check`, edits again and runs `calor check` again: `journal.jsonl` holds two records with `cmd: "check"` and `edited: true`, `result.json` has `iterations: 2`, and `validate-telemetry.sh` accepts the journal. A `calor --version` call by the same stub adds no record.
- A no-provider test whose session edits a `.calr` file and then calls `calor_compile` on the journalled server yields a `result.json` that reports one `calor_compile` call, made after an edit. If the #1770 design entry counts such a call as an iteration, the journal also holds a record with `cmd: "compile"` and `iterations` is 1; otherwise `iterations` is 0.
- If the primer-read log is a journal written by the MCP server, the product change has a test under `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/`, and `expectedTotal` for that project in `eng/test-manifest.json` is raised by the number of tests added.
- The product-backed tests are skipped in CI, which builds no compiler in the job that runs the harness tests; the pull request records the machine and the output of the run.
- `bench/phase0-agent-native/README.md` documents the options, the `check` record, how MCP compiles are counted and the `.g.cs` deviation.
- Or, with the gate shut: the issue is closed as not planned with a link to the #1770 design entry.

## Not in scope

- The `calor init` options themselves (#1773), and the primer command and `calor_help` action (#1771).
- Which variants run, n per variant and the decision rule: #1770.
- Resource-read support in other agent clients: #1820, which cites this issue's primer-read log for Claude Code.
- Blocking `.g.cs` writes in `calor init` workspaces: the deviation is recorded in #1770, not removed here.
- What an ordinary (non-initialized) arm sees.

Part of epic #1761. Depends on #1766, #1764, #1770 (its design entry), #1773 and #1771. Blocks stage 2 of #1605.

issues.title: [0.31] Report script for the 0.30 evaluation: failure classes, opportunity counts, dead-end rate, repeat rate, blocked test writes
issues.body:
## Change

Add a report script under `bench/phase0-agent-native/` (for example `eval-report.py`) that reads an archived epoch directory and prints one JSON document and one Markdown table per arm and pair. It runs after collection, on archives, and invokes no agent. Inputs per run: `result.json`, `journal.jsonl`, `transcript.jsonl`, `agent-builds.jsonl`, `final-src/`, and `initialization.json` where present. Paths below without a directory are under `bench/phase0-agent-native/`.

Terms: a *pair* is one task with a specification, a hidden test suite and a starting fixture per arm; an *epoch* is one archived collection in which all arms ran interleaved; an *arm* is one configuration under test; an *iteration* is a journal record with `edited: true`; an *escaped defect* is a hidden test that still fails when the agent declares the task done; an *opportunity* is a place in a task where a defect of a given class could occur.

Three things are checked in with the script:

- **The class table**, `bench/phase0-agent-native/diagnostic-classes.json` (the name is the implementer's choice): one entry per diagnostic code, `Calor` and `CS`, giving its class. A code that is not in the table is reported as `unclassified`.
- **The definitions**, in a section of `bench/phase0-agent-native/README.md` that other issues can cite. This issue owns the definition of *first-build pass rate*: `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md` does not define it, and #1832 and #1835 use the definition written here.
- **No thresholds.** They are read from the thresholds file that #1770 registers (proposed there as `bench/phase0-agent-native/registrations/eval-0.30.json`), passed by path. Given none, the script prints "threshold not registered" for every outcome.

Each column is defined in that README section, repeated in the script's docstring and pinned by a test:

| Column | Definition |
|---|---|
| Failure class of each failed iteration | A failed iteration is a journal record with `edited: true` that is not green (`heldout_fail > 0`; the harness counts a state that does not build as all hidden tests failing). When the record carries an error diagnostic, its class comes from the class table (the `diagnostics` and `build_diagnostics` arrays of #1764). When it carries none (the build succeeds and hidden tests fail), the class is `logic`. Classes: unknown or removed syntax; type error; null; missing case; resource leak; effect; contract; logic; unclassified. |
| Attempts to write removed forms | Write and Edit tool calls on `.calr` files in the transcript whose content contains a retired `§` marker or an `Option` or `Result` construction. Counted under "unknown or removed syntax" whether or not a build followed. |
| Failure class of each escaped defect | An escaped defect is a hidden test that fails when the agent declares the task done (`heldoutFinal.failedTests`). Its class comes from an optional per-pair map of test name to class, and is `logic` when the pair has no map. |
| Opportunity count per class | Per task, counted on the pair's reference solutions in both languages by a documented rule: nullable-typed values (null), matches or switches over a non-bool type (missing case), `IDisposable` locals or `using` (resource leak). |
| Outcome per class | Above threshold, below threshold, held (between the two) or not measurable (too few opportunities or runs), each as the thresholds file defines it; these are the four readings #1770 registers. Neither held nor not measurable is ever reported as below. |
| C#-habit events per form | Per form in the rubric committed with the registration (#1770 item 9): the number of valid arm runs with at least one failed iteration that the rubric maps to the form, over the valid runs on pairs whose reference uses the form, and the number of pairs. The outcome (admissible, not admissible, not measurable) is read from the thresholds file. |
| First-build pass rate | Share of valid runs whose first edited build-or-test invocation exits 0. The invocation is the first journal record with `edited: true`, whatever its `cmd` (`build`, `test`, `run`, or `check` once #1767 journals it), and the exit code is the agent-visible one (`exit`). A run with no such record is counted in the denominator and not in the numerator. First-try green (`iterationsToGreen == 1`) is reported beside it. |
| `.g.cs` dead-end rate | The definition at `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md:42`, with one stated difference: the share of Calor-arm runs with (a) an attempted Write or Edit on a `.g.cs` path, blocked or not, or (b) at least one wasted iteration on an error located in a `.g.cs` file. Wasted means two consecutive compiles with identical errors (code plus message, with paths and line numbers stripped) and no `.calr` edit between them; for a runtime error, the agent's next action must also reference the `.g.cs` frame. The gates document counts only blocked writes in (a); initialized-workspace arms have no block, so every attempt is counted and the two kinds are reported separately. |
| Calor0006 hits | Per run, the number of iterations whose diagnostics include `Calor0006`. |
| Repeat rate per diagnostic code | Per arm and code: among runs that hit the code, the share that hit it in two or more iterations, and the mean number of iterations. |
| Turns before the first build | Distinct top-level assistant messages before the first build, test or `calor` invocation. |
| Fix coverage | Share of agent-hit diagnostic entries with `hasFix`, and with `isSafeToApply`. Descriptive, not a target. |
| Blocked test writes | In initialized-workspace arms: Write calls on a test-like `.cs` path that the product hook refused. In other arms: reported as not observable, with the number of attempted test-file creations for information. |

A field that an archive lacks (older telemetry, no transcript) prints as "not available", never as zero.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- No script computes any of these. The existing analyzers are specific to one epoch each (`ppe1-analyze.py`, `w5-analyze.py`, `guarantees-analyze.py`, `ppe1-turn-attribution.py`).
- Per run the harness archives `transcript.jsonl` (every event), `agent-builds.jsonl` (each `dotnet build`, `dotnet test` or `calor` call by the agent, with output truncated at 4,000 characters: `harness-capture.py:123`, `:257-329`), `journal.jsonl`, `final-src/` and `result.json`.
- `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md:42` defines the `.g.cs` dead-end rate. The gates document defines no first-build pass rate (its metric list is `:35-43`), so this issue defines one.
- Ordinary Calor arms install a `.g.cs` write block (`run-pair.sh:899`, `:916-919`), and every ordinary arm gets a prompt rule against test files (`:1248`), which nothing enforces. Initialized-workspace arms run the product hook instead. It blocks new `.cs` files with "BLOCKED: Cannot create C# file" (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/HookCommand.cs:297-312`) and allows `.g.cs` writes (`:283-287`); the harness block is not installed there (`run-pair.sh:899`).
- The 50 translated pair files contain no `match`, `enum`, `using` statement, `null` or nullable type, and the C# references contain no `switch`, `using` statement or `null` (grep over `tests/TestData/ActiveSyntax/bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs` and `bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs/*/reference/csharp`). On the current pair set the null, missing-case and resource-leak classes will read "not measurable".
- The July epoch recorded zero escaped defects in 180 runs, one invalid slot aside (`epochs/e1a-attribution/VERDICT.md:62-64`, pre-0.30 syntax).
- Five call sites create a fix marked safe, all under `src/Calor.Compiler/`: `Parsing/Parser.cs:621`, `Parsing/Lexer.cs:398` and `:407` (conditionally), `Formatting/CalorFormatter.cs:441` and `:481`.
- `epochs/ws5-probe-001` holds `loop-telemetry/2` journals for a `calor` and a `csharp` arm and no `transcript.jsonl` (54 runs), which makes it a smoke input for the "not available" path.

## Why

Later milestones build a new guarantee (null gaps, enum exhaustiveness, disposal) only for a defect class that agents are measured to produce, and choose which diagnostics get a fix by how often agents hit and repeat them. Those decisions need a base rate per class with a denominator, and a third outcome for a class the tasks cannot exhibit. Without it every gate reads zero by construction and the item is dropped on no evidence. The same script gives #1605 its descriptive columns and is run unchanged on the per-agent archives in 0.33 (#1811). It works on archives, so it does not hold the run. This issue may slip to 0.32 without holding the 0.31 release.

## Done when

- The script and a test module exist under `bench/phase0-agent-native/`, and the tests run at `.github/workflows/test.yml:124`.
- The class table is committed. A test asserts that every code in it has exactly one class from the list in the first row of the table above, and that it covers every diagnostic code the fixture epoch contains except one left out on purpose.
- That code, present in the fixture and absent from the table, is reported as `unclassified` and listed by code; a test asserts the list.
- A synthetic fixture epoch committed under `bench/phase0-agent-native/tests/fixtures/` exercises every column, including: an iteration with `Calor0006`; a repeated code; a `.g.cs` dead end of each kind; a blocked test write; a class with zero opportunities (expected output "not measurable"); a failing hidden test with and without a class map; a run whose first edited invocation exits 0 and one whose first exits 1 (first-build pass rate 0.5).
- `python3 <script> bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/ws5-probe-001` exits 0 and prints "not available" for the fields that archive lacks.
- Given no thresholds file the script prints "threshold not registered" for every class outcome; given a fixture thresholds file it prints, for four fixture classes, "above threshold", "below threshold", "held" and "not measurable". A test asserts both.
- The fixture epoch has one form above and one below the fixture C#-habit threshold, and a test asserts both outcomes.
- Opportunity counts for the 25 translated pairs are printed, and are zero for null, missing case and resource leak, matching the baseline.
- `bench/phase0-agent-native/README.md` names the script, its inputs and each definition, with the definition of first-build pass rate under a heading that #1832 and #1835 can link.

## Not in scope

- Thresholds, minimum opportunity counts and the reading of each outcome: #1770.
- Cost, token, turn and iteration ratios to the C# arm: defined in #1770 and reported by #1605 from `result.json`.
- The unknown-effect share: #1802.
- Tasks that can exhibit null, missing-case or resource-leak defects: #1789.

Part of epic #1761. Depends on #1764. Blocks #1811.

issues.title: [0.31] Legacy-dialect allowlist and self-check
issues.body:
## Change

0.30 retired the `§` syntax with no rewriter, and 853 `.calr` files in that syntax remain in the tree on purpose. Record which they are and why, and stop new ones from appearing unnoticed. Most are benchmark material: pair fixtures (one task with a starting program per language), and the archived outputs of past benchmark collections (epochs).

1. **Allowlist.** `tests/TestData/ActiveSyntax/inputs.json` already lists every original that has a current-syntax copy (`originalPaths`). Add, in that file under a new key or in a file beside it, a second list of `.calr` paths or directory prefixes that are kept as they are and have no copy, and a map from each directory prefix of `originalPaths` to the same fields (`originalPaths` itself stays a list of strings). Every entry carries three fields:
   - `dialect`: `pre-0.30` for the retired `§` syntax, or `0.30` for 0.30-syntax files that must stay frozen. No `0.30` entry is needed today. The value exists so that 0.30-syntax evidence, for example the archived run outputs of #1605, can be listed before the 0.32 rewrite (#1803) changes the current syntax again.
   - `class`: `frozen-evidence` (archived epoch output and pinned fixtures, never edited), `retained-original` (kept byte-identical behind a translated copy), `legacy-arm-input` (read by the pre-0.30 arm A of #1605) or `pending-1648`.
   - `reason`: one line.
2. **Classification table.** Commit the table from the baseline below, with current counts, where the allowlist lives or in `bench/phase0-agent-native/README.md`. The classes in the table are a proposal. The maintainer accepts or changes them by approving the pull request; that approval is part of the 0.31 tracker sign-off (#1759).
3. **Notes.** In each directory group of the table, add a short note (`LEGACY-DIALECT.md` or a README section): the files here are in the pre-0.30 syntax, are kept byte-identical, belong to the stated class, have their current copy at the stated path if one exists, and are not syntax examples.
4. **Self-check.** A check over tracked `.calr` files that fails when a file contains a retired marker and is on neither list; when a listed path no longer exists; and when a path listed with `dialect: pre-0.30` no longer contains a marker. A retired marker is `§` followed by a letter or `/`, the definition `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/SourceLiteralSyntaxGuardTests.cs:10-12` uses. Implement it as an xUnit test beside `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/ActiveSyntaxInputTests.cs`, or as a script in the `calor-first-guard` job of `.github/workflows/test.yml`; either runs on every pull request.

No retired file is translated, moved or edited by this issue.

Order.

- #1648 records the fate of the six `W-00x` pair directories. If it has done so when this lands, their 52 files carry the class it recorded; if not, they are listed as `pending-1648` and #1648 owns the follow-up edit. The check passes either way, so the dependency on #1648 is an ordering preference: an open #1648 holds neither this issue nor, through it, #1803.
- The check reads `.calr` files only, and no `.calr` file under `tests/E2E` holds a retired marker, so it does not wait for #1736.
- It must be merged before #1803. That change applies the 0.32 rewrite across the repository, skips every path on this allowlist (the rewriter is #1806), and begins by adding the 0.30-syntax evidence that must stay frozen to it.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

853 of 1,823 tracked `.calr` files contain a retired marker (`git ls-files '*.calr'`, then `grep -lE '§[A-Za-z/]'`). 746 of them are in `originalPaths`; 107 have no copy.

| Group | Files | Current copy | Proposed class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/` (`e1-rows-parity-001` 40, `guarantees-probe-001` 90, `w5-parity-001` 40, `w5-parity-002` 40) | 210 | yes | frozen-evidence |
| `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/` (`w-rows-dry-001` 36, `w-rows-dry-002` 18) | 54 | no | frozen-evidence |
| `bench/phase0-agent-native/latency/` | 106 | yes | retained-original |
| `bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs/`, the 25 two-arm pairs | 50 | yes | legacy-arm-input |
| `bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs/W-00*` | 52 | no | pending-1648 |
| `bench/phase0-agent-native/fixtures/d-s1.5/` | 24 | yes | retained-original |
| `bench/phase0-agent-native/templates/calor-arm/permissive-canary.calr` | 1 | no | legacy-arm-input |
| `tests/TestData/Benchmarks/` | 226 | yes | retained-original |
| `tests/TestData/EditScripts/` | 60 | yes | retained-original |
| `tests/Calor.Conversion.Tests/Snapshots/` | 48 | yes | retained-original |
| `docs/design/spikes/effect-rows/` | 15 | yes | frozen-evidence (pinned by `blobSha`, for example `bench/phase0-agent-native/effect-rows-probe-ledger.json:32-33`) |
| `benchmarks/` | 7 | yes | retained-original |

- `originalPaths` has 767 entries; the 21 that carry no retired marker are 10 under `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/SelfTest/` and 11 under `samples/`. The test helper reads the file by named property (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/ActiveSyntaxInputs.cs:21-30`, `:73`), so a new top-level key does not disturb it; `scripts/registered_ledger_historical_replay.py:469` also names the file.
- `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/ActiveSyntaxInputTests.cs:133` parses every registered copy with the current compiler. No test asserts the reverse: that a retired-syntax `.calr` file is registered or listed.
- None of the directory groups has a note that its `.calr` files are retired syntax. `tests/TestData/EditScripts/`, `benchmarks/` and `bench/phase0-agent-native/fixtures/d-s1.5/` have a README, without such a note; the other groups have none.
- No `.calr` file under `tests/E2E` contains a retired marker (58 files, 0 matches). The retired syntax #1736 removes there is in `.json`, `.md`, `.py` and `.sh` files, which this check does not read.
- `eng/test-manifest.json` pins the test count of each test project (`expectedTotal`; 22,559 for `Calor.Compiler.Tests` at `:8`), and CI fails on a different count.

## Why

Agents that could read the checkout in July learned the syntax from whatever `.calr` files they found, and nearly half of those files now teach a dialect the compiler rejects. #1762 keeps benchmark agents out of the checkout, so #1605 does not wait for this issue. The files remain a hazard for people and agents working in the repository, and for the mechanical rewriter planned in 0.32 (#1806), which must skip them: 264 archived epoch outputs and 15 hash-pinned spike fixtures are evidence, and the originals behind translated copies are kept so that historical byte and hash checks keep reading them. One list with a reason per entry, and a check that fails on anything outside it, turns that from convention into something CI enforces. The `dialect` field keeps the list usable after 0.32, when 0.30-syntax evidence becomes legacy in its turn. This issue may slip to 0.32 without holding the 0.31 release, provided it lands before #1803.

## Done when

- The self-check passes on `main`. Its own tests show it failing when a retired-syntax `.calr` file is added outside both lists, when a listed file is deleted, and when a file listed as `pre-0.30` no longer contains a marker; and passing when a marker-free file is listed with `dialect: 0.30`.
- The two lists together cover exactly the files the self-check finds: 746 and 107 at HEAD, with any difference explained in the pull request.
- Every entry and every directory prefix has a `dialect`, a `class` and a `reason`.
- The classification table is committed and the maintainer's approval of it is on the pull request.
- Every directory group in the table has the note.
- `git diff --diff-filter=MD --name-only <base> -- '*.calr'` prints nothing.
- The 52 `W-00x` files carry the class #1648 recorded. If #1648 is still open they are listed as `pending-1648`, and the pull request names #1648 as the owner of the follow-up edit.
- If the check is an xUnit test, `expectedTotal` for `Calor.Compiler.Tests` in `eng/test-manifest.json` is raised by the number of tests added.

## Not in scope

- Wiring the translated pair copies into the harness (#1766) and the non-`.calr` files under `tests/E2E` (#1736, whose own done-when greps them).
- Retired syntax in Markdown and in `CHANGELOG.md`.
- The 220 tracked `.calr.inc` fragments of the paused PP-W research (`git ls-files '*.calr.inc'`; all hold retired markers). The check reads `.calr` files only. They are under `tasks/ppw-redesign` (52), `epochs/w-rows-pilot-001` (52), `epochs/w-rows-001` (52), `task-candidates/1256` (36) and `buildability/1255` (28), all in `bench/phase0-agent-native/`. #1648 classifies them in its closing record. Extending the check to `*.calr.inc` is a follow-up with no issue.
- Keeping benchmark agents out of the checkout: #1762.
- Listing files that do not exist yet. #1605 adds its arm-A outputs, which are pre-0.30 syntax, when it commits them; #1803 adds the 0.30-syntax evidence as its first step.
- Calor0006 guidance (#1788) and a retired-to-current rewriter (#1806 records that decision).

Part of epic #1761. Depends on #1648. Blocks #1803.

issues.title: [0.31] Migrate the E2E agent-task refactoring benchmark to the 0.30 language before its next run
issues.body:
**Current**

The issue asks for the end-to-end agent-task suite under `tests/E2E/agent-tasks/` to be rewritten in 0.30 syntax (task prompts, fixture `CLAUDE.md` files, acceptance and verify scripts), and for the `§` greps in `lib/helpers.sh` to be replaced by 0.30 patterns "or better" by `calor` CLI/JSON output, with the C# arm's counting rules documented. It is done when a grep for retired markers under `tests/E2E` (excluding `benchmark-results/`) prints nothing and a no-agent dry run of each task's setup and acceptance on its `expected/` fixture passes. It has no label and no parent epic.

**Amendment**

Title and milestone are unchanged. Add the label `tests`. Add one paragraph after the opening paragraph, replace item 2 of `## Change`, append items 4 to 7 to it, add a section `## Scope and standing` between `## Change` and `## Done when`, replace the first done-when line, append four done-when lines, and replace the last line.

Add after the opening paragraph (the list of files there is incomplete):

```markdown
The 63 files are 23 `.py` (23 of the 27 `test-*.py` scripts at the top of `agent-tasks/`, which carry retired-syntax sample programs), 16 `.json` (task prompts), 13 `.md` (six fixture `CLAUDE.md` files, six `templates/path-2-gate/*/task.md`, `tests/E2E/README.md`) and 11 `.sh` (six `templates/path-2-gate/*/acceptance.sh`, `lib/helpers.sh`, `lib/verify-lib.sh`, `run-refactoring-benchmark.sh`, `tests/E2E/project-init/run-tests.sh`, `tests/E2E/scenarios/09_codegen_bugfixes/verify.sh`). No `.calr` file under `tests/E2E` contains a retired marker. Recorded results also live in `tests/E2E/agent-tasks/lib/benchmark-results/` (three comparison reports with retired markers); they are evidence and stay.
```

Replace item 2 of `## Change` with:

```markdown
2. **Counts come from the compiler, not from text.** `lib/helpers.sh` counts contracts with `grep -c '§Q'` and `'§S'` (`count_contracts`, `:967-979`), effects with `'§E{'` (`count_effects`, `:983-992`) and functions with `'§F{'` (`count_functions`, `:1211`; `get_refactoring_metrics`, `:1238-1259`). Do not replace these with greps for 0.30 forms. Any count of contracts, effects or functions that the suite keeps must be read from `calor` CLI or MCP JSON output for the file, and the README names the command. At bc80daeb no script outside `lib/helpers.sh` calls these functions (grep over `tests/E2E`, `scripts` and `.github`); delete the ones that stay unused. The same applies to `lib/verify-lib.sh` (`calor_body`, `require_in_body`), which matches retired declaration markers and has no caller.
```

Append to `## Change`, followed by the new section:

```markdown
4. **Verifiers check compilation and behaviour.** The 129 `tasks/*/*/verify.sh` already delegate to `lib/verify-logic.py`, which is compiler-backed. Bring the remaining checks to the same standard: the six `templates/path-2-gate/*/acceptance.sh` scripts either compile the result and exercise it, or are deleted. No check may pass or fail on the presence of a Calor form in source text.
5. **Arm A.** After this change HEAD holds no pre-0.30 end-to-end inputs. The end-to-end leg of #1605 therefore does one of two things, recorded in `tests/E2E/README.md`: arm A is run from the pinned pre-0.30 checkout with that checkout's own copy of the suite, and the report states which prompts and verifiers each arm used; or the leg runs after-only (0.30 and C#) and its report says so in its first line.
6. **Neutral report.** `run-refactoring-benchmark.sh` prints an "Advantage Ratio" (`:176`), a fixed "Key Differentiators" section that credits contracts, effects and in-source ids before any result exists (`:178-192`), and reads a Calor win as evidence for the language but a C# win as possibly "due to the specific tasks selected" (`:196-208`). Remove the ratio and the pre-written analysis; print both arms' pass counts and nothing interpretive.
7. **The verifier tests.** 23 of the `test-*.py` scripts at the top of `tests/E2E/agent-tasks/` embed retired-syntax sample programs (between 11 and 170 matching lines each; list them with `git grep -cE '§[A-Za-z/]' -- 'tests/E2E/agent-tasks/test-*.py'`). They are the no-agent controls for the task verifiers and the runner (the `verify.sh` entry points, `lib/verify-logic.py`, `lib/measured-run.py`) and are run by hand, as `tests/E2E/README.md` describes; no workflow runs them. Rewrite each embedded sample in 0.30 syntax and run the script against a built 0.30 compiler. One of them, `test-logic-old-release.py`, is a compatibility control that builds an archived v0.29 compiler from a pinned commit (`:16`, `:39-58`) and derives that release's syntax from the current samples; decide in the pull request whether it is retired, or kept as an old-release control with its retired-syntax strings, and in the second case list it under "Retained old-release controls" in `tests/E2E/README.md` with the reason.

## Scope and standing

- This issue blocks only the end-to-end leg of #1605. Stages 1 and 2 of #1605 do not wait for it, and it may slip to 0.32 without holding the 0.31 release.
- Until the suite has a neutral design (tasks authored from an arm-neutral specification, one verifier for both arms, an analysis registered before the run), its results are excluded from any advantage claim. Say so at the top of `tests/E2E/README.md` and in the generated report. The evidence ledger (#1774) records the exclusion.
- No paid run is part of this issue. The only CI entry point is the manual `agent_refactoring` input of `.github/workflows/benchmark.yml` (`:23`, default off). A paid run of this suite is not covered by the first signature of the evaluation registration (#1770). It needs its own later entry there, signed after this issue closes, that fixes the task subset, one pinned model, a spend ceiling, the abort triggers and a reading written in advance for each outcome. Its zero-cost dry pass is the no-agent dry run in this issue's done-when. Filing or merging this issue authorises no spend.
```

Replace the first line of `## Done when` (its exclusion misses the second recorded-results directory, so it cannot print nothing without editing evidence) with:

```markdown
- `git grep '§[A-Za-z/]' -- tests/E2E ':!tests/E2E/agent-tasks/benchmark-results' ':!tests/E2E/agent-tasks/lib/benchmark-results'` prints nothing, or prints only lines in files listed under "Retained old-release controls" in `tests/E2E/README.md`. At bc80daeb it lists 63 files and 1,799 matching lines.
```

Append to `## Done when`:

```markdown
- No script under `tests/E2E/agent-tasks` (excluding the two `benchmark-results/` directories) derives a count of contracts, effects or functions from a text match; each count that remains names the `calor` command whose JSON it reads.
- Each of the 23 `test-*.py` scripts named in item 7 exits 0 against a built 0.30 compiler, or is deleted, or is listed as a retained old-release control; the pull request gives the command and the result for each, because no workflow runs them.
- The text `generate_report` in `run-refactoring-benchmark.sh` writes contains neither "Advantage" nor "Key Differentiators"; a no-agent test calls it with fixed pass counts and asserts both.
- `tests/E2E/README.md` states the source of arm A (the pinned pre-0.30 checkout's own suite, or "after-only") and the exclusion from advantage claims.
```

Replace the last line ("Related: #1603, #1605.") with: `Part of epic #1761. Related: #1603, #1605.`

**Why**

As filed, a run would ask agents for a language the compiler rejects and would print a pre-written conclusion in favour of Calor (`run-refactoring-benchmark.sh:178-208`); counts taken from text patterns would break again at the 0.32 respelling; and the issue's own done-when removes the pre-0.30 inputs that arm A of #1605 needs. At bc80daeb the work is also sized differently from what the body says: all 129 per-task verifiers already delegate to the compiler-backed `lib/verify-logic.py` and the counting functions have no caller, while 23 verifier test scripts and a second recorded-results directory are missing from its lists.

issues.title: [0.31] Decision: register and authorise the 0.30 evaluation
issues.body:
## Change

Record, before any paid run, what the 0.30 agent evaluation (#1605) runs, the most it may cost, and how each possible result will be read. These are maintainer decisions. This issue lists the options, their cost and the plan's recommendation; it does not take them. Filing or merging anything under this issue authorises no spend until the spend record carries a dated authorisation.

Terms. A *pair* is one task with a specification, a hidden test suite and a starting fixture per language. An *arm* is one configuration under test. An *epoch* is one complete collection in which all arms run interleaved on one pinned model; numbers are compared only within an epoch (`docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md:12`). The *primer* is the syntax sheet served as `calor://primer`. A *null pass* runs the harness with `--null-agent`, which applies the reference solution in place of an agent and costs nothing. The *penalised pairs* are the two where Calor cost extra iterations in July.

**What is produced**

1. **The design entry**: a new entry in §A.3 of `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md` (the next free `A-1.N`; `A-1.13` if nothing has been added since), with the `Annex version` pointer at `:102` updated. It holds decision 1 and items 1 to 13 below. No row is added to the §A.2 table: these are planning rules, not proof-point gates, and the entry body is what the guard freezes. CI keeps existing entries byte-identical, so every later change is a new entry. The pull request must not touch `scripts/check-annex-freeze.py` or `.github/workflows/experiment-registry-tamper-check.yml`; the guard refuses a pull request that changes the annex together with either.
2. **The thresholds file**: a machine-readable copy of items 5 to 11, proposed at `bench/phase0-agent-native/registrations/eval-0.30.json` (the directory exists and holds the paused PP-W registrations, which this issue does not touch). The design entry cites its SHA-256, and the report script (#1760) reads it. The entry is the registration; where the file differs from it, the entry governs.
3. **The spend record**, proposed at `docs/plans/0.31-evaluation-spend-authorisation.md` and modelled on `docs/plans/pp-w5-spend-authorisation.md`: decision 2. #1605 appends realised spend to it.

Three values do not exist when the design is signed: the hash of the 0.30 commit, the agent client version and the SHA-256 of the primer files. #1605 records them, under the rule in item 4, in one sub-entry per stage (`A-1.N.1`, `A-1.N.2`; the guard allows a sub-version under an existing parent) before the first paid run of that stage.

**Order.** The design entry and the thresholds file are merged first, so that epic #1761 builds only what is registered: #1767 and the arm-A parts of #1766 and #1762 wait for them and for nothing else. The spend record may follow later and exists before any paid run. This issue closes when all three exist.

**Decision 1: the design**

Projected cost uses the July per-run means (pre-0.30 syntax, unpinned model; see Baseline). The low figure assumes the primer helps as it did in July; the high figure assumes it does not. Stage 2 has no cost precedent: its fixtures have no starter and four of its arms run in `calor init` workspaces, three of them with the always-on MCP surface, so its range is the least reliable figure here.

| Option | Runs | Projected | What is lost |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Stage 1 (arms A, B′, B and C# on five pairs) then stage 2 (four delivery arms and C# on two pairs), 10 runs per cell | 200 + 100 | $270 to $400, plus $150 to $325 | Nothing |
| B. Stage 1 only | 200 | $270 to $400 | The delivery rule and the MCP rule are never measured. #1767 is closed as not planned, #1823 records "not measured, default unchanged", #1824 is closed as not planned with this record linked |
| C. Reduced: arm B and C# on the five pairs | 100 | $105 to $150 | Also the before/after comparison: no arm A, no arm B′, and no regression against the old syntax can be filed. #1766 skips its arm-A part |
| D. No paid run | 0 | $0 | The first 0.31 exit criterion is met by its third branch: the spend record carries "Declined: no paid run authorised" and lists the rows that then read "not measured": #1645 steps 1, 4 and 5, #1790, #1788, the #1605 inputs of #1785 and #1800, #1823 and #1824 (their not-run branches), Part B of #1816, part 2 of #1802, and the cost recomputation in #1816 and #1832. The same list is entered in the plan of record (`docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md`) |

The plan recommends A at 10 runs per cell. Reasons: the before/after question is the one #1645 and the 0.32 breaking window are sized from, and stage 2 tests the only lever with a measured effect. Fifteen runs per cell in stage 1 would project to $400 to $600. Thirty runs per variant in stage 2, the July design, would project to $440 to $975; with stage 1 that is $710 to $1,375, which leaves no room under the $1,500 ceiling for an overrun, and this program has recorded two (2.8 times and about 4 times the estimate, see Baseline).

**Contents of the registration.** Each value below is the plan's recommendation; the maintainer confirms or replaces it before signing, and the entry states the final value. Items 6 to 11 are planning judgements with no measurement behind them and are to be labelled as such.

1. **Arms.** Stage 1: A is the pinned pre-0.30 compiler through `--arm-repo-root` and `--calor-dll` from the same checkout (the first does not bind the CLI the journal uses, see Baseline), with that release's primer through `--exemplar` and the original starters; B′ is the 0.30 compiler with that primer mechanically translated and the translated starters; B is the 0.30 compiler with the shipped primer and the same starters; C# has no primer. Stage 2, in `calor init` workspaces on the 0.30 compiler: pointer (as shipped), primer inlined in the agent file, inlined plus starter file, and CLI only (inlined, no MCP server); plus C#.
2. **Pairs.** Stage 1: `N1-003-csv-row` and `W3-003-kv-journal` (penalised), `W1-002-usage-billing`, `W2-003-window-stats` and `W2-004-interval-clip` (at parity in July). Stage 2: the starter-less versions of the two penalised pairs (#1767).
3. **n.** 10 valid runs per arm per pair in both stages. An invalid run is re-run at most twice per slot (`agent-native-gates.md:13`).
4. **Platform and pins.** The design entry names the operating system and the read sandbox the paid runs use, because #1762 builds for it. The plan recommends macOS with `sandbox-exec`, the only sandbox precedent in the tree; choosing Linux adds a mechanism to #1762. All arms of an epoch run on one machine. It names one full versioned model id, passed through `CLAUDE_MODEL` (never `default`), and the tag and commit of the last release before the rewrite, for arm A. It states the rule for the 0.30 commit: it contains #1766, #1762, #1764, #1772, #1745 and #1771, and for stage 2 also #1767 and #1773. Stage 1 arms load no template and no MCP server and read only the primer, so the maintainer may instead require #1771 and part 2 of #1745 only in the stage 2 commit; the entry says which. The commit hash, the client version and the SHA-256 of the three primer files go in the sub-entry #1605 writes.
5. **Measures.** Per pair and arm: mean iterations-to-green (never-green runs count 11, `agent-native-gates.md:39`), mean `total_cost_usd`, input tokens (uncached, cache-write, cache-read), output tokens, `num_turns`. Each as a ratio to the C# arm; pooled as the median of per-pair ratios (`:40`) over the two penalised pairs and over all five. Intervals: 90% percentile bootstrap over runs within pair and arm, 10,000 resamples, seed recorded. In stage 2 a `calor check` that follows an edit counts as an iteration, and so does a call of the MCP tool `calor_compile` that follows an edit, which is how the generated agent file tells the agent to compile; #1767 journals both. Without them the Calor arms would be understated against C# (see Baseline). If the maintainer decides that MCP compiles are not iterations, the entry says so and they are reported beside the count. These are planning rules, not gates under §6.1 of that document: its test is a cluster bootstrap over pairs (`:86`), which two penalised pairs cannot support.
6. **Close rule**, arm B against C#, pooled over the two penalised pairs, thresholds 1.3 on iterations-to-green and 1.5 on cost. *Closed*: both upper bounds are below their thresholds; #1645 opens no green-field follow-up. *Open*: either lower bound is above its threshold; #1645 ranks the cost drivers from the failure-class table and green-field work beyond #1734 may be funded. *Not resolved*: anything else; reported with intervals, nothing new is funded. The #1645 re-run reads the rule again only if both penalised pairs are in its pair set (#1816 Part B); otherwise the reading stays not resolved and no later run in this plan re-reads it.
7. **Before/after readings**, for B against A, B′ against A and B against B′, per pair and pooled, on iterations-to-green and on cost. *Regression*: the interval's lower bound is above 1.0; filed against #1645, attributed to the language change when it shows in B′ against A and to the rewritten primer when it shows in B against B′. *Improvement*: the upper bound is below 1.0. *No difference resolved*: otherwise. All three are published and none holds the release.
8. **Defect-class base rates** for null, missing case and resource leak, on the 0.30 Calor arm (arm B here), counting runs with at least one failed iteration or escaped defect of the class. *Not measurable*: fewer than 5 static opportunities for the class across the pair set, or fewer than 30 valid runs on pairs that have one. *Above threshold*: such events in at least 5 distinct runs and at least 10% of those runs. *Below threshold*: at least 30 runs and events in at most 1. *Held*: anything between. The same rule is applied unchanged to the Calor arm of each later registered run whose pairs have opportunities (the #1645 re-run under #1816 Part B; #1811), within one epoch and never pooled across epochs. Not measurable and held both keep the dependent item (#1800, and #1869, #1871 and #1870 in epic #1872) waiting for the next measurement; neither is a drop. The minimum of 5 opportunities per class is also the floor #1789 authors its pairs to. On the 0.31 pair set all three classes will read not measurable (see Baseline), and the entry says so in advance.
9. **C#-habit threshold**, the count #1785 calls the wrong-form error count. For a Calor form with a different C# spelling (`var`, a header `=>`, `set`, `type:name`, `each`), an event is a failed iteration in arm B whose edit wrote the C# spelling in place of the form. The rubric that maps spellings and diagnostic codes to forms is committed with the entry. A respelling toward C# becomes admissible under #1785 when events occur in at least 20% of the valid arm-B runs on pairs whose reference uses the form, in at least 5 runs, on at least two pairs. Fewer than 20 such runs reads not measurable. This is not the compiler's own wrong-form class (short or mis-cased visibility and modifier words, `CHANGELOG.md:52-55`), which #1790 handles.
10. **Delivery rule** (stage 2), pointer against inlined. #1823 makes the inlined primer the default if the primer is read before the first `.calr` edit in fewer than 90% of pointer-arm runs, or if the pointer arm's mean cost exceeds the inlined arm's by at least 10% and by at least two standard errors of the difference. At 10 runs per cell two standard errors is 9% to 13% of the mean if spread is as in July with the primer and 27% to 29% without, so the read rate is the primary trigger. Otherwise the reading is "pointer sufficient at this n", with the smallest resolvable difference stated. A starter file becomes default only if inlined-plus-starter costs at least 10% and two standard errors less than inlined. A client that cannot read MCP resources (#1820) gets the inlined primer regardless.
11. **MCP rule** (stage 2), inlined with the MCP server against CLI only, on cost per run, with input tokens and iterations-to-green reported beside it. *Does not earn its cost*: the MCP arm costs at least 10% and two standard errors more, with no lower iterations-to-green; #1824 merges or lazy-loads tools. *Earns it*: at least 10% and two standard errors less; #1824 records the present ratchet as the budget. *Not resolved*: otherwise; #1824 records the ratchet and changes no tool. No later run in this plan compares an MCP arm with a CLI-only arm; a second reading needs its own line under Part C of #1832.
12. **Deviations and limits**, stated in the entry: `calor init` arms run without the harness `.g.cs` write block that `agent-native-gates.md:26` requires; the CLI-only arm reads an agent file whose rules name MCP tools it does not have; stage 1 arms load no template and no MCP server; five fixture pairs, one agent, one model; the three parity pairs were at the C# floor in July; nothing is compared across epochs.
13. **End-to-end leg.** Not authorised by the first signature: this registration covers the paid leg of #1736 only through a later entry under it. If wanted, that entry is signed after #1736 closes, stating the task subset, the same model pin, a ceiling no larger than the unspent remainder of the ceilings below, #1736's no-agent dry run as its dry pass, and its reading: a before/after pass rate, excluded from any advantage claim.

**Decision 2: spend**

The maintainer authorises or declines, and sets the final figures; the values below are the plan's recommendation. The run uses the one model pinned in item 4, and the reading of every outcome is fixed by items 6 to 11 before the first run.

- *Ceilings.* Stage 1 $800; stage 2 $600; $1,400 in total, under the $1,500 epoch ceiling. Option C: $300. Costs are read from each run's `agent.json`, never priced by hand.
- *Abort triggers*. `run-epoch.sh` has no spend stop, so the operator sums `total_cost_usd` over the finished runs and evaluates the triggers after every interleaved round; the record says so. (a) After the first two valid runs of every cell, the cost extrapolated to the registered n exceeds the stage ceiling: stop; the maintainer records a smaller n for all cells before any outcome is tabulated, or closes the stage as not run. (b) Realised spend reaches 90% of the ceiling with cells incomplete: stop; no top-up without a new dated entry. (c) An arm canary or isolation canary fails, a cell has more than two invalid slots after re-attempts, or arm A's `compilerHash` equals arm B's: stop and repair; money spent counts against the ceiling. (d) One run costs more than $20, about five times the highest 30-run cell mean in July ($4.20): pause and inspect.
- *Dry pass.* A null pass for every registered arm and pair, with the same options and isolation mode, committed as `<epoch>-null` before the first paid run, every run with `taskSuccess: true`.
- *Not authorised by this record:* the #1645 re-run (#1816), the end-to-end leg unless added, any repeat of a voided epoch beyond the ceiling.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- #1605 says "Use the existing harnesses, with no registration or freeze process" and estimates "2 pairs × 3 arms × n=30 ≈ $300–550".
- The precedent record is `docs/plans/pp-w5-spend-authorisation.md`: authorised before the epoch (`:3-4`), shape and pins (`:8-16`), projection (`:18`), null pre-flight (`:75-79`). It projected about $33 and realised $92.83, 2.8 times, because the first attempt was void: both arms had been built by the same compiler (`:84-99`). `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/guarantees-probe-001/VERDICT.md:20-24` records $79.39 against an estimate under $20.
- `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md:81` sets an epoch API ceiling of $1,500. Annex A starts at `:100`; its newest entry is A-1.12 (`:349`). `scripts/check-annex-freeze.py` keeps every entry that starts `**A-1.` byte-identical to the base branch, requires a new entry for any change to the annex, and requires the version pointer to match; it runs as the `annex-freeze` job (`.github/workflows/experiment-registry-tamper-check.yml:98`) on every pull request to main.
- `epochs/e1a-attribution` (2026-07-16, 180 runs, `modelPin: "default"` in its `pins.json`) cost $370.52, summed from `total_cost_usd` in its 180 `agent.json` files. Mean cost per run: `N1-003-csv-row` Calor $3.65, Calor with exemplar $2.23, C# $0.60; `W3-003-kv-journal` $4.20, $1.17, $0.50. Standard deviation over mean of cost within a cell: 0.30 and 0.32 without the exemplar, 0.10 and 0.14 with it, 0.14 and 0.13 for C#.
- `epochs/hardness-check-001` (2026-07-13, three runs per cell, no exemplar, `modelPin: "default"`) is the only epoch that ran all three parity pairs and the only one with a C# arm on them: Calor $2.06, $1.24 and $1.37 per run; C# $0.54, $0.49 and $0.44 (means of `total_cost_usd`). Its `rollup.json` shows iterations-to-green of 2.67 for Calor on the two penalised pairs and 1.0 on the other three.
- The model pin is passed only when `CLAUDE_MODEL` is set and not `default` (`bench/phase0-agent-native/run-pair.sh:1321-1325`).
- The 50 translated pair files under `tests/TestData/ActiveSyntax/bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs` contain no `match`, `enum`, `using` or `null` (word grep, zero files).
- In `--initialized-workspace` mode the harness does not install its `.g.cs` write block (`run-pair.sh:899`), and the product hook allows `.g.cs` writes (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/HookCommand.cs:283-287`). In the same mode the `calor` wrapper on the agent's path execs the compiler directly (`run-pair.sh:982-985`), so a `calor` build or check is not journaled as an iteration, while `dotnet build` and `dotnet test` are. The generated agent file tells the agent to compile with the MCP tool `calor_compile` after each edit (`src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Templates/CLAUDE.md.template:13`); those calls are not journaled either.
- `--arm-repo-root` binds the arm template, `Calor.Tasks` and the canary build to another checkout (`run-pair.sh:267-281`). The CLI the journal uses is taken from the harness checkout unless `--calor-dll` names another (`run-pair.sh:434-455`), so arm A needs both options or its journal records come from the 0.30 CLI.
- The only read sandbox in the harness directory is macOS `sandbox-exec` (`bench/phase0-agent-native/ppw-gateway-client.py:239-240`, `:314`), part of the paused PP-W gateway.
- `bench/phase0-agent-native/run-epoch.sh` has no spend stop; its header only says to get authorisation before a live epoch (`:10-11`). `--max-budget-usd` is passed to the client only on the paused PP-W ticket path (`run-pair.sh:1368-1376`).
- No per-task cost is recorded for the end-to-end suite (grep for cost fields under `tests/E2E/agent-tasks/benchmark-results`, no match).

## Why

The 0.31 exit gate is a paid run that has grown from the three arms on two pairs #1605 priced to nine arms over two stages, in a program whose realised spend has twice exceeded its estimate (2.8 times and about 4 times), and #1605 as filed asks nobody to authorise it. Several later decisions read thresholds from this run that are written nowhere: the close rule for green-field work (#1645), the base rates that gate new guarantees (#1800, epic #1872), the respelling threshold (#1785), the delivery rule (#1823) and the MCP rule (#1824). Three of them fail if left to be written later: a 10% cost trigger cannot be resolved at ten runs with the spread measured in July, the MCP comparison has no margin, and a base rate reads zero on tasks that cannot exhibit the defect unless "not measurable" is a separate outcome. A threshold written after the report has been read is not a registration. This issue is a decision record and takes no engineering capacity.

## Done when

- The design entry is merged with the `annex-freeze` job green. It states the option chosen in decision 1 with its date, keeps the item numbers above (#1823 and #1824 cite the delivery rule as item 10 and the MCP rule as item 11), gives a value for each of items 1 to 13 marked "as recommended" or "changed to", and states that it was written before any paid run of the evaluation.
- The thresholds file exists at the path the design entry names, and its SHA-256 matches the one the entry cites.
- The spend record exists and carries either "Authorised: <date> by the maintainer" with a ceiling per stage and the abort triggers, or "Declined: <date>" with the option taken instead (for option D, "Declined: no paid run authorised"), and lists what it does not authorise.
- No live epoch of the evaluation exists whose `pins.json` has a `startedAt` earlier than the merge of the design entry or the date on the spend record.
- If option B, C or D was chosen: #1767 is closed as not planned with a link to the record; for C or D the arm-A part of #1766 is marked skipped; for D the spend record lists the rows that read "not measured", the plan of record carries the same list, and #1605 is closed on that record.

## Not in scope

- Running anything: #1605. Building the arms, the isolation or the delivery variants: epic #1761.
- The 0.32 and 0.33 registrations: #1816 and #1832, which append to the same annex.
- The token cap per respelling and the tokenizer set: #1785.

Part of epic #1775. Blocks #1767 and #1605.

issues.title: [0.31] Before/after agent evaluation of the simplified language
issues.body:
**Current**

The issue asks for a before/after agent evaluation of the 0.30 syntax with the pair harness: three Calor arms (A: old compiler and primer; B′: new compiler with the primer mechanically translated; B: new compiler with the new primer), an end-to-end leg, and one small arm inside a `calor init` workspace, "with no registration or freeze process". It is done when results are published, B is not worse than A, and any regressed form is revisited "before 0.30 ships". C# appears only as a report line, and the body ends "Part of #1606".

**Amendment**

Retitle to `[0.31] Before/after agent evaluation of the simplified language`. Replace label `p2` with `p1`. Keep arms A, B′ and B. Make the six replacements below; leave the rest of the body as it is.

1. In `## Goal`, replace the last sentence ("Use the existing harnesses, with no registration or freeze process.") with:

```markdown
Use the existing pair harness. Arms, pairs, n, the model and commit pins, the spend ceiling, the abort triggers and every threshold are fixed in the registration (#1770) before the first paid run. Filing this issue authorises no spend.
```

2. Under `## What the existing harnesses do and don't cover`, in the `run-pair.sh` bullet, replace the sentence "It doesn't load a CLAUDE.md, template or primer, so it doesn't exercise the `calor init` path users run." with:

```markdown
In its ordinary mode it loads no CLAUDE.md, template or primer. Its `--initialized-workspace` mode runs the real `calor init` and always registers the generated MCP server. The agent file `init` writes points at `calor://primer` and does not contain it; the other delivery variants of stage 2 need #1773 and #1767.
```

3. In the same section, replace the last two sentences of the `tests/E2E/agent-tasks` bullet ("Its `verify.sh` scripts grep for specific forms ... The runner also skips `calor init`.") with:

```markdown
At bc80daeb all 129 `tasks/*/*/verify.sh` scripts delegate to the compiler-backed `tests/E2E/agent-tasks/lib/verify-logic.py` and none matches a retired marker. What still names the retired syntax is 16 `task.json` prompts under `tasks/refactoring-benchmark`, six fixture `CLAUDE.md` files and the counting functions in `lib/helpers.sh`; #1736 migrates them. The runner skips `calor init` (`tests/E2E/agent-tasks/lib/helpers.sh:281`).
```

4. Replace the whole `## Design` section with:

```markdown
## Design

This issue runs what the registration (#1770, an entry in Annex A of `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md`) registers and nothing else. If that entry records the reduced design, read "arm B and the C# arm" for stage 1 and skip stage 2.

1. **One epoch per stage, one pinned model.** All arms of a stage run interleaved in one epoch on one machine, with the same model id (`CLAUDE_MODEL`, never `default`) and agent client version. Numbers are compared within an epoch only (`docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md:12`); nothing is compared with the July figures. Each stage is run through the arm list of `run-epoch.sh` (#1766).
2. **Stage 1, the before/after question.** Four arms on the five green-field pairs (`N1-003-csv-row`, `W3-003-kv-journal`, `W1-002-usage-billing`, `W2-003-window-stats`, `W2-004-interval-clip`):
   - **A:** the pinned pre-0.30 compiler through `--arm-repo-root` and `--calor-dll` from the same checkout, that release's primer through `--exemplar`, the original starters.
   - **B′:** the 0.30 compiler, the same primer mechanically translated to 0.30 syntax, starters translated one for one.
   - **B:** the 0.30 compiler, the shipped primer, the same translated starters.
   - **C#:** the C# starters, in the same epoch.

   A against B′ isolates the language change; B′ against B isolates the rewritten primer.
3. **Stage 2, how the primer reaches the agent.** In `calor init` workspaces (`--initialized-workspace`) on the starter-less versions of the two pairs that cost extra iterations in July: pointer (as shipped), primer inlined in the agent file, inlined plus a starter file, and CLI only (primer inlined, no MCP server), with a C# arm in the same epoch. In this stage a `calor check` after an edit counts as an iteration, and an MCP `calor_compile` call after an edit is counted as the registration states (#1767 journals both). The delivery rule and the MCP rule of the registration are applied to the result; #1823 and #1824 act on it.
4. **End-to-end leg.** `tests/E2E/agent-tasks`, after #1736, and only if the registration has a signed end-to-end part. Its results are excluded from any advantage claim.
5. **Dry pass first.** Before the first paid run of a stage, a `--null-agent` epoch (the reference solution applied in place of the agent, at no API cost) passes for every arm and pair of that stage under the same options and isolation mode, and is committed as `<epoch>-null`.
6. **Spend.** Collection stops at the ceiling and on the abort triggers written in the spend record of the registration. `run-epoch.sh` has no spend stop, so the operator sums `total_cost_usd` over the finished runs after every interleaved round and the spend record says so. Nothing is topped up without a new dated entry there.
7. **Report.** Per pair and arm: valid, invalid and censored runs; mean iterations and iterations-to-green; `total_cost_usd`; input tokens (uncached, cache-write and cache-read separately); output tokens; turns. Each also as a ratio to the C# arm of the same epoch. B against A, B′ against A and B against B′ with the registered intervals and readings, and the reading of the close rule. The columns of the report script (#1760), which include the class readings of registration item 8 and the C#-habit counts of item 9. If the script has not landed when stage 1 is published, the report says "pending #1760" for those columns and an addendum is committed beside it when the script lands; #1785 and #1800 read the addendum. A defect class the pair set cannot exhibit is reported "not measurable", never as zero. Teaching-token counts from `TokenBudgetTests`. Commit, model, client version, platform and command lines. Realised spend against the ceiling.
8. **Venue.** The report is committed with the epoch directory and summarised in the 0.31 release notes. Its row in the evidence ledger (#1774) is added at the 0.31 close-out under the checklist in the plan of record; stage 1 counts as published when the report and the release-notes section are merged. `docs/benchmarking/results.md` is generated from `website/public/data/benchmark-results.json` and is not edited. Epoch directories are committed under `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/`; arm A's archived `.calr` outputs are pre-0.30 syntax and go on the legacy-dialect allowlist (#1763) if that check has merged.

Not in this run: modify-a-converted-module tasks (authored in #1789 and measured in the #1645 re-run) and any Rust arm (#1831).
```

5. Replace the three bullets of `## Done when` with:

```markdown
- **Stage 1 is published** at the venue above with a C# arm run in the same epoch on the same pinned model, or the reduced design is published if the registration records it, or, if the spend record of #1770 carries "Declined: no paid run authorised", this issue records "not run" with a link to that record and closes. This is the 0.31 exit criterion; the bullets below do not hold the release.
- The B-versus-A and Calor-versus-C# results are reported with the readings registered in #1770, whatever they are. Every regression, as that entry defines one, is filed against #1645 with the pair, the arms compared, the numbers and the most frequent diagnostic codes in the failed iterations.
- **Stage 2 is published**, or this issue records "stage 2 not run" with a link to the #1770 record. One or the other happens before #1823 is decided.
- **The end-to-end leg is published**, or this issue records "end-to-end leg not run" with the reason.
- For every epoch: a sub-entry under the registration entry (`A-1.N.1` for stage 1, `A-1.N.2` for stage 2) records the 0.30 commit, the agent client version and the SHA-256 of the primer files, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor` shows that the commit contains the changes the registration requires; the sub-entry is merged before the earliest `startedAt`; the `-null` companion and the live epoch directory are committed with `pins.json`; realised spend is appended to the spend record.
- The issue closes when each of the three legs is published or recorded as not run (all three under a declined spend record). #1645, #1790, #1788, #1800, #1651 and #1832 wait only for the stage 1 report; #1823 and #1824 wait for the stage 2 report or its not-run record.
```

6. Replace the last line ("Part of #1606.") with:

```markdown
Part of epic #1775. Blocked by #1770 (the registration) and by #1766, #1762, #1764, #1772, #1745 and #1771, which must be in the pinned 0.30 commit as the registration's pin rule states. Stage 2 is also blocked by #1767 and #1773; the end-to-end leg by #1736.
```

**Why**

Every arm of the issue as filed is Calor, so it cannot say what the 0.30 language costs against C#, and the July cost figures describe a syntax that no longer exists. As the exit gate of 0.31 the body also contradicts itself: it disclaims registration although its thresholds must be fixed before the data, its done-when stays open on an unfavourable result, its deadline has passed, its parent epic is closed, and it names no blocker although the 0.30 arm, the arm isolation, the telemetry fields and the registration must exist before the first paid run. Two sentences about the harnesses are stale at bc80daeb: all 129 `verify.sh` scripts delegate to `lib/verify-logic.py` and none greps for a marker, and `run-pair.sh` has an `--initialized-workspace` mode (`bench/phase0-agent-native/run-pair.sh:223`).

issues.title: [0.31] calor init options for primer delivery (pointer or inline) and an optional starter file; default unchanged
issues.body:
## Change

Give `calor init` two options, so that stage 2 of the 0.30 evaluation (#1605) can compare how the syntax primer reaches the agent. The *primer* is the text served as the MCP resource `calor://primer`. With neither option, every file `calor init` writes is byte-identical to today.

Stage 2 is the first consumer. #1823 is the second: a client that cannot read MCP resources gets the inlined primer whatever stage 2 shows, so this issue is needed even if the registration (#1770) records no stage 2.

1. **Primer delivery.** An option with two values, proposed as `--primer pointer|inline` (the final spelling is set in this issue's pull request; #1767 uses what ships). `pointer` is the default and is today's output. With `inline`, the Calor section of the generated agent file contains the primer text verbatim, as `McpMessageHandler.GetPrimerContentPublic()` returns it, inside the existing `BEGIN CalorC SECTION` / `END CalorC SECTION` markers, and Rule 0 points at the inlined text instead of telling the agent to read `calor://primer`. Compose the text when `init` runs. Do not change the four embedded template files: they are generated, and `calor self-check docs` fails when one drifts from its source.
2. **Starter file.** An option, proposed as `--starter`, that writes one `.calr` file into the project `init` configures. Its content is one complete program from `programs[]` in the teaching source (`src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Teaching/reference.json`), so it is already compiled in CI; the pull request names the program id. It never overwrites an existing file without `--force`. In solution mode the pull request states which project receives the file, and a test pins that choice.
3. **All four agents.** `claude`, `codex`, `gemini` and `github` accept both options. Their templates are identical today and stay so.
4. **Switching back.** Running `init --force` with `pointer` on a workspace initialized with `inline` restores the pointer section byte for byte.
5. **Token statement.** The pull request states, for each combination, the size of the generated Calor section in o200k tokens (the `ProxyTokenizer` in `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/TokenBudgetTests.cs`), and what was added and removed against the pointer form. No budget constant in that file changes; changing the default or a budget is #1823.
6. **Docs.** The options table in `docs/cli/init.md:106-113` and `website/content/cli/init.mdx`.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- `calor init` has four options: `--ai`, `--project`, `--solution`, `--force` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/InitCommand.cs:16-41`). Supported agents are `claude`, `codex`, `gemini`, `github` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Init/AiInitializerFactory.cs:11`).
- The four templates under `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Templates/` (`CLAUDE.md.template`, `AGENTS.md.template`, `GEMINI.md.template`, `copilot-instructions.md.template`) are byte-identical (same MD5). Line 9 reads "Rule 0: Read `calor://primer` before writing Calor; use `calor_help` for other constructs."
- They are generated from the `agentInstructions` field of `reference.json` (`src/Calor.Compiler/SelfCheck/ExemplarCompileChecker.cs:158-162`), and `calor self-check docs` fails when a template drifts from it.
