```markdown
| MediatR | 17 of 32 | 10 of 32 | 5 of 32 |
| FluentValidation | 96 of 139 | 58 of 139 | 5 of 139 |
| Serilog | 54 of 112 | 36 of 112 | 10 of 112 |

- The lossy floors were lowered to the 0.30 measurement by a maintainer decision on 2026-11-18. The recorded cause: 0.30 keeps a file with `namespace X;` and its own `using` directives whole as C#, 14 of 32 MediatR files and 76 of 139 FluentValidation files (`tools/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness/ProjectConfigs.cs:134-137`, `:192-195`; `docs/plans/2026-11-16-milestone-0.30-ci-triage.md:363-367`). `ProjectConfigs.cs` was lowered from 0.40 and 0.48; Serilog's value there (0.25, `:173`) did not change.
- The default floors are the values CI enforces today. Whether they changed during 0.30 is not verified; the triage document records only the lossy floors as lowered.
- Why those files are preserved: the converter sends a namespace that declares its own `using` directives to whole-file preservation (`RequiresWholeFileNamespaceInterop`, `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/CSharpToCalorConverter.cs:2107`), on purpose, "rather than moving its imports or silently changing name lookup" (`docs/design/0.30-syntax-token-decision.md:104-106`). It keeps a native projection of those imports only when the generated C# compiles and declares the same types (`namespace-topology`, `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/FeatureSupport.cs:826-832`).
- Why the harness does not get that projection, by reading the code (not run). The harness converts one file at a time through `CSharpToCalorConverter.Convert` (`tools/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness/RoundTripPipeline.cs:634`, `:1590`). The projection compiles the original together with the sibling syntax trees and metadata references carried in the conversion options (`CSharpToCalorConverter.cs:410-417`), and the harness options set neither (`RoundTripPipeline.cs:1631-1647` for the default leg, `:1649-1690` for the lossy leg), although the harness already resolves each file's project references for its report (`:559`). On the lossy leg two more conditions fail: the lossless projection refuses a conversion that is not lossless with all preprocessor branches (`CSharpToCalorConverter.cs:395-397`), and the lossy one is taken only when `ValidateRoundTripCSharp` is true (`:1306-1312`), which the harness sets to false (`RoundTripPipeline.cs:1687`).
- CI enforces the floors in the two `roundtrip-verification` jobs with `python3 scripts/roundtrip_baselines.py check` (`.github/workflows/test.yml:1045-1048`).
- Not part of this issue: CS8669. In a project with nullable annotations and warnings as errors, a whole-file preserved original that uses `?` reports CS8669 and the files are marked unverified (`CHANGELOG.md:120-124`); #1746 measured MediatR and Serilog entirely whole-file preserved at an earlier compiler commit. #1782 fixes that in 0.31 and hands over what remains. The migrator checks converted Calor with effect enforcement off (`src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/Project/ProjectMigrator.cs:853-854`), so a project it reports as verified has not been built with enforcement on.
```

(3) Replace `## Done when` and the closing line with:

```markdown
## Done when

- On `roundtrip-verification (lossy)`, native files are at least 17 of 32 (MediatR), 96 of 139 (FluentValidation) and 54 of 112 (Serilog). The same pull request raises `blocking_floors.lossy` in `eng/roundtrip-baselines.json` to at least those counts, and `MinimumNativeFraction` in `tools/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness/ProjectConfigs.cs` to at least its pre-0.30 values (0.40 for MediatR, 0.48 for FluentValidation). For a project that cannot reach its mark, the lower floor is recorded as the first decision requires: the pull request lists each file still preserved with its reason, and the maintainer approves it.
- On `roundtrip-verification (default)`, native files stay at or above 5 of 32, 5 of 139 and 10 of 112.
- Default project-mode `calor migrate` writes at least as many native files per project as the first project-mode baseline that #1782 records in `bench/corpus/README.md`, read from the corpus report job (#1779) or, if that job has not landed, from the hand corpus check #1782 records.
- No corpus project fails to build or pass its tests after migration:
  - on both round-trip legs `round_trip_passed` stays at or above the committed values (MediatR 155 of 157, FluentValidation 865 of 866, Serilog 811 of 811), and the `member-oracle` jobs pass. These are the test evidence: the subjects' own suites are not run against the project-mode migrated libraries under this issue unless the maintainer adds that as a part;
  - the migrated MediatR, Serilog and FluentValidation libraries build with exit code 0 through `src/Calor.Sdk/Sdk/Sdk.targets` with `CalorEnforceEffects` left at its default, as shown by the build status in the corpus report job's three reports or, if that job has not landed, by the hand corpus check #1782 records. An error reported by effect enforcement (for example Calor0410) may remain only if the maintainer records it in this issue as an exception, by code and file, with the open epic #1808 issue that owns it; with no such record the criterion is exit code 0;
  - every diagnostic id and build error #1782 handed over is fixed, or listed in this issue with its file count and the reason it remains.
- The three decisions are recorded, each in a merged pull request linked from this issue.

Native coverage for constructs that were never supported belongs to 0.34, not here.

Part of #1649. Depends on #1782, #1779. Blocks #1844, #1848, #1854, #1859, #1866. Its closure is a 0.32 exit criterion and the 0.34 entry criterion.
```

**Why.** "Start-of-0.30 baseline" was undefined, and the one file that looks like its source holds the lowered floors, so the criterion was either already met or unreachable. The numbers and the recorded follow-up make it checkable, and the floor decision gives the issue a way to close when a file is preserved by design. CS8669 is named as out of scope because #1746 attributes it to this issue and it is a different defect with its own 0.31 fix; what that fix leaves over lands here, where the build is judged with effect enforcement on. The recorded exception for effect diagnostics exists because converted corpus code can fail on unknown or undeclared effects, which epic #1808 owns (#1731, #1802); without it the 0.32 exit would wait on that work whether or not the maintainer wants it to.

issues.title: [0.32] Fix coverage for agent-hit diagnostics
issues.displaces: none: new capacity justified in body
issues.body:
## Change

Give agents a fix patch where they actually hit errors. A *fix* is a `SuggestedFix` attached to a diagnostic (`src/Calor.Compiler/Diagnostics/Diagnostic.cs:1595-1621`); a *safe* fix has `isSafeToApply: true` and is the only kind applied without review.

1. **The three most frequent codes.** From the published #1605 report, take the three diagnostic codes the 0.30 Calor arms hit most often. If the report has no per-code counts, compute them from the archived loop telemetry (`journal.jsonl`, field `diagnostics[].code`) and commit the command. For each code, at the sites agents hit, add a fix or record why no deterministic fix exists. If #1605 recorded "no paid run authorised", record "no #1605 report" in `docs/cli/fix.md` and do steps 2 to 7.
2. **Every wrong-form error.** These are the 0.30 errors for a short or mis-cased visibility or modifier, which the release notes say suggest the C# word (`CHANGELOG.md:52-56`). First pin by test which error each such word produces in each header kind (class, member, module-level function), because the hint depends on where the word lands (see the baseline). The inventory is every error whose hint comes from `RemovedVisibilityReplacement` or `RetiredModifierReplacement`, or that suggests the lower-cased spelling of the word written, plus any site that test shows reporting such a word with no hint. Each gets a fix that replaces the word, or a recorded reason. At HEAD the hinting sites are three, in `src/Calor.Compiler/Parsing/Parser.cs`, all plain errors with no fix:
   - Calor0122, unknown visibility (`ParseVisibility`, `:5604-5618`; table at `:5622-5631`);
   - Calor0107, unknown class modifier (`:6481-6492`) and unknown member modifier (`:7091-7099`; table at `:7109-7121`).

   Classify the parameter-modifier case error (`:7048-7053`) as well.
3. **Mark a fix safe only where the rewrite is syntactic and has one reading**, such as `pub` to `public` on a class header, `Static` to `static`, `virt` to `virtual`. A replacement with a second plausible reading stays a suggestion: `int` in the visibility slot maps to `internal`, but a C# author may have meant a return type.
4. **Never mark safe a fix that touches an effect row or a contract.** #1801 pins this with a test; if it has merged, that test passes unchanged. If Calor0410 is among the three codes, it already has an unsafe fix (`src/Calor.Compiler/Effects/EffectEnforcementPass.cs:1068`, `:1084`) and nothing changes.
5. **Make the compound-visibility text agree with the parser.** The hints and the Calor0122 word list spell the two compound visibilities as in C#, `protected internal` and `private protected` (`Parser.cs:5576-5577`, `:5628-5629`), and a declaration header joins those two words (`:4231-4234`). The teaching source says "compound visibility uses protected-internal or private-protected" (`src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Teaching/reference.json:926-927`, generated into `docs/syntax-reference/current-language.md:802-804`) and has no compiled example of either. Add a test that every replacement a wrong-form hint names parses in the slot it is suggested for, and correct whichever text names a spelling the parser rejects (by reading, the reference entry). Regenerate with `calor self-check docs --fix`. This removes no accepted spelling.
6. **Decide the rule for old-form errors.** The 0.32 window (#1784) may turn some 0.30 spellings into errors at the cut-over (#1803). The batch rewriter (#1806) migrates files, but its rules are a separate class: they are never marked safe and are never applied by `calor fix --apply` or the MCP tools. Record in `docs/cli/fix.md` whether the error for such an old form carries its own fix, and when that fix may be safe. Recommended: the same test as step 3, and never for an edit to an effect row or a contract. The patches themselves are added with each cut-over error, not here.
7. **Record reasons** in `docs/cli/fix.md`, which already says why Calor1306 has no patch, and in `website/content/cli/fix.mdx`.

Merge before the commit that #1807 records for the 0.32 paid runs, so that the #1645 re-run measures it, and never between a commit pin and the end of that run's collection: this changes what a measured arm receives.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- 248 diagnostic codes (constants in `Diagnostic.cs`) and 21 fix construction sites (measured by `grep -rn "new SuggestedFix(" src --include=*.cs | grep -v Diagnostics/Diagnostic.cs`).
- Five sites pass `isSafeToApply`: tab indentation and indent width (Calor0008, Calor0009), each only when the file's indentation is unambiguous (`src/Calor.Compiler/Parsing/Lexer.cs:398`, `:407`); trailing whitespace and the conditional-return lint (Calor1300, Calor1305; `src/Calor.Compiler/Formatting/CalorFormatter.cs:441`, `:481`); and legacy closer removal, Calor0830 (`Parser.cs:621`).
- The Calor0830 fix cannot be produced from source text: the 0.30 lexer turns every `§/…` closer into a Calor0006 error token (`Lexer.cs:741-764`), and the test for the fix reaches it by reflection (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/AgentDiagnosticTests.cs:546-567`). Four safe sites are reachable, all whitespace or lint. Not verified by running.
- Only safe fixes are applied automatically: by `calor fix --apply`, by MCP `calor_check` when called with `apply: true`, and by MCP `calor_compile`, whose `autoFix` is on by default (`CHANGELOG.md:60`, `:88-91`; `src/Calor.Compiler/Mcp/Tools/CheckTool.cs:55-58`, `src/Calor.Compiler/Mcp/Tools/CompileTool.cs:189`). `DiagnosticFixes.Repair` refuses a patch that changes the generated C# of a file that compiled (`Diagnostic.cs:1701-1738`).
- Wrong-form errors are reported at the header's start token, not at the offending word (for example `Parser.cs:6474`, `:6491`), so a fix needs the word's own span.
- By reading, not run: a word written after a declaration name that is not a visibility is collected as a modifier (`Parser.cs:4235-4243`). A short visibility such as `pub` then reaches the class-modifier site, which consults the visibility table (`:6486-6487`), or the member-modifier site, which does not (`:7093-7097`), or the module-level function check, which gives no hint (`:1313-1318`). A test pins the class case for `pro` and `pri` (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/ParserTests.cs:45-50`).
- The two-word compound visibilities are pinned as accepted by tests (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/ParserTests.cs:27-40`, `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/NativeEffectHeaderTests.cs:193-194`). Whether a header accepts the hyphenated spelling the reference gives is not verified; the lexer scans `-` as an operator (`src/Calor.Compiler/Parsing/Lexer.cs:523`), and the hyphenated strings in `ParserTests.cs:20-21` are aliases inside a retired `§CL` marker, which that test expects to be rejected.
- `eng/test-manifest.json` pins the test count of each test project (`expectedTotal`), and `scripts/check_trx.py` fails CI on any difference (`.github/workflows/test.yml:603`).

## Why

A safe patch is applied inside the same tool call, so the agent spends no edit on it. Today that happens only for whitespace and one lint. 0.30's wrong-form errors already name the replacement, which is the class where a patch is sound. This work was step 2 of #1645 and is split out so that #1645 can close on regressions. It adds no error and changes no spelling, so it is outside the breaking window and the standing rule for new hard errors does not apply. No existing issue is displaced; the capacity is new, justified because these are the errors agents were measured hitting. Fix coverage is reported and never a target: it could be raised by marking effect-row edits safe, which would undo effect checking.

## Done when

- `docs/cli/fix.md` has a table of the three most frequent agent-hit codes from #1605 with their counts and, for each, the test that covers its new fix or the reason no fix exists; or it says "no #1605 report".
- Each site in the wrong-form inventory has a test in `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/AgentDiagnosticTests.cs` showing its fix, or a recorded reason in `docs/cli/fix.md`.
- For every fix marked safe here, a test applies it through `DiagnosticFixes.Repair` or MCP `calor_check` with `apply: true` and asserts that the result compiles and equals the hand-corrected source. For every other fix added here, a test asserts `IsSafeToApply` is false.
- A test asserts that each replacement named by a wrong-form hint parses in the slot it is suggested for, and `calor self-check docs` passes with the compound-visibility text in agreement.
- `docs/cli/fix.md` states the rule for old-form errors from step 6.
- `DiagnosticTokenBudgetTests` and `TokenBudgetTests` pass with no constant changed, and `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated for the tests added.
- The pull request reports, from the #1605 data where it exists, the share of agent-hit diagnostic occurrences whose code carries a fix and the share that is safe, before and after.

## Not in scope

- Calor0006 guidance for retired markers (#1788), respelling any form (#1784), the batch rewriter (#1806), and the never-safe pin itself (#1801).

Part of #1649. Depends on #1605.

issues.title: [0.32] Calor0006 names the replacement for every retired § marker
issues.displaces: none: new capacity justified in body
issues.body:
## Change

Calor0006 is the lexer error for a retired `§` section marker. Generate its guidance from one table that covers every retired marker, in place of the hand-written `switch` in `Lexer.ScanRetiredSectionMarker` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Parsing/Lexer.cs:741-764`).

1. **First, text only.** The 0.30.0 release note says every `§` marker is the error Calor0006, "which names the native form to use" (`CHANGELOG.md:31-32`, copied at `website/content/changelog.mdx:37-38`). That holds for 15 markers. Correct both copies to say what the error does today. This step changes nothing an agent arm reads and may merge before #1605 publishes.
2. **Inventory.** List every `§` marker a pre-0.30 compiler lexed. Source: the lexer at the pre-0.30 commit `d82f3ae95175ecd09581c6922701706be72b0ca9`, the baseline that `docs/cli/fix.md:52` and `docs/design/0.30-syntax-token-decision.md:7` already use, cross-checked against the markers that occur in `.calr` files in the tree.
3. **Table.** One entry per marker: the replacement in 0.30 words. Where a form has no replacement, the entry says so and says what to write instead: the Option and Result markers (`§SM`, `§NN`, `§OK`, `§ERR`) stay removed (#1617; use nullable types and exceptions), and source IDs are kept by tooling in `.calor/ids.json`.
4. **Message.** `Legacy section marker '<marker>' is removed. <entry>`, on one line. A marker outside the inventory keeps today's generic sentence.
5. **Longer help.** Add a Calor0006 entry to `DiagnosticText.Rules` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Diagnostics/DiagnosticFormatter.cs:47-73`) so that `calor_help` explains the code and the message can stay short.
6. **Order.** Write entries first for the markers #1605 reports agents writing, then by frequency in the tree.

No fix patch is added: retired syntax stays an error with zero edits applied, as two tests pin (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/AgentDiagnosticTests.cs:354`, `:385`). Whether a retired-to-current rewriter exists is decided in #1806.

Steps 2 to 6 change text a measured arm reads. Do not merge them between the commit pin and the end of collection of a registered paid run (#1605, or the runs under #1816).

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- The `switch` names a replacement for 15 markers (`§M`, `§F`, `§MT`, `§AF`, `§AMT`, `§B`, `§E`, `§Q`, `§S`, `§SN`, `§DP`, `§BR`, `§RAW`, `§CS`, `§CSHARP`), gives one sentence for every closer (`§/…`), and gives every other marker "Use canonical lowercase words and ordinary C# expression punctuation." (`Lexer.cs:751-760`).
- In the tree, 853 of 1,823 `.calr` files contain `§`, with 89 distinct marker spellings: 12 of the 15 named ones, 11 closers and 66 that get only the generic sentence. Those 66 are 20,643 of 39,222 occurrences (53%), led by `§R` 5,896, `§A` 4,825, `§C` 2,837, `§IF` 2,176, `§EL` 1,013 and `§ASSIGN` 875 (measured by `grep -rhoE "§/?[A-Za-z0-9_?^]*" --include=*.calr . | sort | uniq -c`). These are legacy files, not agent output.
- Calor0006 has no entry in `DiagnosticText.Rules` and none in `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/error-suggestions.json`. `calor_help` reads its explanation from `DiagnosticText.Explanation` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Mcp/Tools/HelpTool.cs:466`).
- Existing tests: `CanonicalCutover_RejectsEveryLegacyMarkerBoundary` checks the code for 16 markers (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/LexerTests.cs:236-261`), and one test pins the generic sentence for `§NEW` (`tests/Calor.LanguageServer.Tests/State/DocumentStateTests.cs:199`), so that expectation changes with this issue.
- Budget: the median rendered diagnostic must stay within 40 `o200k` tokens (measured 30 over 44 cases, three of them Calor0006), and every rendered diagnostic is one line (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/DiagnosticTokenBudgetTests.cs:25-32`, `:162-204`).
- Not verified: the pre-0.30 lexer's marker list. The checkout used to write this issue holds one commit.

## Why

Nearly half the `.calr` files in the tree (853 of 1,823) are still in the retired dialect, and no rewriter for it shipped with 0.30. An agent that writes a retired marker gets, for 66 of the 89 spellings in the tree, one generic sentence. A specific replacement in the error turns a guess into one edit. The size of the problem is the Calor0006 hits per run that #1605 reports. If it reports none for the 0.30 arms, or recorded "no paid run authorised", only step 1 is required in 0.32 and the rest moves to 0.33 with that count recorded. No existing issue is displaced: the change is one lexer function, one table and its tests. It adds no error and tightens none. It is off the 0.32 exit chain and may slip to 0.33 without holding the release.

## Done when

- `CHANGELOG.md` and `website/content/changelog.mdx` no longer say that Calor0006 names the native form for every marker.
- A test enumerates the inventory and asserts that each marker lexes to Calor0006 with guidance that is not the generic sentence. The 66 spellings measured above are in the inventory, or the pull request lists each one left out with the reason.
- A test asserts that the guidance for the Option and Result markers and for `§Q` does not suggest a removed form.
- `MedianDiagnostic_FitsBudget` and `EveryRenderedDiagnostic_IsOneLine` pass with no constant changed, and the pull request states the token count of the longest Calor0006 message.
- `calor_help` returns an explanation for `Calor0006`.
- The pinned `§NEW` message in `DocumentStateTests.cs` is updated, and `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated for the tests added (`scripts/check_trx.py` fails CI on a count that differs).
- The pull request lists the inventory with its source, and the markers #1605 reported agents writing.

## Not in scope

- A fix patch or rewriter for retired syntax (#1806); the legacy-dialect allowlist and self-check (#1763); the other removed-form errors (Calor0003, Calor0007), which already name their replacement.

Part of #1649. Depends on #1605.

issues.title: [0.32] Author two modify-a-converted-module pairs on one migrated corpus project
issues.displaces: none: new capacity justified in body
issues.body:
## Change

Author two benchmark pairs under `bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs/`, each a modification task on a slice of one corpus project as default migration leaves it. A *pair* is one task with a C# arm and a Calor arm that share a behavioural spec and one hidden test suite; `run-pair.sh` runs one arm of one pair.

1. **Project.** Choose one project under `bench/corpus/` (pins in `bench/corpus/README.md`) from the project-mode baseline table #1782 adds to that file: it must have native files. In the one measurement on record, FluentValidation was the only project with native files (#1746). If the chosen project's migrated slice does not build after #1782, the remaining build errors belong to #1647; add #1647 as a dependency of this issue and say so in a comment.
2. **Slice.** Choose source files that build on their own. The harness writes both arms' project files, with no package reference and no per-pair override (`run-pair.sh:729-778`), and the Calor arm builds with effect enforcement on (`templates/calor-arm/CalorArm.csproj.template`, `CalorEnforceEffects`), which the migrator's own check does not use.
3. **Starters from one commit.** `csharp/` is the slice's C# at the corpus pin. `calor/` is what default project-mode `calor migrate` writes for those files at one recorded compiler commit, unedited. The files the task changes must be native Calor in that output, not preserved C#. Record the project, the pin, the compiler commit and the command in `pair.json` under `parity.notes`, with any hand edit and its reason.
4. **Task.** `spec.md` states one arm-neutral change to existing behaviour and is written before the references. The starters fail the hidden suite; the references pass it.
5. **Hidden suite and shims.** One xUnit suite in `tests/`, bound through `tests/shims/TestShim.csharp.cs` and `tests/shims/TestShim.calor.cs`.
6. **References.** `reference/csharp/` and `reference/calor/`: the solved slice in each language.
7. **Manifest.** `pair.json` valid against `task-spec-schema.json`: category `N1` (neutral; the wedge categories require contracts that converted code does not carry), ids `N1-006-<slug>` and `N1-007-<slug>`, `iterationBudget` 10, and the `parity` counts, which must be within 30% across arms (`docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md:49`).
8. **Opportunities.** An *opportunity* is a place in the code the agent must read or change where a defect of a class can occur: a nullable-typed value (null), a match or switch over a non-`bool` type (missing case), an `IDisposable` local (resource). Across the two pairs each class reaches the minimum that #1770 registers in Annex A of `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md`; if the registration gives none, five. Count them on the references with the counter from #1760 if it has landed, otherwise by hand.
9. **Source location.** These pairs have no retired-syntax original, so their `.calr` files live in the pair directory and not in the `tests/TestData/ActiveSyntax` mirror, which admits only copies of registered originals. If the 0.30 source-selection option that #1766 adds reads Calor sources only from the mirror, extend it to read a pair that has no mirror entry from its own directory, with a harness test.

If this merges before the 0.32 rewrite (#1803), the rewrite migrates the two pairs and #1807 validates them again. If it merges after, author the Calor files in the post-rewrite syntax and run the validation below at the commit #1807 records or later.

This issue runs no paid agent. Validation is `--null-agent`, which applies the reference instead of calling an agent.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

Paths without a directory are under `bench/phase0-agent-native/`.

- The 50 `.calr` files of the 25 pairs translated to 0.30 syntax (`tests/TestData/ActiveSyntax/bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs`) contain no `match`, `switch`, `enum`, `using`, `null` or `?`-suffixed type (measured with `grep -rlE` for each). A count of null, missing-case or resource defects taken on them is zero by construction.
- The existing modification pairs are hand-written single-file fixtures: `pairs/W2-005-scheduler` is one file per arm, 12 functions in the starter and 13 in the reference.
- `run-pair.sh` copies the arm's fixture directory into the workspace (`:736`), writes the C# project inline (`:767-777`) or renders `templates/calor-arm/CalorArm.csproj.template`, which compiles `**/*.calr` with `CalorEnforceEffects` true, and copies `tests/*.cs` plus `tests/shims/TestShim.<arm>.cs` into the hidden project (`:781-782`). Both projects target `net10.0`.
- The migrator checks converted Calor with effect enforcement off (`src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/Project/ProjectMigrator.cs:853-854`), so migrate output that it reports as verified has not been built the way the Calor arm builds it.
- `--null-agent` builds the starter, copies `reference/<arm>` over it, builds again and runs the hidden suite with no API call (`:1270-1293`). `result.json` records `nullAgent`, `taskSuccess` and `escapedBugs` (`:1648-1666`), and every observed build appends a `journal.jsonl` record with `heldout_fail` (`:1167`).
- Two 0.31 results are prerequisites. The Calor arm cannot run 0.30 source today, because the arm canary is retired syntax (`run-pair.sh:553`, `:575`; fixed by #1766). In a project with nullable annotations and warnings as errors, a preserved original that uses `?` reports CS8669 and is written but marked unverified (`CHANGELOG.md:120-124`); #1746 measured MediatR and Serilog with no native file at an earlier compiler commit (re-measured and fixed by #1782).
- `BenchCorpusCompilesTests` compiles each `pairs/*/reference/calor/*.calr` file on its own (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/BenchCorpusCompilesTests.cs:38-72`), so a multi-file reference with cross-file types fails it as written. It is a theory with one case per file, and `eng/test-manifest.json` pins the test count of the project (`scripts/check_trx.py` fails CI on a difference).
- Hidden suites must be shown deterministic by five consecutive green reference runs, committed under `epochs/authoring-validation-*/` (`docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md:13`, `:52`; format in `epochs/authoring-validation-wave3/determinism-log.txt`).
- Not verified: which corpus slices build alone. The corpus submodules were not initialised in the checkout used to write this issue. Serilog is the only one of the three whose library targets `net10.0` at its pin (`bench/corpus/README.md:13-17`).

## Why

The strategy's adoption path is per-module migration, where the Calor already in a module is the agent's reference; the pre-0.30 measurements put modification of existing Calor at parity with C# (`docs/plans/agent-native-strategy.md:370-373`). No pair exercises that on converted code. The green-field pairs also cannot exhibit null, missing-case or resource defects, so a base-rate reading taken on them is "not measurable". These pairs run in the #1645 re-run, after the window cut-off, so their reading feeds the conditional 0.35 guarantees (#1869, #1871) and not the 0.32 window decision (#1800), which uses a static opportunity count. No existing issue is displaced: the capacity is new, justified because without these pairs the #1645 re-run and the base-rate reading have no task on which the three classes can occur.

## Done when

- Both pair directories exist with the layout in steps 3 to 7, and `./run-pair.sh --check-pair-config <pair>/pair.json calor` and `... csharp` exit 0.
- For each pair and arm, `./run-pair.sh --pair pairs/<id> --arm <arm> --null-agent --out epochs/authoring-validation-converted-null` writes a `result.json` with `"nullAgent": true`, `"taskSuccess": true` and `"escapedBugs": 0`, and the first record of the run's `journal.jsonl` (the unmodified starter) has `heldout_fail` above 0.
- Five consecutive such runs per pair and arm are committed as a determinism log beside those results.
- `BenchCorpusCompilesTests` passes with the new references present, and `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated for the added cases. If a reference file cannot compile alone, extend the test to compile that pair's reference as one project; do not exclude the pair.
- The pull request lists the opportunity counts per class with file and line, each class reaches the minimum, and for each pair it states how many files in `calor/` are native and how many are preserved.

## Not in scope

- Running an agent on the pairs (the #1645 re-run, under #1816).
- The opportunity counter (#1760), a third arm or analyzer packages in the C# project (#1815), and pairs on a second corpus project.

Part of #1649. Depends on #1782, #1766. Blocks #1645, #1816.

issues.title: [0.32] Code density: migrated Calor token ratio reported per project
issues.body:
**Current.** A follow-up from #1604 and #1606. It records one hand measurement of 2026-11-20 with the `o200k` proxy tokenizer on project-mode default `calor migrate`: overall 1.016 times the C# tokens, 0.859 on the native subset, with MediatR and Serilog entirely whole-file preserved because of CS8669, which it says is tracked in #1647. It is done when CI reports the ratio per corpus project on each run and the overall ratio is below 1.0 or the target is revised.

**Amendment.** New title: `[0.32] Code density: migrated Calor token ratio reported per project`. Milestone 0.32. Labels `ci`, `enhancement` (the issue has none). Three edits to the body.

(1) In the paragraph under the table, replace "because of CS8669 (tracked in #1647)" with:

```markdown
because of CS8669 (measured at compiler 606dae6f2; re-measured and fixed under #1782. #1647 covers a different regression, on the round-trip harness, and takes over whatever #1782 leaves)
```

(2) Replace the `Done when:` list with:

```markdown
Done when:
1. The corpus report job (#1779) writes, in each project's JSON report (added the way that job documents for later columns) and in its step summary, for MediatR, Serilog and FluentValidation:
   - the native file fraction, from the native and preserved classes the job already assigns from each file's `losses` list;
   - the token ratio overall: tokens of every written `.calr` file over tokens of the C# source file it replaces, summed per project;
   - the token ratio on native files and, separately, on preserved files, each with its file count;
   - a "with contracts" row: the ratio over native files in which the compiler reports at least one parameter refinement or postcondition, with the file count. It reads `n/a (0 files)` when there are none, so that the ratio of contract-free output is never presented as the density of code that carries contracts. The pull request names the compiler output used to detect them.
2. The per-run numbers are counted offline with `o200k_base`, and each column says "o200k proxy". The only o200k counter in the repository is `ProxyTokenizer` in the C# test project (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/TokenBudgetTests.cs:10-25`; packages pinned at `Directory.Packages.props:21-22`). Use the offline counter from #1799 if it has landed; otherwise add a small counter on the same pinned packages. A test asserts that the counter returns the same count as `ProxyTokenizer.Count` on a checked-in `.calr` file and a checked-in `.cs` file. There is no fallback to a word-count estimate (`scripts/token_delta_spot.py` has one and is not used).
3. The numbers come from the job's buildable, default-migrated copies, never from source-only copies. (The existing step at `.github/workflows/test.yml:1028-1034` runs `scripts/default_migrate_report.py` on source-only copies and records `build: not-run`.)
4. The Anthropic `count_tokens` figure is produced once per release, not on every run: one dispatch of `.github/workflows/syntax-token-count.yml`, which needs a protected environment, a maintainer-published payload commit, a digest and a typed confirmation. The notes of the release in which this issue closes carry that figure with its run link, or the line "count_tokens density figure not produced" with the reason. `scripts/count_tokens.py:264-267` accepts only its fixed 41-file population, so corpus files go in as `probes` or through the tool from #1799; this issue does not change that script. Counting all 283 corpus files (32 + 139 + 112) in both languages needs `max_requests` above the workflow's default of 400 (`:34-37`).

The below-1.0× target is no longer part of this issue. It is #1844 (0.34), which depends on this report, on #1647 and on #1742.

Off the 0.32 exit chain: this issue may slip to 0.33 without holding the release.
```

(3) Append after the `Done when:` list:

```markdown
Hand method, for issues that need a density figure before the columns land: run default project-mode `calor migrate` on each restored library project as #1782 records in `bench/corpus/README.md`; count `o200k_base` tokens of every written `.calr` file and of the C# source file it replaces; report the two sums and their ratio per project, with the compiler commit.
```

**Why.** The 0.859 figure comes from one project, because the other two had no native file. The converter writes no contracts (by reading, `RoslynSyntaxVisitor` passes empty precondition and postcondition lists, for example `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/RoslynSyntaxVisitor.cs:3970-3971`), so that figure is the density of contract-free code and the "with contracts" row will read `n/a (0 files)` until something produces them. The issue itself says the existing CI report shows zero native files by construction. An Anthropic count cannot run on every CI run: the only path is a maintainer-dispatched workflow for one model. The job that produces buildable migrated copies is #1779. The target moves behind its prerequisites to #1844. The hand method is written down because the window record (#1784) and the effect work in 0.32 fall back to it if these columns slip.

**Moved from** 0.31 because it reports on output that exists only after #1782 and #1779, it is on no 0.31 exit criterion, and 0.31 is kept to making the instruments run.

issues.title: [0.32] DivisionByZeroChecker double-reports divisions nested under bound wrapper nodes; Calor0926 suggests over-strong contracts for deferred divisions
issues.body:
**Current.** The issue reports two analyzer defects found in a review of #908. A division nested under a wrapper expression is reported once per traversal level, so the `??` probe gives two Calor0920 against one for the plain division. The Calor0926 suggester proposes a function-level condition for a division that only runs conditionally, such as the fallback of `??`, and should consult `BoundChildren.DeferredOf()` first. The body names `DivisionByZeroChecker.CheckExpression` and `ContainsDivision`, is written in retired syntax, and has no done-when.

**Amendment.** The two paragraphs "Double-reporting" and "Over-strong suggestion" are replaced with current-syntax text by the tracker re-baseline (#1759). After that edit, append the following. If step 3 applies, retitle to `[0.32] Calor0926 suggests an over-strong refinement for a conditionally executed division`.

````markdown
## Re-test on 0.30 first

1. Compile this probe with `calor --input Probe.calr --output Probe.g.cs --analyze --all-findings` (Calor0926 is suppressed without `--all-findings`) and count the Calor0920 and Calor0926 diagnostics. It is a candidate in 0.30 syntax; confirm it compiles.

   ```calor
   module Probe
     func Fallback (int?:x, int:y) → int
       !
       return x ?? 10 / y
   ```

2. Do the same with the body `return 10 / y`.
3. If both forms report Calor0920 the same number of times, the double report is gone: strike the "Double-reporting" paragraph, post the two counts as a comment, and narrow this issue to the Calor0926 suggestion.
4. If the `??` form reports more, fix it in `src/Calor.Compiler/Analysis/BugPatterns/TypedBugPatternAnalysis.cs`, which now holds the traversal.

## Done when

- A test in `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/Analysis/BugPatternTests.cs` compiles both forms and asserts the same number of Calor0920 for each.
- A test asserts that Calor0926 is not reported for a division that executes only conditionally (the right operand of `??`), and is still reported for the unconditional `10 / y`.
- `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated for the tests added.
````

**Why.** The double-report half names code that no longer exists: `src/Calor.Compiler/Analysis/BugPatterns/Patterns/DivisionByZeroChecker.cs` is a 23-line wrapper over `TypedBugPatternAnalysis.Check`, which drops a diagnostic it has already reported for the same span, code and message (`src/Calor.Compiler/Analysis/BugPatterns/TypedBugPatternAnalysis.cs:38`, `:2733`). The Calor0926 half is still live by reading: `PreconditionSuggester.CheckExpression` recurses into every child without consulting `BoundChildren.DeferredOf` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Analysis/BugPatterns/Patterns/PreconditionSuggester.cs:154-197`; `src/Calor.Compiler/Binding/BoundNodes.cs:1005`) and suggests the refinement `y | (# != 0)`. Neither was run. The issue stays in 0.32 as diagnostic-quality backlog; it is off the exit chain and may slip to 0.33, or be deferred with a reason, without holding the release.

issues.title: [0.32] Converter: lossy partial-class merge output reports Calor0410 for cross-file types
issues.body: Delivers a correct diagnosis after a lossy partial-class merge: compiling one converted file whose code uses a type declared in another file must not report Calor0410 (undeclared effect); the cross-file type is resolved, or the message says the effect is unknown because of a cross-file reference. It stays in 0.32 as converter loud-failure backlog under this epic, whose done-when allows it to be deferred with a reason; it is off the exit chain and may slip to 0.33 without holding the release. One fact to check first: 0.30 removed the `--lossy` command-line option (`CHANGELOG.md:82-83`), while the lossy fidelity still exists in the converter API (`ConversionFidelity`, `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/CSharpToCalorConverter.cs:58`) and in the round-trip harness's lossy leg. If the defect is reachable only through the removed option, close it as obsolete, as the epic allows.

issues.title: [0.32] Delete the configured-vs-defaulted trap in EffectEnforcementPass's caps (follow-up to #1141)
issues.body: Delivers the removal of a trap in the effect pass: assigning the fixpoint iteration cap at all, even to its default value, silently switches off the size floor, because a private flag records that the cap was set. The issue replaces the flag with a nullable cap so that "not set" means the default, records three constructs of the same shape, and asks for the tightness of the floor to be proved or loosened. The trap is still present at HEAD `bc80daeb` (`_sccCapInjected`, `src/Calor.Compiler/Effects/EffectEnforcementPass.cs:74-111`). It stays in 0.32 as internal hardening with no user-visible change, under this epic's done-when, which allows it to be deferred with a reason; it is off the exit chain and may slip to 0.33 without holding the release.

issues.title: [0.32] Breaking-window decision record
issues.body:
## Change

Create the decision record for the 0.32 breaking window at `docs/design/0.32-breaking-window.md` and keep it current until it is closed. This issue is a record. It changes no compiler code.

The breaking window is the 0.32 milestone: the last release in which an existing spelling may change. It ends when #1805 declares the edition, a written compatibility promise for the language as it then stands. "Breaking" is defined once, in the #1800 rows of this record: a removed or re-meant spelling, a change in what a compiling program does at run time, a newly reserved word, or a new default-on hard error.

The record has seven parts.

**1. The batch table.** One row per pending decision. Columns: item; owning issue; decision (land, keep as is, or defer to a future edition); date decided; changes `.calr` source (yes or no; yes means #1806 needs a rewriter rule); token cost per tokenizer (from part 4); forms used by the soundness packet (which templates of the registered proof-soundness packet contain the affected form, so that a respelling states how many hash-pinned cases must be re-frozen under #1807); landed in (pull request), or the reason for deferral.

Rows at filing:

| Row | Owner | Known at filing |
|---|---|---|
| Each 0.30 spelling whose ranking changes under the amended rule | #1646 | |
| Each respelling toward C# proposed from agent error counts (`var`, header `=>`, `set`, `type:name`, `each`), with its token cost | #1645 | |
| Brace-header forms | #1794 | |
| Union declaration spelling | #1797 | Additive. Changes `.calr` source: no, unless the chosen spelling reserves a word |
| Redundant `public` | #1796 | Enforced by lint only; neither form becomes an error |
| Edition-marker spelling | #1084 | |
| Any new effect spelling, and any program newly rejected, under sound effect contracts | #1731 | |
| Each rejecting guarantee: null remainder (one row per gap), enum-match exhaustiveness, making the bool exhaustiveness check effective, and whether obligation verification may become a default-build check | #1800 | |
| Inherited parameter refinements | #1735 | Changes `.calr` source: no. Changes emitted behaviour: yes |
| An `else` whose body is only an `if` | #1743 | The error shipped in 0.30. Changes `.calr` source: no |
| 0.30 residue removal | #1741 | Internal cleanup. Changes `.calr` source: no |

**2. The cut-off date.** A maintainer decision, recorded as one calendar date.

| Option | Cost |
|---|---|
| (a) A calendar date fixed when the record is created | A decision that is not ready is deferred for a whole edition. |
| (b) No date; the window closes when the last row is decided | The rewriter cannot be written against an open batch, so the marker, rewriter, rewrite, re-registration, both paid collections and the declaration all wait on the slowest decision. |

The plan recommends (a), set on the day the 0.32 milestone opens and set early, because every later step queues behind it. The date itself is the maintainer's. A row with no decision on that date is recorded as "deferred to a future edition": its 0.30 behaviour stays for the whole edition, and a deferred rejecting guarantee can later ship only in a form #1800 allows.

The record also carries a payload date, earlier than the cut-off: the manifest of part 4 is published and dispatched on that date. A spelling row whose payloads are not in that manifest is deferred to a future edition, unless the maintainer records a second dispatch with its own payload commit.

**3. The staging rule.** For every row marked "changes `.calr` source: yes", the old form stays accepted, with a warning at most, until #1803. That one pull request applies the rewrite and turns every old form of the batch into an error. No row makes an old form an error on its own, so the tree is migrated exactly once. A rejecting guarantee that #1800 decides to land follows the same rule: its check reports a warning at most until #1803. Compiler support for a decided form that has no owning implementation issue is carried by #1793. A row whose decision keeps the old form legal (#1796 is enforced by lint only) says so in its decision cell, and #1803 does not turn it into an error.

**4. One payload manifest, one dispatch per tokenizer.** A payload manifest is the JSON file `scripts/count_tokens.py` reads: it lists the text files to count and their variants. Every decision issue adds its candidate payload files to one manifest as `probes` (the validator still requires the fixed 41-file population; see baseline). On the payload date the maintainer publishes it as one payload commit and dispatches the count once per tokenizer in the #1785 set, using the #1799 tooling. The record links the payload commit, its `inputs_sha256` and each run.

**5. The standing acceptance rule, measured once for the batch.** One measurement before and one after, for the batch. If #1803 performs a rewrite, the two commits are its parent commit and its head, and the measurement is always taken, because the cut-over itself makes old forms errors. If #1803 records that no rewrite was needed, the two commits are the parent of the first merged pull request of a row that adds or tightens a hard error and the merge commit of the last such row. The measurement checks:

- the conversion scorecard's native count (the `conversion-scorecard` CI job, artifact `conversion-scorecard.json`) does not fall;
- the density ratio (migrated Calor tokens divided by original C# tokens, per corpus project) does not rise;
- the corpus files that newly fall to whole-file preservation (the converter keeping a C# file verbatim instead of writing native Calor) are counted and named.

The density ratio and the preserved-file list come from the corpus report job (#1779, with the token-ratio columns #1746 adds), dispatched on each of the two commits. If that job or its columns are not available, both values are measured by the hand method #1746 records (project-mode default `calor migrate` on MediatR, Serilog and FluentValidation, counted with the o200k proxy tokenizer), and the record says which method was used.

**6. The order.** The #1084 design record merges before the cut-off (#1800 reads it and the marker spelling is a row). Decisions complete at the cut-off; then the #1084 implementation and #1793 (compiler support for the decided forms, old forms still accepted); #1806 (rewriter); #1803 (the rewrite lands once and performs the cut-over); #1807 (instruments re-registered); then #1816, #1810 and the #1645 re-run pin the post-rewrite commit; then #1805 declares the edition.

**7. Two states.** The record's first line carries its status.

- *Decided*: the cut-off date has passed and every row has a recorded outcome. #1806 and #1793 depend on this state, not on closure.
- *Closed*: #1803 has landed, or its inventory records that no rewrite was needed because no decision changed source.

The record also states that the guard-derived precondition decision (#1847) is not in the batch, because none of its options changes an existing spelling.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- No window record exists. The only spelling record is `docs/design/0.30-syntax-token-decision.md`.
- The pending decisions sit in separate issues: #1646 ("Flip any choice whose ranking changes"), #1645 ("If the form itself is the problem, revisit it"), #1743, #1741, #1735, and the brace-header forms (`docs/plans/2026-11-16-milestone-0.30-ci-triage.md:542-544`).
- A token count is a maintainer action: `.github/workflows/syntax-token-count.yml` runs only on `workflow_dispatch` (`:21-22`), takes a `payload_commit` and an `inputs_sha256` (`:24-33`), needs a typed confirmation (`:70`) and the pre-existing environment `anthropic-count-tokens` (`:121`), and counts for one fixed model (`TARGET_MODEL: "Claude Opus 5.5"`, `:50`). Payloads "are not stored on main" (`:10`).
- `scripts/count_tokens.py` rejects a manifest whose population is not one primer, 20 converted files and 20 agent files (`:264-267`); additional payloads are optional `probes` (`:269`), reported separately.
- The soundness packet at HEAD is in the retired syntax and frozen: 136 templates in `tests/TestData/SoundnessSweep/templates.json`, `"status": "FROZEN-AT-MERGE"` (`tests/TestData/SoundnessSweep/registration.json:9`), "Do not edit the fixture to make the job green" (`bench/Calor.Soundness.Sweep/README.md:69`). The packet column is therefore filled from the 0.30-syntax successor packet that #1778 registers.
- The conversion scorecard is the `conversion-scorecard` job (`.github/workflows/test.yml:672`). Its test pins `BASELINE_FULLY_CONVERTED = 100` (`tests/Calor.Evaluation/Scorecard/ConversionScorecardTests.cs:31`); `CHANGELOG.md:166-168` reports 101 of 106 scorecard inputs native. The two figures are not reconciled here: the "before" value is whatever the job reports on the pre-rewrite commit.
- The density ratio was 1.016 overall on 2026-11-20, measured by hand with the o200k proxy tokenizer on 0.30 syntax (#1746). No CI job reports it per project yet; #1779 and #1746 add that.

## Why

The first 0.32 exit criterion is that this record is closed. Without it the pending decisions land separately, each with its own repository rewrite, its own token dispatch and its own re-freeze of the soundness packet, and the edition would be declared over spellings that were still moving. With it the rewriter has a fixed input, each respelling states what it costs in tokens and in re-frozen cases before it is chosen, and a decision that is not ready by the date is deferred in writing.

## Done when

- `docs/design/0.32-breaking-window.md` exists with the seven parts; the cut-off and the payload date are calendar dates, and the payload date is the earlier.
- **Decided state.** In a commit made on or after the cut-off date the record's status line reads "decided", and every row has a decision and a date, or reads "deferred to a future edition" with a one-line reason.
- The record links one payload commit, one `inputs_sha256` and one run per tokenizer, and every token cost in the table cites those runs. If the maintainer recorded a second dispatch, the record links its payload commit, digest and runs as well, names the rows it served, and gives the reason.
- Every row marked "changes `.calr` source: yes" names its rewriter rule in #1806 and the pull request that added compiler support for the new form (its owning issue, or #1793). The #1743 and #1741 rows read "no". Neither changes what the compiler accepts, so those two rows may link their open issue in place of a pull request and do not hold the record open if the work slips.
- **Closed state.** The status line reads "closed" and all of the following hold:
  - #1803 has merged, or its inventory records that no rewrite was needed.
  - Every other row marked "land" links the pull request it landed in.
  - The record holds the before and after measurement of part 5 with both commit hashes and the method used. The native count is not lower and the density ratio is not higher, or the row responsible has been reverted or deferred. The list of newly preserved files is present, even if empty. Only if no rewrite was performed and no row added or tightened a hard error does the record say so in place of the measurement.

## Not in scope

Implementing any row, the rewriter, the rewrite, the re-registration and the edition declaration. Each has its own issue.

Part of epic #1787. Depends on #1779 (the corpus report job the acceptance measurement reads; the hand method in part 5 is the fallback if it slips), #1785 (the rule every spelling row cites) and #1799 (the counters the dispatch uses). Blocks #1806 and #1793, both from the decided state, not from closure.

issues.title: [0.32] Amend the fewest-tokens rule: a minimum win and a named tokenizer set
issues.body:
## Change

Record an amended spelling rule as the first section of `docs/design/0.32-breaking-window.md` (create the file with only this section if #1784 has not created it yet), and add a one-line pointer to it at the top of `docs/design/0.30-syntax-token-decision.md`. This is a maintainer decision in three parts. Each part lists its options; the maintainer picks one and the record states the choice.

**A. Minimum win.**

| Option | Effect | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| A1. No minimum (today) | Any strict win decides. | One-token wins in one context keep deciding spellings. |
| A2. An absolute minimum of M tokens per probe; a smaller difference is a tie, resolved by the existing tie order (C# spelling, then probe baseline, then fewest UTF-8 bytes) | With M = 2 the one-token wins the 0.30 record calls weak become ties. | #1646 must re-rank every row; some C#-vs-non-C# rows flip to C#. |
| A3. A relative minimum (percent of the probe) | The bar scales with probe size. | The 0.30 record uses absolute deltas because fixed API framing dilutes percentages on small probes (`:7`). |

The plan recommends A2 with M = 2, plus one clause: where neither spelling is the C# spelling, the shipped 0.30 spelling stays unless the challenger wins by at least M. Without that clause `→` (22) against `->` (23, row 8) would become a tie, the rest of the tie order (probe baseline, then fewest UTF-8 bytes) could hand it to `->`, and every function header would be rewritten for no familiarity gain. For scale, at M = 2 the recorded counts make `yield v` against C# `yield return v` a tie (68 against 69, row 33), which the C# spelling would win. Listing every affected row is #1646's work.

**B. Named tokenizer set.** #1651 (0.33) extends the agent evaluation harness to Codex, Gemini and Copilot in addition to Claude Code.

| Option | Cost |
|---|---|
| B1. Anthropic `count_tokens` for one Claude model (today) | Spellings are tuned to one vendor. |
| B2. Three members: Anthropic `count_tokens` for the pinned Claude model (primary); OpenAI `o200k_base`, offline; Google's token counter for a Gemini model named in this record on the decision date. Copilot is counted with the tokenizer of a Copilot model named in this record on the decision date | Two more counters to build (#1799) and one more key-holding environment. |
| B3. Every model each agent can select | Unbounded. |

The plan recommends B2 with this combination rule: a candidate wins only if it clears M on the primary tokenizer and is not worse on any other member. Which encoding the Codex and Gemini models actually use is not verified in the repository; #1799 records it per tool. If #1832 (the 0.33 per-agent registration) later pins a different model, no window decision is reopened; the difference is a finding for #1846.

**C. Agent error counts as a ground for respelling toward C#.**

| Option | Cost |
|---|---|
| C1. Not allowed (today: #1645 confines a revisit to "the one-way and fewest-tokens rules") | A form agents keep writing the C# way cannot be respelled unless it also wins on tokens. |
| C2. Allowed when a stated threshold is met: the form's wrong-form error count in the #1605 report, with its denominator, and a maximum token cost per occurrence. The cap is a number of tokens per occurrence on the primary tokenizer, and the cost on every other member is recorded beside it | The language may get longer by a stated amount. |

If #1605 recorded "no paid run authorised", or its reading for a form is "not measurable", C2 cannot admit that form in this window and its row is "keep" or "deferred". The combination rule in B cannot admit a respelling toward C#, which costs tokens by design; the plan recommends that the record state that a C2 respelling is bounded by the cap in place of that rule.

The plan recommends C2. The threshold on #1605 wrong-form error counts is the one that #1770 (the 0.31 evaluation registration) registers in Annex A of `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md` before the #1605 data exists. This record copies those numbers and cites the annex entry. If #1770 registered no such threshold, this record sets one and states in words that it was set after the #1605 stage 1 report was read.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- The rule: "every 0.30 spelling choice goes to the variant with the fewest tokens, not the most readable one" (`docs/design/0.30-syntax-token-decision.md:3`); ties go to the C# spelling, then the probe baseline, then fewest UTF-8 bytes (`:5`).
- One tokenizer: Claude Opus 5.5 through `count_tokens` (`:7`).
- The sample was "a hand-picked declaration-heavy convenience sample" and non-baseline payloads were "speculative hand-written text, not compiler-accepted syntax" (`:15`).
- Weak decisions by the record's own account: "`→` and `func` win by 1 token each, in one context only" (`:570`); the pattern spellings are "a provisional inventory gate, not a count result or human selection" (`:572`).
- Two 0.30 forms look like C# and mean something else: `var` is "mutability, not a type-inference keyword" (`docs/syntax-reference/current-language.md:59`), and a header `=>` is a postcondition (`:403`).
- The offline tokenizer CI uses is o200k_base, described in the code as a proxy: "o200k counts are not Claude counts" (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/TokenBudgetTests.cs:11-17`).
- The 0.30.0 release "publishes no new benchmark results" (`CHANGELOG.md:15`); #1605 is the first agent measurement on the 0.30 spellings.
- Annex A of `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md` (`:100`) is held append-only in CI by `scripts/check-annex-freeze.py`, run by the `annex-freeze` job (`.github/workflows/experiment-registry-tamper-check.yml:98`).

## Why

Every spelling decision in the window cites this rule, so it has to exist before they are taken. As written, the 0.30 rule lets a one-token difference on one vendor's tokenizer override the spelling C# programmers and models already know, and it gives familiarity no way to win a revisit. Agent reach in 0.33 targets three other agents (Codex, Gemini and Copilot) whose tokenizers the rule never consulted.

## Done when

- The record states, for each of A, B and C: the option chosen, the date, and "maintainer" as the decider, in the style of the 0.30 rule line.
- A: the minimum is a number with its unit, the tie order is stated, and the both-non-C# clause is adopted or declined in words.
- B: each member is named with its model or encoding and whether it is offline; the combination rule is stated.
- C: the threshold numbers and the token cap with the tokenizer it is counted on are present, with the Annex A entry the threshold was copied from or with the sentence that it was set after the #1605 stage 1 report was read; or C1 is recorded.
- `docs/design/0.30-syntax-token-decision.md` points to the amendment in its first ten lines.
- The pull request that closes this issue changes only those two documents. No spelling is decided in it.

## Not in scope

Re-ranking the 0.30 spellings (#1646); building counters (#1799); any individual respelling (#1645).

Part of epic #1787. Depends on #1770 (the registration that holds the part C threshold). Blocks #1799, #1794, #1797, #1646.

issues.title: [0.32] Tokenizer-set tooling: count the same payloads with each tokenizer named by the rule
issues.displaces: none: new capacity justified in body
issues.body:
## Change

Deliver tooling that counts one payload manifest with each tokenizer in the set #1785 names, and says for each whether it runs offline or needs a key.

1. **One manifest for all.** Keep the manifest format `scripts/count_tokens.py` reads (schema version 1: samples, variants, optional probes) and its `inputs_sha256` digest unchanged, so the same reviewed bytes are counted by every tokenizer. The manifest's `target_model` field names the Anthropic model; each sibling counter takes its own model or encoding as an argument and writes it into its results.
2. **One counter per additional tokenizer.** Do not add other providers to `scripts/count_tokens.py`: its header states that only `api.anthropic.com` is used, and `scripts/test_count_tokens.py:44` pins the request URL. Add sibling counters that reuse its manifest validation.
   - o200k_base, offline: use the pinned `Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers` packages so no dependency is added. Where it lives (a small `tools/` console project or a mode of an existing tool) is the implementer's choice.
   - Each key-requiring member (expected: the Gemini model): a script plus a manual workflow modelled on `.github/workflows/syntax-token-count.yml`, with the same guards.
3. **Same output shape.** Each counter writes a results file in the shape `count_tokens.py --output` writes, and one command merges them into a table of payload by tokenizer.
4. **A tokenizer table**, in the tooling's documentation and copied into the window record (#1784): name, model or encoding, offline or key-required, the command or workflow that runs it, and the tool commit.

Counting is not a paid agent run: no completion or generation request is made. The 0.30 record states that Anthropic token counting is free of token charges (`docs/design/0.30-syntax-token-decision.md:13`); charges for other providers' counting endpoints are not verified and are stated in the tokenizer table.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- `scripts/count_tokens.py`: "Only api.anthropic.com is used" (`:5`); "No offline counts exist" (`:24`). It requires a population of one primer, 20 converted files and 20 agent files (`:264-267`) and accepts further payloads as optional `probes` (`:269`).
- `.github/workflows/syntax-token-count.yml`: manual dispatch only (`:21-22`), dispatch from main with the typed confirmation `count-tokens-only` (`:69-70`), pre-existing environment `anthropic-count-tokens` (`:121`), one fixed model (`:50`), "there are no offline or proxy counts" (`:8`).
- `scripts/test_count_tokens.py` holds the offline controls for that script and workflow and runs in CI (`.github/workflows/test.yml:109`).
- The only offline tokenizer is a test helper: `internal static class ProxyTokenizer` wraps `TiktokenTokenizer.CreateForModel("gpt-4o")` (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/TokenBudgetTests.cs:19-25`). It cannot be run on a manifest. The packages are pinned at `Directory.Packages.props:21-22` (version 2.0.1).
- Nothing under `scripts/`, `.github/`, `tools/` or `bench/` calls an OpenAI or Google token counter (grep for `api.openai.com`, `generativelanguage`, `countTokens`). `scripts/token_delta_spot.py` uses `tiktoken` with `cl100k_base` when installed, for a retired-syntax estimate; it does not read manifests.

## Why

#1785 names a tokenizer set covering the agents #1651 adds to the evaluation harness, and nothing in the repository can count with any member except one Claude model. Without this tool #1646 and #1797 cannot apply the amended rule, and the per-agent token counts #1650 needs in 0.33 have no counter. The capacity is new, and it is the measurement half of #1646 moved here so that #1646 becomes application only: the additional work is the non-Anthropic counters and their dispatch workflows. Sharing one manifest also means the whole window needs one maintainer dispatch per tokenizer, where separate issues would each need their own.

## Done when

- For every tokenizer in the #1785 set, one documented command takes a manifest and writes a results file; the merged table is produced by one further command.
- The offline counter, run twice on the same manifest, writes identical output and opens no network connection (test).
- Each key-requiring counter runs only from a manual workflow that requires a payload commit, the inputs digest, a typed confirmation and a pre-existing protected environment; an offline control test in the style of `scripts/test_count_tokens.py` checks those invariants and runs in the same CI step (`.github/workflows/test.yml:109`).
- A missing key, a failed request or a digest mismatch writes no results file (test per counter).
- `python3 scripts/test_count_tokens.py` exits 0 with its existing assertions unedited, so `scripts/count_tokens.py` still sends requests only to `api.anthropic.com`.
- If tests are added to a .NET test project, its `expectedTotal` in `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated.
- The tokenizer table exists with one row per member.
- If a member cannot be counted (no counter exists for the pinned model), the table says so and #1785's set is amended in the record; the member is not silently skipped.

## Not in scope

Preparing the window's payloads or dispatching the count (#1784); deciding any spelling.

Part of epic #1787. Depends on #1785. Blocks #1797, #1646, #1650.

issues.title: [0.32] Decide the brace-header forms accepted "pending a separate decision"
issues.body:
## Change

Decide, and record as a row of the window record (#1784, `docs/design/0.32-breaking-window.md`), what happens to each brace-header form the 0.30 parser still accepts. A brace header is a `{...}` group written directly after a keyword, the way the retired syntax wrote `§F{id:Name:pub}`. This issue decides; it changes no parser code.

First complete the inventory in the baseline by compiling one probe per form (`calor --input probe.calr --output probe.g.cs`) and recording accepted or rejected. The starting list is the 31 call sites of `ParseAttributes` in `src/Calor.Compiler/Parsing/Parser.cs`. The baseline below comes from reading the parser; nothing was run.

The forms fall into three classes:

| Class | Forms | Used today |
|---|---|---|
| A. Undocumented sections | `in{type:name}` and `out{type}` lines after a function, method, constructor or operator header; `where{T:constraint}`; a group after `invariant` | By nothing in the repository |
| B. Emitted by the converter | `proof{"description"} condition`; `assume{category} "text"` | Emitter and tests; `proof` is also documented |
| C. Inert groups | An empty group after `if` or `match`; a group after a block end | By nothing |

Options:

| Option | Cost |
|---|---|
| 1. Keep everything | Class A stays as a second way to declare parameters and a return type, against "one way to write each thing" (`CHANGELOG.md:9`). No rewrite. |
| 2. Reject classes A and C with an error that names the replacement; keep class B as the canonical spelling | Parser deletion and tests. No rewriter rule, because no file uses A or C. |
| 3. Reject every brace header and respell class B | Two documented forms change: a spelling chosen under #1785 with counts from #1799, a rewriter rule in #1806, changes to the emitter, `docs/syntax-reference/contracts.md` and 14 test files. |

The plan recommends option 2. Class A has no user, so rejecting it costs no rewrite and removes the duplicate declaration path. Class B is documented and emitted, and no measurement shows agents failing on it; respell it only if the #1605 report does.

If the decision rejects or respells any form, the parser change is implemented under #1793, the conditional issue that carries compiler changes for decided rows of the window record. Under the window's staging rule the old form produces at most a warning there, and becomes an error only in #1803. The standing acceptance rule applies to that change: the conversion scorecard's native count and the density ratio (migrated Calor tokens over original C# tokens) do not regress, and the number of files that newly fall to whole-file preservation (kept verbatim as C#) is reported.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- The deferral is recorded in `docs/plans/2026-11-16-milestone-0.30-ci-triage.md:542-544`: "Not removed, because input still reaches it: the brace-header forms behind live keywords (`in{...}`, `out{...}` declaration sections and `ParseValue`). Rejecting them changes what the language accepts (#1600 territory), so that is a separate decision." Neither the `CHANGELOG.md` 0.30.0 section nor `docs/syntax-reference/` mentions it.
- The brace reader `ParseAttributes` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Parsing/Parser.cs:4315-4341`) has 31 call sites (grep for `ParseAttributes(`, less the definition); its value reader is `ParseValue` (`:4472`).
- Class A: the function section loop accepts `in` and `out` lines (`Parser.cs:1355-1362`), read by `ParseParameter` (`:1413-1416`) and `ParseOutput` (`:1492-1495`) with no diagnostic for the form itself; the same loop exists for method signatures (`:6363`), method definitions (`:6975`), constructors (`:7933`) and operators (`:8020`). Braced `where` is at `:5837-5840`; `invariant` consumes a group at `:1039-1047`.
- Class B: `proof{"description"} condition` is documented (`docs/syntax-reference/contracts.md:262-264`), parsed at `Parser.cs:1831-1835` and emitted at `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/CalorEmitter.cs:4045-4053`. `assume{category} "text"` is parsed at `Parser.cs:9126-9129`, emitted at `CalorEmitter.cs:3159-3164`, and used in `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/ExtendedFeaturesTests.cs:57` and `tests/TestData/QueryCorpus/project/contracts.calr:2`. It is not in `docs/syntax-reference/`.
- Class C: `if` and `match` read a group and report an error only when it has content (`Parser.cs:3989-3990`, `:3382-3383`, via `ValidateIdentityFreeHeader`, `:4343-4357`); block ends read a group at, for example, `:1396` and `:4151`.
- Use: no `.calr` file, no C# test literal and no page under `docs/` or `website/content/` has a line starting with `in{`, `out{`, `where{` or `invariant{` (grep for `^\s*(in|out|where|invariant)\{`). `assume{` or `proof{` appears in 14 C# test files and one `.calr` file.

## Why

The edition freezes what the compiler accepts. A form that is accepted, undocumented and untested at the freeze either becomes part of the promise by accident or has to be removed later as a breaking change. The 0.30 cleanup left this decision open in writing, and the window is the last point at which rejecting a form is cheap.

## Done when

- The window record has one row per class with the option chosen, the date, "changes `.calr` source" answered, and the probe result for every form in the inventory. Each of the 31 `ParseAttributes` call sites is assigned to a class or listed as reading no user-written group.
- If option 2 or 3: the row lists the forms #1793 must warn on and #1803 must reject, with the replacement each error message names. For option 3 it also names the rewriter rule in #1806 and the chosen replacement spellings with their token counts.
- If option 1: the record says which of the kept forms are documented in `docs/syntax-reference/` and which stay undocumented, with the reason.
- The pull request that closes this issue changes no file under `src/`.

Part of epic #1787. Depends on #1785.

issues.title: [0.32] Union declaration spelling: token-measured decision before the freeze
issues.body:
## Change

Choose the one Calor spelling for "one of a closed set of types" that #1643 (0.34) will implement, and record it as a row of the window record (#1784, `docs/design/0.32-breaking-window.md`). The spelling adds a form: it rewrites no existing declaration. It changes existing `.calr` source only if it reserves a word (step 1). It is decided inside the window so that the edition is not followed at once by a new spelling debate.

1. **List the candidates.** At least: the C# 15 declaration carried over with Calor's existing conventions (lowercase keyword, indentation, `type:name`), and one or more shorter alternatives. State for each whether C# 15 unions and closed hierarchies share it, as #1643 requires ("map both ... to it, or say why they must stay distinct"). The repository does not spell the C# 15 declaration; take it from the C# 15 language reference and cite the page and date in the record. State for each candidate whether it needs a word that programs may use as an identifier today. Such a candidate is either recognised by position, or its word is reserved inside the window: the row is then marked "changes `.calr` source: yes", #1793 carries the reservation and #1803 switches it on.
2. **Write payloads** for each candidate and add them as probes to the window's single manifest: a declaration with three cases; the same declaration followed by a `match` that covers every case; and a closed hierarchy if it shares the spelling. This follows the three-probe pattern the 0.30 record used for `record` (row 22).
3. **Apply the amended rule** (#1785) to the counts from every tokenizer in the set (#1799). This is a maintainer decision with a default: the C# spelling is chosen unless an alternative clears the rule's minimum win.
4. **Record** the candidates, the counts per tokenizer, the margin, the clause of the rule that decided, and the date.

Do not write the candidates in `calor` code fences: they are not compiler-accepted syntax until #1643 lands. Use `text` fences, as the 0.30 record does.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- No parser path builds a union declaration: `UnionTypeDefinitionNode` is referenced in seven files under `src/Calor.Compiler/` and `Parsing/Parser.cs` is not one of them.
- The converter cannot write one: `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/CalorEmitter.cs:2838-2839` throws "UnionTypeDefinitionNode has no 0.30 source form."
- The checker's union type is never constructed: `UnionType` is declared at `src/Calor.Compiler/TypeChecking/CalorType.cs:410` and `new UnionType(` appears nowhere in `src/`. The union arm of the exhaustiveness switch (`src/Calor.Compiler/Analysis/PatternChecker.cs:261`) therefore cannot be reached from source, and 0.30 checks exhaustiveness for `bool` only (`:258-263`).
- #1643 asks for "exactly one Calor spelling ... chosen by fewest tokens (#1597's tool)". Its title and body still use the retired `§W`.
- The typed patterns a `match` arm would use (`case string text` and similar) are recorded as "a provisional inventory gate, not a count result or human selection" (`docs/design/0.30-syntax-token-decision.md:572`).

## Why

#1643 must pick a new spelling, and it is scheduled after the edition is declared. A spelling that reserves no word does not break the edition, but one that does must be reserved inside the window, and choosing either in 0.34 would reopen the token debate on a language that has just been frozen and would need another maintainer token dispatch. Deciding it now uses the window's one manifest and one dispatch, and applies the amended rule while it is being applied to everything else. Exhaustive unions are parity with C# 15's compiler-checked `switch`, not an advantage over it.

## Done when

- The window record row is filled as item 4 describes, with "changes `.calr` source" answered on that basis: "no" for a spelling recognised by position, "yes" with the reserved word named if one is reserved.
- The row states whether unions and closed hierarchies share the spelling.
- Every count in the row cites the window's payload commit and runs.
- The pull request that closes this issue changes only the record: no file under `src/` and no page under `docs/syntax-reference/`.

## Not in scope

Implementing unions, their exhaustiveness check, or the `net10.0` lowering question (#1643). Confirming the typed-pattern spellings (#1646). Option and Result stay removed (#1617).

Part of epic #1787. Depends on #1785, #1799. Blocks #1643.

issues.title: [0.32] Decide whether a redundant public is canonical
issues.body:
## Change

Decide whether writing `public` where it is already the default is canonical Calor, and record the decision as a row of the window record (#1784, `docs/design/0.32-breaking-window.md`). For example, `func Main public () → void` and `func Main () → void` declare the same function. This issue decides; it changes no compiler, lint or sample file.

| Option | Cost |
|---|---|
| 1. Canonical form omits the default `public`; the explicit form stays legal | A new `calor lint` finding with a safe fix, and a formatter rule, implemented under #1793 (the conditional issue that carries compiler and tool changes for decided rows of the window record). The rewrite of existing material (counts below) is a rule of the rewriter (#1806), applied by the single rewrite (#1803). |
| 2. Both are canonical (today) | Public material keeps two spellings; `samples/` disagrees with the generated reference. |
| 3. Canonical form writes `public` | Contradicts the 0.30 decision (row 4) and the converter's output; the generated reference, the primer and the emitter would all change. |

The choice is made under the amended fewest-tokens rule (#1785), on the counts from every tokenizer in its set; the row names the clause that decided.

The plan recommends option 1, for every declaration kind whose default visibility is public. Whatever is chosen, enforcement is a `calor lint` finding and a formatter rule only, never a compile error. The non-canonical form stays legal after the cut-over in #1803, and the row says so, so the decision cannot break a program under the edition. Add payloads with and without the keyword to the window's manifest: the 0.30 measurement compared `pub`, not `public`, against the default (31 against 27 tokens, row 4).

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- `samples/`: 27 of 31 `func` headers write `public` (grep over the 11 `.calr` files); two write `private`, two write nothing.
- The generated reference and the primer never write it: zero matches for a `func` header with `public` in `docs/syntax-reference/current-language.md` and `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/agent-syntax-exemplar.md`. The reference says "public is the default" (`current-language.md:14`).
- Hand-written reference pages do write it: `docs/syntax-reference/types.md:55-57`, `:183`, `:244`; `structure-tags.md:56`; `effects.md:287`, `:329`; four more lines under `docs/semantics/`; 36 lines in 18 files under `website/content/`.
- Whole tree, by `grep -rIE 'func \S+ public\b'`: 402 `.calr` files contain 2,148 such headers, 390 of the files under `tests/TestData/ActiveSyntax/`; 129 C# files under `tests/`, `src/`, `tools/` and `bench/` embed 1,830 more lines in string literals. None of the 50 translated benchmark pair files under `tests/TestData/ActiveSyntax/bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs/` has one.
- The converter omits the default: `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/CalorEmitter.cs:475` and ten further sites emit visibility only when it is not public.
- No lint flags it: the lint findings are Calor1300, 1301, 1305 and 1306 (`src/Calor.Compiler/Diagnostics/Diagnostic.cs:1196-1235`); Calor1307 to Calor1309 are unused. `calor lint --fix` exists (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/LintCommand.cs:27-28`).
- The source formatter keeps every token today: `FormatSource` "Formats source while preserving all non-trivia source text" (`src/Calor.Compiler/Formatting/CalorFormatter.cs:45-48`). A formatter rule that deletes a keyword is a new kind of rule.

## Why

Agents and people write Calor from the examples in front of them, and those examples are not uniform: the samples write a keyword that the generated reference, the primer and the converter never write. After the edition is declared, a canonical-form decision that rewrites samples, documentation and fixtures would need a second repository-wide rewrite, so the decision belongs in the window even though it is enforced only by lint.

## Done when
