issues.title: [0.33] calor init per agent generated from the single reference, budgeted and tested
issues.body:
*The current body is stale: it describes four hand-maintained templates of 1.3–1.7K tokens each and asks for them to be generated from the single reference. Since 0.30.0 all four are generated from one field of that reference, are byte-identical, and measure 317 tokens each on the o200k proxy tokenizer.*

## Change

`calor init --ai claude|codex|gemini|github` writes `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `GEMINI.md` and `.github/copilot-instructions.md`. The four templates are generated from one field of the single teaching reference (`src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Teaching/reference.json`) and are byte-identical (see Baseline). The *primer* is the short syntax introduction the MCP server serves as `calor://primer`; the instruction files point to it. What is missing is everything that should differ per agent, a token count taken the way each agent counts, tests on what `calor init` actually writes (including the path by which an agent adds a test), and documentation that matches the files written. The work may be delivered as up to four ordered pull requests, one per numbered part; the issue closes on the single done-when below. Part 4 changes documentation and one test only, so a commit that holds parts 1 to 3 already ships the setup that #1811, #709 and #711 measure.

1. **Declare the per-agent differences in the single reference.** Keep the shared rule text as the #1823 record left it (one `agentInstructions` field, or the separate agent-file and server-instructions texts of its decision 3). Add to `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Teaching/reference.json` one entry per agent that holds only what differs: the instruction file name; the default value of the delivery option #1773 added, as the #1823 record set it for that agent (inlined regardless for a client the #1820 record lists as unable to read MCP resources); how that agent names the Calor MCP tools, if it differs; and whether `calor init` installs a write hook for that agent, so the generated text never claims a hook that is not there. The entry stores the delivery default only: the inlined file is still composed when `init` runs, by the #1773 mechanism, the embedded templates stay in the pointer form, and both forms stay selectable for every agent. `calor self-check docs --fix` generates the four templates from the shared text plus that entry (the generator is `ExemplarCompileChecker.GenerateTeachingResources`). No per-agent text is hand-edited in a template. In the same part, reword the two sentences that name .NET 10 so that neither names a version: the rule-text sentence (`reference.json:6`) and the primer sentence (`primer.introduction`, `reference.json:2432`, rendered at `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/agent-syntax-exemplar.md:5`), which is part of the instruction file for an agent with the inlined default. #1639 (0.31) makes .NET 11 a supported runtime, and a version number in an always-loaded file goes stale at every .NET release.
2. **Budget each agent's always-loaded text.** This issue changes no budget constant: each agent's file is held to the constant the #1823 record set for the delivery form that agent uses by default (pointer or inlined). Per-agent text fits the allocation the #1823 record gives this issue. If it does not fit, shorten shared text in the same pull request, or move the per-agent detail behind `calor_help` and keep one pointer sentence. A constant changes only through a dated entry the maintainer appends to `docs/plans/0.32-delivery-and-budget-record.md`. For each agent, count the instruction file `calor init` writes at that agent's default plus the MCP server instructions with that agent's tokenizer from the set #1785 named, using the counters #1799 delivered. Where that tokenizer runs offline, the count is a CI assertion in `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/TokenBudgetTests.cs`. Where it needs a key, record one manual count and its date in the comment next to the constant and keep the o200k proxy as that agent's CI gate. The test output names the tokenizer that gates each agent.
3. **Test what `calor init` writes, per agent.** One test per agent runs that agent's initializer at its default into an empty project (through `AiInitializerFactory.Create`, as `InitCommandE2ETests` does) and checks the files on disk, not the embedded templates:
   - (a) every complete Calor program in the generated instruction file compiles (`ExemplarCompileChecker.ExtractCompletePrograms` finds them) and the file passes the removed-form scan used by `AgentDocsSyntaxGuardTests`;
   - (b) every `calor_*` tool and `calor://` resource the file names is registered;
   - (c) the test-authoring path holds: the text that the #1823 record makes the carrier of the rules for that agent (the instruction file under options a and b of its decision 3, the server instructions under option c) carries the sentence #1809 added (an agent may create test files under `tests/`), and the hook entry point named in that agent's generated configuration (`calor hook validate-write`, `calor hook validate-write --format gemini`, or `calor hook codex-write --phase pre`) allows a new file under `tests/` and still blocks a new `.cs` file outside it;
   - (d) for an agent with no hook (Copilot), no hook is configured and the file does not claim one;
   - (e) the non-default delivery form can still be selected and produces the #1773 output;
   - (f) every `calor hook` command in that agent's generated configuration is a registered subcommand and allows the write of a valid 0.30 `.calr` file. This covers `validate-ids`, which the Claude Code and Gemini configurations install although 0.30 sources carry no IDs; if the test shows the hook can no longer block anything, removing it from the generated configuration is part of this issue.

   One further case, run once because the command is the same for every agent: in an initialized project, add a test file under `tests/` and expect `calor check` to run it and not exit 3 ("no tests"). If #1825 (tests written in `.calr`) has merged when these tests are written, add a `.calr` test to the same case. If it has not, #1825 adds that case when it lands, and this issue does not wait for it.
4. **Make the documentation list what each initializer writes.** In `docs/cli/init.md` (the four sections under "AI Agent Support") and in `claude-integration.mdx`, `codex-integration.mdx`, `gemini-integration.mdx` and `github-integration.mdx` under `website/content/getting-started/`, the file table for each agent lists exactly the files that agent's initializer creates or updates, and the prose names only registered `calor_*` tools. Add a test that runs each initializer into an empty project and compares the paths in those tables with the paths the initializer reports (`InitResult.CreatedFiles` and `UpdatedFiles`), so the pages cannot drift again.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- The four templates are generated, not hand-maintained. `ExemplarCompileChecker` writes all four from the `agentInstructions` field of `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Teaching/reference.json` (`src/Calor.Compiler/SelfCheck/ExemplarCompileChecker.cs:138`, `:158-162`), and CI fails on drift (`calor self-check docs`, `.github/workflows/test.yml:267`).
- They are byte-identical: `CLAUDE.md.template`, `AGENTS.md.template`, `GEMINI.md.template` and `copilot-instructions.md.template` under `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Templates/` are 1,165 bytes each with one md5 (measured by `wc -c` and `md5sum`). Nothing in the text differs per agent.
- Each template is 317 tokens and the MCP server instructions 275, so 592 against a budget of 600 (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/TokenBudgetTests.cs:42-47`; figures from that comment, dated 2026-11-20, not recomputed). The count uses one proxy tokenizer, o200k_base (`:19-25`). Anthropic `count_tokens` runs only from a manual workflow for one fixed model (`.github/workflows/syntax-token-count.yml:50`). No other agent's tokenizer is counted anywhere.
- The shared text says "Hooks are best-effort" to every agent (`CLAUDE.md.template:22`). `calor init` installs no hook for Copilot (`src/Calor.Compiler/Init/GitHubCopilotInitializer.cs:10`), and in the one recorded Codex session the generated Codex hooks did not intercept its writes (`bench/phase0-agent-native/CODEX-SMOKE.md:28-29`; 2026-07-22, pre-0.30 syntax).
- The shared text tells every agent never to create a `.cs` file (`CLAUDE.md.template:10`). The three installed write hooks reach one validator, `HookCommand.ValidateWriteWithReason`, which blocks every `.cs` path except `.g.cs` and `obj/` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/HookCommand.cs:256-312`; the Codex hook calls it at `:115`). `calor check` exits 3 when `tests/` holds no top-level `.cs` file (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/TestCommand.cs:31`, `:238-242`, `:404-422`). #1809 changes the validator, its block message and the text in 0.32; nothing yet checks the result through each agent's own hook entry point.
- Besides the write hook, the Claude Code and Gemini configurations install `calor hook validate-ids` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Init/ClaudeInitializer.cs:237`, `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Templates/gemini-settings.json.template:22`; the command is defined at `HookCommand.cs:576-646`). Whether it can still block anything on 0.30 sources, which carry no IDs, is not verified.
- Two always-loaded texts name a .NET version. The shared text says "Calor is a DSL that compiles to C# on .NET 10" (`reference.json:6`, rendered at `CLAUDE.md.template:5`), and the primer says "Calor compiles to C# on .NET 10" (`reference.json:2432`, rendered at `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/agent-syntax-exemplar.md:5`). The repository targets `net10.0` (`Directory.Build.props:4`), and #1639 makes .NET 11 a supported runtime in 0.31.
- `calor init` has no delivery option at HEAD (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/InitCommand.cs:16-41` defines `--ai`, `--project`, `--solution` and `--force`). #1773 adds one in 0.31 that composes the inlined form when `init` runs and leaves the embedded templates in the pointer form; #1823 sets its default per agent.
- Existing per-agent tests check which files are created (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/InitCommandE2ETests.cs:63`, `:144`, `:184`, `:238`). The removed-form scan reads the four template source files, not what `calor init` writes (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/Mcp/AgentDocsSyntaxGuardTests.cs:147-152`). `McpRegistryValidationTests` checks tool and resource names in three templates and omits the Copilot one (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/McpRegistryValidationTests.cs:19-48`). No test compiles programs out of a generated instruction file; today the file contains none.
- The documentation lists files that no initializer writes. `docs/cli/init.md` lists four skill files and a `.mcp.json` for Claude Code (`:127-132`), although the initializer writes `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/settings.json` and registers the server in `~/.claude.json` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Init/ClaudeInitializer.cs:65`, `:84`, `:95-97`); it lists two skill files each for Gemini (`:253-254`) and Copilot (`:307-308`); and its Codex section names `calor_typecheck` and `calor_verify_contracts` (`:209`), which are not registered tools. `gemini-integration.mdx:24-25` and `github-integration.mdx:24-25` list the same skill files. No initializer writes a skill file: the only matches of `grep -rn -i skill src/Calor.Compiler/Init/` are four class comments that say MCP tools replace skill files. The tables at `claude-integration.mdx:19-23` and `codex-integration.mdx:22-26` match their initializers.
- The compiler test shard runs 29 to 30 minutes against a 40-minute cap (`.github/workflows/test.yml:505-508`), which is why the `calor check` case runs once and not per agent.
- `eng/test-manifest.json` pins `expectedTotal` per test project, and `scripts/check_trx.py` enforces it in CI (`.github/workflows/test.yml:603`).

## Why

The generated instruction file is the only Calor text an agent loads on every turn, and 0.33 is the first release that measures it under agents other than Claude Code. Today every agent gets the same text, including statements that are false for some of them: it speaks of hooks to Copilot, which has none. An agent that follows the file must also be able to add a test without breaking a rule the file gives it. #1809 changes the hook and the shared text for that in 0.32, and this issue checks that the result holds through each agent's own hook entry point, not only Claude Code's. The budget is counted per agent because the 600-token budget has only ever been measured with one proxy tokenizer. The documentation is included because it describes files that `calor init` stopped writing, and a user who checks the result of `calor init` against it will conclude the command failed. #1811 measures each agent in the workspace this issue ships, so this issue lands first.

## Done when

- `reference.json` holds one per-agent entry for each of the four agents, the four templates are regenerated from them, and `calor self-check docs` exits 0 in the `test` job of `.github/workflows/test.yml`.
- For each of `claude`, `codex`, `gemini` and `github`, a test in `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/` runs that agent's initializer into an empty project and asserts checks (a) to (f) of part 3 on the written files. All four pass in the `tests (compiler)` shard.
- The `calor check` case in part 3 passes in the same shard.
- A budget test asserts, per agent, instruction file plus MCP server instructions against the #1823 constant with the tokenizer named for that agent, and prints which tokenizer gates which agent. For an agent gated by the proxy, the manual count and its date are in the comment next to the constant. No budget constant differs from the value in `docs/plans/0.32-delivery-and-budget-record.md`.
- `McpRegistryValidationTests` covers the Copilot template.
- A test asserts that no instruction file `calor init` writes, in either delivery form, names a .NET version (no match for the pattern `\.NET \d`), and that the primer does not either.
- The documentation test of part 4 passes: for each agent, the file tables in `docs/cli/init.md` and in that agent's page under `website/content/getting-started/` list exactly the files its initializer writes, and neither page names an unregistered `calor_*` tool.
- `expectedTotal` for `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests.csproj` in `eng/test-manifest.json` is raised by the number of tests added.
- Each pull request states the tokens it adds to and removes from each agent's instruction file, as `TokenBudgetTests` counts them.

## Not in scope

- The delivery option itself (#1773), its default and every budget constant (#1823).
- The hook exemption for `tests/`, the sentence in the rule text that announces it, and the hook's block message, which #1809 rewords to name only what `calor init` installs.
- Whether a live agent follows the generated file. #1811 measures that as the primer-read rate, and the smoke runs of #709 and #711 observe it.
- Tests written in `.calr` (#1825), beyond the one case in part 3.
- Any change to a language spelling.

Part of #1653. Depends on #1823, #1809, #1799, #1773. Blocks #1811, #709, #711, #1846.

issues.title: [0.33] Agent evaluation harness beyond the claude CLI: driver contract and zero-cost pass for Codex, Gemini, Copilot
issues.body:
**Current**

The filed body says the harness drives only the `claude` CLI and that #1605 adds the arm design. It asks for three things: abstract the agent driver so the same task pairs run under Codex, Gemini and Copilot (each driver needs its CLI, model pin, workspace setup through `calor init`, and log capture for turns and tokens); run the C# and Calor arms for each agent on the same pairs and starters; and publish per-agent results on the website with model, commit and command line. It is done when each agent runs through the harness and results are published, including any agent where Calor does worse than C#. It names one dependency, #1605, and carries no spend terms.

**Amendment**

Six edits. They narrow the issue to the part that needs no spend; the paid runs and the publication move to #1811.

1. Retitle to `[0.33] Agent evaluation harness beyond the claude CLI: driver contract and zero-cost pass for Codex, Gemini, Copilot`.

2. In `## Change`, replace the opening paragraph with:

```markdown
The evaluation harness (`bench/phase0-agent-native/run-pair.sh`) drives only the `claude` CLI. #1605 (0.31) measures the 0.30 language with Claude Code against a concurrent C# arm. This issue makes the agent a parameter of the same harness and proves each new agent's path at zero cost. An *arm* is one language condition of a task (Calor or C#). A *driver* is the code that starts one agent CLI and reads what it did. A *zero-cost pass* is a `--null-agent` run: the harness prepares the workspace, applies the reference solution in place of an agent, builds and grades, with no call to any model.

No part of this issue calls a vendor API, so it needs no spend decision and lands whatever #1832 records; #1709 and #1710 reuse the drivers in 0.37. The paid runs and their publication are #1811. In this issue a path with no directory is under `bench/phase0-agent-native/`.
```

3. In `## Change`, replace items 1 to 3 with:

```markdown
1. **Start after #1827 has merged.** The arm abstraction restructures the same 1,893-line script (`wc -l run-pair.sh`). Build on it; do not restructure the script in parallel.
2. **Define a driver contract and move `claude` behind it**, with no change to what a Claude Code run archives. Add an agent parameter to `run-pair.sh`, to `run-epoch.sh` and to the epoch driver #1815 added (the one that interleaves arms and stops on a spend ceiling), defaulting to `claude`. For a CLI that reports no cost, that driver's stop also accepts a run count. A driver declares:
   - the CLI command and its non-interactive flags;
   - how the model is pinned, and how the agent name, CLI version and model reach `pins.json`;
   - workspace setup: `calor init --ai <agent>` and that agent's MCP registration for the Calor arm, nothing for the C# arm, and how user-level MCP servers and instruction files are kept out of both arms (the Claude Code driver uses `--strict-mcp-config`);
   - how the harness's own write blocks (generated `.g.cs` files, the smoke suite) are enforced in arms that do not use the `calor init` hooks: by a hook where the agent has one, by a post-run check that invalidates the run where it does not;
   - how the raw transcript is archived, what is stripped before it is committed (session identifiers, local paths), and how it is normalised into what the harness and the report script read: `transcript.jsonl`, the result envelope in `agent.json`, turns, input, cached-input and output tokens, cost if the CLI reports one, tool calls, and the primer-read event;
   - the primer-read event: whether and when the agent read the primer (the MCP resource `calor://primer`, `calor_help`, or the CLI primer command). If the read log that #1767 added is taken from the MCP server or the `calor` wrapper, the driver reuses it. If that log parses Claude Code's stream-json, or #1767 was closed as not planned, the driver supplies the event from a journal on the server side;
   - the iteration count in initialized workspaces: a `calor check` that follows an edit is journalled as an iteration with `cmd: "check"`, whichever agent ran it. If #1767 was closed as not planned, make that change here (item 5 of that issue's text: journal each `calor check` through the same observation as `dotnet build`, and add `check` to the `cmd` enum of `loop-telemetry.schema.json` and to `validate-telemetry.sh`);
   - the strings that mark an invalid run (rate limit, quota, API error);
   - its spend control: a per-run budget flag if the CLI has one, otherwise the wall-clock timeout plus the cumulative stop of the #1815 epoch driver between runs;
   - the paths the arm isolation from #1762 must allow for this client: its install and its credentials.
3. **Add drivers for Codex, Gemini and Copilot** against each CLI's documented non-interactive mode. The Codex invocation used on 2026-07-22 is recorded in `CODEX-SMOKE.md`. The Copilot driver targets the client the #1820 record checked (`docs/cli/mcp.md`, "Client configuration"), or its optional headless row if that row shows the client loading the Calor server; #1832 names the same client by default and writes it down once this driver exists, so this issue does not wait for that record. `calor init --ai github` registers the MCP server in `.vscode/mcp.json`; whether a headless Copilot client reads that file is not verified and is the first thing the Copilot driver must establish. If no headless Copilot client can load the generated instruction file and MCP registration, deliver the Copilot driver as a stub that fails with "not measurable headlessly" and document the reason. That is an accepted outcome for Copilot.
4. **Zero-cost pass per driver.** With each driver selected, run `--null-agent` on both arms of every pair in the #1605 pair set (the pairs #1770 registered, as re-validated by #1807): the Calor arm with `--initialized-workspace`, so that `calor init --ai <agent>` really runs and its output is archived, and the C# arm in ordinary mode.
5. **Test each driver without its CLI.** A stub executable stands in for each CLI, following `tests/test_initialized_workspace.py:336-404`, which stubs `claude`. Each driver's normaliser has unit tests under `tests/` on a committed, sanitised sample transcript. The sample is hand-built from the CLI's documented output format, taken from a #1820 session transcript, or recorded in a run that #1832 authorised; the test file says which.
```

4. Insert a new section after `## Change`:

```markdown
## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

Where the harness assumes Claude Code today:

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Client command `claude` and its flags (`--print --verbose --output-format stream-json ...`) | `run-pair.sh:1352-1353` |
| Model pin read from `CLAUDE_MODEL`; CLI version from `claude --version` | `run-pair.sh:1325`; `run-epoch.sh:39-40` |
| MCP registration passed as `--mcp-config ... --strict-mcp-config` | `run-pair.sh:1331` |
| Write blocks installed as a Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook in `.claude/settings.json` | `run-pair.sh:899-926` |
| Per-run budget through `--max-budget-usd`, checked against `claude --help`, for registered runs only | `run-pair.sh:1368-1380` |
| Result event filtered out of stream-json into `agent.json`; full transcript archived | `run-pair.sh:1387`, `:1402` |
| Tokens and cost read from the Claude Code result envelope (`modelUsage`, `total_cost_usd`) | `token-usage.py` (module docstring) |
| Turns counted from stream-json assistant message ids | `harness-capture.py:168` |
| Invalid-run markers (Claude Code's rate-limit and API-error strings) matched in `agent.json` | `run-pair.sh:58-82` |
| A run is invalid without a non-empty `agent.json` and `transcript.jsonl` | `run-pair.sh:65-72`, `:93-96` |
| Initialized workspace runs `init --ai claude`, requires `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/settings.json`, and reads the MCP registration from `~/.claude.json` | `harness-capture.py:610-616`, `:634-639` |

- `--null-agent` applies the reference solution with no agent call (`run-pair.sh:1270-1306`). `--initialized-workspace` accepts only the ordinary Calor arm on non-probe pairs (`run-pair.sh:294-310`, `:364-368`). The two combine: a test runs `--null-agent --initialized-workspace` against a built compiler (`tests/test_initialized_workspace.py:459-470`), and another drives a live-mode run with a stub `claude` executable (`:336-404`).
- Iterations are observed by a `dotnet` shim placed first on `PATH` (`run-pair.sh:20-23`, `:1383`), so counting them does not depend on the agent. In an initialized workspace the `calor` wrapper execs the CLI directly, past that shim (`run-pair.sh:982-985`), so a `calor check` leaves no journal record, and the journal's `cmd` enum is `build`, `test`, `run` (`loop-telemetry.schema.json:16`). #1767 changes that in 0.31 unless it is closed as not planned.
- `run-epoch.sh` runs every run of one arm before the next and has no spend stop (`:49-68`). #1815 adds an epoch driver in 0.32 that interleaves one run per arm per pair and starts no run once the summed cost reaches `--spend-ceiling`.
- The local timeout is not a spending guarantee (`run-pair.sh:1308-1309`).
- Harness unit tests live in `tests/` and run in CI in the step "Test bench token-usage helper (#881)" of the `calor-first-guard` job, with no agent CLI installed (`.github/workflows/test.yml:122-125`).
- Nothing records whether an agent read the primer. The MCP server journals writes only (`src/Calor.Compiler/Mcp/Tools/FileWriteTool.cs:65`); a `resources/read` is written to stderr only under `calor mcp --verbose` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Mcp/McpMessageHandler.cs:433`, `:696-702`). #1767 adds a read log in 0.31.
- One non-Claude session is on record: Codex CLI 0.144.6, pair `W1-001-temperature-converter`, 2026-07-22, Calor 0.7.0, pre-0.30 syntax, invoked as `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust --sandbox workspace-write --json`. It was run by hand, not through this harness, and its raw transcripts were not committed because they held session identifiers and local paths (`CODEX-SMOKE.md:11-20`, `:62-65`). No Gemini or Copilot session is recorded.
- The non-interactive modes, transcript formats, token and cost reporting and budget flags of the current Codex, Gemini and Copilot CLIs are not verified; the repository holds no evidence beyond the Codex invocation above.
```

5. Replace `## Done when` with:

```markdown
## Done when

- `run-pair.sh`, `run-epoch.sh` and the #1815 epoch driver take the agent as a parameter, and a stub test shows that driver stopping on a run count when the stub reports no cost. With a stub `claude` executable, a test asserts that the Claude Code driver passes the same argument list as the commit before this change, and `python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/phase0-agent-native/tests` exits 0 in the CI step at `.github/workflows/test.yml:122-125`.
- For each of Codex, Gemini and Copilot, a stub-executable test asserts the argument list the driver builds (non-interactive flags, model pin, no user-level configuration) and that `pins.json` records the agent name, CLI version and model.
- Each driver's normaliser has a unit test on a committed sample transcript that asserts turns, the token fields and the primer-read event, and states where the sample came from. These tests run in the same CI step.
- A stub-agent test in an initialized workspace yields a `cmd: "check"` journal record for each driver: the stub edits a `.calr` file and runs `calor check`, and `journal.jsonl` holds one record with `cmd: "check"` and `edited: true`.
- For each of Codex, Gemini and Copilot, `--null-agent` exits 0 on both arms of every pair in the #1605 pair set with `taskSuccess: true` in every `result.json`, and the archived initialized inputs of the Calor arm contain the files `calor init --ai <agent>` writes. The output is committed under `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/` in a directory whose name ends in `-null`.
- For Copilot only, a stub driver that exits with "not measurable headlessly", with the reason documented in the README, satisfies the three preceding bullets.
- `bench/phase0-agent-native/README.md` documents the driver contract and, per driver, the CLI version it was written against and each behaviour that was not verified against a live run.
- No pull request for this issue needs an API key or an installed agent CLI to pass CI.
```

6. Add a `## Not in scope` section and replace the closing line "Part of #1653. Depends on #1605." with:

```markdown
## Not in scope

- Any paid run and the publication of per-agent results (#1811), and the smoke runs of #709 and #711.
- Arm types other than Calor and C# (#1827), the language-neutral oracle (#1830) and the Rust reading (#1831).
- The three conditions of the 0.37 comparison. #1709 and #1710 reuse these drivers.
- Per-agent `calor init` output (#1650) and MCP client compatibility (#1652).

Part of #1653. Depends on #1605, #1827, #1815, #1820. Blocks #1811, #709, #711, #1709, #1710.
```

**Why**

The filed issue bundles harness code, paid runs on three vendors and a publication. The harness code costs nothing, and #1709 and #1710 need it in 0.37 whether or not the 0.33 spend is approved; the other two need a spend decision that the filed issue never asks for. Narrowing this issue to the driver contract and a zero-cost pass lets that work start without waiting on #1832 and lets 0.33 exit on a recorded decline. #1827 goes first because both issues restructure `run-pair.sh`. The primer-read event joins the driver contract because the per-agent report needs a primer-read rate, and the 0.31 read log may understand only Claude Code's transcript format. The `calor check` record joins it because #1832 allows no paid Calor arm in a `calor init` workspace until that record exists, and #1767, which would add it, is conditional. The agent parameter reaches the #1815 epoch driver because that is the only driver that interleaves arms and stops on a ceiling, which the per-agent runs require.

issues.title: [0.33] Run and publish per-agent results (conditional)
issues.body:
## Change

**Gate.** Start only when the record that #1832 produces (`docs/plans/0.33-paid-run-registration.md`) carries a dated "Authorised" line for an agent under its Part A, the per-agent runs. #1832 is the maintainer's decision on the 0.33 paid runs; it is registered in Annex A of `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md`. The gate has no numeric threshold: it is that decision.

- If Part A reads "Declined" for every agent, close this issue as not planned and link the record. No paid run is made, and the first 0.33 exit criterion is met by the recorded decline.
- If an agent has neither line, the issue is held for that agent: no run is made for it. With no line at all the issue stays open and unstarted, and 0.33 cannot exit on its first criterion until the maintainer signs.
- The record may authorise some agents and decline others. Run the authorised ones and report each declined one as "declined" with the record's reason.

Filing or keeping this issue does not authorise spend.

**What to do once the gate is open.** Terms used below:

- An *arm* is one language condition of a task (Calor or C#). A *pair* is one task with a Calor and a C# starter and a shared hidden test suite. A *driver* is the harness code that starts one agent CLI and reads what it did (#1651).
- An *iteration* is one build-or-test invocation that follows at least one edit. *Iterations-to-green* counts iterations until the hidden tests first all pass. A run is *censored* when they never all pass within the iteration budget.
- A *valid run* is one the harness did not mark invalid (rate limit, API error, missing transcript, isolation violation). *Tokens per accepted task* is an arm's total tokens over its valid runs divided by the number of those runs that pass every hidden test.

1. **Pin.** One commit that contains #1650 and #1651. Per agent, one CLI version and one model id, the same for both arms, written into `pins.json`. "Copilot" means the client the record names.
2. **Zero-cost pass first.** On the pinned commit, `--null-agent` (the harness applies the reference solution in place of an agent, with no model call) passes on both arms of every registered pair with each authorised agent's driver. Its output is archived before that agent's first paid run.
3. **Run** the C# and Calor arms for each authorised agent on the pairs and with the run count in the record, through the epoch driver #1815 added, with the agent parameter #1651 gives it, so the two arms are interleaved and the driver's spend stop is the check of step 4. The runs use the arm isolation from #1762, under which the agent process cannot read the checkout or the reference solutions and a pre-flight canary proves it. The Calor-arm workspace is the one `calor init --ai <agent>` writes on the pinned commit at its default, with no file added or rewritten by the harness, so the runs measure the setup that ships for that agent.
4. **Spend control.** Per agent the record holds a ceiling in dollars, or as a run count where the CLI reports no cost. An agent with no ceiling on record is not run. The ceiling is cumulative and is checked between runs against realised cost, and retries of invalid runs count against it. Stop that agent's collection, and report what exists as incomplete, when any of these happens: the ceiling is reached; a transcript reports a model other than the pin; two consecutive runs in one arm are invalid; the isolation canary fails; or a further trigger that the record lists fires.
5. **Readings written in advance.** No reading is written after the data is seen. The record must hold, per agent, a reading for at least these outcomes, and the report applies them as written:
   - the Calor-to-C# ratio of iterations-to-green and of tokens per accepted task is inside, above or below the band the record states;
   - Calor task success is within or below the margin of C# that the record states;
   - more than 40% of runs are censored in either arm, which reads "not measured on this agent" (the validity limit in `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md:39`);
   - turns or tokens cannot be captured from the CLI, which reads "not measured", with the reason;
   - the Copilot client cannot be driven without its editor, which reads "not measurable headlessly";
   - the primer (the short syntax introduction served as `calor://primer`) is read in fewer Calor-arm runs than the delivery rule requires. That rule was registered in #1770 and decides whether `calor init` inlines the primer in the generated agent file.

   If an outcome occurs for which the record holds no reading, report it as "no reading registered" and draw no conclusion from it.
6. **Report per agent**, Calor against C# within that agent:
   - task success per arm, and the Calor-to-C# ratios of iterations-to-green, input tokens, output tokens, turns, and cost where the CLI reports one;
   - the columns of the report script from #1760, run unchanged on this epoch's archive: failure classes with opportunity counts, the first-build pass rate as that script defines it, the repeat rate per diagnostic code, and the rest of its table;
   - the unknown-effect share from #1802 for the Calor arm: the share of callables that declare `! unknown` and the share of call sites charged `unknown`, computed from each run's final sources;
   - the primer-read rate: valid Calor-arm runs in which the agent read the primer, divided by valid Calor-arm runs, or "inlined" where that agent's `calor init` output inlines the primer;
   - if the record takes the observation-only option for the example bank (#1835) and the pinned commit contains the bank: the report script's "example uses per run" column and the first-build pass rate, with the sentence "no comparison arm; no effect is claimed";
   - model, CLI version, commit, command line, runs attempted, valid and censored, and realised spend next to the ceiling.

   Agents are not ranked against each other, because their models and CLIs differ. No figure is compared with #1605 or any other epoch. An agent where Calor does worse than C# is published like any other. Follow the "Benchmarks" rule in the repository's `CLAUDE.md`: fair comparisons, not biased toward Calor.
7. **Publish** in the 0.33 release notes (`CHANGELOG.md`) and as rows in the evidence ledger (`docs/benchmarking/evidence-ledger.md`, added by #1774). `docs/benchmarking/results.md` is generated and is not edited. Commit the epoch archive under `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/`, with transcripts sanitised as each driver specifies.
8. **Hand over to #1846.** Post on #1846, per agent, the diagnostics that agent hit most often and every removed or unknown form it tried to write. Nothing in this issue changes a spelling.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- The harness starts only the `claude` CLI (`bench/phase0-agent-native/run-pair.sh:1352-1353`), and its initialized-workspace mode runs `init --ai claude` (`bench/phase0-agent-native/harness-capture.py:610-611`). #1651 adds the other drivers.
- One session of another agent is on record: Codex CLI 0.144.6 on 2026-07-22, one pair, Calor 0.7.0 (pre-0.30 syntax), run by hand outside the harness. Its record holds no tokens, turns or cost (`bench/phase0-agent-native/CODEX-SMOKE.md`). No Gemini or Copilot session is recorded.
- The only archived per-run costs are Claude Code's, from July 2026 on the pre-0.30 syntax with the model pin `default`: mean $0.55 per C# run, $3.93 per Calor run and $1.70 per Calor run with an exemplar appended to the prompt; $370.52 for 180 runs, the dearest run $7.97 (measured by summing `total_cost_usd` over `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/e1a-attribution/*/*/run-*/agent.json`; the pin is in `pins.json` beside them). What a run costs on another vendor's CLI, and how each CLI reports cost, is not verified.
- Nothing in the harness stops a collection on spend. `run-pair.sh` passes a per-run budget (`--max-budget-usd`) only on the registered PP-W path (`:1368-1380`) and calls its timeout "NOT a provider spending guarantee" (`:1308-1309`). `run-epoch.sh` loops over pairs and arms with no cumulative check and runs one arm to completion before the next (`:49-68`); its header says a live epoch needs explicit authorisation (`:10-11`). #1815 adds the epoch driver with interleaving and a spend stop in 0.32, and #1651 gives it the agent parameter.
- Two earlier collections overran their estimates: $92.83 realised against a projected range of $15 to $89 (`docs/plans/pp-w5-spend-authorisation.md:18`, `:86`), and $79.39 against an estimate under $20 (`bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/guarantees-probe-001/VERDICT.md:20-23`).
- The gates document allows comparisons only within one epoch on one pinned model set (`docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md:12`) and calls a gate invalid when either arm is more than 40% censored (`:39`).
- Annex A of that document is held append-only in CI by the `annex-freeze` job (`.github/workflows/experiment-registry-tamper-check.yml:98`, `scripts/check-annex-freeze.py`).
- `docs/benchmarking/results.md` is generated from `website/public/data/benchmark-results.json` and marked do-not-edit (`:1-2`). The evidence ledger, the report script, the unknown-effect count and a primer-read log do not exist at HEAD; they come from #1774, #1760, #1802, and #1767 or #1651.

## Why

The first 0.33 exit criterion is per-agent results for Codex, Gemini and Copilot published on one harness, or the maintainer's recorded decline of that spend. The runs cost money on three vendors whose per-run cost has never been measured here, and two earlier collections in this program overran their estimates, so the money is a separate, explicit decision (#1832) and this issue only carries it out. Keeping the paid half apart from #1651 means the driver work is not held by the decision and a decline closes one issue cleanly. The runs use the workspace `calor init` ships for each agent because that is what a user of that agent gets; a hand-tuned prompt would measure a setup nobody ships. Results are read within an agent because models and CLIs differ across vendors.

## Done when

One of the two.

Authorised:

- The 0.33 section of `CHANGELOG.md` and the evidence ledger carry, for each of Codex, Gemini and Copilot, either the report of step 6 with the registered reading applied, or one of the outcomes "not measured", "not measurable headlessly" or "declined" with its reason. An agent where Calor does worse than C# is included.
- The epoch archive is committed under `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/` and holds, per agent, `pins.json` with one model and one CLI version, and a `--null-agent` pass dated before that agent's first paid run.
- Realised spend per agent is stated next to its ceiling. No agent's realised spend exceeds its ceiling by more than the cost of the one run in flight when the check fired.
- The hand-over list of step 8 is posted on #1846.
- This issue links the #1832 record.

Declined:

- The #1832 record carries a dated "Declined" line under Part A for each of the three agents, this issue links it and is closed as not planned, and the 0.33 release notes say that per-agent results were not collected and why. No paid run was made.

## Not in scope

- The decision itself: its options, ceilings, pairs, run counts and readings (#1832).
- The drivers and the zero-cost pass tooling (#1651), and the per-agent `calor init` output (#1650).
- The smoke runs of #709 and #711, the Rust reading (#1831) and a paid example-bank comparison (#1835).
- Ranking agents, and comparing any agent with the Claude Code results of #1605.
- Any change to a spelling. Findings go to #1846; the edition holds.

Part of #1653. Depends on #1651, #1650, #1832, #1760, #1802. Blocks #1846.

issues.title: [0.33] MCP server compatibility tests across agent clients
issues.body:
**Current**

The filed body asks for a compatibility test per client (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, VS Code/Copilot) that covers initialize, tool listing, schema validity under each client's schema rules, resources, and the single build-test-verify call from #1614; for incompatibilities to be fixed in the tool schemas or documented as client limits; and for #673 to be superseded. It is done when every listed client passes the compatibility tests "in CI or a scripted check".

**Amendment**

Six edits. The title does not change.

1. In `## Change`, replace item 1 with:

```markdown
1. **Compatibility checks in CI, with no client installed.** For each client (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, VS Code/Copilot):
   - (a) *Handshake replay.* A test sends that client's `initialize` request to the server, then `tools/list`, and checks both results. The request comes from an archived session of that client: the transcript #1820 archived for Codex, Gemini CLI and Copilot, and an archived harness run that registered the Calor MCP server for Claude Code. Where no archive holds the raw request, the fixture is built from the client's documented protocol version and capabilities, and the fixture file says so.
   - (b) *Schema lint.* A lint checks every tool's `inputSchema` against that client's documented schema rules. Each rule carries a link to its source, and a rule with no source is not added.
   - (c) *The build-test-verify call.* One test makes the single build-test-verify call (`calor_check` with `action: "loop"`, #1614) on a small fixture project after a replayed handshake. It runs once, not once per client: the call does not depend on the handshake, and the compiler test shard runs 29 to 30 minutes against a 40-minute cap.
   - (d) *Workflow arguments.* A test reads the `calor://workflows` resource and asserts, for every step that names a tool, that each key under `args` is accepted by that tool's `inputSchema` at the position the step gives it.

   No client session is run for this issue. The evidence that each real client lists the tools and gets a tool result is the transcript #1820 archived in 0.32, linked from the documentation; #1820 also records whether each client can list and read an MCP resource, and that is not decided again here. If a #1820 transcript does not show the tools listed and one tool call returning, a further session with that client is a paid agent run whenever the client calls a model. It is made only if the #1832 record lists it with one pinned model, a spend ceiling and the expected observation written beforehand; it runs after the replay test of (a) passes for that client, stops at the first invalid attempt, and reuses the #1820 script, extended to list the tools and make one tool call. Filing this issue does not authorise it. Otherwise the gap is documented as a limit.
```

2. In `## Change`, replace item 2 with:

```markdown
2. **Fix** what the lint and the workflow test find, or document it as a client limit. A fix to the `calor://workflows` text is made in `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Teaching/reference.json` and regenerated with `calor self-check docs --fix`. A fix to a tool schema states the tokens it adds and removes against the always-on MCP surface ratchet in `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/TokenBudgetTests.cs`, which had 100 tokens of headroom at 0.30.0. Where a schema fix does not fit under the ratchet, the incompatibility is documented as a client limit and this issue still closes.
```

3. In `## Change`, delete item 3 ("Supersede #673 ..."). #673 is closed in 0.31.

4. Insert a new section after `## Change`:

```markdown
## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- The server registers 19 tools (`src/Calor.Compiler/Mcp/McpMessageHandler.cs:48-92`), announces protocol version `2025-03-26` (`:14`), and handles `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `resources/list`, `resources/read`, `prompts/list`, `prompts/get`, `completion/complete` and `ping` (`:212-223`).
- Every test under `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/Mcp/` drives the handler or `McpServer` in-process (for example `McpServerTests.cs:68` and `:111`, `NativeMcpSurfaceTests.cs:48`). One test elsewhere starts `calor mcp` as a process, with a closed stdin and no handshake (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/ValidationLoopTests.cs:295-303`). No test starts or replays a real client. The pair harness sends its own scripted `initialize` (protocol version `2024-11-05`) and a `resources/read` on `calor://primer` (`bench/phase0-agent-native/harness-capture.py:640-659`), as benchmark plumbing.
- Two tool schemas use composition keywords at the top level, which is where client schema rules are most likely to differ: `calor_check` has `anyOf` with a `const` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Mcp/Tools/CheckTool.cs:121-124`), and `calor_file_write` has `allOf` with `if`/`then`/`else` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Mcp/Tools/FileWriteTool.cs:237-251`). Which clients reject or ignore them is not verified.
- The `calor://workflows` resource is generated from the `workflows.json` catalog in `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Teaching/reference.json` (`:2689`). Its five tasks use three pairs of tool and argument: `calor_compile` with `autoFix`, `calor_compile` with `includeEffectSummary`, and `calor_convert` with `includeEffects` (measured by listing the `args` keys in `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Teaching/Generated/workflows.json`). None is a top-level property of the named tool's input schema, and both schemas set `additionalProperties: false` at the top level (`src/Calor.Compiler/Mcp/Tools/CompileTool.cs:128`, `ConvertTool.cs:161`): `autoFix` is nested under `options` (`CompileTool.cs:50-89`), `includeEffectSummary` does not occur under `src/Calor.Compiler/Mcp/`, and `includeEffects` is a property of `calor_structure` only (`StructureTool.cs:70`). The test of item 1(d) therefore fails at HEAD. #1772 (0.31) corrects the text; if it has merged, the test passes as written and is the regression guard, and if not, the correction is made here under item 2. How the server answers such a call is not verified.
- The always-on MCP surface (the `tools/list` result plus the server instructions) measured 7,900 o200k tokens on 2026-11-20 against a ratchet of 8,000 (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/TokenBudgetTests.cs:65-71`; figure from that comment, not recomputed).
- `calor init` registers the server in a different place per client: `~/.claude.json` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Init/ClaudeInitializer.cs:95-97`), `.codex/config.toml` (`CodexInitializer.cs:47`), `.gemini/settings.json` (`GeminiInitializer.cs:50`) and `.vscode/mcp.json` (`GitHubCopilotInitializer.cs:50`). `docs/cli/mcp.md:213-231` documents the Claude Desktop and VS Code entries and mentions `calor init` for Claude and Gemini only.
- One client session other than Claude Code is on record: Codex CLI 0.144.6, 2026-07-22, Calor 0.7.0, in which Codex read `calor://primer` and called `calor_help` and `calor_compile` (`bench/phase0-agent-native/CODEX-SMOKE.md:26-27`).
- The compiler test shard runs 29 to 30 minutes against a 40-minute cap (`.github/workflows/test.yml:505-508`). `eng/test-manifest.json` pins `expectedTotal` per test project and `scripts/check_trx.py` enforces it in CI (`.github/workflows/test.yml:603`).
```

5. Replace `## Done when` with:

```markdown
## Done when

- For each of the four clients, a test under `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/Mcp/` replays that client's `initialize` fixture and asserts that `initialize` succeeds and that `tools/list` returns every registered tool (19 at HEAD). Each fixture file states whether it was taken from an archived session or built from the client's documentation.
- For each client, every tool `inputSchema` passes the lint of that client's sourced schema rules, or the failing tool and rule are listed in `docs/cli/mcp.md` as a client limit.
- One test makes a `calor_check` loop call after a replayed handshake and asserts a tool result with no protocol error.
- The workflow-argument test of item 1(d) passes: no step in `calor://workflows` passes an argument that its tool's `inputSchema` does not accept.
- These tests pass in the `tests (compiler)` shard of `.github/workflows/test.yml`, and `expectedTotal` for `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests.csproj` in `eng/test-manifest.json` is raised by the number of tests added.
- `TokenBudgetTests.AlwaysOnMcpSurface_FitsRatchet` passes with `McpSurfaceRatchet` not raised, and every pull request that changes a tool schema states the tokens it adds and removes.
- `docs/cli/mcp.md` "Client configuration" states, per client, the file `calor init` writes, a link to an archived transcript of a real session of that client, and every known limit. A client for which no transcript shows the tools listed and one tool call returning is listed as a limit with the reason.
```

6. Replace the closing line "Part of #1653." with:

```markdown
Part of #1653. Depends on #1820.
```

**Why**

The resource-read check left this issue because the `calor init` delivery decision (#1823) needs to know in 0.32 which clients can read `calor://primer`; it is #1820, and this issue reuses its transcripts instead of running its own client sessions. Item 3 goes because #673 is closed in 0.31, and the one check of #673 that is still wanted, that every workflow step argument exists in the tool's input schema, is re-homed here; at HEAD three such arguments do not. The done-when is rewritten because "in CI or a scripted check" did not say which. Item 2 gains the token statement because a schema change moves the always-on MCP surface, which sits 100 tokens under its ratchet.

issues.title: [0.33] Codex support — authored and validated BY Codex
issues.body:
**Current**

The body is one paragraph: ship a `.codex/` configuration that Codex itself authored, then smoke-test it by having Codex complete a benchmark pair with the generated configuration, including write-validation hooks if Codex supports them. Acceptance is "Codex-run smoke green; config documented; exemplar included". It has no labels, no baseline and no statement of what closes it if the hooks do not fire.

**Amendment**

Add the label `tests`. Keep the existing paragraph and append the following below it.

```markdown
## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- The configuration half is delivered. `calor init --ai codex` writes `AGENTS.md`, `.codex/config.toml` and `.codex/hooks.json` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Init/CodexInitializer.cs:31`, `:47`, `:58`). The hooks are Codex-native `PreToolUse` and `PostToolUse` entries that call `calor hook codex-write --phase pre` and `--phase post` (`:196-252`), and `docs/cli/init.md:197-245` documents them.
- The smoke half ran once and is recorded as FAILED: 2026-07-22, Codex CLI 0.144.6, model `gpt-5.6-sol`, Calor 0.7.0 (pre-0.30 syntax), pair `W1-001-temperature-converter`, Calor arm. Codex used the MCP server, built with 0 warnings and 0 errors and passed 24 held-out tests, but neither generated hook intercepted its writes: it added a `.cs` file with no denial and an invalid `.calr` file with no lint feedback (`bench/phase0-agent-native/CODEX-SMOKE.md:3-9`, `:13-18`, `:24-33`; sanitised evidence in `bench/phase0-agent-native/codex-smoke-709/evidence.json`).
- That record lists the reproduction steps (`CODEX-SMOKE.md:79-91`) and states what a green run must show: "both hook phases, MCP consumption, a successful build, and green held-out tests" (`:93-95`).
- The backstop for a write the hooks miss is `scripts/check-calor-first-diff.sh`, which CI runs in the `calor-first-guard` job (`.github/workflows/test.yml:53-76`).
- `AGENTS.md` points to `calor://primer` and does not contain the primer (`src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Templates/AGENTS.md.template:9`).
- Whether current Codex CLI versions run hooks on the file-change path is not verified. The last observation is CLI 0.144.6.

## Smoke run

One live run on a 0.33 commit that contains #1650 and #1651: the Codex driver from #1651, on the Calor side of one benchmark pair (a task under `bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs/` with a Calor and a C# starter and a shared held-out test suite), in the workspace `calor init --ai codex` writes. It follows the reproduction steps in `CODEX-SMOKE.md`: before the task, Codex is asked to add a `.cs` probe outside `tests/` and an invalid `.calr` probe. It is the first live run of that driver and needs no tooling of its own.

This is a paid agent run. It is made only if the record that #1832 produces lists a Codex smoke run under its Part C with a dated "Authorised" line; the Part A authorisation of the per-agent runs does not cover it. While #1832 is open and carries no line for this run, the issue is held and no run is made. The record fixes one pinned model and CLI version, a spend ceiling, and a reading for each outcome under "Done when". Before the live run, `--null-agent` (the harness applies the reference solution, with no model call) passes on the same pair and commit with the Codex driver. Stop without a further attempt if the ceiling is reached, the transcript reports a model other than the pin, or two consecutive attempts are invalid. Filing or keeping this issue does not authorise spend.

## Done when

The issue closes on exactly one of these. The first two are recorded as a new dated section in `bench/phase0-agent-native/CODEX-SMOKE.md` with sanitised evidence beside it.

- **Green.** The run shows all of: the pre-write hook denied the `.cs` probe; post-write lint feedback surfaced for the invalid `.calr` probe; Codex read the primer or called a Calor MCP tool; the build exits 0; the held-out tests pass.
- **Client limit.** MCP use, the build and the held-out tests pass, and one or both hook phases are still not observed. The section records non-interception as a limit of that Codex CLI version. `docs/cli/init.md` and `website/content/getting-started/codex-integration.mdx` name the version and say that `scripts/check-calor-first-diff.sh` in CI is the enforcement. The generated `AGENTS.md` does not say that hooks block writes.
- **Declined.** The #1832 record carries a "Declined" line for a Codex smoke run, or #1832 has closed without listing one. The issue is closed as not planned with that record linked, and the July 2026 verdict stands as the last observation.

A run in which MCP use, the build or the held-out tests fail is not a closing outcome: the defect is fixed or filed, and the run is repeated within the same ceiling.

"Exemplar included" in the original acceptance is replaced by the primer delivery default that #1823 sets and #1650 tests per agent; it is not decided here.

Part of #1653. Depends on #1832, #1650, #1651.
```

**Why**

The acceptance "smoke green" has already failed once on hooks, and nothing says what closes the issue when a client does not run hooks on its file-change path; the client-limit outcome does. The run is paid, so it needs a ceiling, abort triggers, a zero-cost pass, a pinned model and readings fixed in advance, and those are decided in #1832. The epic requires this issue closed, so a declined spend needs a closing outcome as well.

issues.title: [0.33] Gemini support — validated by Gemini
issues.body:
**Current**

The body is one paragraph that asks for the same pattern as #709: `GEMINI.md` and `gemini-settings.json` from the single source, validated by a Gemini-driven smoke task. Acceptance is "Gemini-run smoke green; in drift checks; exemplar included". It has no labels, no baseline and no statement of what closes it if no run is made.

**Amendment**

Add the label `tests`. Keep the existing paragraph and append the following below it.

```markdown
## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- `calor init --ai gemini` writes `GEMINI.md` and `.gemini/settings.json` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Init/GeminiInitializer.cs:28`, `:50`). The settings file holds the MCP server and two `BeforeTool` hooks on `write_file|replace`: `calor hook validate-write --format gemini` and `calor hook validate-ids --format gemini` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Templates/gemini-settings.json.template`). It installs no post-write hook.
- `GEMINI.md.template` is generated from `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Teaching/reference.json` (`src/Calor.Compiler/SelfCheck/ExemplarCompileChecker.cs:158-162`), `calor self-check docs` fails in CI when it drifts (`.github/workflows/test.yml:267`), and its tool and resource names are checked against the registry (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/McpRegistryValidationTests.cs:33-48`). `gemini-settings.json.template` is a hand-maintained file outside that generator; `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/GeminiInitializerTests.cs` covers what the initializer writes.
- No Gemini-driven run is recorded in the repository (searched `bench/`, `docs/` and `scripts/` for "gemini"; the matches are configuration, documentation and passing mentions).
- `GEMINI.md` points to `calor://primer` and does not contain the primer (`src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Templates/GEMINI.md.template:9`).
- `docs/cli/init.md:260` says Gemini CLI has supported hooks since its v0.26 release. Whether current Gemini CLI versions run `BeforeTool` hooks on every file write is not verified.

## Smoke run

One live run on a 0.33 commit that contains #1650 and #1651: the Gemini driver from #1651, on the Calor side of one benchmark pair (a task under `bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs/` with a Calor and a C# starter and a shared held-out test suite), in the workspace `calor init --ai gemini` writes. Before the task, Gemini is asked to create a `.cs` probe outside `tests/`, as the Codex smoke did (`bench/phase0-agent-native/CODEX-SMOKE.md:79-91`). It is the first live run of that driver and needs no tooling of its own.

This is a paid agent run. It is made only if the record that #1832 produces lists a Gemini smoke run under its Part C with a dated "Authorised" line; the Part A authorisation of the per-agent runs does not cover it. While #1832 is open and carries no line for this run, the issue is held and no run is made. The record fixes one pinned model and CLI version, a spend ceiling, and a reading for each outcome under "Done when". Before the live run, `--null-agent` (the harness applies the reference solution, with no model call) passes on the same pair and commit with the Gemini driver. Stop without a further attempt if the ceiling is reached, the transcript reports a model other than the pin, or two consecutive attempts are invalid. Filing or keeping this issue does not authorise spend.

## Done when

The issue closes on exactly one of these. The first two are recorded in a new file `bench/phase0-agent-native/GEMINI-SMOKE.md`, laid out like `CODEX-SMOKE.md`, with sanitised evidence beside it.

- **Green.** The run shows all of: the `BeforeTool` hook denied the `.cs` probe; Gemini read the primer or called a Calor MCP tool; the build exits 0; the held-out tests pass.
- **Client limit.** MCP use, the build and the held-out tests pass, and the hook did not deny the probe. The file records non-interception as a limit of that Gemini CLI version. `docs/cli/init.md` and `website/content/getting-started/gemini-integration.mdx` name the version and say that `scripts/check-calor-first-diff.sh` in CI is the enforcement. The generated `GEMINI.md` does not say that hooks block writes.
- **Declined.** The #1832 record carries a "Declined" line for a Gemini smoke run, or #1832 has closed without listing one. The issue is closed as not planned with that record linked, and `website/content/getting-started/gemini-integration.mdx` says that the generated setup has not been exercised by a Gemini-driven run.

A run in which MCP use, the build or the held-out tests fail is not a closing outcome: the defect is fixed or filed, and the run is repeated within the same ceiling.

Two parts of the original acceptance are met elsewhere. "In drift checks" already holds for `GEMINI.md`, and the per-agent test in #1650 covers the hook commands in `.gemini/settings.json`. "Exemplar included" is replaced by the primer delivery default that #1823 sets and #1650 tests per agent.

Part of #1653. Depends on #1832, #1650, #1651.
```

**Why**

No Gemini-driven run exists, so "smoke green" has never been attempted, and the acceptance does not say what a green run must show or what closes the issue if the hook does not fire or the spend is declined. The run is paid, so it needs a ceiling, abort triggers, a zero-cost pass, a pinned model and readings fixed in advance, and those are decided in #1832. "In drift checks" is already true for `GEMINI.md` and is covered for the settings file by the per-agent test in #1650.

issues.title: [0.33] Arm abstraction in the pair harness
issues.displaces: none: new capacity justified in body
issues.body:
## Change

Give `bench/phase0-agent-native/run-pair.sh` a declared arm type, so that a language is added by writing a definition and fixtures instead of editing the runner. An *arm* is one condition of an experiment. An *arm type* is the toolchain an arm runs on; today there are two, `calor` and `csharp`, and the runner knows both by name. Below, a bare `:NNN` is a line of that script, and file names without a directory are its siblings in `bench/phase0-agent-native/`.

This issue extends the arm definition that #1815 adds in 0.32 and leaves one mechanism, not two. After #1815, `--arm-config <key>` can resolve a JSON arm definition kept outside `pair.json`. Its `language` field is limited to `csharp` or `calor`, and the runner still decides the shims, the build command and the grader from that value. Here the value becomes the name of an arm type that is itself declared by a definition, and everything the runner decides from the language moves into that definition. Read what #1815 merged before starting; this paragraph describes its issue text.

The work may be delivered as up to three ordered pull requests (parts 1 and 2; part 3; parts 4 and 5). The issue closes when the done-when holds.

1. **Arm type definition.** One JSON definition per arm type, with any templates it names, kept beside the #1815 arm definitions and resolved by the same code path, not by a second lookup. An arm type applies to every run, so the `calor` and `csharp` definitions are read whether or not the source-selection option that gates the #1815 definitions is set. It declares what the runner hard-codes today:

   | Declared per arm | Hard-coded today |
   |---|---|
   | Starter and reference directory names | `run-pair.sh:385`; `harness-capture.py:754` |
   | Workspace project file | inline C# project (`:767-777`); `CalorArm.csproj.template` (`:485`, `:762`) |
   | Source globs for the edit hash and the final-source archive | `*.cs`, `*.calr`, minus `obj/` and `bin/` (`:110-118`, `:957`, `:1054`) |
   | Iteration shim (the wrapper on `PATH` that journals build and test calls) and the subcommands that count | `dotnet`; `build`, `test`, `run` (`:986`, `:1037`) |
   | Build command, also quoted to the agent | `dotnet build` (`:1079`, `:1275`, `:1294`, `:1470`; prompt `:1257`) |
   | Grader: run the held-out suite; return passed, failed and failed case names | xUnit project on `Src.dll` (`:780-807`); `dotnet test` (`:1080`, `:1438-1444`); count parsing (`:1082-1085`, `:403-405`) |
   | Preflight before any run | Calor config pin and canary (`:647-676`); none for C# |
   | Generated-file write block | `.g.cs` (`:919`) |
   | Patterns classifying the agent's own build calls | `harness-capture.py:119-121`, `:245-254` |

2. **Port `calor` and `csharp`** to arm type definitions with no change in behaviour. `:282` becomes "a definition exists for this arm type"; `harness-capture.py:1055` takes its `--arm` choices from the definitions, and `:781` stops treating every arm key other than `csharp` as Calor. Every arm definition #1815 committed, its test arm included, keeps resolving: its `language` value now names an arm type definition, and its own fields (project file, side files, starter location, catch channels) override or add to that type.
3. **Manifest.** A versioned successor to `task-spec-schema.json` lets a manifest list any defined arm type and record parity counts for it. Existing `pair.json` files are not edited.
4. **A test arm type that is not .NET**, under `bench/phase0-agent-native/tests/fixtures/`, in bash or python3 (both already required), with its own shim, build command and stub grader. A unittest runs it through `run-pair.sh --null-agent` (a zero-cost run: the reference solution is applied and no agent is called). For this arm type the run needs neither `dotnet` nor a built compiler, so the unittest is not skipped in CI.
5. **README.** An "Adding an arm type" section in the harness `README.md`, next to the arm-definition section #1815 wrote.

Leave the agent invocation alone (`claude` at `:1352-1353`, model pin at `:1325`): that is #1651's driver abstraction, which starts after this merges. The PP-W paths and registration files are not touched, and `run-bundle.sh` (`:143`) and `check-probe-pair.sh` (`:202`) keep their own arm checks. Rust is #1828; the process-level grader is #1830.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- `run-pair.sh` is 1,893 lines (`wc -l`); the table cites the lines read.
- `task-spec-schema.json` requires exactly a `csharp` and a `calor` arm (`:26`), the `dotnet-test` runner (`:20`) and parity counts for those two arms (`:57`). Nothing validates a manifest against it; only `README.md:12` and `:38` and one plan document mention it.
- `bench/phase0-agent-native/tests/test_initialized_workspace.py:454-456` asserts that the text of `run_agent()` equals its text at commit `89f298e99`, and the prompt sentence naming `dotnet build` is inside that function. `test_harness_capture.py:282` and `:1345`, in the same directory, assert literal lines of the script.
- CI runs the harness tests as `python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/phase0-agent-native/tests` (`.github/workflows/test.yml:124`, job `calor-first-guard` at `:53`). That job builds no compiler, so tests guarded by `HAVE_PRODUCT` (`test_harness_capture.py:66`) are skipped there. These Python tests are not counted in `eng/test-manifest.json`, which pins only .NET test projects. `run-pair.sh` calls `jq` and `shasum` throughout; that both are on the `ubuntu-latest` runner image is not verified, and if either is missing the pull request adds an install step to that job.
- At HEAD `--arm-config <key>` (`:196`, `:212`) resolves only against `arms[key]` of the pair's own `pair.json` (`:382`; `harness-capture.py:790-797`). The arm definition outside `pair.json` does not exist yet; #1815 adds it.
- #1766 to #1767 and #1815 change this script before this issue starts. Re-read it; the line numbers are HEAD's.

## Why

The runner binds an arm to .NET in every row of the table, so a third language needs a fork. #1815 moves the first few fields of an arm into a definition for a second C# configuration; #1651 abstracts the agent driver in the same script in this milestone; and #1710 needs three conditions in 0.37. Finishing the arm half first, as a behaviour-preserving change proven by a test arm type, lets all three build on one structure. This is new capacity and displaces nothing: it shortens #1651 and removes a restructure from #1710.

## Done when

- `run-pair.sh --arm <name>` runs for any arm type with a definition and exits 2, naming the definitions directory, for any other. The string `--arm must be calor|csharp` is gone from `run-pair.sh`.
- For `calor` and `csharp`, a `--null-agent` run of one pair gives the same `result.json` values before and after for the fields at `test_initialized_workspace.py:491-500`. This test needs a built Release compiler, so its local output is pasted in the pull request. It replaces the `run_agent()` text pin, and the pull request lists every other textual pin it changed.
- The tests #1815 added for its arm definitions pass with their assertions on `result.json` unchanged; the pull request lists any #1815 definition file it edited and why.

issues.title: [0.33] Language-neutral, process-level oracle for a small headroom task set
issues.displaces: none: new capacity justified in body
issues.body:
## Change

Build a held-out suite that grades any arm through a process boundary, and two tasks that use it. An *arm* is one condition of an experiment (here, a language). The *oracle* is the harness-side program that decides how many held-out cases a workspace passes. A task has *headroom* when some arm has measurably needed more than one iteration on it. Below, `run-pair.sh` is `bench/phase0-agent-native/run-pair.sh`, a bare `:NNN` is a line of it, and paths beginning `pairs/` are under `bench/phase0-agent-native/`.

1. **Vectors.** One arm-neutral `vectors.json` per task: named cases, each an ordered list of steps (operation, arguments, expected return value and, where the task writes files, expected file content). No test is written per arm.
2. **Runner.** A Python program under `bench/phase0-agent-native/` that starts the arm's adapter in a fresh process and temporary directory per case, sends the steps and makes every comparison itself. It fills the grader slot of the #1827 arm type definition with passed, failed and the failed case names. A crash, a timeout or malformed output fails the case.
3. **Adapters.** One fixed, harness-owned adapter per arm type maps the wire protocol onto the task's pinned public surface, as each pair's `tests/shims/TestShim.<arm>.cs` does today. It holds no expected value and stays outside the agent's workspace, like `heldout/` (`:725-727`). The wire format is one versioned document, parseable with each language's standard library alone (Rust's has no JSON parser), and it round-trips every byte in the vectors (the CSV cases contain quotes, commas, CR and LF).
4. **Tasks.** Two, derived from `N1-003-csv-row` and `W3-003-kv-journal`, with new ids, in a new subdirectory of `bench/phase0-agent-native/tasks/`. That directory holds only `ppw-redesign/` today, which this issue does not touch. Each task has a manifest for the #1827 schema, a `spec.md` with an arm-neutral public surface and a per-arm signature table, the vectors, and starters, references and adapters for `csharp` and `calor`. Calor sources are copied from `tests/TestData/ActiveSyntax/bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs/` as it stands when this issue starts. The vectors transcribe the existing xUnit cases one for one, with a committed mapping from test method to case id.
5. **Controls**, each a zero-cost run (`--null-agent`, which applies the reference solution and calls no agent): the reference passes every case; the unmodified starter fails; one C# variant per task that builds but is wrong fails the same cases under the oracle as under the existing xUnit suite.

Up to two more file-class tasks (`W3-001-audit-log`, `W3-002-config-store`) may be added, each labelled "headroom not measured" in its manifest and in every report that uses it. The label states the evidence: 3 runs per arm in July 2026, at or near one iteration (see Baseline). No reading in #1832 depends on them.

Post the two task ids on #1832 when they are fixed: its Rust part names them.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- Grading is xUnit only: `:780-807` generates a test project on the arm's `Src.dll`, binds through the pair's `tests/shims/TestShim.$ARM.cs` (`:782`) and parses `dotnet test` counts (`:1082-1085`).
- Per-arm test authorship is prohibited (`docs/plans/agent-native-strategy.md:130`, `bench/phase0-agent-native/README.md:28`). Per-arm shims are the permitted glue.
- Headroom has been measured on two pairs only. Iterations-to-green, Calor over C#, 30 runs per arm: `N1-003-csv-row` 2.50, `W3-003-kv-journal` 2.27, C# at 1.00 on both (`bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/e1a-attribution/VERDICT.md:15-16`; July 2026, pre-0.30 syntax, model pin `default`). The other three green-field pairs measured 1.0 at 3 runs per arm (`bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/hardness-check-001/VERDICT.md:7-10`).
- The two optional pairs were run once, at 3 runs per arm, in `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/feasibility-dry-001/` (2026-07-02): `iterationsToGreen` in the six Calor `result.json` files is 2, 1, 1 for `W3-001-audit-log` and 1, 1, 1 for `W3-002-config-store`, and 1 in all six C# files. One two-iteration run in three is not a measured penalty, and three runs do not establish the floor either, hence the label.
- The two suites have 20 and 17 cases (`grep -c '\[Fact\]'` on `pairs/N1-003-csv-row/tests/CsvRowHeldOutTests.cs` and `pairs/W3-003-kv-journal/tests/KvJournalHeldOutTests.cs`; neither uses `[InlineData]`). No file matching `bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs/*/tests/*.cs` uses `Assert.Throws`, so return values and file contents are all a vector must express.
- Both pairs have 0.30-syntax copies in the mirror (a starter and a reference each). `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/BenchCorpusCompilesTests.cs` discovers reference programs under `bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs` only (`:32-54`) and compiles each through the mirror (`:59-72`); it does not look under `tasks/`. Both `spec.md` files state the surface as static functions reached through `TestShim.cs` (`pairs/N1-003-csv-row/spec.md:50-54`, `pairs/W3-003-kv-journal/spec.md:42-46`); N1-003 names `List<string>`.
- `bench/phase0-agent-native/tasks/` exists and holds one subdirectory, `ppw-redesign/`.
- Determinism rule: five consecutive green runs against the reference, committed under `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/authoring-validation-*/` (`docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md:13`, `:52`).
- `eng/test-manifest.json` pins `expectedTotal` for `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests.csproj` at 22,559, and `scripts/check_trx.py` fails CI on a different count (`.github/workflows/test.yml:603`).

## Why

A Rust arm, and any 0.37 condition that is not a .NET assembly, cannot be graded by an xUnit project on `Src.dll`, and a second suite written for it would break the rule that keeps escaped bugs comparable across arms. One suite held as data and run through a process boundary keeps the rule, and #1709 asks for exactly that ("the same black-box oracle"). #1709 and #1710 reuse the runner, the wire protocol and the adapter pattern; their tasks come from #1708. The equivalence control is there because a reading taken with an oracle that grades differently from the suite it replaces would be a reading of the oracle. This is new capacity and displaces nothing: without it neither the Rust reading nor a non-.NET condition can be graded.

## Done when

- `run-pair.sh --null-agent` on each task passes every case for `csharp` and `calor` five times in a row; the log is committed under `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/authoring-validation-<name>/`. The same log holds one passing `--null-agent` run per task for `calor` with `--initialized-workspace`, the mode the Rust reading is proposed to use for its Calor arm.
- The starter-only and wrong-variant controls are unittests under `bench/phase0-agent-native/tests/`. For the wrong variant, the oracle's failed cases equal the xUnit suite's failed tests through the mapping. These need a built product and are skipped in CI, so their local output is pasted in the pull request.
- Every test method of the two source suites appears in the mapping (20 and 17 entries), checked by a unittest that needs no .NET.
- A unittest drives the runner against a stub adapter, with no .NET, for a pass, a wrong value, a crash, a timeout and malformed output, and runs in CI (`.github/workflows/test.yml:124`).
- The Calor references of the new tasks compile in CI: `BenchCorpusCompilesTests` discovery is extended to the new subdirectory, or an equivalent test is added, and `expectedTotal` in `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated for the added cases.
- `git diff --name-only <base> -- bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs bench/phase0-agent-native/tasks/ppw-redesign` prints nothing.
- The two task ids are posted on #1832.
