issues.title: [0.33] External anchor: published per-language agent results and what they do not show
issues.body:
## Change

Write `docs/plans/external-anchor-agent-results-by-language.md`: what published benchmarks report about coding agents per programming language, and what those reports cannot tell this project. Documentation only; no agent runs.

1. **Inclusion rule**, stated first. A number appears only if the author of the document read it in the primary source (paper, official leaderboard or official repository) while writing. Anything seen only in a search summary, a third-party post or a quoted abstract goes in a list headed "seen, not read at source", with no number.
2. **Source table.** Per primary source: citation with the version or date read; benchmark; task type; languages; agents and models; metric; per-language figures, each with its table, figure or page; whether Rust and C# both appear; whether they ran on the same harness, agent and model.
3. **Search log.** Date, queries, sources that could not be reached.
4. **What these results do not show.** At least: figures from different benchmarks are not comparable; whether any source runs Rust and C# on one harness with one agent and model ("yes" with the citation, or "none found"); issue-resolution rates are not authoring cost per accepted task, which is what #1831 measures; an explanation from training-corpus size predicts C# at or above Rust, so it cannot explain a Rust lead.
5. **What would confirm or retire Rust as the reference bar**, written as evidence conditions and not as a decision: a same-harness, same-model result with Rust at or above C#; one with Rust clearly below C# on success and cost; each outcome of the #1831 reading. Acting on them is the maintainer's call at a milestone close.

Link the document from the evidence ledger (`docs/benchmarking/evidence-ledger.md`, created by #1774) and from the paragraph of the plan of record (`docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md`, created by #1765) that names Rust as the maintainer's reference bar. Both files exist once 0.31 has closed.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- "Rust" appears in two tracked files (`git grep -Il -w Rust`): `docs/plans/agent-native-strategy.md:210`, which cites Rust editions as a precedent, and `website/src/components/landing/CompetitivePositioning.tsx:34`, a feature table in a component that no page mounts (`docs/cli/self-check.md:172`). Neither is a measurement. A case-insensitive search adds only `scripts/phase5_migrate_docs.py:52`, a list of code-fence language names.
- The strategy names its competitor as "agent-generated evidence in C#" (`docs/plans/agent-native-strategy.md:16`).
- The only open issue that mentions Rust is #1719, as a possible emission target (snapshot of 2026-11-23).
- Search leads, not verified and not to be copied into the document. When this issue was drafted (2026-11) four benchmarks were seen in search summaries only, because arxiv.org and swebench.com could not be reached: one of about 300 tasks over nine languages with Rust ranked first and no C#; one with Rust mostly in single digits; a Rust-specific one of 500 tasks with a best baseline near 21%; a C# one near 40% against about 70% for Python. They are probably SWE-bench Multilingual, Multi-SWE-bench, a Rust SWE-bench variant and SWE-Sharp-Bench; that identification is not verified either.

## Why

The plan of record names Rust as the maintainer's reference bar and states, as a hypothesis, that published agent results for Rust are mixed and that no same-harness Rust-versus-C# result is known. Nothing in the repository supports or contradicts that sentence: it rests on search summaries nobody read at source. It needs a document behind it before money is spent on a Rust reading, and #1832 cites that document for what the reading can and cannot add. Text only: it takes capacity from no other issue.

## Done when

- `docs/plans/external-anchor-agent-results-by-language.md` exists with the five sections. Every number has a citation with table, figure or page, and the "seen, not read at source" list contains no number.
- Section 4 answers "yes" or "none found" on a same-harness Rust-versus-C# result, with the search date.
- If no primary source could be reached, the document says so, contains no number and is still merged; #1832 then records that the external anchor is empty.
- `docs/benchmarking/evidence-ledger.md` and `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md` link to the document.
- `git diff --name-only <base>` lists only paths under `docs/`.

Part of epic #1817. Blocks #1832.

issues.title: [0.33] Rust fixtures and iteration shim for the oracle tasks, with a zero-cost pass
issues.body:
## Change

Add a `rust` arm for the #1830 tasks and show, without calling an agent, that it runs end to end. An *arm* is one condition of an experiment (here, a language). No agent run, paid or otherwise, is part of this issue. Below, `run-pair.sh`, `loop-telemetry.schema.json` and `validate-telemetry.sh` are in `bench/phase0-agent-native/`.

**This issue is conditional.**

| | |
|---|---|
| Gate | The Rust part (Part B) of the 0.33 paid-run record, `docs/plans/0.33-paid-run-registration.md`, which #1832 produces. Only that part is needed: the record's parts may be signed on different dates, and this issue does not wait for the others |
| Open | Part B carries a dated "Authorised" line; or Part B carries "Declined" and the record also carries a dated line keeping the Rust fixtures for the optional fourth condition of #1709 |
| Threshold | None: the gate is that decision |
| Held | Part B carries no decision line yet. The issue stays open and unstarted, and no Rust file is committed |
| Closed | Part B carries "Declined" with no line keeping the fixtures. Close this issue as not planned and link the record |

Steps when the gate is open:

1. **Arm type definition** for `rust`, in the format and location #1827 set. The iteration shim (the wrapper on `PATH` that journals build and test calls) wraps `cargo` and journals the subcommands that give compiler or test feedback: `build`, `check` and `clippy` as `build`, plus `test` and `run`, so the journal's `cmd` values are unchanged. Build command `cargo build --offline`. Source globs `*.rs`, minus `target/`. Grader: the #1830 runner with the Rust adapter.
2. **Toolchain.** One exact stable version in `rust-toolchain.toml`; standard library only, with an empty `[dependencies]` table and a committed `Cargo.lock`, so a build needs no network. A preflight exits 3 when `cargo` or `rustc` is missing or differs from the pin, and records both versions in `result.json`. `bench/phase0-agent-native/README.md` gains install steps. The agent isolation #1762 added admits the toolchain directories for this arm, and that issue's pre-flight canary (reading a reference directory must fail) is run for it.
3. **Fixtures** per #1830 task: a `rust/` starter, `reference/rust/` and the adapter, written from `spec.md` alone in idiomatic Rust, adding the Rust row to the spec's signature table. Declaration count and cyclomatic-complexity sum are within ±30% of the C# reference and recorded in the manifest.
4. **Zero-cost pass.** `run-pair.sh --arm rust --null-agent` (the reference solution is applied and no agent is called) on each task: the starter builds, the reference passes every case five consecutive times, and the starter-only control fails.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- No Rust source, manifest or toolchain file is tracked (`git ls-files | grep -iE '\.rs$|Cargo\.toml|rust-toolchain'` prints nothing).
- There is no harness image: no Dockerfile or devcontainer is tracked. The harness runs on the operator's machine, macOS or Linux (`run-pair.sh:998-999`), so installing the toolchain means a pin, a preflight and README steps.
- Preflight precedent: the Calor arm canary exits 3 before any spend (`run-pair.sh:647-676`).
- The journal's `cmd` field allows `build`, `test` and `run` only (`loop-telemetry.schema.json:16`).
- Authoring rules: fixtures written independently from the spec (`bench/phase0-agent-native/README.md:27`); parity within ±30% (`docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md:49`); five green runs, committed (`:13`, `:52`).
- No workflow under `.github/` mentions `cargo`, `rustc` or `rustup` (`grep -rni`), and the harness tests run in a job without a product build (`.github/workflows/test.yml:124`).

## Why

The Rust reading (#1831) needs an arm proven to work before money is spent: this program lost $38.75 to a void attempt caused by plumbing (`docs/plans/pp-w5-spend-authorisation.md:91`). It is also the first real non-.NET arm, so it tests #1827 and #1830 against more than a stub, and an optional fourth condition in #1709 would reuse it. The issue is conditional because its only certain consumer is the Rust reading: if the maintainer declines that reading and does not keep the fixtures for #1709, nothing reads them. The work is bounded to the #1830 tasks.

## Done when

One of the following.

- **Built.** All of:
  - The zero-cost log for every task (five green reference runs, the failing starter-only control, and a build with `CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true`) is committed under `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/authoring-validation-<name>/` with the `rustc` and `cargo` versions.
  - With `cargo` absent from `PATH`, `run-pair.sh --arm rust` exits 3 before creating a run directory; a unittest covers it.
  - A unittest with a stub `cargo` shows `check`, `clippy`, `build`, `test` and `run` each journaled once after an edit, and the journal passes `validate-telemetry.sh`.
  - Each manifest records parity counts within ±30%.
  - `python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/phase0-agent-native/tests` passes, and `git diff --name-only <base> -- bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs` prints nothing.
  - The issue links the Part B line that opened the gate.
- **Not planned.** Part B of the record reads "Declined" with no line keeping the fixtures; the issue links the record and is closed as not planned. `git ls-files | grep -iE '\.rs$|Cargo\.toml|rust-toolchain'` still prints nothing.

issues.title: [0.33] Decision: register and authorise the 0.33 paid runs — per-agent runs and the Rust reading
issues.body:
## Change

Take and record one maintainer decision in three parts: whether to pay for the per-agent runs (Part A), the Rust cost reading (Part B) and any other agent run in 0.33 (Part C), and on what terms fixed in advance. Two deliverables:

- `docs/plans/0.33-paid-run-registration.md` (below, "the record"), modelled on `docs/plans/pp-w5-spend-authorisation.md`, holding every field below and the decision lines;
- an additive registration in Annex A of `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md`: a new A.3 entry (the next free `A-1.N`) that names the record and states each signed part's fixed fields, with the `Annex version` pointer updated. No A.2 row is added, because no part registers a threshold. Merged entries cannot be edited, so a part signed later, or any later change, is a further A.3 entry. The pull request must not touch `scripts/check-annex-freeze.py` or its workflow.

Filing or closing this issue authorises no spend, and neither does the annex entry. Only a dated decision line in the record does. Paid runs are blocked by the record. Driver work (#1651) is not. This issue closes when every part has a decision line, but the issues it blocks do not wait for that: #1828 and #1831 are released by the Part B line alone, #1811 by the Part A line, and #709, #711 and #1835 by their own Part C lines.

Values marked "recommended" are this plan's proposal. The maintainer may change any before signing and none after the first paid run. The parts may be signed on different dates, and the Part A line may authorise some agents and decline others.

Terms. `run-pair.sh` and `run-epoch.sh` are in `bench/phase0-agent-native/`. An *arm* is one condition under test (here, a language). A *pair* is one task with a starter per arm and a shared held-out test suite. `--null-agent` applies the reference solution instead of calling an agent, at zero API cost. A run is *valid* when the harness did not mark it invalid (rate limit, API error, missing transcript, isolation violation) and *censored* when the held-out tests never all pass within the iteration budget. *Iterations-to-green* counts the build-or-test invocations that follow an edit until the held-out tests first all pass. *Cost per accepted task* is an arm's total cost over its valid runs divided by the number of those runs that pass every held-out case; *tokens per accepted task* is the same quotient on input plus output tokens. #1835 uses this definition.

**Part A: per-agent runs (#1811)**

| Field | Recommended |
|---|---|
| Agents | Codex, Gemini, Copilot; one CLI version and one model id per vendor, written verbatim once the #1651 driver for that agent exists |
| Copilot client | Named verbatim, product and version; by default the client the #1820 record checked. If no Copilot client can be driven without its editor, the registered outcome is "not measurable headlessly" and no Copilot run is made |
| Arms | `csharp` and `calor` per agent; the Calor workspace set up by `calor init` for that agent (#1650) at the #1823 default |
| Pairs | `N1-003-csv-row`, `W3-003-kv-journal`, and one pair that measured parity (`W1-002-usage-billing`, `W2-003-window-stats` or `W2-004-interval-clip`), named in the record |
| Measures | Within one agent only: the Calor-to-C# ratio of iterations-to-green and of tokens per accepted task, task success per arm, and the columns #1811 reports (the #1760 report script, the unknown-effect share from #1802, the primer-read rate). No ranking across agents |
| Cost | The CLI's own accounting where it reports one; otherwise tokens only, with the ceiling as a run count |

| Option | Runs | Cost if every run cost what Claude Code's July runs on the two penalised pairs cost | Ceiling |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 (recommended): 3 pairs, 5 runs per arm | 90 | $75 to $216 | $120 per vendor |
| A2: the five #1605 stage 1 pairs, 5 runs per arm | 150 | $125 to $360 | $200 per vendor |
| A3: decline | 0 | $0 | none |

A1 is recommended: the result is descriptive and within-agent, and three pairs cover the penalised and the parity case. Readings per agent are bands, not gates. The values are the Phase 1 rows of the unfrozen gates draft (`docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md:62-63`) and its censoring cap (`:39`):

- Calor success within 15 points of C#, iterations ratio at most 1.25: "supported at parity".
- Success within 15 points, ratio above 1.25: "supported at a cost"; published with the ratio, and the agent's most frequent diagnostics go to #1846.
- Success more than 15 points below C#: "not yet supported"; published as such, `calor init` text for that agent carries the caveat, and the failure classes go to #1846, which may add syntax and may not change a spelling.
- More than 40% censored runs in either arm, or tokens and turns not capturable: "not measured", with the reason.
- The Copilot client cannot be driven without its editor: "not measurable headlessly", with the reason.
- The primer (the syntax sheet served as `calor://primer`) is read in fewer valid Calor-arm runs than the delivery rule #1770 registered requires: "primer not delivered on this agent". The ratios are published under that label, and the finding goes to #1846. If #1770 registered no delivery rule (no stage 2), the primer-read rate is reported with no reading.

The ratio of tokens per accepted task is reported beside each reading with no band: the gates document records tokens and gates nothing on them (`docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md:41`), and no per-vendor cost baseline exists.

**Part B: the Rust cost reading (#1831)**

Statement fixed in advance: "This reading measures cost distance only: how far apart C#, Calor and Rust are in tokens and dollars per accepted task on two green-field tasks, with one agent and one model. It is not a benefit test. It is reported, not adjudicated, and no issue waits on its value."

| Field | Recommended |
|---|---|
| Agent and model | Claude Code; one model id, written verbatim and passed to the harness as its model pin (`CLAUDE_MODEL` at HEAD, `run-pair.sh:1325`) |
| Tasks | The two #1830 tasks, by id |
| Arms | `csharp`; `calor` as shipped, that is in the workspace `calor init` writes at the #1823 default (the harness's `--initialized-workspace` mode, in which the zero-cost pass is also run); `rust`. One epoch, runs interleaved |
| Primary measures | Tokens per accepted task and cost per accepted task, as defined above |
| Descriptive | Iterations-to-green; the first-build pass rate as #1760 defines it (the share of valid runs whose first edited build-or-test invocation exits 0) |
| Interval | Per task and per primary measure, the ratio of two arms' values with a 90% bootstrap interval, resampling runs within each arm |

| Option | Runs | Projected at July per-run means | Ceiling |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 (recommended): 10 per arm per task | 60 | $43 to $180 | $250 |
| B2: 5 per arm per task | 30 | $22 to $90 | $125 |
| B3: decline | 0 | $0 | none |

The projection brackets Rust between the C# mean and the Calor mean without an exemplar, because no Rust run exists. B1 is recommended on precision. If Rust runs vary as Calor did in July without an exemplar (standard deviation 30 to 32% of the mean, against 13 to 14% for C#), a normal approximation puts the 90% interval on a Rust-to-C# ratio at about ±25% with five runs per cell and about ±18% with ten. B2 could not separate a ratio closer to 1 than about 1.25.

Readings per task, on the Rust-to-C# ratio of cost per accepted task (the token ratio is reported beside it):

- Interval includes 1: "Rust equals C# at the floor on this task." The bars coincide here; Calor's distance to the bar is its distance to C#, already tracked by #1605 and #1645.
- Wholly above 1: "Rust costs more than C# here." C# is the nearer bar; the capability scorecard records the ratio.
- Wholly below 1: "Rust costs less than C# here." Recorded as a second distance; equipped C# stays the gating comparator.
- Calor against Rust is reported the same way, as a distance. No outcome is read as a safety benefit or deficit of any language.
- A cell with fewer than 80% valid runs, or an arm with no accepted run: "not measurable", no ratio.
- The two tasks disagree: "mixed", no pooled figure.

No figure is compared with #1605 or any other epoch (`docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md:12`).

**Part C: any other paid run in 0.33**

No other agent run is authorised unless the record lists it with its own decision line, one pinned model and CLI version, a ceiling, and a reading for each outcome. The authorisation of Part A does not cover any of them. Three are known:

| Item | Options | Recommended |
|---|---|---|
| Codex smoke run (#709) and Gemini smoke run (#711) | One live run each on the Calor side of one pair, read by the outcomes under that issue's "Done when"; or decline, and the issue closes as not planned | List both, each counted inside that vendor's Part A ceiling. If Part A is declined for the vendor, the smoke run's ceiling is the $16 per-run limit below |
| Example-bank measurement (#1835) | (a) the two-arm comparison that issue proposes: 40 Claude Code runs, ceiling $170, with its four readings; (b) observation only, inside the Part A Calor arms, at no added spend; (c) not measured | (b): the measurement gates nothing, and (a) adds a $170 ceiling to the milestone |

**Rules for every part**

- Zero-cost pass first: `--null-agent` green for every arm and task on the pinned commit.
- No Calor arm runs paid in a `calor init` workspace until a `calor check` that follows an edit is journalled as an iteration (item 5 of #1767, or the same change made under #1651 if #1767 was closed as not planned). Without it the Calor arm's iterations-to-green and first-build pass rate are undercounted against `dotnet build` and `cargo build`. `--null-agent` runs no `calor check`, so the evidence is a no-provider run on the pinned commit whose stub edits a `.calr` file and then runs `calor check`: its journal holds a record with `cmd: "check"` and `edited: true`.
- Ceilings are cumulative and enforced between runs from each run's realised cost. Retries of invalid runs (`run-pair.sh:58` allows two) and any void attempt count against the same ceiling. The recommended ceilings are 1.4 to 1.7 times the upper projections; a collection that reaches its ceiling stops, so a low ceiling costs runs and not money.
- Abort triggers, each stopping the collection with what exists reported as incomplete: the ceiling is reached; a transcript reports a model other than the pin; two consecutive invalid slots in one arm; one run costs more than $16 (twice the dearest of the 180 July runs, $7.97); an isolation violation under #1762.
- Before signing, the projections are recomputed from #1605's realised per-run costs on 0.30. If #1605 made no paid run, the July means stand and the record says so. If an upper projection exceeds its ceiling, runs are cut; a ceiling is raised only by a new decision line.
- Decision line: `Authorised: <date>, Part <A|B|C>, <agent or item>, option <id>, ceiling <amount>` or `Declined: <date>, Part <A|B|C>, <agent or item>, <reason>`.
- Decline. If Part A is declined for every agent, #1811 is closed as not planned and the 0.33 exit criterion on per-agent results is met by this record. If Part B is declined, #1831 is closed as not planned, the exit criterion on the Rust cost reference is met by this record, and #1828 is closed as not planned unless the record carries a dated line keeping the Rust fixtures for the optional fourth condition of #1709. A Part C item that is declined or not listed follows the decline branch of its own issue.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- July 2026 per-run means, pre-0.30 syntax, model pin `default`: C# $0.50 and $0.60; Calor $1.17 and $2.23 with an exemplar, $3.65 and $4.20 without (two pairs, 30 runs per cell). The 180 runs cost $370.52 and the dearest cost $7.97. Measured by summing `total_cost_usd` over `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/e1a-attribution/*/*/run-*/agent.json`; the spread figures are standard deviation over mean from the same files, and the pin is in `pins.json` beside them.
- Projections are arithmetic on those means, taking the lowest and the highest cell for each arm. Part A: 45 C# runs at $0.50 to $0.60 plus 45 Calor runs at $1.17 to $4.20 is $75 to $216; with 75 of each, $125 to $360. Part B: per task, one run of each arm costs $0.50 + $1.17 + $0.50 to $0.60 + $4.20 + $4.20, with Rust bracketed between the C# mean and the Calor mean without an exemplar; over two tasks that is $43 to $180 at ten runs and $22 to $90 at five.
- No per-run cost for Codex, Gemini or Copilot is recorded (`bench/phase0-agent-native/CODEX-SMOKE.md` has none). How each vendor's CLI reports cost is not verified. Parity for the three pairs named in Part A was measured at 3 runs per arm (`bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/hardness-check-001/VERDICT.md:7-10`).
- In `--initialized-workspace` mode the harness puts a `calor` wrapper on `PATH` that runs the CLI directly (`run-pair.sh:982-985`), so no `calor` invocation is journalled; the journal's `cmd` values are `build`, `test` and `run` (`bench/phase0-agent-native/loop-telemetry.schema.json:16`). A `--null-agent` run builds with `dotnet build` (`run-pair.sh:1275`, `:1294`).
- `run-pair.sh` has no spend limit outside the PP-W ticket path (`:251-254`, `:1368-1379`) and calls its timeout "NOT a provider spending guarantee" (`:1308`). `run-epoch.sh` has no stop rule. `result.json` carries tokens, not cost; cost is `total_cost_usd` in each run's `agent.json`.
- Recorded overruns: $92.83 realised against a $15 to $89 range (`docs/plans/pp-w5-spend-authorisation.md:18`, `:86`); $79.39 against an estimate under $20 (`bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/guarantees-probe-001/VERDICT.md:20-23`).
- The gates document's epoch ceiling is $1,500, provisional (`docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md:81`). Its metric definitions (`:33-43`) include no first-build pass rate; #1760 defines the one used here.
- Annex A of `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md` starts at `:100`; its version pointer (`:102`) reads A-1.12, the newest entry (`:349`). `scripts/check-annex-freeze.py` keeps existing A.2 rows and A.3 entries byte-identical, requires a new A.3 entry for any change to the annex, and requires the pointer to name the newest entry. It runs as the `annex-freeze` job (`.github/workflows/experiment-registry-tamper-check.yml:98`) from the base branch's copy of the script, and the job refuses a pull request that changes the annex together with the script or the workflow (`:134-146`). An annex registration does not authorise spend (`docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md:1694-1696`).

## Why

Two 0.33 exit criteria depend on paid runs, and no issue fixed their design or asked the maintainer for the money. Rules 4 and 8 of the plan of record (`docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md`) require every paid run to have a ceiling, abort triggers, a zero-cost pass, one pinned model and a reading written in advance, and require spend authorisation to be a maintainer decision with its options written out. The Rust part is fixed as "cost distance only" because C# was at one iteration on both tasks in July, so a Rust arm can show only where it sits on cost. The record is registered in Annex A because that is the one place CI keeps a registration from being edited after the fact.

## Done when

- The record exists with every field of Parts A to C filled, nothing still marked "recommended", and the recomputed projections with the command that produced them (or the statement that #1605 made no paid run and the July means stand).
- For every authorised part whose Calor arm runs in a `calor init` workspace, the record links the no-provider run that shows the `cmd: "check"` record.
- Each part carries a dated decision line from the maintainer; Part A has one per agent and Part C one per listed item.
- The Annex A entry for each signed part is merged in a pull request on which the `annex-freeze` job passed. No existing row or entry changed.
- Part B cites `docs/plans/external-anchor-agent-results-by-language.md` (#1829) and names the two #1830 task ids.
- No epoch directory for a 0.33 paid run has a `startedAt` in its `pins.json` earlier than the date of the decision line that covers it.
- #1811, #1828, #1831, #709, #711 and #1835 link to the record.
- For a declined part, the issues named under "Decline" are closed as not planned, each linking the record.

## Not in scope

- Running anything: #1811, #1831, #709, #711 and #1835.
- The 0.31, 0.32 and 0.37 registrations (#1770, #1816, #1867), which append to the same annex.
- Any threshold that holds or releases another issue. Every reading here is reported, and Rust is never a gating comparator.

Part of epic #1817. Depends on #1829, #1605, #1830. Blocks #1828, #1831, #1811, #709, #711.

issues.title: [0.33] Run and report the Rust cost reading
issues.body:
## Change

Run the Rust cost reading registered in Part B of `docs/plans/0.33-paid-run-registration.md` (below, "the record"; #1832 produces it) and report it. Filing this issue does not authorise spend. The spend ceiling, the abort triggers, the one pinned model and the reading for each outcome are those in the record; this issue changes none of them. As proposed there: at most $250 for 60 runs on one pinned model, a zero-cost pass first, and a reading fixed in advance for each outcome, including "Rust equals C# at the floor". Scripts named below are in `bench/phase0-agent-native/`.

Terms. An *arm* is one condition under test; here the three arms are the languages C#, Calor and Rust. An *epoch* is one complete collection: all arms, one pinned model, runs interleaved. `--null-agent` applies the reference solution instead of calling an agent, at zero API cost. A run is *valid* when the harness did not mark it invalid (rate limit, API error, missing transcript, isolation violation). *Cost per accepted task* is an arm's total cost over its valid runs divided by the number of those runs that pass every held-out case.

**This issue is conditional.**

| | |
|---|---|
| Gate | Part B of the record. It has no numeric threshold: it is the maintainer's decision |
| Open | Part B carries a dated "Authorised" line with a ceiling |
| Held | Part B carries no decision line. The issue stays open and unstarted and no run is made. 0.33 cannot exit on its Rust criterion until the maintainer signs one of the two lines |
| Closed | Part B carries "Declined", or an entry criterion below is still unmet at the close of 0.33. Close this issue as not planned and link the record, which states the reason; the capability scorecard row reads "Rust: not measured" with that link |
| Entry criteria once open, checked on the pinned commit | Every arm passes the zero-cost pass on every registered task in its registered configuration; the starter-only control fails for every arm; the isolation canary from #1762 passes for the `rust` arm; if the registered Calor arm runs in a `calor init` workspace, the record links the no-provider run showing that a `calor check` after an edit is journalled as an iteration; `docs/plans/external-anchor-agent-results-by-language.md` (#1829) is merged |
| Threshold on the result | None: the reading holds or releases nothing |

Steps when the gate is open:

1. **Before any paid run**, commit two things and append the commit hash to the record. Neither changes after the first paid run.
   - The epoch driver. #1815 added a driver that, by its issue text, takes a pair list, an ordered list of arm keys and a run count, interleaves one run per arm, refuses a live run without a confirmation flag, writes `pins.json`, and stops on `--spend-ceiling` or `--run-cost-limit`; read what merged. Extend it to take the #1830 tasks and the `rust` arm, and to stop on the other registered triggers (a transcript reporting a model other than the pin; two consecutive invalid slots in one arm; an isolation violation). Do not write a second driver.
   - The analysis script for the registered measures and intervals, written without sight of any result and tested on a fixture epoch.
2. **Zero-cost pass** on the pinned commit: the driver with `--null-agent` for every arm and task, archived under `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/<epoch-id>-null/`.
3. **Paid runs**: `csharp`, `calor` and `rust` in one epoch, graded by the #1830 oracle, with the registered run count, model, ceiling and triggers.
4. **Report** in `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/<epoch-id>/REPORT.md` (not `VERDICT.md`: nothing is adjudicated): pins, commands, authorised ceiling against realised spend, every run including invalid ones, the registered measures per task and arm, and the registered reading that applies, quoted. It states that the figures are not comparable with #1605 or any other epoch. If an abort trigger fired, it names the trigger and reports the collection as incomplete.
5. **Publish and record**:
   - a section in the 0.33 release notes (`CHANGELOG.md`), under the statement the record fixed in advance ("cost distance only");
   - a row in the evidence ledger (`docs/benchmarking/evidence-ledger.md`, created by #1774);
   - the "Cost per accepted task" row of the capability scorecard in the plan of record (`docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md`, created by #1765), with the three values and the epoch id;
   - realised spend appended to the record.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- `run-epoch.sh` cannot run this epoch: it walks `pairs/*/pair.json` only (`:49`), runs all of one arm's runs before the next arm's (`:58-66`) and has no stop rule. Interleaving exists in `run-m5-epoch.sh:246-251` and a confirmation flag for paid epochs in `run-ppe1-epoch.sh:134-139`. The driver named in step 1 does not exist at HEAD; #1815 adds it for the nine seeded-defect pairs.
- Cost is `total_cost_usd` in each run's `agent.json`; `result.json` has tokens only. `pins.json` records `startedAt` (`run-epoch.sh:36-47`).
- Comparisons are valid only between arms run together on one pinned model within one epoch (`docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md:12`).
- Precedent for committing protocol and analysis before the first live run: `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/e1a-attribution/VERDICT.md:4-8`, `docs/plans/pp-w5-spend-authorisation.md:70`.
- The evidence ledger and the plan of record do not exist at HEAD; #1774 and #1765 create them. No Rust file and no Rust measurement is in the repository (`git ls-files | grep -iE '\.rs$|Cargo\.toml'` prints nothing).

## Why

The maintainer's bar is Rust, and nothing says where that bar sits on authoring cost in this harness. One reading on two tasks answers a narrow question: does Rust sit at the C# floor on cost, or elsewhere. It cannot show a Calor benefit, which is why it is reported and not adjudicated, and why C# and Calor run in the same epoch on the same oracle instead of being read across from #1605. The issue is conditional because the spend is the maintainer's to authorise; if the gate closes, the issue takes no capacity.

## Done when

One of the following.

- **Run.** All of:
  - The epoch directory and its `-null` companion are committed under `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/`.
  - `REPORT.md` has the items in step 4. Realised spend exceeds the ceiling by no more than the cost of the one run in flight when the stop fired; if an abort trigger fired, the report names it and marks the collection incomplete.
  - The commit recorded in step 1 predates `startedAt` in the paid epoch's `pins.json`.
  - The 0.33 section of `CHANGELOG.md`, the evidence ledger row and the scorecard row are merged, and the record shows realised spend.
- **Dropped.** The issue is closed as not planned and links the record, which states the reason (the "Declined" line, or which entry criterion failed), and the scorecard row reads "Rust: not measured" with a link to the record. No paid run was made.

Either outcome meets the 0.33 exit criterion "Rust cost reference reported, or the decision not to run it recorded with the reason".

## Not in scope

- Changing a reading, the run count or the ceiling. A second collection needs a new decision line in the record.
- Comparing any figure with #1605, the per-agent runs (#1811) or another epoch.
- Rust as a gating comparator, or any claim about safety or defects from this reading.

Part of epic #1817. Depends on #1828, #1832.

issues.title: [0.33] calor test and calor check discover tests written in .calr, with one teaching example
issues.displaces: none: new capacity justified in body
issues.body:
## Change

Make `.calr` files in the top-level `tests/` folder of a target directory test sources for `calor test`, `calor check` and the MCP tool `calor_check` (action `loop`), and teach the form with one compiled example. Two ordered pull requests are acceptable: the runners (items 1 to 4), then the teaching text (items 5 to 7).

**Before starting: the edition.** The edition is the set of spellings and default-on errors that the project promises not to break; #1805 declares it at the end of 0.32. This issue lands after that and changes what a file location means: a top-level `tests/*.calr` file is library source today and becomes a test source. Read the wording on tool layout in `docs/plans/0.32-edition-declaration.md`.

- It places tool-layout changes outside the promise (the wording the plan recommends there), or the declaration was deferred: proceed. The change is listed in `CHANGELOG.md` and in the re-affirmation record (#1846).
- It covers them: do not start. Quote the wording on this issue. The maintainer then decides between two options and records the choice on this issue and in the declaration record. An exception for this change costs one weakening of the promise. Discovery only for projects that opt in costs a switch that agents must be taught, whose spelling is then chosen in this issue. The plan recommends the exception, because an opt-in leaves the default at "tests cannot be written in Calor", the gap this issue closes. Until a choice is recorded the issue is held. While it is held, the 0.33 exit criterion that names it is met only by a record: a dated entry in the declaration record or in the re-affirmation record (#1846) that states the hold and what the 0.33 release does (ships without `.calr` tests, or waits).

1. **Discovery and build.** In `src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/TestCommand.cs`, `FindTestFiles` also returns top-level `tests/*.calr`. `ExecutionWorkspace.ResolveSources` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/ExecutionWorkspace.cs`) stops returning those files as library sources. They are compiled in the same Calor compilation as the library sources, so cross-module calls bind, and their generated C# is written into the generated test project (`WriteTestProject`), not into the library project `CalorSrc`. Three callers change: `Execute` (`calor test`), `RunLoopAsync` (`calor check`, `calor_check`) and `calor run`, which shares `ResolveSources` through `ExecutionWorkspace.Prepare` and must leave test files out of the program it builds. The generated test project has to build generated C#: today it enables implicit usings and has no reference to `Calor.Runtime`, unlike the library project. A directory may mix `.cs` and `.calr` tests. Subdirectories of `tests/` keep today's behaviour: `.calr` files there stay library sources and `.cs` files there are not discovered.
2. **Test form.** Use forms that already parse: a class whose test functions carry an xUnit attribute after the function name. The shape below is assembled from forms that parse and has not been compiled (`MathUtil` stands for the module under test); the example this issue ships is the authority.

   ```calor
   module MathTests
     using Xunit
     class MathTests
       func Sum [@Fact] public () → void
         ! unknown
         Assert.Equal(5, MathUtil.Add(2, 3))
   ```

   Add syntax only if these forms cannot express a passing test. A new form must be additive (no program that compiles today stops compiling, so no new reserved word). Its spelling is chosen under the amended fewest-tokens rule (#1785, the first section of `docs/design/0.32-breaking-window.md`) and recorded in the pull request.
3. **Effects in tests.** Record in the pull request how a test body satisfies effect checking: (a) the test framework's assembly reaches the binder and its assertion members get rows in a shipped manifest, or (b) test functions declare `! unknown`. The plan recommends (a) for each member that has a sound row. Under the convention the framework manifests state (`src/Calor.Compiler/Manifests/bcl-framework-interfaces.calor-effects.json:3`), a member that runs user-supplied code is `unknown`, and an assertion that calls `Equals` on its arguments does, so (b) may be the outcome for most members. Test files get no relaxed policy of their own: they are compiled with the options of the library sources in the same run (`UnknownCallPolicy.Strict` in `calor check`; strict in `calor test` unless `--permissive` is passed). Under (b), state in the pull request whether rows in `tests/*.calr` count toward the unknown-effect share that #1802 reports for agent runs.
4. **Text that names the layout.** Update both "No tests found" messages (`TestCommand.cs:242`, `:381-382`), the two `path` argument descriptions (`:38`, `:57`), the `path` description in `src/Calor.Compiler/Mcp/Tools/CheckTool.cs:45`, `docs/cli/index.md:67-68` and `website/content/cli/test.mdx:13-14` and `:35-37`. The `CheckTool` description is part of the always-on MCP surface that `TokenBudgetTests` ratchets.
5. **Teaching example.** Add one complete program for the test form and link it from a construct entry whose `keywords` include `test`, so that `calor_help` returns it for the query `test`. If part 1 of #1835 has merged, store it in the bank store that issue created, which is not rendered into the reference. Otherwise add it to `programs` in `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Teaching/reference.json`, update the count pinned in `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/AgentTaskReferenceTests.cs` (87 at HEAD) and the id pin #1745 added, and state the tokens it adds to the full reference. If it does not fit under `FullReferenceRatchet` as #1734 left it, give it the not-rendered marking of decision 5c of #1823, adding the marking here if #1734 has not. In either store the program carries the field #1745 defines: an expectation, or "cannot run" with its reason. Regenerate the mirrors with `calor self-check docs --fix`; do not edit generated files. `calor self-check docs` compiles every program in `programs` and validates its generated C# against the host's platform assemblies and `Calor.Runtime`, and xUnit is not among them. Record in the pull request how the example gets through the compile check of its store: the reference set gains the test framework, or the block is exempted. Whatever is chosen, the test under Done when compiles and runs the example in CI.
6. **Agent text.** #1809 rewrites Rule 1 in `agentInstructions` and adds one primer line that says tests are xUnit C# files in `tests/` (both in `reference.json`). Change both so they say a test may be a `.cs` or a `.calr` file. State tokens added and removed against `TokenBudgetTests`. Raise no budget constant; if a sentence cannot change inside the budget in force, leave it and rely on `calor_help` and the "No tests found" message.
7. **Per-agent tests.** #1650 tests what `calor init` writes for each agent, with one case that adds a test file under `tests/` in an initialized project and expects `calor check` to run it. If #1650 has merged, add a `.calr` test to that case. If it has not, post a comment on #1650 that links this issue's merged pull request and names the fixture to reuse; #1650 then adds the case.

New product code goes into existing files: `scripts/check-calor-first-diff.sh` rejects new `.cs` files outside `tests/`, `bench/` and `tools/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness/`.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- `FindTestFiles` returns only top-level `tests/*.cs` plus `tests/shims/TestShim.calor.cs` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/TestCommand.cs:404-431`). With none, both commands exit 3 (`:31`, `:240-242`, `:380-383`).
- `ResolveSources` enumerates `*.calr` recursively and excludes only `bin/`, `obj/` and `reference/` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/ExecutionWorkspace.cs:189`, `:222-231`). A `tests/*.calr` file is therefore compiled into `CalorSrc` and never run as a test. `calor run` resolves its sources through the same function (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/RunCommand.cs:38`, `ExecutionWorkspace.cs:132-136`).
- No `.calr` file in the repository has `tests` as its parent directory (checked with `find`), so no fixture or benchmark pair changes meaning.
- The generated test project references xUnit 2.9.2 and `CalorSrc`, and enables implicit usings (`TestCommand.cs:444-465`). The library project disables implicit usings and references `Calor.Runtime.dll` by path (`ExecutionWorkspace.cs:304-327`).
- In an MSBuild project, `Calor.Sdk` compiles every `**/*.calr` file under the project folder (`src/Calor.Sdk/Sdk/Sdk.props:19`). This issue does not change that.
- An attribute after a function name parses: `func Post [@HttpPost] public () → void` (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/AttributeConversionTests.cs:402`). No file in the repository writes `[@Fact` or `[@Theory` (searched `*.calr`, `*.cs`, `*.md`, `*.mdx`, `*.json`).
- Neither command accepts an assembly reference (`ExecutionWorkspace.cs:56-123`, `TestCommand.cs:55-68`). A dotted name that does not resolve is charged `unknown` (`CHANGELOG.md:67`), and a public function must declare its own row (`docs/syntax-reference/effects.md:70-72`). A Calor test would therefore need `! unknown` today. Not verified by compiling: no .NET SDK was available when this was written.
- The write hook allows any `.calr` path (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/HookCommand.cs:277-281`).
- A C# test has to call names the emitter invents: the fixture test calls `MathUtil.MathUtilModule.Add(2, 3)` for a function the source declares as `Add` in `module MathUtil MathUtil block` (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/ValidationLoopTests.cs:22-43`).
- The strategy planned a test construct as additive work (`docs/plans/agent-native-strategy.md:145`, `:183`). None exists, and `test` is not in the keyword table (`src/Calor.Compiler/Parsing/Lexer.cs:22`).
- `calor_help` ranks constructs by their `keywords` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Mcp/Tools/HelpTool.cs:225-231`). No construct in `reference.json` has a keyword containing `test`, and none of its 87 programs has `test` in its id or title (checked with a JSON reader). A test pins the count at 87 (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/AgentTaskReferenceTests.cs:25`).
- The self-check compiles each reference program to C# and then validates that C# against the host's platform assemblies plus `Calor.Runtime` (`src/Calor.Compiler/SelfCheck/ExemplarCompileChecker.cs:236-287`, `:451-480`; the reference set is described at `:482-488`). The compiler project has no xUnit reference. A `drift:ignore` marker before a fenced block exempts it (`:240-245`); whether a `programs` entry can carry that marker is not verified.
- Budgets, o200k proxy tokenizer, measured 2026-11-20: template 317 plus server instructions 275 is 592 of 600; primer 1,569 of 1,600; full reference 16,750 of 17,000; always-on MCP surface 7,900 of 8,000 (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/TokenBudgetTests.cs:41-47`, `:49-54`, `:57-63`, `:65-71`). #1823 may change these constants before this issue starts.
- Existing coverage: `ValidationLoopTests.cs` (`calor check`, CLI and MCP) and `RunTestCommandTests.cs` (`calor run`, `calor test`), both in the `tests (compiler)` shard of `.github/workflows/test.yml`. Run them with `dotnet test tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ValidationLoopTests|FullyQualifiedName~RunTestCommandTests"`.

## Why

An agent told to write Calor has to change language to test it, and the C# it writes must reach generated container names it never wrote, such as `MathUtilModule` above. The capability scorecard in the plan of record (`docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md`, section 3) has the line "Tests written in the language". #1809 answers it only with "C# test files are allowed". This issue makes the answer yes, and the 0.33 exit criterion "calor test and calor check discover tests written in .calr" names it.

It is new capacity and displaces nothing: no open issue covers test authoring. It lands after the edition declaration, so it changes no existing spelling and adds one only if the existing forms cannot express a test.

## Done when

- New cases in `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/ValidationLoopTests.cs`, each run through the CLI and through `calor_check` as the existing theories are:
  - a directory with one `.calr` source, one `tests/*.calr` test and no `.cs` file exits 0 with `testsRun` at least 1;
  - a failing Calor test exits non-zero and its name appears in `failures` under stage `test`;
  - a directory with one `.cs` and one `.calr` test reports both in `testsRun`.
- Cases in `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/RunTestCommandTests.cs`: `calor test <dir>` exits 0 on the `.calr`-only fixture, and `calor run <dir>` on a directory with a `Main` and a `tests/*.calr` file runs the program without compiling the test file into it.
- A test shows that a top-level `tests/*.calr` file is absent from the units written to `CalorSrc`, and that a `.calr` file in a subdirectory of `tests/` is still among them.
- `NoTestFiles_ReturnsDistinctExitThree` still passes, and both messages name `tests/*.cs` and `tests/*.calr`.
- The teaching example is in the store item 5 names. It carries the #1745 field, and the pinned program count and id list are updated if `programs` changed. A test calls `calor_help` with query `test` and receives it. `calor self-check docs` exits 0 (CI step at `.github/workflows/test.yml:267`). A test lays the example out as a directory with the module it tests and gets exit 0 from the check loop.
- `TokenBudgetTests` passes with no constant changed; an example that does not fit the full reference is stored or marked as item 5 says. The pull request states tokens added and removed for the full reference, the primer, template plus server instructions, and the MCP surface.
- The pull request records the edition wording that was read, the choice made in item 3, where the example is stored and how the self-check handles it (item 5) and, if a form was added under item 2, its spelling with the token counts the amended rule requires.
- `docs/cli/index.md` and `website/content/cli/test.mdx` describe the layout, including that `dotnet build` in a `Calor.Sdk` project still compiles `tests/*.calr` into that project. `CHANGELOG.md` records the change, including that top-level `.calr` files under `tests/` are no longer part of the library or of `calor run`.
- The existing compiler tests pass with no edit to an existing fixture, and `expectedTotal` for `Calor.Compiler.Tests` in `eng/test-manifest.json` (`:8`) rises by exactly the tests added.
- Item 7 is done: the #1650 case carries a `.calr` test, or the comment on #1650 exists.

## Not in scope

- Allowing C# test files (#1809).
- `dotnet build` and `dotnet test` in an MSBuild project. Only the project-less runners change. There `dotnet build` compiles `tests/*.calr` into the product project, where xUnit is not referenced, so a project can pass `calor check` and fail `dotnet build`; no issue covers this, and epic #1819 lists it as a follow-up.
- Access from tests to internal members of the library. The generated projects grant none today, and that is unchanged.
- Generating tests from contracts, and property-based testing.

Part of epic #1819. Depends on #1809. Blocks #1846.

issues.title: [0.33] Incremental build: the remaining reuse tier
issues.body:
## Change

This issue is conditional. It does work only where #1818 measured a warm edit over its budget. It has three independent steps, and the gate says which are taken. A body-only edit changes statements inside a function and nothing in any declaration header. A file's companions are the other source files compiled with it.

**Gate.** #1818 publishes a latency record (`bench/phase0-agent-native/latency/ml1-004/VERDICT.md`), posts its figures as a comment on this issue, and checks in a budget file (it proposes `eng/latency-budgets.json`) that marks each quantity within or over and names the issue that owns an overrun. Four of its quantities gate this issue. For (a) to (c) the record also gives the Calor files compiled and skipped. #1818 times (a) and (b) on its project copy P1 (the fixture plus one unrelated module) and (c) on P2 (P1 plus a base and a derived class file). Each is a median of five runs, read against the budget the maintainer set under #1818, which recommends 1 s for each.

| Quantity | What is timed |
|---|---|
| (a) | `CompileCalor` task time in `dotnet build` after a body-only edit to a module that no other file names |
| (b) | The same after a body-only edit to a function that another file calls |
| (c) | The same after a body-only edit to a method of a base class that a class in another file extends |
| (d) | The in-process segment (compile and verification) of `calor check` after a one-file body edit, on the 106-file latency fixture (`tests/TestData/ActiveSyntax/bench/phase0-agent-native/latency/fixture-10k/src`) with one test file |

Before any code, post a sizing comment that quotes the four figures and their budgets and marks each within, over or not measurable. The times of (a) to (c) cannot choose between steps 1 and 2 by themselves: on the fixture, (a) and (b) are expected to recompile almost the same set (the edited file plus every file that names another module, which is `main.calr` and the 35 L1 and 35 L2 files), and (c) recompiles every file because P2 declares an instance class. So for each of (a) to (c) that is over, the comment also gives:

- C, the Calor files the timed build compiled (from the record);
- A, the size of the edit's affected set as step 1 defines it, computed over the project the row was timed on. For (c), state whether step 1 as designed can spare a file while another module declares an instance class; if it cannot, A equals C;
- the projected step 1 time, the measured task time × A / C. It assumes task time is proportional to files compiled and is used only to choose the step.

The comment then names the outcome:

- All four within budget: close this issue as not planned and link the record. The tests that pin today's behaviour stay.
- One of (a) to (c) is over, and every over row's projection is within budget: step 1. The nightly job re-measures after it merges; a row still over then takes step 2.
- An over row's projection is over budget and its A is more than 1: step 2, which spares every unedited file on a body-only edit and so covers the other rows too. Step 1 is then a separate pull request, made only if the maintainer asks for it on this issue.
- An over row with C equal to 1: only the edited file compiled, no step here shortens it, and the comment says so.
- (d) over: step 3, whatever (a) to (c) read.
- A quantity that the record marks not measurable, or that the maintainer left without a budget, opens nothing, and no step is taken for it. If no other quantity is over, the issue stays open with a comment that names the missing figure and moves to the next milestone at the 0.33 close. It is closed as not planned only on measured figures.

Steps 1 and 2 extend the warm-build skip decision shared by `dotnet build`, `calor --cache` and `calor watch`. It lives in `CrossModuleCacheReuse` (`src/Calor.Compiler/CompilationDriver.cs`) and `CrossModuleTypeRegistry.CanReuseIndependentOutput` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Effects/CrossModuleTypeRegistry.cs`). The MSBuild task `CompileCalor` and the CLI driver must keep calling the same code. New code goes into existing files, because `scripts/check-calor-first-diff.sh` rejects new `.cs` files under `src/`.

**Step 1, affected set.** Today a cached output is checked against the names of every other module. Compute the affected set instead: the modules edited in this build plus, transitively, every file whose cached output names something an affected module declares. Reuse every file outside that set. An edit to one module then no longer recompiles a caller of a different module.

**Step 2, declaration surface.** Reuse every unedited file when, for every module edited in this build, all three hold: its declaration surface is unchanged (the declaration-only part of `CrossModuleTypeRegistry.Fingerprint`, plus the function map); no edited member's effect row is inferred from its body; and the per-file compile of a reused file is shown to read only companion declarations. Write the soundness argument as a comment beside the code, as #1732 did (`CrossModuleTypeRegistry.cs:249-274`). Signatures, declared rows and base lists are part of the surface; the tests under Done when pin them. For each of the following the argument states whether it is part of the surface or is proven unread by another file's compile: rows inferred for private and internal members, parameter refinements and postconditions, default argument values, constants, usings and namespace scopes, partial-type membership, and modules that hold preserved C# or preprocessor nodes.

**Step 3, reuse in `calor check`.** `calor check` and `calor_check` share no cache with the build. Let a run reuse the previous run's per-file compile results for files that the shared skip decision allows, with the decision as steps 1 and 2 leave it. Where the state is kept is the implementer's choice and is recorded in the pull request. Three constraints apply. A warm run returns the same result as a run with the state deleted, field for field apart from `durationMs`. A snapshot is still taken before compiling, so an edit during the run cannot change it. The documented guarantee that `check` does not repair source or modify project files still holds. The verification cache is switched off in this path today; the pull request either states why reusing proof outcomes is sound here or reuses compile results only. The `dotnet build` and `dotnet test` child processes are outside quantity (d) and are not changed.

**What #1732 passes on.** #1732 closes in 0.32 and points two leftovers here: its criterion 5, that the frozen edit script ES-04 is revisited "with the caller a cache hit again", and the clause of its criterion 3 that a cross-module `Calor0410` appears and disappears "while the caller is skipped". Neither step delivers them. ES-04 and the test that covers that shape edit the callee's declared row (`! db:w` to `! db:w, net`), a declared row is part of the declaration surface, and so the caller is recompiled. Sparing a caller on a row-only change is a further tier. It is not built here, has no issue and no milestone, and would have to replace the pinned test `CrossModuleViolation_AppearsAndDisappearsWithTheCalleeRow_OnBothSurfaces`; say so in the closing comment. After step 2 the explanation in ES-04's `reuseNote` (every callee edit rebuilds the caller) is no longer the whole rule. Draft an additive amendment to section 7 of F-3′ in `docs/plans/v0.13-freeze-registrations.md` in the pull request description. Applying it stays with the maintainer.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- #1732 shipped in 0.30.0: one decision for the CLI and the task (`src/Calor.Compiler/CompilationDriver.cs:291-417`; called at `:588` and `src/Calor.Tasks/CompileCalor.cs:635`). `CHANGELOG.md:188` describes it. The older statement at `CHANGELOG.md:354-359` is stale.
- A cached output is reused only if it names nothing that any other module declares, edited or not (`src/Calor.Compiler/Effects/CrossModuleTypeRegistry.cs:198-233`). The proof fails for every file when any module holds a non-native node such as preserved C# (`:204`, `:341-345`). It fails for a file when any other file declares an instance class, an interface, or anything else that is not a plain static method in a static class (`:299-326`).
- Pinned consequences. Editing a bystander recompiles a caller that never calls it, and a body-only edit to a callee recompiles its caller (rows `bystander-body` and `library-body`, `tests/Calor.Tasks.Tests/IncrementalSurfaceAgreementTests.cs:82-88`). A body-only edit to a base class recompiles the derived class (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/CrossModuleVarianceTests.cs:1149-1182`).
- The maintainer chose this behaviour for 0.30 and recorded steps 1 and 2 as follow-up (`docs/plans/2026-11-16-milestone-0.30-ci-triage.md:374-384`). No issue was filed for them.
- `Fingerprint` hashes type declarations (`CrossModuleTypeRegistry.cs:45-74`) and then every source's content hash (`:75-78`).
- ES-04 edits the callee's declared row and never its body (`tests/TestData/ActiveSyntax/tests/TestData/EditScripts/ES-04-cross-module-effect/`, the three `callee.calr` files). Its amended `reuseNote` and the reason are section 7 of F-3′ (`docs/plans/v0.13-freeze-registrations.md:563`). `CrossModuleViolation_AppearsAndDisappearsWithTheCalleeRow_OnBothSurfaces` asserts that the caller is compiled when the callee's row changes (`IncrementalSurfaceAgreementTests.cs:159-198`).
- `calor check` does not use the build cache. Each run creates a new temporary workspace (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/TestCommand.cs:150`), compiles a fresh snapshot of every source with no cache argument and the verification cache off (`:173-192`, `:183`), then starts `dotnet build` and `dotnet test --no-build` (`:228-229`, `:248-249`). `docs/cli/index.md:71` states that it does not repair source or modify project files. The build cache is opt-in for plain compiles and always on for `calor watch` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Program.cs:466-472`).
- No test or CI job measures warm rebuild time. `tests/Calor.Performance.Tests` holds allocation, identity, index-build, warm-query and analysis timing and memory tests, and none that rebuilds after an edit. #1818 adds the measurement to the nightly `.github/workflows/performance.yml`.
- Warm results are compared with cold builds by `IncrementalSurfaceAgreementTests.cs:148-155` and by `EditScriptIdentityTests`, run as "Run full-vs-incremental identity gate" (`.github/workflows/test.yml:188-193`).
- Current behaviour is shown by `dotnet test tests/Calor.Tasks.Tests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~IncrementalSurfaceAgreementTests"`.

## Why

After #1732 an edit still recompiles every file that names another module's declarations, and in a project whose modules declare classes, which is what converted .NET code looks like, the proof spares almost nothing. `calor check`, the one command that builds, tests and verifies, reuses nothing between runs. How much either costs an agent per edit is unknown on 0.30, and the reuse decision is soundness-critical: a wrong skip hides a diagnostic. The amount of work here is therefore set by the figures #1818 measures, and it is none if they are within budget. The scorecard line "Fast warm feedback" in the plan of record reads this issue's outcome.

It takes capacity only if the gate opens. The follow-up it implements was recorded in a plan document and never filed. This issue is off the 0.33 exit chain and may slip to the next milestone without holding the release.

## Done when

- The sizing comment exists with the four figures, their budgets, the counts C and A and the projection for each over row of (a) to (c), and the outcome taken.
- Gate closed: the issue is closed as not planned with the latency record linked, and no code changed.
- Step 1, if taken: in `IncrementalSurfaceAgreementTests`, `bystander-body` expects `bystander` compiled and `caller`, `library` skipped. Every other row of `Edits()` is expected to be unchanged (from reading `CanReuseIndependentOutput`, not from a run); a row that does change is listed in the pull request with the reason.
- Step 2, if taken: `library-body` expects `library` compiled and `bystander`, `caller` skipped; `bystander-body` expects only `bystander` compiled; `library-signature`, `library-row-unused`, `library-rename`, `corrupt-output` and `missing-output` are unchanged. The expectations of `sibling-body` and `corrupt-output-and-edit` are kept, or changed with the reason stated in the soundness comment; in either case a file whose output is corrupted or missing is recompiled. `DerivedRecompilesOnAnyBaseEdit_AndItsContractStaysCorrect` is replaced by two tests: the derived class is skipped on a body-only base edit, and recompiled when the base's signature, declared row or base list changes. A new test shows that a body edit which changes an inferred row recompiles the dependent.
- Steps 1 and 2: for every edit row, the CLI and the task skip the same files, and outputs and diagnostics equal a cold build (the existing loop in `CliAndTaskSkipTheSameFiles_AndOnlyProvenIndependentOnes`). `CrossModuleViolation_AppearsAndDisappearsWithTheCalleeRow_OnBothSurfaces`, `EditScriptIdentityTests` and `CliEditScriptIdentityTests` pass unedited.
- Step 3, if taken: new cases in `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/ValidationLoopTests.cs`, through the CLI and `calor_check`, run the loop twice on an unchanged directory and once more after a one-file edit. Each warm result equals the result of a run with the state deleted, apart from `durationMs`. A counter that the implementation exposes to tests shows that the second run reused at least one file and that the edited file was not reused. `Snapshot_IsUnaffectedBySourceMutationDuringTest` passes unedited.
- For each quantity a step was taken for, its entry in the #1818 budget file is changed from over to within, one run of `.github/workflows/performance.yml` on the merged commit passes with that entry, and the before and after figures are in the pull request. If a quantity is still over after its step merged, the issue stays open with the figures posted.
- The closing comment states that the row-only tier was not built, and the pull request description carries the draft amendment for F-3′ section 7 if step 2 was taken.
- `CHANGELOG.md` states which edits now skip which files, and `expectedTotal` in `eng/test-manifest.json` changes only by the tests added or replaced (`Calor.Compiler.Tests` at `:8`, `Calor.Tasks.Tests` at `:98`).

## Not in scope

- Sparing a caller when only a callee's declared effect row changes.
- The `dotnet build` and `dotnet test` child processes of `calor check`, and MSBuild start-up time.
- Changing a budget or the measurement (#1818). Index build time (#1738).
- New frozen edit scripts under `tests/TestData/EditScripts/`. Registering one is the maintainer's freeze procedure.

Part of epic #1819. Depends on #1818.

issues.title: [0.33] Exact effect contracts for the callee families that account for most unknown-charged call sites
issues.displaces: none: new capacity justified in body
issues.body:
## Change

Give exact effect rows to the library members that most often leave Calor code `unknown`, chosen from the #1802 corpus report and bounded before work starts. A call site is unknown-charged when the compiler finds no effect contract for the callee and charges the caller `unknown`. The corpus is the three pinned libraries under `bench/corpus/` (MediatR, Serilog, FluentValidation), migrated by the corpus report job `.github/workflows/corpus-report.yml` (#1779).

Start after #1731 and #1798 are closed. #1731 changes built-in contracts, which moves the count this issue starts from, and records one outcome for each group of built-in members that can run code the effect system does not see (an exact contract, a new declarable effect, or the contract kept as a documented assumption). #1798 adds compile checks on teaching statements that fail when a member this issue touches stops being unknown.

1. **Selection record.** Post a comment on this issue, before any code, built from the report's full callee list (the job artifact) at the starting commit:
   - U, the unknown-charged call sites summed over the three projects, and a statement, with the job's command line, that each project was compiled with its own package references. A framework row applies only when the call binds to the metadata member, so a count taken without references cannot move.
   - Callees grouped into families by the namespace of the declaring type, ranked by call sites.
   - A second ranking from the agent-run table that #1802 commits beside the #1605 results (unknown-charged callees in the final sources of the Calor benchmark runs). If the table does not exist or names no callee, the record says so and the selection uses the corpus alone.
   - The selected families: taken in corpus rank order until they cover at least half of U, and at most five. A family that leads the agent-run ranking and is not selected is added while the count stays at most five; otherwise it is listed as not selected with its count. These bounds are the plan's defaults. The maintainer may change them, or swap a family, in this comment and nowhere else.
   - For each selected family, its call sites split by cause: *addressable* (a library member with no manifest entry), *reviewed unknown* (a manifest says `"unknown"` because the member runs user-supplied code), and *not a library member* (delegate invocation, an unresolved overload, a name with no type).
   - T, the addressable corpus call sites in the selected families divided by U. T is the share this issue commits to. A family taken from the agent-run ranking that the corpus does not call adds nothing to T.

   The maintainer confirms the comment. If T is zero and no agent-run family was selected, close the issue as not planned and link the comment.
2. **Contracts.** For each addressable member, add a row to the matching file under `src/Calor.Compiler/Manifests/`, or to a new `*.calor-effects.json` file there, following the convention stated in the file's `description`. A row lists every effect the member performs. A member whose effects cannot be established from its documentation or source gets no row and is listed in the pull request as "not added, with reason". Add no wildcard and no namespace-wide default to a framework or ecosystem manifest. Check each row with `calor effects resolve <signature>`. The issue may be delivered as one pull request per family; it closes when Done when holds over all of them.
3. **Members that run user code keep `"unknown"`.** No entry that is `"unknown"` at the starting commit becomes a static row in this issue, and no contract that #1731 decided is changed. List these members and their call sites in the pull request as "stays unknown, with reason". A mechanism that could give them a sound row is a design question for the maintainer and would be a new issue.
4. **Tests.** One `[InlineData]` row per added member beside the Tier B theories in `tests/Calor.Enforcement.Tests/EffectResolverTests.cs` (Tier B is the repository's name for the framework and ecosystem manifests, which apply only when the assembly is passed as a reference). One end-to-end test per family beside `TierB_E2E_MultipleFrameworkCalls_AllResolve` in `tests/Calor.Enforcement.Tests/EffectEnforcementTests.cs`: a function that declares the exact row compiles with no `Calor0410` or `Calor0411`, and a function that declares `!` and calls an effectful member reports `Calor0410`. These tests compile against real framework metadata passed as explicit references; a family whose assembly is not among the `CalorFrameworkReference` items of the test project adds one.
5. **Teaching text.** Where the teaching reference says an added member remains unknown, change the statement and its effect claim (the claim list #1798 adds) in `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Teaching/reference.json`. Where the effects page names the member, edit its source, `website/content/syntax-reference/effects.mdx`; `docs/syntax-reference/effects.md` is generated from it. Regenerate both with `calor self-check docs --fix`.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- A member with no contract resolves as unknown (`src/Calor.Compiler/Effects/EffectResolver.cs:246-247`). A manifest can also say `"unknown"` on purpose, and that answer is final (`:517-529`).
- A function that calls such a member must declare `! unknown`. The row stands alone, every caller is charged, and `calor convert` writes it by itself (`docs/syntax-reference/effects.md:280-301`).
- Fifteen built-in manifests under `src/Calor.Compiler/Manifests/` are embedded by a glob (`src/Calor.Compiler/Calor.Compiler.csproj:164`) and load at lowest priority (`src/Calor.Compiler/Effects/Manifests/ManifestLoader.cs:67-90`).
- When this issue was planned, dependency injection, options, logging and async members were expected to lead. At HEAD none of them is an open gap:
  - Logging has exact rows: `ILogger.Log` and `LoggerExtensions.Log*` are `cw` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Manifests/bcl-framework-interfaces.calor-effects.json:8-42`).
  - Dependency injection and options are `"unknown"` by a reviewed 0.30 decision, because they run service constructors and configuration callbacks: `GetService`, `GetRequiredService`, `IOptions<T>.Value` (same file, `:3`, `:87-147`; `CHANGELOG.md:64`). `TierB_MembersThatRunUserCode_AreUnknown` pins it (`tests/Calor.Enforcement.Tests/EffectResolverTests.cs:1397-1418`).
  - `System.Threading.Tasks` has a namespace-wide pure default (`src/Calor.Compiler/Manifests/bcl-runtime.calor-effects.json:339-343`), so an unlisted `Task` member is not unknown.
- Framework and ecosystem manifests have no namespace default, so their unlisted members are unknown (`EffectResolverTests.cs:1426-1446`).
- Framework rows need the assembly passed as a reference (`bcl-framework-interfaces.calor-effects.json:3`; `CHANGELOG.md:66`). The enforcement tests get five framework assemblies by `PackageDownload` (`tests/Calor.Enforcement.Tests/Calor.Enforcement.Tests.csproj:28-48`) and compile with them through `CompileFramework` (`tests/Calor.Enforcement.Tests/EffectEnforcementTests.cs:849-856`).
- Nothing counts unknown-charged call sites today; #1802 adds the count. `calor effects suggest` lists unresolved calls for given files, and `calor effects resolve` and `calor effects validate` check a signature and the manifests (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/EffectsCommand.cs:362`, `:50`, `:82`).
- The corpus is three libraries pinned as submodules (`bench/corpus/README.md:13-17`), not applications. Which families lead is not known.
- The conversion scorecard job is `conversion-scorecard` (`.github/workflows/test.yml:672`). Its test pins 100 of 100 files fully converted (`tests/Calor.Evaluation/Scorecard/ConversionScorecardTests.cs:31`, asserted by `ConversionRate_AboveBaseline`), and `NoRegressionsVsCommittedBaseline` compares each file with `tests/Calor.Evaluation/Scorecard/baseline.json`. The summary count in that file reads 96 and dates from commit `937f79321`; the test constant is the figure in force.

## Why

A function that declares `! unknown` is not effect-checked, every caller above it has to declare the same row, and the converter writes that row wherever a callee has no contract. Effects are the feature other languages lack, so the share of real code that ends up unknown measures whether the feature reaches everyday .NET code. The issue is bounded to a stated number of families and a share fixed in advance, because "the most frequent callees" has no stopping point. The selection comes from the report and not from a list written beforehand, because the families first expected to lead are already exact or are unknown on purpose.

It is new capacity and displaces nothing: no existing issue lowers the share that #1802 reports and that the #1708 task card reads. This issue is off the 0.33 exit chain and may slip to the next milestone without holding the release.

## Done when

- The selection record exists and the maintainer has confirmed it in a reply.
- Each pull request links two runs of `corpus-report.yml`, one at its base commit and one `workflow_dispatch` run on its branch, with the unknown-charged call sites per project from both. The reductions, summed over this issue's pull requests and the three projects, are at least T × U.
- Every added member has a resolver row test and every selected family has an end-to-end test. `TierB_MembersThatRunUserCode_AreUnknown` passes unedited. A row leaves `Ecosystem_UnlistedMembers_HaveNoNamespaceDefault` only if its member gained an entry here.
- `calor effects validate` and `calor self-check docs` exit 0.
- Standing acceptance rule. This issue adds no hard error, but it can change the rows `calor convert` writes, so the rule is applied: the conversion scorecard stays at 100 of 100 fully converted (CI job `conversion-scorecard`); the density ratio per corpus project (Calor tokens over C# tokens, the #1746 columns of the corpus report, or the hand procedure recorded in #1746 if those columns have not landed) is reported twice from the same runs, whole and with effect-row lines (`! ...`) left out of the Calor count, and the second figure does not rise; an exact row is usually longer than `! unknown`, so if the whole ratio rises the pull request gives the rise in tokens and the number of rows that changed, and it merges only with the maintainer's acceptance of that rise recorded in the pull request; and the number of corpus files that newly fall to whole-file preservation is reported from the same runs.
- `CHANGELOG.md` lists the members that gained rows, and `expectedTotal` for `Calor.Enforcement.Tests` in `eng/test-manifest.json` (`:24`) rises by exactly the tests added.

## Not in scope

- Culture-sensitive members, LINQ and `Object` dispatch (#1731).
- A new effect code or a new contract mechanism.
- Lowering the share of functions that declare `! unknown` in hand-written code. Only the corpus figure is committed to.

Part of epic #1819. Depends on #1802, #1731, #1798.

issues.title: [0.33] Example bank: compiler-checked programs by construct and task shape, served through calor_help and calor init
issues.displaces: none: new capacity justified in body
issues.body:
## Change

Turn the teaching programs into an example bank: indexed by construct and by task shape, larger, executed in CI, and served on demand. Deliver the four numbered parts below as four ordered pull requests; the issue closes on the done-when list.

Where the work is. The source is `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Teaching/reference.json`. `GenerateTeachingResources` (`src/Calor.Compiler/SelfCheck/ExemplarCompileChecker.cs:42`) renders it into the generated files, which `calor self-check docs --fix` rewrites and nobody edits by hand. Lookups are in `src/Calor.Compiler/Mcp/Tools/HelpTool.cs`. The tests to extend are `Mcp/Tools/SyntaxLookupToolTests.cs`, `TokenBudgetTests.cs` and `InitCommandTests.cs` under `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/`.

Terms. A *pair* is one benchmark task with a specification, a hidden test suite and a starting fixture per arm; an *arm* is one condition a run is made under; an *epoch* is one collection in which all arms run interleaved on one pinned model; a *valid run* is one the harness did not mark invalid (rate limit, API error, missing transcript, isolation violation).

1. **Index and checks.** Every bank program gets an index entry: `id`, `title`, the construct ids it demonstrates (from `constructs` in `reference.json`), one shape tag from the table below or `construct-only`, one lookup query (a task-phrased query that `calor_help` must answer with this program), and the field #1745 adds to each program: an expectation (a call with its arguments and the expected return value, exception type or console output) or the marker "cannot run" with a one-line reason. Every entry of `programs[]` at the starting commit becomes an entry (87 at HEAD bc80daeb; 88 if #1825 added its test example there); one that fails a check below is corrected and listed in the pull request. No index field is rendered into the reference. New programs do not go into the `programs` array, whose length a test pins (87 at HEAD) and which is rendered whole into `calor://reference`. They are stored (a second array or a sibling file, the implementer's choice) so that `GenerateTeachingResources` packages them for `calor_help` and renders none of them into the reference. If #1825 has not merged, it stores its test example in the bank store this issue creates. Tests hold every bank program to four conditions:
   - it compiles to valid C#, by the check that check 11 of `calor self-check docs` applies to the reference programs (`ExemplarCompileChecker.CheckAgentTaskReference`, `:451`);
   - the #1745 check executes it and compares the result with its expectation, or its entry carries the "cannot run" marker;
   - the formatter leaves it unchanged and the lint reports nothing (the checks behind `calor format --check` and `calor lint --check`);
   - it shares fewer than two function names with any current-syntax reference solution of a pair (at HEAD under `tests/TestData/ActiveSyntax/bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs/*/reference/calor/`). An example must not be the answer to an evaluation task.
2. **Content.** New programs are written for the bank in the current syntax (the edition, if #1805 declared one); none is converter output. By construct: every construct not marked `lookupOnly` has at least one executed program, or its entry carries the "cannot run" marker. By task shape: at least two whole-task programs of 20 to 60 lines per shape. The floor is the length that only one of today's programs reaches and the ceiling is the size of the July exemplar; both numbers are chosen here, not measured.
