In the table, pair categories and pair ids are directories under `bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs/` (the category is in each `pair.json`), end-to-end task categories are directories under `tests/E2E/agent-tasks/tasks/`, and the July figures are iterations until the hidden tests pass, relative to C#, on the pre-0.30 syntax.

   | Shape tag | The program | Where the shape comes from |
   |---|---|---|
   | `file-journal` | reads, appends to and rewrites a text file under `fs:r` and `fs:w` effect rows | pair category W3; `W3-003-kv-journal` took 2.27x the C# iterations in July |
   | `delimited-text` | splits, escapes and joins fields into lists | `N1-003-csv-row`, 2.50x in July |
   | `integer-rules` | integer arithmetic with refined parameters and postconditions | pair category W1 |
   | `array-window` | array and window computations with contracts bounded by a length | pair category W2 |
   | `keyed-state` | a dictionary or list updated in place under `mut` | `N1-002-inventory`, `N1-005-order-pipeline` |
   | `class-state` | a class with fields, a constructor and methods | end-to-end task category `oop-features` |
   | `async-io` | an async function that calls an effectful API | end-to-end task category `async-functions` |
   | `match-enum` | a match over an enum or a pattern | end-to-end task categories `pattern-matching`, `enums` |

   The first pull request may add a shape. Dropping one needs a reason in the pull request.
3. **Serving.** No new tool and no new required parameter. In `src/Calor.Compiler/Mcp/Tools/HelpTool.cs`, `action=syntax` ranks bank programs by construct and by lookup query and still returns at most two complete programs. `action=example` serves the bank in place of the ten self-test scenarios, which stay as `calor self-test` fixtures: `list=true` returns id, title, shape and constructs for every entry, and `name` returns one program with its expectation. The starter file `calor init` writes (the option #1773 adds, at the default #1823 set) stays the program #1773 named, which is a bank entry after part 1. If a pull request replaces it with another bank program, it names the new id, updates the #1773 test, states in `docs/cli/init.md` that the stage 2 reading of #1605 and decision 2 of #1823 were taken with the earlier starter, and changes neither default. Either way a test finds the written file byte-identical to the named bank program. Update `docs/cli/mcp.md`, `docs/cli/init.md` and their website copies, `website/content/cli/mcp.mdx` and `website/content/cli/init.mdx`.
4. **Measurement, the part that costs nothing.** The bank is judged by first-build pass rate (#1760: the share of valid runs whose first edited build-or-test invocation exits 0) and by cost per accepted task (the #1832 record: an arm's total cost over its valid runs divided by the number of those runs that pass every hidden test). This issue delivers:
   - a column "example uses per run" in the report script #1760 adds under `bench/phase0-agent-native/`, with a case in its fixture epoch: `calor_help` calls in `transcript.jsonl` whose result carries a bank program id, plus reads of the starter file; "not available" when the transcript holds no tool calls;
   - two Calor arms whose workspaces the real `calor init` sets up, each passing a zero-cost run on the pairs `N1-003-csv-row` and `W3-003-kv-journal`. One arm is bound to the product build of the commit before the first bank pull request; the other, the with-bank arm, to the build after the last. At HEAD the `bench/phase0-agent-native/run-pair.sh` flags are `--initialized-workspace`, `--calor-dll` with `--arm-repo-root` for the binding, and `--null-agent`, which applies the pair's reference solution and calls no model; if #1827 has replaced them with arm definitions, use those.

**Paid half (conditional).** Filing or closing this issue does not authorise spend. The gate is the dated line for this item in the record #1832 produces (`docs/plans/0.33-paid-run-registration.md`). That record offers three options: (a) a paid comparison of the two arms of part 4; (b) observation only, inside the per-agent runs of #1811, at no added spend; (c) not measured. It recommends (b), because the measurement gates nothing. Until #1832 closes, the item is neither listed nor declined: parts 1 to 4 proceed, no paid run is made, and this issue stays open for its closing record only.

If (a) is authorised, the design is fixed here. 10 runs per arm per pair (40 runs) in one epoch, on the one Claude Code version and model id that the record's line names, after the zero-cost pass of part 4 on the pinned commit. Ceiling $170, cumulative and checked between runs against realised cost: 40 runs at the dearest July per-run mean for a Calor arm, $4.20, is $168 (`W3-003-kv-journal`, 30 runs, the mean of `total_cost_usd` over `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/e1a-attribution/W3-003-kv-journal/calor/run-*/agent.json`; pre-0.30 syntax, model pin `default`). Runs are cut to fit the ceiling; it is not raised. The collection stops, and what exists is reported as incomplete, when the ceiling is reached, a transcript reports a model other than the pin, two consecutive runs in one arm are invalid, one run costs more than $16 (twice the dearest of the 180 July runs, $7.97), or the isolation check of #1762 fails. Four readings, fixed now, per pair; their cut-offs are set here, not measured:

| Outcome | Reading |
|---|---|
| An example use in fewer than half of the valid with-bank runs | "Not used." No effect is attributed to the bank; the pointer to it in the `calor init` text is the next thing to change. |
| Used; first-build pass rate higher with the bank, 90% bootstrap interval of the difference above zero | "The bank raises the first-build pass rate on this pair." Cost per accepted task is reported beside it. |
| Used; the interval includes zero | "No effect measured at this number of runs." |
| Used; the interval is below zero | "A bank program steers agents wrong." The program returned most often is corrected before the next release. |

A pair with fewer than 8 valid runs in either arm gets none of the four: it is reported as "not measurable", with the run counts.

If (b) is recorded, the uses column and the first-build pass rate are reported per agent in the #1811 report with the sentence "no comparison arm; no effect is claimed". That requires parts 1 to 4 to be in the commit #1811 pins; if they are not, (c) applies. If (c) is recorded, or the item is declined or not listed when #1832 closes, the 0.33 release notes (`CHANGELOG.md`) and the evidence ledger (`docs/benchmarking/evidence-ledger.md`, added by #1774) say "example bank shipped; effect unmeasured". No reading gates another issue.

New product code goes into existing files: `scripts/check-calor-first-diff.sh` rejects a new `.cs` file outside `tests/`, `bench/` and `tools/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness/` unless `.calor-csharp-allowlist` on the base branch already names it.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- `reference.json` holds 83 constructs and 87 programs (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/AgentTaskReferenceTests.cs:25` pins 87). A program has three fields: `id`, `title`, `calor`. Programs are 3 to 26 lines, median 7; only one has 20 lines or more (`complex_class`, 26); none declares `Main`. Measured by a script over the `programs` array.
- 81 constructs link at least one program and 64 link exactly one; two are `lookupOnly`. 17 programs, all with `task_N` ids, are linked from no construct. A topic lookup returns only programs linked from the matched construct, so those 17 reach an agent only inside the full reference (`calor_help` with `query=reference`, `HelpTool.cs:112-113`, or the `calor://reference` resource).
- Every program compiles in CI: check 11 of `calor self-check docs` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/SelfCheckCommand.cs:56`, run at `.github/workflows/test.yml:267`). Fifteen are also executed by hand-written tests: 13 in `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/ExemplarCompilesTests.cs` (`:131-143`, `:174`, `:209`) and two in `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/Mcp/AgentDocsSyntaxGuardTests.cs:34-57`. #1745 is open.
- No test was found that applies the formatter or the canonical-usage lint to these programs (grep of the test files that read `reference.json`), and no workflow invokes `calor format` or `calor lint`. Whether the 87 programs pass both today is not verified.
- Every entry in `programs` is rendered into the full reference (`ExemplarCompileChecker.cs:120-131`), which measured 16,750 o200k tokens against a ratchet of 17,000 on 2026-11-20 (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/TokenBudgetTests.cs:57-63`). The always-on MCP surface measured 7,900 against 8,000 (`:65-71`). #1734, #1823 and #1824 (all 0.32) may have changed these figures and constants; re-read them before starting.
- `calor_help` has four actions (`HelpTool.cs:50`); #1771 adds one for the primer. `action=syntax` matches constructs by name and keyword and returns at most two programs (`:167`; pinned at `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/Mcp/Tools/SyntaxLookupToolTests.cs:22`). `action=example` returns the ten code-generation scenarios under `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/SelfTest/` (`HelpTool.cs:566`); two of their descriptions name forms 0.30 removed, `requires` clauses (`:549`) and `Option` and `Result` types (`:550`). No test calls the action and `reference.json` never mentions it (grep).
- `calor init` writes no `.calr` file (grep of `src/Calor.Compiler/Init/` and `src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/InitCommand.cs`). Its template says "use `calor_help` for other constructs" (`src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Templates/CLAUDE.md.template:9`).
- No teaching program shares two or more function names with any of the 25 current-syntax pair reference solutions; the most shared is one (script over both sets).
- July 2026, pre-0.30 syntax, 30 runs per arm: iterations-to-green relative to C# were 2.50x on `N1-003-csv-row` and 2.27x on `W3-003-kv-journal`. With an exemplar of about 60 lines in the prompt they were 2.23x and 1.00x, pooled 2.38x to 1.62x (`bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/e1a-attribution/VERDICT.md:13-17`). On `N1-003-csv-row`, 29 of 30 exemplar runs copied an array type from the exemplar into a signature that needed a list, and failed their first build (`:43-51`). The 180 runs of that epoch cost $370.52 and the dearest cost $7.97 (sum and maximum of `total_cost_usd` over `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/e1a-attribution/*/*/run-*/agent.json`).
- `run-pair.sh` accepts `--null-agent`, `--initialized-workspace`, `--calor-dll` and `--arm-repo-root` (`bench/phase0-agent-native/run-pair.sh:222-236`), and an initialized-workspace arm may carry the last two (`:294-295`) and must write to a new `--out` directory (`:308-309`). That all four combine in one invocation is not verified. `transcript.jsonl` archives every agent event (`:28-31`).

## Why

Agents copy the examples they are shown. The July exemplar result in the baseline is the only measured reduction in the repository of what writing new Calor costs an agent, and the same run shows that one line of the wrong shape is copied just as faithfully. Today's programs are construct illustrations with a median of seven lines. None is a whole task, none has an entry point, and no topic lookup in the tool that the `calor init` text points to can return 17 of them. The task classes where Calor cost most in July, text files and delimited text, are covered by three programs of 5 to 14 lines (`task_35`, `primer_files`, `primer_strings`).

This is new capacity and displaces nothing: no open issue adds examples an agent can look up (#1745 executes the present ones and #1734 trims the reference). It is the 0.33 entry on the capability scorecard line "A reference the agent already knows" in `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md`, and it takes the one route to more in-context material that the token budgets leave open, because an on-demand lookup adds nothing to the surfaces an agent loads without asking. No acceptance criterion here depends on a model having learned Calor; every criterion is a CI check, a tool response or a run record. No 0.33 exit criterion names this issue; it may slip to 0.34 without holding the release.

## Done when

- A test class in `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests` asserts, over the packaged bank: every entry has the index fields of part 1; the four conditions of part 1 hold for every program; every shape has at least two programs of 20 to 60 lines; every construct not marked `lookupOnly` has an executed program or the "cannot run" marker with its reason.
- The #1745 check executes every bank program that has an expectation in CI, and a test asserts that the programs it executes are exactly the index entries that carry one.
- A test sends each shape's lookup query to `calor_help` and receives a program carrying that shape tag. A test calls `action=example` with `list=true` and receives every bank id. `EveryTopic_ReturnsAtMostTwoByteIdenticalCanonicalPrograms_ThatActuallyCompile` still passes.
- A test runs `calor init` with the starter option and finds the written file byte-identical to the named bank program.
- `TokenBudgetTests` passes with no existing constant raised. Two ceilings are added, for the `list=true` response and for the largest single-program response, each at its measured o200k count rounded up to the next multiple of 250 (the convention at `TokenBudgetTests.cs:33`). The pull request states tokens added and removed for `tools/list`, the full reference, the init templates and the primer (`calor://primer`).
- `calor self-check docs` exits 0, and `expectedTotal` for `Calor.Compiler.Tests` in `eng/test-manifest.json` rises by the number of tests added.
- `docs/cli/mcp.md`, `docs/cli/init.md`, `website/content/cli/mcp.mdx` and `website/content/cli/init.mdx` describe the bank and the starter, and `CHANGELOG.md` records both.
- The report script prints "example uses per run", and its fixture test covers a run with a lookup, a run that reads the starter file, and a transcript with no tool calls.
- Both arms of part 4 pass the zero-cost run on both pairs (`result.json` has `"nullAgent": true` and `"taskSuccess": true`), and their output is archived under `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/` in directories whose names end in `-null`. The pull request states the command lines.
- The closing comment links one of three records: under (a), the paid comparison with its reading per pair, its realised spend beside the ceiling, and the same figures in the 0.33 release notes and the evidence ledger; under (b), the per-agent observation published by #1811; under (c), or when the item is declined or not listed, the #1832 record together with the "effect unmeasured" sentence in the release notes and the evidence ledger.

## Not in scope

- How the primer is delivered and whether `calor init` writes a starter by default (#1773, #1823).
- Executing the existing reference programs (#1745) and trimming the full reference (#1734).
- A command-line way to print bank programs for clients without MCP. Those clients get the starter file.
- Publishing the bank outside the repository. #1839 states the rule for that.
- The spend decision (#1832) and the per-agent runs (#1811).

Part of epic #1838. Depends on #1745, #1760, #1773, #1823 and #1832. Parts 1 to 4 do not wait for #1832; only the closing record does.

issues.title: [0.33] Admission rule for public Calor: original, formatted, lint-clean, run in CI
issues.body:
## Change

Write down which Calor source the project publishes. Add `docs/contributing/public-calor.md` (front matter as `docs/contributing/development-setup.md`: `layout: default`, a `title`, `parent: Contributing`, the next `nav_order`) and the same text as `website/content/contributing/public-calor.mdx` (front matter `title`, `section: "contributing"`, the next `order`). Link the page from both contributing index pages and from `website/content/contributing/adding-benchmarks.mdx`. Text only: no compiler, converter, harness or workflow change. The rule below is a proposal; the maintainer accepts or changes it by approving the pull request.

Both pages describe retired forms in words and do not write a retired marker: `calor self-check docs` rejects one in `website/content/**/*.mdx`, and it rejects the current three-part compiler version anywhere under `docs/`.

The page states seven things.

1. **Scope.** Public Calor is any `.calr` file or fenced Calor program that the project shows as an example or ships: `samples/`, `docs/`, `website/content/`, the teaching programs and the example bank (#1835), files written by `calor init`, and anything published outside the repository as a corpus or dataset. Test fixtures, benchmark pairs, archived run outputs and the paths on the legacy-dialect allowlist (the file #1763 creates, named here by its path) are not public Calor.
2. **Admission.** A program is admitted only when all four hold:
   - original: written for the project, not produced by `calor convert` or `calor migrate` from third-party source, and contributed under the project licence;
   - formatted: `calor format --check` exits 0 on it;
   - lint-clean: `calor lint --check` exits 0 on it, which covers the canonical-usage findings `Calor1305` and `Calor1306`;
   - run in CI: a CI check compiles it and, when it has a recorded expectation (as #1745 defines one for the teaching programs: a call with its arguments and the expected return value, exception type or console output), executes it and compares the result.
3. **Converted open-source code is not published.** Output of converting the round-trip corpus (the three open-source C# projects under `bench/corpus/`) is produced in CI runs and is neither committed nor published. Changing that is a maintainer decision, and two things must exist before it is taken: a manifest with one row per published file (source project, tag and commit, licence, copyright notice, NOTICE text, and a statement that conversion changed the file), and a converter test showing that a source file's header comment survives conversion.
4. **Hygiene.** Every public `.calr` file outside the legacy-dialect allowlist is in the current syntax and in canonical form, meaning the second and third conditions of item 2.
5. **Training prior.** Public Calor may one day give models a prior. The roadmap treats that as a by-product: rule 5 of `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md` lets no acceptance criterion depend on it.
6. **Enforcement table.** One row for each public surface in item 1 and one column for each condition in item 2. Each cell names the workflow step or test that enforces the condition today, or says "not enforced"; a check that covers only part of a surface says which part.
7. **Audit.** The commit, the two commands of item 2 run over `samples/` (and over the bank if #1835 has merged), their exit codes, and every failing file. Fixing the files is not part of this issue; one follow-up issue is filed for them.

Add one line beside rule 5 (no training-prior criteria) in `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md` that links to the page.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- No page states an admission rule. The contributing pages invite benchmark programs and examples (`docs/contributing/index.md:19-20`, `website/content/contributing/index.mdx:17-18`). `website/content/contributing/adding-benchmarks.mdx` (339 lines) contains none of `licen`, `lint`, `formatter` or `calor format` (grep).
- The project licence is Apache-2.0 (`LICENSE:1-2`). Its conditions for redistributing a derivative work start at `LICENSE:89`: a copy of the licence (`:94`), a notice on modified files (`:97`), retained copyright and attribution notices (`:100`), and the NOTICE text where the work has one (`:106`).
- The round-trip corpus is three open-source projects vendored as submodules at pinned tags, each recorded as Apache-2.0 (`bench/corpus/README.md:15-17`); MediatR is pinned to its last Apache-2.0 release (`:25`). No converted output of them is tracked: no tracked `.calr` path contains a project name (`git ls-files`). The submodules were not checked out when this was written, so their LICENSE and NOTICE files are not verified.
- The converter keeps XML documentation comments and no others (`src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/CSharpToCalorConverter.cs:126`, `:130-131`; `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/ConversionContext.cs:561`). Under `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/` the ordinary comment kinds are referenced once, in a check on interpolation holes (`RoslynSyntaxVisitor.cs:16717`). A licence header in a natively converted file is therefore lost. Established by reading; not run.
- The converter writes no postconditions: each of the five `postconditions:` arguments in `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/RoslynSyntaxVisitor.cs` is an empty array (the first at `:3971`; grep).
- `calor format --check` exits 1 on an unformatted file (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/FormatCommand.cs:27-29`). `calor lint --check` exits 1 on any finding, canonical-usage findings included (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/LintCommand.cs:35-37`, `:274-277`, `:341-343`; codes at `src/Calor.Compiler/Diagnostics/Diagnostic.cs:1228`, `:1235`). No workflow under `.github/workflows/` invokes either command (grep).
- The converter hoists sub-expressions into temporaries named `_elem`, `_new`, `_chain` and `_idx` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/RoslynSyntaxVisitor.cs:8609-8639`; #1742, 0.34). By the body of #1747 (0.34), converted output has been checked with the canonical-usage lint for one corpus project only, FluentValidation; that is not re-verified here.
- `samples/` holds 11 `.calr` files. 27 of their 31 `func` headers write an explicit `public` (grep). The teaching reference says public is the default (`docs/syntax-reference/current-language.md:30`) and none of its 87 programs writes it. #1796 decides which is canonical and #1803 applies the answer.
- 853 of the 1,823 tracked `.calr` files contain a retired `§` marker (`git ls-files` and grep). #1763 creates the allowlist and a self-check for them.
- Checks that exist, as leads for the enforcement table:
  - `calor self-check docs` (`.github/workflows/test.yml:267`; checks listed at `src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/SelfCheckCommand.cs:45-61`) parses the complete programs fenced in `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/syntax-reference/*.md`, `docs/cli/*.md` and undated `docs/semantics/*.md` (check 6; no other file under `docs/` is covered), compiles the primer and reference programs (checks 8 and 11) and compiles website programs (checks 12 and 13).
  - `PublicNativeReference_CompilesPositiveAndExactNegativeExamples` (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/DocDriftCheckerTests.cs:260`) executes the complete programs of the website pages it lists and compares each result with an expected value. Whether it lists every page that holds a program is not verified.
  - Every `.calr` file under `samples/` is compiled by `Sample_CompilesWithoutErrorsOrTypeWarnings` (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/BenchCorpusCompilesTests.cs:129`) and by the Tier 1 step (`.github/workflows/test.yml:1597`, `scripts/verify_phase1.py`). `samples/Contracts` and `samples/SdkSample` also build with the solution (`Calor.sln:20`, `:26`). No check was found that runs a sample and compares its output.
  - `calor init` writes no `.calr` file today (grep of `src/Calor.Compiler/Init/` and `src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/InitCommand.cs`); the starter option comes from #1773.

## Why

The first time someone proposes publishing Calor outside the repository, the largest body of it to hand will be converter output, and that is the wrong source. It carries converter artefacts such as statement hoists (#1742), has been linted for canonical usage on one project (#1747) and has no postconditions. It also comes from Apache-2.0 projects, and the converter does nothing to meet their notice conditions: it keeps no ordinary comment, so a header notice in a source file is dropped. Hand-written material is not uniform either: the samples and the teaching reference disagree on `public`. A rule written before anything is published costs one page. Without it the first corpus decides the question by accident, and whatever it contains is what a later model would learn.

The issue is text-only and takes capacity from no other issue. #1835 enforces the four conditions on the bank through its own tests; this page states them for every other public surface and records where they are not enforced yet. No 0.33 exit criterion names this issue; it may slip to 0.34 without holding the release.

## Done when

- `docs/contributing/public-calor.md` and `website/content/contributing/public-calor.mdx` exist with the seven items, and the two index pages and `adding-benchmarks.mdx` link to the page.
- The enforcement table has a row for each of the five surfaces inside the repository: `samples/`, fenced Calor in `docs/`, fenced Calor in `website/content/`, the teaching programs and example bank, and files written by `calor init`. No cell is empty.
- The audit paragraph gives the commit, both commands, an exit code per command and surface, and the list of failing files. A follow-up issue is linked, or the list is empty.
- `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md` links to the page.
- `calor self-check docs` exits 0 and the `Website regressions` workflow passes.
- The pull request changes files under `docs/` and `website/content/` only.

## Not in scope

- A CI check that enforces the rule on `samples/` or on website examples. The table records the gap.
- Reformatting `samples/` (#1803 applies the 0.32 decisions to it).
- The licence and notice manifest and the converter header-comment test. They are prerequisites of a decision this issue does not take.
- Publishing a corpus or dataset.

Part of epic #1838. Depends on #1765 (the plan of record the page is linked from) and #1763 (the allowlist the page names).

issues.title: [0.33] Sidecar identity through MCP class rename, LSP rename and cross-class member moves
issues.body:
**Current.** A follow-up from #1600. The body says 0.30 moved declaration IDs into the tooling sidecar `.calor/ids.json`, lists what `DeclarationIdentitySidecarTests` already covers, and names three paths that do not keep identity or are unverified: MCP class rename (refused), LSP rename against the sidecar ("no test found") and moving a member between classes ("no test found"). It is done when each path keeps the ID or refuses with a clear, documented message, and each has a test.

**Moved from** 0.31 because no 0.31 exit criterion needs it, and 0.31 is kept to the work its exit needs. The 0.31 capacity it held is claimed by #1764.

**Amendment.** New title: `[0.33] Sidecar identity through MCP class rename, LSP rename and cross-class member moves`. Milestone 0.33. Keep the body up to and including the sentence that ends "ambiguous renames (which write nothing)." Replace everything after it, from "Three refactoring paths do not keep identity yet or are unverified:" to the end of the "Done when" paragraph, with:

```markdown
## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

Terms. The *sidecar* is `.calor/ids.json`, where tools keep one ID per declaration. A project is *registered* once a build or `calor ids sync` has written it. A *relocation* is an explicit "this ID now belongs to that declaration" mapping that a tool hands to the identity store (`DeclarationRelocation`, `src/Calor.Compiler/Ids/IdEntry.cs:50`).

Test files: **S** is `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/DeclarationIdentitySidecarTests.cs`; **L** is `tests/Calor.LanguageServer.Tests/Handlers/RenameHandlerTests.cs`.

| Path | Behaviour | Pinned by |
|---|---|---|
| MCP `calor_file_write`, `action: "rename"`, on a function | ID kept; the tool passes a relocation (`src/Calor.Compiler/Mcp/Tools/FileWriteTool.cs:121-124`) | `McpRenameUsesPositionsAndKeepsNavigationIdentity` (S:1001) |
| The same action on a class | Refused, nothing written. `RenameEngine` refuses every type declaration because `ProjectSymbolIndex` does not index type references (`src/Calor.Compiler/Refactoring/RenameEngine.cs:73-74`). The MCP error carries only the enum name: `calor_file_write refactoring failed: Rename refused: TypeReferencesNotIndexed` (`FileWriteTool.cs:116`, `:169`) | `McpClassRenameReportsExistingTypeIndexLimitationWithoutEdits` (S:329) |
| `calor rename` (CLI, same engine) in a registered project | Writes through `DeclarationIdentityStore.Apply` with no relocation (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/RenameCommand.cs:131-138`); refuses a class with a full sentence (`:160-162`) | No test runs the command. `RenameHarnessTests` calls `RenameEngine` directly and has no sidecar |
| Editor (LSP) rename of a function or a class, registered project | Returns the source edit and a sidecar edit in one `WorkspaceEdit`; IDs are kept once the client applies both. Refuses with JSON-RPC error -32803 when the client did not declare transactional workspace edits, or when the buffer differs from disk (`src/Calor.LanguageServer/Handlers/RenameHandler.cs:120-163`) | `ClassRenameKeepsSelfTypedMemberIdentityAsync` (L:17), `SidecarRenameRefusesNontransactionalClientsAndUnsavedBuffersExplicitlyAsync` (L:63), `SidecarIdentitySurvivesLspRenameAndSaveWithoutSourceIdsAsync` (L:93), `FileLabelRenamePreservesSidecarIdentityNamespaceAndClrOwnersAsync` (L:1760) |
| Move a member to another class with an explicit mapping | ID kept. Through MCP `action: "move"` the caller supplies the before and after text of every changed file and the tool maps the identity (`FileWriteTool.cs:126-148`) | `MoveBetweenClassesAndFilesKeepsBoundSymbolIdentity` (S:674), `McpMoveAcrossClassesAndFilesRetainsExactIdentity` (S:1022) |
| Move a member by editing text, then `calor ids sync` | By reading `Reconcile` (`IdEntry.cs:687-844`; rule stated in `docs/ids.md:95-100`; not run): inside one file the ID is kept when exactly one vanished and one new declaration share kind and signature. Into a different class in a different file nothing matches, so the old ID is dropped and a new one is minted. `calor ids sync` prints only a declaration count (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/IdsCommand.cs:52`), so nothing tells the user | No test for either case |

Two gaps in the editor row. The tests set `SupportsTransactionalWorkspaceEdits` by hand (L:1951); the code that derives it from the client's capabilities (`RenameHandler.cs:208-221`) has no test, and neither end-to-end client declares a `workspaceEdit` capability (`tests/Calor.LanguageServer.Tests/E2E/Helpers/LspTestClient.cs:24-28`, `LspClient.cs:24-29` beside it). Every sidecar test edits a single source file.

## Done when

1. **MCP class rename** closes on one of two outcomes, named in the pull request. A is preferred, because agents reach rename through MCP and not through an editor; B is acceptable if sharing the type-reference index costs more than this issue can carry.
   - **A, it renames.** `ProjectSymbolIndex` records type references. The language server already finds them (`TypeReferenceIndex`, `src/Calor.LanguageServer/Utilities/SymbolFinder.cs:964`), but the compiler project cannot reference the language server (`src/Calor.LanguageServer/Calor.LanguageServer.csproj:15` points the other way), so that code moves or is shared. The test at S:329 is replaced by one that renames `A` to `B` and asserts that the IDs of the class and of both `Echo` overloads are unchanged, that the project compiles, and that a second file using the type as a parameter type and in a `new` expression was edited. In `TypeSplitGuardUsesActualQualifiedIdentity` (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/RenameEngineSmokeTests.cs:164`) the four `false` rows stop expecting `TypeReferencesNotIndexed` (each expects `RenameRefusal.None`, or another refusal whose reason the test states) and the two `true` rows keep `SplitDeclaration`. `calor rename` gets the same behaviour.
   - **B, it refuses with a sentence.** The MCP error says why and what to do instead, on the model of the CLI text at `RenameCommand.cs:160-162`: write the edited files with a plain `calor_file_write`, or use editor rename. A plain write reconciles identity through `DeclarationIdentityStore.Apply` (`FileWriteTool.cs:452-455`; `McpFileWriteCommitsSourceAndSidecarTogether`, S:942, pins that path for a function, and `TextClassRenamePreservesSelfTypedMemberIdentity`, S:256, pins the reconcile for a class renamed in one file). The test at S:329 asserts the new text.
   - Either way the explanation goes in the error message, not in the tool description or schema: the always-on MCP surface measured 7,900 `o200k` proxy tokens on 2026-11-20 against a ratchet of 8,000 (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/TokenBudgetTests.cs:65-71`).
2. **`calor rename`.** A test runs the command through `CliTestHarness.RunCli` (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/CliTestHarness.cs:201`) on a registered project, renames a function that a second file calls, and asserts exit code 0, the function's ID unchanged, and no `.calor/ids.transaction.json` left behind (the assertions `McpFileWriteCommitsSourceAndSidecarTogether` makes at S:951-953).
3. **Editor capability negotiation.** A protocol-level test under `tests/Calor.LanguageServer.Tests/E2E/` initialises the server with `workspace.workspaceEdit.documentChanges: true` and `failureHandling: "textOnlyTransactional"` (`LspProtocolClient.InitializeAsync`, `E2E/Helpers/LspProtocolClient.cs:73`, takes the capabilities object). In a registered project whose files are saved, it renames a function that a second file calls and receives document changes for both source files and for `.calor/ids.json`. The same request from a client that declares neither capability receives an error whose message contains "transactional".
4. **Text moves.** Two tests cut a member from one class, paste it into another with no relocation, and run `calor ids sync` (or `DeclarationIdentityStore.Sync`): one keeps both classes in one file, the other puts the destination class in a different file. Each asserts the outcome it observes: the old ID on the moved member, a new ID with the old one gone, or a failed sync with its message. By reading, the first keeps the ID and the second mints a new one; if a test shows otherwise, the row above is corrected in the same pull request. A silently minted ID in the second case is neither "keeps identity" nor "refuses with a clear message"; this issue accepts it as a pinned and documented limit, because a text edit is not a tool path and the tool paths (MCP `move`, an explicit relocation) keep the ID. Making `calor ids sync` report or refuse the dropped ID is a behaviour change that this issue does not make and no issue owns.
5. **Documented.** `docs/ids.md` ("Transactions and refactoring" and "Conservative reconciliation") states the outcome of items 1 and 4 (for a text move across files: that the ID is lost without a message, and which tool keeps it), and its sentence on the `TypeReferencesNotIndexed` refusal (`docs/ids.md:141`) matches the outcome chosen in item 1. If the website guide from #1748 exists, its support table is updated in the same pull request.
6. `eng/test-manifest.json` carries the new `expectedTotal` for each project whose test count changed (22559 for `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests` at line 8 and 692 for `tests/Calor.LanguageServer.Tests` at line 66, at HEAD). The CI step "Run exact-span LSP refactoring gate" (`.github/workflows/test.yml:181-186`) passes.

The items may land as separate pull requests, in any order; outcome A of item 1 may itself take two (share the type-reference index, then lift the refusal). The issue closes when all six hold.

## Not in scope

- Types declared across several files. The editor side is #922; this engine keeps `SplitDeclaration`.
- Changing the reconcile rules. Item 4 pins what they do today.
- The public how-to (#1748).

Part of epic #1840. This issue is off the 0.33 exit chain and may move to 0.34 without holding the release.
```

**Why.** Two of the body's three gaps are closed at HEAD bc80daeb: four editor tests exercise rename against the sidecar, and two tests move a member across classes and files with its ID intact. Checking them turned up three paths that the body does not list and that no test covers: the CLI command, the capability negotiation that decides whether a real editor reaches the sidecar path at all, and a text move across files, which by reading loses the ID without a message. The title keeps its three paths; the CLI and capability-negotiation tests are added because both paths carry identity and have no test. The issue is off the 0.33 exit chain and may slip to 0.34 without holding the release.

issues.title: [0.33] LSP rename cannot rename declarations that span files (partial types, multi-file modules) — needs identity groups in the workspace index
issues.body:
**Current.** A follow-up from the #765 review (PR #921). The body says the language server's workspace index keys identity per file, so a module or a `partial` type declared in several files has one symbol per part, and that PR #921 made `RenameHandler` refuse such declarations as a safety floor. It asks for identity groups so that rename edits every part, for type references to a split type to resolve, and for module rename to rewrite importers. Its gate extends `ExactSpanRefactoringGateTests` and swaps three refusal pins for success assertions.

**Moved from** no milestone because it was one of eleven open issues left unscheduled when 0.30.0 shipped, and it is tooling backlog that no exit criterion needs. It joins the two other identity issues in 0.33.

**Amendment.** Milestone 0.33; the title gains the `[0.33]` prefix and is otherwise unchanged, although its "multi-file modules" half names something 0.30 retired (see the Baseline below). Keep the first line ("Follow-up from the #765 review (PR #921, commit 654fe39f)."). Replace the rest of the body (the sections "Current state", "What is missing" and "Gate", and the "Related" line) with the text below. The replacement removes the retired-syntax bullet, so the #922 syntax edit that #1759 carries has nothing left to change; it can be applied before this or skipped, and #1759's check that the body contains no retired marker passes either way.

```markdown
## Change

Make editor (LSP) rename edit every part of a `partial` type that is declared in more than one file, instead of returning no edit.

1. **Identity group.** In the language server's workspace index, the declarations that share a `TypeSymbol.QualifiedName` (the key the index already groups by) resolve to one renameable identity. `FindSymbolOccurrences` returns the declarations and references of every part.
2. **References.** `TypeReferenceIndex.ResolveTypeSymbol` treats the parts of one group as one candidate, so a reference to a split type is indexed instead of dropped.
3. **Handler.** `RenameHandler` stops refusing such a set. Its other gates stay: exact spans, current snapshots, and `ValidateRenameAsync`.
4. **Sidecar.** In a registered project (one that has `.calor/ids.json`, the file where tools keep declaration IDs), the returned `WorkspaceEdit` also carries one sidecar edit that keeps every part's ID.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- 0.30 retired half of this issue's title. A root `module` header now only labels its file, and the optional second name is the namespace (`docs/syntax-reference/current-language.md:23-24`). Two files with the same label are two compilation units. Renaming one label edits one file, and both rename engines already do it, including when another file imports the namespace. For `RenameEngine`: `RenamesFileLabelIndependentlyOfAnotherFilesIdenticalLabel` (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/RenameEngineSmokeTests.cs:115`) and, with an importing file, `McpFileLabelRenamePreservesNamespaceAndEveryPersistedIdentity` (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/DeclarationIdentitySidecarTests.cs:272`). For the editor: `RenameFileLabelPreservesAnExplicitImportedNamespaceAsync` (`tests/Calor.LanguageServer.Tests/Handlers/RenameHandlerTests.cs:2506`). `tests/TestData/RenameScripts/README.md:42-47` records the same change for the rename corpus.
- A `partial` type is what still spans files. The index counts the files that declare each qualified type name and marks a declaration `IsSplitDeclaration` when the count exceeds one (`src/Calor.LanguageServer/State/WorkspaceState.cs:1762-1772`, `:1807-1811`). Each part has its own `TypeSymbol.Id`, so an occurrence set covers one part.
- `RenameHandler.Handle` returns `null` for such a set (`src/Calor.LanguageServer/Handlers/RenameHandler.cs:71-78`): the editor shows no edit and no reason.
- `ResolveTypeSymbol` returns a symbol only when exactly one candidate matches (`src/Calor.LanguageServer/Utilities/SymbolFinder.cs:1258-1285`). The parts of a split type are two candidates.
- The sidecar has one entry per part, because a declaration's key includes its file (`src/Calor.Compiler/Ids/IdEntry.cs:47`). By reading `Reconcile` (`IdEntry.cs:687-844`; not run): two parts renamed in one transaction are two candidates of the same kind and signature in one container, which is rejected as ambiguous ("Ambiguous declaration identity for ...; use an explicit tooling relocation.", `IdEntry.cs:832`) unless the caller passes one `DeclarationRelocation` per part. `PreviewSidecar` accepts relocations (`IdEntry.cs:479`); the handler passes none today (`RenameHandler.cs:144`).
- Refusal pins, all in `RenameHandlerTests.cs`: the two `true` rows of `PartialTypeSplitProtectionUsesActualQualifiedIdentityAsync` (`:1691-1696`) and the `("Worker", "Employee", true)` row of `ExactSpanRefactoringGateTests.RenameDistinguishesFileLabelsFromSplitPartialTypesAsync` (`:2422`). CI runs both classes in the step "Run exact-span LSP refactoring gate" (`.github/workflows/test.yml:181-186`).
- The second engine, `RenameEngine` (behind `calor rename` and MCP `calor_file_write`), refuses the same shape with `SplitDeclaration` and points at this issue in three places: `src/Calor.Compiler/Refactoring/RenameEngine.cs:20-25`, `src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/RenameCommand.cs:151-154` (whose text still says "a module"), and `tests/TestData/RenameScripts/RN-06-partial-type-split-refused/script.json`. It refuses every other type rename too, because it has no type-reference index (#1744).

## Why

Renaming one part of a partial type splits it into two types with no Calor diagnostic: the result either still compiles and means something else, or fails only in the generated C#. The refusal from PR #921 prevents that, but a user who asks for a rename and gets nothing, with no reason, cannot tell a limit from a bug. Renaming every part is the expected behaviour and is what Roslyn does for partial types. This issue is off the 0.33 exit chain and may slip to 0.34 without holding the release.

## Done when

- In the commit that changes behaviour, the three refusal rows above assert success: the edit touches both files, every edited range reads the old name, and the edited workspace reparses, rebinds, emits and compiles with no Roslyn error (`AssertWorkspaceRoslynCleanWithProductionMap`, which those tests already use), with the type found under its new metadata name and not under the old one.
- A test renames a split type that a third file uses as a parameter type and in a `new` expression, and asserts both uses were edited.
- The four `false` rows of `PartialTypeSplitProtectionUsesActualQualifiedIdentityAsync` (`:1697-1708`: a different namespace, a different generic arity, a different containing type, a containing type of different generic arity) still produce one edit, in the first file only.
- A test on a registered project applies the returned source and sidecar edits and asserts that the ID of each part is unchanged (the shape of `ClassRenameKeepsSelfTypedMemberIdentityAsync`, `RenameHandlerTests.cs:17`).
- The CI step named above passes, and `eng/test-manifest.json` carries the new `expectedTotal` for `tests/Calor.LanguageServer.Tests` (692 at HEAD, line 66) if the count changed.
- The three pointers on the `RenameEngine` side are reworded: that engine still refuses a type declared across files, the text says editor rename handles it, and the CLI message no longer mentions a module. `RN-06` keeps `expectedRefusal: SplitDeclaration`.
- `docs/ids.md` ("Transactions and refactoring") says editor rename covers types declared across files. If the website guide from #1748 exists, its support table is updated in the same pull request.

## Not in scope

- Lifting `SplitDeclaration` in `RenameEngine` (MCP and CLI). It needs type references in `ProjectSymbolIndex` first; see #1744.
- Renaming a namespace: the second name on a `module` header and the `using` directives that name it. By reading, neither index records a namespace name as an occurrence, and no issue covers it.

Related: #767 (LSP hardening).

Part of epic #1840.
```

**Why.** The body was written before 0.30 and is stale beyond its one retired marker. A root `module` is now a per-file label, so the "multi-file module" half and the importer bullet describe behaviour that no longer exists, and the module symbol is no longer built from `ast.Id` (`WorkspaceState.cs:1780-1786` uses the sidecar ID, or the label). What remains is the partial-type half, and the sidecar now has to survive the rename as well, which the body could not have asked for. The issue is off the 0.33 exit chain and may slip to 0.34 without holding the release.

issues.title: [0.33] Website: explain declaration identity (ids sidecar) and how to rename through tooling
issues.body:
**Current.** A follow-up from #1623. The body says declaration identity moved into the sidecar `.calor/ids.json` in 0.30, that renames should go through tooling, and that the website mentions this only on the benchmarking metric pages. It is done when the guides, and the syntax reference where IDs used to appear, explain the sidecar, `calor ids sync` and `check`, and how to rename or move without losing identity, in the public-surface register and cross-checked against #1744.

**Moved from** 0.31 because no 0.31 exit criterion needs it, and 0.31 is kept to the work its exit needs. The 0.31 capacity it held is claimed by #1771.

**Amendment.** New title: `[0.33] Website: explain declaration identity (ids sidecar) and how to rename through tooling`. Milestone 0.33. Keep the first line and the first two sentences of the second paragraph. Delete that paragraph's last sentence ("The website mentions this only on the benchmarking metric pages; the guides and the syntax reference do not explain it."). Replace the "Done when" paragraph with:

```markdown
## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

The identity model is already on the website:

- `website/content/philosophy/stable-identifiers.mdx`: name versus identity, which operations keep an ID, transactions and merges, and the `calor ids` commands.
- `website/content/cli/ids.mdx`: `ids sync`, `ids check`, `ids index`, and a paragraph on refactoring and recovery.
- Four hand-written syntax-reference pages carry a short note that IDs are not written in source: `index.mdx:142-147`, `structure-tags.mdx:750-751`, `inheritance.mdx:9` and `control-flow.mdx:375-379` under `website/content/syntax-reference/`. A fifth page, `current-language.mdx:18`, has one line; it is generated from `Teaching/reference.json` and is not edited here.
- Two guides have one sentence each: `website/content/guides/adding-calor-to-existing-projects.mdx:137-138` and `website/content/guides/dependent-types-tutorial.mdx:185-186`.

What is missing:

1. No page shows how to rename or move. No command line, tool call or editor step for it appears under `website/content/guides/`.
2. `calor rename` is undocumented. It is registered (`src/Calor.Compiler/Program.cs:315`), has no page under `website/content/cli/`, and has no row in `website/content/cli/index.mdx`; only `website/content/changelog.mdx:2772` mentions it.
3. `website/content/cli/index.mdx:54` describes `calor ids` as "Check, assign, and index declaration IDs". `ids assign` is retired and exits 1 (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/IdsCommand.cs:21-34`); the subcommands are `sync`, `check` and `index`.
4. `website/content/cli/mcp.mdx:111` lists the `rename` and `move` actions of `calor_file_write` without their arguments. The arguments are written down only in `docs/ids.md:132-139`.
5. No page says which operations each tool supports. "Supported renames and moves" (`cli/ids.mdx:74-75`, `stable-identifiers.mdx:42`) is never spelled out. At HEAD there are four limits. MCP and `calor rename` refuse to rename any type; no website page says so (it is written in `docs/ids.md:141` for MCP and `CHANGELOG.md:3402-3406` for `calor rename`). Editor rename returns no edit for a type declared across files; no document says so. The MCP `rename` and `move` actions refuse in a project that has no sidecar ("Build the active project or run ids sync before refactoring.", `src/Calor.Compiler/Mcp/Tools/FileWriteTool.cs:93-94`); no website page says so. In a project that has a sidecar, editor rename needs a client with transactional workspace edits and saved buffers; the website does say this (`cli/ids.mdx:75-77`, `stable-identifiers.mdx:66-69`).
6. `website/content/cli/lsp.mdx` does not mention rename; `website/content/getting-started/installation.mdx:110` lists "symbol-exact rename" as an editor feature.
7. Outside the website, `docs/cli/ids.md` (342 lines) still documents `calor ids assign` and IDs written in source, and `docs/cli/index.md:44` lists "check, assign, index".

The behaviour to document is pinned by `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/DeclarationIdentitySidecarTests.cs`, `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/RenameEngineSmokeTests.cs` and `tests/Calor.LanguageServer.Tests/Handlers/RenameHandlerTests.cs`, and is stated for contributors in `docs/ids.md:93-147`.

Website examples are themselves under test. `PublicNativeReference_CompilesPositiveAndExactNegativeExamples` (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/DocDriftCheckerTests.cs:260`) has one row per page that fixes the number of complete `calor` programs on it and what each returns (rows for `cli/ids.mdx` at `:166`, `philosophy/stable-identifiers.mdx` at `:212`, and the four syntax-reference pages at `:99`, `:108`, `:129`, `:243`). `PublicIdsGuide_ActualCommandsPreserveSourceAndPersistedIdentity` (`:1667`) runs the commands that `cli/ids.mdx` publishes.

## Done when

- A guide page exists under `website/content/guides/` and is linked from `website/content/guides/index.mdx`, `website/content/cli/ids.mdx` and `website/content/philosophy/stable-identifiers.mdx`. For each of four tasks (rename a function or member, rename a class, rename a file label, move a member to another class or file) it shows what keeps the ID: the `calor rename` command line, the `calor_file_write` call with `action: "rename"` or `"move"` and its required arguments, and editor rename through `calor lsp` with its two requirements. It also says what a plain text edit followed by `calor ids sync` does.
- The page has one support table. Rows: the four tasks plus "rename a type declared across files". Columns: `calor rename`, `calor_file_write`, editor rename, and "text edit, then `calor ids sync`". Each cell is one of: keeps the ID, refuses (with the text the user sees), new ID, not offered, not guaranteed. The pull request lists the test that backs each cell. Where no test pins the behaviour (at HEAD: `calor rename` in a project with a sidecar, and a member moved by text edit), the cell reads "not guaranteed" and names the tool to use instead, until #1744 adds the test. If #1744 has already landed, the cells carry its pinned outcomes instead.
- `calor rename` has a reference page under `website/content/cli/` (arguments from `src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/RenameCommand.cs:18-39`, refusals from `:146-164`) and a row in `website/content/cli/index.mdx`. The `calor ids` row there reads sync, check, index.
- `website/content/cli/mcp.mdx` gives the arguments of the `rename` and `move` actions, or links to the guide for them. `website/content/cli/lsp.mdx` links to the guide.
- The four syntax-reference notes link to the guide. They stay short.
- `docs/cli/ids.md` and `docs/cli/index.md:44` no longer describe `ids assign` or IDs in source. Reusing the text of `website/content/cli/ids.mdx` is enough.
- Every fenced `calor` example on a new or changed page is 0.30 syntax and compiles: `calor self-check docs` exits 0 (CI step "Check agent-facing docs against the implementation (spec drift)", `.github/workflows/test.yml:266-267`), and `.github/workflows/website-tests.yml` passes.
- `DocDriftCheckerTests` passes. A page whose number of complete `calor` programs changed has its row in `PublicNativeReference_CompilesPositiveAndExactNegativeExamples` updated, and a new page that carries a complete program gets a row; if rows were added, `eng/test-manifest.json` carries the new `expectedTotal` for `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests` (22559 at HEAD, line 8).
- The new and changed pages follow `CLAUDE.md`, "Writing for the public surface": the guide explains sidecar, file label, registered project and transactional workspace edit in one clause each on first use, and the pull request description says the pages were read against that section.

The table describes the tools as they are at the commit this lands on. #1744 and #922 update it if they change behaviour afterwards.

Part of epic #1840. This issue is off the 0.33 exit chain and may move to 0.34 without holding the release.
```

**Why.** The body's baseline is false at HEAD bc80daeb: the sidecar and both `ids` commands are explained on two dedicated pages and noted on four syntax-reference pages. What a reader still cannot find is the task itself (which tool call renames or moves a declaration without losing its ID) and which operations each tool refuses, so the amendment turns "explain the sidecar" into a how-to with one support table and fixes the stale `ids assign` references found while checking. The issue is off the 0.33 exit chain and may slip to 0.34 without holding the release.

issues.title: [0.33] Decision: adopter checkpoint — consent recorded, or the fallback applies
issues.body:
## Change

Take and record one maintainer decision at the close of 0.33: has a named external maintainer agreed to the 0.36 pilot? The agent assigned prepares the record from the repository, with the fallback entry drafted in full and every consent field that is not in the repository marked "to be supplied by the maintainer". The maintainer keeps one of the two entries, completes it, and decides by merging. No agent contacts anyone or names a person.

The *external maintainer* is a person outside the project who would own one Calor component inside an existing application they maintain (#1701). The *adopter fallback* is the section of that name in the plan of record, `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md` (#1765): a table, written in advance, of what happens in 0.34 to 0.39 while nobody has consented. It covers which 0.36 issues are held and which still run, the disposition of each of #1708 to #1712, the two options for a fallback 0.37 (F1, no new run; F2, a fixture-scale extension labelled non-independent), the hold on 0.38 and 0.39, and the rows of 0.34 and 0.35 that stay. This issue applies that table and does not restate it.

The record is `docs/plans/0.33-adopter-checkpoint.md`. It is prepared when the three 0.33 exit criteria that other epics own (per-agent results, the Rust cost reference, `.calr` test discovery) are met or their declines are recorded, and it is merged before the release that completes 0.33 is cut. It has five parts:

1. *Inputs*, quoted with links: the adopter entry of `docs/plans/0.31-outreach-decision.md` (authorise, decline, or the default line; #1777) and any later entry that superseded it; the totals of the contact log in that file by outcome (contacts made, no reply, declined, interested, agreed in writing), with no name or message text the log does not already carry; whether `docs/plans/0.36-pilot-recruitment.md` exists and in which milestone it merged (#1791).
2. *Window.* Three dates and the days between them: outreach authorised, recruitment record opened, this checkpoint. If the authorise entry followed an earlier decline or default entry, say so and give that entry's date. If the recruitment record of #1791 merged in 0.32 and not in 0.31, add: "Recruitment had one milestone less than planned." If outreach was never authorised, write instead: "No outreach was authorised. This result is not a failed search."
3. *Outcome*: one dated line from the table below.
4. *Entry*: the consent entry or the fallback entry described below.
5. *How this record changes*: the rule at the end of this section, verbatim.

| Outcome line | Requires | Effect | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| P. `Outcome: consent recorded` | A complete consent entry | The 0.36 entry criterion on the adopter checkpoint is met. The fallback does not apply, and is lifted if #1777 applied it early. 0.34 runs at full scope. | This is the crossing the maintainer reserved (see Baseline). It creates obligations that outlive a later decision to stop: migration paths, the compatibility promise, maintenance expectations, exposure of the adopter. It commits maintainer support hours through 0.36. |
| F. `Outcome: demand unproven; the adopter fallback applies from <date>` | Nothing new | The fallback table applies. | What the table says. As proposed: 0.38, 0.39 and the pilot-dependent issues of 0.36 are held, 0.37 closes on the results already published (F1) or runs at fallback scope (F2), and 0.34 conversion coverage is narrowed. No comparison on independently authored tasks is collected. |

**Recommendation.** The plan prefers neither outcome on its merits. It recommends P only if the consent entry can be completed in full on the date, and F otherwise; a candidate who is interested but has not agreed in writing is F, with that status noted in part 1. It recommends against a third course, holding the 0.33 release for a pending reply: a later entry lifts the hold at no extra cost, while an open checkpoint leaves the scope of 0.34 undecided. P is never automatic. The maintainer may record F with a consenting candidate on file, and states the reason.

**A consent entry (P) records:**

- The adopting project or organisation by name. The person is named if they agree to be named in a public repository, otherwise by role, with the maintainer holding the identity outside the repository.
- That they are external: the person is not the Calor maintainer, the component is not in one of the maintainer's own projects, and at least one reviewer of the component is not the Calor maintainer.
- The agreement: its date, that it is in writing, and where it is held (a public link, or privately by the maintainer). It covers acting as external maintainer of one Calor component in a named application for the pilot #1701 describes. Approval of scope, acceptance criteria and baseline stays in #1701.
- What they were told before agreeing: Calor is pre-1.0 with one maintainer and a tested path back to C#; the compatibility promise as published or deferred under #1805; no economic or safety advantage over C# has been established. What was not promised: native compilation, whole-application migration.
- The support offered (hours; payment or none), within what #1777 authorised.

**A fallback entry (F) records:**

- The words "demand unproven" with the contact totals beside them, and the sentence: "This is a result about demand. It is not evidence about the language."
- The date from which the fallback applies: the date of the #1777 decline if one still stands, otherwise this record's date. If only the #1777 default line stands, say that issues were held from that line's date and that closures, the 0.34 cut and the choice of 0.37 option take effect from this record's date.
- Which of the two fallback-0.37 options applies, F1 or F2. The plan of record holds the rule for choosing. The entry quotes the rule's input: the result published under #1810 (the 0.32 re-run of the nine seeded-defect pairs with a third arm, C# equipped with executable specifications), with the reading #1816 registered for it, or that run's recorded decline. If the maintainer departs from the rule, the entry says so and why.
- A disposition list: one line for each issue the fallback table names, giving its disposition in the table's words (held, moved, re-scoped, closed as not planned, or unchanged).

**In the same pull request,** append one dated line to the list headed "Checkpoint log" at the end of the adopter fallback section of the plan of record: `Checkpoint <date>: <outcome line>; see docs/plans/0.33-adopter-checkpoint.md.` The table itself is not edited.

**After the merge,** the agent applies the record to the tracker. Every comment links the record.

- Under P: #1697 and #1701 each get a comment quoting the outcome line. If the fallback was applied earlier, on a decline or default entry of #1777, each issue it held gets a comment lifting the hold.
- Under F: each issue in the disposition list gets a comment quoting its line. A held issue stays open in its milestone with no work scheduled. An issue the table closes is closed as not planned and its milestone is cleared.
- Under both: #1659 gets a comment stating the scope 0.34 runs at: full scope, or the scope the fallback table gives.

**Default.** If the record is not merged when the 0.33 release is prepared and the other 0.33 exit criteria are met, the agent preparing the release appends one dated line to the checkpoint log, in the release pull request, so that the release is not held: `Checkpoint <date>: not decided, treated as the fallback outcome until changed.` The default has the effect the plan of record gives the #1777 default line. Every issue the fallback table holds is held from that date, and each one that carries no hold comment from #1777 gets one that links the log line and says "held by default, not a maintainer finding". The line is not the maintainer's finding, so "demand unproven" is not written, nothing is closed or re-scoped, and the 0.34 cut and the choice between F1 and F2 wait for a merged outcome. 0.36 is not entered. The line meets the 0.33 exit criterion; this issue stays open until the maintainer merges P or F, and the merged record then supersedes the line.

**The rule for part 5.** "Entries in this file are never edited. After outcome F, the hold is lifted only by a later dated entry in this file, merged by the maintainer, that is a complete consent entry. That entry lists the held issues that resume and any issue closed under the fallback that is reopened. Creator self-evaluation, AI review and the maintainer's own projects do not lift the hold. If consent is withdrawn after outcome P, a later dated entry records it and the fallback applies from that entry's date."

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- The repository records no named or consenting external maintainer. This rests on the three records cited in this section and a search of `docs/` and `website/content/` for a secured or consenting adopter; it is not an exhaustive proof. Call W (2026-08-04) recorded the adopter input as "DEMAND UNPROVEN" because "no adopter is secured" (`docs/plans/call-w-adjudication.md:28-34`), with the policy "do not fund new adoption *depth* ahead of demand" (`:39-41`).
- Naming an adopter is "the maintainer's reserved one-way door" (`docs/plans/call-w-adjudication.md:42-43`; restated in `docs/plans/call-s-adjudication.md:187-190`). The register of one-way doors says the adoption step "Creates obligations that outlive a program decision: migration paths, compatibility promises, maintenance expectations, reputational exposure to adopters if later killed" (`docs/plans/loop-plan-v0.9.md:185`).
- The repository records no authorised outreach. The gate record of 2026-10-01 lists permitted organisations "None", permitted human contacts "None" and "Contacts made" 0 (`docs/plans/safe-delegation-m0/v0.23/r2a-adopter-unavailable.md:25-30`), and says "no campaign was run" (`:53-54`). The record of 2026-09-09 found no dated recruitment log after Call W and says "Unknown activity is not a failed search" (`docs/plans/safe-delegation-m0/supply-status.md:17-25`). It also asks that names and messages are not published without consent (`:83`).
- The registered condition is a "named adopter with ≥1 non-maintainer reviewer, agreed in writing", and failing it concludes "demand unproven" (`docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md:73`). The maintainer's own projects are "pilot substrate only", and adopter failure "produces no benchmark evidence either way" (`docs/plans/agent-native-strategy.md:72-73`).
- #1701 asks for "a named external maintainer and one real component inside an existing application", approved "without being promised native compilation or whole-application migration", and says inability to recruit "is reported as a blocker, not replaced by creator self-evaluation" (tracker snapshot of 2026-11-23).
- The adoption guide says the project "has not established a qualifying adopter" (`website/content/guides/adoption-playbook.mdx:12-13`), and `website/tests/public-claims.spec.ts:607` asserts the phrase.
- None of these files exists yet: `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md` (#1765), `docs/plans/0.31-outreach-decision.md` (#1777), `docs/plans/0.36-pilot-recruitment.md` (#1791), `docs/plans/0.33-adopter-checkpoint.md`.
- This record is a decision, not a registration, so it does not go into Annex A of `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md`, which the `annex-freeze` job holds append-only (`scripts/check-annex-freeze.py`; `.github/workflows/experiment-registry-tamper-check.yml:98`). `docs/plans/evidence/` accepts no new file (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/Plans/EvidenceTreeGuardTests.cs`).

## Why

Milestones 0.36 to 0.39 depend on a person the project does not have. Three records (2026-08-04, 2026-09-09 and 2026-10-01, in the baseline above) show no adopter, and none shows outreach: activity after Call W is recorded as unknown, and the one authorisation on record permitted no contacts. A checkpoint with a date and an else-branch written in advance makes the answer "nobody" change the plan on a known day instead of blocking it on an unknown one. The else-branch has to name issues before it can be applied: a fallback that says only "re-scope 0.37" leaves #1708 waiting on pilot findings that never arrive and #1709 to #1712 waiting on #1708, and does not say which 0.34 rows are cut. The table is therefore written in the plan of record in 0.31, so that an early decline (#1777) and this checkpoint apply the same text, and this issue is where it is applied. The 0.34 and 0.36 entry criteria both read this record.

## Done when

- `docs/plans/0.33-adopter-checkpoint.md` is merged by the maintainer with the five parts and exactly one dated outcome line, worded as in the table.
- Part 1 quotes the adopter entry of `docs/plans/0.31-outreach-decision.md` and gives the contact totals by outcome. Part 2 has the three dates, or the "No outreach was authorised" sentence, and the two shorter-window statements where their conditions hold.
- Under P: every field of the consent entry is filled and none reads "to be supplied by the maintainer"; #1697 and #1701 carry the comment.
- Under F: the words "demand unproven" stand beside the contact totals; the fallback-0.37 option is named with the rule's input quoted; the disposition list has one line for every issue named in the adopter fallback section of the plan of record; each of those issues carries a comment that links this record and states the same disposition; every issue closed as not planned has no milestone; every held issue is open.
- Part 5 contains the rule verbatim.
- #1659 carries the comment on the scope of 0.34.
- `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md` has the dated line in its checkpoint log, and its diff is that one added line.
- If the release was prepared before the merge: the checkpoint log carries the default line word for word, every issue the fallback table holds carries a hold comment, nothing was closed or re-scoped on the strength of the line, and this issue is still open.
- The pull request changes those two files only (`git diff --name-only <base>...HEAD` prints two paths). The record states that it authorises no paid run and names no methods reviewer. No test is added, so `eng/test-manifest.json` does not change.

## Not in scope

- Writing or changing the fallback table (#1765); authorising outreach and keeping the contact log (#1777).
- Approving the pilot's scope, acceptance criteria and baseline (#1701).
- The methods reviewer (#1857) and the collection budget (#1867).
- Changing any public claim. An agreement to start is not a qualifying adopter; the adoption guide's sentence stays until the exit record of #1697.
- Contact with a candidate by an agent, under either outcome.

Part of epic #1826. Depends on #1777, #1765. Blocks #1697, #1701, #1698.

issues.title: [0.33] Re-affirm the edition after #1650 and the per-agent results (#1811) report
issues.body:
## Change

Take and record one maintainer decision at the close of 0.33: does the edition declared under #1805 stand after the first results from agents other than Claude Code? The agent assigned prepares `docs/plans/0.33-edition-reaffirmation.md`. The maintainer decides by merging it, before the release that completes 0.33 is cut. This issue changes no compiler behaviour and runs no agent.

An *edition* is a named set of accepted spellings and default-on hard errors that the project has promised not to break (the promise is #1805; the per-module marker is #1084). Below, **E** is the commit named in the declaration record `docs/plans/0.32-edition-declaration.md`, and **C** is the commit on `main` at which this record is prepared, after #1650 and #1811 are closed and #1825 is closed or held under its tool-layout gate.

The two reports in the title are the per-agent `calor init` output (#1650) and the per-agent results (#1811: the paid runs on the drivers #1651 delivers, and their publication). While the spend for #1811 is neither authorised nor declined, this issue waits.

**The record has five parts.**

1. *Inputs*, each linked: the declaration record (its option, the edition's name, E, any exceptions, and the wording it settled for soundness fixes, tool layout and what is not promised); #1650 as merged; the per-agent results published under #1811 (the 0.33 notes in `CHANGELOG.md` and the rows in `docs/benchmarking/evidence-ledger.md`) with the hand-over list #1811 posts on this issue, or the dated "Declined" line for the per-agent part in `docs/plans/0.33-paid-run-registration.md` (#1832); the outcome of any smoke run under #709 or #711.
2. *Changes since the declaration.* One row per pull request that changed the language surface between E and C, found with `git log --oneline <E>..<C> -- src/Calor.Compiler/Parsing src/Calor.Compiler/Diagnostics/Diagnostic.cs src/Calor.Compiler/Manifests src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Teaching/reference.json CHANGELOG.md`. Read every `CHANGELOG.md` entry added since E as well: a check that was tightened without a new diagnostic code shows only there. A check tightened under an existing code in `src/Calor.Compiler/Analysis`, `Binding`, `TypeChecking` or `Effects` with no changelog entry appears in neither list and is caught only by part 3; the record states that limit. Each row gets one class:
   - `additive`: a new accepted form. No module that compiled at E stops compiling or changes meaning, and no word is newly reserved.
   - `warning`: a new or changed warning, diagnostic text or fix.
   - `tool layout`: a change to what a file location or a command means. #1825 is listed here: top-level `tests/*.calr` files become test sources for `calor test`, `calor check` and `calor_check` and leave the library compilation. If #1825 is held because the declaration's promise covers tool layout and no choice is recorded, there is no such row; the record instead carries a dated entry that states the hold and what the 0.33 release does (ships without `.calr` tests, or waits).
   - `soundness fix`: a change that rejects a program that compiled at E by withdrawing an unsound acceptance (a false proof, an unsound built-in effect contract), with the number of corpus files affected.
   - `excepted form`: a change to a form the declaration listed as an exception.
   - `breaking`: anything else that removes a spelling, changes a meaning, or adds a default-on hard error on a program that compiled at E.

   Quote the declaration's wording on tool layout and on soundness fixes. If it does not place one of them outside the promise, a row of that class is `breaking`, unless the declaration record carries an exception for that change (#1825 records one there if the maintainer chose it); the row is then an `excepted form`. A `breaking` row rules out A and B. Report it to the maintainer before part 5 is drafted: either the change is reverted or made additive in its own pull request and the record is prepared again at the new C, or the decision is C.
3. *Unchanged-source check.* Two comparisons between E and C, each with its command and counts.
   - (a) The `programs` list of `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Teaching/reference.json`, compared by `id`: every program present at E has identical `calor` text at C, or is listed with the pull request that changed or removed it and the reason. With the working tree at C:

     ```
     git show <E>:src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Teaching/reference.json > /tmp/reference-E.json
     python3 -c "
     import json, sys
     old = {p['id']: p['calor'] for p in json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))['programs']}
     new = {p['id']: p['calor'] for p in json.load(open(sys.argv[2]))['programs']}
     print(len(old), 'programs at E; removed:', sorted(set(old) - set(new)), 'changed:', sorted(i for i in old if i in new and old[i] != new[i]))
     " /tmp/reference-E.json src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Teaching/reference.json
     ```
   - (b) `git diff --name-status <E> <C> -- '*.calr'`: every modified, deleted or renamed file outside the legacy-dialect allowlist that #1763 added is listed the same way.

   CI at C compiles the teaching programs (`calor self-check docs`; established for this issue by reading `src/Calor.Compiler/SelfCheck/ExemplarCompileChecker.cs`, not by running it) and the fixtures its tests read, so an unchanged source in those sets that compiled at E compiles at C. An edit that was needed to keep a source compiling is a `breaking` row in part 2. The check shows acceptance for sources CI compiles; meaning is covered only as far as existing tests assert it.
4. *Per-agent findings.* One row per agent: Claude Code (from the most recent published run on the edition's spellings: the #1645 re-run, or #1605 if that re-run was declined), Codex, Gemini, Copilot. A finding names the form or diagnostic code, the count with its denominator, and the source. Findings come from five places: the hand-over list #1811 posts on this issue (per agent, the diagnostics it hit most often and every removed or unknown form it tried to write); whatever the reading registered in #1832 for that agent's outcome sends to this issue; every form whose wrong-form error count for that agent meets the threshold in part C of the amended spelling rule (`docs/design/0.32-breaking-window.md`, #1785), if one was recorded; every per-agent entry #1650 added to `reference.json` that tells one agent how to write a form; any form named in a #709 or #711 record. An agent with none reads "no finding", or carries the outcome #1811 published for it ("not measured", "not measurable headlessly" or "declined") with the reason. Each finding gets one disposition, with a link:
   - `teaching`: reference or per-agent text changed.
   - `diagnostic`: the message or the fix offered for the wrong form was changed. The wrong form was already an error, so nothing that compiled is rejected.
   - `additive`: a form added in 0.33 and spelled under the amended rule, with a test that the edition spelling still compiles to the same C#, and the tokens it added to the teaching reference. It may not bring back Option, Result or `requires` (#1617, #1618).
   - `next-edition candidate`: no change now. The form, the evidence and the measured cost are recorded.
   - `none`, with the reason.
5. *Decision*: one dated line, `Decision: A`, `Decision: B` or `Decision: C`.

Each exception the declaration listed expires here. Mark it *resolved* (its resolving issue is closed) or *lapsed* (the form joins the promise as it stands at C). None is extended.

| Option | Meaning | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| A. Re-affirm | The edition stands. Requires no `breaking` row, a disposition for every finding, and every exception resolved or lapsed. | A form that an agent measurably gets wrong stays for the life of the edition. The only remedies are teaching, diagnostics and additive forms. |
| B. Re-affirm and file a second-edition proposal | As A. In addition one issue is filed, with no milestone, proposing the respelling of each `next-edition candidate` with its `calor fix` rule. No spelling changes in 0.33. | None in 0.31 to 0.39: the proposal is backlog and claims no capacity until a later milestone names what it displaces. The 0.36 pilot starts on the first edition and would migrate later. |
| C. Change a spelling now | A second edition inside 0.33: a new marker value (#1084), a `calor fix` rule that migrates fixtures, benchmark pairs and documentation in the same change (the standing rule #1806 sets), the instruments re-registered as in #1807, and a compiler that accepts both editions. | Nothing in 0.33 is sized for it. The per-agent results just published describe the old spelling, and a re-run needs a new decision line under #1832. The 0.33 exit criterion is then met only by this record stating what the 0.33 release does (ships on the first edition, or waits for the second). The 0.36 entry criterion "Edition in force" is met only when the issue this record names for the second edition is closed and the promise names that edition (#1697). |

**Recommendation.** A when no finding is a `next-edition candidate`. B when at least one is; where #1785 recorded a part C threshold, a finding is a candidate only if its count meets that threshold for at least one agent. The plan recommends against C: it repeats the 0.32 window in a milestone with no room for it, and it makes the measurements that motivated it stale. If the per-agent spend was declined, A is still available; the record then carries the sentence "Re-affirmed without per-agent measurement" and names the last agent run on the edition's spellings with its commit.

**If the declaration was deferred.** If the declaration record holds option C of #1805, there is nothing to re-affirm, and this issue takes the declaration decision itself. Read the deferral terms in that record first: the spellings still open and the milestone it names for retaking the declaration. #1805's gate, options, promise text and list of what is recorded apply. Parts 2 to 4 are its evidence and run from the post-rewrite commit that #1807 posted. The 0.33 exit criterion is met by a declaration taken here, or by a second deferral that records its effect on the 0.36 entry criterion "Edition in force" (a deferral does not satisfy it) and the maintainer's decision on whether 0.33 is released without an edition.

**In the same pull request,** add one line under `## [Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md`, the section the 0.33 release notes are cut from: the decision, the number of `additive` rows, the tool-layout change and a link to the record.

**After the merge,** post the link on #1697, whose entry criteria require the edition in force, and on #1701, whose sign-off lists the promise.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- No edition exists. `git grep -i edition -- src` prints nothing, and neither `docs/plans/0.32-edition-declaration.md` nor `docs/semantics/editions.md` exists (#1805 and #1084 create them).
