The adoption guide says "there is no broader compatibility promise yet" (`website/content/guides/adoption-playbook.mdx:19-20`).
- No agent has been measured on the 0.30 spellings: the 0.30.0 release "publishes no new benchmark results" (`CHANGELOG.md:15`). The pair harness starts only the `claude` CLI (`bench/phase0-agent-native/run-pair.sh:1352-1353`). The only benchmark pair run by another agent that is recorded under `bench/phase0-agent-native/` is one Codex CLI 0.144.6 session on 2026-07-22, with Calor 0.7.0 on the pre-0.30 syntax (`bench/phase0-agent-native/CODEX-SMOKE.md:3`, `:13-16`; the same session is in `bench/phase0-agent-native/codex-smoke-709/evidence.json`).
- The spellings were chosen by fewest tokens on one tokenizer, Claude Opus 5.5 through `count_tokens` (`docs/design/0.30-syntax-token-decision.md:3`, `:7`). That record calls some choices weak: `→` and `func` "win by 1 token each, in one context only" (`:570`). Two forms look like C# and mean something else: `var` "is mutability, not a type-inference keyword" (`docs/syntax-reference/current-language.md:59`), and `=>` before a body is a postcondition (`:403`).
- The four `calor init` instruction templates are byte-identical (one md5 over `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Templates/*.md.template`, measured with `md5sum`), so no per-agent text exists yet.
- A `tests/*.calr` file is library source today. `ExecutionWorkspace.ResolveSources` takes every `*.calr` file under the target except those under `bin/`, `obj/` and `reference/` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/ExecutionWorkspace.cs:189`, `:222-231`), and test discovery reads only top-level `tests/*.cs` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/TestCommand.cs:404-431`).
- Keywords are one global table (`src/Calor.Compiler/Parsing/Lexer.cs:22`, lookup at `:944`): a word added to it is lexed as a keyword in every module. The parser takes a keyword as a name only at the positions that check for one (for example `ParseVerbatimIdentifier`, `src/Calor.Compiler/Parsing/Parser.cs:3161-3165`), so a newly reserved word can reject a program that used it as an identifier. That is why reserving a word is not `additive`.
- The teaching reference holds 87 complete programs (the `programs` list of `reference.json`, counted with a JSON reader), compiled in CI by `calor self-check docs` (`.github/workflows/test.yml:267`). The tree tracks 1,823 `.calr` files, 853 of them in the retired `§` syntax (`git ls-files '*.calr'`, scanned for `§`). Built-in effect contracts are the `*.calor-effects.json` files under `src/Calor.Compiler/Manifests/`.
- No CI job checks source compatibility across compiler versions: `grep -i -n 'edition\|backward\|compatib' .github/workflows/*.yml` finds one unrelated comment in `build-z3.yml`.
- `CHANGELOG.md` opens with an empty `## [Unreleased]` section (`:5`). The release procedure renames it to the version being released (`.claude/skills/create-release/SKILL.md:58`), so a line added there before the 0.33 release appears in the 0.33 release notes.

## Why

The edition is declared at the end of 0.32 on spellings that a single agent has run. 0.33 measures three more. Without a second look, a per-agent result either reopens a spelling quietly, weeks after the project promised not to, or is set aside with no record of why. Re-affirming at the close of 0.33 writes the choice down before 0.36, where an external maintainer signs off on the promise (#1701). The record is also the promise's first check: parts 2 and 3 list every change since the declaration and show whether any source had to be edited to keep compiling.

## Done when

- `docs/plans/0.33-edition-reaffirmation.md` is merged by the maintainer with the five parts and one dated decision line. Where the declaration was deferred, the line is the #1805 decision line.
- Part 2 names E and C and accounts for every commit the stated `git log` command prints. Each row has one class. #1825 is a `tool layout` row with the declaration's wording on tool layout quoted; or, where #1825 is held, the record carries the dated entry stating the hold and what the 0.33 release does.
- Under A or B, part 2 has no `breaking` row.
- Part 3 gives both comparisons with their commands and counts, and lists every changed, removed or renamed source with a reason.
- Part 4 has a row for each of the four agents. Each finding has one disposition and a link. On a decline of the per-agent spend, the record carries the sentence "Re-affirmed without per-agent measurement".
- Every exception from the declaration is marked resolved or lapsed.
- Under B, the proposal issue is linked and has no milestone. Under C, the record names the issue that carries the second edition and states what the 0.33 release does. Where the declaration is deferred a second time, the record states the effect on the 0.36 entry criterion and the same decision on the release.
- `CHANGELOG.md` has the line in the section that becomes the 0.33 release notes, and #1697 and #1701 each carry a comment linking the record.
- The pull request changes `docs/plans/0.33-edition-reaffirmation.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` only. Where the declaration is taken here, it also changes the files #1805 lists for the option taken. No file under `src/` changes. No test is added, so `eng/test-manifest.json` does not change.

## Not in scope

- The declaration and the promise text (#1805), the marker (#1084) and the rewriter (#1806), except in the deferred case above.
- The per-agent runs and their spend (#1811, #1832). This record authorises no run.
- Making an additive change, a teaching change or a diagnostic fix. Each is made in its own issue and only listed here.
- A CI job that checks the promise on every change. No open issue owns one; this record does the check once, by hand.
- Defining or implementing a second edition, and ranking agents against each other.

Part of epic #1826. Depends on #1650, #1805, #1811, #1825. The dependency on #1811 is met by its published results or by its closure on a recorded decline. #1825 is a dependency because its tool-layout change is a row of part 2; it is met by that issue's closure or by its recorded hold.

issues.title: [0.34] Epic: native conversion coverage
issues.body:
**Current.** The body gives a baseline of "48 constructs `NotSupported`" at HEAD 512491093 and a table that assigns 43 registry names to five family issues (#1654 to #1658). It is done when each family converts or has a recorded reason, the native fraction rises on every corpus project, the token ratio falls further below 1.0x, and runtime-equivalence tests cover every newly native construct.

**Amendment.** Replace the whole body with the text under "## Epic body" at the top of this file. The title and labels are unchanged. Five things change in substance:

- The baseline is 58 entries at 0.30.0 plus the C# 15 entries #1638 adds, restated at 0.34 entry and again when #1638 closes if that is later. Each entry is assigned to one owner in a table regenerated from the registry.
- The children gain #1850, #1733, #1747, #1742 and #1844.
- #1654 to #1658 become tracking issues delivered as one pull request per construct, each starting with a count.
- "Native fraction rises" and "ratio falls further below 1.0x" are replaced by "native fraction reported per project and not lower", the standing acceptance rule, and the separate density target #1844. Because the scorecard is already at 100 of 100 it acts only as a floor, and each newly native construct adds a scorecard snippet.
- New source forms are additive, are decided under the rule #1785 amends, and are documented within the budget #1823 records.

**Why.** The registry has 58 unsupported entries, not 48, and record classes and `lock` are already native. 23 entries had no owner, so the 0.34 exit criterion could not be evaluated. #1638 adds registry entries and may close after 0.34 starts, so the baseline is restated at entry and again when it closes. The native fraction that the exit criterion requires, and the numbers every child's standing acceptance rule reads, come from the corpus report job, which is why the epic depends on #1779.

Depends on #1779.

issues.title: [0.34] Native record structs and the record shapes still preserved
issues.body:
*The old body is stale: it says "Today `record` is `NotSupported`", but record classes convert natively at HEAD and the two scorecard snippets it cites (044 and 100) are pinned native.*

## Change

Convert natively the record shapes that the converter still preserves as raw C# (the original text kept inside a raw frame in the `.calr` file). This is a tracking issue delivered as ordered pull requests:

1. **Count.** Count each shape in the table in the library sources of MediatR, Serilog and FluentValidation (git submodules under `bench/corpus/`; the three source directories are listed at `scripts/default_migrate_report.py:22-26`). Count in the original C#, because a file preserved whole records no loss for the shapes inside it. Write the counts and the method into the "Family shapes" part of the coverage record `docs/plans/0.34-native-coverage.md` (#1659 defines its layout; create the file with that layout if #1850 has not).
2. **`record struct` and `readonly record struct`**, positional and nominal. Required.
3. **Every other shape in the table**, one pull request per shape: convert it, or record why it stays preserved.

| Shape | Preservation reason | Decided at |
|---|---|---|
| `record struct`, `readonly record struct` | `record-struct` | `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/FeatureSupport.cs:1533-1534` |
| `partial record` | `record-partial` | `FeatureSupport.cs:1537-1538` |
| Positional parameter with an attribute or a modifier | `record-positional-parameter-metadata` | `FeatureSupport.cs:1541-1544` |
| Record nested in a class, struct or interface | `record-nested-declaration` | `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/RoslynSyntaxVisitor.cs:2337`, `:3051`, `:3640`, `:6087` |
| Member other than a field, property, indexer, constructor, method, operator or conversion (an event, a nested type) | `record-member-<SyntaxKind>` | `RoslynSyntaxVisitor.cs:3389-3390` |
| Base call with a named or `ref`/`out`/`in` argument | `record-base-argument-metadata` | `RoslynSyntaxVisitor.cs:3343-3345` |
| Base type the semantic model cannot classify | `record-unresolved-base-kind` | `RoslynSyntaxVisitor.cs:3350-3351` |
| Record body that contains `#if` regions | `record-conditional-members` | `RoslynSyntaxVisitor.cs:3313-3314` |
| `unsafe record` | `unsafe` | `FeatureSupport.cs:1539-1540` |

Spelling. A record struct needs a source form, and its spelling is decided in this issue. The candidate that adds no keyword reuses the modifier a `class` header already takes after the name (`class Name struct`, `docs/syntax-reference/current-language.md:929-933`) on the existing record header (`record Point (int:X, int:Y)`, `:625-629`). The form is additive and changes no existing spelling. Decide it under the fewest-tokens rule as #1785 amends it, and record the candidates, their token counts and the choice in the "New source forms" part of the coverage record. Document it where the #1823 record puts conversion forms; if that is the language reference, edit `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Teaching/reference.json`, regenerate `current-language.md` with `calor self-check docs --fix`, and stay under the 17,000-token ratchet (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/TokenBudgetTests.cs:57-63`; 16,750 measured on 2026-11-20).

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- `record` is `Full` (`FeatureSupport.cs:60-66`); its description lists record structs, partial or nested declarations, positional parameter attributes and modifiers, and conditional and unrepresented members as preserved. `with` expressions are `Full` (`:581-586`).
- `ConvertRecord` escalates to preservation at the sites in the table (`RoslynSyntaxVisitor.cs:3309-3392`).
- Tests pin both sides. Native: `NativeRecordTests.OriginalScorecardInputs_AreNativeAndReparseWithEffects` (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/NativeRecordTests.cs:118`) for snippets 044 and 100. Preserved: `UnsupportedVariants_PreserveExactCSharpWithExplicitReason` (`:303-318`) for `record-struct`, `record-positional-parameter-metadata`, `record-member-EventFieldDeclaration` and `record-partial`; `RecordVariants_PreserveKindAndCompile`, `RecordNestedInOtherType_IsNeverDropped` and `NestedRecord_IsPreservedAsInterop` (`tests/Calor.Conversion.Tests/RegistryConformanceTests.cs:121`, `:152`, `:207`).
- The reference says record structs and partial or nested declarations "remain exact converter-owned C# fallback" (`docs/syntax-reference/current-language.md:627`, generated from `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Teaching/reference.json:708`).
- `record` has a registered D-S1.5 fixture, `bench/phase0-agent-native/fixtures/d-s1.5/record/`; its `input.cs` contains a record class only. No shape in the table is a registry entry, so none has a level to promote: the `record` entry is `Full` today and stays `Full` (`calor feature-check record` shows the entry).
- How often each shape occurs in the corpus is not measured.

## Why

Records are in everyday C#, and Calor's effect and nullability checks do not apply to the members of a preserved record. Record classes are done; what remains is a list of narrower shapes, and nobody has counted which of them real code uses. Counting first keeps the work on the shapes that raise the native share.

## Done when

- The "Family shapes" part of the coverage record `docs/plans/0.34-native-coverage.md` holds, for each shape in the table, its count per corpus project and the method used.
- `record struct` and `readonly record struct` convert under default `calor convert` with no raw frame and no loss. The preservation assertions for `record-struct` in the tests above are replaced by assertions on the native AST and on the emitted CLR type (a value type that is a record).
- A runtime test compares equality, hash code, `ToString`, deconstruction, `with` and `default` of a converted record struct with the same declaration compiled as C#, as `PositionalRecord_ClrIdentityEqualityCloneDeconstructionAndDefaultsMatchIndependentOracle` (`NativeRecordTests.cs:134`) does for record classes.
- Every other shape in the table is native with its preservation test replaced by an assertion on native output and a runtime test, or has a row in the coverage record with its count and a reason kind (`bucket`, `zero-in-corpus`, `unmodeled`, `no-form` or `not-reached`, defined in #1659 and in the record's header; `no-demand` only if the adopter fallback applies).
- The `record` description in `FeatureSupport.cs` and the record entry in `reference.json` list only the shapes still preserved, and `website/public/data/feature-support.json` is regenerated with `calor feature-check --list`. The phrase "partial or nested declarations" in the record entry is allowlisted in `WebsiteFeatureSupportParityTests.NotClaims` (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/WebsiteFeatureSupportParityTests.cs:66`), and every allowlist entry must be used, so that entry changes with the description.
- A scorecard snippet with a record struct is added to `tests/TestData/CSharpImport/manifest.json`, and `BASELINE_FULLY_CONVERTED`, `BASELINE_ROUNDTRIP`, the total asserted at `tests/Calor.Evaluation/Scorecard/ConversionScorecardTests.cs:115` and `tests/Calor.Evaluation/Scorecard/baseline.json` rise with it.
- Standing acceptance rule, per pull request that makes a shape native: the conversion scorecard's fully converted count does not fall (100 of 100 at HEAD bc80daeb, `ConversionScorecardTests.cs:31`); the per-project Calor/C# token ratio does not rise, read from the corpus report job (#1779) with the columns #1746 adds or, if #1746 has slipped, by the hand method #1746 records; the pull request states how many corpus files newly fall to whole-file preservation.
- `expectedTotal` in `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated for each test project whose test count changes (`scripts/check_trx.py` enforces it in CI).

## Not in scope

- Record classes (native since 0.30).
- `file record`: its reason is `file-scoped-type` (`FeatureSupport.cs:1535-1536`), owned by #1658.
- A new form for conditional compilation. The `record-conditional-members` shape uses the `pp` form that branches around class and struct members already have (`docs/syntax-reference/current-language.md:908-912`); #1657 extends that form to other positions.

issues.title: [0.34] Native using declarations, await using, checked blocks and standalone blocks
issues.body:
*The old body is stale: `lock` is fully supported at HEAD, the line numbers it cites have moved, and it describes the `checked` block by its Lossy-mode behaviour only.*

## Change

Take four statement forms in turn: convert each natively, or record why it stays preserved as raw C# (the original text kept inside a raw frame in the `.calr` file). This is a tracking issue delivered as ordered pull requests. The first is a count of all four forms in the library sources of MediatR, Serilog and FluentValidation (git submodules under `bench/corpus/`; the three source directories are listed at `scripts/default_migrate_report.py:22-26`), taken in the original C# with `SyntaxCapabilityClassifier.Detect` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/FeatureSupport.cs:1621-1699`) for the first three and a syntax walk for `checked` and `unchecked` statements, and written into the coverage record `docs/plans/0.34-native-coverage.md` (#1659 defines its layout; create the file with that layout if #1850 has not). Then one pull request per form:

1. **`using` declaration** (`using var x = ...;`). The registry's own workaround names a candidate that needs no new form: an explicit `using` statement with the same lifetime, that is, the existing block form (`using type:name = resource` with an indented body, `docs/syntax-reference/current-language.md:538-548`) whose body is the rest of the enclosing block. Decide whether that lowering is the canonical form or a declaration form is added.
2. **`await using`**, statement and declaration. There is no native asynchronous-disposal form; the spelling is decided here.
3. **Standalone block** (`{ ... }` as a statement). There is no native lexical-scope node; the spelling is decided here. The `for` lowering already fakes a scope with `if true` wrappers (`src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/RoslynSyntaxVisitor.cs:10216-10223`); if a scope form is added, that lowering uses it.
4. **`checked { }` and `unchecked { }` statements.** Correct the registry entry `checked-block` first: lower its level to `NotSupported`, since default conversion preserves the whole statement, and rewrite its description to say so. A demotion needs no fixture. Then convert natively, which promotes the entry again and needs a registered fixture, or record the reason. Whether the statement form reuses the spelling of the native `checked(expr)` expression or needs a block form is decided here.

Any new form is additive and changes no existing spelling. Its spelling is decided in this issue under the fewest-tokens rule as #1785 amends it, and the candidates, their token counts and the choice are recorded in the "New source forms" part of the coverage record. Document it where the #1823 record puts conversion forms; if that is the language reference, edit `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Teaching/reference.json`, regenerate `docs/syntax-reference/current-language.md` with `calor self-check docs --fix`, and stay under the 17,000-token ratchet (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/TokenBudgetTests.cs:57-63`; 16,750 measured on 2026-11-20).

Semantics to preserve: disposal order across several resources and on exception paths; `DisposeAsync` being awaited; scope boundaries (a name declared in one block and reused in a sibling block); overflow trapping in `checked` and wrapping in `unchecked`.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- `lock-statement` is `Full` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/FeatureSupport.cs:621-626`); `ConvertLockStatement` builds a `SyncBlockNode` (`RoslynSyntaxVisitor.cs:7412-7422`), written `lock gate` (`current-language.md:741-745`).
- `using-declaration` (`FeatureSupport.cs:648-654`), `await-using` (`:634-640`) and `standalone-block` (`:655-661`) are `NotSupported`. `SyntaxCapabilityClassifier.Detect` flags them (`:1671-1691`) and the whole containing member is preserved. Tests that pin this: `MemberLifetimeOrRefSafetySemantics_PreserveWholeMember` (`tests/Calor.Conversion.Tests/RegistryConformanceTests.cs:1264`; the `using` declaration and both `await using` forms), `SyntaxCapabilityClassifier_DetectsRequiredUnsupportedFeature` (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/FeatureCheckCommandTests.cs:747`; all three), `FeatureCheck_NotSupported_ReturnsNotSupportedLevel` (`:505`; `using-declaration` and `standalone-block`) and the `standalone-block` case of `ConverterMarkers_StatementProducerEntriesKeepTheirExactRecordedLoss` (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/CSharpInteropBlockTests.cs:189-193`).
- `checked-block` is labelled `Full` with the description "checked/unchecked wrapper stripped, body statements fully preserved" (`FeatureSupport.cs:563-568`). That describes Lossy fidelity only (`ConversionFidelity.Lossy`, still used by the round-trip harness's `lossy` leg, `.github/workflows/test.yml:966-967`; the `--lossy` command-line option was removed in 0.30, `CHANGELOG.md:82-83`): there the wrapper is dropped with a `Dropped` loss. Under the default Lossless fidelity the whole statement is preserved as a raw frame with reason `checked-block` (`ConvertCheckedStatements`, `RoslynSyntaxVisitor.cs:7437-7467`; pinned by the first case of `ConverterMarkers_StatementFallbacksCarryTheirRecordedReason`, `CSharpInteropBlockTests.cs:156-161`). `MigrationAnalyzerTests.cs:1179` pins that the analyzer does not report it as a blocker.
- `checked(expr)` and `unchecked(expr)` expressions are native (`FeatureSupport.cs:569-580`; `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/CalorEmitter.cs:3698-3702`) and have registered fixtures (`bench/phase0-agent-native/fixtures/d-s1.5/checked-expression/` and `unchecked-expression/`).
- The block form of `using` is native (`ConvertUsingStatement`, `RoslynSyntaxVisitor.cs:10468`).

## Why

A `using` declaration or a bare block preserves the whole member that contains it, so one line removes a method from effect and nullability checking. The disposal spike #1842 counts undisposed locals and cannot say anything about code whose `using` declarations are preserved, so it waits for this issue.

## Done when

- The registry table of the coverage record `docs/plans/0.34-native-coverage.md` has a row for each of `using-declaration`, `await-using`, `standalone-block` and `checked-block` with its count per corpus project and the method used.
- For each construct made native: default `calor convert` produces no raw frame for it; it leaves `SyntaxCapabilityClassifier.RequiredUnsupportedFeatures` (`FeatureSupport.cs:1596-1614`); the tests above assert native output instead of preservation; the registry entry is promoted with a registered fixture under `bench/phase0-agent-native/fixtures/d-s1.5/` whose `fixture.json` names the entry in `featureKey` (schema in the `README.md` there), and the `d-s1.5-fixtures` job is green. The fixture's runtime check observes: for `using` and `await using`, the disposal order of two resources on normal exit and when the body throws; for a standalone block, a name reused in two sibling blocks; for `checked` and `unchecked`, an overflow that throws in one and wraps in the other.
- For each construct not made native: its row carries a reason kind (`bucket`, `zero-in-corpus`, `unmodeled`, `no-form` or `not-reached`, defined in #1659 and in the record's header; `no-demand` only if the adopter fallback applies).
- `checked-block`'s level and description in `FeatureSupport.cs` state what default conversion does, and `website/public/data/feature-support.json` is regenerated with `calor feature-check --list`.
- One scorecard snippet per newly native construct is added to `tests/TestData/CSharpImport/manifest.json`, and `BASELINE_FULLY_CONVERTED`, `BASELINE_ROUNDTRIP`, the total asserted at `tests/Calor.Evaluation/Scorecard/ConversionScorecardTests.cs:115` and `tests/Calor.Evaluation/Scorecard/baseline.json` rise with it.
- Standing acceptance rule, per pull request that makes a construct native: the conversion scorecard's fully converted count does not fall (100 of 100 at HEAD bc80daeb, `ConversionScorecardTests.cs:31`); the per-project Calor/C# token ratio does not rise, read from the corpus report job (#1779) with the columns #1746 adds or, if #1746 has slipped, by the hand method #1746 records; the pull request states how many corpus files newly fall to whole-file preservation.
- `expectedTotal` in `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated for each test project whose test count changes (`scripts/check_trx.py` enforces it in CI).
- When this issue closes, a comment on #1842 says which of `using` declarations and `await using` became native.

## Not in scope

- `lock` (native).
- `await foreach` (`await-foreach`, dispositioned in #1850; it shares the asynchronous-disposal question, so decide the two together).
- Any check that a disposable is disposed: #1842.

Part of #1659. Blocks #1842.

issues.body:
*The old body is stale: three of the entries it lists are already `Full` (`utf8-string-literal`, `char-literal`, `type-pattern`) and two are `Partial` (`complex-is-pattern`, `string-interpolation-hole`).*

## Change

Sixteen registry entries remain `NotSupported`: the converter keeps the construct as raw C# (the original text inside a raw frame in the `.calr` file). Count them first, then convert or record each. This is a tracking issue delivered as ordered pull requests, following the steps below the table. Line numbers are in `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/FeatureSupport.cs`; `calor feature-check <entry>` shows an entry.

| Entry | Lines | What is preserved today |
|---|---|---|
| `file-scoped-type` | 882-888 | The whole `file` class, struct, interface, enum or delegate |
| `using-type-alias` | 903-909 | Not established: the name is produced only by `MigrationAnalyzer` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Analysis/MigrationAnalyzer.cs:531-539`) |
| `extern-alias` | 796-802 | The whole compilation unit |
| `compilation-unit-attribute` | 789-795 | The whole compilation unit (assembly and module attributes) |
| `default-lambda-parameter` | 875-881 | Not established: produced only by `MigrationAnalyzer` (`:487-495`) |
| `partial-property` | 858-864 | Each declaration of a partial property or indexer |
| `iterator-accessor` | 848-854 | The property or indexer whose accessor uses `yield` |
| `ref-struct` | 612-618 | The whole type |
| `scoped-parameter` | 641-647 | The whole member |
| `string-interpolation-handler` | 192-198 | The statement or member |
| `string-interpolation-formattable-constant` | 199-205 | The statement or member |
| `unsupported-compound-assignment` | 929-935 | The member; `>>>=` |
| `unsupported-switch-label` | 977-983 | The member; a pattern label such as `case > 100:` |
| `unsupported-pattern-operator` | 984-990 | The member; the default arm of two operator switches that list every C# 14 pattern operator (`src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/RoslynSyntaxVisitor.cs:11440-11458`), so it may be unreachable |
| `unsupported-prefix-operator` | 991-997 | User-defined, dynamic or unresolved unary `+` |
| `unsupported-slice-subpattern` | 998-1004 | A slice with an inner sub-pattern, `..[1, 2]` |

Steps:

1. **Count.** For each entry, count occurrences in the library sources of MediatR, Serilog and FluentValidation (git submodules under `bench/corpus/`; the three source directories are listed at `scripts/default_migrate_report.py:22-26`). Count in the original C#, not only in conversion losses: a file that is preserved whole never records the constructs inside it. `SyntaxCapabilityClassifier.Detect` (`FeatureSupport.cs:1621-1699`) and `MigrationAnalyzer` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Analysis/MigrationAnalyzer.cs:405-545`) already detect several of these. Write the counts, and how each row was counted, into the registry table of the coverage record `docs/plans/0.34-native-coverage.md` (#1659 defines its layout; create the file with that layout if #1850 has not).
2. **Probe the two analyzer-only entries.** Convert a C# 12 alias of a tuple type and a lambda with a default parameter value with default `calor convert`, add each as a test, and correct each entry's description to what the converter does.
3. **Decide each entry** with the maintainer: convert natively, or keep preserved with a reason kind (`bucket`, `zero-in-corpus`, `unmodeled`, `no-form` or `not-reached`, defined in #1659 and in the record's header; `no-demand` only if the adopter fallback applies). Converting costs a pull request, possibly a new source form and reference tokens; keeping costs nothing now and leaves the construct outside Calor's checks. The plan recommends converting an entry when its corpus count is above zero and an existing canonical form expresses it, and recording the rest. The decision is not taken by filing this issue: record it in the entry's row with who decided and the date.
4. **Convert** the entries decided as native, one pull request per construct or closely related group, each mapped to an existing canonical form where one exists. A new source form is additive, is decided in that pull request under the fewest-tokens rule as #1785 amends it, and is recorded in the "New source forms" part of the coverage record.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- The sixteen entries are `NotSupported`; `utf8-string-literal` (`:889-895`), `char-literal` (`:912-917`) and `type-pattern` (`:1005-1010`) are `Full`; `string-interpolation-hole` (`:206-212`) and `complex-is-pattern` (`:1047-1052`) are `Partial`.
- `tests/Calor.Conversion.Tests/RegistryConformanceTests.cs` pins preservation for several: `UnsignedRightShiftAssignment_EscalatesToMemberInterop` (`:395`), `PrefixUnary_UserDefinedUnaryPlus_EscalatesToInterop` (`:503`), `PatternSwitchLabel_RelationalStatement_EscalatesInsteadOfWildcard` (`:812`), `UnsupportedTypeSemantics_PreserveWholeType` (`:1298`, `ref-struct` and `file-scoped-type`), and the `scoped` case of `MemberLifetimeOrRefSafetySemantics_PreserveWholeMember` (`:1264`).
- `scripts/default_migrate_report.py` already counts preserved units by loss feature (`:63-65`, reported as `passthrough_units_by_reason`, `:102`), in directory mode on source-only copies.
- No frequency table for these entries exists in the repository.

## Why

These entries are individually small and unequal in value: some are common in ordinary code, some may not occur in the corpus at all, and at least one may be unreachable. Counting first puts the work on the entries real code uses, and "preserved, with a reason" is a legitimate end state, so the issue can close without converting all sixteen.

## Done when

- The registry table of the coverage record has a row for each of the sixteen entries with its count per corpus project and the method used, and the two probe results are recorded in their rows.
- Each of the sixteen entries is native or has a reason kind in its row. Native means promoted in `FeatureSupport.cs` with a registered fixture under `bench/phase0-agent-native/fixtures/d-s1.5/` whose `fixture.json` names the entry in `featureKey` (schema in the `README.md` there), the `d-s1.5-fixtures` job green, and its pinning test updated in the same pull request.
- The two `Partial` entries (`string-interpolation-hole`, `complex-is-pattern`) have an updated description if their preserved remainder changed; they are not counted by the 0.34 exit criterion.
- `website/public/data/feature-support.json` is regenerated with `calor feature-check --list` whenever a level or description changes.
- One scorecard snippet per newly native construct is added to `tests/TestData/CSharpImport/manifest.json`, and `BASELINE_FULLY_CONVERTED`, `BASELINE_ROUNDTRIP`, the total asserted at `tests/Calor.Evaluation/Scorecard/ConversionScorecardTests.cs:115` and `tests/Calor.Evaluation/Scorecard/baseline.json` rise with it.
- Standing acceptance rule, per pull request that makes a construct native: the conversion scorecard's fully converted count does not fall (100 of 100 at HEAD bc80daeb, `ConversionScorecardTests.cs:31`); the per-project Calor/C# token ratio does not rise, read from the corpus report job (#1779) with the columns #1746 adds or, if #1746 has slipped, by the hand method #1746 records; the pull request states how many corpus files newly fall to whole-file preservation.
- `expectedTotal` in `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated for each test project whose test count changes (`scripts/check_trx.py` enforces it in CI).

## Not in scope

- `unsupported-binary-operator` (`>>>`) belongs to #1850's list; it is the same operator as `unsupported-compound-assignment` and is best converted in the same pull request.
- `file record` conversion beyond what `file-scoped-type` needs: #1654.

Part of #1659.

issues.title: [0.34] Disposition for the unsupported registry entries outside the five families
issues.displaces: none: new capacity justified in body
issues.body:
## Change

A decision record with a small amount of code. Start after #1647 closes, which is the 0.34 entry criterion. The registry is `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/FeatureSupport.cs`: each entry names a C# construct or a converter diagnostic and its support level, and a `NotSupported` construct is kept as raw C# (the original text inside a raw frame in the `.calr` file).

1. **Restate the baseline.** Run `calor feature-check --list --level notsupported` and reconcile the result with the ownership table in #1659 (58 entries at HEAD bc80daeb, plus what #1638 added). Repeat when #1638 closes if that is later than 0.34 entry. Regenerate `tests/Calor.Evaluation/Scorecard/baseline.json` (command in `tests/Calor.Evaluation/Scorecard/ConversionScorecardTests.cs:11-13`).
2. **Create the coverage record** `docs/plans/0.34-native-coverage.md` with three parts. *Registry table*: one row per baseline entry (the restated `NotSupported` entries and `checked-block`, which is labelled `Full` but preserved by default conversion) with the columns entry, owner issue, occurrences per corpus project and how counted, outcome, reason kind, evidence. *Family shapes*: the same columns for preservation reasons that are not registry entries (the `record-*` reasons of #1654). *New source forms*: candidates, token counts and the chosen spelling for each form a child of #1659 adds. The header defines the outcomes. A registry row is native when its entry is promoted in the registry with a registered fixture (a directory under `bench/phase0-agent-native/fixtures/d-s1.5/`, which the `d-s1.5-fixtures` CI job requires for every promotion); a family-shape row is native when its preservation test is replaced by an assertion on native output and a runtime test is added. A preserved row carries one reason kind: `bucket` (a diagnostic bucket, not a C# construct), `zero-in-corpus` (no occurrence in the three corpus projects at their pins), `unmodeled` (needs semantics Calor does not model, named in the row), `no-form` (needs a new source form whose spelling was declined or deferred, decision linked), `not-reached` (occurs, was planned, and was not converted by the close of 0.34; the row links the open issue and milestone that carry it; also used, with the cause "needs .NET 11 hosts" and a link to #1643, for a C# 15 entry whose default output needs .NET 11 types), or `no-demand` (valid only if the adopter checkpoint #1833 records that the fallback in `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md` applies). Rows owned by #1654 to #1658 start as "open".
3. **Add a test** (suggested `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/NativeCoverageRecordTests.cs`) that reads the registry table and fails when an entry is `NotSupported` in the registry and has no row, when a row marked preserved names an entry that is no longer `NotSupported`, or when a row marked native names an entry that is still `NotSupported`.
4. **Count** the 22 entries below in the library sources of MediatR, Serilog and FluentValidation (git submodules under `bench/corpus/`; the three source directories are listed at `scripts/default_migrate_report.py:22-26`). Count in the original C# where a syntactic detector exists (`SyntaxCapabilityClassifier.Detect`, `FeatureSupport.cs:1621-1699`; `MigrationAnalyzer`, `src/Calor.Compiler/Analysis/MigrationAnalyzer.cs:405-545`), and otherwise from the per-file `losses` in the `calor migrate --report` output that the corpus report job (#1779) keeps. A file preserved whole records no losses for the constructs inside it, so say how each row was counted.
5. **Decide each of the 22.** This is a maintainer decision, and filing this issue does not take it. The last column of the table is a starting recommendation.

Options per entry: (a) convert natively in 0.34, which costs a pull request, possibly a new source form and reference tokens, and gets its own issue under #1659; (b) keep preserved with one of the reason kinds above, which costs nothing now and leaves the construct outside Calor's effect and nullability checks; (c) correct a registry entry that misstates what the converter does. A correction that raises a level is a promotion, so the `d-s1.5-fixtures` CI job requires a registered fixture under `bench/phase0-agent-native/fixtures/d-s1.5/` whose `fixture.json` names the entry in `featureKey` (schema in the `README.md` there). Removing a key needs a supersession note and an allowlist entry (`scripts/check-d-s1.5-fixtures.sh:64-66`). Option (c) does not replace the need for (a) or (b) on what stays preserved.

Lines are in `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/FeatureSupport.cs`; producers are in `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/RoslynSyntaxVisitor.cs` unless stated.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- The registry has 184 entries: 96 `Full`, 30 `Partial`, 58 `NotSupported` (`website/public/data/feature-support.json`, the committed output of `calor feature-check --list`, which `WebsiteFeatureSupportParityTests.TheWebsiteExportIsTheRegistry`, `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/WebsiteFeatureSupportParityTests.cs:239`, keeps equal to the registry).
- 23 of the 58 `NotSupported` entries are named by none of #1654 to #1658 as filed. One of them, `static-abstract-member`, is assigned to #1656, which leaves the 22 in the table.
- `generic-delegate` has no producer anywhere under `src/`. `generic-attribute` is produced only by the analyzer; what the converter does with a generic attribute is not established by any test found.
- `FeatureCheck_BlockerName_ExistsInRegistry` (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/FeatureCheckCommandTests.cs:704`) requires every analyzer blocker name to exist in the registry.
- The committed scorecard baseline `tests/Calor.Evaluation/Scorecard/baseline.json` is stale: its timestamp is 2026-10-30 and its `commitHash` 937f79321, it reports 96 fully converted and lists snippets 044 and 100 as partially converted, while the test constant is 100 of 100 (`ConversionScorecardTests.cs:31`). `NoRegressionsVsCommittedBaseline` (`:171`) compares against that file and requires it to list the same snippet ids as the current run.

## Why

The 0.34 exit criterion is that every row of the coverage record is native or preserved with a recorded reason, where the rows are the unsupported registry entries at 0.34 entry, `checked-block`, and the family shapes preserved under an entry already labelled `Full`, such as `record struct`. Without this issue 22 of the 58 entries have no owner, the record does not exist, and the criterion cannot be evaluated. It displaces nothing: the cost is one counting pass, one record, one test and one decision session, and the alternative is an exit criterion that is waived.

## Done when

- `docs/plans/0.34-native-coverage.md` is merged with its three parts and a registry-table row for every baseline entry. Each of the 22 rows has its counts and is either preserved with a reason kind, or "convert" with a link to an open issue in milestone 0.34 under #1659.
- The record names who decided each of the 22 and when.
- The new test passes, and its own negative cases show it failing for a `NotSupported` entry with no row and for a row marked native whose entry is still `NotSupported`.
- `baseline.json` is regenerated and its `fullyConverted` equals `BASELINE_FULLY_CONVERTED`.
- Registry descriptions corrected under option (c) are in the same pull request, with `website/public/data/feature-support.json` regenerated by `calor feature-check --list` and the `d-s1.5-fixtures` job green.
- `expectedTotal` for `Calor.Compiler.Tests` in `eng/test-manifest.json` is raised by the tests added (`scripts/check_trx.py` enforces it in CI).

## Not in scope

- Implementing the conversions decided under (a): each is its own issue.
- The 36 entries owned by #1654 to #1658.

Part of #1659.

issues.title: [0.34] Re-check marked passthrough: stale-block report and re-conversion (#1621 phase B2)

**Amendment.** New title: `[0.34] Re-check marked passthrough: stale-block report and re-conversion (#1621 phase B2)`. Milestone 0.34. Label: `enhancement`. Add the closing line `Part of #1659.`

In `## Change` item 1 and in the first `## Done when` bullet, replace "`calor build`" with:

> the compile paths (`calor --input`, `calor check`, and the `CompileCalor` MSBuild task in `src/Calor.Tasks/CompileCalor.cs`)

Insert before `## Change`:

> ## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)
>
> - There is no top-level `calor build` command: `build` exists only as `calor index build` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/IndexCommand.cs:38`; the top-level commands are registered at `src/Calor.Compiler/Program.cs:310-338`). Calor compiles through the root command (`calor --input`), `calor check` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/TestCommand.cs:65`) and the `CompileCalor` MSBuild task.
> - A foundation exists with no production caller: `FeatureSupport.AssessPreservation` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/FeatureSupport.cs:1408-1529`) takes the original syntax node and boundary and returns `StillRequired`, `UnknownOrMismatch`, `InsufficientContext` or `ChangedBoundary`. It never returns `NowNative` (declared at `:1336`): a missing guard does not prove native conversion (`:1402-1406`). Its only callers are in `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/FeatureCheckCommandTests.cs`.
> - Conversion receipts exist: `<output>.conversion.json` beside each converted file holds the original source, parse options and raw frames (`src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/CSharpToCalorConverter.cs:3078`, `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/Project/ProjectMigrator.cs:148-153`). Build and language-server validation against receipts is recorded as unwired (`docs/design/0.30-syntax-token-decision.md:473-475`).
> - Marker presence is already enforced: a raw frame whose feature or reason metadata is missing or empty is error `Calor1012`, and the same comment says that reason applicability and staleness need separate validation (`src/Calor.Compiler/Diagnostics/Diagnostic.cs:1102-1106`).

Append to `## Done when`:

> - The stale case in the tests uses a reason that a 0.34 coverage issue retired (for example `record-struct` once #1654 lands), not an invented one.
> - The report is a warning. A stale block is still correct C#, and an error would stop the build of every project migrated with an older compiler. If an error is proposed later, the standing acceptance rule applies: the conversion scorecard's fully converted count and the per-project token ratio do not regress, and the number of files that newly fall to whole-file preservation is reported.
> - A recorded run migrates one corpus project (MediatR, Serilog or FluentValidation) with the compiler built from the 0.34 entry commit, then re-runs `calor migrate` on that tree with the head compiler. Classifying the result with the rules of `scripts/corpus_report.py` (#1779) gives the same class per file as a fresh head migration of the same pin; no file that is native in the fresh migration is whole-file preserved after re-conversion. The pull request links the run and gives the three counts (native, partly preserved, whole-file preserved).
> - `expectedTotal` in `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated for each test project whose test count changes (`scripts/check_trx.py` enforces it in CI).

**Why.** The body names a command that does not exist and omits the foundation already in the tree, so an agent would start in the wrong place. The severity line is there because a new hard error on already migrated projects would need the standing acceptance rule, and a warning does not.

**Moved from** 0.31 because it is on no 0.31 exit criterion and has nothing to report until constructs turn native: every coverage pull request in epic #1659 makes blocks in already migrated projects stale, which is the case this issue exists for.

issues.title: [0.34] Density target: migrated Calor below 1.0x C# tokens on the default path
issues.displaces: none: new capacity justified in body
issues.body:
## Change

Read the density of migrated code (Calor tokens over the tokens of the C# they replace) once the work that moves it has landed, against a rule written before the reading.

1. **Write the rule first.** Commit `docs/plans/0.34-density-target.md` containing the definitions and readings below, before the measuring run.
2. **Measure with the proxy tokenizer.** After #1647 and #1742 have merged and every row of the coverage record `docs/plans/0.34-native-coverage.md` has an outcome (native, or preserved with a reason, `not-reached` included), take from one run of the corpus report job (#1779, with the columns #1746 adds) for MediatR, Serilog and FluentValidation under default project-mode `calor migrate`: C# tokens, Calor tokens, the ratio on all files, on native files and on preserved files (files kept as raw C#), and the native fraction.
3. **Measure once with Anthropic `count_tokens`** for the release figure: one dispatch of `.github/workflows/syntax-token-count.yml` on the same migrated output, or one run of the tool #1799 delivers if it has replaced that workflow. `scripts/count_tokens.py` accepts only its fixed 41-file population (`:264-267`), so corpus files go into the manifest as `probes`, which it reports separately (`:18-19`). This is not a paid agent run: the workflow sends count requests only, with no completion or agent call (`.github/workflows/syntax-token-count.yml:3-8`), and the earlier count runs record that Anthropic does not charge for token counting (`docs/design/0.30-syntax-token-decision.md:13`). It counts with the one model the workflow pins (`TARGET_MODEL`, `:50`). It still needs the maintainer, who publishes the payload commit, passes its digest and dispatches from `main`; filing this issue does not authorise the dispatch.
4. **Record the outcome** in the same file. Commit the measured per-project proxy ratios as reference values in a file the corpus report script reads, so that every later run prints each project's ratio and its difference from the reference. Whether a ratio above its reference fails the job follows the decision #1647 records for native floors on that job: if floors there are blocking, these ceilings block the same way; if the job is report-only, the script reports the difference and exits 0.

Definitions. The ratio is Calor tokens divided by the tokens of the C# files the migration replaced. "Overall" sums the three projects. The target applies to default-path output as emitted, which carries no contracts; the "with contracts" variant #1746 reports is recorded, not targeted.

Readings, fixed in advance:

- **Met:** overall ratio below 1.000 on the `count_tokens` figure. The release notes (`CHANGELOG.md`) of the milestone in which this issue closes state it with tokenizer, model, Calor commit and corpus pins, and the figure is entered in the evidence ledger (#1774).
- **Tokenizers disagree** about which side of 1.000 the overall ratio is on: the `count_tokens` figure governs any published statement; both are recorded.
- **No `count_tokens` dispatch:** the proxy figure is recorded as provisional, the outcome line says so, and no density claim is published.
- **Not met:** the record adds, per project, the native share of C# tokens, the ratio on native and on preserved files, and the five preservation reasons that carry the most preserved tokens. The maintainer then chooses: (a) keep the target and file named follow-up issues, each with the token gain it is expected to deliver, costing later milestone capacity; or (b) revise the target to a statement the numbers support (for example "native files below 1.0x; overall reported") with the reason recorded, costing the headline claim. The plan recommends (a) only if the listed follow-ups close the gap by the record's own arithmetic, otherwise (b). No density claim is published while the target is unmet.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- The only measurement is by hand, in the body of #1746 (2026-11-20, compiler 606dae6f2, o200k proxy, default project-mode migrate); it is not recorded in the repository and has not been re-run. Ratios: MediatR 1.104, Serilog 1.055, FluentValidation 0.972, overall 1.016; native files 0.859. #1746 says MediatR and Serilog were entirely whole-file preserved because of CS8669 (the gap is described at `CHANGELOG.md:120-124`), so the native figure comes from FluentValidation alone.
- By those figures a preserved file costs 5.5% to 10.4% more than its C#. A project then needs roughly 28% to 42% of its C# tokens in native files to fall below 1.0x at a native ratio of 0.859. This is arithmetic on one sample. An earlier close-out, measured before 0.30, found the code of most interest (stateful, guard-bearing) disproportionately in the half that did not convert natively (`docs/plans/wedge-real-scale-closeout.md:119-125`), so the files that are native first are likely the simpler ones.
- No CI job reports a token ratio. `scripts/default_migrate_report.py` reports file counts and preserved units by reason, on source-only copies with build and tests `not-run` (`:103-104`).
- The offline tokenizer in the test suite is o200k (`ProxyTokenizer`, `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/TokenBudgetTests.cs:19-25`), a proxy for Claude's tokenizer.
- `.github/workflows/syntax-token-count.yml` is dispatched by hand from `main` (`:69`), needs the protected environment `anthropic-count-tokens` (`:16-19`), and targets one model (`TARGET_MODEL: "Claude Opus 5.5"`, `:50`). The manifest format is in the header of `scripts/count_tokens.py`, which requires the population of one primer, 20 converted files and 20 agent files (`:264-267`).

## Why

0.30 set the target that migrated Calor be smaller than the C# it replaces, and #1746 carried it with a done-when of "below 1.0x, or the target is revised with a recorded reason". #1746 is now the reporting half; this issue is the other half of that existing done-when, so it adds no scope the tracker did not already hold. It is scheduled last in 0.34 because the one measurement on record was dominated by preserved files, and three things move it: #1647, #1742 and the coverage work in #1659. A family issue that is still open does not hold the measuring run once its rows have an outcome. It is on no 0.34 exit criterion and may slip to 0.35 without holding the release.

## Done when

- `docs/plans/0.34-density-target.md` exists; the commit that adds the rule is older than the measuring run it cites.
- The file holds the per-project table for both tokenizers (or the proxy alone, marked provisional), links to the corpus report run and the `count_tokens` run, and one outcome line: met, provisional, or not met with the maintainer's choice of (a) or (b), the name and the date. It also names the Calor commit measured, with the number of coverage-record rows that were `not-reached` at that commit.
- Per-project proxy reference ratios are committed in a file the corpus report script reads, and a later run prints each project's ratio and its difference from the reference. A test of the script on a synthetic report shows that output and, if #1647 made floors on the job blocking, a non-zero exit code when a ratio exceeds its reference.
- If the outcome is (a), the follow-up issues exist and are linked. If the target is met, the release notes state the figure with tokenizer, model, commit and pins, and the evidence ledger (#1774) has the entry.

## Not in scope

- Reporting the ratio: #1746.
- Emitting contracts, or measuring their token cost as a target.
- Any change to an existing spelling to save tokens. Spelling changes are decided in the 0.32 breaking window (#1784), not here.

Part of #1659. Depends on #1647, #1742 and #1746.

issues.title: [0.34] Guard census on the pinned corpus and on agent-authored outputs
issues.displaces: none: new capacity justified in body
issues.body:
## Change

Count throw guards, read-only, and publish one reading. No converter, compiler or verifier behaviour changes, and no agent is run.

A *guard* is a statement or expression in a member that has parameters, whose condition reads at least one parameter and whose only action when the condition holds is to throw.

The work is four parts, delivered as up to three ordered pull requests (part 1; part 2; parts 3 and 4).

1. **Register first.** Commit `docs/plans/0.34-guard-census-registration.md` before any count is run on the corpus. It fixes the definitions and readings below and records that the maintainer confirmed or edited the threshold values. Its commit must precede the first commit that contains census numbers.
2. **Corpus pass.** Add a `guard-census` subcommand to `tools/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness` (dispatch in `Program.cs:20-44`; the read-only `failure-census` command at `:554-599`, with `TaskGen/FailureCensus.cs` and `tests/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness.Tests/FailureCensusTests.cs`, is the model). It walks the library C# of the three pinned corpus projects with Roslyn, with a semantic model so that exception types and helper methods resolve, and writes one record per guard. The corpus report job (#1779: a scheduled job, `scripts/corpus_report.py`, that migrates buildable copies of the corpus with default `calor migrate` and writes one JSON report per project) runs it as a column: the records and totals are stored under the key `guards` in each report's `columns` object, joined by path to the report's `per_file` list for `file_status`.
3. **Agent-output pass.** Run the same count over agent-written final sources: the `final-src/` directories that `archive_final_src` writes per run (`bench/phase0-agent-native/run-pair.sh:106-125`). C# files use the Roslyn pass. Calor files are parsed with the compiler built from the commit the epoch pinned (the #1605 epochs are 0.30 syntax, which the head compiler rejects if the 0.32 rewrite changed a form they use; the later epochs are edition syntax); the result names the compiler commit per source; count `if` plus `throw` guards and, separately, parameter refinements (`type:name | (condition on #)`), so the report shows how often an agent wrote a refinement where C# has a guard. Sources (each an epoch, one complete collection of agent runs): the epochs of #1605 (the 0.31 evaluation), the #1645 re-run (which includes the modify-a-converted-module pairs of #1789, the one task type built from corpus code), and the 0.33 per-agent runs (#1811, on the drivers of #1651). A source whose run was declined, or whose archive does not exist when this part is done, is recorded as absent. Archives older than 0.30 are out of scope: they do not parse at 0.30 and contain no `throw` (Baseline).
4. **Publish.** Commit `docs/plans/0.34-guard-census-result.md` with the tables and one reading.

Fields per guard:

| Field | Values |
|---|---|
| `shape` | `if-throw`; `coalesce-throw` (`p ?? throw ...`); `throw-helper` (a static `ThrowIf...` method of a `System` exception type); `project-helper` (a call to a project method whose body is only guards; list the helpers by name) |
| `exception` | resolved type name |
| `custom_message` | a message argument other than the parameter name |
| `container` | constructor, method, accessor, operator, local function, lambda |
| `dispatch` | static, instance, virtual/abstract/override, interface implementation |
| `leading` | preceded in the body only by other guards |
| `dominating` | a top-level statement of the body with a side-effect-free condition |
| `null_guard` | the condition is a null test |
| `param_types` | type of each tested parameter |
| `param_written` | a tested parameter is assigned, incremented or passed by `ref`/`out` in the member |
| `file_status` | `native`, `partly_preserved` or `whole_file_preserved`: the class the corpus report gives the file after default `calor migrate` (native: written as Calor with no recorded loss; partly preserved: some members or types kept as C#; whole-file preserved: the original C# kept whole) |

`liftable` is derived: shape `if-throw`; leading; throws exactly `System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException` naming a tested parameter; the condition reads only parameters and constants and contains no call; not a null guard; `param_written` false; `dispatch` is static or non-virtual instance (not virtual/abstract/override, not an interface implementation); `custom_message` false; `file_status` is `native`. These are the qualifying rules of #1866, so the reading counts only guards that issue may lift. Also report `liftable_wide`, the same count without the dispatch, shape and custom-message conditions, split by each; it carries no threshold.

Readings. The values are recommended planning judgements with no measurement behind them; the maintainer confirms or edits them in the registration, never after a count has been read. Apply the rows in order and take the first that matches:

| Reading | Rule |
|---|---|
| not measurable | fewer than 100 guards of any kind in native files, summed over the three projects; held, not dropped |
| go | at least 25 liftable guards in native files, in at least 2 of the 3 projects, and liftable is at least 10% of all guards in native files |
| drop | fewer than 10 liftable guards in native files |
| hold | any other result; re-read from the corpus job at the 0.35 close |

The reading gates the opt-in lift (#1866). Three numbers are reported without a threshold: `dominating` guards by exception type and parameter type, which inform option (a) of #1847; the share of all guards that are null guards; and the number of dominating null guards in native files, which the decision on modelling reference null (#1860) reads. If agent outputs contain fewer than 20 guards plus refinements, that half is recorded "not measurable on this task set" and the corpus reading stands alone.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- The converter emits no contracts: 16 `preconditions: Array.Empty<RequiresNode>()` sites in `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/RoslynSyntaxVisitor.cs` (the first three at `:2887`, `:3505`, `:3970`).
- No guard count exists for the corpus. The only figure available describes Calor's own compiler source: 569 lines under `src/` match `?? throw new ArgumentNullException` (measured by `grep -rn '?? throw new ArgumentNullException' src | wc -l`).
- The corpus is three git submodules pinned in `bench/corpus/README.md:15-17`: MediatR `v12.4.1`, Serilog `v4.3.1`, FluentValidation `12.1.1`. Their library sources are under `src/MediatR`, `src/Serilog` and `src/FluentValidation` (`tools/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness/ProjectConfigs.cs:125`, `:157`, `:185`). Which guard helpers they define is not verified (the submodules were not checked out when this was written).
- The only in-repository subject with guards is `tests/Calor.RoundTrip.Synthetic/SyntheticLib` (the harness project `Synthetic`, `ProjectConfigs.cs:64-76`): five leading guards (`Calculator.cs:22-23`, `:29-30`; `DateHelper.cs:18-19`; `StringUtils.cs:7-8`; `FizzBuzz.cs:18-19`) and one unconditional trailing throw (`DateHelper.cs:41`), which is not a guard. One of the five meets every source-level condition of `liftable` (`DateHelper.DaysInMonth`, a static method, `DateHelper.cs:16-19`).
- Native files on the round-trip harness at 0.30.0, lossy leg: 10 of 32 (MediatR), 36 of 112 (Serilog), 58 of 139 (FluentValidation) (`docs/plans/2026-11-16-milestone-0.30-ci-triage.md:363-367`). The default leg's blocking floors are 5 of 32, 10 of 112 and 5 of 139 (`bench/corpus/README.md:345-347`; `eng/roundtrip-baselines.json`, `blocking_floors.default`). Under project-mode `calor migrate`, a hand measurement on 2026-11-20 found MediatR and Serilog preserved whole (#1746). #1647 restores the share and is a dependency.
- Agent outputs archived today: 264 `.calr` files in 264 `final-src/` directories under `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/`, in six epochs, all Calor arms (an arm is one language condition of a task), all in the retired pre-0.30 syntax. None contains `throw` (measured by `grep -li throw` over those files). No C# arm source is archived. No source file outside `tests/` under `bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs` or `tests/TestData/ActiveSyntax/bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs` contains `throw`. Existing material therefore reads zero by construction.

## Why

#1849 (facts from dominating guards) and #1866 (the opt-in lift) are worth building only if the guards they target exist in native code in useful numbers, and #1860 needs the count of dominating null guards. The April 2026 flow checker was built before its base rate was known and found nothing; `docs/design/tier1a-postmortem.md:256` prices that check at thirty minutes. This is new capacity that displaces nothing: it is a read-only pass on a job that already runs, and it replaces deciding #1847 without data.

## Done when

- `docs/plans/0.34-guard-census-registration.md` is committed with the definitions, the readings table and the maintainer's confirmation of the values (the commit is authored or approved by the maintainer), and `git log` shows it before the first commit that contains census numbers.
- A unit test in `tests/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness.Tests` runs the pass over `tests/Calor.RoundTrip.Synthetic/SyntheticLib` and asserts: five guards with the exception types `DivideByZeroException`, `ArgumentException` (twice), `ArgumentNullException` and `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`; the trailing throw at `DateHelper.cs:41` is not counted; exactly one guard is liftable (`DateHelper.DaysInMonth`, a static method) when every file is given `file_status` `native`. A second case asserts that the same guard on an interface implementation, and one with a custom message, count in `liftable_wide` and not in `liftable`. The `expectedTotal` of that test project in `eng/test-manifest.json` (472 at HEAD) is raised by the number of tests added.
- One linked run of the corpus report job has `columns.guards` in each of the three reports, with every field above per guard and the `liftable` and `liftable_wide` counts.
- `docs/plans/0.34-guard-census-result.md` states one reading from the registered table with the numbers behind it, `liftable_wide` with its three splits, the null-guard share, the number of dominating null guards in native files, and for each agent-output source: counted (with the compiler commit that parsed its Calor files), absent, or not measurable.
- No pull request of this issue changes a file under `src/Calor.Compiler`.

## Not in scope

Lifting any guard; any verifier change; any agent run or spend (the agent pass reads archives only).
