issues.title: [0.34] Decision: guard-derived preconditions — which form?
issues.body:
## Change

Record one maintainer decision in `docs/plans/0.34-guard-precondition-decision.md`. Converted C# validates its inputs with throw guards (`if (month < 1) throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(month));`); Calor's precondition form is a refinement on the parameter (`int:b | (# != 0)`). The decision is whether, and how, Calor derives anything from guards. The options are compatible, so the record answers each one separately: yes or no for (a) and (c); yes, no or "not now" for (b).

| Option | What it is | What it costs | Follow-up |
|---|---|---|---|
| none (no to all) | Guards stay ordinary body statements. Contracts on converted code come only from authoring (#1843). | Nothing. Converted code contributes no facts and no caller-side obligations. | #1849 and #1866 closed as not planned |
| (a) | Verifier-only facts: after a guard that dominates the rest of the body, the verifier assumes the negated condition for the code that follows. No source change, no runtime change. | One verifier change with seeded unsound and safe controls in the soundness sweep. Helps proofs inside the member only; callers get nothing. | #1849 |
| (b) | An opt-in `calor convert` switch that rewrites a guard as a refinement. Never part of the default (Lossless) path. Limited to leading guards that already throw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` for one named parameter that the member never assigns. Each lift is recorded in the loss ledger (`ConversionLossKind` and `ConversionLoss`, `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/ConversionContext.cs:131-193`) under the three conditions below the table. | It puts a non-Lossless switch back on a command from which 0.30 removed `--lossy` as destructive (`CHANGELOG.md:82-83`). Converter work in a 17,630-line visitor (`src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/RoslynSyntaxVisitor.cs`, measured by `wc -l`). The exception message changes; the type and parameter name do not. Callers gain obligations only after call-site obligations exist for class members (#1864, #1863). | #1866, last row of its epic |
| (c) | Let a refinement carry an exception type and a message, so any guard can be lifted. | New syntax, emitter and teaching text; it reverses #1618, which removed `requires` and custom messages one release ago (`CHANGELOG.md:41-50`). | None in this plan |

**Recommendation.** (a) yes. (b) yes only if the guard census (#1848) reads "go"; on "hold" or "not measurable" record "not now"; on "drop" record no. (c) no: this is the recorded default, because #1618 is settled and choosing (c) would need a separate decision that reopens it. Reasons: (a) is the only option that changes no observable behaviour and trips no gate; (b) covers the one class of guard for which a refinement is a faithful respelling, and the census says how large that class is.

**Conditions on (b).** A ledger entry has side effects today that would defeat the acceptance of the lift (Baseline), so a yes to (b) records these three, or states what replaces them:

1. The lift gets a `ConversionLossKind` of its own that is not a semantic loss (or a fidelity value of its own), so that Lossless conversion does not refuse the file.
2. For a file that contains a lift, member-oracle differences are counted before the loss-recorded waiver is applied.
3. Acceptance of a switch-on round-trip run is pass counts equal to the switch-off run. The native fraction of a switch-on run is reported, not gated, because a lifted file leaves the native count.

The record also says whether guards with a custom message or an `actualValue` argument, and `ThrowIf...` helpers, may be lifted; the recommendation is no to both, which is what the `liftable` count of the census assumes.

"Not now" for (b) means #1866 stays open and unstarted until the census is read again from the corpus job at the 0.35 close. The re-read is done under #1866. The record is append-only after sign-off: a later dated maintainer entry may change (b) from "not now" to yes or no, and #1866 reads the latest entry.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

Why a plain lift (every guard becomes a refinement, by default) is not on the list:

- A refinement emits `throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(p), "Violation of ...")` (`EmitRefinementParameterGuards`, `src/Calor.Compiler/CodeGen/CSharpEmitter.cs:6463-6499`). The reference says this happens in every contract mode including `--contract-mode off`, before the body runs, and again whenever the body assigns the parameter (`docs/syntax-reference/contracts.md:37-41`; `docs/syntax-reference/refinement-types.md:17-19`). So it fires before any guard kept in the body.
- A refinement has no custom message; the reference says to keep a body guard when an API needs a particular exception type (`contracts.md:299-301`; `docs/syntax-reference/current-language.md:388`).
- `tests/Calor.RoundTrip.Synthetic/SyntheticLib` has five leading guards, each pinned in `tests/Calor.RoundTrip.Synthetic/SyntheticLib.Tests` by `Assert.Throws<T>`, which requires the exact type. Four throw another type and would fail after a lift: `DivideByZeroException` (`Calculator.cs:23`; `CalculatorTests.cs:41`), `ArgumentException` (`Calculator.cs:30`, `FizzBuzz.cs:19`; `CalculatorTests.cs:56`, `FizzBuzzTests.cs:51`), `ArgumentNullException` (`StringUtils.cs:8`; `StringUtilsTests.cs:23`). Only `DateHelper.cs:18-19` survives (`DateHelperTests.cs:61-62`).
- The member-level oracle (the `member-oracle` CI job, which drives the original and the round-tripped build of each file with generated inputs) compares thrown exception types (`bench/corpus/README.md:223`). Default conversion is Lossless and keeps the original C# when any semantic loss is recorded (`src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/CSharpToCalorConverter.cs:658-662`). `CHANGELOG.md:1905-1906`: "Conversion does not invent defaults, throws, or implicit unwraps."
- On a member that implements an interface, a precondition the interface lacks is the error `StrongerPrecondition` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/ContractInheritanceChecker.cs:1631-1643`). That check runs on every compile whatever the contract mode (`src/Calor.Compiler/Program.cs:979-985`), so the round-trip jobs would show it. What they do not show, because both compile paths run with contracts off and effects unenforced (`tools/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness/RoundTripPipeline.cs:679-680`, `:1598-1599`), is an inherited precondition check or a postcondition check in the emitted C#; #1795 adds the leg that does.

What options (a) and (b) would build on:

- The verifier scopes an `if` condition to the body it guards and gives the code after `if (c) throw` no fact (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Obligations/FactCollector.cs:25-29`, `:561-591`).
- Call-site obligations are generated only in the loop over `module.Functions` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Obligations/ObligationGenerator.cs:58-62`) and only when every argument is exactly `int` or `bool` (`:120-134`). The converter produces a module-level function only for C# top-level statements (`src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/RoslynSyntaxVisitor.cs:293-308`), so a refinement lifted onto a converted class member creates no caller-side obligation today.
- The contract translator refuses null literals (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Z3/ContractTranslator.cs:836-841`), so a null guard yields no fact under either option.
- Refinement inference exists only for top-level functions (`src/Calor.Compiler/Analysis/ContractInference/ContractInferencePass.cs:43-45`).
- What a ledger entry does today: Lossless conversion refuses a file with any semantic loss (`IsSemanticLoss`, `ConversionContext.cs:190-193`; `CSharpToCalorConverter.cs:1631-1638`) and `calor convert` can select no other fidelity; the member oracle waives every difference in a file whose conversion recorded a loss other than `InteropPreserved` or `EmitterFallback` (`tools/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness/Oracle/OracleRunner.cs:293`, `:399-402`); and a file with any ledger entry stops counting as native (`bench/corpus/README.md:366-367`).

## Why

Lifting every guard into a refinement during conversion looks like the cheapest way to give converted code contracts. It changes which exception a program throws, which the converter's Lossless rule and the member-level oracle exist to reject, and it creates no caller-side obligation on class members today (Baseline). The question still has to be closed in writing because #1849 and #1866 are conditional on the answer. None of the options changes an existing spelling, so the decision does not belong to the 0.32 breaking window.

## Done when

- `docs/plans/0.34-guard-precondition-decision.md` is committed and contains: the #1848 reading with its numbers; yes or no for (a) and (c), and yes, no or "not now" for (b), each with a reason; if (b) is yes, the name of the switch or the statement that #1866 chooses it, the three conditions on (b) or what replaces them, and the answer on custom-message guards and `ThrowIf...` helpers; the date; and the maintainer's sign-off (the commit is authored or approved by the maintainer).
- #1849 carries a comment "proceed" if (a) is yes, otherwise it is closed as not planned with a link to the record.
- #1866 carries a comment "proceed, subject to its other gates" if (b) is yes and the census reads "go", "held" if (b) is "not now" or if (b) is yes while the census reading is not "go", otherwise it is closed as not planned with a link to the record. A later dated entry that changes (b) is commented on #1866 the same way.
- If the census has not produced a reading, the record says so, (b) is recorded "not now", and (a) is still decided. The 0.34 exit criterion "Guard-precondition decision recorded" is met by the committed record in every case.

Part of epic #1845. Depends on #1848. Blocks #1849, #1866.

issues.title: [0.34] Count converted modules that carry the nullable-oblivious header, and set a path to shrink the number
issues.displaces: none: new capacity justified in body
issues.body:
## Change

A module whose header ends with `nullable oblivious` treats a value with no nullability information as C# does with nullable annotations disabled: it can be passed to a non-null parameter, returned, bound or used as a receiver with no null diagnostic (`docs/syntax-reference/structure-tags.md:65-67`). Count these modules, find out how many need the header, and write down how the number comes down.

1. **Count.** Add a column to the corpus report job (#1779: `scripts/corpus_report.py` migrates the three corpus projects with default `calor migrate` and writes one JSON report per project; a later issue adds its numbers as a key under the report's `columns` object). Under `columns.nullable_oblivious`, per project: the number of written files that have a module header, split into native and partly preserved (the classes in the report's `per_file` list); how many of each carry the header; and the project's `<Nullable>` value. The converter writes the header as the last words of the `module` line (`src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/CalorEmitter.cs:247-248`); the parsed form is `ModuleNode.HasObliviousNullability()` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Ast/ModuleNode.cs:52-57`).
2. **Probe.** On a scratch copy of each migrated project, remove ` nullable oblivious` from every module line that has it and compile the copy with the build step the job already runs. Record, per oblivious module, "compiles clean" or the count of each diagnostic code reported in it (the receiving-boundary codes are `Calor0272`, `Calor0273` and `Calor0274`, `src/Calor.Compiler/Diagnostics/Diagnostic.cs:380`, `:396`, `:411`). The migrated output the job publishes is not changed.
3. **Scorecard.** Report the same count for the 100 inputs of the conversion scorecard (`tests/TestData/CSharpImport/manifest.json`), converted one file at a time with the scorecard's own converter settings (`tests/Calor.Evaluation/Scorecard/ConversionScorecardRunner.cs:16`). Record the command used.
4. **Path.** Commit `docs/plans/0.34-nullable-oblivious-path.md`. It gives the numbers and chooses among: (i) leave the count as it is and report it each release; (ii) drop the header wherever the probe compiles clean, as a step of `calor migrate` or a `calor fix` rule; (iii) give single-file `calor convert` the project's nullable context, so sources from nullable-enabled projects are not emitted as oblivious; (iv) any other step the numbers suggest. For each chosen step it files a follow-up issue. This issue implements none of them.

**Standing acceptance rule.** This issue adds no error. Any follow-up that removes a header or narrows what an oblivious module accepts tightens hard errors for that module, so it must show that the conversion scorecard's fully converted count does not fall (`BASELINE_FULLY_CONVERTED`, `tests/Calor.Evaluation/Scorecard/ConversionScorecardTests.cs:31`) and that the per-project Calor/C# token ratio does not rise (the columns #1746 adds to the corpus report job), and must report how many files newly fall to whole-file preservation. The path document states the predicted value of each for every option, taken from the probe.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- 0.30 added the header and its relaxed checks; the release notes credit it with 8 more native conversions on the scorecard (`CHANGELOG.md:159-168`). Semantics: `docs/syntax-reference/structure-tags.md:48-79`.
- The binder treats an unannotated reference type in such a module as oblivious (`src/Calor.Compiler/Binding/Binder.cs:1320-1321`). Generated C# gets `#nullable disable annotations` and `#nullable enable warnings` (`src/Calor.Compiler/CodeGen/CSharpEmitter.cs:1676-1682`).
- The converter writes the header (`src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/CalorEmitter.cs:247-248`) when the file has no `#nullable` directive, the nullable context it is given is disabled, and at least one declaration's nullability metadata would differ with annotations enabled; it tries that form first (`src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/CSharpToCalorConverter.cs:643-657`, `:695-728`, `:789-816`). `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/CanonicalNamespaceTests.cs:252-287` pins "header if and only if the context is Disable" for one such file.
- The oblivious form is accepted only after the generated C# is compiled inside the original compilation and its declared nullability metadata is found identical (`CSharpToCalorConverter.cs:734-745`). An unannotated reference declaration in an oblivious module has metadata `NullableAnnotation.None`; without the header it is `NotAnnotated` (`structure-tags.md:61-62`; `CanonicalNamespaceTests.cs:284-287`). So removing a header changes the module's public metadata even when the module compiles clean, and option (ii) must say how it treats that.
- Where the context comes from differs by command. Project-mode `calor migrate` passes the project's `<Nullable>` value (`src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/Project/ProjectMigrator.cs:735-736`, `:1945`). Single-file `calor convert` has no nullable option (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/ConvertCommand.cs:329-374`) and an unspecified context is treated as disabled (`CSharpToCalorConverter.cs:719`), so a file with no `#nullable` directive is treated as nullable-disabled whatever its project says. `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/NativeMetadataClosureTests.cs:20-29` shows the default converter emitting the header.
- No count exists. Whether the three corpus projects enable nullable is not verified (the submodules were not checked out when this was written).
- The scorecard in the tree has 100 inputs (`tests/TestData/CSharpImport/manifest.json`) and `BASELINE_FULLY_CONVERTED = 100` (`ConversionScorecardTests.cs:31`). `CHANGELOG.md:166-168` speaks of 106 inputs, 101 of them native; a 106-input set was not found in the tree. The result must name the set it measured.

## Why

Null enforcement at three receiving boundaries (`Calor0272` to `Calor0274`) is one of the build-time guarantees Calor claims over C#, and inside an oblivious module it is relaxed for every value that has no nullability information. If most converted modules carry the header, the guarantee is mostly absent from converted code, and nobody knows the share. The header also has a measured benefit, 8 more native scorecard conversions, so removing it has a cost that must be counted first. This is new capacity that displaces nothing: one column and one probe on a job that already runs. The issue is off the 0.34 exit chain and may slip to 0.35 without holding the release.

## Done when

- One linked run of the corpus report job has `columns.nullable_oblivious` in each of the three reports, with the file counts per class, the counts that carry the header, the project's `<Nullable>` value, and the probe result per oblivious module.
- The self-test #1779 adds for the report script (`scripts/test_corpus_report.py`) has a case for this column and passes.
- `docs/plans/0.34-nullable-oblivious-path.md` is committed with: those numbers; the same count for the scorecard inputs, with the command that produced it and the input set named; the chosen steps; the predicted effect of each on the three quantities of the standing rule; and a link to each follow-up issue filed (or the statement that option (i) was chosen).
- The pull request changes no conversion or compilation behaviour: it edits no file under `src/Calor.Compiler` and no file under `tests/Calor.Evaluation/Scorecard`, and the `conversion-scorecard` job (`.github/workflows/test.yml:672`) passes.

Part of epic #1845. Depends on #1779.

issues.title: [0.34] Disposal spike after #1655: design note and a count in agent outputs
issues.body:
## Change

A spike: one design note and one count. No compiler change. Deliverable: `docs/design/disposal-check-spike.md`.

**Gate.** Start when #1655 (native `using` declarations and `await using`) is merged; its state is the gate, and there is no numeric threshold. The resource-leak class reading of #1605 does not gate this issue; this count is the next measurement that reading waits for. If #1655 is closed as not planned, close this issue and #1870 as not planned with a link. If #1655 moves to a later milestone, this issue moves with it.

1. **Rule first.** The first commit of the note contains only the definitions and the rule below. The rule is the resource-leak rule that the registration of the 0.31 evaluation (#1770, item 8 of its entry in Annex A of `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md`) sets for defect-class base rates. The note quotes it and applies it to this count with one stated deviation: an *event* here is a run whose final sources hold at least one hand-checked leak as defined below, not a failed iteration, because a leak fails no test. A *run* is a valid run on a pair that has at least one opportunity. The rule is read on the Calor arm, as registered; the C# arm is reported beside it. If the Annex A entry was registered without a resource-leak rule, the maintainer confirms these same values in this first commit.
   - *Opportunity*: a local whose type implements `IDisposable` or `IAsyncDisposable`, created in code the agent wrote or changed.
   - *Leak*: an opportunity that is not disposed on some path and does not escape (is not returned, stored in a field, or passed to a call or constructor).
   - Values as #1770 item 8 states them. *Not measurable*: fewer than 5 opportunities across the pair set, or fewer than 30 runs. *Above threshold*: events in at least 5 distinct runs and at least 10% of runs. *Below threshold*: at least 30 runs and events in at most 1. *Held*: anything between.
   - Verdict: go = above threshold; drop = below threshold; hold = held; not measurable holds #1870, it does not drop it.
2. **Count.** Apply the definitions to agent-written final sources (`final-src/` under `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/`, written by `archive_final_src`, `bench/phase0-agent-native/run-pair.sh:106-125`) from the #1605 epochs, the #1645 re-run (which includes the modify-a-converted-module pairs of #1789) and the 0.33 per-agent runs (#1811, on the drivers of #1651). A source that was declined or has no archive is recorded as absent. Count both arms (an arm is one language condition of a task: Calor or C#) with the same definition, state the method in the note (reading by hand, or a Roslyn pass over the C# arm and over the C# generated from the Calor arm), report opportunities, leaks, runs and events per source and per arm, and check every reported leak by hand. This issue runs no agent and authorises no spend: it reads archives only.
3. **Design note.** Sections: what a must-dispose check would report and where it would run (as a bug-pattern checker under `--analyze`); the escape rules; what #1655 added to the control-flow graph for `using` declarations; expected false positives; the cheaper alternative of running a C# disposal analyzer over generated C#; an estimate of the work.
4. **Verdict.** go: #1870 proceeds. hold or not measurable: #1870 stays open and unstarted until the next agent run adds sources, and the note names that run. drop: #1870 is closed as not planned.
5. **Comparator.** Whatever the verdict, record in the note and in a comment on #1709 that the equipped C# condition (C# given analyzers and executable assertions comparable to Calor's checks) gets disposal analyzers, and name them, so that #1709 uses the same ones. Candidates to evaluate: the .NET code-analysis rules CA2000 and CA2213 (not verified against the pinned SDK).

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- The obligation engine has five kinds, none about resources (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Obligations/ObligationTracker.cs:33-49`).
- The bug-pattern checkers cover division by zero, index bounds, null dereference, overflow and off-by-one, plus a precondition suggester (`src/Calor.Compiler/Analysis/BugPatterns/TypedBugPatternAnalysis.cs:13-20`; `BugPatternChecker.cs:147-174`). None is about resources.
- The control-flow graph models the dispose step of a block-form `using` as `SyntheticOperationKind.UsingDispose` inside a finally region (`src/Calor.Compiler/Analysis/Dataflow/ControlFlowGraph.cs:45`, `:1220-1229`). Nothing reads that kind except one test (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/Analysis/ExplicitDataflowAnalysisTests.cs:282`).
- Block-form `using` is native Calor (`docs/syntax-reference/current-language.md:538-548`). `using-declaration` and `await-using` are `NotSupported` in the converter registry (`src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/FeatureSupport.cs:648-654`, `:634-640`) until #1655.
- Existing archives cannot answer the question. The 264 archived agent outputs (`final-src/` under `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/`; all Calor arms, pre-0.30 syntax) contain no `IDisposable`, `Dispose`, `Stream`, `HttpClient` or `SqlConnection` (measured by `grep -l`), and no source file outside `tests/` under `bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs` does either. The count depends on the 0.32 and 0.33 runs.
- The strategy defers full ownership and linear types to after 1.0 (`docs/plans/agent-native-strategy.md:215-217`). A must-dispose check does not need them.

## Why

No measurement says how often agents leak resources, and the compiler has nothing to build a disposal check on (Baseline). The post-mortem of the reverted April 2026 flow checker asks for a base-rate check and an explicit hold outcome before building (`docs/design/tier1a-postmortem.md:252`, `:256`). One spike answers both questions and keeps disposal out of every milestone until the answer exists. The issue is off the 0.34 exit chain and may slip to 0.35 without holding the release.

## Done when

- `docs/design/disposal-check-spike.md` is committed; `git log` shows the definitions and the rule committed before the counts, and the note quotes the rule #1770 registered or, if Annex A has none, the values the maintainer confirmed, and states the deviation in what counts as an event.
- The note reports opportunities, leaks, runs and events per source and arm (or "absent" for a source), the counting method, and exactly one verdict from the rule.
- #1870 carries a comment with the verdict and a link, and is closed as not planned if the verdict is drop.
- #1709 carries a comment naming the disposal analyzers the equipped C# condition will use.

## Not in scope

Any checker or diagnostic; any change to the control-flow graph; ownership or linear types.

Part of epic #1845. Depends on #1655. Blocks #1870.

issues.title: [0.34] Feasibility gate: can the real-scale venue reopen under its two registered re-entry conditions?
issues.body:
## Change

The real-scale venue (agent tasks generated by injecting defects into the three converted open-source corpus projects) was retired on 2026-08-05 with two registered re-entry conditions. Measure both, measure whether the venue has any eligible task, and commit `docs/plans/0.34-real-scale-venue-feasibility.md`. This issue runs no agent and authorises no spend.

**Gate on attempting.** Attempt only if #1647 is closed and the native file count of the lossy round-trip leg (the harness run that converts with Lossy fidelity, which the task generator also uses) exceeds the count the August run had (15 of 32 MediatR, 44 of 110 Serilog, 74 of 139 FluentValidation) in at least two projects. Read the current count from `blocking_floors.lossy` in `eng/roundtrip-baselines.json` at the commit measured: native fraction times the project's file count. These are floors that the nightly baselines job raises to what it measures, so the reading is a lower bound. The threshold is a recommended floor with no measurement behind it; the maintainer may confirm it, replace it or remove it (so that the measurement always runs once #1647 is closed) before the measurement, not after. The first commit of `docs/plans/0.34-real-scale-venue-feasibility.md` contains only the gate threshold as the maintainer confirmed, replaced or removed it, the read rules of steps 1 to 3 (70 considered in both runs, eligible above zero in both runs, the instrument condition) and the commit of `eng/roundtrip-baselines.json` the gate will be read from. It precedes any `gen-tasks` run. While #1647 is open the issue is held and slips with it. If #1647 is closed and the counts are below the threshold, add a three-line entry "not attempted: native share has not recovered" with the counts to that file, and close this issue as not planned with the record linked.

1. **Supply.** After `git submodule update --init --recursive`, run the registered configuration twice: `dotnet run --project tools/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness -- gen-tasks MediatR Serilog FluentValidation --stratum expressible --max-candidates 0 --target 0 --native-bar 0.70 --output <dir>`. From each run's `task-generation-report.json` record `TotalConsidered` (the candidates that survive build and recovery, which the registered condition calls evaluable) and `TotalEligible`. Registered condition 1 is read as met if `TotalConsidered` is at least 70 in both runs.
2. **Eligible supply.** A task is *eligible* when it passes every exclusion rule of the generator. Met if `TotalEligible` is greater than zero in both runs (the command exits 0 only then, `tools/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness/Program.cs:549`). This is not a registered condition. It is part of the verdict because every eligible task of the August run came from one mutation operator whose signal has since been retired (Baseline), so the venue could pass condition 1 with nothing to run.
3. **Instrument.** Registered condition 2 is met if one generated task can be run with `--null-agent` (a zero-cost pass that applies the reference fix instead of calling an agent) through a runner whose Calor arm contains `.calr` files and builds them with the Calor compiler, and a Calor diagnostic for the injected defect appears in that arm's build output before the fix is applied. Today's runner is `bench/phase0-agent-native/run-bundle.sh --bundle <dir> --arm csharp|calor --null-agent`, whose Calor arm is plain C#. If step 1 generated no task, or no runner meets the condition, record "not met", what is missing, and an estimate of the work.
4. **Verdict.** *Feasible* only if steps 1, 2 and 3 are all met. Otherwise *not feasible*, and the record names each step that failed. When the eligible count is zero, the record also says whether step 1 passed, because the one known change that restores eligible supply is the "pin the contract" option of #1177, which #1859 decides.

**Maintainer decision recorded in the same file.** It is open until the measurement exists.

| Option | What it costs |
|---|---|
| Keep the venue retired | Nothing now. The proof-depth claim keeps having no measurement on real-scale code (`docs/plans/call-s-adjudication.md:169-173`). |
| Open a successor plan | A registration, a spend authorisation, and a bundle runner whose Calor arm builds `.calr`. None of these is an issue in this milestone, and this issue grants none of them. |

The plan recommends keeping the venue retired unless the verdict is "feasible". The record states the option chosen, the date and the maintainer's sign-off.

Consequences. "Feasible", with a decision to open a successor plan, un-holds #851. "Not feasible", "not attempted", or a decision to keep the venue retired closes #851 as not planned; if the verdict failed on eligible supply alone, #851 stays held until #1859 has decided #1177, and #1177 states what then happens to #851 on each branch. #1859 reads the verdict in every case.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- Re-entry conditions (`docs/plans/call-s-adjudication.md:175-185`): (1) supply: the collapse from 203 enumerated to 26 evaluable candidates at build and recovery is repaired, or the corpus is widened until at least 70 evaluable candidates survive it; (2) instrument: a Calor arm that invokes the Calor compiler, so that the diagnostic reaches the agent.
- August 2026 result: 203 candidates enumerated, 26 evaluated after build and recovery, 8 eligible against a bar of 70 (`call-s-adjudication.md:13-26`, `:147-154`; `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/s1-funnel-001/FINDING.md:13-23`, `:79`). The run used the command in step 1 and took about 8 minutes (`FINDING.md:3`, `:8`).
- The task generator writes `TotalConsidered` and `TotalEligible` to `task-generation-report.json`; the August report has 26 and 8 (`bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/s1-funnel-001/task-generation-report.json`). `gen-tasks` converts on the lossy leg (`HarnessConversionMode.Lossy` is the default, `tools/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness/RoundTripConfig.cs:130`).
- The venue's Calor arm is round-tripped C# with no Calor build (`bench/phase0-agent-native/run-bundle.sh:15`, `:519`; `docs/plans/substrate-arm-validity-finding.md`).
- Native files in the August run: 15 of 32, 44 of 110, 74 of 139 (`epochs/s1-funnel-001/task-generation-report.md:41`, `:48`, `:67`). Lossy leg at 0.30.0: 10 of 32, 36 of 112, 58 of 139 (`docs/plans/2026-11-16-milestone-0.30-ci-triage.md:363-367`; `eng/roundtrip-baselines.json`, `blocking_floors.lossy`), so the gate is shut at HEAD. `bench/corpus/README.md:335-336` warns that the August fractions and current reports differ in mode and denominator; the gate uses the counts as a floor only.
- All 8 eligible August tasks were `EffectViolation` tasks (the eight directories under `epochs/s1-funnel-001/bundles/`). #1173 has since retired that operator's signal: `tests/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness.Tests/TaskGenAddressabilityTests.cs:55` pins that it is no longer addressable. Eligible supply at HEAD is therefore expected to be zero for that operator (not re-measured).

## Why

A real-scale benchmark cannot simply be scheduled again: the venue has registered re-entry conditions, and nobody has re-checked them since the converter changed. A measurement that takes minutes closes the question either way and decides #851 and the overlay question of #1859, which matter only if the venue returns. The issue is off the 0.34 exit chain and may slip to 0.35 without holding the release.

## Done when

- `docs/plans/0.34-real-scale-venue-feasibility.md` is committed with: the commit measured; the gate counts; the commands; `TotalConsidered` and `TotalEligible` for both runs; the result of the instrument check; the verdict; and the maintainer's decision with date and sign-off. Or, if the gate was shut, the "not attempted" entry is committed. In both cases `git log` shows the rule commit before the commit that adds counts.
- #851 carries a comment with the verdict and a link, and is un-held or closed as not planned accordingly.
- #1859 carries a comment with the verdict and a link.

## Not in scope

Reopening the venue; any agent run; building a runner whose Calor arm compiles `.calr`; fixing task-generation precision (#851); the `EffectViolation` decision (#1177).

Part of epic #1845. Depends on #1647. Blocks #851, #1859.

issues.title: [0.34] WS-W4 Slice-E hardening: task-gen filter precision (prefix-anchor + custom-DisplayName exclusion rate)
issues.body:
**Current**

The issue records two non-blocking notes from the review of PR #849 about the task generator of the real-scale venue. First, the visible-suite filter uses not-contains on the method name, so holding out `Validate` also hides the tests of `ValidateAsync`. ```markdown
## Status (0.34)

It is worked only if the feasibility record of #1854 (`docs/plans/0.34-real-scale-venue-feasibility.md`) gives the verdict "feasible" and records the maintainer's decision to open a successor plan. If that decision is "move the operator", close this issue as not planned. issues.title: [0.34] EffectViolation's Calor0410 differential was a converter artifact and #1173 retired it — pin the contract, or move the stratum
issues.body:
**Current**

The issue publishes a supply loss. The `EffectViolation` mutation operator of the real-scale venue injected a file-system effect and relied on `Calor0410` firing on the converted code; that only happened because the converter missed effects inside `using` bodies, and #1173 fixed the converter. The issue asks which of two things replaces the signal: probe the mutated body against the clean file's effect row ("pin the contract"), or accept that the operator is not addressable on converted code ("move the operator"). It says this is a decision about the instrument, not a bug fix.

**Amendment**

The title does not change. Set the milestone to 0.34 and add the label `tests`. Insert this section before `## Related`:

```markdown
## Where this is decided (0.34)

The maintainer decides this in the same record as the authored-contract overlay (#1859, `docs/plans/0.34-overlay-and-1177-decision.md`), after the feasibility record of the real-scale venue (#1854, `docs/plans/0.34-real-scale-venue-feasibility.md`) exists. `VerificationAddressability.Probe` (`tools/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness/TaskGen/VerificationAddressability.cs:65`) belongs to the task generator of that venue, which was retired on 2026-08-05 (`docs/plans/call-s-adjudication.md`). All 8 eligible tasks of the last funnel run were `EffectViolation` tasks (`bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/s1-funnel-001/bundles/`), so this choice decides whether the venue has any eligible supply. Until the #1859 record exists, this issue stays open and unstarted.

- **Move the operator** (recommended while the venue stays retired). This is the behaviour at HEAD `bc80daeb`, pinned by `TaskGenAddressabilityTests.EffectViolation_IsNotAddressable_BecauseAConvertedRowCannotContradictItsOwnBody` (`tests/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness.Tests/TaskGenAddressabilityTests.cs:55`). No code changes. The venue then has no known source of eligible tasks.
- **Pin the contract** (recommended only if the maintainer intends to reopen the venue, which includes the case where #1854 failed on eligible supply alone). In `Probe`, check the mutated body against the effect row synthesised from the clean file. That row is computed before the mutation exists, so it is blind to the injected defect. It is still derived from an implementation, so results that rest on it are labelled "derived", reported separately from authored-contract evidence, and never counted as specification-backed (the rule #1709 and #1711 apply to derived contracts).

## Done when

- The #1859 record names one option and the reason.
- Move: this issue is closed with a link to the record, and #851 is closed as not planned with the record linked.
- Pin: a test in `TaskGenAddressabilityTests` shows `Calor0410` reported for the `EffectViolation` mutation against the clean file's row and not for the clean file itself; the task-generation report labels the stratum "derived"; `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated if the test count changes; and the `gen-tasks` measurement of #1854 is run again, with `TotalEligible` appended to its record. The appended entry in `docs/plans/0.34-real-scale-venue-feasibility.md` restates the verdict with the new `TotalEligible` (feasible only if steps 1, 2 and 3 of #1854 are then all met) and carries a dated maintainer line: keep the venue retired, or open a successor plan. #851 is un-held only on "feasible" plus a successor plan; otherwise it is closed as not planned with that entry linked.

This issue may slip past 0.34 without holding the release.
```

**Why**

The right answer depends on whether the venue reopens, and a contract derived from the code under test moves with any defect seeded in that code unless it is pinned from the clean baseline. The eligible supply that #1854 measures depends on this choice, because all 8 eligible tasks of August were `EffectViolation` tasks. Deciding it together with the overlay keeps the maintainer's research decisions in one record.

**Moved from** 0.32 because it is on no 0.32 exit criterion, 0.32 is the most loaded milestone of the roadmap, and its inputs (#1854, #1859) are 0.34 items. It leaves the child table of #1649 (the #1649 amendment drops the row).

issues.title: [0.34] Decision: the authored-contract overlay — a feasibility record on one module, or explicit deferral
issues.body:
## Change

Record one maintainer decision in `docs/plans/0.34-overlay-and-1177-decision.md`, after the feasibility record of the real-scale venue (#1854, `docs/plans/0.34-real-scale-venue-feasibility.md`) exists. The *overlay* is a set of hand-authored contracts laid over converted code, so that a benchmark on real code has specifications for the verifier to check. It was planned in August 2026 with three requirements: deterministic, re-appliable after the code is converted again, and blind by construction, meaning derivable without reference to any injected defect. It was never built and no open issue tracks it.

| Option | What is done | What it costs |
|---|---|---|
| A. Feasibility record | On one natively converted FluentValidation module, chosen after #1647: author refinements and postconditions from the library's documented behaviour; state where they are stored; show that re-running `calor migrate` and re-applying them gives byte-identical output twice; show that they were committed before any defect was selected. Publish the finding either way. | Authoring and a re-apply mechanism that has no design yet. Useful only to a venue that is currently retired. If the finding is positive, the mechanism itself is a separate issue. |
| B. Explicit deferral | Record that the overlay format and re-apply tooling wait until the venue's feasibility record reads "feasible" (#1854). Record that hand-authored contracts on named native modules are produced in 0.35 (#1843) for proof-yield measurement, and that they are not an overlay. State "deferred, not shown infeasible". | Nothing now. The proof-depth claim keeps having no real-scale measurement channel, which the record must say. |
| C. Published negative | Declare the overlay infeasible and retire it. | Requires evidence; none exists without option A. |

**Recommendation.** B if #1854 records "not feasible" or "not attempted"; A if it records "feasible". C is not recommended without A.

**#1177 in the same record.** Choose "pin the contract" or "move the operator" for the `EffectViolation` stratum, as set out in #1177. The plan recommends "move" while the venue stays retired. It recommends "pin", with results labelled "derived", only if the maintainer intends to reopen the venue; that includes the case where #1854 failed on eligible supply alone, because all 8 eligible tasks of August came from this operator.

**Blindness rule to restate in the record.** A contract derived from the code under test moves with any defect seeded in that code, so it proves nothing about the defect. Only contracts authored independently, or pinned from the clean baseline before a defect is chosen, may be used as benchmark specifications.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- The overlay was workstream WS-S4: "deterministic, re-appliable, and blind by construction (derivable without reference to the injected defect, or the arm proves nothing)", with exit criterion "mechanism shipped or D-S4.2 negative published" (`docs/plans/substrate-plan-v0.12.md:107-114`).
- It closed unresolved, "the single largest open question handed to v0.13" (`docs/plans/call-s-adjudication.md:169-173`). The same record notes that a real Calor arm is cheaper than the overlay (`:183-185`).
- The venue it served is retired (`call-s-adjudication.md:3`, `:109-116`).
- In the venue's first dry run every injected mutation was arithmetic, off-by-one or boundary, a class that "a mechanical (non-authored) contract" cannot catch (`bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/w4-dryrun-001/VERDICT.md:58-63`).
- Converted code carries no contracts (16 empty-precondition sites in `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/RoslynSyntaxVisitor.cs`, first at `:2887`).
- FluentValidation has the most native files of the three projects: 58 of 139 on the lossy round-trip leg at 0.30.0, against 10 of 32 for MediatR and 36 of 112 for Serilog (`docs/plans/2026-11-16-milestone-0.30-ci-triage.md:363-367`).

## Why

The real-scale benchmark of August 2026 failed on a supply collapse, a Calor arm that never ran the compiler, and this missing overlay. The project had registered the overlay as the only channel to its proof-depth claim and then closed it without a decision. Capacity is short, so the plan recommends the smaller branch, but the choice is the maintainer's and must be written down. This issue is off the 0.34 exit chain and may slip to 0.35 without holding the release.

## Done when

- `docs/plans/0.34-overlay-and-1177-decision.md` is committed with: the #1854 verdict it read; the option chosen and why; for A, the feasibility finding with the determinism and blindness evidence; for B, the condition that ends the deferral; the #1177 choice and reason; the blindness rule; the date and the maintainer's sign-off (the commit is authored or approved by the maintainer).
- #1177 carries a comment with the choice and a link.

## Not in scope

Building overlay tooling beyond the one-module record; reopening the venue; the 0.35 authored contracts (#1843).

Part of epic #1845. Depends on #1647, #1854. Blocks #1177.

issues.title: [0.34] Native C# 15 unions and closed hierarchies with exhaustive match
issues.body:
**Current**

Convert C# 15 union types and closed hierarchies to native Calor under one spelling chosen by fewest tokens, check `§W` over them for exhaustiveness as C# 15 checks `switch`, and emit C# 15 `union` for `net11.0` targets with a decision for `net10.0`. Done when both convert natively, the match is exhaustiveness-checked, round-trip runtime tests pass and converter metrics are at baseline. The title and body use the retired `§W` marker, and the body depends on issues that have closed (#1597, #1598).

**Amendment**

New title: `[0.34] Native C# 15 unions and closed hierarchies with exhaustive match`. Milestone 0.34. Replace the whole body with:

````markdown
## Change

Give Calor one native form for "one of a closed set of types", convert C# 15 `union` declarations and closed hierarchies to it, and check `match` over it for exhaustiveness. This is parity with the exhaustive `switch` that the C# 15 compiler checks, not an advantage over it.

1. **Source form.** Implement the declaration spelling recorded by #1797 in `docs/design/0.32-breaking-window.md`. Do not choose or adjust the spelling in this issue. If that record keeps unions and closed hierarchies as two forms, implement both. The parser builds `UnionTypeDefinitionNode`, `CalorEmitter` writes it (today it throws), and `calor format` round-trips it. No word is added to the global keyword table unless the window record shows it was reserved in #1803; otherwise the declaration word is recognised by position.
2. **Exhaustiveness.** A declaration yields a `UnionType`, so that the union arm of `PatternChecker.AnalyzeCoverage` is reached. Extend `CheckUnionCoverage` to count typed patterns (`TypePatternNode`); it counts positional and property patterns only. A `match` that omits a case and has no `case _` arm is the existing error Calor0500. Reaching the union arm for a variable means giving the checker a target type, which it does not have in a default build. Giving the checker a target type must not make Calor0500 fire on a bool match where it is silent at the edition commit, unless #1800 recorded that outcome; a test compiles a one-armed match over a bool parameter and pins the recorded behaviour.
3. **Conversion.** `RoslynSyntaxVisitor` converts the C# 15 union and closed-hierarchy syntax that #1638 classified as preserved. A C# `switch` statement over such a type may legally omit cases and a Calor `match` may not, so the converted code must still compile: either an explicit `case _` arm that does nothing, or the member preserved with a reason. A test pins which.
4. **Emission (an open decision).** The compiler writes C# 15 `union` and closed-hierarchy syntax when it is told the consuming project compiles as C# 15 or later. What it writes otherwise is not decided. The options are in the table below. Record the option, the reason and the date in a comment on this issue before the second pull request, and have the maintainer confirm it there; whoever implements the issue proposes and does not choose alone. Whatever is chosen, say where the language version comes from, because the compiler has no such input for emission today (see Baseline).
5. **Registry, fixtures, record.** Promote the registry entries #1638 added for these constructs in `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/FeatureSupport.cs`. Register one D-S1.5 fixture per promoted entry under `bench/phase0-agent-native/fixtures/d-s1.5/` (a registered conversion fixture with a runtime value check, which CI requires for every registry promotion; schema in that directory's `README.md`). Every fixture has to pass on a 10.x runtime, because the test that converts, compiles and runs it has no other host (see Baseline). If the item 4 decision leaves the default output of a construct unable to compile or run against .NET 10, stop and say so on this issue: its entries are then not promoted, and their rows in the coverage record read preserved with the reason kind `not-reached`, cause "needs .NET 11 hosts", and link this issue. That meets the 0.34 exit criterion while the fixture hosts stay on .NET 10. The issue then stays open past 0.34, with everything else in it landed, until those hosts run on 11.x; #1855 decides which SDK builds releases, and no issue yet moves the fixture and scorecard hosts. Do not get a promotion through by making the fixture test skip or drop its value check on some runtimes: that `README.md` freezes the fixture schema and counts a fixture that does not build as failing. Regenerate `website/public/data/feature-support.json` with `calor feature-check --list`. Fill the entries' rows in the coverage record `docs/plans/0.34-native-coverage.md` (one row per registry entry; #1850 creates it).
6. **Reference.** Document the form in `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Teaching/reference.json`, within the token-budget decision recorded by #1823.

**Options for item 4: output when the language version is older than C# 15, or is not supplied**

| Option | What it costs |
|---|---|
| (a) Error: a module that declares the form compiles only for C# 15 or later | No lowering to maintain. The fixture test and the scorecard compile through the compiler with no language version supplied, so on their 10.x hosts the form does not compile; item 5 then stops and the entries are not promoted in 0.34. |
| (b) Lower to ordinary C# types when the version is older or not supplied; write C# 15 syntax only when C# 15 or later is supplied | Two emission paths, each with tests. The same Calor source yields two public C# shapes. The lowering must keep the runtime behaviour of a converted C# 15 union; the existing record lowering (see Baseline) predates C# 15 and declares each variant as a new record. Fixtures and the scorecard can run on 10.x hosts. |
| (c) Always lower | One path and no new input. A converted C# 15 `union` no longer round-trips to a `union`, and C# callers of the generated code lose compiler-checked exhaustiveness. This departs from the issue as first filed, which asked for C# 15 `union` output on `net11.0`. |

The plan recommends (b), because it is the only option under which the registry entries can be promoted while fixtures, the scorecard and the release test job run on .NET 10, and it keeps C# 15 output for C# 15 consumers. If no lowering preserves the behaviour of a converted union, fall back to (a) and apply the stop rule of item 5.

This may land as three ordered pull requests: the source form and exhaustiveness (items 1, 2 and 6, on the existing lowering); conversion with the registry and fixtures (items 3 and 5); the C# 15 emission path (item 4), which needs a .NET 11 leg from #1641 to run its output.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- There is no source form. `UnionTypeDefinitionNode` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Ast/TypeNodes.cs:94`) is built by no parser or converter path; the only `new UnionTypeDefinitionNode(` in the repository is in `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/DeclarationIdentitySidecarTests.cs:1241`. `CalorEmitter` throws "has no 0.30 source form" for it and for `VariantDefinitionNode` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/CalorEmitter.cs:2838-2843`). No file under `src/Calor.Compiler/TypeChecking/` or `src/Calor.Compiler/Binding/` mentions the node (`grep -rl UnionTypeDefinitionNode src/Calor.Compiler` lists seven files, none there), so nothing turns a declaration into a type.
- The C# emitter handles the node: it writes `public abstract record <Name>;` and one `public sealed record <Variant>(...) : <Name>;` per variant (`src/Calor.Compiler/CodeGen/CSharpEmitter.cs:4781-4803`). That is not C# 15 `union` syntax, and C# does not treat that hierarchy as closed.
- `PatternChecker.AnalyzeCoverage` checks `bool` and `UnionType` and treats every other type, enums included, as exhaustive (`src/Calor.Compiler/Analysis/PatternChecker.cs:258-263`). `UnionType` is declared at `src/Calor.Compiler/TypeChecking/CalorType.cs:410` and `new UnionType(` appears nowhere under `src/` or `tests/`, so only `bool` is checked in practice. A non-exhaustive match is Calor0500 at error severity in statement and expression position (`PatternChecker.cs:230-240`).
- `CheckUnionCoverage` reads case names from `PositionalPatternNode` and `PropertyPatternNode` only (`PatternChecker.cs:302-307`). The parser builds `TypePatternNode` for a typed pattern such as `case string text` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Parsing/Parser.cs:3643`, `src/Calor.Compiler/Ast/PatternNodes.cs:426`).
- Current `match` syntax, from `docs/syntax-reference/current-language.md` (example task_18):

  ```calor
  module AgentReference18
    func GetStatus (int:code) → string
      !
      return match code
        case 200 → "OK"
        case 404 → "Not Found"
        case 500 → "Server Error"
        case _ → "Unknown"
  ```

- In a default build the pattern checker is constructed with no type environment (`new PatternChecker(diagnostics)`, `src/Calor.Compiler/Program.cs:913`), so the bool check does not fire for variable targets. Whether it is made effective is a #1800 decision.
- Keywords are one global table (`src/Calor.Compiler/Parsing/Lexer.cs:22-82`); `union` is not in it. A word in that table cannot be used as an identifier, so adding one rejects programs that use it.
- The converter's Roslyn is 5.3.0 (`Directory.Packages.props:18`). `FeatureSupport.cs` has no entry whose key contains "union" or "closed"; #1638 adds them.
- The compiler does not know the consumer's language version when it emits C#: `CompilationOptions` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Program.cs:1340`) has no such property, and the MSBuild task passes `$(LangVersion)` only to validate the generated C# (`src/Calor.Sdk/Sdk/Sdk.targets:96`, `src/Calor.Tasks/CompileCalor.cs:959`).
- Whether C# 15 `union` output compiles against the .NET 10 framework assemblies is not verified. CI has no .NET 11 job before #1639 adds one consumer job and #1641 adds legs for the test shards.
- A registered fixture is checked by `DS15FixtureRegistryTests.AllFixtures_AreCompleteConvertExactlyAndCompile` (`tests/Calor.Conversion.Tests/DS15FixtureRegistryTests.cs:336`). It converts `input.cs`, compiles `expected.calr` and `test.calr` through `Program.Compile` with no language version (`:608`), compiles the generated C# with `LanguageVersion.Latest` against the assemblies of the runtime the test host runs on, loads the result and invokes the entry point (`:701-743`). The test runs in three places, all on a 10.x runtime: the `d-s1.5-fixtures` job (job key `ds15-fixtures`, `.github/workflows/test.yml:613`, SDK at `:660`), the `conversion` shard of `remaining-tests` (`:515-516`), and the `test` job of `.github/workflows/publish-nuget.yml` (line 69), which installs only the release SDK 10.0.401.
- The conversion scorecard stands at 100 of 100 fully converted and 100 of 100 round-trip (`tests/Calor.Evaluation/Scorecard/ConversionScorecardTests.cs:31-32`), over the 100 files listed in `tests/TestData/CSharpImport/manifest.json`; a test asserts the total is exactly 100 (`ConversionScorecardTests.cs:115`). Its round trip compiles generated C# in the test process (`tests/Calor.Evaluation/Scorecard/ConversionScorecardRunner.cs:233`), which runs on .NET 10 (`conversion-scorecard` job, `test.yml:672`, SDK at `:688`).

## Why

In 0.30 a `match` is checked for exhaustiveness only over `bool`, and C# 15 checks it over unions and closed hierarchies. Without this issue a C# 15 file that declares a union can only be kept as preserved C# (the original text inside a raw frame, with no effect, contract or nullability checking), and Calor code cannot declare a closed set of cases at all since `Option` and `Result` were removed (#1617). The union form is new syntax, so its exhaustiveness error rejects no program that compiles under the edition declared at the close of 0.32 (#1805); with the two constraints in items 1 and 2 (no newly reserved word, no newly effective bool check) it is additive under the edition promise. The issue is off the 0.34 exit chain apart from its coverage rows, and may slip to the next milestone without holding the release.

## Done when

- Parser tests accept the #1797 spelling, and a test shows that `calor format` output of a declaration parses back to an equal tree. The two throws at `CalorEmitter.cs:2838-2843` are gone.
- Tests in `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/PatternCheckerTests.cs`: a `match` over a union value that names every case with typed patterns compiles; one that omits a case reports Calor0500 and names the missing case; one that ends in `case _` compiles. The same three for a closed hierarchy if it is a separate form.
- Conversion tests: a C# 15 `union` declaration and a closed hierarchy each convert with no preserved block, and a C# `switch` statement that omits a case converts to Calor that compiles, by the route item 3 chose.
- The item 4 decision is recorded on this issue with option, reason, date and the maintainer's confirmation, and names the source of the language version.
- Emission tests compile and run the generated C# for each branch of the item 4 decision. The C# 15 branch compiles and runs its output in a .NET 11 shard leg from #1641; the branch for older or unsupplied language versions runs on the .NET 10 legs. No test is skipped on either leg: `scripts/check_trx.py` holds every leg to the totals and skip counts in `eng/test-manifest.json`, so a test whose output needs an 11.x runtime still asserts the emitted text on a 10.x host.
- Every union and closed-hierarchy entry is `Full`, or `Partial` with the preserved remainder named in its description. `scripts/check-d-s1.5-fixtures.sh` passes with one fixture per promoted entry, `DS15FixtureRegistryTests` is green on a 10.x host (the `d-s1.5-fixtures` job and the `conversion` shard), and `WebsiteFeatureSupportParityTests.TheWebsiteExportIsTheRegistry` passes.
- Each of those entries' rows in `docs/plans/0.34-native-coverage.md` reads native with its fixture path, or preserved with one of that record's reason kinds. A row closed under the stop rule of item 5 reads `not-reached`, cause "needs .NET 11 hosts", and links this issue; this issue then closes when the entry is promoted with a green fixture.
- A test compiles a module that uses the declaration word as an identifier and pins the behaviour the window record gives (accepted, unless #1803 reserved the word). A test compiles a one-armed `match` over a bool parameter and pins the behaviour #1800 recorded.
- Standing acceptance rule for new hard errors. The pull request states: the conversion scorecard's fully converted count (not below `BASELINE_FULLY_CONVERTED` at the base commit (100 at HEAD bc80daeb), `conversion-scorecard` job); the Calor/C# token ratio per project from the corpus report job (#1779, with the columns #1746 adds or, if #1746 has slipped, by the hand method #1746 records; not higher); and the number of corpus files that newly fall to whole-file preservation (files whose loss list gains `whole-file-preservation`). The three corpus projects are pinned at released tags that build on the .NET 10 SDK (`bench/corpus/README.md`), so they contain no C# 15 syntax and the expected change is none; say so with the numbers.
- One scorecard snippet per newly native construct is added under `tests/TestData/CSharpImport/` and listed in its `manifest.json`, if its round trip compiles on .NET 10. The pull request then raises together the total asserted at `ConversionScorecardTests.cs:115`, `BASELINE_FULLY_CONVERTED`, `BASELINE_ROUNDTRIP` and `tests/Calor.Evaluation/Scorecard/baseline.json`, and states the old and new counts. If the round trip does not compile on .NET 10, the pull request says so, adds no snippet, and #1856 carries the round-trip evidence.
- `TokenBudgetTests` pass (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/TokenBudgetTests.cs:63`: the full reference must stay at or under 17,000 o200k tokens, measured 16,750 on 2026-11-20). `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated for the tests added.

## Not in scope

- Choosing the spelling (#1797), the Roslyn upgrade and the classification of C# 15 syntax kinds (#1638).
- Exhaustiveness over enum matches (#1871).
- A C# 15 project in the round-trip corpus (#1856). If that project has landed, raise its native floors in the pull request that makes unions native.
- Moving the hosts of the fixture test, the scorecard or the release test job to an 11.x runtime. #1855 decides which SDK builds releases.
- `Option` and `Result` stay removed (#1617).

Part of epic #1852. Depends on #1638, #1797, #1641.
````

**Why**

The issue is parity with C# 15, its spelling is decided before the edition is declared, and its title and body must use the current `match` form. It adds a reachable hard error, so it carries the standing acceptance rule. The old body also had no baseline; four facts in the new one change the work (the union arm of the checker exists but cannot be reached, typed patterns are not counted, the C# emitter already lowers to records, and every registered fixture is compiled and run on a .NET 10 host, which constrains what the compiler may emit by default).

**Moved from** 0.31 because the declaration spelling is decided inside the 0.32 breaking window (#1797) and the implementation is off the 0.31 and 0.32 exit chains. It is additive syntax, which the edition promise allows after the freeze.

issues.title: [0.34] Effect manifests and nullability metadata for .NET 11 BCL additions; CI check for missing entries
issues.body:
**Current**

Diff the public API surface of the .NET 11 reference assemblies against .NET 10, add effect-manifest entries for the new APIs in the commonly used namespaces, confirm that nullability metadata is read from the .NET 11 reference assemblies, and add a CI check that lists public BCL APIs with no manifest entry. Done when the manifest covers the new APIs in the listed namespaces and the check runs in CI.

**Amendment**

New title: `[0.34] Effect manifests and nullability metadata for .NET 11 BCL additions; CI check for missing entries`. Milestone 0.34. Replace the whole body with:

````markdown
## Change

Make the built-in effect manifests (the JSON files that say which effects a .NET call has) and metadata binding account for what .NET 11 adds to the base class library (BCL), and add a check that catches the same gap for later versions.

1. **Diff.** Commit a script that lists the public types and members present in the .NET 11 reference assemblies and absent from the .NET 10 ones, restricted to a namespace list written in the script. The list covers the six families the built-in manifests already serve: IO, networking, cryptography, collections, text, threading. The script's output records the two framework versions it compared. Reference assemblies ship in the targeting packs (the `Microsoft.NETCore.App.Ref` packages), which restore as NuGet packages without that SDK being installed; whether an 11.0 pack is published is not verified here.
2. **Classify.** For every addition, record how `EffectResolver` resolves it today: an explicit member entry, a `*` wildcard, the type's `defaultEffects`, a namespace default, or unknown.
3. **Decide each addition.** Each one gets a reviewed decision in a committed file (suggested: `eng/bcl-additions-net11.json`, beside the other registries CI reads from `eng/`): an explicit entry in the matching `src/Calor.Compiler/Manifests/bcl-*.calor-effects.json`; or a line saying it may resolve through a named default, and why; or a line saying it stays unknown, and why. An addition must not count as pure only because its type or namespace has a pure default.
4. **Metadata reach.** List the assemblies of the 11.x `Microsoft.NETCore.App` shared framework that the compiler cannot bind on an 11.x runtime, because they are missing from the embedded metadata manifest's assembly list. Read first which route #1639 recorded in `docs/plans/0.31-toolchain-and-sweep-record.md`. If it generated a second manifest from an 11.x shared framework, that list is expected to be empty; confirm it. If it widened the range of the one 10.x manifest, an assembly that exists only in 11.x cannot simply be added, because every manifest entry must be present in the running runtime (see Baseline); the list then needs to be kept per major version. Add each missing assembly, or record why it stays excluded.
5. **Nullability.** Add a probe that uses an API new in .NET 11: binding its nullable result to a non-nullable variable reports Calor0272, and passing a nullable argument to its non-nullable parameter reports Calor0274. Run it where the compiler runs on an 11.x runtime. The simplest home is a script step of the .NET 11-only consumer job that #1639 added (`net11-only-consumer`), next to that job's existing Calor0272 probe. A unit test would also run on 10.x hosts, where the API does not exist, and it may not skip there (`scripts/check_trx.py` holds skip counts to `eng/test-manifest.json`).
6. **CI check.** A job, or a step of an existing job, re-runs steps 1 to 3 and fails when an addition has no decision. It runs a self-test on every invocation (removing one decision must make it fail), as `scripts/check-d-s1.5-fixtures.sh --self-test` does. A comment in the script says how to re-point it when .NET 12 ships. A new job that runs a `dotnet` build, test, run, pack or restore command must call `./.github/actions/bootstrap-z3` once before it (`scripts/test_z3_hermetic.py:265-299`).

This may land as two pull requests: steps 1 to 3 with the check (step 6), then steps 4 and 5.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- Ten `bcl-*.calor-effects.json` files under `src/Calor.Compiler/Manifests/` hold 177 type mappings (counted by loading the files). 73 of them carry `"defaultEffects": []`, which means pure, and 25 carry a `*` wildcard. Five of the files add 11 namespace defaults; five of those are pure (`System.Reflection`, `System.Threading`, `System.Threading.Tasks`, `System.Collections.Immutable`, `System.Linq`).
- Resolution order is member entry, wildcard, type default, namespace default, IL analysis, unknown (`src/Calor.Compiler/Effects/EffectResolver.cs:7-13`, `:202-247`). So a member that .NET 11 adds to one of the 73 types, or a type it adds to one of the five pure namespaces, is treated as pure and nobody has looked at it. An addition elsewhere is an unknown external call (Calor0411, `src/Calor.Compiler/Diagnostics/Diagnostic.cs:498`).
- The manifests are embedded resources (`src/Calor.Compiler/Calor.Compiler.csproj:164-166`) loaded by `ManifestLoader.LoadBuiltInManifests` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Effects/Manifests/ManifestLoader.cs:95`). `calor effects resolve` prints the resolution of one signature (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/EffectsCommand.cs:50`). Nothing enumerates a framework's surface: no file under `scripts/` or `.github/` mentions `calor-effects` or `Manifests/`.
- Metadata binding, nullability included, takes the framework from the runtime the compiler is running on: the process's trusted platform assemblies (`src/Calor.Compiler/CodeGen/CSharpEmitter.cs:10631`), filtered to the 167 names in `bench/phase0-agent-native/metadata-references-manifest.json` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Binding/Metadata/MetadataContext.cs:637-649`), in a compilation with nullable enabled (`:133-139`). A project's own references are admitted beside them, but one whose simple name is already in that set is skipped, so a project's `System.*` reference assemblies never replace the runtime's copies (`:239-260`). What the compiler knows about a .NET 11 API in those assemblies therefore depends on the runtime it runs on, not on the consumer's target framework.
- An assembly that is new in 11.x is not on the list. It is visible only where a project passes it as an explicit reference, and not to a plain `calor` invocation. At HEAD the manifest admits 10.x only (line 3 of that file); #1639 changes that in 0.31.
- The manifest is embedded in the compiler (`src/Calor.Compiler/Calor.Compiler.csproj:176-177`) and generated by `scripts/generate-metadata-references-manifest.sh`. Every entry must be found among the running runtime's assemblies, or binding throws "Metadata manifest drift" (`MetadataContext.cs:651-667`); every name must also pass the in-code allow-list `MetadataAllowedNamePrefixes` (`:623-635`).
- The existing nullability probe is `CopiedCliOutsideCheckout_UsesEmbeddedManifestWithNoTypeCheck` (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/Binding/BindingRoutingCliTests.cs:257-292`), which expects Calor0272 for an API that exists in .NET 10.
- The old body named post-quantum cryptography as an example of a .NET 11 addition. Not verified; take the additions from the diff.

## Why

The built-in effect tables were written against .NET 10. Two failures follow on .NET 11. A new API with no entry is charged as unknown, which under the default strict policy is an error the user must work around. Worse, a new member on a type with a pure default is accepted as pure with no review, which is an unsound built-in contract. A one-time sweep would decay at .NET 12, so the check is the deliverable that lasts. #1705 (0.36) reuses this work for the pilot's platform matrix.

## Done when

- The diff script and its output are committed, and the output names the two framework versions compared and the namespace list.
- The decision file has one line for every addition in the namespace list. No addition resolves to unknown, or through a type or namespace default, without a line that says so and why.
- The pull request lists the assemblies found in step 4 and what was done with each. If there are none, it says how that was checked.
- The nullability probe passes on an 11.x runtime in CI, reports Calor0272 and Calor0274 for the two cases, and names the API it uses.
- The CI check is green on `main`, and its self-test fails when one decision is removed (shown by the self-test's own output in the job log).
- `ManifestLoaderTests` (`tests/Calor.Enforcement.Tests/ManifestLoaderTests.cs`) and `calor effects validate` pass with the new entries. `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated for the tests added.
- Standing acceptance rule. An explicit entry that gives effects to a call the compiler accepts as pure today (an API that existed in .NET 10, or a .NET 11 addition that resolved through a pure default or wildcard) turns a program that compiles into an error. For each such entry the pull request says so, the release notes name the call and the effect to declare, and the pull request reports: the conversion scorecard's fully converted count (`conversion-scorecard` job; not lower), the Calor/C# token ratio per project from the corpus report job (#1779, with the columns #1746 adds or, if #1746 has slipped, by the hand method #1746 records; not higher), and the number of corpus files that newly fall to whole-file preservation. For entries on .NET 11 additions the expected change is none, because the three corpus projects build for `net8.0` and `net10.0` (`tools/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness/ProjectConfigs.cs:128`, `:161`, `:189`); say so with the numbers.
- The same entries respect the edition promise that #1805 declared. If the promise lets a fix that withdraws an unsound acceptance reject programs within an edition, the entry ships as above. If it does not, the entry is not added in this edition: its line in the decision file reads "resolves through a pure default; deferred to the next edition", with the effect it should carry.

## Not in scope

- Admitting an 11.x runtime in the metadata manifest: #1639 (0.31).
- Effect contracts for the callee families behind most unknown-charged call sites on the corpus: #1841.
- APIs outside the namespace list. Widening the list is a follow-up once the check exists.

Part of epic #1852. Depends on #1639. Blocks #1705.
````

**Why**

The one urgent slice of this issue (the manifest must admit an 11.x runtime) went to #1639 in 0.31. What remains had no checkable finish: "covers the new APIs" had no list behind it, a check that lists every public BCL API without an entry would print most of the framework (177 type mappings exist), and the body pointed at reference assemblies, while for framework assemblies the compiler reads the copies of the runtime it runs on.

**Moved from** 0.31 because nothing on the 0.31 exit chain needs it once #1639 carries the runtime-admission slice, and from 0.32 because that milestone was overloaded and this row is off its chain.

issues.title: [0.34] CI legs for .NET 11 alongside .NET 10
issues.body:
**Current**

Add .NET 11 legs next to .NET 10 for the test shards, `cli-tool-consumer`, `z3-consumer-matrix`, the SDK consumer matrix and `roundtrip-verification`, as parallel matrix entries, possibly with only a subset on pull requests. Done when every listed job has a .NET 11 entry and total pull-request wall time does not grow by more than one parallel leg.

**Amendment**

New title: `[0.34] CI legs for .NET 11 alongside .NET 10`. Milestone 0.34. Replace the whole body with:

````markdown
## Change

Add .NET 11 legs to `.github/workflows/test.yml` beside the .NET 10 legs (a leg is one job or matrix entry), for:

- the 11 test shards of `remaining-tests` (one test project per matrix entry);
- both modes of `roundtrip-verification`.

The starting point is the one .NET 11 job CI has after 0.31: `net11-only-consumer`, the Linux x64 job #1639 added, which consumes the packed tool and SDK where only .NET 11 is installed. This issue leaves that job as it is, reuses its way of installing an 11.0.x SDK, and adds legs for the jobs that run in the checkout. The consumer matrices (`sdk-package-consumer`, `cli-tool-consumer`, `z3-consumer-matrix`) are #1855, which builds on this issue. Keep every .NET 10 leg.

**What a .NET 11 leg is.** In a shard leg, the test host and the `calor` processes it starts run on an 11.x runtime. In a round-trip leg, the corpus subjects are built by an 11.0.x SDK. Each leg proves which it got.

- *Test shards.* Read the tool-framework decision that #1639 recorded in `docs/plans/0.31-toolchain-and-sweep-record.md`. If `calor` stays a `net10.0` tool that rolls forward, the leg builds as the .NET 10 leg does, installs an 11.0.x SDK beside 10.0.x, and makes the test host run on the 11.x runtime. A `net10.0` test host uses a 10.x runtime when one is installed, so the leg has to force the newest major, for the test host and for the `calor` processes the tests start (for example with the `DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD` environment variable; check it against the .NET documentation, including its effect on the SDK's own commands). If the projects were made to target both frameworks, the leg runs the shard for `net11.0`. If the tool became `net11.0` only, record that and add nothing for the shards.
- *Round trip.* The harness builds each corpus subject (a project the round-trip job converts, compiles back and tests) in a working copy outside the checkout with whatever SDK is newest on the runner. A .NET 11 leg installs an 11.0.x SDK beside the two the job already installs, so the subjects and their round-tripped copies are built by the .NET 11 SDK. The harness and the converter still run on the runtime the checkout builds for. Each mode uploads its reports under a fixed artifact name that the `roundtrip-summary` job reads (`test.yml:982-985`), so a .NET 11 leg uses its own artifact names.

**Constraints.**

1. Add the legs as new jobs, or as matrix entries that leave the frozen steps untouched. The determinism protocol (a registered list of CI steps that may not be weakened) covers "Run project tests" and "Enforce test inventory" in `remaining-tests`. Validation fails if that job gains `if`, `continue-on-error`, `env` or `defaults`, if the workflow gains a top-level `env` or `defaults`, or if "Run project tests" is not exactly the registered call with no other key. `scripts/run-shard-tests.sh` is pinned by hash, so changing it needs a reviewed re-pin. Do not set a variable for the registered job through `$GITHUB_ENV` in an earlier step either: that changes how the frozen step runs without the validator seeing it. A new job may call the same script with its own `env`.
2. Each .NET 11 shard leg runs `scripts/check_trx.py` against `eng/test-manifest.json` as the .NET 10 leg does. A test that cannot pass on .NET 11 is fixed. The manifest has no per-runtime field today (`expectedTotal` and `expectedSkipped` are per project), so if an exception is unavoidable, add a field for it with a reason, teach `scripts/check_trx.py` to read it, and cover it in that script's `--self-test`. Do not filter tests out in the workflow.
3. Every job that runs a `dotnet` build, test, run, pack or restore command calls `./.github/actions/bootstrap-z3` exactly once, before the first such command (`scripts/test_z3_hermetic.py:265-299`, run by the `calor-first-guard` job). Decide whether the new shard legs are registered as test-host cells in `eng/z3-consumers.json` (`matrix`) and say so in the pull request.
4. Choose which legs run on pull requests and which on `main` only, and record the choice in this issue. If #1590 is still open when this starts, the compiler shard's .NET 11 leg runs on `main` only. If #1590 is still open, add the shard legs as new jobs and leave the `remaining-tests` job untouched: any commit that changes that job restarts the 30-run window #1590 is measured over. If a matrix entry in `remaining-tests` is unavoidable, post the commit on #1590 so its window is restarted knowingly.

This may land as two pull requests: the shard legs, then the round-trip legs.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- `.github/workflows/test.yml` defines 18 jobs that expand to 43 with their matrices (counted from the file). Its 14 `dotnet-version` entries are `10.0.x` or `8.0.x`.
- `remaining-tests` (`test.yml:496`) has 11 shards (`:511-534`). The compiler shard has a 40-minute limit and the others 15 (`:508`). The compiler shard runs four parts and a historical-replay host at once and adds 8 GB of swap to fit (`scripts/run-shard-tests.sh`).
- Registered gate steps: `tests/TestData/DeterminismProtocol/protocol.json` (`gates`) lists four steps in `test.yml`: "Run project tests" and "Enforce test inventory" in `remaining-tests`, "Run verifier-runtime differential gate" in `test`, and the protocol's own validation step in `calor-first-guard`. It lists the same two shard steps for the `test` job of `.github/workflows/publish-nuget.yml`. "Run project tests" is registered as exactly `bash scripts/run-shard-tests.sh "${{ matrix.name }}" "${{ matrix.project }}"`, with the script pinned by SHA-256 (`scriptSha256`). The structural checks are in `scripts/determinism_protocol.py:155-196`, and CI runs them with `python3 scripts/determinism_protocol.py validate --root . --baseline-ref origin/main`.
- `eng/test-manifest.json` pins `expectedTotal` and `expectedSkipped` per test project (22,559 tests for `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests`); `scripts/check_trx.py` enforces both in the "Enforce test inventory" step.
- 350 of the 351 tracked project files target `net10.0`, 340 by their own declaration and 10 through `Directory.Build.props:4` (the exception is a `netstandard2.0` Roslyn analyzer under `tests/Calor.Evaluation/Analyzers/`). `global.json:3-4` pins SDK 10.0.100 with `latestMinor`, so commands run inside the checkout resolve a 10.0.x SDK even when 11 is installed.
- `roundtrip-verification` (`test.yml:949`) has two modes and a 40-minute limit (`:976`) and installs .NET 10 and .NET 8 (`:1002-1010`). The harness copies each subject to a temporary directory and drops its `global.json` (`tools/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness/RoundTripPipeline.cs:308-309`, `:352-357`). Floors are enforced by `python3 scripts/roundtrip_baselines.py check` (`test.yml:1045-1048`). One later step hard-codes `bin/Release/net10.0/calor.dll` (`test.yml:1032`).
- `tests/Shared/Z3ConsumerGuardTests.cs` is linked into every test host and fails, never skips, when the host is not what the job expects (`CALOR_Z3_EXPECTED_RID`, `test.yml:1524`). It is a model for a runtime guard.

## Why

After #1639 a user can run Calor where only .NET 11 is installed, but CI proves it with one Linux x64 job. The compiler then runs on a runtime it was not built against and binds user code against framework assemblies no test has seen. Legs for the shards show whether the 22,559 compiler tests and the others hold on that runtime; legs for the round trip show whether corpus subjects built by the .NET 11 SDK still meet the floors. #1856 needs the round-trip leg to add a C# 15 project, and #1855 reuses the mechanism for the consumer matrices.

## Done when

- A .NET 11 leg exists for each of the 11 shards and both round-trip modes, and all of them are green on five consecutive `main` runs without a rerun.
- Each shard leg fails unless its test host ran on an 11.x runtime. The pull request shows the guard discriminating: a run with the expected major set to a wrong value fails.
