````markdown
- Each shard leg passes `scripts/check_trx.py` with the totals and skip counts in `eng/test-manifest.json`. Every .NET 11 exception is a registered manifest entry with a reason, read by `scripts/check_trx.py` and covered by its `--self-test`. The manifest is updated for the tests this issue adds.
- Each round-trip leg prints `dotnet --version` from a directory outside the checkout, fails unless it begins `11.`, and passes `scripts/roundtrip_baselines.py check` on the committed floors (the per-subject minimums in `eng/roundtrip-baselines.json`). A floor that cannot be met under the .NET 11 SDK is recorded with its cause and changed only by the reviewed route described in that file (`_update_workflow.lowering`).
- `python3 scripts/determinism_protocol.py validate --root . --baseline-ref origin/main` exits 0, and `python3 scripts/test_determinism_protocol.py` and `python3 scripts/test_z3_hermetic.py` pass. The `remaining-tests`, `test` and `calor-first-guard` jobs have gained no `if` or `continue-on-error`, `remaining-tests` has gained no `env` or `defaults`, and `scripts/run-shard-tests.sh` is unchanged or re-pinned with `repinnedFrom` recorded.
- Wall time: the median duration of the first ten successful pull-request runs of the `Tests` workflow after the merge (from `gh run list --workflow test.yml --event pull_request --status success --json createdAt,updatedAt`) is at most 5 minutes above the median of the ten before it. The 5-minute bound is a proposal the maintainer may change when approving this issue; the earlier wording, "not more than one parallel leg", named no number. If the bound fails, move legs to `main` only until it holds.
- The split between pull-request legs and `main`-only legs is recorded in a comment on this issue.

## Not in scope

- The consumer matrices on .NET 11, the release SDK pin and `global.json`: #1855.
- .NET 11 legs for the `test`, `quality-ratchets`, `id-validation`, `conversion-scorecard`, `d-s1.5-fixtures` and `member-oracle` jobs, the scheduled workflows, and the release workflow.
- A C# 15 project in the round-trip corpus: #1856.

Part of epic #1852. Depends on #1749, #1639. Blocks #1855, #1856, #1643, #1705.
````

**Why**

Parallel legs were scheduled while the compiler shard was at its limit, so the issue follows the CI-health work. The old body also left three things an agent could not act on: it did not say what a .NET 11 leg is while every project targets `net10.0` and the SDK is pinned to 10.0.x; its suggestion of a pull-request subset cannot be made with a condition on the registered jobs; and its wall-time bound named no number. The consumer matrices belong to #1855.

**Moved from** 0.31 because it adds CI load while the compiler shard is near its 40-minute limit and must follow #1749 (and #1590 where it can); no 0.31 or 0.32 exit criterion needs it.

issues.title: [0.34] Dependency refresh: System.CommandLine beta4 → stable, Roslyn/MSBuild packages, drop unused old test TFMs
issues.body:
**Current**

Bring three packages to current stable releases: `System.CommandLine` from `2.0.0-beta4.22272.1` to stable 2.0.x with every command's observable behaviour unchanged, `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp` to the C# 15 release (assigned to #1638), and `Microsoft.Build.Utilities.Core` to the version matching the chosen SDK (assigned to #1639). Delete old target frameworks that serve no purpose. Done when no prerelease dependencies remain, CLI tests pass with unchanged output, and every remaining old target framework has a stated reason.

**Amendment**

New title: `[0.34] Dependency refresh: System.CommandLine beta4 → stable, Roslyn/MSBuild packages, drop unused old test TFMs` (only the prefix changes). Milestone 0.34. Replace the whole body with:

````markdown
## Change

Move `System.CommandLine` from the 2022 prerelease to a stable release with the CLI's observable behaviour unchanged, and leave no prerelease dependency.

| Package | Today (`Directory.Packages.props`) | Target | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `System.CommandLine` | `2.0.0-beta4.22272.1` (line 25) | the current stable 2.x release when the work starts | this issue |
| `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp` | 5.3.0 (line 18) | the release that parses C# 15 | #1638. Once #1638 has closed, delete this row. |
| `Microsoft.Build.Utilities.Core` | 18.0.2 (line 16) | decided with the release SDK | #1855 |

Three parts, as ordered pull requests.

1. **Pin the surface before touching the package.** Add a snapshot test, generated from the beta4 build, that records for the root command and each of the 29 registered subcommands and their nested subcommands: the `--help` text; each option's names, aliases, arity and default; and the exit code and standard-error text for an unknown option and for a missing required argument. Suggested home: `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/CliSurfaceSnapshotTests.cs`, driving the built tool through `CliTestHarness.RunCli` as the existing CLI tests do, with the snapshot committed under `tests/TestData/`.
2. **Migrate.** Replace the beta4 API (option and argument construction, handlers, binding, invocation) in `src/Calor.Compiler`, in `tests/Calor.Evaluation`, and in the tests that build commands directly. Regenerate every `packages.lock.json`.
3. **Target frameworks.** Nothing is left to delete (see Baseline). Add a one-line comment to `tests/Calor.Evaluation/Analyzers/EffectDiscipline.Analyzers.csproj` saying why it targets `netstandard2.0`.

**Gate.** Part 2 merges only after every paid agent collection of 0.31 to 0.33 (a benchmark run that spends on a model API and drives `calor` through the harness in `bench/phase0-agent-native/`) has published its results or been declined: #1605, #1810, the paid re-run in #1645, #1811 and #1831, and the example-bank comparison of #1835 if the #1832 record authorised it (option (a)). Each run's registration (#1770, #1816, #1832) is meant to pin its arms (the sides of a paired benchmark run) to commits, so a collection in flight should not be corrupted either way; the gate keeps every harness invocation on one argument parser across the three milestones whose results are compared. While one of them is authorised but not yet published, part 2 waits; parts 1 and 3 do not.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- `System.CommandLine` is the only prerelease: `git ls-files '*.csproj' '*.props' '*.targets' | xargs grep -nE 'Version(Override)?="[0-9][^"]*-'` prints only `Directory.Packages.props:25`.
- 30 files under `src/Calor.Compiler` import `System.CommandLine`: 29 in `Commands/` and `Program.cs`. They hold 253 `new Option<` or `new Argument<` constructions, 45 `SetHandler` calls and 38 uses of `InvocationContext` (counted with `grep`).
- `Program.cs` registers 29 subcommands (`src/Calor.Compiler/Program.cs:309-337`), parses once early to read the telemetry options (`:342-344`) and then invokes (`:354`).
- Outside the compiler, `tests/Calor.Evaluation/Program.cs` and two files under `tests/Calor.Evaluation/Equivalence/` define commands, and seven test files import the namespace (five in `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests`, one in `tests/Calor.Evaluation/Tests`, one in `tests/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness.Tests`).
- 56 test files drive the CLI as a subprocess through `CliTestHarness.RunCli` (206 call sites, counted with `grep`). Only two tests pass `--help`, and each asserts only that one or two named strings are present or absent (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/DocDriftCheckerTests.cs:1827`, `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/Migration/LosslessConversionContractTests.cs:932`). No test records the help text or the option tables. The benchmark harness itself calls `--help` to check that a compiler build is runnable (`bench/phase0-agent-native/run-pair.sh:442-443`).
- 31 pages under `website/content/cli/` describe commands and options by hand.
- Target frameworks: of 351 tracked `.csproj` files, 340 declare `net10.0`, 10 inherit it from `Directory.Build.props:4`, and one declares `netstandard2.0`: the Roslyn analyzer `tests/Calor.Evaluation/Analyzers/EffectDiscipline.Analyzers.csproj:4`, which also pins `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp` 4.8.0 for itself (line 29). The `net6.0`, `net462`, `net8.0` and `net9.0` targets the old body mentioned are gone. The remaining mentions of old frameworks are data, not targets: the ranking in `src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/ImportCommand.cs:447-458`, the corpus subjects built at `net8.0` (`tools/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness/ProjectConfigs.cs:128`, `:189`), and test fixtures.
- Restore runs in locked mode (`Directory.Packages.props:5-6`) and there are 38 `packages.lock.json` files.
- The old body gave 2.0.13 (2026-10-13) as the stable release and asked to evaluate 3.0 once it is stable with .NET 11. Neither version is verified from the repository; check nuget.org when the work starts.

## Why

The CLI's argument layer rests on a four-year-old prerelease whose API was replaced before the stable release, so every command file changes. The risk is not the edit but a silent change in what the tool accepts or prints: agents, the benchmark harness, the MCP server's callers and 31 documentation pages depend on option names, defaults and exit codes, and no test records them today. Pinning the surface first turns the migration into a diff against a snapshot.

## Done when

- The snapshot test from part 1 is merged before part 2, and after part 2 it passes with the snapshot unchanged. Any intended difference is listed in the pull request with its reason and has a `CHANGELOG.md` entry.
- `git ls-files '*.csproj' '*.props' '*.targets' | xargs grep -nE 'Version(Override)?="[0-9][^"]*-'` prints nothing.
- Every job of the `Tests` workflow is green, including `cli-tool-consumer` and `sdk-package-consumer` on all five platforms (the package closure changes) and the `packages` job of `reproducible-builds.yml`.
- One zero-cost harness pass still works: `bench/phase0-agent-native/run-pair.sh --pair <dir> --arm calor --null-agent` exits 0 on one pair under `bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs/` that runs on the current syntax (#1766 wires the harness to it). `--null-agent` applies the reference solution and spends nothing. The pull request names the pair.
- The pull request for part 2 links, for each collection in the gate, its published result or its recorded decline.
- `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated for the tests added.
- The `netstandard2.0` project file carries its reason.

## Not in scope

- The Roslyn upgrade (#1638) and the MSBuild package version (#1855).
- New options, renamed options, or help-text edits. Do them separately, after the migration, so the snapshot diff stays empty.
- A move to `System.CommandLine` 3.x.
- Other packages in `Directory.Packages.props`. They are stable releases; refreshing them is not part of this issue.

Part of epic #1852. Depends on #1605, #1810, #1645, #1831, #1811, #1835.
````

**Why**

The command-line migration is scheduled after the paid collections; the Roslyn row of the table belongs to #1638 and the MSBuild row to #1855. Checked against HEAD, the old-framework half of the issue is already done, and "pin it with the existing CLI tests" would have pinned almost nothing, because no test records help text or option tables.

**Moved from** 0.31 because it rewrites the argument layer of every command and is off every exit chain through 0.33; it lands after the 0.31 to 0.33 paid collections.

issues.title: [0.34] Complete net11.0 support (remainder of #1639)
issues.displaces: none: new capacity justified in body
issues.body:
## Change

Finish what #1639 left when it was cut to the 0.31 minimum (one Linux x64 job, packages built by the .NET 10 SDK). Four parts, in this order; each can be its own pull request.

1. **Consumer matrices on .NET 11.** Extend the Linux x64 .NET 11-only consumer job that #1639 added (`net11-only-consumer`) to every RID (runtime identifier: the operating system and architecture a leg runs on) of `sdk-package-consumer` and `cli-tool-consumer` in `.github/workflows/test.yml` (five each: linux-x64, linux-arm64, osx-arm64, win-x64, win-arm64). In each leg the packages are built by the repository's SDK, as the existing consumer jobs build them, and are consumed where only 11.x SDKs and runtimes are listed, by the technique of #1639's job, with the checks the .NET 10 legs run (`.github/scripts/test-sdk-package.sh`, `.github/scripts/test-cli-tool-consumer.sh`). Give `z3-consumer-matrix` (four RIDs, test hosts in a checkout) a .NET 11 entry with the mechanism #1641 chose for the test shards. Follow the split #1641 recorded between legs that run on pull requests and legs that run on `main` only.
2. **Decision: which SDK builds releases, and the repository pin.** Put the options below to the maintainer and record the answer. If the answer moves the pin, change every pin site in one pull request and prove byte reproducibility again on the new SDK.
3. **Z3 packaging under the .NET 11 SDK.** Show that packages built by an 11.0.x SDK carry the same verified Z3 files: `ValidateZ3Assets` runs, and both packages hold the native library for every supported RID. If releases stay on the .NET 10 SDK, this is one CI job that packs from a copy of the checkout whose `global.json` admits the 11 SDK; if releases move, the release jobs are the evidence. Loading Z3 at run time on .NET 11 was already required by #1639 and is not repeated here.
4. **Documentation, the MSBuild package and the language server.** Update the lines listed under Baseline. Decide whether `Microsoft.Build.Utilities.Core` moves (this row came from #1642) and record the version and the reason. Record the disposition of `calor-lsp`, the separate `net10.0` executable that `calor lsp` spawns (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/LspCommand.cs:19`; `src/Calor.LanguageServer/Calor.LanguageServer.csproj`): either it gets the roll-forward setting #1639 chose for `calor` and a step in a .NET 11-only consumer leg starts it and completes an `initialize` request, or the record states that the language server needs a 10.x runtime and `website/content/getting-started/installation.mdx` says so.

**Decision for the maintainer (part 2)**

| Option | What changes | What it costs |
|---|---|---|
| A. Releases stay on SDK 10.0.401; `global.json` stays at 10.0.100 with `latestMinor` | Nothing in the release pipeline. | The repository cannot be built on a machine that has only the .NET 11 SDK. Packaging under the .NET 11 SDK is proven by one CI job, not by releases. |
| B. Releases move to one exact 11.0.x SDK; `global.json` moves to 11.0.100 | Every pin site in Baseline, in one pull request. | New byte-reproducibility evidence, because the existing evidence holds for 10.0.401 only. Contributors need the .NET 11 SDK. The .NET 10 legs of #1641 then need a 10.x runtime installed beside it. |
| C. `global.json` allows either major (`rollForward: latestMajor`); releases stay pinned by the action | One line. | Non-release jobs resolve whatever SDK is newest on the runner image, so the SDK under test can change with no commit; each job would have to name its SDK. |

The plan recommends A for 0.34. .NET 10 is the long-term-support release and .NET 11 is a standard-term release (#1639 body); nothing a user receives depends on which SDK built the package once the consumer legs of part 1 pass; and B spends a reproducibility re-proof for no user-visible change. Two earlier records can remove the choice. If #1639 already moved the pin in 0.31 (its decision 3, option (ii), which its tool-framework options 1(b) and 1(c) force), part 2 records that and only checks that the pin sites agree. If #1638 recorded that the Roslyn upgrade cannot build on the .NET 10 SDK, B is forced. Record the option, the reason, the date, and the event that reopens the question (for example the end of .NET 10 SDK servicing) as a dated entry in `docs/plans/0.31-toolchain-and-sweep-record.md`, beside the three decisions #1639 recorded there. Filing this issue decides nothing.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- Consumer jobs in `.github/workflows/test.yml`: `sdk-package-consumer` (line 1378, five RIDs), `cli-tool-consumer` (line 1420, five RIDs, 35-minute limit), `z3-consumer-matrix` (line 1468, four RIDs; linux-x64 is covered by the main jobs). The release workflow repeats the SDK matrix as `sdk-consumer` (`.github/workflows/publish-nuget.yml:198-237`). Each installs `10.0.x` or the pinned release SDK.
- The package layout names the framework: `tasks/net10.0/` (`src/Calor.Sdk/Calor.Sdk.csproj:117`, `.github/scripts/inspect-sdk-nupkg.sh:36-42`) and `tools/net10.0/any/` (`.github/scripts/test-cli-tool-consumer.sh:65`, `.github/workflows/publish-nuget.yml:475-476`). The consumer template targets `net10.0` (`tests/SdkConsumer/CalorLib/CalorLib.csproj:7`, `tests/SdkConsumer/CalorLib.Tests/CalorLib.Tests.csproj:5`).
- Release SDK pin sites: the composite action installs `10.0.401` into a job-private directory and fails unless `dotnet --version` is `10.0.401` (`.github/actions/setup-release-sdk/action.yml:23`, `:46-48`); `ReleaseSdkPinTests` holds six workflows to it (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/Release/ReleaseSdkPinTests.cs:18`, `:22-26`); `check-runtime --sdk 10.0.401 --prune` is in `.github/workflows/reproducible-builds.yml:43` and `.github/workflows/publish-nuget.yml:443`, and `scripts/test_reproducible_builds.py:345` asserts that string.
- `global.json:3-4` pins 10.0.100 with `latestMinor`, so no 11.x SDK can build the repository.
- Byte reproducibility: the `packages` job of `.github/workflows/reproducible-builds.yml` builds the packages twice at two paths and compares every entry. The action's own description says the evidence holds for Microsoft's SDK 10.0.401 only (`action.yml:3-4`).
- Z3 packaging: `ValidateZ3Assets` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Calor.Compiler.csproj:84`) verifies the bootstrapped files before references resolve, and `AddZ3AssetsToOutput` (`:112-114`) adds the five native libraries. `scripts/check-packaged-z3.py` checks a package (`.github/workflows/publish-nuget.yml:475-476`); the supported RIDs are in `eng/z3-consumers.json`.
- `Microsoft.Build.Utilities.Core` is 18.0.2 (`Directory.Packages.props:16`), referenced by `src/Calor.Tasks/Calor.Tasks.csproj:23`. The package deliberately ships no `Microsoft.Build.*` assembly, because the consumer's MSBuild supplies them (`.github/scripts/inspect-sdk-nupkg.sh:119-124`). A version newer than the oldest supported SDK's MSBuild is therefore a compatibility question, not a routine bump.
- User pages that name only .NET 10 and that #1639 does not touch: `website/content/getting-started/installation.mdx:137` (download link), `:142` (`dotnet-sdk-10.0`) and `:298`, `website/content/getting-started/hello-world.mdx:14`, `website/content/getting-started/how-it-works.mdx:16`, `website/content/benchmarking/metrics/effect-discipline.mdx:54`, and the sample project at `website/content/guides/adoption-playbook.mdx:57`. `grep -rn 'NET 10\|net10\|dotnet-sdk-10\|dotnet/10' website/content --include=*.mdx` lists them with the two lines #1639 updates (`installation.mdx:12`, `index.mdx:38`) and two build-output paths (`website/content/contributing/development-setup.mdx:201`, `website/content/guides/cross-module-effect-propagation.mdx:223`), which change only if the tool's framework did.
- Every workflow job that runs a `dotnet` build, test, run, pack or restore command, or one of the two consumer scripts, must call `./.github/actions/bootstrap-z3` exactly once before it (`scripts/test_z3_hermetic.py:265-299`). `eng/z3-consumers.json` (`matrix`) registers which job covers which RID for the test hosts, the SDK package and the tool package, and the same script checks those cells (`:301-330`).
- `calor lsp` starts a separate process named `calor-lsp` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/LspCommand.cs:19`). That executable is `src/Calor.LanguageServer/Calor.LanguageServer.csproj` (`AssemblyName` `calor-lsp`, line 5), which targets `net10.0` through `Directory.Build.props:4`. The installation page describes `calor lsp` (`website/content/getting-started/installation.mdx:109`). #1639 covers the `calor` tool, `Calor.Tasks` and generated projects, not this executable.
- Agent-facing text that said "compiles to C# on .NET 10" at HEAD (`src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Teaching/reference.json:6` and `:2432`, and the files generated from them: the four templates under `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Templates/`, `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/agent-syntax-exemplar.md:5`, `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Teaching/Generated/server-instructions.md:1`). #1650 (0.33) removes the version from both source sentences and adds a test. This issue checks that the test exists and passes; only if #1650 has not landed does it edit the two source fields in `reference.json` and regenerate with `calor self-check docs --fix`. No generated file is edited by hand. The generated files are under token budgets (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/TokenBudgetTests.cs:47`, `:63`).
- Contributor text that names the SDK pin: `CLAUDE.md:3`, `:13`, `:61`; `AGENTS.md:4`, `:14`, `:62`; `.github/copilot-instructions.md:3`, `:13`.

## Why

#1639 closes in 0.31 on the smallest scope that makes a .NET 11-only machine work, so three items of its original body would be dropped when it closes: the five-RID consumer matrix on .NET 11, the release SDK decision with its pin sites, and Z3 packaging under the .NET 11 SDK. After 0.31, .NET 11 is proven on Linux x64 alone, while Calor ships native Z3 libraries for five RIDs and the failure this guards against (a solver that does not load, so every contract is silently skipped) is per platform. This issue takes no capacity from another: its work was counted in #1639 before that issue was cut. #1705 (0.36) reuses it for the pilot's platform matrix.

## Done when

- On `main`, `sdk-package-consumer` and `cli-tool-consumer` each have a green .NET 11-only leg on all five RIDs. Each leg asserts that `dotnet --list-sdks` and `dotnet --list-runtimes` print only 11.x lines on the consumer side, and runs the same script checks as its .NET 10 leg, including the solver verdict (contracts Proven, none Skipped, no Calor0710) and the Calor0712 canary in the MSBuild task.
- `z3-consumer-matrix` has a green .NET 11 entry on its four RIDs with zero skips, or this issue records why #1641's mechanism cannot be applied to it.
- The decision entry exists in `docs/plans/0.31-toolchain-and-sweep-record.md` with option, reason, date and reopening event, and is linked from this issue.
- The pin sites agree with the decision: the version in `action.yml:23` and `:46`, `ReleaseSdkPinTests.PinnedSdk`, the two `check-runtime --sdk` arguments, the string asserted in `scripts/test_reproducible_builds.py`, and `global.json`. `ReleaseSdkPinTests` and `python3 scripts/test_reproducible_builds.py` pass, and the `packages` job of `reproducible-builds.yml` is green. If the pin moved, the entry links the two-build comparison on the new SDK.
- A job, or under option B the release packaging job, packs `calor` and `Calor.Sdk` with an 11.0.x SDK and passes `scripts/check-packaged-z3.py` for both packages with `--all-rids`, `.github/scripts/inspect-sdk-nupkg.sh`, and the Linux x64 consumer check on those packages. If restore in locked mode fails under the .NET 11 SDK, the job restores its copy with locked mode off, and the entry records that and which lock files differ.
- The new consumer legs are registered in `eng/z3-consumers.json` (`matrix`), or the pull request says why not, and `python3 scripts/test_z3_hermetic.py` passes.
- The chosen `Microsoft.Build.Utilities.Core` version is recorded with its reason, and the consumer legs on .NET 10 and on .NET 11 both pass with it.
- Each user-page line listed under Baseline names .NET 10 and .NET 11 as supported, or no longer names a version. The #1650 test that no generated agent text names a .NET version passes (or, if #1650 has not landed, the two source sentences are reworded here), `TokenBudgetTests` pass, and `calor self-check docs` exits 0. The contributor text matches `global.json`. The pull request lists each line with its new text and, if it reworded the source sentences, states the token change to the four `calor init` templates and the server instructions against their budget (`TokenBudgetTests.cs:47`: 600 tokens at HEAD; #1823 may have changed it).
- The `calor-lsp` disposition is recorded in `docs/plans/0.31-toolchain-and-sweep-record.md`. Either a step of a .NET 11-only consumer leg starts `calor lsp`, completes an `initialize` request and fails if it does not; or the record says the language server needs a 10.x runtime and `installation.mdx` states that next to its `calor lsp` paragraph.

## Not in scope

- Making a .NET 11-only machine work, the tool-framework decision and the roll-forward policy: #1639 (0.31).
- .NET 11 legs for the test shards and the round trip: #1641.
- Effect and metadata coverage for APIs new in .NET 11: #1640.
- The `System.CommandLine` migration: #1642.
- Dropping .NET 10 support.

Part of epic #1852. Depends on #1639, #1641. Blocks #1705.

issues.title: [0.34] A C# 15 project in the round-trip corpus
issues.displaces: none: new capacity justified in body
issues.body:
## Change

Add a small C# 15 project to the round-trip corpus, so that every conversion change is tested against real C# 15 code that is built, converted, compiled back and run. A subject is one project of that corpus; a floor is a committed minimum (tests passed, native fraction, coverage fraction) that the round-trip job enforces for a subject.

1. **The subject.** Add a third in-repository subject beside `tests/Calor.RoundTrip.Synthetic` and `tests/Calor.RoundTrip.Synthetic2`: a library and an xunit test project that target `net11.0` and compile as C# 15 (directory name suggested: `tests/Calor.RoundTrip.Synthetic3`). The library uses every node kind in the C# 15 syntax-kind list that #1638 committed, unions and closed hierarchies among them, and each use has a test that asserts its runtime behaviour. Keep it out of `Calor.sln`, as the other two are. Commit its `packages.lock.json` files; they have to be generated with a .NET 11 SDK, which `global.json` does not admit inside the checkout unless #1855 moved the pin, so generate them from a copy outside it.
2. **Register it** everywhere the corpus is enumerated: `ProjectConfigs` (the `Get` switch, `KnownProjects`, and `SyntheticProjects`, which marks a subject as in-repository and not a pinned submodule), `eng/roundtrip-baselines.json`, `scripts/roundtrip_baselines.py`, the `ROUNDTRIP_PROJECTS` line of the `roundtrip-summary` job in `.github/workflows/test.yml`, `eng/test-manifest.json` (`excludedProjects`), `scripts/test_supply_chain.py`, and the tables in `bench/corpus/README.md`.
3. **Per-leg inventory.** The subject cannot build on the .NET 10 legs. Teach the harness, the floor check and the `roundtrip-summary` job which subjects a leg is expected to run, from the SDK the leg has, so that the .NET 10 legs report the subject as not applicable (neither passed nor failed) and the .NET 11 legs from #1641 must run it. The two project lists are also the default sets of other harness commands (see Baseline); apply the same rule there, so that none of them tries to build the subject where no .NET 11 SDK is installed.
4. **Floors.** Commit the subject's floors for both conversion modes at what the .NET 11 leg measures on `main` when this lands, by the manual procedure in `eng/roundtrip-baselines.json` (`_update_workflow.manual`).

This may land as two ordered pull requests: the per-leg inventory rule (part 3, with its test and no new subject), then the subject with its registration and floors (parts 1, 2 and 4).

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- The corpus has five subjects: two in the repository (`Synthetic`, `Synthetic2`) and three pinned submodules under `bench/corpus/` (`tools/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness/ProjectConfigs.cs:48`, `:54`). `run --all` covers all five.
- Both in-repository subjects target `net10.0` (`ProjectConfigs.cs:76`, `:97`; `tests/Calor.RoundTrip.Synthetic/SyntheticLib/SyntheticLib.csproj:3`). `Calor.sln` contains neither.
- The harness copies a subject to a temporary directory, drops its `global.json` and builds with `dotnet` from the path (`tools/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness/RoundTripPipeline.cs:308-309`, `:352-357`; `--dotnet dotnet` at `.github/workflows/test.yml:1025`). The job installs .NET 10 and .NET 8 only (`test.yml:1002-1010`), so a C# 15 project cannot build there until #1641 adds a leg with the .NET 11 SDK.
- The harness parses with the converter's Roslyn, 5.3.0 at HEAD (`Directory.Packages.props:18`), which #1638 upgrades.
- The floor check requires a report for exactly the listed projects: `PROJECTS` at `scripts/roundtrip_baselines.py:20`, and "incomplete project inventory" at `:116-117`. `DefaultModeOptionsParityTests` holds `ROUNDTRIP_PROJECTS` (`test.yml:1228`) equal to `KnownProjects`.
- Floors for both modes are in `eng/roundtrip-baselines.json` (`blocking_floors.lossy`, `blocking_floors.default`) and in `ProjectConfigs.cs`. The floors of `Synthetic` are 52 of 52 round-trip tests and native and coverage fractions of 1, in both modes.
- The nightly `roundtrip-baselines.yml` installs `10.0.x` and `8.0.x` (lines 35-39) and runs `run --all`.
- `KnownProjects` and `SyntheticProjects` are also the default project sets of other harness commands: `oracle --all` (`tools/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness/Program.cs:119`), `run --all` (`:305`), task generation with `--synthetic` or `--all` (`:500-502`) and `mine --all` (`:1023`). A subject outside `SyntheticProjects` is treated as a pinned submodule (`:793-795`, `:859`).
- `scripts/test_supply_chain.py:93-96` requires the standalone test projects of the two existing subjects to pin `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk` with a `VersionOverride`, and `eng/test-manifest.json` lists them under `excludedProjects` as "round-trip corpus fixture". The same script requires a committed `packages.lock.json` beside every project file that has package references (`:86-91`); the existing subjects have one per project.
- The member-level oracle runs the in-repository subjects in one matrix entry (`test.yml:1160`) against `eng/member-oracle-expected.json`. #1641 adds no .NET 11 leg for that job.

## Why

#1638 teaches the converter to parse C# 15 and classifies each new construct as native or preserved, but its fixtures can only assert parsing and the conversion outcome, because CI runs on the .NET 10 SDK in 0.31. Nothing yet builds a C# 15 project, converts it, compiles the result and runs its tests, which is the only check that a converted union or closed hierarchy behaves as the original did. That check needs the .NET 11 round-trip leg from #1641, so this item was split out of #1638, which closes in 0.31. It takes no capacity from another issue: it is work item 3 of #1638 as originally filed, and it restores the first line of the original epic's done-when ("A C# 15 project in the corpus migrates").

## Done when

- On `main`, both .NET 11 `roundtrip-verification` legs run the subject: no library file is reverted or failed (coverage fraction 1, which the harness computes as files converted natively or with recorded losses over all candidates, `tools/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness/RoundTripReport.cs:560`), the round-tripped build passes all of the subject's tests, and `scripts/roundtrip_baselines.py check` passes with the subject's committed floors.
- On the .NET 10 legs the subject is reported as not applicable, the floor check passes without it, and the `roundtrip-summary` comment shows it as not applicable, not as missing. `python3 scripts/test_roundtrip_baselines.py` has a case showing that a .NET 11 leg whose reports lack the subject fails.
- A test in `tests/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness.Tests` parses the subject's library and fails if a node kind in #1638's committed list does not occur in it.
- `DefaultModeOptionsParityTests` and `python3 scripts/test_supply_chain.py` pass. `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated for the tests added and for the new excluded project.
- The nightly `roundtrip-baselines.yml` either installs the .NET 11 SDK and ratchets the subject's floors, or excludes the subject with a comment that says why.
- The member-level oracle covers the subject, or the pull request records why it cannot yet (no .NET 11 leg for that job).
- If #1643 has not landed when this merges, the union and closed-hierarchy files count as converted with losses, the committed native floor reflects that, and #1643 raises it.

## Not in scope

- Parsing C# 15 and classifying its syntax kinds (#1638); converting unions natively (#1643).
- A C# 15 open-source project as a pinned submodule. An in-repository subject is enough for the check above; add an external one when a suitable project exists.
- Adding the subject to the corpus report job (#1779) or to the benchmark task supply.

Part of epic #1852. Depends on #1638, #1641.

issues.title: [0.35] Epic: verification depth
[0.35] Proof-status inventory on the conversion corpus
issues.displaces: none: new capacity justified in body
issues.body:
## Change

Build one counter that reports what the verifier establishes about a set of `.calr` files, and run it on the conversion corpus (MediatR, Serilog and FluentValidation, pinned under `bench/corpus/`).

1. **The counter.** A console project under `tools/` (for example `tools/Calor.ProofInventory`) that takes `.calr` files or a directory and writes the JSON below. It is a measurement tool, not a `calor` command: whether obligation results get a CLI surface is the decision in #1868, which may adopt this counter. It must not depend on the corpus job, because #1703 re-runs it on the pilot component in 0.36.
2. **Both channels.** An *obligation* is one thing the verifier is asked to establish. Call `Program.Compile` on each file with both options set, as the soundness-sweep harness does (`bench/Calor.Soundness.Sweep/BaselineHost.cs:56-61`):
   - the contract channel (`CompilationOptions.VerifyContracts`; results in `CompilationOptions.VerificationResults`): one result per postcondition and one per parameter refinement. The refinement result is a satisfiability check, not a proof about callers; it gets its own column and is never counted as `proven`;
   - the obligation channel (`CompilationOptions.VerifyRefinements`; results in `CompilationOptions.ObligationResults`): one entry per `ObligationTracker` obligation, by kind (`RefinementEntry`, `RefinementReturn`, `ProofObligation`, `IndexBounds`, `Subtype`).

   A corpus file refers to types in other files of its project. If compiling files one at a time leaves most of them not verified, compile them with their project context, the way the build task passes references and cross-module types (`src/Calor.Tasks/CompileCalor.cs:810-826`).
3. **Columns.**

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| Files | given, verified, and not verified with the first error code of each |
| Obligations | total, by channel and by kind |
| Status | `proven`, `assumed`, `refuted`, `unknown`, `timeout`, `unsupported`, `unavailable` (the `ProofStatus` wire names) and `runtime-only`; the eight sum to the total |
| Assumed by assumption | one count per assumption name, the text before ` — ` in the assumption string: `string-model`, `reference-model`, `checked-arithmetic`, `exceptional-paths:division`, `exceptional-paths:contract-division`. An obligation with two assumptions counts under each and once in `assumed` |
| Unsupported by reason | every reason string with its count in the JSON; the record prints the ten most frequent and always the reason "Null literals are not modeled by the contract translator.", which #1860 reads |
| Refinement satisfiability | satisfiable, unsatisfiable, undecided |

   `runtime-only` is an obligation the solver never sees and the emitter always guards: `ObligationStatus.Boundary`. An obligation left `Pending` because no solver ran counts as `unavailable`. The counter reads each obligation's proof outcome: Discharged is `proven`, Failed is `refuted`, a demoted proof is `assumed`. Under the default obligation policy a failed obligation is a compilation error (Calor1121, or Calor1140 for a `proof` obligation; `src/Calor.Compiler/Program.cs:1104-1105`). A file whose only errors are those two codes is counted as verified, and those obligations as `refuted`.

   Call-site obligations share the kind `Subtype` with assignment obligations at HEAD. #1864 (epic #1861) adds a field that tells them apart, and the by-kind table reports them as their own row once that field exists: if #1864 merged first, this issue adds the row; otherwise #1864 does, in the counter.
4. **On the corpus.** #1779 delivers the corpus report job (`scripts/corpus_report.py`, `.github/workflows/corpus-report.yml`), whose per-project report has a `columns` object that later issues fill. Add a column function that runs the counter on the migrated working copy and stores its output under the key `proof_status`. Count the files the job classifies as native and, separately, those it classifies as partly preserved (some members kept as raw C#).
5. **Record.** Publish the first run in `docs/plans/0.35-proof-status-inventory.md`: Calor commit, corpus tags, the table per project, the number of files verified and not verified, and a ranked list of what keeps obligations from `proven` (each assumption name and each unsupported reason, by count). Post the list on #1662.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- No job reports proof status on the corpus. `calor migrate` has a verification phase (`src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/Project/ProjectMigrator.cs:2214`), but it runs the contract channel only, folds `Assumed` into `Unproven` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/ProofOutcome.cs:390`), and counts a file that yields no result as skipped with no reason (`ProjectMigrator.cs:2297`, `:2302`).
- The converter writes no contracts: every `preconditions:` and `postconditions:` argument in `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/RoslynSyntaxVisitor.cs` is `Array.Empty` (21 occurrences, counted with `grep -c "preconditions:\|postconditions:"`), and the 0.30.0 notes say conversion does not recover contracts that exist only as `throw` guards (`CHANGELOG.md:39-40`). On converted code the contract channel has nothing to check.
- What converted code does have is index-bounds obligations, one per array access and indexed write (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Obligations/ObligationGenerator.cs:798-817`) in the bodies of functions, methods, constructors and operators; accessor bodies and members of nested classes are not visited (`:57-86`). They exist only under `VerifyRefinements` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Program.cs:1074`), which no CLI command sets. The MCP tool `calor_refine` sets it (`src/Calor.Compiler/Mcp/Tools/RefineTool.cs:104`), and so does the sweep harness (`bench/Calor.Soundness.Sweep/BaselineHost.cs:59`), which is a model for calling the compiler with both options.
- A discharged index-bounds obligation is reported `Assumed` with `reference-model` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Obligations/ObligationSolver.cs:326-357`).
- A parameter refinement that the contract channel reports as `Proven` is one that is satisfiable (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Z3/Z3Verifier.cs:183-203`), and `calor verify` adds it to its `Proven Rate` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/VerifyCommand.cs:570`).
- Where the vocabulary lives: `ProofStatus` (`ProofOutcome.cs:15-46`), the five assumption strings (`Z3Verifier.cs:27-70`), `Boundary` (`ObligationGenerator.cs:664`, `:691`, `:851`).

## Why

0.35 sets out to prove more about real programs, and there is no number for what is proved about them today. The inventory orders #1660 and #1661, gives #875, #1851 and #1862 something to report against, supplies the numbers the decisions #1860 and #1868 read, and is repeated by #1703 on the pilot component to size the 0.37 claim. Read from the code, the first run should find no contract-channel obligations on converted code and no `proven` index-bounds obligation. That prediction has not been run; the record must say where it was wrong.

This is new capacity and displaces no issue: it is report-only, and the milestone's first exit criterion cannot be checked without it.

## Done when

- The counter runs on a directory of `.calr` files with no corpus job present, and a test covers it.
- A test gives the counter a fixture with one array access and no contract and finds at least one `IndexBounds` obligation. This guards against an inventory that reads zero because it ran one channel.
- Each of the three per-project corpus reports contains the columns above under `proof_status`, and in each the eight status counts sum to the obligation total. The pull request links the run that produced them.
- A file that cannot be verified is listed with its error code. An `unavailable` count above zero fails the job, because the solver was missing. A test gives the counter a file whose only error is a failed obligation and finds the file counted as verified with one `refuted` obligation.
- The JSON holds every unsupported reason with its count. If #1864 has merged, the by-kind table has a call-site row and a test covers it.
- `docs/plans/0.35-proof-status-inventory.md` exists with the first run and the ranked list, and the list is posted on #1662. For each project it gives the number of native and partly preserved files verified and not verified. If fewer than half of a project's native files were verified (threshold set by this issue), the record says the inventory is not representative for that project and names the missing project context.
- `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated for the tests added (`scripts/check_trx.py` fails CI when a project's test count differs from its `expectedTotal`).
- No existing command changes its exit code, its diagnostics or the C# it emits.

## Not in scope

- Changing any verdict.
- A `calor` option or build property for obligation verification (#1868 decides).
- Authored contracts and the before-and-after metric (#1843). The pilot component (#1703).

Part of #1662. Depends on #1779. Blocks #1843, #875, #1851, #1862, #1868, #1660, #1661, #1860, #1866 and #1703.

issues.title: [0.35] Where the 0.35 contracts come from, and a proof-yield metric on real programs
issues.displaces: none: new capacity justified in body
issues.body:
## Change

1. **Name the set.** Add `bench/proof-yield/manifest.json` (new directory). Candidates are the natively converted files in the #1779 corpus output at the commit of the #1853 record. The rule is fixed here so that the set is not chosen by its results: per corpus project, order the native files by number of public members, descending, path as tie-break, and take the first four that have a member with an `int`, `string`, array or `List<T>` parameter or result and that compile on their own with default `Program.Compile` options. Copy them to `bench/proof-yield/modules/<project>/` with source path, corpus tag and converter commit. List each skipped candidate with its first error code. Four per project, twelve in all, is set by this issue. If fewer than six qualify in total (half the intended set, also set here), stop and report the count on #1662 before authoring anything. The maintainer then records one of two outcomes on #1662: (a) a relaxed selection rule, written before any yield is computed, under which this issue continues; or (b) "not measurable on the corpus", in which case `manifest.json` lists the modules that did qualify, `before.json` is committed over that smaller set with the reason, the release notes report the yield with that caveat, and the issues this one blocks are released.
2. **Author the contracts in two layers.** Neither is produced by a tool that lifts `throw` guards.
   - `hand`: for every public member with an `int`, `string`, array or `List<T>` parameter or result, at least one parameter refinement or postcondition that is true of the code, or a line in the manifest saying why there is none.
   - `agent`: the same starting files given to one coding agent with `docs/syntax-reference/current-language.md` and a prompt committed beside the manifest. Record the model id. Contracts that do not compile are removed and counted. There is no floor: an empty layer is recorded and the issue still closes.

   This is authoring in an ordinary session. Nothing about cost, iterations or success is read from it, and no criterion depends on how well the agent writes Calor. Producing the layer through the benchmark harness would be a paid run that needs its own registration; this issue does not authorise one.
3. **Metric.** *Proof yield* is the number of obligations by status over the set, produced by running the #1853 counter (the console project that issue adds under `tools/`) on each layer. Do not write a second counter. The headline is `proven`, `assumed` by assumption and `unsupported` by reason. Refinement satisfiability stays in the counter's own column and is never added to `proven`: a satisfiable parameter refinement says the function can be called, not that anything was proved. A step of the corpus report workflow (`.github/workflows/corpus-report.yml`, added by #1779) runs the counter on the set, uploads `proof-yield.json` and prints it beside the committed baseline.
4. **Before value.** Commit `bench/proof-yield/before.json`: the yield per layer, the *entry commit* and the command that produced the numbers. The entry commit is the commit of `main` recorded on #1662 when the 0.35 entry criteria were met; the `before` value is the yield of the compiler built from it, so that it does not depend on which verifier changes have merged since. If `git diff --stat <entry commit> HEAD -- src/Calor.Compiler` is empty, measure at `HEAD`. Otherwise check out the entry commit, apply `bench/proof-yield/` and the counter as it was at the #1853 merge commit (a later counter may read compiler members the entry commit lacks, such as #1864's call-site field) and measure there; `before.json` names that counter commit.
5. **Test and record.** `tests/Calor.Verification.Tests/ProofYieldManifestTests.cs` checks that every manifest module and both layers exist and compile, and that the status counts in `before.json` sum to its totals. `bench/proof-yield/README.md` states where the contracts come from, the selection rule, the one command that prints the before-and-after table for release notes, and that a contract the verifier refutes is corrected with the reason recorded, or kept and counted, never deleted to raise the yield.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- Converted code carries no contracts: `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/RoslynSyntaxVisitor.cs` passes `Array.Empty` for every `preconditions:` and `postconditions:` argument (21 occurrences, counted with `grep -c "preconditions:\|postconditions:"`), and the 0.30.0 notes say conversion does not recover contracts that exist only as `throw` guards (`CHANGELOG.md:39-40`).
- The four contract samples (`samples/Contracts/contracts.calr` and the three files in `samples/Verification/`) total 92 lines (measured by `wc -l`) and contain no `string`, array or `List<T>`.
- A postcondition that names `result` is `Unsupported` unless the body is made only of returns, immutable bindings and if/else-if/else (`FunctionBodyEncoder.TryEncodeResult`, `src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Z3/Z3Verifier.cs:814`; refusal at `:424-433`), and whenever the function returns an array (`:414-420`). A successful proof that touches a string, array or user-type term is `Assumed` (`:586-631`).
- The `Proven Rate` of `calor verify` cannot serve as the metric: it counts a satisfiable parameter refinement as `Proven` (`Z3Verifier.cs:183-203`) and folds `Assumed` into `Unproven` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/ProofOutcome.cs:390`).
- Nothing named proof yield exists in the repository.

## Why

The first 0.35 exit criterion is proof yield (Proven, Assumed, Unsupported) reported before and after on a named set of native modules, or, if fewer than six corpus modules qualify under the selection rule of this issue, the outcome the maintainer recorded on #1662. Converted code carries no contracts, so without authored ones the milestone would have only test pairs to prove, and "the verifier got deeper" would be measured on fixtures written to pass. The layers are kept apart because hand-written contracts show what the verifier can do with careful input and agent-written ones show what it is given in practice. From the baseline, `before` is expected to be mostly `unsupported` and `assumed`; that is read from the code, not measured.

This is new capacity and displaces no issue: it is the only source of the number the milestone exits on.

## Done when

- `bench/proof-yield/manifest.json` names the modules with their provenance and lists the skipped candidates.
- If fewer than six modules qualified, #1662 carries the maintainer's recorded outcome, (a) or (b) of step 1, dated before any yield was computed, and the manifest and `before.json` follow it: under (a) they name the relaxed rule; under (b) they cover the modules that did qualify and state the reason.
- The `hand` layer meets the coverage rule in step 2. The `agent` layer exists with its prompt, model id and count of removed contracts.
- `bench/proof-yield/before.json` is committed. It names the entry commit recorded on #1662, the counter commit and the command that produced the numbers, and its refinement-satisfiability counts are separate from `proven`.
- `ProofYieldManifestTests` passes in CI, and `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated for the tests added (`scripts/check_trx.py` fails CI when a project's test count differs from its `expectedTotal`).
- One run of the corpus report workflow prints the current yield beside `before.json` and uploads `proof-yield.json`. The pull request links the run.
- `CHANGELOG.md` has, under `## [Unreleased]`, the `before` table (obligations `proven`, `assumed` by assumption, `unsupported`, per layer) and the command that prints the same table at any commit. The 0.35 close-out (the "publish the proof-yield after value" item of the release close-out checklist in `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md`) adds the value at the release commit beside it; with that line the first exit criterion is met.

## Not in scope

- Changing the verifier.
- Lifting contracts from guards in the converter (#1866, conditional).
- A ratchet that fails CI when the yield drops.

Part of #1662. Depends on #1853. Blocks #875, #1851, #1862, #1660 and #1661, which may not merge before `before.json` is committed.

issues.title: [0.35] Lift the string-proof demotion where non-null is established
issues.body:
*The existing body is in the retired syntax, asks for binder enforcement that shipped in 0.22 as Calor0272 to Calor0274, and reports a false `Proven` that the v0.12 demotion has since closed. What remains is the lift named in its first paragraph.*

## Change

Today every successful proof that touches the solver's string theory is demoted: it is reported `Assumed` under the named assumption `string-model` instead of `Proven`, and its runtime check is kept instead of elided (removed from the emitted C#). Lift that demotion when every string term in the query is established non-null. Keep it for every other string proof.

A string term is established non-null when it is:

1. a string literal, or the result of `Concat` or `Substring` over established terms;
2. a parameter or local, read at a point dominated by a check that establishes non-null and is kept in the emitted C#, with no assignment in between. The checks are the ones the binder's flow narrowing already recognises: a comparison with `null`, and `string.IsNullOrEmpty` or `string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace` being false (`src/Calor.Compiler/Binding/Binder.cs:5486-5544`);
3. an immutable `let` whose initializer is established;
4. `result`, when every `return` expression of the function is established.

Calor0272 and Calor0273 already reject possibly-null initializers and returns, but passing them is not sufficient: an unguarded `string` parameter passes both and is null when a C# caller passes null. The demotion therefore stays for an unguarded parameter, a `var`, a field or property, a generic payload, a `string?` that has not been narrowed, and every module declared `nullable oblivious`. A .NET member annotated as returning non-null does not count as a source unless the pull request argues for it and records the decision in `docs/verification-modeled-forms.md`.

How:

- Decide per term, in the translator. The trigger changes from "a string term was minted" (`ContractTranslator.TouchedStringTheory`) to "a string term that is not established was minted". The binder supplies the facts; the unused `StringInfo(bool IsNullable)` record either carries them or is deleted.
- Recognise the guard structurally, in the body encoder (`FunctionBodyEncoder`) and the fact collector (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Obligations/FactCollector.cs`). Do not translate a null comparison: the translator refuses null literals, and modelling reference null is the decision in #1860. This issue owns structural null-guard recognition for strings whatever #1860 decides and whether or not #1849 (facts after a throwing guard) is built; #1851 reuses it for arrays.
- Lift where a proof removes a check: postconditions (`Z3Verifier.VerifyPostcondition`) and refinement obligations (`ObligationSolver`). The implication prover and the precondition vacuity checks keep today's behaviour.
- Before lifting any proof that uses `Length`, `IndexOf` or `Substring`, settle in writing whether count and index operations agree with .NET on non-ASCII strings (divergences D12 and D13). Either show agreement with a test over a symbolic non-ASCII string and correct the document, or restrict the lift to the predicate operations (`Contains`, `Equals`, `IsNullOrEmpty`, ordinal `StartsWith` and `EndsWith`, `Concat`).

Do not merge before #1843 has committed `bench/proof-yield/before.json`: this issue changes verdicts, and the milestone's before-and-after number is read against that file.

The reproduction, which must stay demoted because a C# caller can pass `null` (written from `docs/syntax-reference/current-language.md` and not compiled; compile it before using it as a fixture):

```calor
module D3Repro
  func Echo (string:s) → string
    !
    => (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(result)) || (result == "")
    return s
```

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- The demotion is applied at `src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Z3/Z3Verifier.cs:586-631` (postconditions), `src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Obligations/ObligationSolver.cs:326-357` (refinement obligations) and `src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Z3/Z3ImplicationProver.cs:240-276`; the vacuity checks at `Z3Verifier.cs:195` and `:351` read the same flag. `Z3Verifier.cs:65-67` says lifting it is tracked by this issue.
- The trigger is coarse on purpose. Declaring a `string` parameter sets it (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Z3/ContractTranslator.cs:1587`, `:1880-1885`), so the reproduction is `Assumed` today and its check is kept. `StringObligation_IsAssumedNotProven` and `StringTypedParameter_DemotesEvenNumericObligation` in `tests/Calor.Verification.Tests/W1Slice1SoundnessTests.cs` pin this. Read from the code and the tests; not run.
- Null enforcement at three receiving boundaries shipped in 0.22.0 (`CHANGELOG.md:1871-1876`). Later assignment, member writes, constructor inputs and generic payloads are documented as unchecked (`CHANGELOG.md:1908-1915`), and `nullable oblivious` modules, which the converter emits for nullable-disabled C#, relax the checks (`Binder.cs:4419`).
- The emitter writes no null check for a `string` parameter: `ThrowIfNull` and `ArgumentNullException` do not occur under `src/Calor.Compiler/CodeGen/`.
- `StringInfo` and `_stringInfo` (`ContractTranslator.cs:125-126`) have one write (`:1883`) and no read. The translator refuses null literals (`:837-841`).
- Not verified: whether comparing a non-nullable `string` parameter with `null` compiles without a diagnostic in 0.30. The narrowing code handles the comparison for any variable (`Binder.cs:5486-5505`); if the comparison is rejected on a non-nullable parameter, source 2 applies to `string?` values narrowed by the guard and to `IsNullOrEmpty` guards only.
- On count and index operations the sources disagree. `Z3Verifier.cs:62-64` says the length gap is closed since #1413. `docs/verification-modeled-forms.md:82` and `:167-169` say D12 is open and needs a separate fix, and `:85` lists D13 as open although `ContractTranslator.cs:1845-1878` adds substring range conditions.

## Why

The demotion takes proof status and elision from every string postcondition, including those where the value cannot be null. Until it is lifted, the string modelling in #1660 reports `Assumed` and the 0.35 proof-yield number cannot move for string code. Earlier narrow fixes in this area each missed a vector (`docs/verification-modeled-forms.md` section 4.1), which is why establishment is defined from the source of the value and why controls are part of the change. This is not a breaking change: no program that compiles today is rejected.

## Done when

- Tests in `tests/Calor.Verification.Tests/` show `proven` for each safe shape, using a predicate operation: literal-only, an immutable `let` of an established value, `result` over established returns, and a parameter read after a kept guard.
- Tests show `assumed` with `string-model` for the reproduction and for each excluded source: unguarded parameter, `var`, field, generic payload, un-narrowed `string?`, `nullable oblivious` module. `StringObligation_IsAssumedNotProven` passes unchanged. `StringTypedParameter_DemotesEvenNumericObligation` passes unchanged, or as #1862 left it if that issue merged first.
- A test compiles the reproduction with and without `--verify`, calls `Echo(null)` from C#, and gets the same postcondition failure both times: the check was not elided.
- The same shapes are in the registered packet of the soundness sweep (`bench/Calor.Soundness.Sweep`, which compares each proof the verifier claims with an independent oracle; packet in `tests/TestData/SoundnessSweep/`) as seeded unsound controls, whose property is false at runtime and must not be reported proven, and safe controls, whose property holds. Rows are added the way the packet's design record prescribes (`docs/plans/0.31-toolchain-and-sweep-record.md`, written by #1769); expected verdicts are set with `scripts/soundness_sweep_gate.py freeze` (`bench/Calor.Soundness.Sweep/README.md`, "Updating the expected verdicts") from a macOS ARM64 run. The pull request lists every existing case whose verdict changed. The scheduled sweep is green with the new rows: none is FALSE-PROOF or FINDING.
- The verifier/runtime differential gate (`tests/Calor.Verification.Tests/VerifierRuntimeDifferential/`) reports zero mismatches. It lists `string-model` as the allowed assumption for string forms (`DifferentialFormRegistry.cs:52`, `:193`, `:206`, `:488`) and hashes `docs/verification-modeled-forms.md` (`DifferentialGate.cs:21`, `:728-739`); both are updated under the amendment rules in `docs/plans/v0.13-freeze-registrations.md`.
- The number of obligations that moved from `assumed` (`string-model`) to `proven` is reported from the #1853 inventory and from the #1843 module set. The #1843 number is the one that matters. The corpus number is expected to be zero, because converted code carries no contracts; the report says so if it is.
- `_stringInfo` is read by the lift or deleted.
- `Z3Verifier.cs:56-68` and `docs/verification-modeled-forms.md` (rows D3, D12 and D13, and section 4.1) say the same thing about count and index operations, and a test pins it.
- `ContractTranslator.SemanticsVersion` is bumped together with `ContractTranslatorSemanticsVersionGuardTests`, so that cached `Assumed` verdicts are not served.
- `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated for the tests added (`scripts/check_trx.py` fails CI when a project's test count differs from its `expectedTotal`).
- Standing acceptance rule. The conversion scorecard's native count and the corpus density ratio do not regress against the values CI reports on the base commit, and the number of corpus files that newly fall to whole-file preservation is reported. All three are expected to be unchanged. Reference values: 101 of 106 scorecard inputs native at 0.30.0 (`CHANGELOG.md:166-168`; the CI job is `conversion-scorecard` in `.github/workflows/test.yml`, and the committed `tests/Calor.Evaluation/Scorecard/baseline.json` still records 96 of 100 at commit 937f79321); density 1.016 overall, measured once by hand on 0.30 output with a proxy tokenizer (#1746).

## Not in scope
