issues.title: [0.35] Lift the reference-model demotion for arrays where non-null is established, or record why not
issues.displaces: none: new capacity justified in body
issues.body:
## Change

Today every successful proof whose solver query contains an array is demoted: it is reported `Assumed` under the named assumption `reference-model` instead of `Proven`, and its runtime check is kept instead of elided (removed from the emitted C#). The solver's arrays are never null; a .NET array reference can be. Lift the demotion when every array in the query is established non-null. Keep it for every other array and for every user-type value.

Use the establishment rule and the structural guard recognition that #875 delivers for strings. Do not write a second one. An array is established non-null when it is:

1. an array creation or initializer expression ("Array Creation/Initialization" in `docs/syntax-reference/current-language.md`);
2. a parameter or local, read at a point dominated by a comparison with `null` that establishes non-null and is kept in the emitted C#, with no assignment in between;
3. an immutable `let` whose initializer is established.

Passing the null checks at the three receiving boundaries (Calor0272 to Calor0274) is not sufficient: an unguarded array parameter passes them and is null when a C# caller passes null. The demotion therefore stays for an unguarded parameter, a `var`, a field or property, a nullable array type that has not been narrowed, and every module declared `nullable oblivious`.

How:

- Decide per term, in the translator. `ContractTranslator.TouchedNullableReferenceSort` is set wherever an array constant or an array's length companion is minted. Change that trigger from "an array term was minted" to "an array term that is not established was minted", as #875 does for strings. User-type sorts keep setting the flag unconditionally.
- Lift at the two sites where a proof removes a check: postconditions (`Z3Verifier.VerifyPostcondition`) and obligations (`ObligationSolver`). The implication prover and the precondition vacuity checks keep today's behaviour.
- Do not model null in the translator. That is the decision in #1860.

Three points are settled inside this issue and written into section 4.1 of `docs/verification-modeled-forms.md`:

- **Dereference as evidence.** On converted code arrays are expected to be mostly unguarded parameters (not measured; the #1853 inventory shows whether they are), and the rule above leaves their index-bounds obligations `Assumed`. Two dereferences could establish non-null without a guard: an earlier read of `xs.Length` on every path to the access (the header of `for i from 0 to xs.Length - 1`) with no assignment to `xs` in between; and, for an index-bounds obligation, the access `xs[i]` that the obligation is about. Decide whether either counts as a source for arrays. Before deciding, trace which runtime guard a discharged index-bounds obligation removes for a plain array (the call sites of `CSharpEmitter.ShouldEmitObligationGuard`, `src/Calor.Compiler/CodeGen/CSharpEmitter.cs:682`; not traced for this issue): if the access itself still throws on a null array, accepting it as evidence removes nothing a caller can observe. The default is no. A yes needs the extra unsound controls listed under Done when, and it is a change to the shared rule: the same pull request then either applies the dereference source to strings as well (with the three extra unsound controls in their string form, and the #875 tests updated), or records in section 4.1 why it holds for arrays and not for strings.
- **`List<T>`.** A `List<T>` is a user-type sort with a `Count` accessor, not an array, and its `Count` changes when the list is mutated. This issue does not lift its demotion. Say so, so that #1660 expects `assumed` for collection operations on lists.
- **Or why not.** If a control exists that the rule cannot exclude and that the sweep reports as a false proof, do not ship a partial lift. Record the control and the reason, close this issue on that record, and post on #1660 and #1661 that array results stay `assumed` with `reference-model` in 0.35.

Do not merge before #1843 has committed `bench/proof-yield/before.json`: this issue changes verdicts, and the milestone's before-and-after number is read against that file.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- The demotion reads `TouchedNullableReferenceSort` after a successful proof, at `src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Z3/Z3Verifier.cs:592-596` and `:620-624` (postconditions) and at `src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Obligations/ObligationSolver.cs:326-357` (obligations).
- The flag is set where an array constant is created (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Z3/ContractTranslator.cs:1642`, `:2578`), where an array's `$length` companion is minted (`MarkArrayLength`, `:1779-1783`, including the on-demand mint at `:2545-2555`), and where an uninterpreted sort for a user type is created (`MarkUninterpretedSort`, `:1753-1757`).
- An index-bounds obligation on an array is `index >= 0 && index < Length(array)` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Obligations/ObligationGenerator.cs:855-880`). Proving it always mints the length companion, so a discharged one is reported `Assumed`.
- The translator declares arrays of the eight integer element types only (`ContractTranslator.cs:1633-1637`). A postcondition that names `result` on a function returning an array is `Unsupported` (`Z3Verifier.cs:414-420`). A `List<T>` variable is a constant of an uninterpreted sort with a `Count` accessor (`ContractTranslator.cs:1558-1569`).
- Null enforcement at three receiving boundaries covers supported arrays (`CHANGELOG.md:1871-1876`; `src/Calor.Compiler/Binding/NullabilityChecker.cs:36-83`). Later assignment, member writes and constructor inputs are unchecked, and array annotations do not prove element slots initialised (`CHANGELOG.md:1908-1915`). The second limit does not affect arrays of integers.
- The binder narrows any variable compared with `null` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Binding/Binder.cs:5486-5505`).
- `ArrayCarriedObligation_IsAssumedNotProven`, `ArrayParameter_DemotesEvenAPurelyNumericPostcondition` and `OnDemandArrayLength_SetsTheReferenceModelFlag` in `tests/Calor.Verification.Tests/W1Slice1SoundnessTests.cs` (`:668`, `:730`, `:769`) pin the demotion.
- The false proof the demotion closed is recorded as divergence D14 (`docs/verification-modeled-forms.md:83`): a postcondition `a.Length >= 0` over a never-assigned array field was `Proven`, and the program crashed with a `NullReferenceException` without verification and exited 0 with it. A field is not an established source under the rule above.
- The verifier/runtime differential gate lists `reference-model` as the allowed assumption for array forms (`tests/Calor.Verification.Tests/VerifierRuntimeDifferential/DifferentialFormRegistry.cs:72`, `:489-490`) and hashes `docs/verification-modeled-forms.md` (`DifferentialGate.cs:21`, `:728-739`).

## Why

Index-bounds obligations are the only obligations converted code has without authored contracts, and each is reported `Assumed` whatever #1661 proves about the loop around it. The collection half of #1660 ends in the same place. #875 does not help, because it lifts the string demotion only. Without this issue the 0.35 proof-yield number cannot move for array code, and #1661 cannot meet a done-when that says `proven`. Earlier narrow fixes in this area each missed a vector (`docs/verification-modeled-forms.md` section 4.1), which is why the rule starts from the source of the value, why controls are part of the change, and why "record why not" is an accepted outcome. This is not a breaking change: no program that compiles today is rejected.

This is new capacity and displaces no issue: #1660 and #1661 are already in 0.35, and their done-when cannot say `proven` for arrays without it.

## Done when

Either the lift ships:

- Tests in `tests/Calor.Verification.Tests/` show `proven` for each accepted source, in each channel that can express it: an index-bounds obligation on an immutable `let` bound to an array creation, and a postcondition and an index-bounds obligation on a parameter read after a kept null guard.
- Tests show `assumed` with `reference-model` for each excluded source: unguarded parameter, `var`, field (the D14 reproduction), un-narrowed nullable array, `nullable oblivious` module, and a `List<T>` or class-typed value. `ArrayCarriedObligation_IsAssumedNotProven` and `OnDemandArrayLength_SetsTheReferenceModelFlag` pass unchanged. `ArrayParameter_DemotesEvenAPurelyNumericPostcondition` passes unchanged, or as #1862 left it if that issue merged first.
- A test compiles one function per accepted source with and without verification and calls it from C# with a `null` array: the exception is the same both times.
- If a dereference was accepted as evidence, three more unsound controls stay `assumed`: the array variable assigned between the dereference and the access; a dereference on a path that does not dominate the access; a dereference inside a `try` whose handler continues to the access.
- The same shapes are in the registered packet of the soundness sweep (`bench/Calor.Soundness.Sweep`, which compares each proof the verifier claims with an independent oracle; packet in `tests/TestData/SoundnessSweep/`) as seeded unsound controls, whose property is false at runtime and must not be reported proven, and safe controls, whose property holds. Rows are added the way the packet's design record prescribes (`docs/plans/0.31-toolchain-and-sweep-record.md`, written by #1769); expected verdicts are set with `scripts/soundness_sweep_gate.py freeze` (`bench/Calor.Soundness.Sweep/README.md`, "Updating the expected verdicts") from a macOS ARM64 run. The pull request lists every existing case whose verdict changed. The scheduled sweep is green with the new rows: none is FALSE-PROOF or FINDING.
- The differential gate reports zero mismatches. Its registry and the document hash are updated under the amendment rules in `docs/plans/v0.13-freeze-registrations.md`.
- Section 4.1 of `docs/verification-modeled-forms.md` states one establishment rule for strings and arrays and lists every difference between them with its reason, the decision on dereferences with its reason, and that `List<T>` and other user types stay demoted.
- The number of obligations that moved from `assumed` (`reference-model`) to `proven` is reported from the #1853 inventory, by kind, and from the #1843 module set.
- `ContractTranslator.SemanticsVersion` is bumped together with `ContractTranslatorSemanticsVersionGuardTests`, so that cached `Assumed` verdicts are not served.
- `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated for the tests added (`scripts/check_trx.py` fails CI when a project's test count differs from its `expectedTotal`).

Or the lift does not ship:

- Section 4.1 of `docs/verification-modeled-forms.md` names the control that could not be excluded and says why, with the document hash re-pinned under the amendment rules. That control is in the registered sweep packet as an unsound control and the scheduled sweep is green with it. Comments on #1660, #1661 and #1662 link the record.

## Not in scope

- User-type sorts, including `List<T>` and class instances.
- An array parameter that the proof never reads: #1862.
- Modelling null in the translator (#1860).
- Postconditions that name an array-typed `result`, which are `Unsupported` today.
- The implication prover, where a lift can turn the `Calor0819` warning into the `Calor0810` error (`CHANGELOG.md:193`).
- Rejecting more programs for null (#1800, #1869).

Part of #1662. Depends on #1853, #1843 and #875. Blocks #1660 and #1661.

issues.title: [0.35] Scope proof demotion and unsupported-type refusal to the variables a query reads
issues.displaces: none: new capacity justified in body
issues.body:
## Change

Today the verifier declares every parameter of a callable in the solver before it translates anything. Declaring a `string` marks the query as touching the string theory. Declaring an array, a `List<T>` or any type the translator does not know marks it as touching a reference sort. A `float` or `double` parameter cannot be declared and refuses the whole obligation. So a proof that reads only integers is reported `Assumed` (proved under a named assumption, runtime check kept) or `Unsupported` because of a parameter it never reads. Declare only the variables the query reads.

1. **Where.** `Z3Verifier.VerifyPrecondition` and `Z3Verifier.VerifyPostcondition` (the contract channel) and `ObligationSolver` (the obligation channel). `Z3ImplicationProver` already declares only the parameters its contracts read and is the model.
2. **What "reads" means.** The query is everything asserted into the solver for one obligation: its condition, every precondition and collected fact asserted with it, and, for a postcondition that names `result`, the function body as encoded. A variable is read if any of those refers to it. `result` is declared only when read.
3. **How.** Keep the trigger where it is: the two flags stay set at the point a sort is minted. Change what gets minted. Prefer deferring the mint to first use inside the translator (register each name with its type up front, create the solver constant when a reference, array access or length is first translated) over walking the syntax tree in advance. The first version of the string trigger walked the contract, missed the body and let a false proof through (`docs/verification-modeled-forms.md:126-140`).
4. **True types only.** A name that is read is declared with its declared type, or the obligation is refused. It must never reach the translator's on-demand defaults, which create an `i32` array and a free length for a name they do not know (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Z3/ContractTranslator.cs:1496-1511`, `:2545-2555`). Those defaults are safe today only because every parameter is declared first.
5. **Refusal.** A parameter of a type that cannot be declared refuses the obligation only when the query reads it. The refusal text does not change.
6. **The tests and text that pin today's behaviour.** `StringTypedParameter_DemotesEvenNumericObligation` and `ArrayParameter_DemotesEvenAPurelyNumericPostcondition` assert the coarse behaviour as a decision. Replace each with a pair: the same signature with an obligation that does not read the parameter (now `proven`), and one where the parameter is read only through the body (still `assumed`). Rewrite the two paragraphs of `docs/verification-modeled-forms.md` that document the coarseness (`:142-145`, `:157-165`).

This issue and the two lifts are independent and can merge in either order. This one narrows which terms enter the query; #875 and #1851 decide which of the terms that do enter are trusted to be non-null.

No program is rejected in a default build. Under verification two results can change in the stricter direction: a postcondition that was `Unsupported` can now be reported as refuted, which is a warning; and with refinement verification on, an obligation that was `Unsupported` can now fail, which the default obligation policy reports as an error (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Obligations/ObligationPolicy.cs:33`). No CLI command or build property turns refinement verification on (#1868), so no build breaks. The pull request lists every such change it finds in the sweep packet and in the #1843 module set.

Do not merge before #1843 has committed `bench/proof-yield/before.json`.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- Contract channel: `ContractVerificationPass.VerifyFunction` passes every parameter of the function (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/ContractVerificationPass.cs:124-126`), and `Z3Verifier` declares all of them, and `result`, before it translates anything (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Z3/Z3Verifier.cs:143-151`, `:265-286`). A declaration that fails returns `Unsupported` for the obligation.
- Obligation channel: `ObligationSolver` declares every parameter (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Obligations/ObligationSolver.cs:97-114`). A declaration that fails is skipped for index-bounds obligations (`:103-107`) and returns `Unsupported` for every other kind.
- What declaring does (`ContractTranslator.cs`): a `string` sets `TouchedStringTheory` (`:1587`, `:1880-1885`); an array sets `TouchedNullableReferenceSort` (`:1642`); a `List<T>` or any other type name becomes a constant of an uninterpreted sort and sets the same flag (`:1558-1569`, `:1590`, `:1753-1757`); `f32`, `f64`, `float` and `double` cannot be declared (`:1589`), nor can an array whose element type is not one of the eight integer types (`:1633-1637`).
- After a successful proof the two flags demote the result to `Assumed` (`Z3Verifier.cs:586-596`, `ObligationSolver.cs:326-327`).
- `Z3ImplicationProver` declares only the parameters the contracts refer to (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Z3/Z3ImplicationProver.cs:127-142`; `ReferencedRoots`, `:334`).
- The coarseness is documented (`docs/verification-modeled-forms.md:142-145`, `:157-165`: "Only a signature made entirely of modeled primitives still elides") and pinned by the two tests named in step 6 (`tests/Calor.Verification.Tests/W1Slice1SoundnessTests.cs:613`, `:730`).
- The same document records why the trigger asks the translator and not the syntax tree (`:116-140`; `Z3Verifier.cs:580-585`).
- The comment on the on-demand array default says it cannot be reached from contracts because parameters are declared with their true types first (`ContractTranslator.cs:1498-1505`).

## Why

Converted C# is mostly class members whose signatures carry strings, arrays and class types. On such code a signature-wide demotion puts a successful proof in `assumed` whatever the proof reads, so neither the modelling in #1660, the loop work in #1661 nor the call-site obligations of epic #1861 can raise the `proven` count on it. That expectation is read from the code and has not been measured; the #1853 inventory and the #1843 baseline give the numbers this issue reports against. The coarse rule was chosen because a narrower trigger had let a false proof through. This issue keeps the trigger and narrows what is declared, and its controls target the failure that was recorded: a term that reaches the solver through the body and not through the contract.

This is new capacity and displaces no issue: without it the first 0.35 exit number is bounded by signatures and not by what the verifier can prove.

## Done when

- Tests in `tests/Calor.Verification.Tests/` show, in both channels, that an integer-only obligation is `proven` on a callable that also takes an unread `string`, an unread array, an unread class-typed parameter and an unread `double`.
- Tests show that a parameter the query reads still demotes or refuses, whatever path it is read through. `assumed` with `string-model`: a `string` parameter read only by the returned expression, and one read only through an immutable `let`. `assumed` with `reference-model`: an array parameter read only in the body. `assumed`: a `string` read only by a parameter refinement on another parameter, with an integer postcondition. `unsupported`: a `double` parameter read by a branch condition in the body.
- One of the string cases is the recorded false proof with the string moved out of the contract: a `bool` function with the postcondition `=> result` whose body returns `(!string.IsNullOrEmpty(s)) || (s == "")`. The property is false at runtime for a `null` argument, so the case is a seeded unsound control and must not be `proven`.
- A test declares a `byte` or `long` array parameter that only the body reads and states a property that holds for `i32` elements and fails for the real element type. The result is `refuted` or `unsupported`; `proven` or `assumed` would mean the default element type was used.
- The two tests named in step 6 are replaced by the pairs described there.
- The same safe and unsound shapes are in the registered packet of the soundness sweep (`bench/Calor.Soundness.Sweep`, which compares each proof the verifier claims with an independent oracle; packet in `tests/TestData/SoundnessSweep/`). A seeded unsound control is a case whose property is false at runtime and must not be reported proven; a safe control is one whose property holds. Rows are added the way the packet's design record prescribes (`docs/plans/0.31-toolchain-and-sweep-record.md`, written by #1769); expected verdicts are set with `scripts/soundness_sweep_gate.py freeze` (`bench/Calor.Soundness.Sweep/README.md`, "Updating the expected verdicts") from a macOS ARM64 run. The pull request lists every existing case whose verdict changed, with its old and new status. The scheduled sweep is green with the new rows: none is FALSE-PROOF or FINDING.
- The verifier/runtime differential gate (`tests/Calor.Verification.Tests/VerifierRuntimeDifferential/`) reports zero mismatches. Its registry derives an expected assumption from a parameter's type (`DifferentialFormRegistry.cs:52`, `:72`) and its gate hashes `docs/verification-modeled-forms.md` (`DifferentialGate.cs:21`, `:728-739`); both are updated under the amendment rules in `docs/plans/v0.13-freeze-registrations.md`.
- The number of obligations that left `assumed` and the number that left `unsupported`, each by new status, are reported from the #1853 inventory and from the #1843 module set.
- `ContractTranslator.SemanticsVersion` is bumped together with `ContractTranslatorSemanticsVersionGuardTests`, so that cached verdicts are not served.
- `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated for the tests added and removed (`scripts/check_trx.py` fails CI when a project's test count differs from its `expectedTotal`).
- Standing acceptance rule. The conversion scorecard's native count (CI job `conversion-scorecard` in `.github/workflows/test.yml`) and the corpus density ratio (#1746) do not regress against the values CI reports on the base commit, and the number of corpus files that newly fall to whole-file preservation is reported. All three are expected to be unchanged, because converted code carries no contracts and no command runs obligation verification.

## Not in scope

- Which strings and arrays are trusted to be non-null (#875, #1851).
- Dropping a precondition or fact that shares no variable with the goal. File it separately if the #1843 numbers show the need.
- The implication prover, which is already scoped this way, and `GuardDiscovery`, which validates suggested guards for the MCP tool and removes no check (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Obligations/GuardDiscovery.cs:266-272`).
- Modelling floating point.

Part of #1662. Depends on #1853 and #1843.

issues.title: [0.35] Decision: an opt-in CLI and build surface for obligation verification
issues.body:
## Change

Record one maintainer decision in `docs/plans/0.35-obligation-surface-decision.md`: whether obligation verification gets a user-facing switch. *Obligation verification* (the code calls it refinement verification) is the compiler mode `CompilationOptions.VerifyRefinements`. It generates and solves call-site refinement obligations, return refinements, `proof` obligations and index-bounds obligations, and it removes the runtime guard of an obligation it discharges. This issue is closed by the record. It changes no compiler code, and nothing below is decided yet.

| Option | What it adds | What it costs |
|---|---|---|
| A. An opt-in option on `calor verify` | An option (spelling chosen with the decision) that also runs obligation verification and reports every obligation by status in the text and `--format json` output. The counter #1853 builds can be its implementation. `calor verify` reports; it is not the command a project builds with. | One CLI option and one JSON shape to keep stable; a section of `docs/cli/verify.md`; an exit-code rule for a failed obligation (`calor verify` already exits non-zero on a refuted contract, `docs/cli/verify.md:71-79`). No emitted C# changes. |
| B. A, plus an opt-in build property | An MSBuild property beside `CalorVerify`, and the matching compile option, so that a project can build with obligation verification: discharged obligations lose their guards and failed ones stop the build. | Everything in A. Emitted C# changes under the property. Build time grows by the solver time per project (not measured). A choice between the default obligation policy, where a failed obligation is an error, and the permissive one, where it is a warning with a guard. A statement of whether the edition promise (#1805) covers builds that opt in, because every obligation kind added later (#1864 adds call-site obligations for class members) can fail a program that built before, and so can a change such as #1862, which can turn an `Unsupported` obligation into a failed one. |
| C. No CLI or build surface | The record states that the MCP tool `calor_refine` and the soundness sweep are the intended consumers, and `docs/cli/verify.md` says that `calor verify` does not run obligations. | Nothing to build. The results of #1661, #1864 and #1863 stay invisible to `calor verify`, `calor check` and builds; the #1853 inventory and the #1843 proof yield stay the only places a maintainer sees them. |

Whether obligation verification may run in a default build was decided by #1800 (candidate 4: (a) opt-in only for the whole edition, or one of two routes to default-on). Quote the option it recorded. Under (a) no option here turns it on by default. Under (b) or (c), option B states how its property relates to that route. This issue does not reopen that decision.

**Recommendation.** A. Most of the verifier work in 0.35 (#1661, #1851, #1864, #1863) produces results that only an MCP tool call can show today. The counter exists once #1853 lands, so A costs an option, a JSON shape and a documentation page, and it changes no emitted code, so it adds no soundness or compatibility exposure. B is better decided after 0.35: it puts guard elision by the obligation engine into shipped builds, and the evidence for that is the sweep staying green with the 0.35 controls and the #1843 after value, neither of which exists when this decision is due. The maintainer may choose otherwise; the record gives the reason.

**Read first.** The #1853 record (`docs/plans/0.35-proof-status-inventory.md`): how many obligations converted code has, by kind and status. If it shows that converted code has no obligations outside `runtime-only`, C with a note to revisit after #1864 is a defensible reading; say so in the record if that is the choice.

**What the record contains.** The option chosen and the reason; the #1800 candidate 4 option in force, which option B and the edition question must respect; the inventory numbers read, with the run they came from; the date and the maintainer's sign-off. For A or B: the option and property spellings, the exit-code rule, the obligation policy for each surface, whether the edition promise covers it, and the number of the implementation issue filed. That issue requires that default builds and default `calor verify` output are byte-identical with the option off. For C: the sentence added to `docs/cli/verify.md`, in the same commit.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- `CompilationOptions.VerifyRefinements` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Program.cs:1546`) gates obligation generation and solving (`:1074-1090`).
- It is set by the MCP tool `calor_refine` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Mcp/Tools/RefineTool.cs:104`, `:190`, `:255`, `:364`, `:434`), by the soundness-sweep harness (`bench/Calor.Soundness.Sweep/BaselineHost.cs:59`) and by tests. Nothing under `src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/` sets it; `calor verify` sets `VerifyContracts` only (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/VerifyCommand.cs:280-289`).
- The build task maps the `CalorVerify` property to `VerifyContracts` (`src/Calor.Sdk/Sdk/Sdk.targets:103`, `src/Calor.Tasks/CompileCalor.cs:820`). There is no property for obligations.
- `CHANGELOG.md:3726` (0.12.0 notes) says "`VerifyRefinements` has no CLI flag", as the reason one false proof was reachable only through the MCP tool. A comment at `src/Calor.Compiler/CodeGen/CSharpEmitter.cs:10449` mentions `--verify-refinements`; no such option exists.
- Under the default obligation policy a failed obligation is a compilation error, and a timed-out, unsupported or unsolved one is a warning with a runtime guard (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Obligations/ObligationPolicy.cs:30-45`). A permissive policy that makes nothing an error exists (`:67`).
- A discharged obligation's guard is left out of the emitted C# unless guards are kept (`CSharpEmitter.cs:682-734`, `ShouldEmitObligationGuard`).
- `docs/cli/verify.md` describes contract verification only. `docs/cli/mcp.md:52` lists `calor_refine`.

## Why

0.35 improves what the obligation engine can prove: loop invariants feed index-bounds obligations (#1661), array proofs can leave `Assumed` (#1851), and class members get call-site obligations (#1864, #1863). None of it is visible from the command line or a build, because no command turns the engine on. Whether that is a gap or the intended design has never been written down, and each later issue would otherwise settle it by accident. The plan files maintainer decisions as decisions, with the options and their costs, and does not build a surface before one is chosen.

Displaces nothing: this is a decision record, and any implementation is filed by it.

## Done when

- `docs/plans/0.35-obligation-surface-decision.md` is committed with the content listed under "What the record contains", authored or approved by the maintainer.
- For A or B, the implementation issue exists, is linked from the record and from #1662, and carries the byte-identical requirement. For C, the sentence in `docs/cli/verify.md` is in the same commit as the record.
- The record cites the #1853 inventory run it read and quotes the #1800 candidate 4 option.

## Not in scope

- Implementing the option or the property.
- Turning obligation verification on by default (#1800 decides whether that is ever allowed).
- The MCP tool's own interface.

Part of #1662. Depends on #1853 and #1800.

issues.title: [0.35] Model more BCL in Z3: string ops, collections, Math
issues.body:
**Current.** The issue extends Z3 modelling of BCL calls with three groups: the 12 string operations listed as unsupported in `ContractTranslator` (ordinal semantics only), `Count`, `Contains` and indexing on lists and arrays, and `Math.Abs`, `Min`, `Max` and `Clamp`. It is done when each modelled operation has a Proven/Failed test pair and sweep cases, with no false proofs.

**Amendment.** The title does not change.

1. In `## Change`, replace the first paragraph (from "Extend Z3 modeling" to "Add:") with:

> Extend Z3 modelling of BCL calls. Recognition by receiver type landed in 0.30: an operation is added by giving it an arm in `NormalizeBclCall` or `NormalizeBclProperty` and a translation (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Z3/ContractTranslator.cs:318-461`). Work through the operations in the order the #1853 record (`docs/plans/0.35-proof-status-inventory.md`) and the #1843 baseline (`bench/proof-yield/before.json`) rank them by `unsupported` count. An operation that neither measurement encountered may be dropped, with that recorded on this issue. The three groups may land as separate pull requests; the issue closes with the last. Add:

2. In the same section, replace the first list item with:

> - the 12 string operations that `DiagnoseStringOperation` names as unsupported (`ContractTranslator.cs:2652-2656`): `ToUpper`, `ToLower`, `Trim`, `TrimStart`, `TrimEnd`, `PadLeft`, `PadRight`, `Split`, `Join`, `Format`, `IsNullOrWhiteSpace` and `Regex.IsMatch`. Each is either modelled or left refused with the reason recorded in section 3 of `docs/verification-modeled-forms.md`. Ordinal semantics only: an overload whose .NET behaviour depends on the current culture is refused, as `StartsWith` without a comparison mode is today. `Replace` is not one of the 12: it is a deliberate refusal (first occurrence in the solver, all occurrences in .NET, `:2162`) and stays refused unless it is modelled with all-occurrences semantics;

3. Add this section after `## Change`:

> ## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)
>
> - Recognised today, in `NormalizeBclCall` (`ContractTranslator.cs:419-432`) and `NormalizeBclProperty` (`:318-343`): ten string operations, `Length` on arrays, and `Count` on `System.Collections.Generic.List<T>`. Element access is modelled for array variables only (`TranslateArrayAccess`, `:1484`). A `List<T>` variable is an uninterpreted-sort constant with a `Count` accessor (`:1558-1569`), so list indexing and `Contains` on a collection are not modelled. The translator has no reference to `Math`.
> - A successful proof that mints a string term is reported `Assumed` with the assumption `string-model`. One that mints an array or user-type sort, which includes every `List<T>`, is `Assumed` with `reference-model`. The runtime check is kept (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Z3/Z3Verifier.cs:586-631`, `src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Obligations/ObligationSolver.cs:326-357`). #875 lifts the first where the string is established non-null. #1851 lifts the second for arrays established non-null, or records why it cannot; it does not lift it for `List<T>` or other user types.
> - `docs/verification-modeled-forms.md` is hashed by the verifier/runtime differential gate (`tests/Calor.Verification.Tests/VerifierRuntimeDifferential/DifferentialGate.cs:21`, `:728-739`). Editing it means re-pinning the hash under the amendment rules in `docs/plans/v0.13-freeze-registrations.md`.

4. Replace the final paragraph (from `**Done when:**` to `Part of #1662.`) with:

> ## Done when
>
> - Every operation added has a test pair in `tests/Calor.Verification.Tests/`: a contract that holds, and a contract the solver refutes with a counterexample that the generated C# reproduces at runtime.
> - String operations: where every string in the proof is established non-null under #875, the holding contract is reported `proven`. Elsewhere it is `assumed` with `string-model` as its only assumption.
> - Collection operations on an array: where #1851 lifted the demotion and the array is established non-null under its rule, the holding contract is reported `proven`. Elsewhere, and for every operation on a `List<T>`, it is `assumed` with `reference-model` as its only assumption. If #1851 closed on a "why not" record, `assumed` is the expected status for every collection operation.
> - `Math` functions on the integer types the translator models: the holding contract is `proven`. `Math.Abs` of the minimum value and `Math.Clamp` with `min > max` both throw in .NET; each has an unsound control.
> - Seeded unsound controls and safe controls for every operation added are in the registered packet of the soundness sweep (`bench/Calor.Soundness.Sweep`, which compares each proof the verifier claims with an independent oracle; packet in `tests/TestData/SoundnessSweep/`). An unsound control is a case whose property is false at runtime and must not be reported proven; a safe control is one whose property holds. Rows are added the way the packet's design record prescribes (`docs/plans/0.31-toolchain-and-sweep-record.md`, written by #1769), and expected verdicts are set with `scripts/soundness_sweep_gate.py freeze` (`bench/Calor.Soundness.Sweep/README.md`, "Updating the expected verdicts"). The scheduled sweep is green with them: no row is FALSE-PROOF or FINDING. Each pull request lists every existing case whose verdict changed, with its old and new verdict, and every row whose classification changed. At HEAD bc80daeb three rows hold cases over operations this issue models, all expected `Unsupported` or `Assumed`: STR-UNMODELED-OPS (5 cases over `Replace`, `ToUpper`, `Trim` and `ToLower`), CALL-IN-CONTRACT (5 cases, `Math.Abs` in a postcondition) and OBL-UNGATED-FORMS (8 cases, one form of which is `Math.Abs` in a `proof`). A changed verdict is a re-registration under `docs/release-policy.md` (#1783) and restarts the proof-claim count; say so in the pull request, with the date of the first counted run.
> - Sections 2 and 3 of `docs/verification-modeled-forms.md` and its generated appendix list every operation as modelled or refused. `ModeledFormsTests.Doc_GeneratedAppendix_MatchesCodeWhitelist` passes and the differential gate's document hash is re-pinned.
> - `ContractTranslator.SemanticsVersion` is bumped together with `ContractTranslatorSemanticsVersionGuardTests`.
> - `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated for the tests added (`scripts/check_trx.py` fails CI when a project's test count differs from its `expectedTotal`).
> - Each pull request reports the change in the #1853 inventory and in the #1843 proof yield: how many obligations left `unsupported`, and which status they moved to.
>
> Part of #1662. Depends on #875, #1853, #1843 and #1851.

**Why.** Until the #875 lift lands, string results report `Assumed`, not the `Proven` the current done-when asks for, and array results do the same until #1851; results on `List<T>` stay `Assumed` throughout 0.35. The second 0.35 exit criterion requires sweep controls for every verifier step, and the third dates the release from the last freeze that changed an existing verdict, which modelling `ToUpper`, `ToLower`, `Trim` and `Math.Abs` does. The baseline corrects two stale statements: recognition has landed, and `Replace` is a refusal, not one of the 12.

issues.title: [0.35] Promote k-induction and loop-invariant synthesis into the verification pipeline
issues.body:
**Current.** The issue promotes `KInductionProver` and `LoopInvariantSynthesizer` from test-only code into the verification pipeline: cover counted and `while` loops (named by their retired markers), feed synthesized invariants to obligations through `FactCollector`, and add a time budget per loop. It is done when loop-dependent obligations that are Unknown today become Proven with no false proofs, measured by the sweep.

**Amendment.** The title does not change.

1. Replace the body from the `## Change` heading up to, but not including, the paragraph that starts `**Done when:**` with:

> ## Change
>
> `KInductionProver` and `LoopInvariantSynthesizer` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Z3/KInduction/`) produce invariants that nothing consumes. Promote them into the obligation engine (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Obligations/`), which runs under `CompilationOptions.VerifyRefinements`.
>
> Promotion means three things. Synthesis runs inside the obligation engine whenever `VerifyRefinements` is set, with no second switch. A synthesized invariant is an expression the solver receives as a fact, not a string in a diagnostic. And the result changes the status of an obligation. It does not mean on in default builds: no CLI command or build property sets `VerifyRefinements`, and #1868 decides whether one will. The existing switch `VerificationAnalysisOptions.EnableKInduction`, which only produces the diagnostics Calor0950 and Calor0951, is kept as it is or removed; say which in the pull request.
>
> 1. **Loops covered.** The snapshot form `for i from a to b step s`, the reevaluated form `for i = a; condition; i = next`, and `while condition`. `each` and do-while loops are out of scope and report no invariant.
> 2. **Use the results.** A synthesized invariant becomes a fact that `FactCollector` scopes to the loop body and, with the negated loop condition, to the code after the loop. Consumers, in this order: index-bounds obligations, refinement obligations, then postconditions on functions whose body contains a loop. The third needs the body encoder to accept a loop summarised by its invariant and may land as a second pull request.
> 3. **Budget.** A time limit per loop and per function. When k-induction does not converge, the obligation keeps the status it has today and its reason says the loop budget was exhausted.
> 4. **Order.** Start with the loop shapes behind the most index-bounds obligations that are not discharged in the #1853 inventory (`docs/plans/0.35-proof-status-inventory.md`).

2. Add this section after `## Change`:

> ## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)
>
> - `LoopAnalysisRunner` (`LoopInvariantSynthesizer.cs:317`) is called from `VerificationAnalysisPass` only when `VerificationAnalysisOptions.EnableKInduction` is true (`src/Calor.Compiler/Analysis/VerificationAnalysisPass.cs:512-524`). The default is false (`:43`). The `Thorough` preset that sets it (`:83`) is selected by no command, and the MCP analyze tool sets it false (`src/Calor.Compiler/Mcp/Tools/AnalyzeTool.cs:144`, `:251`). In practice it runs from `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/Analysis/KInductionTests.cs` only.
> - Its output is two diagnostics, Calor0950 and Calor0951. The invariant is a string (`LoopInvariantResult.Invariant`, `LoopInvariantSynthesizer.cs:13`) and is not given to `FactCollector` or to any obligation.
> - `SynthesizeForLoop` handles the snapshot form and returns Unsupported for the reevaluated form (`LoopInvariantSynthesizer.cs:53-57`). `SynthesizeWhileLoop` exists (`:96`). `KInductionProver.SynthesizeAndProve` accepts `BoundForStatement` only (`KInductionProver.cs:204`). The defaults are k up to 10 and 10 seconds (`KInductionProver.cs:57`, `:62`).
> - Index-bounds obligations are generated for every array access and indexed write in function, method, constructor and operator bodies, with no authored contract (`ObligationGenerator.cs:798-817`, `:820-881`); accessor bodies and members of nested classes are not visited (`:57-86`). They are generated only under `VerifyRefinements` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Program.cs:1074`), which no CLI command sets; the MCP tool `calor_refine` and the sweep harness do.
> - `FactCollector` already supplies counted-loop bounds and the `while` condition inside the loop body (`FactCollector.cs:250-277`, `:656`).
> - A discharged index-bounds obligation reads the array's length companion, so it is reported `Assumed` with `reference-model`, not `Proven` (`ObligationSolver.cs:326-357`, `src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Z3/ContractTranslator.cs:1779-1783`). #1851 lifts that for arrays established non-null, or records why it cannot.
> - A postcondition that names `result` on a function whose body contains a loop is `Unsupported`: the body encoder accepts returns, immutable bindings and if/else-if/else only (`FunctionBodyEncoder.TryEncodeResult`, `src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Z3/Z3Verifier.cs:814`; refusal at `:424-433`).

3. Replace the final paragraph (from `**Done when:**` to `Part of #1662.`) with:

> ## Done when
>
> - Compiler tests show, for each covered loop form, an obligation that is `unknown`, `timeout` or `unsupported` at the parent commit and is decided with the invariant. For an obligation over integers only the decided status is `proven`. For an array index obligation it is `proven` where #1851 lifted the demotion and the array is established non-null under its rule; otherwise, and always if #1851 closed on a "why not" record, it is `assumed` with `reference-model` as its only assumption.
> - The invariants are consulted only where the solver already runs (`VerifyContracts`, `VerifyRefinements`). With the loop budget set to zero, the same tests give the statuses recorded for the parent commit.
> - Seeded unsound controls and safe controls are in the registered packet of the soundness sweep (`bench/Calor.Soundness.Sweep`, which compares each proof the verifier claims with an independent oracle; packet in `tests/TestData/SoundnessSweep/`). An unsound control is a case whose property is false at runtime and must not be reported proven; a safe control is one whose property holds. Rows are added the way the packet's design record prescribes (`docs/plans/0.31-toolchain-and-sweep-record.md`, written by #1769), and expected verdicts are set with `scripts/soundness_sweep_gate.py freeze` (`bench/Calor.Soundness.Sweep/README.md`, "Updating the expected verdicts"). The unsound controls include at least: an off-by-one upper bound, an index changed inside the body, the array rebound inside the loop, a reevaluated `for` whose bound changes in the body, and an induction variable that overflows. The scheduled sweep is green with them: no row is FALSE-PROOF or FINDING. The pull request lists every existing case whose verdict changed, with its old and new verdict. At HEAD bc80daeb two rows hold loop cases, all expected `Unsupported`: BODY-LOOP-CALL-MUTABLE (8 cases, a postcondition on `result` over a counted loop) and OBL-LOOP-VARIABLE (2 cases, a `proof` obligation inside a counted loop). If the list is not empty the freeze is a re-registration under `docs/release-policy.md` (#1783) and restarts the proof-claim count; say so in the pull request, with the date of the first counted run.
> - The loop budget is documented, and a test shows the stated reason when it is exhausted.
> - `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated for the tests added (`scripts/check_trx.py` fails CI when a project's test count differs from its `expectedTotal`).
> - Each pull request reports the change in the #1853 inventory (index-bounds obligations by status) and in the #1843 proof yield.
>
> Part of #1662. Depends on #1853, #1843 and #1851.

**Why.** Index-bounds obligations are generated for array accesses with no authored contract, so this issue has work on converted code today; the baseline adds where that work is reachable and what status it can end in, which for arrays depends on #1851. The second 0.35 exit criterion requires sweep controls for every verifier step, and the third dates the release from the last freeze that changed an existing verdict, so the pull request must show whether the registered loop rows moved. The current body uses retired loop markers and says the prover is reached only from tests, which is true in effect but hides the switch that already exists, so the amendment says what promotion means.

issues.title: [0.35] Call-site refinement obligations for class methods and constructors (operator bodies as callers)
issues.displaces: none: new capacity justified in body
issues.body:
## Change

Generate call-site refinement obligations for calls made from, and to, class members of the same module. A *call-site obligation* states that the arguments of one call satisfy the callee's parameter refinements; the solver discharges it, refutes it or refuses it. The work is in `src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Obligations/ObligationGenerator.cs`.

1. **Callers.** Run the walk that `GenerateCallObligations` (`:106-207`) performs for module functions over the bodies of class methods, constructors and operator overloads (the loops at `:72-86`). Record each obligation under the member's `Id`; `ObligationSolver.BuildFunctionInfo` already builds solver state for all three (`ObligationSolver.cs:523-621`, same directory).
2. **Callees.** Besides module functions, resolve methods of classes declared in the module, static and instance, in every spelling the parser accepts (`this.M(...)`, `Type.M(...)`, `receiver.M(...)`), and constructor calls `new T(...)` (`NewExpressionNode`, which the walk at `:136-145` does not visit). Take the callee's conditions from `ContractVerifier.EffectivePreconditions`, as `:192` does.
3. **Exactness.** Generate a provable obligation only when the call resolves to exactly one source declaration and binds exactly. Keep the existing conditions (`:157-164`, and `ExactArgumentType` at `:120-134`) and add two:
   - the callee is not `virtual`, `abstract`, `override` or an interface implementation, because the member that runs may be another declaration;
   - every name the callee's refinements read is one of its own parameters. In a class a refinement can read instance state, and the receiver of `other.M(...)` is not the caller's `this`. `FactCollector.SubstituteCallParameters` already refuses a dotted read such as `this.limit`, but leaves any other bare name in place (`FactCollector.cs:916-917`, same directory), where it would be read in the caller's scope and could collide with a caller variable of the same name. Whether the binder resolves a bare name in a refinement to a field is not verified; refuse it either way.

   When a candidate callee has a refined parameter and the call does not qualify, add the existing refusal obligation (`:182-190`, status Unsupported). A candidate is the declaration the call resolves to or, when resolution fails, any same-module member of that name. No call to a refined same-module member may be skipped silently.
4. **No guard is removed.** A discharged call-site obligation deletes no runtime check; the callee keeps its entry guard.
5. **Landing form.** #1800 records whether call-site obligations are a default-build break. At HEAD they are not (see Baseline). Re-check when you start. An opt-in surface chosen by #1868 is not a default build and changes nothing here; say in the pull request how a Failed call-site obligation appears on it. If a default command or a default build runs refinement verification by then, land in a form #1800 allows for a rejecting guarantee (a warning in this edition, or behind the per-module opt-in) and say which in the pull request.
6. **Countable.** At HEAD a call-site obligation has kind `Subtype`, which it shares with assignment obligations (`ObligationTracker.cs:33-49`), and is told apart only by its description. Add a field on `Obligation` (`ObligationTracker.cs:54`), for example the callee's name, set where the generator creates the refusal and the provable call-site obligation (`ObligationGenerator.cs:184-186`, `:199-201`), so that a tool can count call-site obligations without matching text. Keep the kind and the description: existing tests select on them.
7. **Controls.** Add cases to the registered packet of the soundness sweep (`bench/Calor.Soundness.Sweep`, the daily job that compares each proof the verifier claims with an independent oracle; packet in `tests/TestData/SoundnessSweep/` at HEAD). A *seeded unsound control* has a claim that is false on a reachable input, so Discharged is a false proof. A *safe control* has a claim that holds on every input. Add rows the way the packet's design record prescribes (section "Successor soundness packet: design" of `docs/plans/0.31-toolchain-and-sweep-record.md`, written by #1769), and set expected verdicts with `python3 scripts/soundness_sweep_gate.py freeze` (`bench/Calor.Soundness.Sweep/README.md`, "Updating the expected verdicts") from a macOS ARM64 run; `freeze` refuses a run that contains a finding. At HEAD the harness takes as a case's claim the single obligation of the template's `obligationKind` (`bench/Calor.Soundness.Sweep/CaseExecutor.cs:150-154`) and looks for a guard marker per kind (`:206-211`); a call-site case has one `Subtype` obligation and no guard at the call. If the harness in force cannot judge such a case, extending it is part of this issue. Minimum set:
   - unsound: a method passes a violating literal to a refined method of its class; a two-parameter relation `(int:lo, int:hi | (# > lo))` called with the arguments swapped; `new T(arg)` with an argument that can violate the constructor's refinement; a call through a base-typed receiver to a `virtual` method; an overloaded callee; a caller that reassigns its parameter before the call; a callee name shadowed by a local; a callee whose refinement reads a field, by bare name and through `this`, called on another instance from a caller that has a parameter of the field's name;
   - safe: a method whose own refinement implies the callee's; a constructor call with a satisfying literal; a static call `Type.M(1)`.

Example (written from `docs/syntax-reference/current-language.md`; not compiled):

```calor
module Metering
  class Meter
    func Clamp private (int:value | (# >= 0)) → int
      return value

    func Read (int:raw | (# >= 0)) → int
      !
      return this.Clamp(raw)

    func ReadRaw (int:raw) → int
      !
      return this.Clamp(raw)
```

At HEAD neither call produces an obligation. After this change each produces one: by reading the solver, not executed, Discharged in `Read` and Failed in `ReadRaw`. The parity tests below are the authority.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- `Generate` calls `GenerateCallObligations(func, module.Functions)` only inside `foreach (var func in module.Functions)` (`ObligationGenerator.cs:58-62`). Enum-extension methods (`:63-69`) and class constructors, methods and operators (`:72-86`) get parameter-entry, proof, assignment and index-bounds obligations (and return obligations, except constructors), and no call-site obligations.
- The callee is looked up by bare call-target name among module functions (`:108-109`, `:153`). Only `CallExpressionNode` and `CallStatementNode` are walked (`:140`); lambdas and local functions are skipped (`:138`). Arguments are bound against the caller's parameter list only (`:118`, `:123`).
- A call-site obligation has kind `Subtype` and a description that starts "Call to" (`:184-186`, `:199-201`); the tests at `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/InlineRefinementContractTests.cs:90`, `:112`, `:130`, `:147` and `:226` select it that way.
- The entry obligation of a refined parameter is a Boundary assumption that the solver never checks (`:660-666`), and under the default policy its runtime guard is always emitted (`ObligationPolicy.cs:39`; `src/Calor.Compiler/CodeGen/CSharpEmitter.cs:6463-6498`).
- Obligations are generated and solved only when `CompilationOptions.VerifyRefinements` is true (`src/Calor.Compiler/Program.cs:1074-1146`). Under `src/`, only the MCP tool `calor_refine` sets it (`src/Calor.Compiler/Mcp/Tools/RefineTool.cs:104`, `:190`, `:255`, `:364`, `:434`); `CHANGELOG.md:3726` says "`VerifyRefinements` has no CLI flag". There, under the default policy, a Failed obligation is the error Calor1121 (`ObligationPolicy.cs:33`; `Program.cs:1105`, `:1112-1113`).
- The solver declares every parameter of the caller before it solves (`ObligationSolver.cs:98-114`). A string, array or other non-primitive parameter demotes any proof in that callable to Assumed (`:326-357`). A `float` or `double` parameter makes every obligation except index bounds Unsupported (`:101-112`; `src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Z3/ContractTranslator.cs:1589`). Expect those statuses on such callers until #1862 lands; they are not defects of this change.
- No row of the registered packet claims a call-site obligation. Each of its 17 obligation templates claims one `proof` or refinement obligation (`tests/TestData/SoundnessSweep/templates.json`: the templates whose `claimSite` is `obligation`, and the second entry of `conventions`).

## Why

Converted C# consists of class members: a static class becomes a named static module, which the AST holds as a class definition. A refinement on such a member creates no call-site obligation today, so the proof-yield measurement of #1843, whose modules are converted files with authored contracts, would count none. The conditional guard lift #1866 reports the call-site obligations its lifted refinements create, a number that stays zero until this lands. This is new capacity in 0.35 and displaces no issue: it is the smallest change that makes the milestone's exit measurement non-empty for calls between class members.

## Done when

- New tests in `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests` cover each caller kind (method, constructor, operator body) and each callee kind (module function, static method, instance method, constructor).
- Parity: for each shape pinned at `InlineRefinementContractTests.cs:90`, `:112`, `:130`, `:147` and `:226`, a class-member version has the obligation status the module-function version has at HEAD. The existing tests in that file pass unchanged.
- A call to a `virtual`, `abstract`, `override` or interface-implementing callee, to an overloaded callee, to a generic callee, to a callee whose refinement reads a field or property, and a call with `ref` or `out` each produce one Unsupported obligation, never Discharged or Failed.
- For a discharged call, the generated C# still contains the callee's `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` guard, and invoking the callee directly with a violating argument throws (the pattern of `NonProvenOutcome_KeepsEntryAndPostconditionGuards` and `PrivateRefinement_IsCheckedAtCallerNotUniversallyRefutedAtDeclaration`, `InlineRefinementContractTests.cs:203`, `:226`).
- A test reads the new field of item 6 on a call-site obligation and finds it unset on an assignment obligation. The proof-status counter that #1853 adds under `tools/` reports call-site obligations as their own row; if that counter has not merged when this issue does, a comment on #1853 names the field.
- The controls of item 7 are in the registered packet with entries in `tests/TestData/SoundnessSweep/expected-verdicts.json`, the pull request lists every existing case whose verdict changed (expected: none), and the `sweep` job of `.github/workflows/soundness-sweep.yml` is green on the pull request and on the first scheduled run after merge.
- Standing acceptance rule for new hard errors: the conversion scorecard's native count (`conversion-scorecard` job, `.github/workflows/test.yml`) and the density ratio (migrated Calor tokens over C# tokens per project, from the corpus report job with the columns #1746 adds or, if they have not landed, by the hand method #1746 records) do not regress, and the pull request states how many corpus files newly fall to whole-file preservation. Expected: unchanged and zero, because conversion and default compilation do not run refinement verification.
- `expectedTotal` in `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated for each test project whose count changes (enforced by `scripts/check_trx.py`).
- The pull request states the landing form.

## Not in scope

Follow-ups, none of them filed by this plan; file one when the "after" value of #1843 shows the need:

- operator and conversion applications as call sites (`a + b` resolving to a user `op`);
- constructor initializers (`base(...)`, `this(...)`) and property and indexer accessors as call sites;
- members of nested classes, which get no obligations of any kind today (neither the generator at `ObligationGenerator.cs:72` nor the solver at `ObligationSolver.cs:523` visits `NestedClasses`);
- arguments that read locals, fields or properties, and callee refinements that read instance state.

Also out of scope: lambdas and local functions; argument types other than `int` and `bool` (#1863); cross-module calls; narrowing the Assumed demotion (#875, #1851, #1862); a CLI or build switch for refinement verification (#1868).

Part of epic #1861. Depends on #1800. Blocks #1863, #1866.

issues.title: [0.35] Widen call-site obligation argument types to the integer types the translator already models
issues.displaces: none: new capacity justified in body
issues.body:
## Change

A *call-site obligation* states that the arguments of one call satisfy the callee's parameter refinements. In `ExactArgumentType` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Obligations/ObligationGenerator.cs:120-134`), accept every integer type the contract translator models, in addition to `int` and `bool`: `sbyte`, `short`, `long`, `byte`, `ushort`, `uint`, `ulong`.

- The rule stays exact. An argument qualifies only when its bound type has the same width and signedness as the callee parameter's type. No implicit conversion is modelled.
- Derive the accepted set from the translator, not from a second hand-written list: `ContractTranslator.CanonicalScalarType` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Z3/ContractTranslator.cs:735-747`, private today) or `ModeledForms.ScalarTypes` (`:2972-2973`) without `str`. Add a test that fails if the generator's set and the translator's set differ.
- Controls. Add cases to the registered packet of the soundness sweep (`bench/Calor.Soundness.Sweep`, the daily job that compares each proof the verifier claims with an independent oracle; packet in `tests/TestData/SoundnessSweep/` at HEAD). A *seeded unsound control* has a claim that is false on a reachable input, so Discharged is a false proof. A *safe control* has a claim that holds on every input. Add rows the way the packet's design record prescribes (section "Successor soundness packet: design" of `docs/plans/0.31-toolchain-and-sweep-record.md`, written by #1769), and set expected verdicts with `python3 scripts/soundness_sweep_gate.py freeze` (`bench/Calor.Soundness.Sweep/README.md`, "Updating the expected verdicts") from a macOS ARM64 run; `freeze` refuses a run that contains a finding. Minimum set:
  - unsound: for each implicit widening C# allows at a call (`int` argument to `long` parameter, `byte` to `int`, `uint` to `long`), a refinement whose truth differs between the two widths; a same-type call at 8, 16 and 64 bits, signed and unsigned, where the caller's facts do not imply the callee's refinement at the type's minimum or maximum; arithmetic on `byte`, `sbyte`, `short` or `ushort` operands, in an argument and in a callee refinement, which C# evaluates at `int` width and an 8-bit or 16-bit model would wrap;
  - safe: for each of the seven added types, a same-type call that the caller's own refinement implies.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- `ExactArgumentType` returns true only for `int` and `bool` (`ObligationGenerator.cs:126-131`). Any other argument type turns the call into the refusal obligation, status Unsupported (`:173-177`, `:182-190`).
- The translator declares `sbyte`, `short`, `int`, `long`, `byte`, `ushort`, `uint` and `ulong` as bit-vectors of their width and signedness and `bool` as a boolean, and refuses `float` and `double` (`ContractTranslator.cs:1574-1589`). `ModeledForms.ScalarTypes` lists the same eight integer types plus `bool` and `str` (`:2972-2973`; `docs/verification-modeled-forms.md:264`).
- A call that needs a numeric conversion is refused, and a test pins it: `CallRequiringNumericConversion_IsNotProvenInTheWrongWidth` passes an `int` to a `long` parameter refined `(# > 2147483647)` and requires Unsupported (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/InlineRefinementContractTests.cs:130`).
- Obligations are generated and solved only under `CompilationOptions.VerifyRefinements` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Program.cs:1074`), which no CLI command or build property sets; under the default policy a Failed obligation is the error Calor1121 (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Obligations/ObligationPolicy.cs:33`).

## Why

C# code uses `long`, `byte`, `uint` and their relatives for sizes, offsets and counters. The solver models them, but the generator refuses every call whose arguments are not `int` or `bool`, so those calls are counted Unsupported in the proof-yield measurement of #1843. This is new capacity that displaces no issue. It is confined to one function, and without it #1864 creates provable obligations for `int` and `bool` parameters only.

## Done when

- A theory test over the seven added types shows that a same-type call has the status the same program has with `int` at HEAD: Discharged when the caller's refinement on the passed parameter implies the callee's, and the `int` program's status when the passed parameter is unconstrained.
- Calls that need an implicit conversion are Unsupported, and the test at `InlineRefinementContractTests.cs:130` passes unchanged.
- `char`, `nint`, `nuint`, `decimal`, `float`, `double`, enum and `string` arguments still produce the refusal obligation.
- The drift test between the generator's set and the translator's set passes.
- The controls are in the registered packet with entries in `tests/TestData/SoundnessSweep/expected-verdicts.json`, the pull request lists every existing case whose verdict changed (expected: none), and the `sweep` job of `.github/workflows/soundness-sweep.yml` is green on the pull request and on the first scheduled run after merge.
- Standing acceptance rule for new hard errors (calls that were refused can now be Failed): the conversion scorecard's native count (`conversion-scorecard` job, `.github/workflows/test.yml`) and the density ratio (migrated Calor tokens over C# tokens per project, from the corpus report job with the columns #1746 adds or, if they have not landed, by the hand method #1746 records) do not regress, and the pull request states how many corpus files newly fall to whole-file preservation. Expected: unchanged and zero, because conversion and default compilation do not run refinement verification.
- `expectedTotal` in `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated for each test project whose count changes (enforced by `scripts/check_trx.py`).

## Not in scope

- Implicit numeric conversions at the call, including an `int` literal passed to a parameter of another integer type. They stay Unsupported.
- `string` arguments (#875, #1660), `char`, native-size integers, floating point, `decimal` and enums.

Part of epic #1861. Depends on #1864. Blocks #1866.

issues.title: [0.35] Import numeric-range and array-length preconditions into the bug-pattern checkers (repaired safe controls)
issues.body:
**Current.** #1723 is the follow-up to #901 and PR #1721 and has no milestone and no labels. It lists five safe controls in the benchmark subjects on which an analysis still warns: two in the taint analysis, three in the bug-pattern checkers. It asks for better precision on them without losing any seeded unsafe finding and without trusting a helper by its name.

**Amendment.**

New title: `[0.35] Import numeric-range and array-length preconditions into the bug-pattern checkers (repaired safe controls)`. Add the label `enhancement`.

1. In the first paragraph, replace "all 25 seeded unsafe EXPECTED diagnostics fire" with "all 24 seeded unsafe EXPECTED diagnostics fire (count at HEAD bc80daeb)". Then replace the sentence "Five remaining false positives are explicitly pinned in BenchmarkSubjectRegressionTests:" and its table with:

> Three false positives are in scope. Each is a safe control (a function marked `// EXPECTED: No warnings`) whose parameter refinement the checker ignores. They are pinned as `SafeCaseGaps` in `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/Analysis/BenchmarkSubjectRegressionTests.cs:20-27`.
>
> - `arithmetic/overflow.calr`, `SafeSmallValues`: Calor0923 on `x * 100`, with `int:x | ((# < 1000) && (# > 0))`.
> - `arithmetic/overflow.calr`, `SafeBoundedShift`: Calor0923 on `x << 2`, with `int:x | ((# >= -536870912) && (# <= 536870911))`.
> - `loops/bounds-violation.calr`, `SafeWithPrecondition`: Calor0921 on `items[index]`, with `int:index | (# >= 0), int[]:items | (index < #.Length)`.
>
> The two taint controls (`SafeEscapedCommand`, Calor0982; `SafeSanitizedPath`, Calor0983) moved to #1858.

2. Delete the paragraph that begins "SQL has an additional explicit modeling boundary" and the paragraph that begins "The configured benchmark profile therefore matches 20/25". The first concerns taint analysis and is carried by #1858. The second is stale: at HEAD bc80daeb the test's inline data (`BenchmarkSubjectRegressionTests.cs:30-36`) sums to 24 seeded findings and 26 safe controls, of which 21 are matched.

3. Add a section:

> ## Change
>
> Seed the bug-pattern flow analysis with every entry fact a parameter refinement gives, not only "non-zero".
>
> - Today the analysis learns one thing from a refinement: that the parameter is not zero. `VerificationAnalysisPass` collects the parameters whose refinement excludes zero, by name in `ExtractPreconditionGuardedParams` and by symbol in `BuildGuardedParameterIds` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Analysis/VerificationAnalysisPass.cs:218-299`, `:561-638`, both through `CollectProvablyNonZeroNames`, `:334`), and `TypedBugPatternAnalysis.CreateInitialState` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Analysis/BugPatterns/TypedBugPatternAnalysis.cs:156-183`) applies only `ExcludesZero`.
> - Apply each refinement of the callable to the initial state through the narrowing the analysis already performs on conditional edges (`RefineEdge` `:302`, `RefineCondition` `:316`, `RefineNumericComparison` `:601`, `RefineSequenceBound` `:710`), so that a numeric range and an index-against-length bound hold at entry.
> - An imported fact must not be assumed after an assignment to any parameter it mentions.
> - Update the sentence in `docs/verification-modeled-forms.md:178-181` that says the precondition maps "contain only constraints that prove nonzero". That file is pinned by its SHA-256 (`tests/Calor.Verification.Tests/VerifierRuntimeDifferential/DifferentialGate.cs:21-22`, `:728-739`): update the pin and add an additive re-pin entry to registration F-4 in `docs/plans/v0.13-freeze-registrations.md` (`:603-620`), as an earlier bug-pattern edit of that file did (`:613-615`).
> - Update `benchmarks/README.md:21-31`, which counts the pinned limitations and lists these three controls.

4. Replace the final paragraph ("Acceptance: …") with:

> ## Done when
>
> - `SafeCaseGaps` has no entry for the three controls, and `Subjects_ParseBindCompileAndVerifySeededFindings_WithNamedSafeCaseGaps` (`BenchmarkSubjectRegressionTests.cs:37`) passes with no Calor0923 or Calor0921 on them.
> - Every seeded unsafe finding still fires: no existing `// EXPECTED: Calor…` line in the seven subjects changes.

>   - `int:x | ((# > 0) && (# < 100000000))` with `x * 100`: Calor0923;
>   - a range joined by `||` instead of `&&`: Calor0923;
>   - a range on a parameter other than the operand: Calor0923;
>   - `int:index | (# >= 0), int[]:items | (index <= #.Length)`: Calor0921;
>   - an upper bound with no `(# >= 0)` on the index: Calor0921;
>   - `set index index + 1` before the access: Calor0921.
> - Each new control, and one safe control per imported fact kind, is also a case in `BugPatternRuntimeOracleTests.Corpus` (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/Analysis/BugPatternRuntimeOracleTests.cs:16`), which executes the generated C# and requires the finding to agree with the runtime outcome (`:482`). `NonNegativePreconditionAllowsZero` (`:30-40`) is the model: a refined parameter and the argument that makes the program throw.
> - One test shows the import on a class method, not only on a module function.

If the sweep's design record (`docs/plans/0.31-toolchain-and-sweep-record.md`, #1769) gave it one, the same controls are also added there through its freeze procedure.

The other three are the one contract consumer that already runs on class members: the non-zero import covers methods, constructors and operators (`VerificationAnalysisPass.cs:241-296`), and ranges and lengths are the missing facts. The controls bullets are what the 0.35 exit criterion on controls requires of a bug-pattern step.

**Moved from** no milestone because it was unscheduled, and it belongs with the other consumers of preconditions.

issues.title: [0.35] Taint-analysis precision on the two repaired safe controls (split from #1723)
issues.displaces: none: new capacity justified in body
issues.body:
## Change

Remove two false positives of the taint analysis (`src/Calor.Compiler/Analysis/Security/TaintAnalysis.cs`) on safe controls, without trusting anything by name. A *safe control* is a benchmark function marked `// EXPECTED: No warnings`; a *seeded finding* is one marked `// EXPECTED: Calor…`. The two controls are `SafeEscapedCommand` (Calor0982, command injection) and `SafeSanitizedPath` (Calor0983, path traversal).

1. **Show by execution that each control is safe, before modelling it.** Nothing executes either control today; only the SQL subject has runtime tests. Add one test per control over hostile inputs:
   - command: for inputs that contain `'`, `"`, `\`, `;` and `$(...)`, the script `/bin/sh` receives is exactly one `echo` whose argument is the input;
   - path: for `..`, `.`, `../../etc/passwd`, `a/../b` and an absolute path, the control returns before the read or the path it reads is inside `/safe/directory/`.

   `benchmarks/README.md:4-7` says not to run the security subjects against a real shell, filesystem or database. Either keep to that by recording what would be passed (the argument vector after .NET's own splitting; the path), as the SQL subject is tested through an injected recorder, or run a shell only on payloads whose worst effect is a marker file in a temporary directory, on platforms that have `/bin/sh`, and amend that sentence. Say in the pull request which, and how the test is excluded on other platforms (`eng/test-manifest.json` pins skipped-test counts per project).

   The command control is expected to fail this test as written (see Baseline). If it does, do not model it. Correct the control so that the test passes, keeping its name and its `// EXPECTED: No warnings` line; passing the script through `ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList`, as `SafeArrayExec` in the same subject passes its arguments, removes the argument-string step that breaks the quoting. Add the old form as a seeded finding, and state the change in the pull request.

   Step 1 may land as its own pull request ahead of steps 2 to 5: it checks a benchmark control and does not depend on the taint model.
2. **Command injection.** Clear the command-execution taint only for the POSIX single-quote form: the value is `"'" + x.Replace("'", "'\\''") + "'"`, built across immutable bindings, and it reaches the shell inside one `-c` script. A later transform can undo the quoting, so state which later operations keep the value clean; concatenating untainted text on either side is the minimum. Admit a further transformation only if the test of step 1 covers it.
3. **Path traversal.** Clear the file-path taint only when the value is the result of `System.IO.Path.GetFileName`, resolved by symbol, and control flow has excluded `"."` and `".."` before it is appended to an untainted prefix.
4. **Document each model.** Add a short section to `docs/verification-modeled-forms.md` that states the transformation recognised and its assumptions (POSIX `sh` quoting; the platform's path separators; trusted parent directories, with no protection against symlinks). That file is pinned by its SHA-256 (`tests/Calor.Verification.Tests/VerifierRuntimeDifferential/DifferentialGate.cs:21-22`, `:728-739`): update the pin and add an additive re-pin entry to registration F-4 in `docs/plans/v0.13-freeze-registrations.md` (`:603-620`). Update `benchmarks/README.md:21-28`: the sentence that counts the pinned limitations and the two rows for these controls.
5. **Negative controls**, each a seeded finding in the subject file:
   - command: `Replace` without the surrounding quotes; quotes without `Replace`; a different replacement string; double quotes instead of single quotes; a later `Replace("'", "")` on the quoted value; the control's present form, if step 1 showed it unsafe;
   - path: `GetFileName` without the two rejections; rejection of `"."` only; the rejections applied but the unsanitised input concatenated; a user-declared function named `GetFileName`. Declare that helper in a named static module inside the subject, as the SQL subject declares `SqlEscaping`, and extend the bound-function count at `BenchmarkSubjectRegressionTests.cs:50`, because every module-level function of a subject needs an `EXPECTED` line.

## Baseline (HEAD bc80daeb)

- The two gaps are pinned in `SafeCaseGaps` (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/Analysis/BenchmarkSubjectRegressionTests.cs:22-23`). `Subjects_ParseBindCompileAndVerifySeededFindings_WithNamedSafeCaseGaps` (`:37`) requires exactly Calor0982 on `SafeEscapedCommand` and Calor0983 on `SafeSanitizedPath`.
- The subjects the test reads are the current-syntax copies `tests/TestData/ActiveSyntax/benchmarks/security/command-injection.calr` and `path-traversal.calr` (resolved by `ActiveSyntaxInputs.ForCurrentCompiler`, `:115-116`). Each has three seeded findings and three safe controls (`:30`, `:32`).
- `SafeEscapedCommand` (`command-injection.calr:37-47`) builds `'…'` with `Replace("'", "'\\''")`, then doubles every backslash and escapes every double quote, and calls `Process.Start("/bin/sh", "-c \"…\"")`. .NET splits such an argument string by the rule that a backslash is literal unless it precedes a double quote, so `'\''` reaches the shell as `'\\''`, which ends the quoted word. A simulation of the string building with that rule re-implemented and a real `/bin/sh` ran an injected `echo` for the input `'; echo INJECTED; '` and gave a shell syntax error for `it's`. Not run on .NET: the first step of this issue settles it.
- `SafeSanitizedPath` (`path-traversal.calr:31-41`) takes `System.IO.Path.GetFileName(user_input) ?? ""`, returns on `"."` and `".."`, and reads `"/safe/directory/" + sanitized`.
- No test executes either control. The SQL subject is executed through an injected recording provider (`SqlSubjects_SendRealQueriesToInjectedContract`, `:198`).
- A sanitizer is a rule matched by call identity (`BuiltInSanitizers`, `TaintAnalysis.cs:391-400`; `IdentifySanitizer`, `:806-808`; `TaintAnalysisOptions.AdditionalSanitizers`, `:228`). A string transform such as `Replace` keeps the taint of its receiver and arguments (`Taint_StringTransformPreservesReceiverAndArgumentFlows`, `BenchmarkSubjectRegressionTests.cs:271`).
- The SQL subject shows the pattern to follow. Its escape helper is modelled only when registered by exact symbol id (`SqlContracts`, `:119-131`), and a negative control requires the warning when the model is absent (`SqlEscaping_RequiresExplicitSymbolContract_NotNameBasedTrust`, `:134`). That model assumes standard SQL string literals without backslash escapes; this issue does not change it.
- `BugPatternRuntimeOracleTests` has no taint cases; `BenchmarkSubjectRegressionTests` with the subject files is the only test that reads taint findings on the subjects.

## Why

#1723 pinned five false positives. Three are precondition imports and stay in that issue; these two are taint cases that need different reasoning. They are not contract consumers, and the issue sits in this epic because it is the other half of #1723. It is new capacity that displaces no issue: two of the nine security safe controls warn today, so "no warnings on safe code" cannot be stated for the security subjects, and one of the two may not be safe at all, which is worth knowing before any model is written for it. The issue may slip to 0.36 without holding the 0.35 release; the plan recommends that step 1 still lands in 0.35, because a control that is labelled safe and is not misstates the benchmark whatever the analyzer does.

## Done when

- The two runtime tests of step 1 pass in CI, and the pull request states whether `SafeEscapedCommand` was changed and why.
- `SafeCaseGaps` has no entry for the two controls, and the test at `:37` passes with no Calor0982 on `SafeEscapedCommand` and no Calor0983 on `SafeSanitizedPath`.
- The nine seeded findings of the three security subjects still fire; no existing `// EXPECTED: Calor…` line changes.
- Every negative control of step 5 is in its subject file with its `// EXPECTED: Calor…` line, and the inline counts at `:30` and `:32` are updated.
- No rule keyed on a bare method name is added to `BuiltInSanitizers`.
- The subject files with `BenchmarkSubjectRegressionTests` are the registered instrument for the taint analysis. If the sweep's design record (`docs/plans/0.31-toolchain-and-sweep-record.md`, #1769 decision 4) gave the sweep a diagnostics channel, the negative controls of step 5 and the two safe controls are also added there through its freeze procedure.
- The section in `docs/verification-modeled-forms.md` exists, its pin and F-4 entry are updated, and `benchmarks/README.md` names no limitation for the two controls.
- `expectedTotal` in `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated for each test project whose count changes (enforced by `scripts/check_trx.py`).

## Not in scope

The SQL escaping model, any general "escaping helper" recognition, and Windows command-line quoting.

Part of epic #1861.

issues.title: [0.35] Fall-through fact after a dominating if (c) throw (conditional)
issues.body:
## Change
