```markdown
- Sign-off requires the edition to be in force as entry criterion 3 of #1697 defines it: declared with its written compatibility promise (#1805, or #1846 after a 0.32 deferral), not deferred.
- Related #1659 (and #1609, closed) are converter work, not a requirement for complete migration or checked passthrough.

Parent #1697.
```

2. In `## Acceptance`, append one bullet:

```markdown
- The maintainer's written sign-off, kept in the recruitment record under a heading `Sign-off` that this issue adds, lists the published compatibility promise (#1805; #1846 if the declaration was taken there): the path and commit of the document, the edition the component's `.calr` modules are written in (an edition is a named version of the syntax whose existing spellings no longer change; the per-module marker is #1084), and any exceptions the declaration listed. The sign-off is not accepted while the edition is undeclared or deferred.
```

3. In the fourth `## Acceptance` bullet, replace the clause "inability to recruit a maintainer is reported as a blocker, not replaced by creator self-evaluation." with:

```markdown
inability to recruit a maintainer is recorded at the adopter checkpoint (#1833) as "demand unproven" and holds this issue; it is not replaced by creator self-evaluation.
```

**Why**

The issue says recruitment can start immediately, but outreach has never been authorised (no permitted contacts and "Contacts made: 0" in `docs/plans/safe-delegation-m0/v0.23/r2a-adopter-unavailable.md:25-30`), so the start moves behind the maintainer's decision in 0.31 and gets a dated checkpoint with a written else-branch. An external maintainer who accepts `.calr` as the maintained source carries the cost of any later syntax change, and 0.30.0 was a breaking release with no rewriter for 0.29 source (`CHANGELOG.md:9-13`), so the compatibility promise has to be part of what they sign.

issues.title: [0.36] Enforce separate authorization for obligation and implementation changes
issues.body:
**Current**

The issue asks for a minimal enforceable approval boundary for the pilot: humans govern public contracts, allowed effects, independent acceptance checks and budgets, and an agent may propose changes to them but cannot authorise its own. The work builds on `.github/CODEOWNERS` and the required checks, separates implementation-only changes from obligation changes, binds approval to the reviewed revision and protects the policy and checker themselves. Acceptance is a set of demonstrations (rejected unauthorised edits, rejected stale approvals, accepted implementation-only changes) plus inspection by the external maintainer; the Dependencies section says activation depends on #1701 and "policy design may begin independently".

**Amendment**

The title does not change.

1. Replace the `## Dependencies` section with:

```markdown
## Dependencies
- This issue has two halves. The pilot-independent half is the policy, the checker, the classification command of the fifth Acceptance bullet, and the demonstrations of the first three Acceptance bullets. Pilot activation is the inventory of protected obligations for the #1701 component, the controls switched on in the pilot repository, and the external maintainer's inspection in the fourth Acceptance bullet; it depends on #1701.
- The pilot-independent half may start before the adopter checkpoint (#1833, the decision at the close of 0.33 that records whether a named external maintainer has consented). If none has, the pre-written fallback applies: that half still runs, delivered when the fallback table of the plan of record (`docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md`, #1765) says (in 0.37, ahead of any 0.37 collection), and pilot activation is held. This issue then stays open in 0.36: it cannot close under the fallback, because pilot activation needs the external maintainer.
- This issue is a prerequisite of any 0.37 task counted as effect-boundary evidence, that is, a task whose result is attributed to an effect row or a contract stopping a wrong change (#1711 controls; the #1710 harness applies the classification command to every run). For that purpose "landed" means the pilot-independent half is merged on `main` and a comment on this issue links the merged changes; it does not mean this issue is closed. Until then no 0.37 task is counted as effect-boundary evidence.

Parent #1697. No new syntax or autonomous authorization.
```

2. In `## Acceptance`, append a fifth bullet:

```markdown
- The classification of a change as implementation-only or obligation-changing runs without the pilot repository's hosting controls. One documented command takes a base and a head revision of a Calor project and an approval record, and exits non-zero when the head changes an effect row (`!`), a parameter refinement, a postcondition (`=>`), an `invariant`, an independent acceptance check or the policy itself (the policy file names the protected paths) and no approval is recorded for that head revision. The format and location of the approval record are part of this issue's policy; the command reads it from the working tree or an argument, never from a hosting API, so the #1710 harness can run it on a task workspace. Tests run the command on local revisions with no network access and cover at least: an edit that only adds an effect to a public function's row, which is the fix the compiler suggests for Calor0410 (exit non-zero); a changed postcondition on a class method (exit non-zero); a body-only change (exit 0). `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated for the added tests.
```

3. In `## Work`, append one bullet:

```markdown
- Before building a comparison, inspect what exists. `calor verify <frozen.calr> <final.calr> --weakening-check <declaration-id>` prints a JSON verdict on whether one function's parameter refinements and postconditions were weakened (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/VerifyCommand.cs:719-919`; tests in `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/WeakeningCheckCliTests.cs`, which call it through `CliTestHarness.RunCli`). It compares two files, not two revisions; it looks the declaration up among module-level functions only (`VerifyCommand.cs:765-766`); it does not compare effect rows; and it exits 0 whenever it reaches a verdict, including "weakened" (`VerifyCommand.cs:716-717`). Class members, effect rows, a base-to-head comparison and a failing exit code are the gap this issue closes. `calor review-packet --baseline-ref <git-ref>` already derives the changed declarations from a git diff (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/ReviewPacketCommand.cs:34-38`).
```

**Why**

When a function uses an effect it does not declare, the fix the compiler attaches to Calor0410 is to add that effect to the function's row (`src/Calor.Compiler/Effects/EffectEnforcementPass.cs:1061-1087`). In a 0.37 run an agent can therefore make an effect error disappear by widening the row, and without this boundary the run would still be graded a success, so no task may be counted as effect-boundary evidence before it exists. 0.37 names this issue as a prerequisite while it sits in a milestone that is held if no external maintainer consents; its own body already says the policy design does not need the pilot, and the amendment states which half that is, what "landed" means for 0.37, and how the 0.37 harness calls it.

issues.title: [0.36] Bind property-level evidence to the exact built and deployed artifact
issues.body:
**Current**

The issue asks for a small versioned evidence record and a release check for the pilot, extending the existing build-state and reproducible-build infrastructure instead of creating a parallel platform. The record identifies source, obligations, generated C#, toolchain, dependencies, build options and the final artifact by content digest, records each obligation as proved, tested, assumed, unknown or unchecked, and is bound to the artifact actually deployed. Implementation "may proceed independently of recruitment"; final release use requires #1704.

**Amendment**

The title does not change.

1. Replace the first `## Work` bullet with:

```markdown
- Inspect src/Calor.Compiler/Incremental/BuildStateCache.cs (src/Calor.Tasks/BuildStateCache.cs holds only global-using aliases to it), src/Calor.Tasks/CompileCalor.cs, existing agent build-state capture, docs/design/roundtrip-evidence.md, and reproducible-build workflows before adding fields or commands.
```

2. In `## Work`, append two bullets:

```markdown
- Before designing the evidence a reviewer is shown, inspect the existing `calor review-packet` command (src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/ReviewPacketCommand.cs, built by src/Calor.Compiler/Reporting/ReviewPacketBuilder.cs). It already assembles a per-change report that leads with the unproven remainder, lists assumptions and discloses waivers, takes `--baseline-ref` to derive the changed declarations from a git diff, and emits JSON with `--json`. Extend it or reuse its output in the evidence record; if it is not used, the pull request says why.
- Repeat the proof-status inventory of #1853 on the pilot component. #1853 builds one counter that reports, for a set of `.calr` files, how many verification obligations fall under each status it defines (among them proven, assumed grouped by the named assumption, unsupported, and checked only at run time), and runs it on the conversion corpus. Run that counter, unchanged and with the same status definitions, on the pilot component's Calor sources at the release candidate's source revision; do not write a second one. Do not derive the counts from `calor verify --format json` alone: it reports per-contract status and assumption names (src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/VerifyCommand.cs:430-437), but array-bounds and other refinement obligations are generated only when `CompilationOptions.VerifyRefinements` is set (src/Calor.Compiler/Program.cs:1074), which no CLI command did at v0.30.0. Store the counts in the evidence record beside the artifact digest, and state how each inventory status maps onto this issue's five statuses (proved, tested, assumed, unknown, unchecked).
```

3. In `## Acceptance`, append two bullets:

```markdown
- The pilot component's proof-status inventory is published in the #1697 exit record: one count per inventory status, the named assumption behind every assumed count, and the source revision and artifact digest it was computed on. The same record sizes the 0.37 proof claim to it: #1708 task cards, #1709 condition documents and the #1712 verdict describe an obligation kind as proved only if this inventory shows it proven on the pilot component, and describe kinds under any other status as runtime-checked contracts. A proven count of zero is published as zero, and 0.37 then makes no proof claim for the pilot's task class.
- If the adopter fallback applies, a comment on this issue records the inventory repeat as "not run: no pilot component" and links the #1833 record. No count from another code base is published as the pilot's.
```

4. Replace the `## Dependencies` section with:

```markdown
## Dependencies
- Pilot-specific records consume #1701. Implementation may proceed independently of recruitment. It still runs if the adopter checkpoint (#1833, the decision at the close of 0.33 that records whether a named external maintainer has consented) finds none and the pre-written fallback applies; the fallback table of the plan of record (`docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md`, #1765) says when it is delivered (in 0.37, ahead of any 0.37 collection), and this issue stays open in 0.36 with its pilot-specific records held.
- The inventory repeat needs the counter from #1853 and a pilot component. Under the fallback there is no pilot component and the repeat is recorded as not run. The fallback table then says which inventory bounds any 0.37 proof claim: the corpus inventory (#1853) and the proof yield on named native modules (#1843) are the ones that exist without a pilot.
- Final release use requires #1704 evidence readiness.

Parent #1697.
```

**Why**

At HEAD `bc80daeb` a successful proof that touches the solver's string theory, or an array or user-type sort, is returned as Assumed with the runtime check kept (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Z3/Z3Verifier.cs:586-631`); the trigger is any signature that mentions an array or a non-primitive type (`docs/verification-modeled-forms.md:157-165`), and calls inside contracts are Unsupported (`docs/verification-modeled-forms.md:59`). A component in a real application is mostly strings, collections and objects, so counting its statuses with the counter 0.35 used on the corpus keeps the 0.37 comparison from claiming proofs the pilot does not have. The two inspection leads are repository facts: `src/Calor.Tasks/BuildStateCache.cs` is a ten-line file of aliases to `src/Calor.Compiler/Incremental/BuildStateCache.cs`, and `calor review-packet` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/ReviewPacketCommand.cs:10-17`) already builds a reviewer-facing evidence report.

issues.title: [0.36] Establish pilot evidence readiness and fail closed on invalid validation runs
issues.body: Delivers an executable readiness check for the pilot release: #1694's cause dispositioned and retained valid runs linked (its body asks for "the fixing change"; where #1694 closed on a disposition that has no fix, the linked disposition evidence stands in for it), injected invalid evidence and known counterexamples failing the release path, exit codes and missing or skipped results checked instead of inferred from a green report file, and the readiness result consumed by #1703's evidence record. It stays in 0.36 unchanged because it integrates readiness for one immutable release candidate and, by its own first paragraph, does not duplicate the sweep repair; the plan does that repair earlier (#1694 and the successor packet in 0.31, re-registration after the 0.32 rewrite in #1807), and entry criterion 2 of #1697 covers the standing health of the sweep. Its controls (known-invalid implementation, unavailable solver, missing result, stale evidence, invalid harness execution) do not need the pilot, so it is one of the three children that still run if the adopter checkpoint (#1833) applies the fallback; only its requirement for fresh results on the pilot release candidate waits for #1701. The reuse leads in its body are current at HEAD `bc80daeb`: `scripts/soundness_sweep_gate.py` (subcommands `gate`, `check-fixture`, `freeze`), its self-tests `scripts/test_soundness_sweep_gate.py`, the runner `scripts/run-soundness-sweep.sh`, and the daily job in `.github/workflows/soundness-sweep.yml`, whose sweep job runs on `macos-15` because the harness is macOS ARM64 only (`bench/Calor.Soundness.Sweep/README.md:14-15`). One line in its Dependencies is stale and needs no action: the three issues it asks to coordinate with (#1115, #1157, #1159) were all closed on 2026-10-29; the maintainer may delete the sentence when applying the plan.

issues.title: [0.36] Deliver mixed C#/Calor integration, diagnostics, and supported-platform deployment
issues.body:
**Current**

The issue asks for the pilot to be a normal buildable application with one maintained Calor component: a conventional public .NET interface, install/restore/build/test/publish instructions that work from a clean environment with a pinned toolchain, compile and runtime failures traced back to Calor source, and deployment exercised on the OS, architecture and runtime matrix approved in #1701, with untested targets excluded from the support statement. Its Dependencies section names #1701 for the selection, says release integration consumes #1703 and #1704, and says to reuse "#1639-#1641/#1650-#1652" instead of duplicating their generic SDK and agent work.

**Amendment**

The title does not change. In `## Dependencies`, replace the sentence "Reuse #1639-#1641/#1650-#1652 rather than duplicate their generic SDK/agent work." with:

```markdown
Reuse #1639 (0.31), #1640, #1641 and #1855 (0.34), and #1650 to #1652 (0.33), rather than duplicate their generic SDK/agent work.
```

Nothing else in the body changes. Every acceptance bullet needs the #1701 component and the external maintainer, so the issue is held if the adopter checkpoint (#1833) applies the fallback.

**Why**

The range "#1639-#1641" no longer names the work this issue reuses. #1639 closes in 0.31 on a narrower scope (init, check and an SDK consumer build on a machine with only the .NET 11 SDK), #1640 and #1641 move to 0.34, and the remainder of #1639 becomes #1855: the five-runtime-identifier consumer matrices on .NET 11 (`sdk-package-consumer`, `.github/workflows/test.yml:1378-1397`; `sdk-consumer`, `.github/workflows/publish-nuget.yml:198-216`), the release SDK pin (`global.json` pins 10.0.100 at HEAD `bc80daeb`) and Z3 packaging under the .NET 11 SDK. That remainder is what the clean-environment and per-target deployment acceptance of this issue builds on.

issues.title: [0.36] Ship one useful pilot improvement with independent acceptance and measured costs
issues.body: Delivers one accepted and deployed change to the maintained pilot component that solves the maintainer's actual problem within the cost ceiling agreed in #1701, with the baseline, commands, held-out outcomes, costs, creator interventions and unsuccessful attempts published. It stays in 0.36 unchanged because it is the deliverable the epic's exit record is about: a framework without a useful maintained component does not complete #1697. It cannot start without the #1701 component, the #1702 controls and the #1705 integration, and its release acceptance needs #1703 evidence and #1704 readiness, so it is held if the adopter checkpoint (#1833) applies the fallback. Nothing substitutes for it: its body already rules out marking a synthetic speedup or a relaxed requirement as delivered. Its body has an implementation agent produce the change with inference cost recorded under the #1701 ceiling and carries no paid-run terms (spend ceiling in money, pinned model, abort triggers, zero-cost dry pass); whether that is ordinary-session authoring or a paid run needing those terms is settled by the maintainer when the #1701 cost ceiling is agreed, and filing or keeping this issue authorises no spend. Its findings are an input to final task approval in #1708.

issues.title: [0.36] Rehearse agent-unavailable incident recovery and explicit C# divergence
issues.body: Delivers an operating guide and an observed recovery drill in which the external maintainer, without the creator or a coding agent, locates the deployed build, diagnoses an incident supplied by an independent person, repairs it in Calor source, rebuilds the evidence and deploys. It also tests the emergency path: a temporary authoritative C# fork that a later Calor build cannot overwrite, reconciled before authority returns to Calor. It stays in 0.36 unchanged as the last step of the epic's sequence: it uses the releasable component from #1706 together with the #1702 controls, #1703 evidence and #1705 integration, so it is held if the adopter checkpoint (#1833) applies the fallback. Its runbook, transcript and timings go into the #1697 exit record and are an input to final task approval in #1708.

issues.title: [0.37] Epic: earn the language
issues.body:
**Current**

The epic asks where maintained Calor source adds value over equally capable C# workflows, as a falsifiable hypothesis. It defines three conditions (conventional C#, C# with comparable explicit specifications, Calor), lists five children (#1708 to #1712), and requires #1712 to publish a proceed/narrow/revise/stop verdict. It reads as a first test: it does not mention the one adjudicated positive, has no entry criteria, does not say which comparison decides the verdict, and does not say what happens without an external pilot or without an authorised budget.

**Amendment**

Replace the body with the text under "Epic body" above. The title does not change. Against the current body the replacement changes these places and nothing else:

1. `## Outcome`: the second paragraph, the three-item prior record and the closing sentence are new.
2. Two new sections after `## Outcome`: `## Entry criteria` and `## If the adopter checkpoint is not passed`.
3. `## Work breakdown`: names each child, marks #1711 as the primary source of discrimination, adds #1865, #1857 and #1867, and says #1712 commits the analysis before collection.
4. `## Comparison`: condition 2 gains the parenthesis; the paragraph beginning "Condition 2 is the single gating comparator" is new.
5. `## Acceptance`: the second and sixth bullets and the final "Exit" bullet with its three records are new; the other five are unchanged.
6. `## Dependencies and decision` is renamed `## Reuse and dependencies`; "an explicitly authorized collection budget" becomes "the budget authorised in #1867"; the edge list is new.
7. `## Non-goals`: the second and third sentences are new.
8. `## Tracked child issues`: three lines added.
9. `## Sequencing and decision gate` is renamed `## Sequencing and release acceptance`; the first bullet gains its first sentence; the second, fourth and fifth bullets and the last sentence of the final bullet are new; in the bullet on #1712 collection, "and a separately authorized budget" becomes "the analysis script committed, and the #1867 authorisation".

When the plan is applied, replace each `NEW-NN-xx` placeholder in the body with the issue number it was filed under.

**Why**

One Calor-versus-C# result was adjudicated a hit and one venue a miss, so 0.37 confirms a probe-scale positive under fairer controls and must say so. Choosing tasks Calor should win cannot be the selection rule; equipped C# is the single gating comparator and discrimination comes from #1711. The chain to 0.37 runs through an external maintainer nobody has been authorised to recruit, so the epic needs entry criteria, written dependency edges, a cited fallback, and the inputs the September stop recorded as absent. A spend decision with no decline branch cannot be an exit criterion, and the 0.37 exit criterion reads "The language investment verdict published, or the #1867 decline recorded, or the fallback disposition recorded, as #1698 defines", so the three exit records are spelled out in `## Acceptance`.

issues.title: [0.37] Define independent engineering tasks, held-out acceptance, and economic targets
issues.body:
**Current**

The issue asks for a small, versioned, independently assessed task set rooted in pilot needs: one supportable performance task and one harder task that exposes limits, with arm-neutral requirements and black-box acceptance written before any implementation and owned separately from the implementing agents. Improvement criteria, cost ceilings, invalid-run rules, stop conditions and the analysis are agreed before comparative outcomes are seen. Its last acceptance bullet makes "collection approval" name the spending and time limits.

**Amendment**

The title does not change.

1. In `## Work`, insert after the first bullet:

```markdown
- Start from the protocol draft that #1791 opened in 0.31, `docs/plans/0.37-comparison-protocol.md`. It covers outcome measures, cost accounting, independence and invalid-run rules. Task selection, stratification and the admission rule were held there until #1648 closed; they are finished here.
- Stratify before screening. Define three strata: effect-and-contract (an effect row or a contract is expected to decide the outcome), neutral, and C#-favoured. Before any candidate is screened, write in the protocol each stratum's share of the task set and its minimum number of admitted tasks; they do not change afterwards. The performance task and the harder task above are classified like any other candidate (the existing category registry lists performance work as C#-favoured, `bench/phase0-agent-native/categories.json:64-70`). Beside them the set must include at least one task in which effect rows or contracts decide the outcome.
- Screen every candidate against the admission rule in the closing record of #1648; that record governs where it and this summary differ. In summary: a task counts as effect or contract evidence only if a wrong implementation exists that passes the visible tests (the ones the agent can run) and is no more work than the honest one. Record every candidate with its source, stratum, verdict and, for a rejection, the reason. This issue owns the rule as the protocol states it and the per-candidate verdicts; #1865 owns the counts against the sizing minimum and copies the verdicts without re-deciding them. Rejected candidates stay in the record; rejection is the expected outcome for most candidates (`docs/plans/2026-09-05-ppw-rows-fixture-redesign.md:136-137`). A candidate that fails the rule may enter the neutral or C#-favoured stratum, where it is not effect or contract evidence.
- Do not use small well-specified functions as tasks. About 165 valid runs on fixtures of up to 16 functions produced zero escaped bugs in either arm (`bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/hardness-check-002/VERDICT.md:8-12`), so such tasks cannot separate the conditions.
- Freeze the strata, shares, minimums, the admission rule as the protocol states it, the exclusion threshold (see Acceptance) and the reading of each outcome where CI rejects a later edit: Annex A of `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md`, the one registry the plan of record (`docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md`) names for every registration. Append a new entry to the annex revision log (section A.3) and move the `Annex version` pointer at the head of the annex to it. The `annex-freeze` job in `.github/workflows/experiment-registry-tamper-check.yml` runs `scripts/check-annex-freeze.py`, which fails a pull request that edits or removes an existing entry, so a later change to a frozen value is a new dated entry that names what it supersedes.
```

2. In `## Acceptance`, insert after the third bullet ("Task cards list ..."):

```markdown
- Each task card also gives its stratum, its admission verdict, and one number, the unverified-boundary share: the functions on the change path that declare `! unknown` as their own effect row, or that sit in preserved C# (code the converter kept verbatim as C#, whether a whole file or a single member), divided by all functions on the change path. The protocol defines "change path" before any share is computed (proposed: the functions the reference change edits, plus their direct callers and callees) and fixes a numeric threshold, justified from the per-project unknown-effect shares that #1802 reports. The recorder #1802 adds reports counts per source file, not per function. Where the change path covers every function of a file, its counts are used as reported; where it covers only some, those functions are counted from their declared rows in the source, and the card says so. Whole-file preserved C# does not appear in the recorder's output, because the effect pass sees no functions there, so those functions are counted from the preserved files themselves. The card names the command and the commit. A task above the threshold still runs and is reported in its stratum; it is excluded from effect evidence.
- The commit that adds the Annex A entry (last Work bullet) is an ancestor of the commit that records the first screening verdict, the `annex-freeze` job passed on its pull request, and the screening record lists every candidate, rejected ones included.
- The approved set has at least one admitted task in each stratum. If no effect-and-contract candidate passes the admission rule, the record says so and #1712 reports that stratum as "no admissible task"; a task is not substituted because Calor is expected to win it.
- The analysis plan reports every measure per stratum. A pooled figure never appears without the per-stratum figures beside it.
- The frozen protocol has been submitted for the review #1857 holds, by the methods reviewer named under #1777. If #1777 named no reviewer, #1857 records the vacancy, this bullet is recorded as not applicable, and #1712 does not start.
```

3. In `## Acceptance`, replace the last bullet ("Collection approval names spending/time limits and authorized scope. Filing this issue alone authorizes neither paid runs nor paused PP-W research.") with:

```markdown
- Paid collection is authorised only by the decision record #1867, which names the spend ceiling, the time limit and the authorised scope. This issue supplies that record's inputs (protocol, stratum minimums, repetitions) and authorises nothing. Filing this issue alone authorizes neither paid runs nor paused PP-W research.
```

4. Replace the `## Dependencies` section with:

```markdown
## Dependencies
#1648 (closed in 0.31; its record carries the admission rule) before stratification and screening. Pilot findings #1701/#1706/#1707 for final task approval; if the adopter checkpoint (#1833) recorded "demand unproven", the task source and this issue's disposition are the ones the fallback table in the plan of record (`docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md`) gives. Protocol drafting started in 0.31 (#1791). #1802 supplies the recorder behind the task-card number. Feeds #1709, #1710, #1711, #1865 and #1857; collection is authorised only by #1867. Parent #1698.
```

5. Append to `## Work`:

```markdown
- Parts, each of which may be its own pull request, in this order: (1) the finished protocol with strata, shares, minimums and threshold, and its Annex A entry; (2) the screening record; (3) the task cards and fixtures for the admitted tasks. The issue closes when all three are merged.
```

**Why**

"Tasks where effect rows decide the outcome" cannot be the selection rule, because the repository has shown such tasks are mostly redundant with behavioural tests (zero escapes on both arms in 28 valid runs, `docs/plans/2026-09-05-ppw-rows-fixture-redesign.md:31-33`, `:76-81`); it can be one stratum fixed in advance, screened by the #1648 rule, with code whose effects are `unknown` or preserved kept out of effect evidence. The budget line had two owners, so it now points at #1867, and the screening record and the supply inventory were nearly one artifact, so this issue owns the verdicts and #1865 the counts.

issues.title: [0.37] Build fair conventional C#, semantically equipped C#, and Calor conditions
issues.body:
**Current**

The issue asks for three runnable authoring conditions for the #1708 tasks, without implementation search: conventional C#, C# with comparable explicit specifications and validation "wherever practical", and Calor. It requires the same requirements and acceptance for all three, transparent cost accounting, and a statement of which obligations are proved, tested, assumed, unknown or unchecked in each. Its third acceptance bullet requires an independent reviewer to inspect condition fairness before collection, without saying who.

**Amendment**

The title does not change.

1. In `## Work`, append four bullets:

```markdown
- Define the semantically equipped C# condition as the bolt-on analogue of what Calor enforces by default in one build: analyzers for effect boundaries (for example a banned-API analyzer), contracts written as executable assertions, and disposal analyzers. Use the disposal analyzers that #1842 named in its comment on this issue (its candidates were the .NET code-analysis rules CA2000 and CA2213, not verified against the pinned SDK); if that comment does not exist, evaluate those two here and record the choice. Record each tool with its package and version, and a table with one row per Calor guarantee the tasks exercise, naming the C# tool that stands in for it or "no equivalent". A Rust-plus-verifier condition is out of scope.
- Label as "derived" every contract obtained mechanically from the implementation (lifted from a guard, generated from the code under test, or inferred from a body), in every condition. Derived contracts are reported in their own column and are never counted as specification-backed proofs. Each one is accompanied by a mutated-guard control: the same derivation run after the guard it came from has been mutated, to show whether the contract moves with the defect.
- Optional fourth condition, Rust: reported, never adjudicated. It applies only to #1708 tasks that meet both conditions. (a) The task is graded by a process-level oracle: a grader that runs the built program and compares its output, built with the runner, wire protocol and adapter pattern of #1830. The pair harness otherwise grades through .NET test shims, which a Rust program cannot satisfy. (b) The task has measured headroom: in the calibration stage of #1867 at least one conventional C# run was not accepted on its first attempt. A task on which every calibration run of conventional C# is accepted first time has none. The condition reuses the Rust arm definition and iteration shim from #1828. Its spend is a separate line in #1867, authorised or struck there. This issue closes on the definition for the tasks that meet (a); (b) is applied after the calibration, under #1712. If #1828 was closed as not planned, no task has a process-level oracle, no task has measured headroom, or the line is struck, the condition is dropped and the reason recorded in the condition document; nothing else in this issue changes.
- Parts, each of which may be its own pull request, in this order: (1) the three condition definitions, the tool list and the guarantee-by-guarantee table; (2) the derived-contract list with its mutated-guard controls and the cost accounting, which completes the fairness review package; (3) the optional Rust condition, or the record that it was dropped. The issue closes when all three are merged.
```

2. In `## Acceptance`, append to the second bullet ("Document which obligations are proved, tested, assumed, unknown, and unchecked ..."):

```markdown
For the Calor condition, "proved" follows the proof-status inventory that #1703 repeats on the pilot component: an obligation kind is listed as proved only if that inventory shows it Proven, and kinds that are Assumed, Unsupported or checked only at run time are listed as runtime-checked. Under the adopter fallback there is no pilot component, and the inventories the plan of record (`docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md`) names bound the claim instead: the corpus inventory (#1853) and the proof yield on named modules (#1843).
```

3. In `## Acceptance`, replace the third bullet ("An independent reviewer inspects condition fairness and the semantically equipped C# baseline before collection.") with:

```markdown
- The fairness review package is complete and has been submitted for the review #1857 holds, by the methods reviewer named under #1777. The package is the condition definitions, the tool list with versions, the guarantee-by-guarantee table, the derived-contract list with its mutated-guard controls, and the cost accounting. #1857 owns the review, its objections and its clearance. A separate agent session working from a rubric is a quality control and does not count as this review. If #1777 named no reviewer, #1857 records the vacancy and #1712 does not start; this issue still closes on the complete package.
```

4. Replace the `## Dependencies` section with:

```markdown
## Dependencies
#1708 task/requirements design. The fairness review is held by #1857 and precedes comparative execution. Reuse #1651 drivers, #1703 evidence, the equipped-C# fixture pattern from the 0.32 replication (#1813) and the process-level oracle pattern of #1830. The disposal analyzers are the ones #1842 names. The optional Rust condition also needs #1828. Parent #1698.
```

**Why**

Calor's difference from other ecosystems is integration and default-on enforcement in one build, so the fair comparator is C# with the same checks bolted on. Proofs that touch strings, arrays or user types are returned as Assumed today (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Z3/Z3Verifier.cs:576-631`), so "proved" must follow the measured inventory. A contract derived from the code under test moves with a defect seeded in that code, so it needs its own label and a mutated-guard control. Rust may be offered only as a reported condition, on tasks where conventional C# is not already at the floor, and the equipped arm gets disposal analyzers. The reviewer line named no reviewer and would have had two owners once #1857 existed; #1857 now holds the review. At HEAD `bc80daeb` the C# arm's project is generated inline with nullable analysis and code-style enforcement only (`bench/phase0-agent-native/run-pair.sh:767-777`).

issues.title: [0.37] Extend the existing agent harness for three conditions and full-effort accounting
issues.body:
**Current**

The issue asks for an incremental extension of `bench/phase0-agent-native` and the #1651 multi-agent drivers that runs the three no-search conditions with pinned identities and complete cost records, including human effort. Acceptance is by deterministic fake-driver tests, result validation that rejects mismatched identities, an "approved smoke run ... when separately authorized", and intact archives. It names #1651 as the only thing it reuses.

**Amendment**

The title does not change.

1. In `## Work`, insert after the first bullet:

```markdown
- Reuse, do not rebuild: the arm abstraction (#1827); the language-neutral process-level oracle (#1830), of which the runner, the wire protocol and the adapter pattern carry over and the 0.33 tasks do not, because #1708 supplies the tasks; the agent drivers (#1651); and the three-condition support written for the 0.32 seeded-defect replication (#1815). Begin with an inventory, in the pull request description, of which of these are present and what each still lacks for the #1708 tasks. At v0.30.0 none existed: `bench/phase0-agent-native/run-pair.sh` accepted only the `calor` and `csharp` arms (line 282), generated the C# project inline with no place for an analyzer package (lines 767-777), graded through per-arm `TestShim.<arm>.cs` files (line 782) and launched only the `claude` client (line 1353). If any of those is still true when this issue starts, a prerequisite that this issue's scope needs has not landed: report it and stop instead of patching around it here.
- For every run, apply the classification command from #1702 to the run's final workspace against its starting revision, and record whether the agent changed an effect row, a parameter refinement, a postcondition or an acceptance check without approval. Such a run is recorded as an unauthorised obligation change, not as an accepted task. If #1702 has not landed, record "not checked" and mark the run ineligible as effect-boundary evidence.
```

2. In `## Acceptance`, replace the third bullet ("An approved smoke run demonstrates end-to-end execution when separately authorized; dry-run/test coverage alone is labeled as such.") with:

```markdown
- A zero-cost pass succeeds for every #1708 task under every #1709 condition, the optional Rust condition included if #1709 defines one. The zero-cost pass is `run-pair.sh --null-agent` or its successor: it applies the reference solution instead of invoking an agent and exercises workspaces, shims, tests and metrics with no API spend.
- This issue closes on the fake-driver tests and the zero-cost pass, labelled as such. A paid smoke run is authorised only as the calibration stage of #1867 and is run under #1712.
- The fake-driver tests run in the existing harness test job (`python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/phase0-agent-native/tests`, `.github/workflows/test.yml:124`). If a test is added to or removed from a .NET test project, `expectedTotal` for that project in `eng/test-manifest.json` is updated in the same pull request; `scripts/check_trx.py` enforces the count in CI.
```

3. Replace the `## Dependencies` section with:

```markdown
## Dependencies
#1708 protocol and #1709 condition interfaces. #1827 and #1830 provide the arm and oracle interfaces, #1651 the generic client drivers, and #1815 the three-condition support; none is duplicated here. #1702 provides the classification command; without it runs are recorded as "not checked". If the adopter checkpoint (#1833) recorded "demand unproven", this issue's scope and disposition are the ones the fallback table in the plan of record (`docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md`) gives; the #1702 classification command is applied to every run under either scope. Parent #1698.
```

**Why**

The pair harness is bound to two arms and to .NET grading, and the arm abstraction and oracle that #1709 and #1710 need are built in 0.33; restructuring `bench/phase0-agent-native/run-pair.sh` (1,893 lines at HEAD `bc80daeb`, measured by `wc -l`) again here would duplicate that work. Every paid run needs one authorisation, which is #1867, and the #1702 boundary only protects 0.37 evidence if the harness applies it to each run.

issues.title: [0.37] Add blinded implementation, specification, and boundary-defect controls
issues.body:
**Current**

The issue asks for an independently authored defect-control set for the #1708 tasks: implementation defects with unchanged obligations, incorrect or weakened specifications that still verify, and boundary defects, plus valid unchanged controls. Defect identities and the held-out oracle stay outside the implementing agent's and the blinded reviewer's control, detections are classified by channel (compiler, prover, test, reviewer), and the three defect families are reported separately. It does not say which controls may count as evidence about effect boundaries.

**Amendment**

The title does not change.

1. In `## Deliverable`, append:

```markdown
These controls are the comparison's primary source of discrimination between conditions. Discrimination must not come from choosing tasks that favour one condition; #1708 fixes the strata in advance.
```

2. In `## Work`, append two bullets:

```markdown
- Apply the "derived" rule from #1709: a contract obtained mechanically from the implementation is labelled derived, reported separately, never counted as a specification-backed proof, and accompanied by a mutated-guard control. A control whose contract was derived from code that already contained the seeded defect is invalid; pin the contract from the clean baseline.
- A control counts as effect-boundary evidence (evidence that an effect row or a contract stopped a wrong change) only if all of these hold, and the check of each is recorded with the control: (a) #1702 has landed, meaning its policy, checker and classification command are on `main`, and the #1710 harness applies that command to every run, so an agent that makes an effect error disappear by widening the row is recorded as an unauthorised obligation change; (b) the code on the change path is native Calor, not preserved C# (code the converter kept verbatim as C#); (c) the effect rows and contracts on the change path existed before the change under test and were not written by the implementing agent; (d) the control passes the #1648 admission rule as the #1708 protocol states it; (e) while #1731 is open, the change path does not run through LINQ operators, delegate invocation or culture-sensitive formatting and parsing. Where (e) cannot be avoided, the control still runs: list each such call site in the report as assumed, and report the effect-boundary result with and without that control.
```

3. In `## Acceptance`, append:

```markdown
- Every control counted as effect-boundary evidence has the five checks (a) to (e) recorded. If #1702 has not landed, the report has no effect-boundary evidence category and says why.
```

4. Replace the `## Dependencies` section with:

```markdown
## Dependencies
#1708 tasks and #1709 conditions; integrate with #1710 before collection. #1648 (admission rule) and #1731 (sound contracts for LINQ, delegates and culture-sensitive members). #1702 for any control counted as effect-boundary evidence. Builds on Machine Zone sections 7/12 (`docs/plans/machine-zone.md`), not its superseded structured-editing hypothesis. Parent #1698.
```

**Why**

About 165 valid runs at fixture scale showed zero escaped bugs in either arm (`bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/hardness-check-002/VERDICT.md:8-12`), and in the July probe only 2 of 6 effect-class defects produced a difference between arms (`bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/ws5-probe-001/VERDICT.md:42-50`), so discrimination has to come from blinded controls. The compiler's own suggested fix for an undeclared effect is to add it to the row (`src/Calor.Compiler/Effects/EffectEnforcementPass.cs:1068-1071`), so effect evidence is meaningless until an agent cannot approve its own row change. Derived contracts fail the blindness rule unless labelled and controlled.

issues.title: [0.37] Execute the approved no-search comparison and publish the language investment verdict
issues.body:
**Current**

The issue runs the pinned, repeated, counterbalanced comparison and publishes an honest decision on whether Calor adds value for a specific task class, especially against semantically equipped C#. Its entry criteria list #1708 to #1711 and the #1697 findings and say "Obtain explicit authorization for paid collection before starting" without naming where that authorisation is recorded. It must publish a proceed/narrow/revise/stop decision for 0.38.

**Amendment**

The title does not change.

1. Replace the `## Entry criteria` section with:

```markdown
## Entry criteria
#1708 tasks and protocol, frozen and reviewed; #1709 conditions, reviewed for fairness; #1710 validated harness with a zero-cost pass on every task and condition; #1711 independently owned defect controls; and the maintained-component findings from #1697, or under the adopter fallback the scope the plan of record (`docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md`) gives this issue.

Three records must exist before the first paid run: the task supply inventory (#1865); the methods review record with both reviews cleared (#1857); and the collection authorisation (#1867) with an authorise outcome that has not lapsed. #1867 is the only authorisation for paid collection, a paid calibration or smoke run included. It fixes the spend ceiling, the abort triggers, the one pinned model, the time limit and the reading of each outcome. Filing or amending this issue authorises no spend.

- Held: while #1867 is undecided, or #1857 has not yet cleared both reviews, this issue stays open and makes no paid run. Work that costs nothing may proceed: the analysis script and the zero-cost pass.
- Gate closed: if #1857 records that no reviewer was named, or that a review did not clear, this issue does not start. If #1867 records a decline, the dated default "not decided, treated as decline until changed" included, close this issue as not planned with that record linked; #1698 then records the verdict as "not collected". A later dated authorise entry on the #1867 record reopens it.

This work does not resume paused PP-W research or borrow its ledger/budget.
```

2. In `## Work`, insert as the first two bullets:

```markdown
- Before the first paid run, calibration included, commit the analysis script: one executable under `bench/phase0-agent-native/` that reads the run archives and computes every measure in the frozen #1708 analysis plan, per stratum and per condition. It states a rule for every ratio that can be undefined (for example cost per accepted task when a condition accepts no task, a ratio to conventional C# when that condition's count is zero, a stratum with no admissible task) and prints the cell as undefined with the rule applied; it never substitutes zero or drops the cell. A unittest under `bench/phase0-agent-native/tests/` (the pattern of `test_ppe1_analyze.py`) runs it on a small synthetic archive that contains each undefined case. Append the script's commit and SHA-256 to the #1867 registration, as a new revision-log entry in Annex A of `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md`. Results are computed by that commit; a later change to the script is disclosed as a deviation with both outputs published. The precedent for an adjudicator written before any run is `bench/phase0-agent-native/w5-analyze.py` (`docs/plans/pp-w5-spend-authorisation.md:70-73`).
- On the collection commit, repeat the zero-cost pass (`--null-agent`) before the first paid run. Then run only what #1867 authorised: its stages, its line items, its pinned model, its ceiling and its time limit. The Rust condition runs only if its line was authorised, and its results are reported, never adjudicated. When an abort trigger fires, stop and publish what was collected as "aborted"; the budget is not topped up inside this issue. Large run outputs go in workflow artifacts or an archive branch, not under `docs/plans/evidence/` (`CLAUDE.md`, "Evidence and review records").
```

3. In `## Acceptance and decision`, insert after the first bullet:

```markdown
- The analysis script's commit is an ancestor of the commit that records the first paid run, its SHA-256 is in the Annex A entry, and its unittest passes in the harness test job (`python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/phase0-agent-native/tests`).
- Report every measure per stratum fixed in #1708 and per condition, computed by the registered commit of the analysis script. The verdict is decided on Calor against semantically equipped C#; conventional C# and Rust are reported and do not decide it. State which of the readings written in advance in #1867 the result matched, and record that reading in #1698.
- Publish the verdict in the 0.37 release notes and enter it in the evidence ledger (#1774). `docs/benchmarking/results.md` is generated and is not edited by hand.
```

**Why**

Rust may ride along only as a reported condition with its budget inside this issue's authorisation. The budget approval had two owners and no decline branch; #1867 now owns it and the decline has a written outcome. The verdict is decided against equipped C# and reported per stratum. The study stop of 2026-09-09 listed "executable estimators, undefined-ratio rules, and joint simulation" among the inputs whose absence prevented any sizing (`docs/plans/safe-delegation-m0/decision.md:51`), so the analysis is committed and registered before collection starts.

issues.title: [0.37] Task supply inventory
issues.displaces: none: new capacity justified in body
issues.body:
## Deliverable
One record, `docs/plans/0.37-task-supply-inventory.md`, that counts the candidate tasks available for the 0.37 comparison in each stratum after screening, compares each count with the minimum the design needs, and says per stratum whether supply is sufficient. It makes no paid runs and changes no code.

Terms. A *stratum* is one of the three task groups #1708 fixes in advance: effect-and-contract, neutral, C#-favoured. The *admission rule* comes from the closing record of #1648: a task counts as effect or contract evidence only if a wrong implementation exists that passes the visible tests and is no more work than the honest one. #1708 owns that rule as its protocol states it and the verdict on each candidate; this issue owns the counts against the minimum.

Why it is new work and displaces nothing: the study stop of 2026-09-09 recorded that no design could be sized because "actual historical and future source-task supply" was absent (`docs/plans/safe-delegation-m0/decision.md:43-46`) and classed supply as insufficient information (`docs/plans/safe-delegation-m0/supply-status.md:94-96`); the one real-scale venue screened 8 tasks against a bar of 70 (`docs/plans/call-s-adjudication.md:114-115`). #1708 defines and screens tasks but does not count them against a minimum. The cost is one document.

## Work
- Read the frozen #1708 protocol (strata, shares, minimum admitted tasks per stratum) and its screening record, and the sizing record from #1786 (`docs/plans/0.37-sizing-and-budget-request.md`) as last refreshed at a milestone close. If the two give different minimums, use the larger and say so.
- One row per candidate: an identifier (privacy-safe for adopter material; source content stays outside the repository, `supply-status.md:68-69`), its source, who owns the task statement and who owns its acceptance checks, stratum, admission verdict and reason, the unverified-boundary share from its task card (the share of functions on the change path that declare `! unknown` as their effect row or are preserved C#), whether its oracle is process-level (the task is graded by running a program and comparing its output, which makes it eligible for the optional Rust condition in #1709), and its source cluster. Stratum, verdict, reason and share are copied from the #1708 screening record and task cards and are not re-decided here; a verdict that looks wrong is raised on #1708.
- Label each source: pilot change requests (#1701, #1706, #1707); under the adopter fallback, the source the plan of record (`docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md`) names; existing benchmark pairs. The 31 pairs under `bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs/` at HEAD `bc80daeb` (by the `category` field of each `pair.json`: N1 4, W1 3, W2 5, W3 4, W5 9, PP-W-rows 6, and none in C1 to C3) are listed as maintainer-authored fixtures and are not counted as supply (`supply-status.md:31-34`; #1708 excludes small well-specified functions).
- Count independent source clusters, not variants of one underlying change (`supply-status.md:61-62`).
- Per stratum, give: candidates, admitted, admitted with acceptance checks owned by someone other than the implementing agents, the minimum required with its source, and the verdict "sufficient" or "short by k".
- Where a field cannot be filled, write "unavailable". Do not impute a value or substitute repository issue counts (`supply-status.md:86-88`). A short stratum is reported as short; the admission rule is not relaxed and no task is reclassified to fill it.

## Acceptance
- The file exists, and every candidate in the #1708 screening record appears in it exactly once; the row count equals the candidate count stated at the top of the file.
- Each stratum has the four numbers above and a verdict, and each minimum cites the section of the protocol or sizing record it came from.
- Every row names its source and the owner of its acceptance checks, or says "unavailable".
- The file states that it authorises no collection, and #1698 links it.
- Nothing is written under `docs/plans/evidence/` (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/Plans/EvidenceTreeGuardTests.cs` fails if anything is).

## Dependencies
#1708 (frozen protocol and screening record) and, through it, #1648. The sizing record from #1786. Blocks #1867 and #1712. Parent #1698.

issues.title: [0.37] Independent methods review of the protocol and the fairness check
issues.body:
## Deliverable
One record, `docs/plans/0.37-methods-review.md`, showing that the independent methods reviewer has reviewed and cleared two artifacts before #1712 starts: the frozen #1708 protocol and the #1709 fairness package. The reviewer is not chosen here. The 0.31 outreach decision (#1777, `docs/plans/0.31-outreach-decision.md`) names the reviewer in a dated entry or records the seat vacant, and this issue reads that record. If no reviewer was named, this record states the vacancy and #1712 does not start.

A *methods reviewer* checks, before any comparative run, that the design can support the conclusions it is registered to draw: the strata, the admission screening, the analysis plan, the repetitions and stated power, and whether the three conditions are comparable. *Independent* means a person who is not the maintainer, has not contributed to Calor, does not author the #1708 tasks or acceptance checks or the #1711 controls, and has no stake in the result.

The seat has been vacant on every record so far: "Vacant; no consenting person evidenced", with the review allowance "Not authorized" (`docs/plans/safe-delegation-m0/authorization.md:68-69`, 2026-09-09; also `docs/plans/safe-delegation-m0/decision.md:93` and `docs/plans/roadmap-v0.20.md:43-45`). On 2026-10-01 the maintainer substituted cross-family AI review, and that record states the substitution "is not independent human review" and satisfies no requirement that names one (`docs/plans/safe-delegation-m0/v0.23/r1-methods-governance.md:17-31`).

This issue takes no implementation capacity: its output is a record of reviews, and the fixes a review asks for are made under #1708 and #1709.

## Work
**Part 1, the reviewer.** Copy from the dated entry of the #1777 record that names the reviewer, with a link and its date: the reviewer's name and affiliation, published with their consent; the independence statement against the four conditions above; conflicts disclosed; scope (the two artifacts and nothing else); the review allowance in hours and any fee, as a ceiling; and a deadline for each review. Where that record does not state one of these, write "not recorded" and ask the maintainer for a dated entry there. This record authorises nothing: no review allowance and no collection spend.

**Vacancy.** If the #1777 record names no reviewer (reviewer outreach was declined, was left as "not decided, treated as decline until changed", or found nobody who consented), write "seat vacant" with that record's link and date, link this file from #1698 and #1867, and comment on #1712 that it does not start. The vacancy lifts only through a later dated entry on the #1777 record naming a consenting reviewer; parts 2 and 3 then run.

**What does not fill the seat.** The 2026-10-01 cross-family AI review, run under `docs/plans/safe-delegation-m0/v0.23/review-protocol.md`, is by its own record a quality control and not independent review (`review-protocol.md:7-9`), and its reviewers' competence is unmeasured beyond one planted-defect probe (`r1-methods-governance.md:65-67`). The same holds for a separate agent session working from a rubric, which is how the 0.32 replication's fairness check was done (#1813). Either may be run before the human review to catch defects early. Neither clears anything, and neither is recorded here as a review.

**Objection rules.** Reuse the severity and stopping rules of `review-protocol.md:73-95`: each objection is BLOCKING, MAJOR or MINOR; the proposer accepts it with a fixing commit or rejects it with a reason; a review clears when no BLOCKING objection is unresolved and every MAJOR one has a disposition; the maintainer may not override an unresolved BLOCKING objection. Fixes are made under #1708 or #1709, reopened if already closed.

**Parts 2 and 3, the reviews.** The reviewer receives the frozen #1708 protocol with the sizing (#1786), then the #1709 fairness package. The reviewer sees no comparative outcomes. Following `CLAUDE.md` ("Evidence and review records"), objections and dispositions go in the description of the pull request that updates this record; the record carries one line per review: reviewed commit, date, outcome, link. If a review still has an unresolved BLOCKING objection at its part 1 deadline, write "not cleared" with the open objections listed; #1712 does not start.

## Acceptance
- The file exists, and part 1 either names the reviewer, with the link to the #1777 record and the independence statement, or says "seat vacant" with that link.
- Reviewer named: parts 2 and 3 each name the reviewed commit and end either with the reviewer's statement that no blocking objection remains or with "not cleared" and the open objections. A later change to a frozen protocol value or to a condition definition is re-submitted before #1712 starts.
- Seat vacant, or a review not cleared: #1698 and #1867 link the file, #1712 carries a comment that it does not start, and no document describes AI review or an agent session as independent review.
- No paid agent run is made under this issue. Nothing is written under `docs/plans/evidence/` (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/Plans/EvidenceTreeGuardTests.cs` fails if anything is) or under `docs/plans/safe-delegation-m0/v0.23/`, the closed 0.23 record, whose Markdown files and review-file names `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/Plans/SafeDelegationV023BoundaryTests.cs` checks.

## Dependencies
#1777 (the reviewer, or the vacancy). Part 2 needs the frozen #1708 protocol; part 3 needs the #1709 package. Blocks #1867 and #1712. Parent #1698.

issues.title: [0.37] Decision: authorised collection budget
issues.body:
## Deliverable
The maintainer's decision on whether to pay for the 0.37 comparison, recorded before any paid run in `docs/plans/0.37-collection-spend-authorisation.md` and, when it authorises, registered in Annex A of `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md`. It is the only authorisation #1712 accepts and it replaces the budget-approval lines #1708 and #1712 used to carry. Filing this issue authorises no spend; only the recorded decision does. The agent assigned prepares the record; the maintainer decides.

## Work
Prepare the record on the model of `docs/plans/w4-dryrun-spend-authorisation.md` (what is and is not authorised, calibration, budget envelope, abort triggers, authorisation record) and `docs/plans/pp-w5-spend-authorisation.md`. It contains:

1. **Preconditions**, each with a link: the frozen #1708 protocol and its Annex A entry; #1865 with its per-stratum verdicts; #1857 with both reviews cleared; #1709 conditions; the #1710 zero-cost pass on every task and condition; #1711 controls validated; #1702 landed, or "no effect-boundary evidence"; the three entry criteria of #1698. If #1857 records the seat vacant or a review not cleared, options A to C below are not open: the record is D with that reason, and it cannot waive the review.
2. **The design**: tasks by stratum, conditions, repetitions, control runs. Line items that can be struck separately: the gating comparison, the #1711 controls, and the optional Rust condition (reported only; it runs only on tasks that meet both eligibility conditions in #1709, the second of which is read from the calibration stage).
3. **One pinned model** for every condition, with its availability window (`docs/plans/roadmap-v0.20.md:174-175`) and the commit pins.
4. **Projected spend** from the refreshed sizing (#1786) and per-run cost per condition from the most recent runs on the same harness and syntax (#1605, #1810 and, if it ran, #1811), read from the agent's own `total_cost_usd`, never priced by hand from token counts (`pp-w5-spend-authorisation.md:18-21`). Older reference points, all pre-0.30 syntax: at fixture scale $0.55 per run for C#, $3.93 for Calor and $1.70 for Calor with an exemplar (July 2026, model not pinned, measured by summing `total_cost_usd` over the 180 `agent.json` files under `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/e1a-attribution/`, total $370.52); at real scale $0.45 for C# and $3.47 for Calor (three calibration runs, 2026-08-03, `w4-dryrun-spend-authorisation.md:46-58`).
5. **Soft target and hard ceiling**, in dollars. Realised spend has exceeded projection by 2.8x ($92.83 against about $33, `pp-w5-spend-authorisation.md:18`, `:86`) and by about 4x ($79.39 against under $20, `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/guarantees-probe-001/VERDICT.md:20-24`), so the hard ceiling covers the projection at 4x or the record says why not. The standing per-epoch ceiling is $1,500 (`docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md:81`, marked provisional at `:57`); a higher ceiling is stated as an explicit change, or the collection is split into registered stages each under it.
6. **Abort triggers**, as numbers, on the pattern of `w4-dryrun-spend-authorisation.md:84-94`: calibration projects over the hard ceiling; realised spend reaches the hard ceiling (collection stops); the invalid-run rate after retries exceeds a stated fraction; verdicts are incoherent or held-out data leaked; the pinned model is withdrawn.
7. **Stages**: the zero-cost pass (`--null-agent`, which applies each reference solution without calling an agent) on the collection commit; a paid calibration of a stated number of runs per condition, which replaces the estimate with a measured projection and shows which tasks have headroom for the Rust line; then the collection.
8. **The reading of each outcome**, copied from the frozen #1708 protocol, per stratum, in #1698's terms (supported task class, unresolved, negative) with the proceed/narrow/revise/stop consequence for 0.38, and including "aborted" and "inconclusive at the stated power".
9. **Time limit**: the collection window, and a lapse date after which no paid run may start under this record. A lapsed authorisation is void, not extended; collection after it needs a new dated entry.
10. **Registration.** Under A, B or C, the pull request that records the decision also appends a new entry to the annex revision log (section A.3) of `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md` and moves the `Annex version` pointer at the head of the annex to it. The entry carries the design, the pinned model, both ceilings, the abort triggers, the readings and the lapse date, or names this record at a commit with its SHA-256. The `annex-freeze` job in `.github/workflows/experiment-registry-tamper-check.yml` runs `scripts/check-annex-freeze.py`, which fails a pull request that edits or removes an existing entry, so a later change is a new dated entry. Under D there is no design to register: the decline is recorded in this file and linked from #1698. If the maintainer also wants declines in the annex, the same pull request appends a one-line entry naming this record; nothing else in this issue changes.

**Options for the maintainer.**

| Option | What it costs |
|---|---|
| A. Authorise the registered design | The full ceiling. |
| B. Authorise a reduced design (fewer repetitions or tasks; a stratum #1865 found short is left out and named as not collected) | Less spend and less power. The record states, from the sizing, the smallest difference the reduced design can detect. |
| C. A or B plus the Rust line | Extra spend for a reading that decides nothing. |
| D. Decline | No spend. #1712 is closed as not planned with this record linked, #1698 records the verdict as "not collected", 0.38 and 0.39 stay held, and the #1708 to #1711 assets are kept. |

The plan recommends A when every precondition is met and the sizing shows the design can separate the registered readings; B only if the sizing shows the reduced design can still separate "Calor better than equipped C#" from "no difference" in at least one stratum; otherwise D, because a collection that can only return "unresolved" does not change the 0.38 decision. It recommends leaving the Rust line out unless #1709 lists at least one task with a process-level oracle: the 0.33 reading (#1831) already locates Rust's cost, and this line decides nothing. If #1857 recorded the seat vacant or a review not cleared, only D can be recorded, because #1712 does not start without a cleared review.

A decline does not wait for the preparation. D may be recorded as soon as #1857 records the seat vacant or a review not cleared, or whenever the maintainer decides not to pay; preconditions not yet met are then listed as "not reached", and parts 2 to 9 may be left as far as they were prepared. Options A to C need every precondition.

If no decision is recorded by the date the record sets for it, write "not decided, treated as decline until changed", so the milestone is not held. A later dated authorise entry replaces that default and reopens #1712.

## Acceptance
- Under A, B or C the file has all ten parts; every precondition has a link; ceilings and abort triggers are numbers; exactly one model id is named; the lapse date is a calendar date. Under D or the default it has part 1, with each precondition linked or marked "not reached", and the decision line.
- The decision line gives the option, the date and the maintainer's words, and under A, B or C its commit is an ancestor of the commit that records the first paid run.
- Under A, B or C: Annex A of `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md` has a new revision-log entry for this record, and the `annex-freeze` job passed on the pull request that added it.
- Under D or the default: #1712 is closed as not planned with the record linked, and #1698 carries "not collected".
- #1698 links the record.

## Dependencies
For an authorise outcome: #1865 and #1857, the refreshed sizing (#1786, `docs/plans/0.37-sizing-and-budget-request.md`), and #1708 to #1711 complete. A decline needs none of them. Blocks #1712. Parent #1698.

issues.title: [0.38] Epic: earn greater autonomy
issues.body:
**Current**

The epic asks whether bounded implementation search and evidence-assisted review produce additional accepted improvements economically, and whether accepted change scope can grow without proportional human supervision. It extends the three 0.37 authoring conditions with and without search (six conditions) through five children, #1713 to #1717. Toward 0.37 it says only to use #1698 findings to select or reject the task class and that "A negative 0.37 result requires an explicit revised hypothesis, not automatic progression"; it has no entry criterion, says nothing for a verdict that was never collected or for the case where no external maintainer consented, and does not state when the milestone is finished.

**Amendment**

Replace the body with the text under "Epic body" above. The title does not change. Against the current body the replacement changes these places and nothing else:

1. A new section, `## Entry criteria and hold rule`, between `## Outcome` and `## Work breakdown`.
2. `## Work breakdown`: "task selection and a six-condition protocol" becomes "task selection, a six-condition protocol and the maintainer's decision on its cost limits and spend".
3. A new section, `## Exit record`, between `## Acceptance` and `## Dependencies and decision`.
4. `## Dependencies and decision`: the sentence "A negative 0.37 result requires an explicit revised hypothesis, not automatic progression." is replaced by the sentence that begins "A negative, unresolved or uncollected 0.37 result"; the list of dependency edges after the paragraph is new.
5. `## Authorization`: everything after the first sentence is new.
6. `## Sequencing and decision gate`: the first bullet is replaced (it read "#1713 consumes #1712's verdict before approving a search task class and collection protocol."); in the third bullet "a separately authorized budget" becomes "the collection authorisation recorded under #1713".

When the plan is applied, replace each `NEW-NN-xx` placeholder in the body with the issue number it was filed under.

**Why**

Milestones 0.36 to 0.39 are gated on an external maintainer nobody has been authorised to recruit (no permitted contacts, no outreach window and "Contacts made: 0" in `docs/plans/safe-delegation-m0/v0.23/r2a-adopter-unavailable.md:25-30`; "DEMAND UNPROVEN" in `docs/plans/call-w-adjudication.md:28`), so 0.38 needs a hold written in advance and its dependency edges written into the epic. The current body covers one of the three ways the 0.37 verdict can fail to be positive, a negative result; it is silent on a verdict that was never collected (the decline branch of #1867) and on the no-adopter fallback. The fallback table is cited from the plan of record instead of restated, so there is one copy to keep current. The exit record is added because the 0.38 exit criterion is "one of the three exit records #1699 defines is posted" and the current body defines none; it has a declined-budget branch because an exit that depends on a spend decision needs a written outcome for a decline.

issues.title: [0.38] Approve the bounded-search task class, six-condition protocol, and cost limits
issues.body:
**Current**

The issue asks for a small prospective extension of 0.37: consume #1712's verdict and select the supported task class; define six conditions (conventional C#, semantically equipped C# and Calor, each with and without search); fix candidate, time, inference, build, solver and benchmark limits, stopping rules, winner selection on development data, held-out evaluation and economic acceptance before outcomes are observed; and preserve #1702 authority. Its acceptance asks for approved task cards, a total-cost definition, a "small dry-run plan" and an explicit "collection authorization" that "names budget and authorized scope separately", or a recorded stop/redirect. It does not say where that authorisation is recorded, what it must fix or what follows a decline, and its first Work bullet lets a negative or unresolved 0.37 result go forward through "a revised hypothesis" and "explicit approval before expensive implementation or collection".

**Amendment**

The title does not change. Five edits.

1. Append to `## Deliverable`:

```markdown
This issue is also the registration-and-spend decision for 0.38. The maintainer decides two things, recorded in `docs/plans/0.38-collection-spend-authorisation.md`: whether the protocol is approved, and whether paid collection is authorised. The agent assigned prepares the record; the maintainer decides. Filing or amending this issue authorises no spend; only the recorded collection authorisation does.
```

2. In `## Work`, replace the first bullet ("Consume #1712's verdict. Select the supported task class; if the prior result is negative or unresolved, ...") with:

```markdown
- Start when the entry criterion is recorded on #1699: a comment there that links #1712's published verdict and names the supported task class. Consume that verdict and select the task class it names, or a subset. If the prior result is negative, unresolved or not collected, the milestone is held under #1699: this issue stays open and unapproved, and it may record a revised hypothesis or a stop/redirect. Approval of a revised hypothesis does not start implementation or collection. If the maintainer records on #1699 that the epic will not be pursued, close this issue as not planned with that record linked.
```

3. In `## Work`, append:

```markdown
- Write the decision record, `docs/plans/0.38-collection-spend-authorisation.md`, on the model of `docs/plans/w4-dryrun-spend-authorisation.md` (what is and is not authorised, calibration, budget envelope, abort triggers, authorisation record) and `docs/plans/pp-w5-spend-authorisation.md`. Before any paid agent run it fixes:
  1. **Spend ceiling.** A soft target and a hard ceiling in dollars that count every candidate (one implementation attempt produced during search) in every condition, not only winners. Project spend from the per-run cost per condition in #1712's published spend, read from the agent's own `total_cost_usd` and never priced by hand from token counts (`docs/plans/pp-w5-spend-authorisation.md:18-21`), multiplied by the candidate limit. Realised spend in this program has exceeded projection by 2.8x ($92.83 against about $33, `docs/plans/pp-w5-spend-authorisation.md:18`, `:86`) and by about 4x ($79.39 against under $20, `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/guarantees-probe-001/VERDICT.md:20-24`), so the hard ceiling covers the projection at 4x or the record says why not. The standing per-epoch ceiling is $1,500 (`docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md:81`, marked provisional at `:57`); a higher ceiling is stated as an explicit change, or the collection is split into registered stages each under it. The agent client's `--max-budget-usd` flag is an estimate with no verified overshoot bound (`bench/phase0-agent-native/README-ppw-spending.md:25-27`, `:35-36`), so the record states how spend by candidates already running is bounded, or reports it as unknown.
  2. **Abort triggers**, as numbers, on the pattern of `docs/plans/w4-dryrun-spend-authorisation.md:84-94`: a calibration stage projects over the hard ceiling; realised spend reaches the hard ceiling; the invalid-run rate after retries exceeds a stated fraction; verdicts are incoherent, or held-out data reached a candidate workspace; the pinned model is withdrawn.
  3. **Zero-cost pass.** `--null-agent`, which applies each task's reference solution without calling an agent (`bench/phase0-agent-native/run-pair.sh:13-15`), on every task in all six conditions on the collection commit, with the fake driver of #1714 (a stand-in for the agent that returns scripted candidates and makes no paid call) supplying candidates in the three search conditions. No paid run starts until it passes. At HEAD `bc80daeb` the runner accepts only two arms, `calor` and `csharp` (`bench/phase0-agent-native/run-pair.sh:282`; an arm is the language setup a run uses); the six conditions run through the arm abstraction of #1827 as #1710 and #1714 extend it.
  4. **One pinned model** for all six conditions: exactly one model id, with its availability window and the commit pins. The six conditions are the three 0.37 authoring conditions with and without search; the optional Rust condition #1709 may carry in 0.37 is not among them. If the pinned model is not the one #1712 used, the three no-search conditions are rerun concurrently or the limitation is stated, as the second Work bullet requires.
  5. **The reading of each outcome**: what each outcome will be taken to mean, written before any paid run, in the terms of #1717's decision (expand, narrow, revise, stop). It covers search against no search within each condition, Calor plus search against semantically equipped C# plus equivalent search, "aborted", and "inconclusive at the stated power".
  6. **Decision date**: the date by which the collection authorisation is decided.
- Put the decision to the maintainer as two lines in that record, each with the option taken, the date and the maintainer's words. **Protocol approval** releases #1714, #1715 and #1716. **Collection authorisation** is the only authorisation for a paid run in 0.38, and #1717 requires it. The options:

  | Option | What it costs |
  |---|---|
  | A. Approve the protocol and authorise the collection | Up to the hard ceiling, plus the work of #1714 to #1716. |
  | B. Approve the protocol and authorise a reduced design (fewer tasks, repetitions or candidates per task; the comparison of Calor plus search with semantically equipped C# plus search is kept) | Less spend and less power. The record states which readings the reduced design can no longer separate. |
  | C. Approve the protocol and defer the collection authorisation to the decision date | The work of #1714 to #1716 is done before the spend is known to be available. |
  | D. Decline the collection | No spend. #1717 and whichever of #1714 to #1716 are still open are closed as not planned with this record linked, merged work is kept, and #1699 records the comparison as "not collected". |
  | E. Stop or redirect: no justified task or hypothesis remains | No spend and no build. #1714 to #1717 are closed as not planned and #1699 exits on this record. |

  The plan recommends deciding both lines together, A or B, when the projection at the candidate limit fits the hard ceiling and the run-to-run variability #1712 published shows the design can separate the registered readings; C only when per-candidate cost cannot be projected until #1714 exists; otherwise D, because a runner built for a collection that is never paid for produces no result. If the decision date passes with no collection decision, write "not decided, treated as decline until changed" on that line, so the milestone is not held open. A later dated authorise entry replaces that default.
- Register the approved protocol. The pull request that records the protocol approval also appends a new entry to the annex revision log (section A.3) of `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md` and moves the `Annex version` pointer at the head of the annex to it. The entry carries the task class, the six conditions, the limits, the stopping and selection rules, the pinned model, both ceilings, the abort triggers and the readings, or names the decision record at a commit with its SHA-256.
```
