The `annex-freeze` job in `.github/workflows/experiment-registry-tamper-check.yml` runs `scripts/check-annex-freeze.py`, which fails a pull request that edits or removes an existing entry, so a later change, a deferred collection authorisation included, is a new dated entry. A decline or a stop/redirect registers nothing: it is recorded in the decision record and linked from #1699.

4. In `## Acceptance`, replace the third bullet ("A small dry-run plan validates feasibility without implying authorization for paid calls. Explicit collection authorization names budget and authorized scope separately.") with:

```markdown
- `docs/plans/0.38-collection-spend-authorisation.md` exists and contains: a hard ceiling and abort triggers as numbers; exactly one model id; the zero-cost pass as a command; a reading for each outcome, "aborted" and "inconclusive" included; a decision date; and the two decision lines. The collection authorisation names the budget and the authorised scope separately. The dry-run plan implies no authorisation for paid calls.
- Under A, B or C: Annex A of `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md` has a new revision-log entry for the protocol, and the `annex-freeze` job passed on the pull request that added it. When the collection is authorised (A or B, at once or after C), the commit of that authorisation is an ancestor of the commit that records the first paid run in #1717.
- Under D, the dated default or E: the issues the option names are closed as not planned with the record linked, and a comment on #1699 links the record as the milestone's exit record.
- This issue closes when both lines carry a decision. Under C it stays open until the collection line is decided or the default is written.
```

5. In `## Dependencies`, replace "Protocol drafting can begin earlier; execution cannot." with:

```markdown
Protocol drafting can begin earlier, as text only. Approval waits for the entry criterion recorded on #1699. #1714, #1715 and #1716 start on the protocol approval; no paid run starts without the collection authorisation.
```

**Why**

This issue is the only place 0.38 decides to spend money, and its body named neither the record, the pinned model, the readings nor an outcome for a decline. A paid agent run needs the first three fixed before it starts, and a spend gate with no decline branch cannot sit under the milestone's exit criterion, which is why the decision is filed with its options written out. The first Work bullet read as a second way into 0.38 after a negative verdict, which contradicts the entry criterion #1699 now carries: after such a verdict 0.38 is held.

issues.title: [0.38] Implement bounded candidate search with cancellation and complete cost accounting
issues.body: Delivers a minimal search extension of #1710's runner, usable in every approved condition: candidate generation, development validation, selection and stopping as #1713 fixes them; bounds on candidate count, wall time, inference spend, build and solver effort and benchmark work, with budget reserved before each additional candidate; cancellation, timeouts and resumption with durable accounting; and the cost of every candidate recorded, not only the winner's. It stays in 0.38 unchanged because it implements #1713's approved protocol on top of the 0.37 runner, starts only on the protocol approval recorded under #1713 (so not while #1699 is held), and already has acceptance that can be checked with no paid call (fake-driver tests for budget exhaustion before and after dispatch, cancellation, timeout, invalid candidate, no acceptable candidate, interrupted and resumed runs, and unavailable cost reporting). Leads at HEAD `bc80daeb`: `bench/phase0-agent-native/run-pair.sh` runs one pair in one arm per invocation (`:6`), with a per-run wall-clock limit read from the pair's `pair.json` (`timeoutSeconds`, default 600, `:396-398`) and enforced by `timeout` or a polling watchdog (`:1384`, `:1404-1407`). The word "candidate" does not occur in it, it has no handler for user cancellation (its three `trap`s only remove temporary directories and a telemetry lock, `:567`, `:1049`, `:1799`), and it does not resume an interrupted run: the nearest mechanism is a starting run index that keeps a later invocation from overwriting earlier runs (`:173-176`). The harness unit tests live in `bench/phase0-agent-native/tests/` and run with no paid call in the `calor-first-guard` job (`.github/workflows/test.yml:122-125`), which is where the fake-driver tests belong; a test added to a .NET test project instead changes that project's `expectedTotal` in `eng/test-manifest.json`, which `scripts/check_trx.py` enforces in CI. The spend-reservation code in the tree was built for the paused PP-W-rows research and carries its name: `bench/phase0-agent-native/ppw-spending.py`, reached from `run-pair.sh:1368-1380` only when `--ppw-spend-ticket` is passed (`:229-230`). Its README records that the client's `--max-budget-usd` is an estimate with no verified overshoot bound, so the hard maximum is "unknown" (`bench/phase0-agent-native/README-ppw-spending.md:14-40`), and the request-reserving gateway is under an operational hold with $51.04 of unresolved exposure (`bench/phase0-agent-native/README-ppw-gateway.md:8-14`). #1714 may reuse that design knowledge for its own overshoot reporting; consistent with #1710 (do not fork the paused PP-W experiment) and #1717 (do not borrow its budget or history), it does not reuse the PP-W tickets, ledger or history.

issues.title: [0.38] Independently validate candidates and prevent held-out benchmark overfitting
issues.body: Delivers an independent final validation path for #1714's candidates: the development tests and benchmarks used during search kept apart from protected held-out acceptance and representative performance inputs; the submitted candidate built through trusted configuration, with proofs, behaviour checks and #1703-style evidence bound to the exact accepted artifact; unauthorised changes to obligations, approval policy, harness, benchmark configuration or workload rejected through #1702's controls; and explicit handling of held-out reuse and of selection bias across many candidates. It stays in 0.38 unchanged because every input it names is produced earlier in the plan (#1713 and #1714 in this epic; #1702, #1703 and #1704 in 0.36), nothing in this plan changes its scope, and it starts on the protocol approval recorded under #1713. Leads at HEAD `bc80daeb`: the pair runner already builds its held-out suite (tests the agent never sees) outside the agent's workspace (`bench/phase0-agent-native/run-pair.sh:727`, `:780-783`) and runs it silently after every build or test (`:20-23`), but that suite is the pair's own committed `tests/*.cs`, the same for every iteration of every run, so there is no development and held-out split to reuse and the separation is new work; what stops an agent reading those files in the checkout is the arm isolation of #1762 (0.31). The compiler's existing obligation comparison is `calor verify <frozen.calr> <final.calr> --weakening-check <declaration-id>`, which looks the declaration up among module-level functions only (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/VerifyCommand.cs:765-766`) and compares parameter refinements and postconditions, not effect rows (`:768-773`); class members and effect rows are outside it. Closing that gap belongs to #1702, whose command that classifies a base-to-head change this issue consumes instead of building a second comparison.

issues.title: [0.38] Evaluate staged evidence-assisted review and independent defect detection
issues.body:
**Current**

The issue asks for a bounded review study that compares conventional implementation review with evidence-assisted review, and evidence-led review only where entry criteria justify it. Reviewers are blinded to injected defects drawn from #1711's controls, public obligation changes are presented separately from implementation evidence, all effort is recorded, body inspection stays available with no penalty, and detection is reported separately for implementation, specification and boundary defects. It names no existing tool that produces the evidence a reviewer would be shown.

**Amendment**

The title does not change. Two edits; the second is independent of the first and may be struck without affecting it.

1. In `## Work`, append one bullet:

```markdown
- Before designing the evidence a reviewer is shown, inspect the existing `calor review-packet` command (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/ReviewPacketCommand.cs`, built by `src/Calor.Compiler/Reporting/ReviewPacketBuilder.cs`; tests in `tests/Calor.Verification.Tests/ReviewPacketTests.cs`). It already assembles a per-change report that leads with the unproven remainder, lists assumptions, discloses waivers and lists callers of the changed declarations; it takes `--baseline-ref` to derive the changed declarations from a git diff and emits JSON with `--json`. Use or extend it for the evidence-assisted stage; if it is not used, the study record says why.
```

2. In `## Dependencies`, replace "paid or participant execution requires explicit authorization." with:

```markdown
a paid agent run requires the collection authorisation recorded under #1713 (`docs/plans/0.38-collection-spend-authorisation.md`) and runs under that record's spend ceiling, abort triggers and pinned model; participant execution requires that record to name it in its authorised scope.
```

**Why**

The evidence an evidence-assisted reviewer would be handed already has a generator at HEAD `bc80daeb`: `calor review-packet` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/ReviewPacketCommand.cs:10-17`, `:69-70`; 12 tests in `tests/Calor.Verification.Tests/ReviewPacketTests.cs`), and without the pointer an agent could build a second presentation beside it. The study apparatus itself is still new work: a keyword search of `bench/`, `scripts/`, `src/` and `tests/` (outside `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/`) finds no reviewer blinding and no capture of review effort. The Dependencies edit names where the "explicit authorization" the body already requires is recorded, since #1713 is the one place 0.38 authorises spend. Nothing else changes. Its rule that body inspection is never penalised matches what the repository already recorded (`docs/plans/machine-zone.md:108` calls the earlier body-reads metric gameable, with "zero achievable by complacency"; `:122` records that forbidding body reads removes the channel through which reviewers notice specification errors), and its last Acceptance bullet already covers the case that no independent reviewer is available (`docs/plans/roadmap-v0.20.md:36-45` records no secured adopter and no agreed external methods reviewer).

issues.title: [0.38] Run the approved search comparison and publish the autonomy decision
issues.body:
**Current**

The issue runs the six approved conditions within budgets and stopping rules fixed in advance and publishes an owned expand/narrow/revise/stop decision on whether search and greater agent freedom improve accepted engineering outcomes for the selected task class. Its entry criteria list the #1713 protocol, a "separately authorized budget", the #1714 runner, #1715 validation, #1716 review controls and "the prior #1712 proceed/narrow/revise decision". It does not say where the budget authorisation is recorded, and it admits a `revise` decision, under which the milestone is held.

**Amendment**

The title does not change. Three edits.

1. Replace the `## Entry criteria` section with the text below. Against the current section it changes two phrases ("separately authorized budget" and "proceed/narrow/revise decision") and adds the sentence on a decline:

```markdown
## Entry criteria
#1713 approved protocol and the collection authorisation recorded under #1713 (an authorise outcome in `docs/plans/0.38-collection-spend-authorisation.md`); #1714 tested runner; #1715 independent validation; #1716 review controls; and the prior #1712 proceed or narrow decision, recorded as the entry criterion on #1699. If the #1713 record carries a decline, the dated default "not decided, treated as decline until changed" included, close this issue as not planned with that record linked; #1699 then records the comparison as "not collected". Do not silently resume PP-W research or borrow its budget/history.
```

2. In `## Work`, insert as the first bullet:

```markdown
- Make paid runs only under the #1713 decision record: its spend ceiling, its abort triggers, its one pinned model and the readings it wrote in advance for each outcome. On the collection commit, run the zero-cost pass (`--null-agent`, which applies each task's reference solution without calling an agent) on every task in all six conditions before the first paid run. When an abort trigger fires, stop and publish what was collected as "aborted"; the budget is not topped up inside this issue. Filing or amending this issue authorises no spend. Large run outputs go in workflow artifacts, not under `docs/plans/evidence/` (`CLAUDE.md`, "Evidence and review records").
```

3. In `## Acceptance`, append:

```markdown
- State which of the readings written in advance in the #1713 decision record the result matched. Publish the results and the decision in the 0.38 release notes and enter them in the evidence ledger (#1774). `docs/benchmarking/results.md` is generated and is not edited by hand.
```

**Why**

A `revise` decision from #1712 holds 0.38 under the entry criterion on #1699, so the entry criteria may not list it. #1713 is now the one place the 0.38 spend is decided, so this issue names that record, applies the paid-run rule it fixes, states the outcome of a decline, and publishes where the plan publishes agent results. This is the row the 0.38 exit reaches through #1699 (exit record 1). Its instruction not to resume PP-W research refers to the four issues in the tracker milestone "PP-W-rows research (paused)" (#1254, #1262, #1267, #1436), which #1648 decides in 0.31, and to the spending ledger and gateway described in `bench/phase0-agent-native/README-ppw-spending.md` and `bench/phase0-agent-native/README-ppw-gateway.md`.

issues.title: [0.39] Epic: scale demonstrated value
issues.body:
**Current**

The epic asks for the next capability justified by external pilot demand and measured outcomes, through three children: an investment decision (#1718), a conditional native-deployment spike (#1719), and delivery with external validation (#1720). Its gates are all inside the epic (#1720 is unscheduled until #1718 records a selection; #1719 needs an explicit go); toward earlier milestones it says only "Consume #1697/#1698/#1699 results as available; do not treat negative results as a delivery mandate". It has no entry criterion, says nothing for a 0.37 verdict that was never collected, for the case where no external maintainer consented, or for a pilot that has ended, and lists acceptance items without the records on which the milestone closes.

**Amendment**

Replace the body with the text under "Epic body" above. The title does not change. The new body differs from the current one in the three places quoted below; every other line is unchanged. When the plan is applied, replace each `NEW-NN-xx` placeholder in the body with the number the issue was filed under.

1. Insert one new section between `## Outcome` and `## Work breakdown`:

```markdown
## Entry criteria and hold rule
This milestone is entered only when both entry criteria below are met. Until then it is held: its issues stay open in the 0.39 milestone and only what "While held" allows may be done. The order of milestones, the fallback for the case that no external maintainer consents, and the cases "0.37 verdict not collected" and "0.37 verdict not positive" are written in advance in the plan of record, `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md` (#1765); this epic cites that document and does not restate its fallback table.

**Entry criteria.** Both are read from published records and are not re-judged here.

1. **The 0.37 verdict is positive.** Both must hold:
   - #1712 is closed and its language investment verdict comes from a comparison that was collected: the collection budget decision (#1867) was authorised, and the run was the full 0.37 comparison, not the fallback scope.
   - The verdict names at least one task class in which Calor added value beyond semantically equipped C#, that is, C# given comparable explicit specifications and validation, the single gating comparator of 0.37.

   #1712 also records a proceed, narrow, revise or stop decision for 0.38. That decision governs the entry of #1699 (0.38) and is not read here. This milestone may therefore be entered while 0.38 is in progress, or while 0.38 is held because that decision was `revise` or `stop` or because the task class with demonstrated value is not one 0.38 could search.
2. **The pilot is continuing.** The component accepted under #1697 (0.36) is still maintained as Calor source by a named maintainer outside the project: its `.calr` files are the maintained source, the generated C# is build output, and the component has not been permanently exported to maintained C# (the export #1707 documents; a temporary emergency fork under #1707's rules is not an export). The external maintainer says so in a dated statement that is no older than the #1712 verdict. Maintenance by Calor's creator does not meet this criterion (#1701).

When both hold, record it in one comment on this epic that links the verdict, names the task class and links the external maintainer's statement. That comment releases #1718. It selects no investment and authorises no spend.

The pilot is an entry criterion because every child needs it: #1718 is accepted only when a named external maintainer confirms the need, #1719 opens only on a named external pilot's blocking requirement, and #1720 is accepted only when the named maintainer uses and accepts the capability in an externally maintained component.

**Hold rule.** In each of the following cases the milestone stays held, and the case is recorded in a comment on this epic with a link to the record that establishes it:

- **(a) The adopter fallback applies.** The adopter checkpoint at the close of 0.33 (#1833) recorded "demand unproven" instead of the consent of a named external maintainer, or the outreach decision (#1777) was declined, or left at its default line "not decided, treated as decline until changed", and the plan of record holds this milestone from that date. The fallback table in the plan of record holds 0.39. Nothing published under the fallback's 0.37 scope meets criterion 1, and with no pilot criterion 2 cannot be met.
- **(b) The verdict was not collected.** The collection budget decision (#1867) recorded a decline, in any of the forms that issue defines, so #1712 did not run and #1698 records the verdict as not collected.
- **(c) The verdict is not positive.** #1712 published a verdict that names no task class in which Calor added value beyond equipped C#: it is negative or unresolved for every task class. Its decision for 0.38 does not settle this case: a `revise` or `stop` for 0.38 beside a task class with demonstrated value still meets criterion 1.
- **(d) The pilot is not continuing.** The external maintainer has withdrawn, the component has been permanently exported to maintained C#, or the statement criterion 2 asks for has not been given.

**While held.**
- #1719 and #1720 do not start. No implementation, native prototype, participant work or paid work happens under this epic.
- #1718 stays open with no decision recorded. Its body allows evidence gathering and user interviews before its final decision. Under the hold, drafting from results that are already published is text only and may proceed. An interview is contact with a person outside the project: it takes place only with the pilot's external maintainer while the pilot is continuing, or with a contact the outreach decision (#1777) authorised.
- A hold is not the stop, narrow or redirect that #1718 may record. That decision is made inside an entered milestone, from a positive verdict and observed pilot demand. A held milestone is reported as held, with its case and record, and never as an investment decision or a delivery.
- Work outside this epic is unaffected: existing correctness and stabilization work continues (Non-goals).

**Lifting or ending the hold.** The hold lifts only when both entry criteria are recorded. In case (a) that first requires the 0.36 hold to lift, which needs a later dated entry by Calor's maintainer on the #1833 record that names a consenting external maintainer (see #1697), and then 0.36 and the full 0.37 comparison to complete. In case (b) it requires the collection budget to be authorised later and #1712 to run. In case (c) it requires a further comparison under the 0.37 protocol (#1708), with its own budget decision, to publish a positive verdict; the plan of record schedules none, so it would be filed as new work. In case (d) it requires a named maintainer outside the project to resume or take over maintenance of the component, with consent and source ownership recorded as #1701 requires. The hold has no timer. If Calor's maintainer decides this epic will not be pursued (a negative verdict from #1712, or the end of the pilot, is the occasion to decide), close the epic and its open children as not planned and link the record that caused the hold.

**Exit.** Once entered, the milestone exits on exactly one of three records. The record is posted as a comment on this epic and entered in the evidence ledger, the repository's list of published and adjudicated results (#1774):

1. **Delivered.** #1720 is closed as completed: the named maintainer used and accepted the selected capability against the criteria recorded before implementation, and the results, costs and the expand/narrow/redirect/stop recommendation are published in the release notes of the 0.39 release. The Acceptance items below are met.
2. **No investment selected.** #1718 is closed with a recorded stop, narrow or redirect because no useful investment was supported (the third Acceptance bullet of #1718), and #1720 is closed as not planned with that decision linked.
3. **Stopped before delivery.** #1718 selected an investment and the investment was stopped before useful delivery; #1720 is closed as not planned and the outcome is reported in the release notes of the 0.39 release (the fourth Acceptance bullet of #1720).

In all three, #1719 is closed either with its published continue/stop/alternative decision or as not planned with the #1718 decision linked. Records 2 and 3 are honest investment decisions, not a shipped capability. A held milestone has not exited.
```

2. In `## Dependencies and conditional completion`, keep the existing paragraph and append after it:

```markdown
A negative, unresolved or uncollected 0.37 verdict does more than withhold a mandate: it holds this milestone under the hold rule above. The 0.38 result is consumed as available, in whatever form exists when #1718 decides: the exit record #1699 defines (#1717's published decision, or the record that closed 0.38 without one), or, while 0.38 is in progress or held, that state as recorded on #1699. This milestone does not wait for 0.38.

Dependency edges ("A → B" reads "A must complete before B"):

Into the epic:
- #1777 (outreach decision) → #1833 (adopter checkpoint) → #1697 (0.36 pilot accepted) → #1712 (0.37 verdict) → the exit record of #1698 → entry criterion 1.
- #1701 (named external maintainer, component and source ownership) and the #1697 exit record → entry criterion 2.
- #1697 pilot findings (#1706 improvement and costs, #1707 recovery) and the #1712 verdict → #1718.
- #1705 (0.36) → #1719: the support matrix and deployment checks #1705 publishes are the supported .NET deployment, Native AOT included where the pilot application is compatible, against which #1719's entry criteria reproduce the limitation.

Inside the epic:
- Entry criteria recorded on this epic → #1718.
- #1718 → #1720 in every case. #1718 → #1719 only when #1718 explicitly authorises and funds the native investigation; otherwise #1719 is closed as not planned.
- #1719 → #1720 only when the selected path needs the native experiment.

Out of the epic:
- None. No issue in the plan of record depends on this epic.

Not an edge:
- 0.38. #1718 reads whichever 0.38 record exists when it decides and does not wait for #1699 or #1717.
- The Rust cost reading of 0.33 (#1831) measures Rust as a language an agent writes, and it is reported, never adjudicated. #1719 names Rust only as something the compiler might emit. That reading is neither an entry criterion nor a success criterion of #1719.
```

3. In `## Conditional work and delivery gate`, replace the first bullet ("#1718 selects one investment using #1712/#1717 results and external pilot demand. These alternatives are not parallel commitments.") with the first bullet below, and insert the second bullet after the existing #1720 bullet ("#1720 remains unscheduled until ..."):

```markdown
- The entry criteria are recorded on this epic first. #1718 then selects one investment using the #1712 verdict, whichever 0.38 record exists (the exit record of #1699, or its recorded state while 0.38 is in progress or held) and external pilot demand. These alternatives are not parallel commitments. The decision is published as a document under `docs/plans/` (precedents: `docs/plans/call-w-adjudication.md`, `docs/plans/safe-delegation-m0/decision.md`) and linked from a comment on #1718; nothing is added under `docs/plans/evidence/`.
- When #1720 is updated with the selected deliverable, it states how the deliverable meets the planning rules of the plan of record, `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md` (#1765). Three apply here. Paid agent runs: a written spend ceiling, abort triggers, a zero-cost dry pass (`--null-agent`, which applies a reference solution instead of calling an agent), one pinned model and a reading written in advance for each outcome; filing or updating an issue authorises no spend. Breaking changes: under the compatibility promise that the edition declaration (#1805) publishes, existing spellings do not change; additive syntax is allowed, and a breaking change made despite that ships with a rewriter that migrates fixtures, benchmark pairs and documentation in the same change. New or tightened hard errors: the conversion scorecard's native count (files converted to Calor) and the density ratio (Calor tokens over C# tokens) do not regress, and the number of files that newly fall to whole-file preservation (kept as their original C#) is reported.
```

**Why**

Milestones 0.36 to 0.39 are gated on an external maintainer nobody has been authorised to recruit. The last gate record lists no permitted contacts, no outreach window and "Contacts made: 0" (`docs/plans/safe-delegation-m0/v0.23/r2a-adopter-unavailable.md:25-30`), the last adjudicated demand record is "DEMAND UNPROVEN" (`docs/plans/call-w-adjudication.md:28`), and naming an external adopter is a decision the maintainer reserved (`docs/plans/call-s-adjudication.md:187-190`). The current body is silent on a verdict that was never collected, on the no-adopter fallback and on a pilot that has ended, although each child's acceptance names an external maintainer and cannot be met without one; the amendment writes the hold and the dependency edges in advance and cites the fallback table from the plan of record instead of restating it. The exit paragraph is added because the 0.39 exit criterion reads "The selected capability delivered, or an investment decision or stop recorded, as #1700 defines" and the current body defines no closing record; its three records are taken from the children's own Acceptance bullets. The planning-rules bullet sits in the epic because the deliverable of #1720 is unknown until #1718 decides. Rust is a reported cost reading in 0.33; the "not an edge" line keeps that reading apart from #1719, where Rust appears only as a possible emission target.

issues.title: [0.39] Select one customer-backed investment and publish alternatives and stop criteria
issues.body:
**Current**

The issue asks for an owned investment decision, confirmed by a named external maintainer, that selects one bounded capability from pilot demand and measured results or records a stop, narrow or redirect, with the baseline, cost ceiling, acceptance criteria, rejected alternatives and counterevidence, and with the native spike (#1719) either authorised or marked not planned. Its first Work bullet synthesises the #1697 findings, the #1712 language verdict and the "#1717 search/autonomy verdict", and its Dependencies line requires "#1712 and #1717 conclusions for the final decision", so as written the decision waits for #1717 to publish.

**Amendment**

The title does not change. In `## Dependencies`, replace the first sentence ("#1712 and #1717 conclusions for the final decision; #1697 pilot findings.") with the text below. The two sentences after it ("Evidence gathering and user interviews may proceed earlier. Parent #1700.") stay.

```markdown
The #1712 verdict for the final decision, and #1697 pilot findings. For 0.38, read whichever record exists when the decision is made, in place of a #1717 decision: the exit record #1699 defines, or, while 0.38 is in progress or held, that state as recorded on #1699. Name the record read, with a link, in the decision; the "#1717 search/autonomy verdict" in the first Work bullet is read the same way. This decision does not wait for 0.38: 0.39 is entered on a positive #1712 verdict and a continuing pilot, as #1700 defines.
```

**Why**

The entry of 0.39 requires only a positive 0.37 verdict and a continuing pilot, so the milestone may be entered while 0.38 is in progress, or held on a `revise` or `stop` decision from #1712. 0.38 can also close without a #1717 decision, because #1699 defines exit records that leave #1717 unrun (a declined budget, for example); the current Dependencies line would make this decision wait for a record that may never exist.

issues.title: [0.39] Conditional: evaluate native deployment only against an unmet pilot requirement
issues.body: Delivers, only if #1718 explicitly selects and funds it, a bounded investigation of native deployment against one unmet pilot requirement: one representative task, an exact target OS and architecture, a budget and time cap and stop conditions approved before coding; the smallest executable slice that tests the requirement; a comparison against the best supported .NET option on equivalent hardware and workloads, losses included; the semantic gaps and the remaining runtime, library and debugging work; and a continue/stop/alternative decision. Otherwise it is closed as not planned with the #1718 decision linked. It stays in 0.39 unchanged because it is already written the way the plan requires of a conditional issue: it states the gate (an explicit go and funding), where the gate's value comes from (#1718), and what happens if the gate stays closed. The gate is a decision, so it has no numeric threshold. While #1718 is undecided, or the milestone is held under #1700, the gate is neither open nor shut: the issue stays open and no work starts. It is the only open issue that mentions Rust (tracker snapshot of 2026-11-23: one occurrence in 89 open issues, "Compare practical paths such as Rust emission or LLVM"). Rust there is something the compiler would emit. It is not a comparator, so the plan's rule that Rust is reported and never gates does not touch this issue, and the 0.33 Rust cost reading (#1831) is neither an input to it nor a reason to open it. The leads in its body are current at HEAD `bc80daeb`. `docs/semantics/normal-form.md:7-10` marks Calor Normal Form (CNF, an intermediate representation between the syntax tree and code generation) "unintegrated design", and the production path constructs `CSharpEmitter` directly (`src/Calor.Compiler/Program.cs:1207`; `docs/semantics/dotnet-backend.md:7-8`). The CNF prototype is three files under `src/Calor.Compiler/IR/` (1,517 lines, by `wc -l`). `CnfLowering` is constructed only from tests (`tests/Calor.Semantics.Tests/SemanticsTestHarness.cs:37` and three files under `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/`), it throws `NotSupportedException` for re-evaluated `for` conditions and for expression-valued callees (`src/Calor.Compiler/IR/CnfLowering.cs:269-271`, `:428`), and the specification says the prototype skips some unsupported statements and substitutes placeholders for some expressions (`docs/semantics/normal-form.md:74-77`), which is the silent dropping this issue forbids. No Rust or LLVM emitter exists: `src/Calor.Compiler/CodeGen/` holds only `CSharpEmitter.cs`, neither word occurs under `src/` (`git grep -i -w -e rust -e llvm -- src` prints nothing), and the website copy of the CNF page says Calor does not supply IL or LLVM back ends (`website/content/semantics/normal-form.mdx:34`). No tracked file sets `PublishAot` or mentions Native AOT, so the reproduction "using supported .NET deployment and Native AOT where applicable" that its entry criteria require starts from the support matrix #1705 publishes in 0.36, not from anything in the repository today.

issues.title: [0.39] Deliver the selected capability and validate external maintenance outcomes
issues.depends_on: #1718, #1719 (only if the selected path needs the native experiment)
issues.body: Delivers the one capability #1718 selected, integrated into the externally maintained pilot component and accepted by its named maintainer against criteria recorded before implementation, with the baseline and result, exact artifacts, commands, costs, interventions, supported targets and limitations published, and an expand/narrow/redirect/stop recommendation that compares the observed benefit with the investment decision. If #1718 selects nothing, or the investment is stopped before useful delivery, it is closed as not planned with that decision or outcome linked (exit records 2 and 3 of the amended epic). It stays in 0.39 unchanged because it is the row the milestone exit reaches through #1700 (exit record 1 of the amended epic), and it is already written as a conditional issue: it "remains unscheduled until that decision exists", depends on #1718's selection and approval, and depends on #1719 only if the selected path needs the native experiment. Its first paragraph requires an update before implementation (named customer and component, exact deliverable, affected surfaces, cost ceiling, deployment targets, acceptance checks, dependencies, stop conditions). That update is where the planning rules listed in #1700 are applied to the selected capability (paid runs, breaking changes, hard errors), and where the work is split into child issues if the deliverable is larger than one pull request; neither can be done before #1718 decides. The re-runs its Work lists (acceptance, installation, build and deployment, maintainer change and review, agent-unavailable recovery) reuse 0.36 assets and do not rebuild them: the #1703 evidence record, #1704 readiness, the #1705 installation, build and deployment instructions, and the #1707 recovery runbook. Published results follow the repository rule for evidence at HEAD `bc80daeb`: nothing is added under `docs/plans/evidence/`, large run outputs go in workflow artifacts, and review records go in the pull request (`CLAUDE.md:398-404`, "Evidence and review records"; `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/Plans/EvidenceTreeGuardTests.cs`).

epics.title: [0.31] Epic: tracker and plan of record re-baselined against 0.30.0
epics.body:
## Goal

Bring the tracker and the written plan into line with what 0.30.0 shipped, in one pass at the start of 0.31. After this epic every open issue has a milestone, a title, labels and a body that are true of the current compiler. The reworked 0.31–0.39 plan is in the repository in two forms: the bundle it was filed from, under `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39/`, and the plan of record, `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md`, which holds the planning rules, the dependency edges between milestones, the fallback for the case that no external maintainer is found, the capability scorecard, and a close-out checklist that keeps these current at every milestone close.

## Why

Coding agents are handed one issue each with no other context, so a stale issue is executed as written. At HEAD bc80daeb (v0.30.0) and in the tracker snapshot of 2026-11-23 (89 open issues):

- 11 open issues have no milestone (#673, #851, #875, #922, #1084, #1670, #1694, #1723, #1726, #1731, #1732). One of them, #1694, is the failing soundness sweep.
- Titles carry the wrong release or none. #1594 and #1590 say `[0.29]` and #1605 says `[0.30]`; all three are in milestone 0.31. Eight issues that have a milestone have no prefix (#709, #711, #909, #1142, #1177, #1511, #1555, #1728).
- 35 open issues have no label.
- Bodies describe the pre-0.30 compiler. #1654 says "Today `record` is `NotSupported`"; `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/FeatureSupport.cs:60-66` marks it Full. #1659 gives a baseline of 48 unsupported constructs; the registry has 58 (`grep -c "Support = SupportLevel.NotSupported"` on that file). #1555 and #1670 are written against `§` markers, each of which is lexer error Calor0006 since 0.30 (`CHANGELOG.md:28-32`).
- The reworked plan is in no file of the repository. Its rules (displacement, base rate before new guarantees, conditions on paid runs, no breaking change after the 0.32 edition), the order between milestones, and what happens to 0.36–0.39 if no external maintainer consents are written nowhere that an issue can cite.

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1759 | Apply the plan of record to the tracker: commit the plan bundle, file the new epics and issues, record the placeholder-to-number map, apply every milestone, title, label and body change to existing issues, sign off |
| #1765 | Publish the plan of record `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md` (rules, registry, dependency edges, scorecard, adopter fallback, restated assessment) and add the milestone close-out checklist to `docs/release-policy.md` |
| #673 | Close: superseded by #1652 and the 0.30 teaching work; its one live defect moves to #1772 and #1652 |
| #1555 | Close: the `§ARR` form it concerns is a lexer error in 0.30; the dead helper it names goes on the #1741 residue list |
| #1670 | Re-test on 0.30 syntax, then close, or file the remaining defect as a conditional child of #1649 |

## Sequence

1. #1759 first. Its first step commits the plan bundle, and its filing step gives every new issue the number that other issues cite. #673 and #1555 are closed as rows of its checklist.
2. #1765 after #1759, so that the plan of record cites issue numbers and not placeholders. It merges before #1777 (the adopter-outreach decision) is decided, because the decline branch of that decision applies the fallback table this document holds, and before the spend record of #1770 is signed, because a "no paid run authorised" outcome is recorded in this document as well.
3. #1670 at any point in 0.31. It may slip to 0.32 without holding the release.

## Done when

- #1759 is closed with the maintainer's sign-off comment: `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39/` holds the bundle and `placeholder-map.json`; no open issue is without a milestone; every open issue in milestones 0.31 to 0.39 except #1694 has the `[0.NN]` prefix of its milestone and at least one label; and the per-milestone open counts equal the table in #1759.
- `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md` is merged with its six sections, `docs/release-policy.md` has a `## Milestone close-out` section with seven steps that `.claude/skills/create-release/SKILL.md` links to, and `calor self-check docs` exits 0.
- #673 and #1555 are closed as not planned, with no milestone, with the comments in this epic.
- #1670 is closed with a recorded 0.30 re-test, or has moved to 0.32 with its amended body.

## Not in this epic

- The text of any amendment, rewrite or new issue outside this epic. #1759 applies text; each owning epic writes it.
- The resolution of #1728 and the retitles of #1594, #1590 and #1738 (epic #1594), and the allowlist classification (#1763, epic #1761). They are signed off in the same sitting as #1759 but their text is not here.
- The evidence ledger and the README correction (#1774, epic #1775). The plan of record links to the ledger and does not duplicate it.
- The adopter-outreach decision (#1777, epic #1776). This epic only writes the fallback that decision may apply.
- Any compiler change. The only code this epic can add is the pinning test in #1670.

epics.title: [0.31] Epic: the benchmark harness runs the 0.30 language in isolation
epics.body:
## Goal

`bench/phase0-agent-native/run-pair.sh` runs the three kinds of arm the 0.30 evaluation (#1605) needs: the 0.30 Calor arm, the pinned pre-0.30 Calor arm ("arm A") and the C# arm. It runs them from workspaces in which the agent can neither name nor read a Calor checkout, and it records the telemetry that evaluation reports. Everything in this epic is verified without a paid agent run.

## Why

The pair harness is the instrument behind every agent result this project has published. At 0.30.0 it cannot run the language it exists to measure. Paths below without a directory are under `bench/phase0-agent-native/`.

- **It cannot run a 0.30 Calor arm.** All 102 `.calr` files under `bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs/` are in the retired `§` syntax, and so is the arm check the harness builds before any agent starts (`templates/calor-arm/permissive-canary.calr`). The 0.30 lexer rejects every such file with `Calor0006`. Translated copies of 25 starters and 25 reference solutions exist under `tests/TestData/ActiveSyntax/bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs/`, but no harness script reads them.
- **Agents read the checkout.** In the July attribution epoch (`epochs/e1a-attribution`, 60 runs of the Calor arm without an exemplar, pre-0.30 syntax), 16 final messages report finding the task's reference solution in the repository and 2 say the implementation follows it (keyword scan of `agent.json`; the command is in #1762). Several name the route: "the Calor repo referenced by the csproj". The arm's project file embeds the absolute path of the repository, so creating workspaces outside the checkout, as the harness does, does not close that route.
- **The telemetry cannot support the report.** A journal entry for a diagnostic holds a code and a declaration id. Nothing is recorded for the C# arm. At HEAD the capture is also skipped for every Calor arm whose label is not exactly `calor`, which is every Calor arm of #1605.
- **CI does not exercise it.** The harness tests run in a job that builds no compiler (`.github/workflows/test.yml:124`), so the cases that drive `run-pair.sh` end to end are skipped there.

The first exit criterion of 0.31 is the publication of #1605 stage 1 (or the reduced design, or a recorded "no paid run authorised"). Stage 1 is blocked by the first three issues below. Stage 2 and the end-to-end leg do not hold the release.

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1766 | `run-pair.sh` runs the 0.30 Calor arm from the translated sources with a 0.30 arm check, and the pinned pre-0.30 arm A; `run-epoch.sh` takes an arm list and interleaves it; 25 pairs pass `--null-agent` and the nine seeded-defect pairs pass `check-probe-pair.sh` |
| #1762 | Arm isolation: staged product copy, read sandbox, pre-flight canary, log of reads outside the workspace |
| #1764 | Loop telemetry: fix flags on diagnostic entries, build diagnostics for both arms, capture for labelled arms |
| #1767 | Harness support for the delivery variants of #1605 stage 2: variant selection, no-MCP switch, primer-read log, starter-less fixtures, `calor check` journalled as an iteration |
| #1760 | Report script: failure classes, opportunity counts, first-build pass rate (defined here), dead-end rate, repeat rate, C#-habit events per form, blocked test writes |
| #1763 | Legacy-dialect allowlist, per-directory notes and a self-check |
| #1736 | End-to-end agent-task suite migrated to 0.30 (amended: counts from compiler output, the 23 verifier tests, arm-A source, neutral report) |

## Sequence

1. #1766 first. Nothing else can be tested until a 0.30 arm builds. Its arm-A parts start after the design entry of #1770 (epic #1775) is merged, and only if that entry registers arm A.
2. #1762 directly after it. Both edit `run-pair.sh` and `templates/calor-arm/CalorArm.csproj.template`.
3. #1764 after #1762, because it changes the observation path that #1762 moves out of the agent's process tree, and before the first paid run, because its fields cannot be recovered from an archive afterwards.
4. #1767 after #1764, #1770, #1773 and #1771. It gates stage 2 of #1605 only; stage 2 must publish, or be recorded on #1605 as not run, before #1823 is decided.
5. #1760 after #1764. #1763 follows #1648 where it can, lists the `W-00x` files as pending where it cannot, and must merge before #1803 (0.32) starts. #1736 has no predecessor. These three are off the 0.31 exit chain and may slip to 0.32.

## Done when

- #1766, #1762 and #1764 are closed. Together they mean: both arms of each of the 25 translated pairs pass `--null-agent` under isolation, the isolation canary fails closed, and journal records carry the new fields for every arm label.
- #1767 is closed, or closed as not planned with a link to the #1770 design entry that registered no stage 2.
- #1760, #1763 and #1736 are closed, or moved to 0.32 with a one-line reason on the issue.
- Every epoch directory added by this epic's pull requests has `mode: "--null-agent"` in its `pins.json`: no issue here ran a paid agent.

## Not in this epic

- What is run, at what n, on which model and commits, the spend ceiling and every threshold: #1770 (epic #1775).
- The evaluation itself and its report: #1605.
- `calor init` delivery options (#1773) and the primer outside MCP resources (#1771).
- A third arm (equipped C#), a spend stop in the epoch driver and the catch-channel analyzer for seeded defects: #1815.
- Follow-up with no issue: the 220 tracked `.calr.inc` fragments of the paused PP-W research (`git ls-files '*.calr.inc'`; all 220 hold retired markers) are outside the #1763 self-check, which reads `.calr` files only. #1648 classifies them in its closing record; no check enforces that class.
- Follow-up with no issue: whether an MCP `calor_compile` call after an edit counts as an iteration. The #1770 design entry states the rule; #1767 records the calls either way.
- Arm types other than `calor` and `csharp`: #1827.
- The six `W-00x` pair directories (52 files, no translated copy): #1648 decides them.
- Corrections to the teaching text before the evaluation's commit is pinned: #1772 (epic #1775). Calor0006 guidance: #1788, after the measurement.
- A CI job that runs `run-pair.sh` against a built compiler. None exists and none is added in 0.31.
- Re-validation of the harness after the 0.32 rewrite: #1807.

epics.title: [0.31] Epic: measure the 0.30 language once, including how the reference reaches the agent
epics.body:
## Goal

Publish one agent measurement of the 0.30 language: the pre-0.30 compiler against the 0.30 compiler, each against a C# arm run in the same epoch on the same pinned model, under a registration fixed before any money is spent. A second stage measures how the syntax primer reaches the agent inside a `calor init` workspace. Alongside it, publish a ledger of what the project's agent results do and do not establish, and correct the README to match.

## Why

- **Nothing has been measured with an agent on 0.30.** The release notes say so: "Diagnostic token budgets and before/after iterations-to-green are not measured yet" (`CHANGELOG.md:182`). The last measurement is from July 2026, on the pre-0.30 syntax with an unpinned model: 2.38 iterations to green against 1.00 for C#, pooled over two pairs at 30 runs per arm (`bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/e1a-attribution/VERDICT.md:13-17`).
- **The one lever with a measured effect ships behind a pointer nobody has tested.** In that epoch a syntax sheet of about 60 lines appended to the prompt removed 55% of the excess iterations (2.38 to 1.62) and cut the mean cost per run from $3.65 to $2.23 on one pair and from $4.20 to $1.17 on the other (summed from `total_cost_usd` in the archived `agent.json` files). In 0.30 the successor of that sheet, the primer (`src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/agent-syntax-exemplar.md`, 191 lines), is reachable only as the MCP resource `calor://primer`, and the file `calor init` generates tells the agent to read it. Whether agents do has never been measured.
- **#1605 as filed cannot be the exit gate.** It says it uses "no registration or freeze process", has no C# arm, requires "B is not worse than A" to close, tells the reader to revisit forms "before 0.30 ships", and is "Part of #1606", the 0.30 epic, which closed on 2026-11-22. The amended design is about 300 runs where the issue priced 180, and this program has recorded cost overruns of 2.8 times and about 4 times its estimates.
- **The measured arm would read guidance the compiler contradicts.** The teaching reference and the primer say `Contains(string)`, `Substring`, trimming, `Enumerable.Where` and `ToArray` are unknown to the effect checker and show hand-written loops; the effect manifests declare them pure, and the reference solution of one of the two penalised pairs calls `Contains(string)` from a pure function and `Substring` from one that declares only mutation and allocation.
- **The README claims what the results page disclaims.** `README.md:95` says Calor "shows measurable advantages"; `docs/benchmarking/results.md:20-23` says the same static outputs "do not establish a language, coding-agent productivity, correctness, or safety advantage".

Every sizing decision in 0.32 reads this measurement: which constructs to fix (#1645), which diagnostics get a fix (#1790), what `calor init` writes by default (#1823), the MCP budget (#1824) and which rejecting guarantees may land (#1800).

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1770 | Decision record: register the evaluation (arms, pairs, n, pins, close rule, class thresholds, delivery rule, MCP rule) and authorise or decline the spend |
| #1605 | The evaluation itself, amended: concurrent C# arm, two stages, registered readings, report venue |
| #1773 | `calor init` options to inline the primer in the agent file and to write a starter file; default unchanged |
| #1771 | The primer through `calor_help` and through a CLI command, for clients and arms without MCP resources |
| #1772 | Correct the teaching statements about effects that the manifests contradict, and the workflow steps that name an option `calor_compile` does not have |
| #1745 | Execute the teaching-reference examples in CI, not only compile them (amended: a definition of "runnable" that is not empty) |
| #1774 | Evidence ledger, README correction, and a claims check that reads `README.md` |

## Sequence

1. #1770, design half (arms, pairs, stages, thresholds). #1766, #1762 and #1767 in epic #1761 build only what it registers.
2. #1772, #1745 and #1771 merge before the 0.30 commit that #1605 pins for stage 1. Each changes what a measured arm reads or can reach, so none may land between the pin and the run. #1773 merges before the stage 2 pin.
3. #1770, spend half, before any paid run.
4. #1605 stage 1: zero-cost dry pass, collection, report. Its publication is the first 0.31 exit criterion.
5. #1605 stage 2 after #1767; it publishes, or is recorded on #1605 as not run, before #1823 is decided. It does not hold the release.
6. #1774 at any point. The #1605 rows are added to its ledger at the 0.31 close-out.
7. After the run, in 0.32, because each rewrites text the run measures: #1734, #1788, #1822.

## Done when

- The #1770 registration is merged, and its spend record carries an authorisation or a decline, before the first paid run.
- #1605 stage 1 is published with a C# arm run in the same epoch on the same pinned model, or the reduced design is published if the maintainer chose it, or the spend record carries "Declined: no paid run authorised" with the rows that read "not measured" listed and #1605 is closed on it.
- If a stage 1 epoch runs, the 0.30 commit recorded for it contains the merges the registration's pin rule names, as recommended #1772, #1745 and #1771 (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <merge> <pinned commit>` exits 0 for each).
- #1774 is merged: the ledger exists, the README paragraph is replaced, and a check that reads `README.md` runs on every pull request that changes it.
- Stage 2 and the end-to-end leg are each published, or recorded on #1605 as not run. #1773 is closed.

## Not in this epic

- Harness wiring, arm isolation, telemetry, delivery-variant support, the report script and the end-to-end suite migration: epic #1761 (#1766 to #1763, #1736).
- Acting on the results: #1645, #1790, #1788 (0.32).
- Changing the `calor init` default or any token budget constant: #1823 and #1824.
- The CI check that keeps effect statements true: #1798. Trimming the full reference: #1734.
- Modify-a-converted-module tasks: #1789, measured in the #1645 re-run.
- Other agent clients (#1820, #1651), a Rust arm (#1831) and the external anchor document (#1829).
- The seeded-defect replication with an equipped C# arm: epic #1812.
- Follow-up with no issue: a second reading when the close rule or the MCP rule of #1770 comes out not resolved. The #1645 re-run re-reads the close rule only if both penalised pairs are in its pair set (#1816 Part B), and no later run compares an MCP arm with a CLI-only arm unless #1832 lists one.

epics.title: [0.31] Epic: the proof-soundness instrument is restored
epics.body:
## Goal

The soundness sweep judges programs written in the 0.30 language again. A successor packet of generated cases in 0.30 syntax is registered, its expected verdicts are frozen from a macOS run with every changed verdict explained, and the daily job on `main` has been green for the number of consecutive runs the release rule sets for the 0.31 exit.

## Why

The soundness sweep (`bench/Calor.Soundness.Sweep`, run daily by `.github/workflows/soundness-sweep.yml`) is the only instrument that checks a "proven" result of the verifier against something independent. It generates 710 single-function cases from the packet in `tests/TestData/SoundnessSweep/`, compiles each with the compiler under test, and executes a hand-written C# rendering of the same property over a registered input domain. A *false proof* is a property the verifier reports proven while that oracle finds an input that violates it.

At HEAD `bc80daeb` the instrument does not work:

- **It is failing.** The scheduled job opened #1694 with 10 gate failures (issue body; the tracker dates it 2026-10-28). The issue has no milestone and no priority label.
- **It cannot judge 0.30 at all.** All 136 templates are in the retired syntax: 799 lines of `templates.json` contain a `§` marker (`grep -c '§'`), and so do four string literals in the generator and the harness. 0.30 makes every such marker the lexer error `Calor0006` (`CHANGELOG.md:31-32`). Reading the harness, a 0.30 compiler fails the solver-availability controls and the run stops with exit code 5 before any sweep case (`bench/Calor.Soundness.Sweep/Program.cs:91-94`). No run was inspected to confirm this.
- **Pull-request CI does not notice.** The one compiler test that checks the cases still lex and parse returns early when the front-end files differ from the v0.22.0 blobs the packet pins (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/SoundnessRegistration/SoundnessRegistrationTests.cs:134-137`). At HEAD 29 of the 31 pinned files differ, including all eight front-end files (`git hash-object` against `tests/TestData/SoundnessSweep/manifest-B1.json`).
- **Later milestones are measured by it.** #1660, #1661 and #1662 (0.35) state their results in terms of the sweep, each 0.35 verifier step on the contract and obligation engines adds controls to it, and #1697 (0.36) requires #1694 resolved before a release claim rests on it.

The work has a calendar floor that effort does not remove. The sweep runs once a day (`.github/workflows/soundness-sweep.yml:26`), so each required green run costs a day after the freeze merges. That is why this epic starts first in 0.31. It spends nothing on agent runs, and macOS runner minutes are free for this public repository (`:6-7`).

The instrument checks contract and obligation proofs. It says nothing about effect checking or null safety.

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1694 | The tracker for the failing sweep. Step 0: failure reports keep landing on it even if another issue is later given its label. Step 1: record what the scheduled runs say, before the artifact of the run named in the issue expires. Step 2: every failure fixed or dispositioned on the ported cases, until a run is fit to freeze. |
| #1769 | Decision record for the successor packet: where it lives, its slots and channels, how preconditions map now that they are parameter refinements, which rows are retired, the procedure for adding rows later, the disposition of the frozen whitelist and of the baseline manifests, and the state of the fixture between port and freeze. |
| #1781 | The port: templates, generator and harness literals in 0.30 syntax. The validity test runs on every pull request again. |
| #1778 | The registration: expected verdicts frozen from a `macos-15` run, in a reviewed pull request that classifies every changed verdict as port-only or real. |
| #1783 | The release rule: how many consecutive green daily runs the 0.31 exit needs, and the larger count for 0.35 entry, 0.36 entry and any release note that says "proven". Then the record that the 0.31 count was met. |

## Sequence

1. #1694 steps 0 and 1, immediately. The new issues of this epic do not carry the `soundness-sweep` label, which is reserved for #1694, so failure reports keep landing on #1694; step 0 makes the lookup robust by title. The artifact of the run named in #1694 is kept 30 days; for a run of 2026-10-28 that is until about 2026-11-27.
2. #1769, and with it part 1 of #1783, whose restart rule cites a command the design record names. Both are maintainer decisions recorded in `docs/plans/0.31-toolchain-and-sweep-record.md`, in the same session as the toolchain decisions of #1639.
3. #1781. The port needs the design.
4. #1694 step 2. The failures can be fixed and verified only on cases a 0.30 compiler can read.
5. #1778. The freeze command refuses a run that fails a check, so #1694 comes first.
6. #1783 part 2. Daily green runs are counted from the #1778 merge. The 0.31 release cannot be earlier than that merge plus the exit count in days.

## Done when

- The successor packet is registered and frozen (#1778 closed), and `EveryCaseIsValidCalorBeforeVerification` runs without an early return in the `tests (compiler)` check.
- #1694 is closed with a disposition for each of its failures, and no issue titled "Soundness sweep failing on main" is open.
- `docs/release-policy.md` states both run counts and the rule for when a count restarts.
- No issue other than #1694 carries the `soundness-sweep` label.
- The scheduled sweep has passed its gate on `main` for the 0.31 exit count, counted from the #1778 merge, and the counted runs are listed in `docs/plans/0.31-toolchain-and-sweep-record.md` (#1783 closed). This is the second exit criterion of 0.31.

## Not in this epic

- Re-registering the packet after the 0.32 rewrite: #1803 and #1807. The count for 0.35 entry restarts there if a case changes.
- New controls for new verifier steps: #875, #1660, #1661 and the other 0.35 issues, which use the row-addition procedure #1769 defines.
- Controls for the bug-pattern and taint analyses: #1723 and #1858 (0.35). #1769 only decides which instrument holds them.
- The end-to-end agent-task suite, the other stale instrument: #1736.
- The pilot evidence-readiness check that consumes #1694's resolution: #1704 (0.36).
- Running the harness anywhere but macOS ARM64.
- The `net10.0` output paths in `scripts/run-soundness-sweep.sh:18` and `:31`, which change only if #1639 changes the tool framework.

epics.title: [0.31] Epic: default migration yields Calor again, measured by a corpus job
epics.body:
## Goal

Default project-mode `calor migrate` (the command given a `.csproj`) no longer fails its own project check, or the build of the migrated project, because a preserved C# original is compiled as generated code (CS8669). The first project-mode native file counts for the pinned corpus projects are recorded, and a scheduled job keeps reporting, per corpus project, how many files are native and how many are preserved as C#.

## Why

Project-mode output has been measured once, by hand, in #1746 (2026-11-20, compiler 606dae6f2, o200k proxy tokenizer). MediatR and Serilog came out entirely as whole-file preserved C# (the original file kept byte for byte inside a `.calr`), which #1746 attributes to CS8669. Those two projects hold 149,211 of the 291,307 Calor tokens in that measurement (51%, summed from the #1746 table).

The documented defect is that a preserved original is compiled from a file named `*.g.cs`. The C# compiler treats such a file as generated code with nullable annotations off, so in a project with `<Nullable>enable</Nullable>` and `TreatWarningsAsErrors` every `?` annotation in it is the error CS8669 (`CHANGELOG.md:120-124`, `docs/cli/migrate.md:121-126`). At HEAD the migrator marks every file of such a project unverified and the migrated project does not build. Whether it also still drops every native file is not known; #1782 establishes that first.

Three things read migrated corpus output and are empty or wrong until this is fixed:

- **Density.** Half of the Calor tokens measured in #1746 are preserved C# from these two projects, so its ratio says little about Calor.
- **Adoption.** Per-module migration is the one workflow where agents needed no more iterations in Calor than in C# (1.0x on modifying existing Calor, against 2.7x on new code), because existing Calor is the agent's reference (`docs/plans/agent-native-strategy.md:370-373`, measured on pre-0.30 syntax). A project migrated to whole-file C# gives the agent no Calor to read.
- **Later reports.** The modify-a-converted-module pairs (#1789), the unknown-effect share (#1802), the before-and-after measurement of the 0.32 breaking-change batch (#1784), the opportunity count for the rejecting-guarantee decision (#1800), the per-project native fraction that 0.34 exits on (#1659), the guard census (#1848), the nullable-oblivious count (#1834) and the proof-status inventory (#1853) all need migrated corpus projects.

No CI job produces project-mode output. The one CI measurement of default migrate (`scripts/default_migrate_report.py`, a step of `roundtrip-verification (default)`, `.github/workflows/test.yml:1028-1034`) copies only the `*.cs` files and runs directory mode, with no project file and no references.

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1782 | Reproduce the #1746 result at HEAD, then make preserved C# originals compile under the nullable context their source file had: the project check stops reporting CS8669, the migrated MediatR and Serilog projects build, regression tests cover it, the first project-mode native counts are recorded for all three corpus projects, and what remains is handed to #1647 |
| #1779 | Scheduled corpus report job: restored working copies of MediatR, Serilog and FluentValidation migrated by default project-mode `calor migrate`, one JSON report per project, with a place for later issues to add columns |

## Sequence

1. #1782: reproduce at HEAD, fix, record the first project-mode baseline. #1779 automates the hand run it records, and #1789 takes its starter files from a project migrated after the fix.
2. #1779: the scheduled job that keeps that baseline measured. The 0.32 entry criterion reads: the #1782 baseline is recorded, and the corpus report job (#1779) is running before #1802, #1784 and #1800 start.

Neither issue is named by a 0.31 exit criterion. #1782 may follow in a 0.31.x point release and #1779 may slip into 0.32; the 0.31 release waits for neither. In 0.32, #1789 and #1647 wait for #1782, and #1647, #1746, #1802, #1784 and #1800 wait for #1779.

## Done when

- #1782 is closed. Its record in `bench/corpus/README.md` shows, for default project-mode migrate on MediatR and Serilog, no CS8669 and the native, partly preserved and whole-file preserved file counts per project, with the same counts recorded for FluentValidation. Its handover comment is posted on #1647.
- #1779 is closed: one run of the corpus report workflow on `main` has published the three reports.
- An issue that is still open when 0.31 is released carries a comment naming where it moved (a 0.31.x point release or 0.32), and this epic stays open until both are closed.

## Not in this epic

- Raising the round-trip harness floors back to their pre-0.30 values, and "give the harness project context": #1647 (0.32). Those floors fell for a different recorded cause.
- Token-ratio columns on the corpus report: #1746 (0.32). The below-1.0x target: #1844 (0.34).
- What an agent should do with a preserved file: #1822 (0.32).
- Modify-a-converted-module benchmark pairs: #1789 (0.32).
- Native conversion of constructs the converter does not support: #1659 (0.34).
- Follow-up with no issue: running each subject's own test suite against its project-mode migrated copy. #1647 judges tests on the round-trip harness legs and judges the migrated copies by their build, so the report's `tests` field stays `not-run`.

epics.title: [0.31] Epic: .NET 11 minimum (first part of #1644)
epics.body:
## Goal

A user whose machine has only the .NET 11 SDK can install `calor`, run `calor init` and `calor check`, and build a project that uses `Calor.Sdk`. The converter parses C# 15 source. The rest of .NET 11 and C# 15 support moves to 0.34.

## Why

The toolchain has moved under the project. Package managers have resolved `dotnet` to SDK 11.0.100 since 2026-11-16 (not verifiable from the repository; `dotnet --version` on a fresh install confirms it). The getting-started page asks for the ".NET 10.0 SDK or later" (`website/content/getting-started/index.mdx:38`) and the CLI's own error text says "10.0 or later" (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/ExecutionWorkspace.cs:22`). At v0.30.0 neither statement holds on a machine with only .NET 11, for four reasons found by reading the code (no CI job installs .NET 11, so nothing has been run there):

- `calor` is a `net10.0` tool with no roll-forward setting (`Directory.Build.props:4`, `src/Calor.Compiler/Calor.Compiler.csproj:28`).
- Metadata binding, which reads .NET framework assemblies to resolve types, overloads and nullability, rejects any runtime outside 10.x (`src/Calor.Compiler/Binding/Metadata/MetadataContext.cs:565-583`). The MSBuild task runs the compiler inside the build's own runtime (`src/Calor.Sdk/Sdk/Sdk.targets:51`), so this also affects every `Calor.Sdk` build under the .NET 11 SDK.
- `calor run`, `calor test` and `calor check` generate `net10.0` projects (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/ExecutionWorkspace.cs:321`, `src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/TestCommand.cs:448`).
- `calor init` writes a `tools/net10.0/any` path into the user's project (`src/Calor.Compiler/Init/CsprojInitializer.cs:183`, `:322`).

The other children of the original epic are not needed by that user, and each has a reason to wait. #1641 adds CI legs while the compiler shard is near its 40-minute limit (#1590). #1642 changes the argument layer of every command, so it lands after the paid agent collections of 0.31 to 0.33. #1643 needs a union spelling, which is decided in the 0.32 breaking window (#1797). #1640 covers effect and nullability entries for APIs that are new in .NET 11, which existing programs do not call.

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1639 | A .NET 11-only machine works: the tool starts, metadata binding accepts an 11.x runtime, generated projects and the `calor init` path follow the installed runtime, three maintainer decisions are recorded in `docs/plans/0.31-toolchain-and-sweep-record.md`, and one Linux x64 CI job proves it. Closes on this scope. On the 0.31 exit chain; may ship as a 0.30.x point release. |
| #1638 | The converter parses C# 15: Roslyn upgrade, syntax-kind classification, registry entries, parse fixtures. Off the exit chain; may slip to 0.34, except for its package upgrade if #1639 turns out to need it (see Sequence). |

Moved to 0.34, epic #1852 (`[0.34] Epic: complete .NET 11 and C# 15 support (remainder of #1644)`, to be filed):

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1640 | Effect manifests and nullability metadata for .NET 11 BCL additions; CI check for missing entries |
| #1641 | CI legs for .NET 11 alongside .NET 10 |
| #1642 | Dependency refresh: `System.CommandLine` stable, Roslyn and MSBuild packages, unused old test target frameworks |
| #1643 | Native C# 15 unions and closed hierarchies with exhaustive match |
| #1855 | Remainder of #1639: the consumer matrices on .NET 11 for all five runtime identifiers (RIDs: linux-x64, linux-arm64, osx-arm64, win-x64, win-arm64), the release SDK pin, reproducible-build checks, Z3 packaging when the packages are built by the .NET 11 SDK, and the documentation pass over the pages that still name only .NET 10 |
| #1856 | Remainder of #1638: a C# 15 project in the round-trip corpus |

## Sequence

Neither issue depends on the other. Two things fix the order in practice:

1. #1639 starts first, because it is on the 0.31 exit chain. Its three decisions (tool framework, roll-forward policy, release SDK pin) are taken in the same maintainer session as the soundness-sweep records #1769, #1778 and #1783, and are written to the same file, `docs/plans/0.31-toolchain-and-sweep-record.md`. It does not wait for the 0.30 evaluation (#1605).
2. #1638 is the first issue to leave 0.31 if the milestone runs short. One conditional edge can change that: if the .NET 11 job of #1639 shows that Roslyn 5.3.0 cannot read .NET 11 framework assemblies, the package upgrade in #1638 (its work item 1) becomes a prerequisite of #1639 and can no longer slip. The finding is recorded on both issues when it is made; from then on #1639 depends on #1638, and only work items 2 to 4 of #1638 may still move.

## Done when

- #1639 is closed: its .NET 11-only CI job is green on `main` and its section of `docs/plans/0.31-toolchain-and-sweep-record.md` is merged. This satisfies the 0.31 exit criterion: with the released packages (built by the .NET 10 SDK), on a machine with only the .NET 11 SDK, `calor init`, `calor check` and `dotnet build` of a `Calor.Sdk` consumer succeed.
- #1638 is closed, or has been moved to epic #1852 with a comment that names the milestone it moved to. If the conditional edge in Sequence applied, its package upgrade was merged before #1639 closed.
- Every issue in the second table carries its 0.34 milestone, and #1640 to #1643 end with "Part of" the #1852 epic instead of "Part of #1644." (applied by #1759).

## Not in this epic

- Effect and nullability entries for new .NET 11 APIs (#1640), .NET 11 CI legs (#1641), the dependency refresh (#1642), native unions (#1643). All 0.34.
- Moving the release SDK pin off 10.0.401, the .NET 11 consumer matrices over all five RIDs, and reproducible-build checks on a new pin (#1855).
- A C# 15 project in the round-trip corpus (#1856).
- The union declaration spelling (#1797, 0.32).
- Building the Calor repository itself with only the .NET 11 SDK. `global.json:3-4` pins SDK 10.0.100 with `latestMinor`; changing it is part of #1855.
- `calor lsp` on a .NET 11-only machine. It spawns `calor-lsp`, a separate `net10.0` executable that no workflow packs or publishes (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/LspCommand.cs:19`); #1855 records what happens to it.

epics.title: [0.31] Epic: test and CI health
epics.body:
## Goal

A fast, non-flaky test suite and release run that people trust when it is green and believe when it is red, on the 0.30 code base. For 0.31 that means three measurable things: the release jobs pass without a flake rerun (#1749), the index build is back within twice its 0.29 cost (#1738), and the compiler test shard's wall time is measured against its 30-minute target at the 0.30 inventory (#1590). None of the three is a release gate. The 0.31 exit asks only that the release CI flakes are fixed or the reruns of the 0.31 release are recorded: #1749 is a release-process prerequisite.

## Why

This epic was opened for 0.29 and is still open in 0.31. Of the 18 issues in its 0.29 body, 17 were closed on 2026-10-29 (GitHub close dates). Only #1590 remained, and `CHANGELOG.md:422-423` records its wall-time target as unmet at 0.29.0. The 0.30 rewrite then made CI time a binding constraint:

- **Compiler shard.** `Calor.Compiler.Tests` grew from 16,075 cases (`scripts/compiler-shard-filter.sh:11`) to 22,559 (`expectedTotal`, `eng/test-manifest.json:8`). On CI its tests summed to 2,364 s against 1,223 s on `main` before the merge, historical replays excluded (`docs/plans/2026-11-16-milestone-0.30-ci-triage.md:507`). On the 0.30 branch the `tests (compiler)` job was cancelled at its 40-minute limit (`.github/workflows/test.yml:508`) on 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-20, and once more at 40.3 minutes (same document, `:444`, `:469`, `:558`). The job now starts five test hosts at once on a 4-vCPU, 16 GB runner (four parts and a host that rebuilds archived compilers) and adds an 8 GB swap file first (`scripts/run-shard-tests.sh:47-87`).
- **Release.** Three failures during the 0.30.0 publish runs passed on rerun with no code change, and each rerun repeats a job of about 60 minutes (#1749). The 0.30.0 release also ran a dry run and then a real dispatch (`eng/performance-baselines.json:10`, `tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/Release/ReleaseWorkflowTests.cs:588-593`), which the release policy says not to do (`docs/release-policy.md:13-14`).
- **Performance gate.** The index build over the 106-file fixture went from 0.38 s at 0.29.0 to about 10 s. After a first fix it measures 3.10 to 5.56 s on CI, which is 8 to 15 times the 0.29 figure. The suite ceiling moved 24.0 → 48.0 → 41.0 s and has about 5% headroom on the slowest runner class seen. Two wall-clock smoke budgets in the same suite have each failed once on a shared runner with no code cause: the 0.1 ms budget in #1749, and `DataflowAnalysis_ComplexCFG_IsTimingSmokeTest` at 60.9 ms against 25 ms. Apart from the #1749 failure, every figure in this bullet is from `eng/performance-baselines.json:10`.

Later work adds CI load on top of this. The .NET 11 CI legs (#1641, 0.34) wait for #1749, and the corpus report job (#1779) is scheduled outside the pull-request shard for the same reason.

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1590 | Compiler test-host memory and compiler-shard wall time. The leak sources found in 0.29 are repaired and an unsplit run of 16,075 cases peaked at 3,183 MiB (`scripts/compiler-shard-filter.sh:8-13`); nothing has verified the 22,559-case inventory. The p90 target (under 30 minutes over the last 30 successful `test.yml` runs on `main`) has not been measured on the 0.30 shard layout. The amendment replaces the half of the body that predates the 0.29 repairs. May slip. |
| #1738 | Index build within 2x of 0.29.0 (at most 0.80 s on CI over the 106-file fixture; 3.10 to 5.56 s today), then the performance ceiling lowered from 41.0 s. Stays open until that measurement is met. May slip. |
| #1749 | Release CI flakes: the wall-clock smoke budgets that have failed with no code cause (0.1 ms CFG, 25 ms dataflow), the historical formatter replay losing its extracted tree, and five concurrent test hosts starving the runner. A release-process prerequisite: 0.31.0 may ship with its reruns recorded on this issue. Its three closing dry runs are maintainer dispatches. May slip. |
| #1726 | Website cold-mobile asset test times out waiting for `networkidle`. May slip. |
| #1728 | Release promotion: the design is implemented and was used for 0.30.0. Left: time one release from a single dispatch after #1749 closes and correct the policy text, or close (maintainer decision). May slip. |

No other child is open. The other ten work items of the 0.29 body (#959, #1121, #1032, #1031, #1042, #1115, #1116, #901, #1030, #1134) and its seven proposed closures (#859, #884, #948, #1131, #1157, #1159, #1011) were closed on 2026-10-29.

## Sequence

One dependency: #1728 depends on #1749. The other orderings are not dependencies; they avoid wasted runs.

1. #1749 first. It is the release-process prerequisite, and its third item changes how the compiler shard runs (`scripts/run-shard-tests.sh`). Its three closing dry runs are dispatched on `main` commits before the 0.31.0 candidate is chosen, and none is the candidate commit.
2. #1728 after #1749. The release it times is the first one published after #1749 closes, because a release with flake reruns is not a measurement of the promotion path.
3. #1590's 30-run window counts `main` runs after the last change to the shard's layout, so it starts when item 3 of #1749 lands.
4. #1749 item 1 before the calibration dispatches of #1738 where possible. A failed smoke budget ends a gate run before it measures (`scripts/run_performance_gate.py:88-90`), and one calibration dispatch of the first #1738 fix failed that way and had to be rerun (`eng/performance-baselines.json:10`).
5. #1726 has no ordering.

## Done when

- **Release flakes (the 0.31 exit criterion "Release CI flakes are fixed, or the reruns of the 0.31 release are recorded").** Either #1749 is closed by its own criterion (each failure it lists has a fix or a recorded decision, and `test (compiler)` and `release-quality` in `publish-nuget.yml` pass three consecutive dry runs without a rerun), or a comment on #1749 lists every job of the 0.31.0 `publish-nuget.yml` run that needed more than one attempt, with the run id, the attempt count and the failure. #1749 is a release-process prerequisite, not a gate: the release may ship with a rerun recorded. Only the maintainer dispatches `publish-nuget.yml`, dry runs included (`.claude/skills/create-release/SKILL.md:33-34`), so the three dry runs are maintainer actions for 0.31; each repeats the release validation (36.62 elapsed minutes and 122.22 job-minutes at v0.29.0, `docs/release-policy.md:105`).
- #1749, #1590, #1738, #1726 and #1728 are each closed, or on the day 0.31.0 is released are moved to milestone 0.32 with the `ci` label and a comment that carries the latest reading: for #1749 the rerun record above and which of its three items are fixed, for #1738 the latest `IndexBuildStaysWithinItsBudget` readings and their ratio to 0.38 s, for #1590 the latest p90 and the leak record described in the next bullet, for #1726 and #1728 the reason.
- **0.31 and this epic may close with the #1590 leak on record instead of fixed.** The record is one comment on #1590 that states either (a) a completed unsplit run of the full 0.30 inventory with its peak RSS, or (b) "not verified at the 0.30 inventory; the four-part split is kept on purpose", with the 0.29 evidence linked (`docs/plans/performance-gate-strategy.md:117-122`). The repository does not record the leak as unfixable: it records the sources found in 0.29 as repaired and the 0.30 inventory as unverified.
- When the first two bullets hold and 0.31.0 is released, this epic is closed. Moved issues stand alone in 0.32 with no parent epic. The epic is not retitled or carried to another milestone.

## Not in this epic

- .NET 11 CI legs: #1641 (0.34). It depends on #1749.
