- Dispatching `publish-nuget.yml`, as a dry run or a release: a maintainer action. No issue here authorises one.
- Warm `calor check` and MCP write latency, and a CI budget for edit-to-diagnostic time: #1818 (0.32).
- The remaining incremental-build reuse tier: #1836 (0.33).
- The corpus report job on its own schedule: #1779.
- The soundness sweep failing on `main`: #1694.
- Converter regressions after 0.30 on the default `calor migrate` path and the round-trip harness legs: #1647 (0.32).

epics.title: [0.31] Epic: adoption decisions that gate 0.36 and later
epics.body:
## Goal

Take in 0.31 the maintainer decisions that milestones 0.36 to 0.39 wait on, and open the paperwork with the longest lead time:

- whether anyone may be asked to become the external maintainer of a pilot component, or the independent methods reviewer of the 0.37 comparison;
- what happens to the paused PP-W-rows research;
- a first draft of the 0.37 protocol, and a first sizing of what that comparison would cost.

Every deliverable is a document under `docs/plans/`. No issue here changes the compiler, uses CI time, spends money or has an agent contact anyone.

## Why

- 0.36 needs "a named external maintainer" and treats a missing one as "a blocker, not replaced by creator self-evaluation" (#1701). 0.37 takes its final tasks from that pilot (#1708) and cannot start collection without an independent fairness review (#1709, #1712). 0.38 and 0.39 consume the 0.37 verdict.
- Outreach has never been authorised. The last gate record lists no permitted contacts, no outreach window and "Contacts made" at 0 (`docs/plans/safe-delegation-m0/v0.23/r2a-adopter-unavailable.md:25-30`, 2026-10-01). The methods reviewer seat is recorded "Vacant; no consenting person evidenced" (`docs/plans/safe-delegation-m0/authorization.md:68`, 2026-09-09).
- Naming an external adopter is a decision the maintainer reserved (`docs/plans/call-s-adjudication.md:187-190`), so no agent can advance it. Left where they are, both absences are discovered at the last step: #1701 sits in 0.36 and the reviews in 0.37.
- #1648 was filed in 0.32, although three things wait on it earlier or name it as their predecessor: the #1708 protocol draft that starts in 0.31 (#1791) needs the admission rule its closing record carries forward (the test a task must pass before it counts as evidence about effect rows or contracts), #1711 depends on the same rule, and the 0.31 legacy-dialect allowlist (#1763) must list the 52 retired-syntax `.calr` files whose class it decides.

These items need the maintainer, not an agent and not CI, and they can be taken in one sitting: #1777, #1648 and, if its draft is ready, the request in #1786.

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1777 | Decision: authorise or decline outreach for an external adopter and for an independent methods reviewer; a contact log on the authorise branch; a default so the release is not held |
| #1648 | Decide the paused PP-W-rows research (resume with a plan or close), with a closing record that carries the admission rule forward and classifies the retired-syntax fixtures |
| #1791 | Open the #1708 protocol draft and, only if outreach is authorised, the #1701 recruitment record |
| #1786 | One-page sizing and budget request for #1708 and #1712, drafted from the archived E1a run-to-run spread |

## Sequence

1. #1765 (epic #1758) merges first. The decline branch of #1777 applies the adopter fallback that document holds.
2. #1777 and #1648 are decided in the same session. #1648 waits on nothing and may be decided earlier; #1763 (epic #1761) reads its result.
3. #1791 after both: the recruitment record exists only on the authorise branch of #1777, and the task-selection sections of the protocol draft are written from the closing record of #1648. Its two files may merge separately; the recruitment record waits only on #1777.
4. #1786 at any point. If it is ready, it is put in front of the maintainer in the same session; nothing waits for it in 0.31.

## Done when

- `docs/plans/0.31-outreach-decision.md` is merged with at least one dated entry for each of the two items: authorise, decline, or that item's default line, which contains the words "not decided, treated as decline until changed". This satisfies the 0.31 exit criterion on the outreach decision on every branch of the #1605 criterion, "no paid run authorised" included.
- #1648 is closed with `docs/plans/0.31-ppw-rows-disposition.md` merged, and #1254, #1262, #1267 and #1436 are either closed as not planned or carry a dated plan.
- `docs/plans/0.37-comparison-protocol.md` exists as a draft; on the authorise branch `docs/plans/0.36-pilot-recruitment.md` exists too. Or #1791 has moved to 0.32 with the note #1833 must carry.
- `docs/plans/0.37-sizing-and-budget-request.md` exists as a draft with its refresh log, or #1786 has moved to 0.32.

## Not in this epic

- Writing the adopter fallback table (#1765, epic #1758) and applying it at the checkpoint (#1833). This epic cites the table and, on a decline, records the date from which it applies.
- Recording an adopter's consent or naming the adopter: #1833 and #1701.
- The two methods reviews (#1857), the task supply inventory (#1865) and the collection budget decision (#1867).
- Freezing and registering the #1708 protocol in Annex A of `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md`: #1708.
- The registration and spend decision for the 0.31 evaluation: #1770.
- Putting the `W-00x` files on the legacy-dialect allowlist: #1763 applies the class #1648 records.
- Any paid run, any contact made by an agent, any compiler or harness change.
- Three follow-ups that no issue owns. Each is filed as a new issue only if the #1648 closing record calls for it, and none is 0.31 work:
  - Under option (b) of #1648, changing the published status from "paused by the user" to "closed without a verdict" on three website pages, together with the assertions in `website/tests/public-claims.spec.ts` that pin the wording.
  - If the maintainer wants the six `W-00x` pair directories removed: removing them together with the blob-SHA pins, the tests and the tooling that hold them byte-identical.
  - Enforcing a class for the 220 `.calr.inc` fragments of the redesigned experiment. The #1763 check reads `.calr` files only, so the class #1648 records for them is a statement that no check enforces.

epics.title: [0.32] Epic: stabilize the 0.30 language
epics.body:
## Goal

Act on what the 0.30 agent evaluation (#1605) measured, bring the converter's native output back to its pre-0.30 level on the paths users and CI run, and clear the loud-failure and diagnostic-quality backlog. No child of this epic changes a spelling: form changes are decided in the breaking window (epic #1787) and applied by the single rewrite (epic #1792).

## Why

0.30 rewrote the grammar, the emitter, two verification paths and every teaching surface with no backward compatibility, and its release published no new benchmark results (`CHANGELOG.md:15`). #1605 publishes at the 0.31 exit and is the first agent measurement of the 0.30 language. This epic is the capacity reserved to act on it before 0.33 builds agent reach on the language: fixes for the constructs that regressed, fix patches for the diagnostics agents actually hit, and replacement guidance for the retired forms they still write.

The converter also lost ground. On the round-trip harness's lossy leg, native files fell from 17 to 10 of 32 (MediatR), from 96 to 58 of 139 (FluentValidation) and from 54 to 36 of 112 (Serilog), and the floors were lowered to match (`docs/plans/2026-11-16-milestone-0.30-ci-triage.md:363-367`). The 0.34 coverage work, the density target and every report that reads migrated corpus output start from those numbers, so "#1647 closed" is a 0.32 exit criterion.

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1645 | Act on the #1605 evaluation: fix every regression that is not a form change, refer form changes to the window record, re-run the affected pairs on the post-rewrite commit |
| #1646 | Apply the amended fewest-tokens rule to every 0.30 spelling with each tokenizer the rule names; hand candidate flips to the window record |
| #1647 | Default-path converter regressions: round-trip native files back to 17 of 32, 96 of 139 and 54 of 112; the migrated corpus projects build with effect enforcement on |
| #1790 | Fix coverage for agent-hit diagnostics: the three most frequent codes, and every wrong-form error |
| #1788 | Calor0006 names the replacement for every retired `§` marker |
| #1789 | Two modify-a-converted-module pairs on one migrated corpus project |
| #1746 | Token ratio and native fraction reported per corpus project |
| #909 | Division analysis: re-test the double report on 0.30; fix the over-strong Calor0926 suggestion |
| #1511 | Spurious Calor0410 after a lossy partial-class merge |
| #1142 | Remove the configured-vs-defaulted trap in EffectEnforcementPass caps |

Close any of these that 0.30 makes obsolete.

Conditional child: #1670 (0.31) re-tests whether `///` documentation text reaches the generated C#. If it does not, that re-test files a new issue against this epic ("`///` documentation text is not emitted into generated C#"), and the issue joins the table as backlog that may be deferred with a reason. If the re-test finds no defect, no child is added.

## Sequence

1. #1647 starts when 0.32 opens. Its harness part waits on nothing; the parts that take over what #1782 leaves read the #1782 baseline and the corpus report job (#1779). Both are 0.32 entry conditions.
2. #1789 needs two 0.31 results: project-mode migration that verifies (#1782) and a harness that runs the 0.30 arm (#1766). It merges before the spend record (#1816) is decided, because that record registers the pair set.
3. #1645 (triage and fixes), #1790 and #1788 start when #1605 has published stage 1 or the reduced design. All three read its report, and the last two change text that a measured arm reads. If #1605 recorded "no paid run authorised", there is no report, and each of the three says what it then records.
4. #1646 runs after the amended rule (#1785) and the tokenizer tooling (#1799), and hands its candidate flips to the window record (#1784) before that record's cut-off date.
5. The #1645 fixes and #1790 merge before the commit that #1807 records. A fix that merges later is not measured by the re-run.
6. The #1645 re-run is last: on the commit after the rewrite (#1803) and the instrument re-registration (#1807), under the spend record (#1816), with the #1789 pairs in its pair set. #1645 closes, on the published re-run or the recorded decline, before the edition is declared (#1805).
7. #1746 follows the corpus report job (#1779).

Off the 0.32 exit chain, and free to slip to 0.33 without holding the release: #1788, #1746, #909, #1511, #1142.

## Done when

- Every #1605 regression is fixed or its form decision revisited (#1645 closed).
- The token measurements use the real tokenizer (#1646 closed: every 0.30 spelling choice has a count from each tokenizer the amended rule names; the density ratio is reported by #1746 with an offline proxy on every run and an Anthropic count once per release).
- The backlog above is closed or explicitly deferred with a reason. #1647 cannot be deferred: its closure is a 0.32 exit criterion.

## Not in this epic

- Any change to an existing spelling and any new hard error: the breaking-window record and its decisions (#1784, #1794 to #1800, #1743, #1741, #1735), epic #1787.
- The fewest-tokens rule itself (#1785) and the tokenizer tooling (#1799): epic #1787.
- The edition marker, compiler support for a decided form, the rewriter, the single rewrite, instrument re-registration and the edition declaration (#1084, #1793, #1806 to #1805): epic #1792.
- The spend record that authorises the #1645 re-run (#1816), and the seeded-defect replication: epic #1812.
- The rule that effect-row and contract fixes are never marked safe (#1801): epic #1808.
- What an agent does with a preserved C# file (#1822): epic #1804.
- Teaching-reference size (#1734) and the `calor init` delivery default (#1823): epic #1821.
- CS8669 on preserved originals in project-mode `calor migrate` (#1782) and the corpus report job (#1779): 0.31, epic #1780.
- The below-1.0x density target (#1844) and native coverage for constructs that were never supported (#1659): 0.34.
- Follow-up with no issue: running the corpus subjects' own test suites against the project-mode migrated libraries. #1647 judges tests on the round-trip legs and the member oracle, and the corpus report job (#1779) records `tests: not-run`.
- Former children of this epic: #1573 (closed 2026-10-22), #1555 (closed under epic #1758), #1648 (moved to 0.31), #1177 (moved to 0.34).

epics.title: [0.32] Epic: last breaking window — the decisions
epics.body:
## Goal

Take every decision that would change a spelling the 0.30 compiler accepts, or reject a program that compiles today, once: under one amended spelling rule, measured from one payload manifest, by one dated cut-off. Anything undecided on that date keeps its 0.30 behaviour and waits for a future edition.

## Why

The 0.30 syntax is still open on purpose. #1646 says "Flip any choice whose ranking changes ... a parse-error change plus a repo rewrite". #1645 says "If the form itself is the problem, revisit it". #1735 changes what compiled programs do at run time. The parser still accepts brace-header forms that the 0.30 cleanup left as "a separate decision" (`docs/plans/2026-11-16-milestone-0.30-ci-triage.md:542-544`). At the same time #1653 (0.33, agent reach) is premised on a stable language: "Launching earlier would teach agents a language that's about to change."

The last breaking change was expensive. 0.30 shipped "with no automatic rewriter for 0.29 source" (`CHANGELOG.md:12-13`), a full compiler-test run during its cut-over had 1,130 of 22,251 tests failing (`docs/plans/2026-11-16-milestone-0.30-ci-triage.md:9`), and the proof-soundness packet is still frozen in the retired syntax (`tests/TestData/SoundnessSweep/templates.json`, 136 templates). If the pending decisions land one at a time, each one repeats part of that cost and each one invalidates the instruments that 0.31 restores. Taken as one batch, one rewriter (#1806) applies one rewrite (#1803), the instruments are re-registered once (#1807), and the edition can be declared (#1805).

The rule the decisions are taken under needs amending first. The 0.30 rule is "the variant with the fewest tokens, not the most readable one", with the C# spelling only as a tie-break, measured on one tokenizer (`docs/design/0.30-syntax-token-decision.md:3-7`), and the record lists its own one-token wins as weak (`:570`).

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1784 | Breaking-window decision record: the batch table, the cut-off date, the staging rule, one payload manifest, the batch acceptance measurement, and the order of the steps that follow |
| #1785 | Amend the fewest-tokens rule: a minimum win, a named tokenizer set, and agent error counts as a ground for respelling toward C# |
| #1799 | Tooling that counts one payload manifest with each tokenizer the rule names |
| #1794 | Decide the brace-header forms the 0.30 parser still accepts |
| #1797 | Decide the union declaration spelling (additive unless it reserves a word; implemented by #1643 in 0.34) |
| #1796 | Decide whether a redundant `public` is canonical |
| #1800 | Decide every rejecting guarantee: null remainder, enum-match exhaustiveness, making the bool exhaustiveness check effective, obligation verification as a default-build check, and what counts as breaking |
| #1743 | The converter never emits an `else` whose body is only an `if`; the shipped error is recorded (not a breaking decision; may slip) |
| #1741 | Remove 0.30 residue: legacy `dbr`/`dbw` effect values, Lisp-era operator hints, inline-sibling counter, dead `AttributeHelper` code (not breaking; may slip) |
| #1735 | Inherited parameter refinements behave like direct ones |
| #1795 | Round-trip leg compiled with the default contract mode and with effects enforced, plus three compile-options canary tests |

## Sequence

1. #1784 opens the record first (table, cut-off date, staging rule, order) and stays open until the rewrite has landed.
2. #1785 (the rule) before any spelling decision, because every spelling decision cites it.
3. #1799 (tooling) before the token count is dispatched, because the rule names tokenizers nothing in the repository can count with.
4. The spelling decisions share one payload manifest and one dispatch per tokenizer: the #1646 and #1645 rows (epic #1649), #1794, #1797, #1796 and the edition-marker spelling (#1084, epic #1792). The manifest is published on the record's payload date, which precedes the cut-off.
5. In parallel with 2 to 4: #1800, once the #1605 report (or its recorded "no paid run authorised"), the corpus report job (#1779) and the #1084 design record, which defines the opt-in mechanism, are available; #1735 together with #1795.
6. On the cut-off date the record is decided. #1793 and #1806 (epic #1792) start from the decided record. #1784 is closed after #1803 has landed, or after the rewrite inventory records that no rewrite was needed; its before and after acceptance measurement reads the corpus report job (#1779).
7. #1743 and #1741 are off this chain. Neither changes an accepted spelling; each can land at any time and may slip to 0.33.

## Done when

- The amended rule is recorded (#1785) and one command per tokenizer counts the same manifest (#1799).
- Every row of the window record carries a decision dated on or before the cut-off, or reads "deferred to a future edition" with a reason.
- #1800 has recorded one outcome for each rejecting candidate.
- #1735 has landed and the strict round-trip leg (#1795) runs in CI.
- #1784 is closed: every row was decided or deferred by the cut-off date, every row decided "land" has merged, and the rewrite has landed or the inventory records that none was needed. This is the first 0.32 exit criterion.
- #1743 and #1741 are closed, or moved to 0.33 with their rows in the window record filled.

## Not in this epic

- The per-module edition marker (#1084), compiler support for the decided forms (#1793), the rewriter (#1806), the rewrite itself (#1803), re-registering the instruments (#1807) and the edition declaration (#1805): epic #1792.
- Applying the amended rule to the 0.30 spellings (#1646) and acting on #1605 regressions (#1645): epic #1649. Their outcomes are rows in this epic's record.
- Sound effect contracts (#1731): epic #1808. Only a new effect spelling, or a program it newly rejects, is a row here.
- The guard-derived precondition decision (#1847): none of its options changes an existing spelling.
- Implementing unions (#1643, 0.34), null-gap checks (#1869) or enum exhaustiveness (#1871).
- Follow-up with no owning issue: reporting the static opportunity counts #1800 reads (enum-typed `match` targets, null-gap sites) as columns of the corpus report job (#1779). Until an issue owns that, #1800 takes the counts by commands written into its record.
- Option and Result stay removed (#1617). `requires` stays removed (#1618).

epics.title: [0.32] Epic: one rewrite, instruments re-registered, then the edition
epics.body:
## Goal

Land every source-changing decision of the 0.32 breaking window in the repository in one change made by a shipped rewriter, re-register the instruments on the result, and only then declare the language an edition, with a per-module marker and a written compatibility promise.

## Why

The breaking window is the 0.32 milestone: the last release in which an existing spelling may change. An edition is a named set of accepted spellings and default-on errors that later compilers keep accepting.

0.30 changed the whole syntax with no rewriter (`CHANGELOG.md:13`, `:36`). A week after the cut-over, a full local run of the compiler tests on the milestone branch had 1,130 failures out of 22,251, and roughly 70% of all failures triaged that day were stale tests or fixtures that still asserted the retired syntax or behaviour (`docs/plans/2026-11-16-milestone-0.30-ci-triage.md:9`, `:13`, `:29`). The instruments (the soundness-sweep packet, the benchmark pairs and the end-to-end agent tasks) were left behind as well. At HEAD `bc80daeb` all 136 soundness-sweep templates (`tests/TestData/SoundnessSweep/templates.json`), the 102 `.calr` files under `bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs` and 63 live end-to-end task files (the count in #1736) are still in the retired syntax.

0.31 restores those instruments on the 0.30 spellings. The 0.32 window (epic #1787) may then respell forms they use. Without a fixed order the second rewrite would repeat the first: hash-pinned cases orphaned again, paid agent runs taken on spellings that are about to change, and an edition declared on forms no agent has run.

The strategy committed to "Syntax editions before any further breaking change" (`docs/plans/agent-native-strategy.md:210`), and 0.30 went ahead without one. This epic supplies the mechanism (the marker and the rewriter), does the rewrite once, and puts the declaration last.

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1084 | Per-module edition marker: design record and implementation (rewritten from the v0.14 self-migration residue) |
| #1793 | Conditional: compiler support for each form the window decided that has no implementing issue, with the old form still accepted |
| #1806 | `calor fix` rewriter for the breaking-window batch, with tests; the decision on a rewriter for pre-0.30 source; the standing rule for later breaking changes |
| #1803 | Apply the rewrite once across the inventory; the old forms become errors in the same change |
| #1807 | Re-register the instruments on the post-rewrite commit: soundness packet, benchmark pairs, arm canary, end-to-end suite |
| #1805 | Decision: declare the edition and publish the compatibility promise, or record the deferral |

## Sequence

1. #1084, first pull request (the design record), before the cut-off date of the window record (#1784). #1800 reads it, the marker's spelling is a row of the record's batch table, and whether the marker is required decides whether the rewrite inserts it into every file.
2. When the record is decided (its cut-off date has passed and every row has an outcome): #1084, second pull request (implementation), and #1793. Both leave every old form accepted. #1793 is closed as not planned if no decided row needs it.
3. #1806. A rule can only be written for a decided row whose new form the compiler accepts.
4. #1803, once, after the legacy allowlist (#1763) exists. Until it merges, no window row turns an accepted form into an error.
5. #1807, directly after. The soundness packet pins a hash per case, and the green-run count for 0.35 entry restarts at any re-registration (#1783).
6. The paid runs (#1810 in epic #1812, and the #1645 re-run in epic #1649) pin the commit that #1807 posts.
7. #1805, after each of those runs has published or its decline is recorded (#1816), so that the edition is not declared on spellings no agent has run, and after the window record is closed with every "land" row inside the commit #1807 posted.

## Done when

- The compiler parses and validates a per-module edition marker, and `docs/design/0.32-edition-marker.md` records the design, including what a module writes to opt in to a rejecting check (#1084).
- Every decided row of the window record that needs a compiler change and has no implementing issue links a merged pull request, or #1793 is closed as not planned with the record linked.
- `.calr` files outside the legacy allowlist were migrated by the shipped rewriter (#1806) in one merged change, and `docs/plans/0.32-rewrite-inventory.md` lists every class of embedded Calor text (test literals, sweep templates, documentation fences) with how it was migrated; or that file records that no rewrite was needed because no decision changed source (#1803).
- `docs/plans/0.32-instrument-re-registration.md` records the instruments validated again after the rewrite, with the soundness packet re-registered if any case changed, and the commit for the paid runs to pin is posted (#1807).
- `docs/plans/0.32-edition-declaration.md` records the edition declaration, or the decision to defer with its effect on 0.33 (#1805).

## Not in this epic

- Which spellings flip and which guarantees reject: epic #1787, recorded in #1784.
- Compiler work for window rows that have their own issue: #1731, #1735 and any implementation child #1800 creates.
- Authorising and running the paid collections: #1816, #1810, #1645.
- Restoring the instruments on 0.30 syntax: #1766, #1781, #1778, #1736 (0.31).
- The legacy-dialect allowlist and its self-check: #1763.
- Re-affirming the edition after the per-agent results: #1846.
- A second edition. #1084 delivers the marker for the first edition only.
- Follow-up with no issue of its own: implementing the per-module opt-in. The #1084 design record states the mechanism (what a module writes); the first issue that ships an opt-in check implements it (the candidates are an implementation child of #1800, or the 0.35 issues that put a rejecting check behind an opt-in).

epics.title: [0.32] Epic: effect precision on everyday .NET code
epics.body:
## Goal

Before the edition is declared, make it known and checkable how much everyday .NET code the effect system really covers. Decide the built-in contracts that are known to be unsound inside the breaking window (#1731). Report how much converted and agent-written code ends up `unknown` (#1802). Tie every teaching statement about what is pure or unknown to a compile check (#1798). Pin that no tool applies an effect-row or contract edit on its own (#1801). Stop `calor effects suggest --merge` from writing unresolved calls into the project manifest as pure (#1814).

## Why

Effect rows are a feature that neither C# nor Rust has. At HEAD `bc80daeb` five facts limit what they can claim.

- The built-in manifest gives an empty effect list to members that can run code the effect system does not see: every `System.String` method through a wildcard, `Parse`, `TryParse` and `ToString` on `int`, `long`, `double` and `bool`, 61 LINQ operators, `Object.Equals` and `GetHashCode`, and the methods and properties of `Nullable<T>` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Manifests/bcl-system.calor-effects.json:43-47`, `:66-107`, `:461-526`, `:541-554`). These contracts were withdrawn and then restored during 0.30; tests name "the restored 0.29 BCL manifest" (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/StringInterpolationTests.cs:270-272`). #1731 tracks them and has no milestone.
- Since 0.30 a member that the framework and ecosystem manifests do not list is charged `unknown` (`CHANGELOG.md:64`). A callable that declares `! unknown` is not checked and forces the same row on every caller, and `calor convert` writes that row itself (`docs/syntax-reference/effects.md:292-302`). No report counts how much code carries it.
- The teaching reference tells agents that `Contains(string)`, `Substring`, trimming, `Enumerable.Where` and `ToArray` "remain unknown under strict checking" (`docs/syntax-reference/current-language.md:580`, `:1153`). The manifest lists them as pure, and a benchmark reference solution that calls `Contains(string)` under a pure row is compiled in CI (`tests/TestData/ActiveSyntax/bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs/N1-003-csv-row/reference/calor/CsvRow.calr:3-5`).
- The compiler's suggested fix for an undeclared effect is to add the effect to the row (`src/Calor.Compiler/Effects/EffectEnforcementPass.cs:1068`, `:1084`). One test covers one of the two shapes of that fix. The language server marks every fix it offers as the preferred action, safe or not (`src/Calor.LanguageServer/Handlers/CodeActionHandler.cs:77`), and the workflow catalog and the `calor_compile` tool description tell agents that effect errors are fixed automatically.
- `calor effects suggest --merge` writes an empty effect list, which a manifest reads as pure, for every unresolved call into the project's live `.calor-effects.json` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/EffectsCommand.cs:623-631`, `:703-722`). The `Calor0411` message tells the user to add a manifest entry (`src/Calor.Compiler/Effects/EffectEnforcementPass.cs:5952`). One command turns `unknown` into pure with no review.

The timing follows from the edition. Once #1805 declares it, a tightened built-in contract is a new hard error on programs that compile. The planned compatibility promise treats that as a breaking change unless the maintainer adopts the soundness exemption that #1805 puts to them. These contracts are known to be unsound now, so #1731 is decided in this window either way. Replacing an `unknown` charge with an exact contract only accepts more programs; that work continues in 0.33 (#1841) and is sized by the report #1802 produces.

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1731 | Sound contracts for the built-in members known to run unseen code: one recorded outcome per member group, decided inside the breaking window |
| #1802 | Unknown-effect share per corpus project and per agent run, from one measurement in the effect pass |
| #1798 | A compile check behind every "pure" or "unknown" statement in the teaching text, the primer's `[needs ...]` annotations and the effects reference |
| #1801 | Pin: no effect-row or contract edit is applied automatically, by `calor fix`, the MCP tools or the language server |
| #1814 | `calor effects suggest --merge` never writes an unresolved call into the project manifest as pure |

## Sequence

1. #1802, part 1 (the corpus columns), as soon as the corpus report job (#1779) exists. It gives #1731 its before figure and #1841 its sizing input. Part 2, the agent-run table, may follow.
2. #1731 records its breaking outcomes in the window record (#1784) before that record's cut-off date.
3. The contract changes of #1731 land. An outcome that changes `.calr` source gives its rule to the rewriter (#1806) and starts rejecting programs only in the single rewrite (#1803).
4. #1798 and #1801 pin the result. #1798 follows #1772 and #1745; whichever of #1798 and a #1731 contract change merges second updates the affected claims in its own pull request. #1801 has no dependency and should merge before #1790 starts marking new fixes safe.
5. #1814 has no ordering.

Calor text that these issues embed in tests or in the teaching source before #1803 merges is part of that rewrite's inventory.

## Done when

- The corpus report shows the unknown-effect share for MediatR, Serilog and FluentValidation (#1802, part 1). This is the 0.32 exit criterion "Unknown-effect share reported per corpus project"; the agent-run table of part 2 may follow.
- #1731 is closed: every member group has a recorded outcome in the window record (#1784), the landed ones carry the standing acceptance figures, and the deferred ones are listed as assumptions in the effects reference (`website/content/syntax-reference/effects.mdx`, generated into `docs/syntax-reference/effects.md`).
- `calor self-check docs` exits non-zero when a teaching statement about a member's effects no longer matches the compiler (#1798).
- The safe-fix pin runs in pull-request CI, and the language server marks a fix as preferred only when it is safe to apply (#1801).
- After `calor effects suggest --merge`, a pure function that calls an unresolved member still reports `Calor0410` for `unknown` (#1814).

## Not in this epic

- Correcting the teaching statements themselves: #1772 (0.31), before the #1605 pin.
- Exact contracts for the callee families behind most unknown charges: #1841 (0.33).
- Which diagnostics get fixes and which fixes are marked safe: #1790 (epic #1649).
- A round-trip leg compiled with effects enforced: #1795 (epic #1787).
- The legacy `dbr`/`dbw` effect codes (#1741, epic #1787) and the iteration caps of the effect pass (#1142, epic #1649).
- Whole-file preserved C#, which gets no effect checking at all. Raising the native fraction is #1647 and epic #1659.
- Rejecting guarantees other than effects (null remainder, enum exhaustiveness): #1800.
- Effect diagnostics in the editor. The language server does not run the effect pass, so no effect-row fix reaches an editor and the preferred-flag change in #1801 is preventive. No issue tracks running the pass there; it is a named follow-up.

epics.title: [0.32] Epic: seeded-defect replication on the edition syntax with three conditions
epics.body:
## Goal

Re-run the nine seeded-defect pairs on the post-rewrite language under three conditions (conventional C#, C# equipped with executable specifications, and Calor) and publish the result with catches by channel and cost per condition. If the maintainer declines the spend, record the decline. The 0.32 exit criterion reads: "Seeded-defect replication with three conditions published on the post-rewrite commit, or the maintainer's decline recorded; if a collection is authorised but unpublished at release, the edition declaration is deferred (#1805) and this criterion is recorded as carried to 0.33".

## Why

The project has one adjudicated result in which Calor beat C#. In `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/ws5-probe-001` (2026-07-28, model `claude-opus-4-8`, nine pairs each carrying one defect planted by the maintainer, two arms, meaning two conditions under test, three runs each, 54 of 54 runs valid) the Calor arm ended with 9 of 9 defects removed and the C# arm with 4 of 9 (`VERDICT.md:21-26` in that directory). The delta of 5 cleared a threshold of 3 fixed before the run and was adjudicated a hit (`bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/m5-compare-001/VERDICT.md:83-85`).

Three things limit what that result says.

- **The control had no executable specification.** The C# arm carried each property only as a doc comment (the same `VERDICT.md`, `:67-68`; for example `bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs/W5B-001-shipping-quote/csharp/Quote.cs:12-15`). The Calor arm carried it as a postcondition or an effect declaration that the toolchain enforces.
- **Three of the five deltas are by construction.** For the three contract pairs, fixture acceptance requires the agent-visible smoke suite to fail on the defective Calor starter and pass on the defective C# starter (`bench/phase0-agent-native/check-probe-pair.sh:19-23`, `:185-189`). The other two deltas are effect defects (W5A-003 and W5C-003); both arms caught the remaining four effect defects (the same `VERDICT.md`, `:40-50`).
- **It ran on the pre-0.30 syntax**, and the C# arm has not been run on these pairs since (`ls -d bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/*/W5*/csharp` lists only that epoch).

0.37 plans the fair version of this comparison at real scale (epic #1698, with the three conditions built by #1709), behind an external pilot that has no secured maintainer. The same question can be asked now on the nine pairs for a projected $59 to $94 at archived per-run costs (derivation in #1816). Either answer is useful. If Calor's lead survives an equipped C# arm, the July result is a language effect at fixture scale. If it does not, the July result was mostly "a specification was present", and 0.35 and the #1698 hypothesis are adjusted as #1816 writes in advance. The harness and fixtures built here are also the first use of what #1709, #1710 and #1711 need.

The run comes after the 0.32 rewrite, so that the first fair benefit test is not published on spellings the same milestone retires. It comes before the edition declaration (#1805), so that the edition is not declared on spellings no agent has run.

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1815 | Harness for three conditions: arm definitions outside `pair.json` with per-arm project content, third-arm fixture acceptance, a three-arm epoch driver with a spend stop, and a catch-channel analyzer that works on 0.30 sources |
| #1813 | Equipped C# fixtures for the nine pairs, the list of what C# tooling cannot match, and a fairness review against a written rubric, labelled non-independent |
| #1816 | Decision: register and authorise the 0.32 paid runs (this replication and the #1645 re-run): thresholds, a consequence written in advance for every outcome, ceilings, abort triggers, decline branches |
| #1810 | Run and publish the replication on the post-rewrite commit, and apply the registered consequence |

## Sequence

1. #1815, #1813 and #1816 are prepared while the breaking window (epic #1787) is open. None changes a spelling or what the compiler accepts. #1815 comes first, on the 0.31 harness work it extends (#1766, #1764), because the fixtures and the registration are written against its formats, and #1813 can start authoring once parts 1 and 2 of #1815 (arm definitions, third-arm acceptance) have merged; #1813 comes before #1816 because the registration names what the equipped arm can and cannot check.
2. #1816 has two parts, which may be signed on different dates. Part A (this replication) needs #1815 and #1813. Part B (the #1645 re-run) also needs the regressions #1605 filed and the two pairs #1789 authors.
3. No live agent run of the three-condition set happens before Part A is signed. A trial run would show results before the thresholds are fixed.
4. #1810 runs on the commit that #1807 posts after the rewrite (#1803), and publishes before #1805 decides the edition. Until Part A carries a decision line and that commit is posted, #1810 is held: it stays open and makes no paid run. If Part A is authorised and the result is unpublished when 0.32 is released, #1805 defers the edition declaration and the exit criterion is recorded as carried to 0.33.

## Done when

- #1815 and #1813 are closed.
- The registration is merged as a new entry in Annex A of `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md`, and the spend record `docs/plans/0.32-paid-run-registration.md` carries a dated decision line for each of its two parts (#1816).
- Either the replication is published on the post-rewrite commit (epoch directory with `VERDICT.md`, a section in the 0.32 release notes in `CHANGELOG.md`, a row in `docs/benchmarking/evidence-ledger.md`), or the decline is recorded in the spend record and #1810 is closed as not planned with that record linked. If the collection is authorised and unpublished at the 0.32 release, the criterion is recorded as carried to 0.33, #1805 has deferred the edition declaration, and this epic stays open until one of the two holds.
- The consequence registered for the outcome (outcome D if Part A was declined) is posted on #1662, on the epics #1861 and #1872, and on #1698.
- No pull request under #1815, #1813 or #1816 adds an epoch directory whose `pins.json` has `mode: "live"`.

## Not in this epic

- Running a 0.30 Calor arm at all, arm isolation and loop telemetry: #1766, #1762, #1764 (0.31).
- Re-validating the nine pairs and the arm canary after the rewrite: #1807.
- The #1645 re-run itself (epic #1649). Only its registration and authorisation are here, in #1816.
- Arm types other than `calor` and `csharp`: #1827.
- Tasks and controls authored by someone other than the maintainer, natural defects, real scale: #1708 to #1712 (0.37).
- New seeded-defect pairs, or any change to the nine pairs' defects, specifications or tests.
