epics.title: [0.32] Epic: one toolchain — write, test and check in Calor (part 1)
epics.body:
## Goal

By the end of 0.32 an agent that follows the rules `calor init` gives it can add a test and run it. The time between an edit and its diagnostics is a measured number with a budget on each of the three feedback paths. The incremental-build fix that shipped in 0.30.0 is recorded as shipped. There is one tested answer to "how do I change C# that the converter kept".

## Why

The plan of record (`docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md`, section 3) keeps a capability scorecard of what a Rust user takes for granted. Three of its lines are about the toolchain: tests written in the language, one command that builds, tests and checks, and fast warm feedback. At HEAD `bc80daeb` four gaps stand behind them.

- **Tests cannot be added through the sanctioned path.** `calor check` returns exit 0 only when at least one test ran (`docs/cli/index.md:83`). It and `calor test` discover only top-level `tests/*.cs` xUnit files (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/TestCommand.cs:404-431`). Rule 1 of the text `calor init` writes says "Never create new `.cs` files" (`src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Templates/CLAUDE.md.template:10`), and the write hook it installs blocks both creating and editing every `.cs` path outside `obj/` that is not a `.g.cs` file (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/HookCommand.cs:256-323`, `:347-348`). The adoption guide's first suggested agent task asks the agent to "add tests" (`website/content/guides/adding-calor-to-existing-projects.mdx:130-131`).
- **Feedback latency is unmeasured on 0.30.** The last record is dated 2026-08-01, on a fixture in the retired syntax, for the MCP write path only (`bench/phase0-agent-native/latency/ml1-003/VERDICT.md`). `calor check` is new in 0.30.0 (`CHANGELOG.md:170`), and no record, test or CI job times it. What `dotnet build` recompiles after an edit is pinned by tests and not timed.
- **The incremental-build fix shipped and its issue is still open.** The 0.30.0 release notes say both that `dotnet build` is incremental again (`CHANGELOG.md:188`, citing #1732) and that it recompiles every file after any edit (`CHANGELOG.md:354-359`).
- **Preserved C# has contradictory instructions.** A preserved file is a `.calr` file in which the converter kept the original C#, because it could not express it as Calor. Rule 2 tells the agent to convert C# and "then edit the `.calr` file" (`CLAUDE.md.template:11`). The teaching reference says "Do not handwrite raw C# passthrough" (`docs/syntax-reference/current-language.md:22`). The hook blocks editing the original `.cs`. On the default leg of the round-trip harness the native-file floors are 5 of 32 (MediatR), 5 of 139 (FluentValidation) and 10 of 112 (Serilog) (`native_fraction` 0.156, 0.036 and 0.089 under `blocking_floors.default` in `eng/roundtrip-baselines.json`; the file totals are in `docs/plans/2026-11-16-milestone-0.30-ci-triage.md:363-365`). The fraction counts files converted with no recorded loss (`tools/Calor.RoundTrip.Harness/RoundTripReport.cs:512-531`), so on that leg most files of a project either hold at least one recorded loss or were not converted.

This is part 1. It takes what can be done with one validator change, one measurement and text. Part 2 (epic #1819, in 0.33) takes what needs compiler work: tests written in `.calr` and the remaining incremental-reuse tier.

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1809 | Agents may create and edit C# test files under `tests/`: one exemption in the write-hook validator, the rule text, and messages that name the path. A 0.32 exit criterion |
| #1732 | Verify the shipped fix against its acceptance criteria, correct the stale release note, close; what remains goes to #1836 |
| #1818 | Edit-to-diagnostic time on 0.30 for the MCP write path, `dotnet build` and `calor check`, each with a budget; a nightly CI job; the sizing input for #1836 |
| #1822 | One sanctioned, tested procedure for changing converter-preserved C#, stated the same way by the template rule, the teaching reference and the hook (may slip) |

## Sequence

1. #1732 and #1818 have no prerequisite and can start when 0.32 opens. Part 1 of #1809 (validator and messages) depends on no issue, but merges only after the commit pin of stage 2 of #1605, or after #1605 records stage 2 as not run, so that stage 2 is measured on the unexempted hook.
2. Part 2 of #1809 (rule text) and #1822 follow #1823, which sets the `calor init` delivery default and the token budgets their text must fit.
3. #1809 and #1822 both change `HookCommand.ValidateWriteWithReason` and the rule text in `reference.json`. Whichever merges second rebases on the first.
4. The Calor text that #1818 adds (the sources for its timed project and its 0.30 edit script) and the Calor literals in the tests of #1809 and #1822 are 0.30 text. Whatever exists before the single rewrite (#1803) merges is part of that rewrite's inventory.

## Done when

- #1809 is closed. This is the 0.32 exit criterion "Agents may create test files through the sanctioned path": it needs both the write-hook exemption and the rule text in whichever of the agent file and the MCP server instructions the #1823 record leaves carrying the rules.
- #1732 is closed as completed, and the 0.30.0 entry "`dotnet build` recompiles every Calor file after any edit" carries a dated correction in `CHANGELOG.md` and in `website/content/changelog.mdx`.
- The latency record of #1818 is published with the three paths reported separately, each budgeted quantity is marked within or over, the nightly job runs, and #1836 carries the figures it is sized by.
- #1822 is closed, or it is moved to 0.33 with a comment that says so. It is off the 0.32 exit chain.

## Not in this epic

- Tests written in `.calr`, and discovery beyond top-level `tests/*.cs`: #1825 (0.33).
- Making any feedback path faster: #1836 (0.33). Index build time: #1738 (0.31).
- The `calor init` delivery default and every token budget constant: #1823. The always-on MCP budget: #1824.
- Tests on what `calor init` writes for each agent, including the test-authoring path: #1650 (0.33).
- Reducing how many files are preserved: #1647 and epic #1659. Preserved originals that fail under their own nullable context (CS8669): #1782.
- Counting how often agents were blocked when creating a test file in the #1605 run: #1760.
- Two follow-ups that no issue owns:
  - Sparing a caller from recompilation when only a callee's declared effect row changes (criterion 5 of #1732 and the "while the caller is skipped" clause of its criterion 3). #1836 covers body-only edits and does not build this tier.
  - Receipt handling in the MCP tools `calor_convert` and `calor_migrate`, which write `.calr` files without reading or writing the conversion receipt that `calor convert` and `calor migrate` check. #1822 names one entry point for its procedure and documents the mismatch; it does not remove it.

epics.title: [0.32] Epic: act on the delivery measurement — calor init default, budgets, teaching reference
epics.body:
## Goal

At the close of 0.32, what `calor init` writes by default and the token budgets on the text an agent loads every turn are decisions on record, taken from the 0.31 delivery measurement by the rules registered before that measurement ran. Each agent client other than Claude Code has a recorded answer to whether it can read `calor://primer`. The full teaching reference is trimmed only after the measurement that read it.

Terms. The *primer* is the syntax sheet the MCP server offers as the resource `calor://primer`. The *agent file* is the instruction file `calor init` writes for an agent (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`). *Stage 2* is the part of the 0.30 evaluation (#1605) that runs inside `calor init` workspaces and compares four ways of delivering the primer: a pointer to it (as shipped), the primer inlined in the agent file, inlined plus a starter file, and inlined with no MCP server.

## Why

- **The one measured lever ships behind a pointer nobody has tested.** In July 2026, on the pre-0.30 syntax, a syntax sheet of about 60 lines in the prompt removed 55% of the excess iterations of writing new Calor (`bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/e1a-attribution/VERDICT.md:13-28`). In 0.30 the agent file says "Read `calor://primer`" (`src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Templates/CLAUDE.md.template:9`) and the primer exists only as an MCP resource (`src/Calor.Compiler/Mcp/McpMessageHandler.cs:124-130`). Stage 2 measures whether agents follow the pointer and whether the MCP server earns what it costs on every turn. The rules for reading both results are fixed in advance by the registration #1770. This epic is where those rules are applied.
- **Every teaching surface is at its ceiling.** In o200k tokens, the offline proxy for Claude's tokenizer that the budget tests count with (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/TokenBudgetTests.cs:10-25`; measured 2026-11-20, `:41-71`): agent file plus MCP server instructions 592 of 600; primer 1,569 of 1,600; full reference 16,750 of 17,000; always-on MCP surface 7,900 of 8,000. #1809 and #1822 add rule text in 0.32, #1650 and #1825 add or reword always-loaded text in 0.33, and the 0.34 conversion work adds forms to the reference. Each needs a decided budget to fit into.
- **Stage 2 measures one client.** It runs Claude Code only. For Codex, Gemini CLI and Copilot the repository holds one manual Codex session from July, on the pre-0.30 syntax (`bench/phase0-agent-native/CODEX-SMOKE.md:27`). A pointer to a resource the client cannot read delivers nothing, so that capability is recorded before the default is decided.
- **#1734 rewrites the reference that #1605 measures.** It moved out of 0.31 so that the measured arm and the trimmed text are not confused. It ranks below the delivery decision: #1605 puts the July effect of the syntax sheet at about 1.1M input tokens per run and the effect of cutting 1.7K always-on tokens at 30K to 55K, and the full reference is not even always-on.

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1820 | A script and one short session per client that records whether Codex CLI, Gemini CLI and Copilot (VS Code agent mode, the client `calor init --ai github` configures) can list and read `calor://primer`; client limits documented |
| #1823 | Decision record (`docs/plans/0.32-delivery-and-budget-record.md`): the `calor init` default (pointer or inlined primer, starter file or not) per agent, what the agent file and the MCP server instructions may repeat, the budget constants, the division of the remaining always-loaded headroom among #1809, #1822, #1650 and #1825, and where conversion-only forms are documented; then the default and constants are changed to match. A 0.32 exit criterion |
| #1824 | Conditional: the always-on MCP budget recorded, or the tool surface reduced, as the registered MCP rule reads; closed as not planned if stage 2 did not run |
| #1734 | Trim the full teaching reference toward the #1597 estimate without touching an example program (moved from 0.31; may slip) |

## Sequence

1. #1820 has no prerequisite and starts when 0.32 opens. Its table must be merged before #1823 is decided.
2. #1823 waits for stage 2 of #1605 to be published or recorded as not run (a 0.31 record of "no paid run authorised" is such a record), for #1820, and for the `calor init` options #1773 built in 0.31. #1809 (rule text), #1822, #1734 and #1650 wait for it, because their text must fit the budgets it sets.
3. #1824 waits for the same stage 2 record. It does not wait for #1823, and writes its section into the same record file.
4. #1734 is last: after #1745 (0.31) so that a trim which breaks an example fails CI, and after #1823 so that it knows where conversion material goes.

## Done when

- The #1820 table in `docs/cli/mcp.md` is merged with an outcome for each of Codex CLI, Gemini CLI and Copilot in VS Code agent mode.
- #1823 is closed: `docs/plans/0.32-delivery-and-budget-record.md` holds a dated decision on each of its five points, and `calor init` and `TokenBudgetTests` match it. This is the 0.32 exit criterion "calor init delivery default decided".
- #1824 is closed as completed (budget recorded, or surface reduced and the ratchet lowered) or as not planned with a link to the "stage 2 not run" record.
- #1734 is closed, or moved to 0.33 with a comment that says so. It is off the 0.32 exit chain.

## Not in this epic

- Registering the rules and running stage 2: #1770 and #1605 (0.31).
- Building the `calor init` delivery and starter options, and serving the primer through `calor_help` and the CLI: #1773 and #1771 (0.31).
- The rule text about test files and about converter-preserved C#: #1809 and #1822 (epic #1804). They fit the budgets this epic sets.
- Per-agent generation of the agent files, per-agent tokenizers and tests on what `calor init` writes: #1650 (0.33).
- Whether each agent reads the primer when only the agent file tells it to: #1811 (0.33, if its spend is authorised; drivers in #1651). Client compatibility beyond the resource check: #1652 (0.33).
- Follow-up with no owner: a second measurement of an MCP-enabled arm against a CLI-only arm after stage 2. No 0.33 issue runs one; it exists only if the maintainer lists it under Part C of the #1832 record.
- New example programs for agents: #1835 (0.33).
- Any change to a language spelling: epic #1787.

epics.title: [0.33] Epic: agent reach
epics.body:
## Goal

Make Calor a first-class language for every major coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and GitHub Copilot) and show it with measurements taken the same way for each.

## Why

Through 0.32 every agent measurement of Calor is a Claude Code measurement. The pair harness (`bench/phase0-agent-native/run-pair.sh`) starts only the `claude` CLI, and its initialized-workspace mode runs `calor init --ai claude`. `calor init` already writes a setup for four agents, but the four instruction files are byte-identical and are budgeted with one proxy tokenizer. Of the three setups other than Claude Code's, only Codex's has been exercised by its own agent: once, in July 2026 on the pre-0.30 syntax, where the generated write hooks did not fire.

The epic sits after 0.32 because launching earlier would teach agents a language that is about to change. The edition now enforces that reason: 0.33 opens on the edition declared in #1805, or on its recorded deferral. Either way no issue in this epic changes an existing spelling, and whatever each agent reveals about the language is recorded for the re-affirmation in #1846.

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1650 | `calor init` per agent: per-agent differences declared in the single reference, a token count per agent, tests on what `calor init` writes (including the test-authoring path), and documentation that lists what each initializer writes |
| #1651 | A driver contract in the pair harness with the Claude Code driver moved behind it, drivers for Codex, Gemini and Copilot, and a zero-cost pass per driver. No spend |
| #1811 | Run the C# and Calor arms for each agent on those drivers and publish the results. Conditional on Part A (the per-agent runs) of the #1832 record |
| #1652 | MCP server compatibility checks across agent clients, in CI |
| #709 | Codex support validated by a Codex-driven smoke run, or its hook limit recorded |
| #711 | Gemini support validated by a Gemini-driven smoke run, or its hook limit recorded |

## Sequence

1. Five 0.32 issues come first: #1823 (delivery default and budget constants; a 0.33 entry criterion), #1809 (agents may create test files under `tests/`), #1799 (tokenizer tooling), #1820 (which clients can read MCP resources) and #1815 (the epoch driver that interleaves arms and stops on a spend ceiling). #1650 builds on the first three, #1652 on #1820, and #1651 on the last two.
2. #1827 (arm abstraction, epic #1817) merges before #1651 starts. Both restructure the same 1,893-line script, `bench/phase0-agent-native/run-pair.sh`.
3. #1651 needs no spend decision. It merges whatever #1832 records, because #1709 and #1710 reuse its drivers in 0.37.
4. #1832 is recorded before any paid run. #1811 reads the Part A line for each agent; #709 and #711 each read their own Part C line. Filing or keeping these issues does not authorise spend.
5. #1650 and #1651 merge before #1811, #709 or #711 starts, so that each agent is measured through its driver in the workspace its own `calor init` ships.
6. The smoke runs of #709 and #711 are the first live runs of the Codex and Gemini drivers. They need no tooling of their own.
7. #1652 depends only on #1820 and has no ordering constraint inside the epic. The correction of the `calor://workflows` arguments is made in 0.31 by #1772; #1652 adds the test that keeps it corrected.
8. #1846 (epic #1826) reads #1650 and the outcome of #1811 after both close.

## Done when

- `calor init` writes a budgeted, tested and documented setup for each of the four agents (#1650).
- Codex, Gemini and Copilot each have a driver in the pair harness that passes the zero-cost pass, or, for Copilot only, a recorded "not measurable headlessly" (#1651).
- Per-agent results for Codex, Gemini and Copilot are published from one harness in the 0.33 release notes and the evidence ledger, including any agent where Calor does worse than C# (#1811); or the maintainer's decline of that spend is recorded in #1832 and #1811 is closed as not planned with the record linked.
- Each listed MCP client passes the compatibility checks in CI, or its limit is documented (#1652).
- #709 and #711 are closed, each on one of the outcomes its done-when lists.

## Not in this epic

- The arm abstraction, the language-neutral oracle and the Rust reading (epic #1817).
- The spend decision for every paid run named here (#1832).
- Whether a client can read MCP resources (#1820), the `calor init` delivery default (#1823), and the hook exemption for `tests/` together with the wording of the hook's block message (#1809); all three are 0.32.
- Tests written in `.calr` (#1825) and the example bank (#1835).
- The three conditions of the 0.37 comparison (#1709, #1710), which reuse the drivers.
- Any change to an existing spelling. A per-agent result that argues for one is recorded for #1846; after the edition only additive syntax is allowed.
- Ranking one agent against another. Models and CLIs differ, so results are read within an agent, Calor against C#.

epics.title: [0.33] Epic: arm abstraction, a language-neutral oracle, and the Rust cost reference
epics.body:
## Goal

Let the pair harness run an arm in a language other than Calor or C#, grade every arm with one held-out suite that does not depend on .NET, and use both to take one Rust reading of authoring cost. The reading is reported, not adjudicated, and no issue waits on its value.

An *arm* is one condition of an experiment (here, a language). A *zero-cost run* is `run-pair.sh --null-agent`, which applies the reference solution instead of calling an agent.

## Why

Rust is the maintainer's reference bar and nothing in the repository measures against it: the word appears in two tracked files (`git grep -Il -w Rust`: `docs/plans/agent-native-strategy.md:210`, `website/src/components/landing/CompetitivePositioning.tsx:34`), neither a measurement. The harness cannot take the measurement today. `bench/phase0-agent-native/run-pair.sh:282` rejects any arm but `calor` or `csharp`, iterations are counted by a `dotnet` wrapper on `PATH` (`:20-23`), and grading is an xUnit project on the arm's `Src.dll` through a per-arm C# shim (`:780-807`).

#1709 ("the same black-box oracle") and #1710 (three conditions) need the same two pieces whatever happens with Rust, and #1651 restructures the same 1,893-line script (`wc -l`) in this milestone to abstract the agent driver. #1815 (0.32) already adds a first arm definition outside `pair.json` for a second C# configuration. Building the arm abstraction once, on that definition and before #1651, avoids two mechanisms and two competing restructures.

On the only two pairs where Calor has paid a measured penalty, C# was first-try green in 60 of 60 runs (`bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/e1a-attribution/VERDICT.md:65`; July 2026, pre-0.30 syntax). A Rust arm can only tie or lose on iterations there, so the reading is declared in advance to measure cost distance only. 0.33 also carries the first paid runs on other vendors' agents (#1811, on the drivers from #1651); #1832 registers every paid run of the milestone and gives each a decline branch, so 0.33 can exit either way.

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1827 | Arm abstraction in the pair harness: arm types declared by definition files, extending the arm definition from #1815; `calor` and `csharp` ported with unchanged results |
| #1830 | Language-neutral, process-level oracle, and two tasks with measured headroom that use it |
| #1829 | External anchor: published per-language agent results and what they do not show (documentation only) |
| #1828 | Rust arm: fixtures, `cargo` iteration shim, pinned toolchain, zero-cost pass (conditional on the Rust part of #1832) |
| #1832 | Decision: register and authorise the 0.33 paid runs (the per-agent runs of #1811, the Rust reading, any other paid run), registered in Annex A of `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md` |
| #1831 | Run and report the Rust cost reading (conditional on the Rust part of #1832) |

## Sequence

1. #1827 first, after #1815 (0.32), whose arm definition it extends. It merges before #1651 starts its driver abstraction, because both restructure `run-pair.sh`.
2. #1829 at any time. It needs no code, and #1832 cites it.
3. #1830 after #1827: the oracle plugs into the grader slot the arm type definition creates.
4. #1832 once #1829 is merged, #1830 has fixed the task ids and #1605's realised costs exist. Its parts may be signed on different dates; the Rust part is decided before #1828 starts, so that no Rust fixture is built for a run that is then declined.
5. #1828 after #1827, #1830 and the Rust part of #1832, and only if that part is not declined (or the record keeps the fixtures for #1709).
6. #1831 last, and only on the authorise branch of the Rust part of #1832.

Driver and fixture work for the other agents (#1651) does not wait for #1832; only paid runs do.

## Done when

- `run-pair.sh` runs any arm whose arm type has a definition, the `calor` and `csharp` arms give the same `result.json` fields as before, and the #1815 arm definitions still resolve (#1827).
- Two tasks are graded for `csharp` and `calor` from one vectors file through a process boundary, with committed determinism and control evidence (#1830).
- The external anchor document is merged (#1829).
- The 0.33 paid-run record carries a dated decision for each part and is registered in Annex A of `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md` with the `annex-freeze` job green (#1832). This is the spend record in the 0.33 decisions list.
- The `rust` arm's zero-cost log is committed, or #1828 is closed as not planned with the record linked.
- The Rust cost reading is reported in the 0.33 release notes, in the evidence ledger and on the capability scorecard of the plan of record, or #1831 is closed as not planned with the reason in the record. Either satisfies the 0.33 exit criterion "Rust cost reference reported, or the decision not to run it recorded with the reason".

## Not in this epic

- Agent drivers for Codex, Gemini and Copilot: #1651, after #1827. The paid per-agent runs and their publication: #1811.
- The equipped C# arm (C# with executable specifications): #1815, #1813 and #1709.
- Rust as a gating comparator, a Rust-plus-verifier arm, or Rust as an emission target (#1719).
- A fourth, non-gating Rust condition in the 0.37 comparison: #1709, budget inside #1867.
- Any comparison of the reading with #1605 or another epoch.
- Moving the seeded-defect pairs or the paused PP-W pairs onto the new oracle.

epics.title: [0.33] Epic: one toolchain (part 2) — tests in Calor, incremental reuse, fewer unknown effects
epics.body:
## Goal

Finish the toolchain work that part 1 (epic #1804, in 0.32) could not do with a hook exemption and a measurement. An agent can write its tests in Calor. Where the 0.32 latency measurement shows a warm edit over its budget, the tools stop recompiling files the edit cannot affect. The library calls that most often force `! unknown` on the corpus get exact effect rows.

## Why

The plan of record (`docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md`, section 3) keeps a scorecard of what a Rust user takes for granted. Two of its lines are toolchain gaps at 0.30.0: tests cannot be written in the language, and warm feedback is unmeasured. A third gap is not a scorecard line. Effect rows are the feature other languages lack, and a call to a framework member with no effect contract is charged `unknown`; a function that declares `! unknown` is not effect-checked, and every caller above it has to declare the same row.

0.32 takes the minimum for each. Agents may create C# test files (#1809), warm latency is measured and budgeted (#1818), and the unknown share is reported per corpus project (#1802). Each of those produces the input that one issue here needs, which is why this half is in 0.33.

The epic runs after the edition is declared (#1805), so no existing spelling changes and no issue here adds a hard error. One change is not purely additive: #1825 changes what a file location means, because a `tests/*.calr` file stops being library source. The declaration settles whether its promise covers such tool-layout changes, and #1825 reads that wording before it starts.

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1825 | `calor test`, `calor check` and `calor_check` discover tests written in `.calr`; one compiled teaching example. A 0.33 exit criterion |
| #1836 | Conditional: the remaining incremental reuse tier, and reuse inside `calor check`, each only where the #1818 measurement is over budget (may slip) |
| #1841 | Exact effect contracts for the callee families behind most unknown-charged call sites, selected from the #1802 report (may slip) |

## Sequence

1. The three issues do not depend on one another and can run in parallel.
2. #1825 starts when #1809 has merged, because it edits the rule text and the "No tests found" messages that issue writes.
3. #1836 starts when #1818 has posted its figures, because they decide whether there is any work.
4. #1841 starts when #1802 has reported and #1731 and #1798 are closed. The report selects the families, #1731 changes built-in contracts and with them the count, and #1798 adds the compile checks on teaching statements that this issue has to keep passing.
5. #1825 and #1650 may merge in either order; whichever merges second adds the `.calr` case to the per-agent init tests. #1846 lists the #1825 change and is prepared after it closes.

## Done when

- #1825 is closed: a directory whose only tests are `.calr` files passes `calor check` and `calor test` with exit code 0 in CI tests, and the teaching reference carries one test example that CI compiles and runs. This is the 0.33 exit criterion "calor test and calor check discover tests written in .calr". If #1825 is held because the edition promise covers tool layout, the criterion is met instead by the record that states the hold and what the release does. The scorecard line "Tests written in the language" in section 3 of `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md` is updated at the 0.33 close.
- #1836 is closed under its gate: either the work is merged for every quantity that was over budget, or the issue is closed as not planned with the latency record linked. Otherwise it is moved to the next milestone with a comment that says why. It is off the 0.33 exit chain.
- #1841 is closed: the corpus report shows unknown-charged call sites down by the share recorded on the issue, or the issue is closed as not planned with its selection record linked. Otherwise it is moved to the next milestone with a comment. It is off the 0.33 exit chain.
- `TokenBudgetTests` passes with no budget constant raised by any of the three.

## Not in this epic

- Letting agents create C# test files under `tests/` (#1809, 0.32).
- Verifying and closing #1732 and correcting `CHANGELOG.md:354-359` (0.32).
- Measuring warm latency and setting its budgets (#1818, 0.32). Index build time (#1738, 0.31).
- Producing the unknown-share report (#1802), the soundness of built-in contracts (#1731) and compile checks on "remains unknown" teaching statements (#1798), all 0.32.
- The example bank (#1835) and the per-agent `calor init` tests (#1650).
- Any change to an existing spelling, and any new reserved word.
- Follow-up with no issue: sparing a caller from recompilation when only a callee's declared effect row changes. Criterion 5 of #1732 and the "while the caller is skipped" clause of its criterion 3 need this tier; #1836 does not build it.
- Follow-up with no issue: test files in an MSBuild project. `Calor.Sdk` compiles every `**/*.calr` (`src/Calor.Sdk/Sdk/Sdk.props:19`) and the .NET SDK every `**/*.cs`, so a test under `tests/` (C# under #1809, Calor under #1825) is compiled into the product project by `dotnet build`, where xUnit is not referenced. Needed: exclude top-level `tests/` from the default items, or state the supported layout for `calor init` projects, and run `dotnet build` beside `calor check` in the #1650 case.

epics.title: [0.33] Epic: the in-context example bank
epics.body:
## Goal

Put working Calor in front of the agent while it works: grow the compiler-checked teaching programs into an example bank indexed by construct and by task shape, serve it through `calor_help` and the `calor init` starter file, and write down which Calor source the project publishes at all.

## Why

No model has a training prior for Calor, and nothing on this roadmap waits for one. The strategy puts the prior at "~zero Calor" (`docs/plans/agent-native-strategy.md:80`), and 0.20.0 to 0.30.0 took 72 days (`CHANGELOG.md:7`, `:2019`); the plan's premise is that 0.31 to 0.39 is shorter than a model training cycle. A published corpus therefore cannot change any result here, and no criterion in this epic depends on a model having learned Calor.

What can change a result is the text the agent reads during the task. In July 2026, on the pre-0.30 syntax, a syntax sheet of about 60 lines appended to the prompt (the exemplar) cut the iterations an agent needed to write new Calor from 2.38 to 1.62 times the C# figure, pooled over two tasks (`bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/e1a-attribution/VERDICT.md:13-17`). The same run showed what an example of the wrong shape costs: one exemplar line led 29 of 30 runs on one task into a first build that could not pass (`:43-51`).

Two constraints shape the work. The agent surfaces are at their CI token budgets, measured in o200k tokens on 2026-11-20: each `calor init` template plus the MCP server instructions is at 592 of 600, the always-on MCP surface at 7,900 of 8,000, and the full reference at 16,750 of a 17,000 ratchet (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/TokenBudgetTests.cs:41-47`, `:65-71`, `:57-63`). The bank therefore grows behind on-demand lookups and not inside the reference. Any paid measurement of the bank needs a dated line in the #1832 record, with a spend ceiling, abort triggers, a zero-cost pass, one pinned model and a reading written in advance for each outcome.

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1835 | Example bank: index, coverage by construct and by task shape, CI execution, serving through `calor_help` and the `calor init` starter, and the zero-cost half of its measurement |
| #1839 | Admission rule for public Calor: original, formatted, lint-clean, run in CI; converted open-source code stays unpublished |

## Sequence

1. Earlier milestones supply the inputs. #1745 (0.31) adds the check that executes each teaching program against a recorded expectation, and #1835 reuses it. #1760 (0.31) supplies the report script and the definition of first-build pass rate. #1773 (0.31) and #1823 (0.32) supply the `calor init` starter option and its default. #1765 and #1763 (0.31) supply the plan of record and the legacy-dialect allowlist that the #1839 page links and names.
2. Parts 1 to 4 of #1835 need no spend decision. Its closing record waits for the #1832 line that lists, omits or declines an example-bank measurement.
3. #1839 is text-only and can be written at any point in 0.33. #1835 applies the same four admission conditions to bank programs through its own tests, so neither issue waits for the other.
4. No 0.33 exit criterion names either issue. Each may slip to 0.34 without holding the release.

## Done when

- #1835 is closed: the bank meets its coverage floor, every bank program with an expectation is executed in CI, `calor_help` and the `calor init` starter serve it, and the tokens it adds are stated against `TokenBudgetTests`.
- #1839 is closed: the admission rule is published with its enforcement table and one recorded audit.
- At the 0.33 close, the scorecard line "A reference the agent already knows" in `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md` states the size of the bank and whether its effect was measured.

## Not in this epic

- How the primer reaches the agent and what `calor init` writes by default (#1773, #1771, #1823).
- Executing the existing reference examples (#1745) and trimming the full reference (#1734).
- Whether a redundant `public` is canonical (#1796), and the legacy-dialect allowlist (#1763).
- The canonical-usage lint on converted output (#1747) and converter statement hoists (#1742), both 0.34.
- The teaching example for tests written in `.calr` (#1825 adds its own).
- Authorising spend (#1832) and the per-agent runs (#1811).
- Publishing a training corpus or dataset, and publishing converted open-source code.
- Three follow-ups that no issue owns; #1839 records each gap in its enforcement table or its audit:
  - a CI step that runs `calor format --check` and `calor lint --check` over `samples/` and over the complete programs in `docs/` and `website/content/`;
  - correcting the public files that the #1839 audit finds failing (that issue files one follow-up for them);
  - the per-file licence and notice manifest and the converter test that a header comment survives conversion, both needed only if the maintainer decides to publish converted code.

epics.title: [0.33] Epic: identity and rename tooling
epics.body:
## Goal

Every rename or move of a declaration made through a tool (MCP `calor_file_write`, `calor rename`, editor rename) either keeps its ID in the tooling sidecar (`.calor/ids.json`) or refuses with a message that says why. What a plain text edit followed by `calor ids sync` does to an ID is pinned and documented. Each outcome has a test, and the website tells a user which tool to use for which operation.

## Why

0.30 moved declaration IDs out of source and into the sidecar. Diagnostics (`declarationId` in the diagnostic envelope), `calor verify --weakening-check` and the declaration index (`calor ids index`) all address a declaration by that ID, so a rename that silently mints a new one detaches whatever pointed at the old one.

Three issues were left open after 0.30. The 0.31 re-baseline moved #1744 and #1748 out of 0.31 because no 0.31 exit criterion needs them. The plan of record (`docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md`) has every new issue name the issue it takes capacity from, and their 0.31 capacity went to #1764 and #1771. #922 was one of eleven open issues with no milestone. The three are grouped here, apart from the toolchain epic #1819, because they share one subject and nothing else in 0.33 depends on them.

All three bodies are stale against HEAD bc80daeb. #922 was written before 0.30; #1744 and #1748 were written against `main` at e2deb8805 (their first lines say so). Most of what they ask for exists at HEAD: editor rename already carries the sidecar, MCP and store-level moves already keep identity, a file label renames on its own, and the website already has a page on the identity model. The amendments below narrow each issue to what is still missing.

Nothing in this epic changes what the compiler accepts, so the edition (#1805) is unaffected. The epic is not on the 0.33 exit chain: any of the three issues may slip to 0.34 without holding the release.

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1744 | Close the remaining identity gaps: MCP class rename (rename it, or refuse with a sentence), `calor rename` and editor capability negotiation under test, text moves pinned |
| #922 | Editor rename edits every part of a type declared across files |
| #1748 | Website: a how-to for renaming and moving, a per-tool support table, a reference page for `calor rename` |

The three issues have no required order and no dependency on each other. The support table that #1748 publishes describes the tools as they are at the commit it lands on; if #1744 or #922 changes behaviour after that, the same pull request updates the table, and both issues say so in their done-when.

## Done when

- #1744, #922 and #1748 are each closed, or moved to 0.34 with one sentence on the issue saying why.
- `docs/ids.md` states, per tool, which renames and moves keep the ID and which are refused, and each statement is backed by a named test. Once #1748 has closed, the website's support table says the same.

## Not in this epic

- The sidecar format, the meaning of `calor ids sync` and `calor ids check`, and the reconcile rules (`DeclarationIdentityStore.Reconcile`). #1744 pins existing behaviour with tests; it does not change the rules.
- Renaming a type declared across files through MCP or `calor rename`. That engine keeps its `SplitDeclaration` refusal; #922 covers the editor only.
- Follow-up, no issue: renaming a namespace (the second name on a `module` header and the `using` directives that name it). By reading, neither rename index records a namespace name as an occurrence.
- Follow-up, no issue: making `calor ids sync` report or refuse when a text edit drops an ID and mints a new one. Today it prints only a count (`src/Calor.Compiler/Commands/IdsCommand.cs:52`). #1744 pins and documents that outcome and does not change it.
- Follow-up, no issue, only if #1744 closes on its outcome B: renaming a type through MCP or `calor rename`, which needs type references in `ProjectSymbolIndex`.
- MCP compatibility across agent clients (#1652) and per-agent `calor init` output (#1650), both in epic #1653.

epics.title: [0.33] Epic: checkpoints at the close of 0.33
epics.body:
## Goal

Record two dated maintainer decisions before 0.33 is released. What milestones 0.34 to 0.39 contain depends on both.

- **Adopter checkpoint.** Either a named external maintainer has agreed in writing to the 0.36 pilot, or "demand unproven" is recorded and the fallback written in advance in the plan of record (`docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md`) applies.
- **Edition re-affirmation.** After the first results from agents other than Claude Code, the edition declared at the end of 0.32 stands, with everything that changed since the declaration listed and classified; or the edition is declared here after a 0.32 deferral; or the record says what happens instead.

Each decision is recorded in one document under `docs/plans/`, prepared by an agent and decided by the maintainer's merge. The adopter record is then applied to the tracker as comments, holds and closures. Nothing in this epic changes the compiler, spends money, or has an agent contact anyone.

## Why

- **The adopter.** 0.36 needs "a named external maintainer" and treats a missing one as "a blocker, not replaced by creator self-evaluation" (#1701). 0.37 takes its final tasks from that pilot (#1708), and 0.38 and 0.39 consume the 0.37 verdict (#1699, #1700). The repository records no adopter and no authorised outreach: the one authorisation on record permitted no contacts, and "Contacts made" is 0 (`docs/plans/safe-delegation-m0/v0.23/r2a-adopter-unavailable.md:25-30`). Without a date, the absence is found at the start of 0.36, after 0.34 and 0.35 have been scoped for a pilot that does not exist. The checkpoint puts the date at the close of 0.33, and its else-branch is a table written in 0.31 that names the issues it holds, re-scopes or closes.
- **The edition.** The edition is declared at the end of 0.32 (#1805) on spellings that only Claude Code has run. 0.33 is where Codex, Gemini and Copilot first run them (#1650, #1651, #1811), and where one change to what a file location means lands after the declaration (#1825). The first external maintainer signs off on the compatibility promise (#1701), and 0.36 requires the edition in force. The close of 0.33 is the last point at which a problem with a spelling can be put on record before someone outside the project depends on it.

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1833 | Decision: the adopter checkpoint. Consent of a named external maintainer recorded, or "demand unproven" recorded and the adopter fallback applied to the tracker |
| #1846 | Decision: re-affirm the edition. Changes since the declaration classified, per-agent findings dispositioned, the #1825 tool-layout change listed |

## Sequence

1. #1833 needs two things from 0.31: the adopter fallback in the plan of record (#1765) and the outreach decision with its contact log (#1777). #1846 needs the declaration record from 0.32 (#1805).
2. Both are the last work of the milestone and are put to the maintainer in one sitting; `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39/0.33.md` lists them as one batch of decisions.
3. #1833 reads the contact log up to its own date, so it is prepared after the three 0.33 exit criteria that other epics own (per-agent results, the Rust cost reference, `.calr` test discovery) are met or their declines are recorded.
4. #1846 is prepared after #1650 and #1811 (published, or closed on a recorded decline) are closed and #1825 is closed or held under its tool-layout gate.
5. Neither waits for the other.

## Done when

- `docs/plans/0.33-adopter-checkpoint.md` is merged by the maintainer with exactly one of its two outcomes, and the tracker comments it requires are posted (#1833). This meets the 0.33 exit criterion "Adopter checkpoint recorded (#1833), or 'not decided, treated as the fallback outcome until changed'" and the 0.34 entry criterion that reads it. If the record is not merged when the release is prepared, the default line #1833 defines meets the exit criterion and #1833 stays open.
- `docs/plans/0.33-edition-reaffirmation.md` is merged by the maintainer with one dated decision line (#1846). The 0.33 exit criterion reads "Edition re-affirmed after #1650 and the per-agent results report, or declared here after a 0.32 deferral, or a second deferral recorded with its effect on 0.36 entry". Decision A or B meets its first branch; where the declaration was deferred, the record meets the second or third. If the record says that a spelling changes (Decision C), or that #1825 is held because the promise covers tool layout, the criterion is met by the record stating what the 0.33 release does.

## Not in this epic

- Writing the adopter fallback (#1765), authorising outreach (#1777) and opening the recruitment record (#1791).
- Approving the pilot's scope, acceptance criteria and baseline (#1701).
- The methods reviewer (#1777, #1857) and any collection budget (#1867).
- Declaring the edition and writing the promise (#1805), the marker (#1084) and the rewriter (#1806).
- The per-agent runs and their spend (#1811, #1832), and test discovery for `.calr` files (#1825).
- Any compiler change, any change to a spelling, any paid run, any contact made by an agent.
- Follow-up with no owning issue: a CI job that compiles a pinned snapshot of edition sources (for example the teaching programs at the edition commit) with the current compiler and fails on a new rejection. #1846 does that check once, by hand.
- A second-edition proposal, if #1846 files one (Decision B). It is backlog: it has no milestone and claims no capacity until a later milestone names what it displaces.

epics.title: [0.34] Epic: native conversion coverage
epics.body:
## Goal

Convert more C# natively, measured against a baseline restated on 0.30.0, and leave no unsupported construct without an owner. Since 0.30 every C# file that parses is migrated (#1609, `CHANGELOG.md:107-113`); each construct the converter cannot express is kept as preserved C# (the original text inside a raw frame in the `.calr` file). Preserved code costs more tokens than the C# it wraps (5% to 10% for a file preserved whole, measured by hand in #1746), and Calor's effect, contract and nullability checks do not apply to it.

## Why

The previous body of this epic described the converter before 0.30.0:

- It counted 48 unsupported entries. At HEAD bc80daeb the registry `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/FeatureSupport.cs` has 184 entries: 96 `Full`, 30 `Partial`, 58 `NotSupported`. The committed export `website/public/data/feature-support.json` carries the same counts and is kept equal to the registry by `WebsiteFeatureSupportParityTests.TheWebsiteExportIsTheRegistry` (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/WebsiteFeatureSupportParityTests.cs:239`).
- Record classes (`record`, `FeatureSupport.cs:60-66`) and `lock` (`lock-statement`, `:621-626`) are already `Full`. Three entries listed under #1658 are `Full` and two are `Partial`.
- 23 of the 58 entries were named in no child issue, so "each family converts or has a recorded reason" could not be evaluated.
- The conversion scorecard already reports 100 of 100 snippets fully converted (`tests/Calor.Evaluation/Scorecard/ConversionScorecardTests.cs:31`), so it can act only as a floor: it shows a coverage gain only when a snippet is added.
- The density target depends on how much of a project is native, and the one measurement on record was taken with MediatR and Serilog preserved whole (#1746). The target is therefore read after this coverage work (#1844), not before it.

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1654 | Record structs and the record shapes still preserved (record classes are native) |
| #1655 | `using` declarations, `await using`, standalone blocks, `checked` and `unchecked` blocks (`lock` is native) |
| #1656 | Interface member semantics and delegate declarations, including the registry entry `static-abstract-member` |
| #1657 | Conditional compilation and directives in the positions still preserved |
| #1658 | The 16 smaller entries that are still unsupported |
| #1850 | Disposition for the 22 entries outside the five families; the coverage record, the test that ties it to the registry, and the refresh of the scorecard baseline file |
| #1733 | Report preserved blocks whose recorded reason no longer applies, and re-convert them |
| #1747 | Canonical-usage lint on converted output for every round-trip project |
| #1742 | Nested expressions instead of statement hoists |
| #1844 | Density target: read the per-project token ratio after the work above and record the outcome |

**Entry ownership.** Every `NotSupported` entry at HEAD bc80daeb has one owner. Regenerate the list at 0.34 entry with `calor feature-check --list --level notsupported` (or read `website/public/data/feature-support.json`) and reconcile it with this table; #1850 does that as its first step, and again when #1638 closes if that is later than 0.34 entry.

| Owner | Count | Registry entries |
|---|---:|---|
| #1654 | 0 | none; it owns the `record-*` preservation reasons, which are not registry entries |
| #1655 | 3 | `using-declaration`, `await-using`, `standalone-block`; also `checked-block`, which is labelled `Full` but is preserved by default conversion |
| #1656 | 7 | `interface-member`, `interface-method-semantics`, `interface-property-semantics`, `interface-indexer-semantics`, `interface-semantics`, `delegate-semantics`, `static-abstract-member` |
| #1657 | 10 | `conditional-member`, `conditional-statement`, `conditional-namespace`, `conditional-top-level-statement`, `conditional-unmodeled-placement`, `top-level-directive-ordering`, `compilation-unit-using-ordering`, `warning-directive`, `error-directive`, `line-directive` |
| #1658 | 16 | `file-scoped-type`, `using-type-alias`, `extern-alias`, `compilation-unit-attribute`, `default-lambda-parameter`, `partial-property`, `iterator-accessor`, `ref-struct`, `scoped-parameter`, `string-interpolation-handler`, `string-interpolation-formattable-constant`, `unsupported-compound-assignment`, `unsupported-switch-label`, `unsupported-pattern-operator`, `unsupported-prefix-operator`, `unsupported-slice-subpattern` |
| #1850 | 22 | `array-element-block`, `pointer`, `stackalloc`, `event-subscription`, `await-foreach`, `csharp-script`, `alias-qualified-value`, `untyped-block-lambda`, `generic-attribute`, `unsupported-binary-operator`, `embedded-assignment`, `compound-assignment-order`, `compound-assignment-narrowing`, `default-member-collision`, `generic-delegate`, `conversion-error`, `unknown-expression`, `unknown-literal`, `unknown-pattern`, `nullable-directive`, `typed-reference`, `varargs` |

Entries that #1638 adds for C# 15: the union and closed-hierarchy entries belong to #1643 (epic #1852); any other entry it adds at `NotSupported` joins #1850's list. #1638 may close after 0.34 entry; the baseline is restated when it does, and the registry test #1850 delivers fails until each new `NotSupported` entry has a row.

**The coverage record.** One file, `docs/plans/0.34-native-coverage.md`, created by #1850 (a family pull request that merges first creates it with the same layout). It has three parts:

- *Registry table*: one row per baseline entry (the 58 above, the `NotSupported` entries #1638 added, and `checked-block`), with the columns entry, owner issue, occurrences per corpus project and how they were counted, outcome, reason kind, evidence.
- *Family shapes*: preservation reasons that are not registry entries but belong to a family. Today these are the `record-*` reasons of #1654. Same columns. The 0.34 exit criterion reads every row of the registry table and of this part.
- *New source forms*: for each form a child adds, the candidates considered, their token counts and the spelling chosen.

**Outcomes.** A row ends in one of two states.

- *Native*: the entry's level in `FeatureSupport.cs` is `Full`, or `Partial` with the preserved remainder named in its description and given a reason kind in the row. The promotion carries a registered fixture under `bench/phase0-agent-native/fixtures/d-s1.5/` whose `fixture.json` names the entry in `featureKey` and whose runtime value check passes (schema in the `README.md` there; `record/` is an example in current syntax). The CI job `d-s1.5-fixtures` (job id `ds15-fixtures`, `.github/workflows/test.yml:613`; script `scripts/check-d-s1.5-fixtures.sh`) fails a promotion that has no fixture, and `DS15FixtureRegistryTests.AllFixtures_AreCompleteConvertExactlyAndCompile` (`tests/Calor.Conversion.Tests/DS15FixtureRegistryTests.cs:336`) converts, compiles and runs every fixture directory. A new directory needs a case in `ExpectedOwner` in that file (`:664-690`), which throws for an unregistered name. The tests that pinned the entry's preservation are updated in the same pull request. A family-shape row has no registry key to promote; it is native when its preservation test is replaced by an assertion on native output and a runtime test.
- *Preserved, with a reason* of one of these kinds: `bucket` (a diagnostic bucket, not a C# construct; the row gives its count on the corpus); `zero-in-corpus` (no occurrence in the three corpus projects at their pins; the row says how it was counted); `unmodeled` (native conversion needs semantics Calor does not model; the row names them); `no-form` (needs a new source form and the maintainer declined or deferred the spelling; the row links the decision); `not-reached` (it occurs, was planned, and was not converted by the close of 0.34; the row gives the count and links the open issue and milestone that now carry it). A C# 15 entry whose default output needs .NET 11 types may close as `not-reached` with the cause "needs .NET 11 hosts" and a link to #1643, while the fixture hosts stay on .NET 10.

**If the adopter fallback applies.** The adopter checkpoint (#1833) is a 0.34 entry criterion. If it records that the fallback applies, the fallback table in the plan of record `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md` sets this epic's scope: #1654 to #1658 and #1850 convert natively only the constructs that cause preservation in at least one file of the three corpus projects under default `calor migrate`, as the corpus report job (#1779) reports, and every other row is recorded as preserved with the reason kind `no-demand`. That kind is valid only under the fallback.

**Rules for the family issues and for every pull request that makes a construct native.**

1. Count first. #1654 to #1658 are tracking issues, each delivered as one pull request per construct. The first pull request of each is the count: occurrences of each of its constructs in the library sources of MediatR, Serilog and FluentValidation (git submodules under `bench/corpus/`, pinned in `bench/corpus/README.md:13-17`; the three source directories are listed at `scripts/default_migrate_report.py:22-26`), written into the coverage record with the method used. Count in the original C#: a file preserved whole records no loss for the constructs inside it.
2. Use an existing canonical form where one expresses the construct. A new source form is additive: it changes no existing spelling, so it is compatible with the edition whether #1805 declares it or defers it. The child proposes the spelling under the fewest-tokens rule as #1785 amends it, the maintainer confirms it in the pull request, and the candidates, their counts and the choice go into the "New source forms" part of the coverage record. Filing a family issue decides no spelling.
3. A new form is documented in `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/Teaching/reference.json`, from which `calor self-check docs --fix` regenerates `docs/syntax-reference/current-language.md` (that file's header, `:9`). The full reference has a no-growth ratchet of 17,000 o200k tokens and measured 16,750 on 2026-11-20 (`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/TokenBudgetTests.cs:57-63`), which leaves 250 tokens. The delivery and budget record of #1823 decides whether conversion-only forms added in 0.34 are documented outside the ratcheted reference; follow it. Where a form goes into the reference, stay under the ratchet by removing the fallback sentences the change makes obsolete. Raising `FullReferenceRatchet` is a maintainer decision, not something a child pull request does on its own.
4. Regenerate `website/public/data/feature-support.json` with `calor feature-check --list` when a level or description changes.
5. Standing acceptance rule. (a) The conversion scorecard's fully converted count does not fall (100 of 100 at HEAD, `tests/Calor.Evaluation/Scorecard/ConversionScorecardTests.cs:31`, enforced by the `conversion-scorecard` job, `.github/workflows/test.yml:672`). (b) The per-project Calor/C# token ratio does not rise. It is read from the corpus report job (#1779) with the ratio columns #1746 adds or, if #1746 has slipped, by the hand method #1746 records (o200k proxy tokenizer on default project-mode `calor migrate` output). (c) The pull request states how many corpus files newly fall to whole-file preservation (a file whose loss list gains `whole-file-preservation`), and the `member-oracle` job (`.github/workflows/test.yml:1140`) reports no new difference with `eng/member-oracle-baseline.json` unchanged. Native code is checked for effects and nullability where preserved code was not, so a construct that converts but then fails a check can push its whole file back to preserved C#. The corpus report job's schedule runs on `main`; a pull request dispatches `corpus-report.yml` on `main` at its base (before) and on its branch (after), as #1779 provides, and links both runs with their rows; running `scripts/corpus_report.py` locally on both commits is accepted when the dispatch is not available. The first scheduled run after the merge confirms the rows.
6. Because the scorecard is already at 100 of 100, add one scorecard snippet per newly native construct (`tests/TestData/CSharpImport/manifest.json`) and raise `BASELINE_FULLY_CONVERTED`, `BASELINE_ROUNDTRIP`, the total asserted at `ConversionScorecardTests.cs:115` and `tests/Calor.Evaluation/Scorecard/baseline.json` with it, so that the count rises with coverage.
7. A pull request that adds or removes tests updates `expectedTotal` for that test project in `eng/test-manifest.json`; `scripts/check_trx.py` fails CI on a mismatch.

## Sequence

1. Entry. #1647 is closed and the adopter checkpoint (#1833) is recorded: these are the 0.34 entry criteria. The corpus report job (#1779) is running, because the native fraction and every child's standing-rule numbers come from it; this epic depends on #1779.
2. #1850 starts first: it restates the baseline, creates the coverage record and its registry test, and refreshes the scorecard baseline file. The family issues do not wait for it to close.
3. #1654, #1655, #1656, #1657, #1658 and #1742 in any order. Each family issue begins with its count.
4. #1733 after at least one family pull request has made a construct native, so that a real stale block exists to test against. #1747 after the family work, so the lint sees the newly native output.
5. #1844 last: it depends on #1647, #1742 and #1746 and reads the result of everything above. It is off the 0.34 exit chain and may slip to 0.35.

## Done when

- The registry table of the coverage record has one row for every entry of the restated baseline (the 58 above, the `NotSupported` entries #1638 added, and `checked-block`), the "Family shapes" part has one row for every shape #1654 lists, and each row is native or preserved with a reason as defined above. The test delivered by #1850 passes.
- Every native registry row has its registry promotion and a registered fixture, and the `d-s1.5-fixtures` job is green on `main`; if `checked-block` is native, it was demoted to `NotSupported` before it was promoted. Every native family-shape row has its preservation test replaced and a runtime test added.
- The corpus report job (#1779) reports the native file fraction for MediatR, Serilog and FluentValidation: written files with an empty `losses` list over all files, under default project-mode `calor migrate`. The closing comment on this epic quotes the native file count per project at 0.34 entry and at close, and no count is lower at close.
- The closing comment also gives, for entry and close: the scorecard's fully converted count (not lower), the token ratio per project (not higher), and the number of corpus files that newly fell to whole-file preservation during the milestone, with the cause of each.
- Every child issue is closed. #1844 alone may instead have moved to 0.35, in which case the closing comment says so.

## Not in this epic

- Restoring native conversion that regressed in 0.30: #1647 (0.32), which is this milestone's entry criterion.
- The corpus report job and the token-ratio columns: #1779 and #1746.
- C# 15 unions and closed hierarchies: #1643 (epic #1852).
- Contracts derived from converted code: the guard census and the guard-precondition decision (#1848, #1847, epic #1845). Nothing in this epic makes the converter emit contracts.
- Disposal checking: #1842 follows #1655.
- What an agent does with a preserved file: #1822.

Each such row must link an open issue in a later milestone; those issues are filed at the 0.34 close-out, and the capacity they take is recorded in the plan of record `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md` at that point.
- Option, Result and `requires` stay removed (#1617, #1618).

epics.title: [0.34] Epic: decisions and conditional steps on converted code
epics.body:
## Goal

Before 0.35 builds anything on converted code, count what converted code and agent-written code contain (throw guards, `nullable oblivious` modules, undisposed resources) and record the decisions that depend on those counts: which form of guard-derived precondition Calor adopts, if any; whether the retired real-scale benchmark venue can reopen; and what happens to the authored-contract overlay and to #1177. Every child states its gate in advance and closes as not planned, with the record linked, if the gate stays shut.

## Why

- The converter emits no contracts. Every converted function is built with `preconditions: Array.Empty<RequiresNode>()` at 16 sites in `src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/RoslynSyntaxVisitor.cs` (the first at `:2887`), and `CHANGELOG.md:39-40` says conversion does not recover contracts that exist only as `throw` guards.
- The obvious remedy, turning guards into parameter refinements, changes which exception a program throws. A failed refinement always throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` (`src/Calor.Compiler/CodeGen/CSharpEmitter.cs:6496-6497`), and four of the five leading guards in `tests/Calor.RoundTrip.Synthetic/SyntheticLib` are pinned by tests to a different type.
- A lifted precondition has almost no consumer today. Call-site obligations are generated only for module-level functions (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Obligations/ObligationGenerator.cs:58-62`) whose arguments are exactly `int` or `bool` (`:120-134`). The converter produces a module-level function only for C# top-level statements (`RoslynSyntaxVisitor.cs:293-308`); every other converted member is a class member.
- Nobody has counted. The April 2026 flow checker was reverted because the shape it targeted did not occur in converted code; its post-mortem asks for a base-rate check before building and an explicit hold outcome (`docs/design/tier1a-postmortem.md:252`, `:256`). The same applies to guards, to modules where null checks are relaxed, and to resource leaks: none has a count.
- Two questions from August 2026 were closed unresolved: the re-entry conditions of the real-scale venue (`docs/plans/call-s-adjudication.md:175-185`) and the authored-contract overlay (`:169-173`). #851 and #1177 are leftovers of that venue.

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1848 | Guard census: register the readings, then count guards by shape in the corpus and in agent outputs |
| #1847 | Decision record: which form of guard-derived precondition, if any (a 0.34 exit criterion) |
| #1834 | Count converted modules that carry `nullable oblivious`, probe which headers can be dropped, write the path to shrink the number |
| #1842 | Disposal spike after #1655: design note, count in agent outputs, go, hold or drop |
| #1854 | Feasibility record for the real-scale venue: its two registered re-entry conditions and its eligible supply |
| #851 | Task-generation filter precision; held behind #1854 |
| #1177 | `EffectViolation`: pin the contract or move the stratum; decided in the #1859 record |
| #1859 | Decision record: the authored-contract overlay (feasibility on one module, or deferral), and #1177 |

## Sequence

1. #1848, then #1847: the decision quotes the census reading. #1848 needs the corpus report job (#1779) and the restored native share (#1647).
2. #1834 at any time once the corpus report job (#1779) exists.
3. #1655 (epic #1659), then #1842: the spike needs `using` declarations to convert natively.
4. #1647, then #1854; #1854, then #851 and #1859; #1859, then #1177.

Only the first chain holds the 0.34 release. #1834, #1842, #1854, #851, #1177 and #1859 may slip to 0.35 without holding it. The maintainer decisions (#1847, the verdicts of #1842 and #1854, #1859 with #1177) can be signed in one session once the counts exist.

## Done when

- `docs/plans/0.34-guard-precondition-decision.md` is committed (#1847). This satisfies the 0.34 exit criterion "Guard-precondition decision recorded".
- Every other child is closed by its record, closed as not planned with the gate value that kept it shut, or (the six children that may slip) moved to 0.35 with a comment naming what it waits for.
- #1849, #1866 and #1870 each carry a comment saying proceed, held, or closed as not planned, with a link to the record that decided it.

## Not in this epic

- Any implementation that follows from these decisions: the fall-through fact (#1849), the opt-in guard lift (#1866), the must-dispose checker (#1870). All are 0.35 and conditional.
- Contract consumers (#1864, #1863) and the authored contracts 0.35 proves (#1843).
- The round-trip leg compiled with the default contract mode (#1795) and inherited-refinement behaviour (#1735); both are 0.32.
- Native conversion coverage and the density target (epic #1659); .NET 11 (epic #1852).
- Any paid agent run, and any reopening of the real-scale venue. #1854 records feasibility only.
- Settled decisions: `requires` stays removed (#1618); Option and Result stay removed (#1617).
- Follow-ups that no issue owns yet, each filed only if its record calls for it: the steps chosen in the path document of #1834 (dropping `nullable oblivious` headers where the probe compiles clean; giving single-file `calor convert` the project's nullable context); and a storage and re-apply mechanism for authored contracts, if #1859 chooses option A and the finding is positive.

epics.title: [0.34] Epic: complete .NET 11 and C# 15 support (remainder of #1644)
epics.body:
## Goal

Finish .NET 11 and C# 15 support after the 0.31 minimum. CI exercises Calor on .NET 11 beside .NET 10. The packages are proven on .NET 11 on every supported platform. The built-in effect tables and metadata binding account for what .NET 11 adds. C# 15 unions and closed hierarchies convert natively, with an exhaustive `match`. A C# 15 project is in the round-trip corpus. No prerelease dependency remains.

## Why

- 0.31 keeps only what a user on a .NET 11-only machine needs: #1639 on a minimal scope and the C# 15 parse support of #1638, under the re-scoped epic #1644. The original epic put all six of its children in 0.31, a milestone that was adding work and displacing none. When #1639 and #1638 were cut to that minimum, the parts they stopped carrying (the consumer matrices, the release SDK pin and Z3 packaging from #1639; the C# 15 corpus project from #1638) needed issues of their own, so that nothing is dropped when the two close. This epic holds that remainder and the four children that moved.
- Each child had a reason to wait. #1641 adds parallel CI legs, and the compiler shard already runs five test hosts under a 40-minute limit (`.github/workflows/test.yml:508`, `scripts/run-shard-tests.sh`), so it follows the CI-health work (#1749, #1590). #1642 replaces the argument layer of 29 commands, so it follows the paid agent collections of 0.31 to 0.33 (benchmark runs that spend on a model API and drive the `calor` command line). #1643 needs the Roslyn upgrade (#1638) and a declaration spelling, which is decided inside the 0.32 breaking window (#1797). #1640 concerns APIs that are new in .NET 11, which no existing program calls.
- The epic is off the 0.34 exit chain except for its coverage rows: the rows of `docs/plans/0.34-native-coverage.md` for the C# 15 entries #1638 adds, which #1643 fills, fall under the first 0.34 exit criterion. Everything else here is held to this epic's own done-when, not to the release.
- At HEAD bc80daeb no workflow or action under `.github/` installs an 11.x SDK: the 14 `dotnet-version` entries in `.github/workflows/test.yml` are `10.0.x` or `8.0.x`. Releases build with SDK 10.0.401 only (`.github/actions/setup-release-sdk/action.yml:23`). `System.CommandLine` is a 2022 prerelease (`Directory.Packages.props:25`).
- #1705 (0.36, the pilot's deployment work) reuses #1640, #1641 and #1855.

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1641 | .NET 11 legs for the 11 test shards and both round-trip modes, beside the .NET 10 legs |
| #1855 | Remainder of #1639: consumer matrices on .NET 11 on every supported platform, the release-SDK decision and pin, Z3 packaging when the packages are built by the .NET 11 SDK, the documentation pass |
| #1856 | Remainder of #1638: a C# 15 project in the round-trip corpus |
| #1643 | Native C# 15 unions and closed hierarchies with exhaustive `match` (parity with C# 15, not an advantage over it) |
| #1640 | Effect and metadata coverage for .NET 11 BCL additions, and a CI check that catches the same gap in later versions |
| #1642 | `System.CommandLine` from the 2022 prerelease to stable; no prerelease dependencies |

## Sequence

1. #1641 first, after #1749 (0.31) and #1639 (0.31). It supplies the .NET 11 legs that #1855, #1856 and the emission part of #1643 build on.
2. #1855 after #1641. Its release-SDK decision is taken before its pin and packaging parts.
3. #1856 after #1638 and #1641: the project needs a parser that reads C# 15 and a job that has the .NET 11 SDK.
4. #1643 after #1638 and #1797. Its parser, checker and conversion work does not need the CI legs. Its emission part does: a test that runs C# 15 `union` output needs an 11.x runtime, so that part lands after #1641.
5. #1640 at any time after #1639. Part 1 of #1642 (the surface snapshot) can start at once; its migration merges after the last paid agent collection of 0.31 to 0.33 (#1605, #1810, the re-run in #1645, #1811, #1831, and the example-bank comparison of #1835 if the #1832 record authorised it) has published or been declined.

If #1638 slipped out of 0.31, it lands here first; #1643 and #1856 wait for it.

## Done when

- #1640, #1641, #1642, #1855 and #1856 are closed. #1643 is closed, or it is open only because a C# 15 entry's default output needs .NET 11 types (last bullet).
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` runs .NET 10 and .NET 11 legs on `main` (#1641), and `sdk-package-consumer` and `cli-tool-consumer` each have a green .NET 11-only leg on all five RIDs (#1855).
- The record of which SDK builds releases is merged, and every pin site agrees with it (#1855).
- A C# 15 project converts and round-trips in both conversion modes in CI (#1856).
- `Directory.Packages.props` holds no prerelease version (#1642).
- The rows that #1643 owns in `docs/plans/0.34-native-coverage.md` are native or preserved with a recorded reason. This is this epic's share of the first 0.34 exit criterion. A C# 15 entry whose output needs .NET 11 types may close as preserved with the reason kind `not-reached`, cause "needs .NET 11 hosts", linking #1643, while the fixture hosts stay on .NET 10; #1643 then stays open past 0.34 without holding the release.

## Not in this epic

- The .NET 11 minimum (#1639) and C# 15 parsing (#1638): epic #1644, 0.31.
- The union declaration spelling: #1797, 0.32.
- Exhaustiveness over enum matches: #1871, 0.35, conditional on a measured base rate.
- Native conversion of every other construct, and the coverage record itself: epic #1659 (#1850 creates the record).
- Exact effect contracts for the callee families behind most unknown-charged call sites: #1841, 0.33. #1640 covers .NET 11 additions only.
- The pilot's platform matrix and deployment: #1705, 0.36.
- Follow-up with no issue: moving the hosts of the D-S1.5 fixture test, the conversion scorecard and the release test job to an 11.x runtime. #1855 decides only which SDK builds releases. If #1643 leaves a C# 15 entry preserved as "needs .NET 11 hosts", its promotion waits for this move.
- Under the adopter fallback in the plan of record (`docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md`), every row of this epic stays; only the reuse by #1705 lapses.

epics.title: [0.35] Epic: verification depth
epics.body:
## Goal

Make the verifier's proofs count on the Calor that the converter and agents actually produce. Measure what is reported Proven, Assumed and Unsupported today; lift the demotions that can be lifted soundly; decide whether obligation results get a command-line surface; then model more of the BCL and prove loop properties, in the order the measurement supports.

## Why

At HEAD bc80daeb a successful proof is reported `Proven` only if the solver query contains no string, array or user-type term, and every parameter of the callable is put into the query before anything is translated. A proof that touches the solver's string theory comes back `Assumed` under the named assumption `string-model`; one that touches an array or user-type sort comes back `Assumed` under `reference-model`. The runtime check is kept in both cases (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Z3/Z3Verifier.cs:576-631`, `src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Obligations/ObligationSolver.cs:326-357`, `docs/verification-modeled-forms.md` section 4.1). Each demotion closed a false proof that deleted a failing check. While they stand, the string and collection modelling in #1660 and the index-bounds proofs of #1661 report `Assumed`, not `Proven`. Three issues narrow them. #875 lifts the string demotion where non-null is established. #1851 does the same for arrays, or records why it cannot. #1862 stops a parameter that the query never reads from demoting or refusing the proof. User-type sorts, which include `List<T>`, stay demoted in 0.35, and no release text may call a proof over them proven.

Four more facts set the order of work:

- There is no count of where proofs stop today, so "more Proven" cannot be checked and the issues below cannot be ordered (#1853).
- The converter writes no contracts (`CHANGELOG.md:39-40`), so the contracts 0.35 proves have to be authored (#1843).
- Refinement obligations, including the index-bounds obligations generated for array accesses, exist only under `CompilationOptions.VerifyRefinements` (`src/Calor.Compiler/Program.cs:1074`). No CLI command and no build property sets it; the MCP tool `calor_refine` does. #1868 decides whether a command should.
- The k-induction prover runs only behind a switch that no command sets, and its only output is two diagnostics (`src/Calor.Compiler/Analysis/VerificationAnalysisPass.cs:43`, `:512-524`).

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1853 | Proof-status inventory on the conversion corpus: Proven, Assumed by named assumption, Unsupported and runtime-only, over both verification channels |
| #1843 | Name the native modules, author their contracts by hand and by agent, and report proof yield on them before and after the milestone |
| #875 | Lift the string-proof demotion where non-null is established; keep it everywhere else |
| #1851 | Lift the `reference-model` demotion for arrays where non-null is established, or record why not |
| #1862 | Declare only the variables a query reads, so that an unread string, array, user-type or floating-point parameter no longer demotes or refuses a proof |
| #1868 | Decision: an opt-in CLI and build surface for obligation verification |
| #1660 | Model more BCL in Z3: the unsupported string operations, collection `Count`/`Contains`/indexing, common `Math` functions |
| #1661 | Promote k-induction and loop-invariant synthesis into the verification pipeline for `for` and `while` loops |

## Sequence

1. **Entry.** Work starts when (a) the scheduled soundness sweep has been green on `main` for the proof-claim count in `docs/release-policy.md` (#1783), counted as that section prescribes from the latest re-registration of the packet: #1778, #1807 if the rewrite changed a case, or any later freeze that changed an existing case or verdict (a freeze that only adds rows does not restart the count), and (b) the seeded-defect replication is published or declined and the consequence #1816 registered for that outcome has been applied to the table above, with a comment on this epic naming the rows it changed. The same comment lists the counted runs (first and last run URL, and the count) and records the commit of `main` at which both held. That commit is the *entry commit*: #1843 measures its `before` value with the compiler built from it.
2. **#1853** first. It is report-only and tells the rest what to do first.
3. **#1843** next. Its `before` value is committed before any issue below changes a verdict. **#1868** is a decision that changes no verdict; it can be taken any time after the #1853 record exists.
4. **#875**, then **#1851**, which reuses #875's establishment rule and guard recognition. **#1862** is independent of both and may land before, between or after them.
5. **#1660** after #875 (string half) and #1851 (collection half). **#1661** after #1851. Within and between them, the order the #1853 record and the #1843 baseline rank.
6. #875, #1851, #1862, #1660 and #1661 each add controls to the registered sweep packet. Under the release rule in `docs/release-policy.md` (#1783), a freeze that only adds rows continues the proof-claim count, and a freeze that changes the verdict of an existing case is a re-registration and restarts it. All five can change existing verdicts. A case that is `Assumed` or `Unsupported` today may become `Proven`; #1660 models operations that the registered rows STR-UNMODELED-OPS and CALL-IN-CONTRACT expect to be refused; #1661 targets loop shapes that the rows BODY-LOOP-CALL-MUTABLE and OBL-LOOP-VARIABLE expect to be refused. At HEAD bc80daeb `tests/TestData/SoundnessSweep/expected-verdicts.json` expects `Assumed` for 53 of its 710 cases and `Unsupported` for 164 (counted from the file; recount on the packet #1778 registers). The proof-claim count therefore restarts at the last freeze that changes an existing verdict, and the 0.35 release cannot be earlier than that freeze plus the proof-claim count in days. So #875, #1851 and #1862 merge as close together as practical, and the pull requests of #1660 and #1661 that touch those rows merge as early as their dependencies allow.

## Done when

- The #1853 inventory record is published and linked from this epic.
- Proof yield (obligations `proven`, `assumed` by assumption, `unsupported`) on the #1843 module set is published in the 0.35 release notes with two values, the committed `before` and the value at the release commit, each with its compiler commit. The `after` value is published at the 0.35 close-out, as an item of the release close-out checklist in `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md`. If fewer than six corpus modules qualified under the selection rule of #1843, the outcome the maintainer recorded on this epic applies instead: a relaxed rule fixed before measuring, or "not measurable on the corpus" with the yield reported under that caveat.
- Every child that changes a verdict has added seeded unsound controls and safe controls to the registered sweep packet through the freeze procedure, and the scheduled sweep is green at the release commit.
- The release is not earlier than the last freeze in the milestone that changed an existing sweep verdict plus the proof-claim count (`docs/release-policy.md`, #1783) in days. The release-health notes state the streak: the count, the date of the last run and its link.
- `docs/verification-modeled-forms.md` states, for every string and collection form, whether a proof is reported `Proven` or `Assumed`, under which assumption, and what lifts the demotion.
- The #1868 decision record is committed.
- Every child is closed, or deferred with a recorded reason.

## Not in this epic

- Call-site obligations for class members, wider argument types, precondition import into the bug-pattern checkers, guard facts and the reference-null decision: epic #1861.
- New rejecting guarantees (null gaps, enum exhaustiveness, disposal): epic #1872.
- Modelling null in the translator (#1860, epic #1861).
- Building whatever surface #1868 chooses: that decision files the implementation issue. Whether obligation verification may ever run in a default build is decided by #1800, not here.
