- Lifting the `reference-model` demotion for `List<T>` and other user-type sorts has no issue in this plan. It needs heap-state reasoning for `Count`; it is a named follow-up, to be filed after 0.35 if the #1853 inventory shows list obligations in number.
- Any converter change, including lifting `throw` guards into refinements (#1866, conditional).
- The proof-status inventory on the pilot component: #1703 in 0.36.

epics.title: [0.35] Epic: contract consumers
epics.body:
## Goal

Make a precondition on a class member do verification work. Generate and solve the obligations it implies at call sites in class members, feed its ranges to the bug-pattern checkers, and decide how throw guards and `null` enter the verifier. Only after that, and only if its gates open, add an opt-in guard lift to `calor convert`.

## Why

- A precondition in 0.30 is a refinement on a parameter (`int:b | (# != 0)`). The obligation generator creates a call-site obligation ("the arguments of this call satisfy the callee's refinements") only when a module-level function calls a module-level function of the same module (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Obligations/ObligationGenerator.cs:58-62`, callee lookup `:108-109`, `:153`), and only when each argument is exactly `int` or `bool` (`:120-134`).
- Converted C# has no such functions. Classes convert to classes, and a static class converts to a named static module that the AST also holds as a class definition (`src/Calor.Compiler/Migration/RoslynSyntaxVisitor.cs:3198`; `src/Calor.Compiler/Ast/ClassNodes.cs:296`, `:581`). A refinement there creates no call-site obligation today.
- The converter emits no contracts (`CHANGELOG.md:39-40`). A refinement always throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` for its parameter with a generated message (`src/Calor.Compiler/CodeGen/CSharpEmitter.cs:6496-6497`), so turning a throw guard into one changes the exception type a caller sees unless the guard already throws that type for that parameter, and changes the message in every case. So the consumers come first, and the lift is last, opt-in and conditional.
- Two limits bound what this epic can report as Proven, and other issues own them. Obligations are solved only under refinement verification, which no CLI command or MSBuild property enables (`src/Calor.Compiler/Program.cs:1074`; under `src/` only the MCP tool `calor_refine` sets it); #1868 (epic #1662) decides whether a command should. And a callable with a string, array or other reference-typed parameter has every proof demoted to Assumed, while one with a `float` or `double` parameter has its obligations refused (`src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Obligations/ObligationSolver.cs:98-114`, `:326-357`; `docs/verification-modeled-forms.md:157-165`). #1862 scopes both to the variables a query reads, #875 and #1851 lift the demotion for strings and arrays that are established non-null (all three in epic #1662), and #1860 decides whether the translator models `null` at all.

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1864 | Call-site refinement obligations for calls made from, and to, class methods and constructors (operator bodies as callers) |
| #1863 | Accept the eight integer types the translator models as call arguments, exact type match only |
| #1723 | Import numeric-range and array-length preconditions into the bug-pattern checkers (three repaired safe controls) |
| #1858 | Taint precision on the two remaining safe controls, split from #1723 (may slip) |
| #1849 | Fall-through fact after a dominating `if (c) throw` (only if #1847 answered yes to option (a)) |
| #1860 | Decision record: model reference `null` in the contract translator, or record why not |
| #1866 | Opt-in guard lift in `calor convert` (only if #1647 is closed, the guard census reads "go", #1847 answered yes to option (b) and #1816 does not hold it) |

## Sequence

Work starts when the 0.35 entry criteria are recorded as met on #1662 (epic #1662). Before any row starts, apply the consequence that #1816 registered for 0.35 in Annex A of `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md`: its record names which rows of this epic are kept for each outcome of the seeded-defect replication. A row it holds stays open and unstarted with that record linked, until the record's own lifting condition is met; a row it removes is closed as not planned. Under outcome S ("specifications were present") the only affected row is #1866, which is held.

1. #1864, then #1863: both change the same generator function, and the second widens what the first generalises.
2. #1723 and #1858 at any time; they touch the bug-pattern and taint analyses, not the obligation engine.
3. #1860 after the proof-status inventory (#1853, epic #1662) and the guard census (#1848) have published numbers, because the recommended rule reads both.
4. #1849 only after #1847 has recorded yes to option (a).
5. #1866 last: after #1864 and #1863, because it reports the obligations they create; after #1853, because that issue's counter produces the report; and only while its four gates are open.

The "before" value of the proof-yield measurement (#1843) is taken with the compiler built from the 0.35 entry commit recorded on #1662, so no row here waits for it. The effect of #1864, #1863 and #1849 appears in the "after" value.

#1864, #1863 and #1849 each add cases to the soundness packet. Under the release rule that #1783 writes into `docs/release-policy.md`, a freeze that only adds cases continues the count of consecutive green sweep runs, and one that changes the verdict of an existing case restarts it. All three are expected to be additive. A pull request that does change an existing verdict lists the cases, and has to merge early enough for the count to be reached again before the release.

## Done when

- #1864, #1863 and #1723 are closed as completed.
- `docs/plans/0.35-reference-null-decision.md` is committed (#1860).
- #1849 is closed as completed, or closed as not planned with the #1847 record linked.
- #1866 is in exactly one state: closed as completed; closed as not planned with the records that shut its gate linked; or held as its body defines and moved to the next milestone with a comment. If it is held at the 0.35 close, the census reading re-read from the corpus job is appended to `docs/plans/0.34-guard-census-result.md` and the maintainer has added a dated entry to the #1847 record.
- #1858 is closed, or moved to 0.36 with a comment.
- Every verifier step that landed has seeded unsound controls and safe controls in the registered instrument for its analysis, and that instrument is green in CI: the soundness packet and the `sweep` job of `.github/workflows/soundness-sweep.yml` for #1864, #1863 and #1849; `BenchmarkSubjectRegressionTests` and `BugPatternRuntimeOracleTests` for #1723; `BenchmarkSubjectRegressionTests` for #1858. This is this epic's share of the 0.35 exit criterion on controls.
- The "after" value of the proof-yield measurement (#1843) reports call-site obligations on class members by status, using the marker #1864 adds.

## Not in this epic

- The proof-status inventory and the proof-yield metric (#1853, #1843), lifting the string and array demotions (#875, #1851), scoping the demotion to the variables a query reads (#1862), a CLI or build switch for refinement verification (#1868), BCL modelling (#1660) and loop invariants (#1661): epic #1662.
- Null gaps, enum exhaustiveness and must-dispose: epic #1872.
- The guard census and the guard-form decision (#1848, #1847): 0.34.
- Follow-ups that no issue in this plan owns; file one when the "after" value of #1843 shows the need:
  - cross-module call-site obligations;
  - operator and conversion applications, constructor initializers and accessors as call sites; members of nested classes; arguments that read locals, fields or properties (listed in #1864);
  - fall-through facts after an early `return`, `break` or `continue` (listed in #1849);
  - the implementation of reference-null modelling, which #1860 files only if it decides to model.
- Settled decisions: `requires` stays removed (#1618), so a refinement carries no exception type or message; Option and Result stay removed (#1617).

epics.title: [0.35] Epic: base-rate-gated guarantees (conditional)
epics.body:
## Goal

Decide from measured defect counts which of three candidate guarantees are built in 0.35, and build only those: checks for the documented gaps in null enforcement, exhaustiveness for a `match` over an enum, and a must-dispose check. Nothing in this epic may add a default-on error to a module that compiles under the edition (the compatibility promise #1805 declares at the end of 0.32).

## Why

- The flow checker reverted in April 2026 was built before anyone counted the defect it targeted. Its post-mortem asks for a base-rate check before building, an example from the target corpus, and an explicit hold when nothing is found (`docs/design/tier1a-postmortem.md:250-256`). A *base rate* is the number of defects of one class that agents produced in measured runs, read against the number of *opportunities* (places in the task where that defect could occur).
- No base rate exists for any of the three classes. The 50 benchmark pair files in 0.30 syntax contain no `match`, no `enum`, no nullable type or `null`, and no `using` resource statement (grep over `tests/TestData/ActiveSyntax/bench/phase0-agent-native/pairs`), so a count on them is zero by construction. That reading is "not measurable", which is not the same as "below threshold": a class the tasks cannot exhibit has not been shown to be rare.
- Strictness has a recorded price: relaxing null checks for `nullable oblivious` modules let 8 more of the 106 scorecard inputs convert natively (`CHANGELOG.md:159-168`).
- The null-gap and enum checks would reject or flag programs that compile today. Under the edition a new default-on error on such a program is a breaking change, so #1800 fixes, inside the 0.32 window and before the edition is declared, the form each may take. The must-dispose check runs only under `--analyze`, so it needs no such form.
- At HEAD bc80daeb: null is enforced at three receiving boundaries and, since 0.30, on a possibly-null `string` used as the receiver of a `System.String` member, and not at the documented gaps (`CHANGELOG.md:1871-1876`, `:360-363`, `:1910-1914`); the exhaustiveness check knows `bool` and union types only, and in a default build reaches a verdict only for a literal target (`src/Calor.Compiler/Analysis/PatternChecker.cs:257-263`; details in #1871); no analysis looks at resources (`src/Calor.Compiler/Analysis/BugPatterns/TypedBugPatternAnalysis.cs:13-20`).

## Work

| Issue | Item |
|---|---|
| #1869 | Decision record: which documented null gaps cleared the gate, with one implementation issue filed per cleared gap |
| #1871 | Exhaustiveness over enum matches, in the form #1800 recorded (only if the missing-case class cleared its threshold) |
| #1870 | Must-dispose bug-pattern checker under `--analyze` (only if the disposal spike #1842 reads "go") |

## Sequence

The three rows do not depend on each other. Each waits on its own gate.

1. Before any row starts, apply the consequence that #1816 registered for 0.35. Its record names which rows of this epic are kept for each outcome of the seeded-defect replication. A row it removes is closed as not planned with that record linked.
2. A class's reading is one of the four the 0.31 registration defines (#1770, Annex A of `docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md`): above threshold, below threshold, held (a count between the two thresholds), or not measurable (too few opportunities or too few runs). The registration states its thresholds in runs: the runs that had at least one event of the class. This epic sets no threshold and no minimum.
3. The reading is taken from the failure-class table (report script, #1760) of the most recent published agent run whose pair set has at least the registered minimum of opportunities for the class. The candidates are #1605, the #1645 re-run (#1816 Part B) and #1811. The #1645 re-run is the first whose pairs can exhibit these classes, because it adds the modify-a-converted-module pairs (#1789). If no run qualifies, or all were declined, the reading is "not measurable".
4. Above threshold opens the gate. Below threshold closes the row as not planned with the report linked. Held or not measurable holds the row: it stays open and unstarted, and at the close of 0.35 it moves to the milestone of the next agent run with a comment naming that run. A held row is not dropped. Recording the hold is all the 0.35 close requires of it, so a held row does not hold the release.
5. #1870 takes its reading from the verdict of the disposal spike (#1842) in place of items 2 and 3: "go" opens the gate, "drop" closes the row as not planned, "hold" and "not measurable" hold it.

## Done when

- `docs/plans/0.35-null-gap-decision.md` is committed with one outcome per gap, and every cleared gap has a filed issue (#1869).
- #1871 and #1870 are each in exactly one state: closed as completed; closed as not planned with the deciding record linked; or held as defined in the sequence.
- Each check that was built has its seeded-defect controls and safe controls in the instrument its issue names, and that instrument is green in CI. For the must-dispose check these are `BenchmarkSubjectRegressionTests` and `BugPatternRuntimeOracleTests`, which is this epic's share of the 0.35 exit criterion on controls.
- No check built under this epic reports an error in a default build: each has a test that compiles its seeded-defect controls through `Program.Compile` with default options, in a module that has not opted in, and asserts that the check adds no error; and the `conversion-scorecard` job (`.github/workflows/test.yml:672`) passes on each pull request with `tests/Calor.Evaluation/Scorecard/baseline.json` unchanged.

## Not in this epic

- Registering thresholds and minimum opportunities (#1770), the report script (#1760), and tasks that can exhibit these classes (#1789).
- Deciding the form a rejecting guarantee may take (#1800) and declaring the edition (#1805).
- The disposal spike (#1842) and the disposal analyzers of the equipped C# condition (#1709).
- Exhaustiveness for unions and closed hierarchies (#1643, 0.34).
- Trusting non-null in the verifier (#875, epic #1662) and modelling reference `null` in the contract translator (#1860, epic #1861).
- Shrinking the number of `nullable oblivious` modules (#1834).
- Three follow-ups that no issue owns:
  - Fixing the false Calor0502 "duplicate pattern" warning on the second dotted enum-member case of a statement match. The defect is unconditional, but only #1871 touches it (rule 6), and that issue may never start.
  - Archiving the exception type of each failing hidden test and each failing agent-run test. Until the harness does, #1869 attributes null events by hand and re-runs hidden suites locally.
  - Correcting the case totals in `benchmarks/README.md` (25 and 25) to those `BenchmarkSubjectRegressionTests` runs (24 and 26). #1870 corrects them only if it starts.
- Settled or deferred: no null ban without an edition mechanism; Option and Result stay removed (#1617); ownership and linear types stay after 1.0 (`docs/plans/agent-native-strategy.md:215-217`).

epics.title: [0.36] Epic: maintainable beyond its creator
epics.body:
## Outcome
Ship one useful, authoritative Calor component inside an existing application that an external maintainer can integrate, change, diagnose, deploy, and recover without the creator's intervention. Humans govern obligations; agents govern implementation. Performance is an initial use case, not an assumed advantage.

## Entry criteria
This milestone is entered only when all three hold. Until then it is treated as held (defined in the next section), with two exceptions that may proceed: the recruitment and baseline record of #1701, if the outreach decision (#1777) authorised it, and the pilot-independent parts of #1702, #1703 and #1704. Record each criterion, with a link, in a comment on this epic when it is met.

1. **Adopter checkpoint passed.** The checkpoint decision at the close of 0.33 (#1833) records the consent of a named external maintainer. If it records "demand unproven" instead, this milestone is held and the fallback below applies.
2. **Proof-soundness instrument healthy.** #1694 is closed with one disposition and its linked evidence for every failure, as its done-when defines (a fixing pull request where the disposition is a fix). No open issue carries the `soundness-sweep` label. The label is reserved for the tracking issue, titled "Soundness sweep failing on main", that the scheduled soundness sweep (`.github/workflows/soundness-sweep.yml`, daily on `main`) opens after a failed run, or comments on when one is already open. The sweep has passed its gate on consecutive daily runs for at least the proof-claim count in `docs/release-policy.md`. #1783 writes two counts there: a smaller one for the 0.31 exit, and the larger proof-claim count for 0.35 entry, 0.36 entry and any release note that says "proven". The count runs from the most recent re-registration of the sweep packet (the pinned cases and expected verdicts the sweep compares against; at HEAD `bc80daeb` they are under `tests/TestData/SoundnessSweep/`): a freeze that changes a case or an expected verdict restarts it, and a freeze that only adds rows does not.
3. **Edition in force.** An edition (a named version of the syntax whose existing spellings no longer change) is declared with its written compatibility promise published: #1805 records option A or B and #1846 records Decision A or B, or #1805 deferred and the #1846 record carries the declaration (option A or B of #1805). If #1846 records Decision C (a second edition), the criterion is met only when the issue that record names for the second edition is closed and the promise names that edition. The compiler release the pilot pins reads the per-module edition marker (#1084). A recorded deferral does not satisfy this criterion.

## If the adopter checkpoint is not passed
The fallback is written in advance, as a table, in the plan of record, `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md` (#1765). This epic cites that table and does not restate it. It applies when #1833 records "demand unproven", and earlier if the outreach decision (#1777) records a decline. For this epic it means:

- **Still run**, because their own bodies say they do not need the pilot: #1702 (the policy, the checker, the classification command and their demonstrations), #1703 (the evidence record and release check, without pilot-specific records; its inventory repeat is recorded as not run) and #1704 (the readiness controls). The table says when those parts are delivered (in 0.37, ahead of any 0.37 collection); the three issues stay open in 0.36.
- **Held**: #1701, #1705, #1706, #1707, and the pilot-specific parts of #1702, #1703 and #1704. A held issue stays open with a comment that links the #1833 record; no work is scheduled on it, and it is not closed as not planned.
- This epic stays open. The three running children cannot close it: a framework without a useful maintained component does not complete this epic.
- The hold lifts only through a later dated maintainer entry on the #1833 record that names a consenting external maintainer. Creator self-evaluation does not lift it (#1701).

## Work breakdown
Child issues cover pilot selection and source ownership; obligation-change authorization; artifact-linked evidence; evidence-pipeline readiness; mixed-project integration and deployment; one useful measured improvement; and agent-unavailable incident recovery.

## Acceptance
- Record the named maintainer's build/change/deploy/recovery exercise, costs, and every author intervention.
- Calor is maintained source; generated C# is build output. Export and emergency divergence have explicit ownership and reconciliation rules.
- Obligation changes require authorization beyond the implementation agent's authority.
- Evidence describes exact artifacts and what was proved, tested, assumed, unknown, or unchecked.
- A developer-agreed useful improvement passes independently controlled acceptance checks and held-out workloads within an agreed cost ceiling.
- Relevant evidence failures, including #1694 or successors, are resolved and demonstrated healthy before their results support release claims.

## Reuse and dependencies
Consume existing correctness, interoperability, language stabilization, agent integration (#1650-#1652), and applicable verification (#1660-#1661). Reuse Calor.Sdk/Calor.Tasks, build-state capture, reproducible-build checks, and the soundness sweep. Those issues keep the scope and milestone the plan of record (#1765) gives them; this epic neither pulls them forward nor postpones their fixes.

Dependency edges ("A → B" reads "A must complete before B"):

Into the epic:
- #1777 (outreach authorised) → #1791 (recruitment record opened) → #1833 (consent recorded) → entry criterion 1 and #1701.
- #1694 closed with a disposition for every failure, the successor sweep packet registered (#1769 to #1778) and re-registered after the 0.32 rewrite (#1807), and the run-count rule written (#1783) → entry criterion 2 and #1704.
- #1805 (edition declaration and compatibility promise) → #1846 (re-affirmation at the 0.33 close, or the declaration itself after a 0.32 deferral). Both, and #1084 (per-module edition marker) → entry criterion 3. #1805 → the #1701 sign-off.
- #1639 (0.31), #1650 to #1652 (0.33), #1640, #1641 and #1855 (0.34) → #1705.
- #1853 (proof-status inventory on the conversion corpus, 0.35) → #1703, which repeats it on the pilot component.

Inside the epic:
- #1701 → the pilot-specific parts of #1702, #1703, #1704 and #1705.
- #1704 → release use of #1703. #1703 and #1704 → release integration of #1705.
- #1701, #1702 and #1705 → #1706; #1703 and #1704 → release acceptance of #1706.
- #1701, #1702, #1703, #1705 and #1706 → #1707.

Out of the epic:
- #1702 → any 0.37 task counted as effect-boundary evidence, meaning a task whose result is attributed to an effect row or a contract stopping a wrong change (#1711; the #1710 harness applies the #1702 classification command to every run). Until the pilot-independent half of #1702 has landed, as #1702 defines "landed", no 0.37 task is counted as such.
- #1703 → #1709, and its inventory on the pilot component bounds the proof claim #1698 and #1712 may make.
- #1701, #1706 and #1707 → final task approval in #1708.
- Pilot acceptance under this epic, or the fallback scope in the plan of record → entry to 0.37 (#1698). This epic's exit record → #1712.
- #1699 (0.38) must preserve this epic's source ownership, obligation controls, artifact-linked evidence and recovery path (#1713, #1715 and #1716 reuse #1702, #1703, #1704 and #1707). 0.39 (#1700, #1718) is entered only while the pilot continues.

## Exit record
Link the maintained component, exact artifact/evidence, acceptance results, operating guide, recovery transcript, costs, and limitations. Include the pilot component's proof-status inventory from #1703 (a count of verification obligations for each status #1853 defines, among them proven, assumed, unsupported and checked only at run time) and the 0.37 proof claim sized to it. Post the record as a comment on this epic and enter it in the evidence ledger (`docs/benchmarking/evidence-ledger.md`, #1774); the epic closes when both exist. A framework without a useful maintained component does not complete this epic.

## Non-goals
No new backend, broad syntax redesign, exhaustive C# parity, whole-application migration, autonomous optimizer, or removal of implementation review. Planning does not authorize paid collection or reactivate paused PP-W research.

## Tracked child issues
- [ ] #1701 - Select an external pilot and define component ownership and acceptance
- [ ] #1702 - Enforce separate authorization for obligation and implementation changes
- [ ] #1703 - Bind property-level evidence to the exact built and deployed artifact
- [ ] #1704 - Establish pilot evidence readiness and fail closed on invalid validation runs
- [ ] #1705 - Deliver mixed C#/Calor integration, diagnostics, and supported-platform deployment
- [ ] #1706 - Ship one useful pilot improvement with independent acceptance and measured costs
- [ ] #1707 - Rehearse agent-unavailable incident recovery and explicit C# divergence

## Sequencing and release acceptance
- #1701 recruitment does not start on this epic's authority. It starts in 0.31 only if the maintainer authorises outreach (#1777), in the recruitment record #1791 opens; consent is recorded at #1833. #1702 policy design, #1703 implementation and #1704 controls may proceed before the checkpoint; none of them postpones #1694, which is scheduled in 0.31.
- Activate #1702 authority controls and scope #1703 evidence/#1705 integration against the chosen component.
- Ship #1706 only with approved obligations, working integration, and valid artifact-linked evidence; then complete #1707 external recovery.
- Acceptance is the complete maintained-component experience, not seven independently green reports. Record unresolved blockers and all creator interventions.

epics.title: [0.37] Epic: earn the language
epics.body:
## Outcome
Determine where maintained Calor source adds useful value over equally capable C# workflows, including adoption and maintenance costs. This is a falsifiable language/workflow hypothesis, not a promised positive result.

It is a confirmation, under fairer controls, of one probe-scale positive. It is not a first test. The record it starts from:

- **One hit, at fixture scale.** In `ws5-probe-001` (2026-07-28, pre-0.30 syntax, nine defects seeded by the project in its own fixtures, three runs per condition) the Calor condition caught 9 of 9 defects and conventional C# caught 4 of 9: a difference of 5 against a threshold of 3 fixed in advance (`bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/ws5-probe-001/VERDICT.md:21-26`; adjudicated a hit at `bench/phase0-agent-native/epochs/m5-compare-001/VERDICT.md:83-85`). For the three contract defects the C# condition carried the contract only as a doc comment (`ws5-probe-001/VERDICT.md:64-68`). Calor took 1.63 iterations against 1.0 and 247,304 output tokens against 69,545 (`ws5-probe-001/VERDICT.md:72-73`).
- **One miss, at real scale.** The real-scale venue was adjudicated a miss and retired on 2026-08-05 (`docs/plans/call-s-adjudication.md:3-5`).
- **One replication.** The 0.32 run (#1810) repeats the nine defects on the syntax as it stands after the 0.32 breaking window, with a third condition, C# with executable specifications. Its outcome is recorded under Entry criteria.

What this epic adds to that record: semantically equipped C# as the comparator, tasks and acceptance checks owned by someone other than the implementing agents, blinded defect controls, results per task stratum fixed in advance, and full engineering cost.

## Entry criteria
Preparation (#1708 to #1711, #1865, #1857) may start earlier. #1712 starts only when all three are recorded, each with a link, in a comment on this epic.

1. **Adopter branch.** Either 0.36 pilot acceptance, meaning #1697 is closed on its exit record (posted as a comment on that epic and entered in the evidence ledger), or the adopter checkpoint (#1833) recorded "demand unproven" and this epic runs at the fallback scope below.
2. **Obligation boundary.** #1702 has landed, or the comment states that no task is counted as effect-boundary evidence (evidence that an effect row or a contract stopped a wrong change). "Landed" means its pilot-independent half is on `main`: the policy, the checker, and the command that classifies a base-to-head change as implementation-only or obligation-changing, with their demonstrations. Activation on a pilot repository is not required.
3. **Replication recorded.** The outcome of #1810 (the Calor-minus-equipped-C# delta out of nine defects, "not adjudicated", or "declined"), and the paragraph "What changes in the #1698 hypothesis" that the #1816 registration wrote in advance for that outcome, quoted from the registration. It registers four outcomes. A delta of at least 3 of 9 is a language effect at fixture scale: this epic tests whether the effect holds on independently authored tasks. A smaller delta means the July result was mostly "specifications were present": the hypothesis narrows as the registration states, and the #1708 targets and the sizing (#1786) are refreshed for the smaller expected difference before #1867 is decided. Not adjudicated: record "replication not adjudicated" with the reason. Declined: record "no equipped-C# reading exists at fixture scale".

## If the adopter checkpoint is not passed
The fallback is written in advance, as a table, in the plan of record, `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md` (#1765). The table gives the disposition of each of #1708 to #1712 and of #1865 to #1867 (re-scoped or closed); says what a fallback 0.37 adds beyond the 0.32 replication, or that this epic closes on the existing results with no new run; names the inventory that bounds any proof claim when there is no pilot component; and defines the cases "verdict not collected" and "verdict not positive". This epic cites that table and does not restate it. Four rules of this epic hold whatever the table keeps: paid collection still needs #1867; results from tasks whose requirements or acceptance checks were written by the maintainer or the implementing agents are labelled non-independent (#1708); 0.38 and 0.39 stay held; and nothing published at fallback scope opens 0.38.

## Work breakdown
Child issues cover independent, stratified tasks and economics (#1708); three comparable authoring conditions (#1709); reuse of the multi-agent harness without search (#1710); blinded implementation, specification and boundary-defect controls, which are the primary source of discrimination between conditions (#1711); three inputs the study stop of 2026-09-09 recorded as absent (`docs/plans/safe-delegation-m0/decision.md:18-21`, `:43-52`), namely a count of task supply (#1865), an independent methods review (#1857, by the reviewer named under #1777) and an authorised budget (#1867); and approved execution with a published investment decision (#1712), which also commits the executable analysis, with its rules for undefined ratios, before collection starts.

## Comparison
1. Conventional C# tooling.
2. C# with comparable explicit specifications and validation capabilities wherever practical ("semantically equipped C#": analyzers, executable assertions and disposal analyzers, bolted on).
3. Calor with integrated contracts, effects, and applicable verification.

Condition 2 is the single gating comparator: the verdict is decided on condition 3 against condition 2. Condition 1 is reported; it separates what executable specifications alone buy (2 against 1) from what the language adds (3 against 2). A Rust condition may be reported on eligible tasks (#1709). It is never adjudicated and no verdict statement depends on it.

All receive the same behavioral requirements and independent acceptance criteria. Disclose unavoidable capability differences and charge setup/maintenance costs fairly. Do not handicap C# or constrain its algorithms to Calor's representation.

## Acceptance
- Use 0.36 pilot findings and a developer-valued, currently supportable performance task plus a harder task exposing real limits.
- Tasks are assigned to strata fixed in advance (effect-and-contract, neutral, C#-favoured), and every result is reported per stratum (#1708). Tasks are not chosen because Calor is expected to win them.
- Pin model/tool/source/build configurations, control budgets and order effects, record assistance and invalid runs, and justify repetitions from variability and available budget.
- Count specification authoring, integration, agent/validation execution, review, rework, and maintenance. Scope/risk is independently defined, not lines changed.
- Separate seeded-defect detection from natural failure rates; zero observed defects is not equivalent safety.
- No task is counted as effect-boundary evidence unless #1702 has landed and the task meets the rule in #1711. Contracts derived mechanically from the implementation are labelled "derived" and never counted as specification-backed proofs (#1709, #1711).
- Publish reproducible wins, losses, uncertainty, costs, and limitations, particularly against semantically equipped C#.
- Exit. The milestone exits on one of three records, linked from a comment on this epic:
  1. **Verdict published.** #1712 is closed, with its proceed/narrow/revise/stop decision published in the 0.37 release notes and entered in the evidence ledger (#1774).
  2. **Decline recorded.** #1867 records a decline (an explicit decline; the dated default "not decided, treated as decline until changed"; or a decline because #1857 shows no cleared review), #1712 is closed as not planned with that record linked, and this epic records the verdict as "not collected".
  3. **Fallback disposition recorded.** Under the adopter fallback, a comment on this epic links the #1833 record and the table and states the option. Under F1 (no new run) that comment is the exit record: the verdict is recorded as "not collected: no independent tasks" and this epic closes when #1833 is applied. Under F2 (a fixture-scale extension) the epic stays open and exits on record 1, with the verdict labelled "non-independent, fixture scale" and 0.38 held, or on record 2 if #1867 declines.

## Reuse and dependencies
Build on #1651 rather than duplicate its client drivers, and on #1697 for maintained-component experience. Preparation can proceed independently; execution consumes approved tasks/controls/harness and the budget authorised in #1867. Identify a supported task class, an unresolved hypothesis, or a negative result; narrow or redirect 0.38 accordingly.

Dependency edges ("A → B" reads "A must complete before B"):

Into the epic:
- #1697 (0.36, closed on its exit record) or #1833 (0.33, the adopter checkpoint, on its "demand unproven" branch) → entry criterion 1. #1810 (0.32, the replication result) → entry criterion 3.
- #1648 (0.31, admission rule) → #1708 stratification and screening, #1711 controls.
- #1791 (0.31, protocol draft) → #1708. #1786 (0.31, sizing, refreshed at each milestone close) → #1865, #1867.
- #1777 (0.31, the outreach decision, which names the methods reviewer or records the seat vacant) → #1857.
- #1605 (0.31) → #1651 (0.33, agent drivers) → #1709, #1710. #1827 (0.33, arm abstraction) → #1710. #1830 (0.33, process-level oracle) → #1709, #1710.
- #1815 (0.32, three-condition harness support built for the replication) → #1710. #1813 (0.32, equipped-C# fixtures) → #1709.
- #1802 (0.32, unknown-effect share) → the #1708 task-card number. #1731 (0.32) → #1711.
- #1702 (0.36) → #1711 and any task counted as effect-boundary evidence. #1703 (0.36, proof-status inventory on the pilot component) → the size of any proof claim in #1709 and #1712. #1701, #1706, #1707 (0.36) → final task approval in #1708.

Inside the epic:
- #1708 → #1709 → #1710 → #1711; each also needs every issue before it in that chain.
- #1708 → #1865. The #1708 protocol and the #1709 review package → #1857.
- #1865, #1857, #1710, #1711 → an authorise outcome of #1867. A decline needs none of them.
- #1708, #1709, #1710, #1711, #1865, #1857, #1867 → #1712.

Out of the epic:
- This epic's exit record → #1699 (0.38) and #1700 (0.39). The #1712 verdict → #1713 (0.38). 0.38 and 0.39 are entered only on a positive verdict for the task class in question.

## Non-goals
No implementation search yet, universal advantage claim, production native backend, new syntax thesis, or reactivation of paused PP-W research. No Rust-plus-verifier condition; Rust is reported, never a gating comparator. No acceptance criterion that depends on models having learned Calor from training data. Filing work does not authorize paid collection.

## Tracked child issues
- [ ] #1708 - Define independent engineering tasks, held-out acceptance, and economic targets
- [ ] #1709 - Build fair conventional C#, semantically equipped C#, and Calor conditions
- [ ] #1710 - Extend the existing agent harness for three conditions and full-effort accounting
- [ ] #1711 - Add blinded implementation, specification, and boundary-defect controls
- [ ] #1712 - Execute the approved no-search comparison and publish the language investment verdict
- [ ] #1865 - Task supply inventory
- [ ] #1857 - Independent methods review of the protocol and the fairness check
- [ ] #1867 - Decision: authorised collection budget

## Sequencing and release acceptance
- #1708 protocol drafting started in 0.31 (#1791). Finalize #1708 using 0.36 pilot findings; develop #1709 fair conditions, #1710 harness, and #1711 defect controls against the same tasks.
- The four close in the order #1708, #1709, #1710, #1711, because each consumes the ones before it. Work on a later one may begin against drafts of the earlier ones.
- #1710 consumes the generic client-driver work in #1651 rather than duplicating it.
- #1865 counts admitted tasks per stratum against the minimum the design needs. The methods reviewer is named under #1777; #1857 holds that reviewer's two reviews, of the #1708 protocol and of the #1709 fairness package. If no reviewer was named, #1857 records the vacancy and #1712 does not start.
- #1867 is the maintainer's decision on the collection budget. An authorisation is taken after #1865, #1857, #1710 and #1711; a decline may be recorded at any time. It is the only authorisation for paid collection.
- #1712 collection requires approved tasks, reviewed conditions, validated harness/controls, the analysis script committed, and the #1867 authorisation.
- #1712 must publish a proceed/narrow/revise/stop verdict. A negative or inconclusive result does not automatically authorize 0.38 execution. A decline in #1867 closes this epic with the verdict "not collected".

epics.title: [0.38] Epic: earn greater autonomy
epics.body:
## Outcome
Test whether bounded implementation search and evidence-assisted review produce additional accepted improvements economically, and whether accepted change scope can grow without proportional human supervision or weakened acceptance quality.

## Entry criteria and hold rule
This milestone is entered only when the entry criterion below is met. Until then its issues stay open in the 0.38 milestone and only what "While held" allows may be done. The order of milestones, the adopter fallback, and the cases "0.37 verdict not collected" and "0.37 verdict not positive" are written in advance in the plan of record, `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md` (#1765); this epic cites that document and does not restate its fallback table.

**Entry criterion.** #1712 (0.37) has published its language investment verdict, and the verdict is positive for the task class this epic would search. "Positive" is read from the published records and is not re-judged here. All three must hold:

1. #1712 is closed as completed and #1698 carries its "verdict published" exit record. The verdict comes from the full 0.37 comparison, collected under an authorised budget decision (#1867), not from the fallback scope.
2. The decision #1712 records for 0.38 is `proceed` or `narrow`. (#1712 records one of proceed, narrow, revise or stop, with an owner and a rationale.)
3. The verdict identifies a supported task class: at least one task class in which Calor added value beyond semantically equipped C#, under the readings written before collection (the #1708 protocol, registered with #1867). Semantically equipped C# is C# given comparable explicit specifications and validation; it is the single gating comparator of 0.37 (#1698). #1713 may select only that task class or a subset of it.

When all three hold, record it in a comment on this epic that links the verdict and names the task class. That comment releases #1713. It authorises no spend (see Authorization).

**Hold rule.** While 0.37 is still in progress the milestone is not yet entered and no record is needed. In each of the following cases it is held, and the case is recorded in a comment on this epic with a link to the record that establishes it:

- **(a) The adopter fallback applies.** The adopter checkpoint at the close of 0.33 (#1833) recorded "demand unproven" instead of the consent of a named external maintainer, or the outreach decision (#1777) was declined and the fallback was applied early. The fallback table in the plan of record holds 0.38. Nothing published under the fallback's 0.37 scope meets the entry criterion: item 1 requires the full comparison, and without a pilot component the source ownership (#1701) and recovery path (#1707) that this epic must preserve do not exist.
- **(b) The verdict was not collected.** The collection budget decision (#1867) recorded a decline, so #1712 was closed as not planned and #1698 records the verdict as "not collected".
- **(c) The verdict is not positive.** #1712 recorded `revise` or `stop`, or its verdict is negative or unresolved for every task class #1713 could select.

**While held.**
- #1714, #1715, #1716 and #1717 do not start. No implementation, participant work or paid collection happens under this epic.
- #1713 stays open and unapproved. Protocol drafting is text only. In case (c) #1713 may record a revised hypothesis, or a stop/redirect, which ends the epic as "Lifting or ending the hold" describes.
- Approval of a revised hypothesis starts no implementation and no collection, and does not meet the entry criterion (#1713). #1717 accepts only a `proceed` or `narrow` decision.

**Lifting or ending the hold.** The hold lifts only when the entry criterion is met. In case (a) that first requires the 0.36 hold to lift, through a later dated maintainer entry on the #1833 record that names a consenting external maintainer (see #1697), and then 0.36 and the full 0.37 comparison to complete. In case (b) it requires a later dated authorise entry on the #1867 record, and #1712 to run and publish. In case (c) it requires a further no-search comparison under the #1698 protocol, with its own budget decision, to publish a positive verdict; no issue in milestones 0.31 to 0.39 schedules one, so it would be filed as new work. The hold has no timer, and a held milestone is not reported as delivered. If the maintainer records that this epic will not be pursued (a `stop` from #1712, or a stop/redirect recorded in #1713 under the hold, is the occasion to decide), close the epic and its open children as not planned and link the record that caused the hold.

## Work breakdown
Child issues cover task selection, a six-condition protocol and the maintainer's decision on its cost limits and spend; bounded search and cost accounting; independent candidate validation and artifact evidence; staged review with blinded defect assessment; and approved execution plus an autonomy decision.

## Comparison
Extend the 0.37 three authoring conditions with and without search. Calor-plus-search must be compared with C# given equivalent search and validation, not only Calor without search. Reuse 0.37 assets where still valid; record any changed model, task, or tooling conditions rather than treating historical runs as concurrent controls.

## Acceptance
- Humans retain authorization over public obligations, independent tests, and budgets; agents may propose implementation candidates and separate obligation changes.
- Bound candidate count, elapsed time, inference spend, build/solver effort, and benchmarking. Include review, rework, and recovery costs.
- Evaluate held-out performance and behavior, separate incorrect-specification detection from incorrect-implementation detection, and retain explicit unknown/unchecked boundaries.
- Progress from conventional review to evidence-assisted review; evidence-led review is justified only for bounded cases. Never forbid body inspection or reward zero reads.
- Publish gains, costs, failures, uncertainty, and the decision about whether greater autonomy is warranted.

## Exit record
Once entered, the milestone exits on exactly one of three records, posted as a comment on this epic and entered in the evidence ledger (#1774):

1. **Decision published.** #1717 is closed as completed, with its results and its owned expand/narrow/revise/stop decision published in the 0.38 release notes and entered in the evidence ledger (#1774), and the Acceptance items above are met.
2. **Stop or redirect.** #1713 is closed with a recorded stop/redirect because no justified task or hypothesis remained (its last Acceptance bullet), and #1714 to #1717 are closed as not planned with that record linked.
3. **Budget declined.** The collection authorisation in the #1713 decision record is a decline: an explicit decline, or the dated default "not decided, treated as decline until changed". #1717 and whichever of #1714 to #1716 are still open are closed as not planned with that record linked, merged work is kept, and this epic records the comparison as "not collected".

Records 2 and 3 are honest conclusions, not a delivered capability. A milestone that was never entered has no exit record: it stays held, or ends as "Lifting or ending the hold" describes. #1718 (0.39) reads whichever of these records exists when it makes its decision. 0.39 is not gated on this milestone: its entry needs a positive 0.37 verdict and a continuing pilot (#1700), so it does not wait for one of these records.

## Dependencies and decision
Use #1698 findings to select or reject the task class before execution. Preserve #1697 source ownership, obligation controls, artifact-linked evidence, and agent-unavailable recovery. A negative, unresolved or uncollected 0.37 result holds this milestone under the rule above; a revised hypothesis may be written under the hold and is not progression. No separate unbounded optimizer product.

Dependency edges ("A → B" reads "A must complete before B"):

Into the epic:
- #1777 (0.31, outreach decision) → #1833 (0.33, adopter checkpoint) → #1697 (0.36, pilot accepted) → #1712.
- #1708, #1709, #1710, #1711, #1865 (task supply), #1857 (methods review) and #1867 (collection budget) → #1712 → the "verdict published" exit record of #1698 → the entry criterion → #1713.
- #1702 (0.36, obligation-change authority) and the #1708 to #1711 assets (0.37) → #1713.
- #1710 (0.37, three-condition runner) → #1714.
- #1702, #1703 and #1704 (0.36) → #1715.
- #1711 (0.37, blinded defect controls) → #1716. #1707 (0.36) supplies the recovery path #1716 keeps available.

Inside the epic:
- The protocol approval recorded under #1713 → #1714, #1715 and #1716.
- #1714 → #1715 → #1716.
- #1714, #1715, #1716 and the collection authorisation recorded under #1713 → #1717.

Out of the epic:
- The exit record of this epic → #1718 (0.39), which reads it when it exists. It is not an entry criterion of 0.39.

## Authorization
Planning is not authorization for paid collection, production autonomous deployment, removal of human review, new backends, or reactivation of paused PP-W research. Paid collection in this milestone is authorised only by the collection authorisation in the #1713 decision record (`docs/plans/0.38-collection-spend-authorisation.md`), a maintainer decision with a decline branch. The paid-run rule applies to every paid agent run in this milestone (#1717, and any agent run under #1716): a written spend ceiling, abort triggers, a zero-cost dry pass (`--null-agent`), one pinned model, and a reading written in advance for each outcome, all fixed in that record before the first paid run. Filing or amending an issue authorises no spend.

## Tracked child issues
- [ ] #1713 - Approve the bounded-search task class, six-condition protocol, and cost limits
- [ ] #1714 - Implement bounded candidate search with cancellation and complete cost accounting
- [ ] #1715 - Independently validate candidates and prevent held-out benchmark overfitting
- [ ] #1716 - Evaluate staged evidence-assisted review and independent defect detection
- [ ] #1717 - Run the approved search comparison and publish the autonomy decision

## Sequencing and decision gate
- The entry criterion is recorded on this epic first. #1713 then consumes #1712's verdict and approves a search task class and collection protocol only for a task class that verdict names as supported; the same issue records the maintainer's decision on the collection spend.
- #1714 runner and #1715 independent validation form the candidate pipeline; #1716 evaluates review/detection without prohibiting source inspection.
- #1717 execution requires the approved protocol, working runner, independent validation/review controls, and the collection authorisation recorded under #1713.
- Compare against equivalently equipped C# with search; report all costs, failures, and specification versus implementation detection separately. Expansion is conditional on accepted outcomes, not faster review alone.

epics.title: [0.39] Epic: scale demonstrated value
epics.body:
## Outcome
Deliver the next capability justified by external pilot demand and measured outcomes, not architecture preference. A failed or inconclusive experiment may narrow, redirect, or stop a proposed investment.

## Entry criteria and hold rule
This milestone is entered only when both entry criteria below are met. Until then it is held: its issues stay open in the 0.39 milestone and only what "While held" allows may be done. The order of milestones, the fallback for the case that no external maintainer consents, and the cases "0.37 verdict not collected" and "0.37 verdict not positive" are written in advance in the plan of record, `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md` (#1765); this epic cites that document and does not restate its fallback table.

**Entry criteria.** Both are read from published records and are not re-judged here.

1. **The 0.37 verdict is positive.** Both must hold:
   - #1712 is closed and its language investment verdict comes from a comparison that was collected: the collection budget decision (#1867) was authorised, and the run was the full 0.37 comparison, not the fallback scope.
   - The verdict names at least one task class in which Calor added value beyond semantically equipped C#, that is, C# given comparable explicit specifications and validation, the single gating comparator of 0.37.

   #1712 also records a proceed, narrow, revise or stop decision for 0.38. That decision governs the entry of #1699 (0.38) and is not read here. This milestone may therefore be entered while 0.38 is in progress, or while 0.38 is held because that decision was `revise` or `stop` or because the task class with demonstrated value is not one 0.38 could search.
2. **The pilot is continuing.** The component accepted under #1697 (0.36) is still maintained as Calor source by a named maintainer outside the project: its `.calr` files are the maintained source, the generated C# is build output, and the component has not been permanently exported to maintained C# (the export #1707 documents; a temporary emergency fork under #1707's rules is not an export). The external maintainer says so in a dated statement that is no older than the #1712 verdict. Maintenance by Calor's creator does not meet this criterion (#1701).

When both hold, record it in one comment on this epic that links the verdict, names the task class and links the external maintainer's statement. That comment releases #1718. It selects no investment and authorises no spend.

The pilot is an entry criterion because every child needs it: #1718 is accepted only when a named external maintainer confirms the need, #1719 opens only on a named external pilot's blocking requirement, and #1720 is accepted only when the named maintainer uses and accepts the capability in an externally maintained component.

**Hold rule.** In each of the following cases the milestone stays held, and the case is recorded in a comment on this epic with a link to the record that establishes it:

- **(a) The adopter fallback applies.** The adopter checkpoint at the close of 0.33 (#1833) recorded "demand unproven" instead of the consent of a named external maintainer, or the outreach decision (#1777) was declined, or left at its default line "not decided, treated as decline until changed", and the plan of record holds this milestone from that date. The fallback table in the plan of record holds 0.39. Nothing published under the fallback's 0.37 scope meets criterion 1, and with no pilot criterion 2 cannot be met.
- **(b) The verdict was not collected.** The collection budget decision (#1867) recorded a decline, in any of the forms that issue defines, so #1712 did not run and #1698 records the verdict as not collected.
- **(c) The verdict is not positive.** #1712 published a verdict that names no task class in which Calor added value beyond equipped C#: it is negative or unresolved for every task class. Its decision for 0.38 does not settle this case: a `revise` or `stop` for 0.38 beside a task class with demonstrated value still meets criterion 1.
- **(d) The pilot is not continuing.** The external maintainer has withdrawn, the component has been permanently exported to maintained C#, or the statement criterion 2 asks for has not been given.

**While held.**
- #1719 and #1720 do not start. No implementation, native prototype, participant work or paid work happens under this epic.
- #1718 stays open with no decision recorded. Its body allows evidence gathering and user interviews before its final decision. Under the hold, drafting from results that are already published is text only and may proceed. An interview is contact with a person outside the project: it takes place only with the pilot's external maintainer while the pilot is continuing, or with a contact the outreach decision (#1777) authorised.
- A hold is not the stop, narrow or redirect that #1718 may record. That decision is made inside an entered milestone, from a positive verdict and observed pilot demand. A held milestone is reported as held, with its case and record, and never as an investment decision or a delivery.
- Work outside this epic is unaffected: existing correctness and stabilization work continues (Non-goals).

**Lifting or ending the hold.** The hold lifts only when both entry criteria are recorded. In case (a) that first requires the 0.36 hold to lift, which needs a later dated entry by Calor's maintainer on the #1833 record that names a consenting external maintainer (see #1697), and then 0.36 and the full 0.37 comparison to complete. In case (b) it requires the collection budget to be authorised later and #1712 to run. In case (c) it requires a further comparison under the 0.37 protocol (#1708), with its own budget decision, to publish a positive verdict; the plan of record schedules none, so it would be filed as new work. In case (d) it requires a named maintainer outside the project to resume or take over maintenance of the component, with consent and source ownership recorded as #1701 requires. The hold has no timer. If Calor's maintainer decides this epic will not be pursued (a negative verdict from #1712, or the end of the pilot, is the occasion to decide), close the epic and its open children as not planned and link the record that caused the hold.

**Exit.** Once entered, the milestone exits on exactly one of three records. The record is posted as a comment on this epic and entered in the evidence ledger, the repository's list of published and adjudicated results (#1774):

1. **Delivered.** #1720 is closed as completed: the named maintainer used and accepted the selected capability against the criteria recorded before implementation, and the results, costs and the expand/narrow/redirect/stop recommendation are published in the release notes of the 0.39 release. The Acceptance items below are met.
2. **No investment selected.** #1718 is closed with a recorded stop, narrow or redirect because no useful investment was supported (the third Acceptance bullet of #1718), and #1720 is closed as not planned with that decision linked.
3. **Stopped before delivery.** #1718 selected an investment and the investment was stopped before useful delivery; #1720 is closed as not planned and the outcome is reported in the release notes of the 0.39 release (the fourth Acceptance bullet of #1720).

In all three, #1719 is closed either with its published continue/stop/alternative decision or as not planned with the #1718 decision linked. Records 2 and 3 are honest investment decisions, not a shipped capability. A held milestone has not exited.

## Work breakdown
Child issues cover an evidence-backed investment decision; an optional, explicitly gated native/deployment spike; and delivery plus external validation of the selected capability. Alternatives are not a commitment to implement every option.

## Candidate investments
Verification/model coverage, language work demonstrated necessary by pilots, integration/diagnostics/libraries, recovery/maintenance, packaging and supported OS/architecture deployment, or Native AOT where applicable. A native backend is eligible only when observed requirements block adoption and supported .NET options are insufficient.

## Acceptance
- Identify the customer/task, observed bottleneck, baseline, expected benefit, rejected alternatives, counterevidence, scope, cost ceiling, and acceptance criteria.
- Deliver the selected capability into an externally maintained component; measure acceptance quality, adoption/maintenance economics, deployment, and recovery.
- Preserve authoritative Calor source, explicit export semantics, human-governed obligations, artifact-linked evidence, and unknown/unchecked boundaries.
- Publish whether delivery justifies expansion, narrowing, a tooling-focused direction, or stopping. A decision document alone is not delivery.

## Dependencies and conditional completion
Consume #1697/#1698/#1699 results as available; do not treat negative results as a delivery mandate. Native investigation is conditional and must be explicitly marked not planned if its entry criteria are unmet. A documented stop/redirect is an honest investment decision, not a claim that a capability shipped.

A negative, unresolved or uncollected 0.37 verdict does more than withhold a mandate: it holds this milestone under the hold rule above. The 0.38 result is consumed as available, in whatever form exists when #1718 decides: the exit record #1699 defines (#1717's published decision, or the record that closed 0.38 without one), or, while 0.38 is in progress or held, that state as recorded on #1699. This milestone does not wait for 0.38.

Dependency edges ("A → B" reads "A must complete before B"):

Into the epic:
- #1777 (outreach decision) → #1833 (adopter checkpoint) → #1697 (0.36 pilot accepted) → #1712 (0.37 verdict) → the exit record of #1698 → entry criterion 1.
- #1701 (named external maintainer, component and source ownership) and the #1697 exit record → entry criterion 2.
- #1697 pilot findings (#1706 improvement and costs, #1707 recovery) and the #1712 verdict → #1718.
- #1705 (0.36) → #1719: the support matrix and deployment checks #1705 publishes are the supported .NET deployment, Native AOT included where the pilot application is compatible, against which #1719's entry criteria reproduce the limitation.

Inside the epic:
- Entry criteria recorded on this epic → #1718.
- #1718 → #1720 in every case. #1718 → #1719 only when #1718 explicitly authorises and funds the native investigation; otherwise #1719 is closed as not planned.
- #1719 → #1720 only when the selected path needs the native experiment.

Out of the epic:
- None. No issue in the plan of record depends on this epic.

Not an edge:
- 0.38. #1718 reads whichever 0.38 record exists when it decides and does not wait for #1699 or #1717.
- The Rust cost reading of 0.33 (#1831) measures Rust as a language an agent writes, and it is reported, never adjudicated. #1719 names Rust only as something the compiler might emit. That reading is neither an entry criterion nor a success criterion of #1719.

## Non-goals
No preapproved compiler rewrite, production native backend, direct assembly strategy, broad syntax expansion, universal performance advantage, or removal of implementation review. Existing correctness/stabilization work continues. No paid collection or research reactivation is authorized by planning.

## Tracked child issues
- [ ] #1718 - Select one customer-backed investment and publish alternatives and stop criteria
- [ ] #1719 - Conditional: evaluate native deployment only against an unmet pilot requirement
- [ ] #1720 - Deliver the selected capability and validate external maintenance outcomes

## Conditional work and delivery gate
- The entry criteria are recorded on this epic first. #1718 then selects one investment using the #1712 verdict, whichever 0.38 record exists (the exit record of #1699, or its recorded state while 0.38 is in progress or held) and external pilot demand. These alternatives are not parallel commitments. The decision is published as a document under `docs/plans/` (precedents: `docs/plans/call-w-adjudication.md`, `docs/plans/safe-delegation-m0/decision.md`) and linked from a comment on #1718; nothing is added under `docs/plans/evidence/`.
- #1719 is conditional native exploration only after an explicit go decision; if criteria are unmet, close it as not planned with rationale.
- #1720 remains unscheduled until the selected capability and prospective acceptance criteria are recorded. It depends on #1719 only for a native path that needs that experiment.
- When #1720 is updated with the selected deliverable, it states how the deliverable meets the planning rules of the plan of record, `docs/plans/roadmap-0.31-0.39.md` (#1765). Three apply here. Paid agent runs: a written spend ceiling, abort triggers, a zero-cost dry pass (`--null-agent`, which applies a reference solution instead of calling an agent), one pinned model and a reading written in advance for each outcome; filing or updating an issue authorises no spend. Breaking changes: under the compatibility promise that the edition declaration (#1805) publishes, existing spellings do not change; additive syntax is allowed, and a breaking change made despite that ships with a rewriter that migrates fixtures, benchmark pairs and documentation in the same change. New or tightened hard errors: the conversion scorecard's native count (files converted to Calor) and the density ratio (Calor tokens over C# tokens) do not regress, and the number of files that newly fall to whole-file preservation (kept as their original C#) is reported.
- A stop/redirect is an honest decision but must not be reported as a shipped capability. Keep existing compiler correctness/stabilization work moving.
